For each shape the probe solves `solve_alone(&Train::alone(shape, 2.0, 0.0))` and prints the train's reported contact_ratio, limited_by, efficiency, max pressure, worst position and mesh notes. It also rebuilds the tip-limited path through `Screw::path_of_contact_at` and calls `limited_by_face` directly.

It then computes the face-bounded zone independently, sharing none of `half_span`, `axial_centre` or the EPSILON guard. For each member i, the axial coordinate along the line is z_i(s) = (through - O_i)·a_i + s·(n·a_i), with O_0 = 0, a_0 = z, O_1 = (a, 0, 0) and a_1 = (0, sin Σ, cos Σ). Each face requires |z_i(s)| <= b_i/2, which is linear in s. Intersecting those intervals with the tip zone gives eps = max(0, length) / normal base pitch.

Smallest inputs:
- (A) `arr::pair([17,43])`, Σ = 0.5°, clearance 0.02, both faces 10 mm, `with_additional_helix(20)`.
- (B) `arr::crossed([17,23], 20)` with first helix 10°, x = +1/-1, zero clearance, both faces 8 mm.
- (C) `arr::crossed([17,23], 30)` with first helix 30° (so the second member is spur), clearance 0.5, first face 30 mm, spur face 4.7 mm.
repro.note:
I re-judge severity as high, the same as the ledger.

Why high:
- The failure is silent. It gives a false "sound" answer where no tooth contact exists on the face.
- It is non-monotone: a narrower face gives a higher ratio.
- It suppresses the one warning (contact_ratio_below_one) meant to catch exactly this.
- Efficiency, locking friction and the worst-position rating all run along a zone the faces do not hold.
- It reaches ordinary designs, not only near-parallel ones: case B is a 20° crossed pair with a shift and an 8 mm face at module 2.

Independence: the correct value (eps 0 once the interval is empty) comes from a closed-form linear intersection over the path's public geometry (through, normal, zone, centre_distance, shaft angle). It agrees with the crate to 6 digits wherever the zone is non-empty (A at 30/16/12 mm, B at 60/30 mm, C at 30/4.8 mm), so it is checking the same geometry and diverges only where the crate falls back.

Fix direction (verifier's refinement, which I endorse):
- Write each bound as |z_i0 + s·(n·a_i)| <= b_i/2. This handles n·a_i = 0 with no epsilon: the plane is either wholly inside the face or wholly outside it.
- Return an explicit empty-zone value instead of None. Route it through the no-contact policy: eps 0, the below-one note, and the pitch-point efficiency fallback.
- Fix `PointBuilt::zone` (shape.rs:2500-2505, `.map_or(*path, ..)`) and `point_mesh_report` (shape.rs:2719-2722, `unwrap_or((*path, Face))`), which both currently fall back to the full tip path.
- Correct docs/state.md:711-716.

Suggested gates:
- Case A at 10 mm must give eps 0 with the note.
- Case C at a 4.7 mm spur face must give eps 0.
- Eps must be non-increasing as either face narrows.

I created no worktree and made no changes in the repository.

title: face_widths_for mirrors a one-sided interval and ignores faces centred off the contact, so the 'width for continuity' does not deliver eps = 1
claim: When want > 2*near, the needed interval is [near - want, near] if the upper zone end is the near one, and [-near, want - near] otherwise. The code builds [half - want, half] and [-half, want - half] with half = want - near. That is the mirror image, and it pokes past the zone's near end. Each member's width is then 2*rate*max|end - centre| about its own mid-plane, so an off-centre face also covers zone the interval did not ask for. The reported width therefore gives far less or far more than the target. The existing gates only use centred, symmetric zones (near > want/2).
evidence: Probe 'cont': at 0.5 deg with 0.02 clearance, the widths [10.85, 10.87] give eps 0.261, not 1. At 5 deg with 0.02 clearance, [2.11, 1.91] give 1.216. Probe 'shift' at train level, zero clearance: 45 deg x1=1 reports [3.857, 2.152] and those faces give eps 0.234; 20 deg x1=0.6 reports [3.57, 3.36] giving 0.805; 20 deg x1=1 reports [9.95, 9.26] giving 0.363. The centred cases give exactly 1.000, which is why a_face_width_sized_for_continuity_delivers_exactly_that_contact_ratio and the_width_a_crossed_pair_reports_for_continuity_buys_exactly_continuous_contact pass.
proposal: Size each member on its own, in closed form. For member i with mid-plane parameter c_i and tip zone [z0, z1], the covered length is L_i(h) = max(0, min(z1, c_i + h) - max(z0, c_i - h)). It is piecewise linear in h (slopes 2, 1, 0) and non-decreasing. Solve L_i(h) = want for the least h by the slope cases; width_i = 2 h sin(beta_b,i). Report the joint result as what limited_by_face gives for both widths together. Better still, place one window of length want inside the zone as close as possible to both c_i (clamp the mean of the c_i into [z0 + want/2, z1 - want/2]) and size both faces to cover it. State in reference.md which of the two the figure is.
validation: Law: limited_by_face(face_widths_for(target)).contact_ratio == target to 1e-12, over shaft angles 0.5..110, shifts -1..1, clearances 0..0.3 and one-sided zones. The last need a small addendum on one member or x2 = -x1 = 1. HEAD fails at five of the probe's cases.

verdict.reason:
Holds as stated. Take the case want > 2·near with the upper end near. The code's interval [half - want, half] = [-near, want - near] runs past z1 = near and leaves the part below -near uncovered, so it is the mirror of the needed [near - want, near]. Each width is then 2·rate·max|end - c_i| about that member's own mid-plane, so an off-centre face also takes in zone the interval did not ask for. Both errors cancel only when c_i ≈ 0, because a face symmetric about 0 covers the mirror too. That is why both gates, and one-sided zones with shift sum 0, come out at exactly 1.

Severity is medium rather than high. The figure sizes nothing (reference.md says so). A designer who types it back in gets a contact ratio that is reported correctly while the contact stays partly on the face, and the 'contact ratio below one' note does fire then, so the error shows itself. It is still a stated contract off by a factor of 1.2 to 4 on shifted pairs.
verdict.evidence:
Mode f1, on the path exactly as the train builds it (the members' own tips and running distance):

| Case | Reported widths (mm) | eps at those widths | Scale needed on widths for eps 1 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.5 deg, 0.02 mm clearance | [10.85, 10.87] | 0.2612 | 1.131 |
| 5 deg, 0.02 mm clearance | [2.109, 1.910] | 1.2163 | 0.811 |
| 45 deg, x1 = 1, zero clearance | [3.857, 2.152] | 0.2338 | 1.756 |
| 20 deg, x1 = 0.6 | [3.572, 3.362] | 0.8052 | not recorded |
| 20 deg, x1 = 1 | [9.945, 9.265] | 0.3627 | not recorded |

The centred cases give exactly 1: 90 deg (1.0000), 90 deg with x = ±0.5 (0.99999999999999), and the worm (1.0). So do one-sided zones with shift sum 0, for example 90 deg with x = [1, -1], zone [0, 4.78] (mode onesided). Train-level resolves at the reported widths reproduce 0.233752, 0.805164 and 0.362660.
verdict.proposal_note:
The first proposal, sizing each member on its own to cover `want`, is wrong. The contact ratio is set by the intersection of the two faces' windows, not by each window alone. Take the auditor's own 20 deg, x1 = 1 case. Member 0 (centre +28) would cover [0.23, 3.18] and member 1 (centre -27.9) would cover [-0.54, 2.41]. The intersection is 2.18 mm, eps 0.74.

Use the 'better still' form. Choose one window [w0, w0 + want] inside [z0, z1], then set width_i = 2·|n·a_i|·max(|w0 - c_i|, |w0 + want - c_i|). Name a rule for w0 in reference.md, for example the one that minimises the larger width, or the clamp of mean(c_i) that the auditor gives. With the clamp, this example gives [9.33, 9.87] mm and eps exactly 1.

Keep the law 'limited_by_face(face_widths_for(t)) = t' over off-centre cases.

title: The locking friction along the path assumes the path locks below the pitch point; false for forward drive, so it silently falls back and mixes models
claim: CrossedPath::locking_friction brackets the root of the path-average efficiency on [0, pitch-point threshold]. The doc says the path average is 'always inside' that interval because 'along the path there is more sliding'. It is not always inside. When the bracket fails, brent returns None, and PointBuilt::locking_friction substitutes the pitch-point threshold beside a path-average efficiency: exactly the mixing the doc says must not happen. The test law 'the path average can only lose' (path eta <= pitch eta, both directions) is also false in general.
evidence: Probe 'above', 512 samples, tips r+m: 28 of 80 forward cases with a pitch threshold below 0.3 had a path efficiency still > 0 at that threshold. Examples: 2/41 at 90 deg, beta1 4.5, threshold 0.0740, path eta there 0.00346; 1/25 at 110 deg, beta1 22, threshold 0.0328, eta 0.00196; 11/37 at 90 deg, beta1 9, 0.1488, eta 0.00077. The path average exceeded the pitch-point efficiency in 45 of 2940 (pair, shaft angle, split, mu, direction) cases, by up to 0.0072. Example: 1/25 at 90, beta1 4.5, mu 0.06: path 0.19248 against pitch 0.18776. Probe 'bracket', all thresholds: 236 of 532 had no bracket. At absurd friction (mu 26-54) the path average reaches 3-7.7, where the local input torque changes sign along the path.
proposal: Bracket by expansion: start at the pitch-point threshold and double while the path eta is still > 0, up to a stated ceiling such as mu = 1. Return None only when no root lies below the ceiling, and report that as a fact about the path. Drop the pitch-point fallback in PointBuilt::locking_friction. In screw.rs:1203-1213, reference.md and the crossed.rs test docs, replace 'locks at a slightly lower friction' and 'always inside' with the measured statement. Restrict the 'can only lose' law to the case it holds in (backward drive), or delete it.
validation: Law over the probe grid, both directions: wherever a threshold is reported, path.efficiency(threshold) is 0 within 1e-12, positive at 0.99x and negative at 1.01x. It fails on HEAD at 2/41, 90 deg, beta1 4.5.

verdict.reason:
All three sub-claims hold.
- The bracket [0, pitch threshold] fails in forward drive when the driving member has the high lead (a wheel-like member driving a worm-like one). There the path average locks ABOVE the pitch-point threshold, brent returns None, and PointBuilt::locking_friction substitutes the pitch-point figure beside a path-average efficiency. That is the mixing the doc says must not happen.
- The 'can only lose' law is false in general.

Severity is low rather than medium. At plausible friction (thresholds below 0.15) the path root sits within about 1 % of the pitch threshold, so the inconsistent window is thin; the gaps reach 9-14 % only where thresholds are 0.3-0.5. The law's largest violation is 0.0072 in efficiency. It is still a false physical statement in a doc comment and in a test's doc.
verdict.evidence:
Mode f2: 8 tooth pairs × 5 shaft angles × 7 helix splits, tips at r + m, 2048 samples. Of 512 finite positive pitch thresholds, 195 have no path root in the bracket, 39 of them with a threshold below 0.5.

True path roots, found by expanding the bracket (mode f2root):
- 2/41, 90 deg, β1 4.5 forward: pitch 0.07396, path 0.07421 (×1.0035).
- 1/25, 90 deg, β1 18 forward: 0.30532 against 0.33238 (×1.089).
- 1/25, 90 deg, β1 27 forward: 0.47880 against 0.54530 (×1.139).
- 1/40, 110 deg, β1 33 forward: ×1.042.
- Backward, and forward at 17/23 at 45/45 deg: ×0.98-0.99, as documented.

Train level (mode f2mix): 2/41 at 90 deg, first helix 4.5, faces 200 mm. At μ = 0.074 the train reports forward η 0.00143 (not locked) beside a threshold of 0.07396 (the pitch fallback), and the note is 'near forward locking' with friction 0.074 over threshold 0.0740.

The path average beats the pitch point in 34 of 1512 cases, worst +0.00722 (1/25, 90 deg, β1 4.5, μ 0.06: 0.19248 against 0.18776). Five of those 34 are backward, all at 110 deg, and tiny: for example 17/23, β1 22, μ 0.1 gives 0.2364961 against 0.2364488.
verdict.proposal_note:
A fixed ceiling such as μ = 1 is itself a magic number. It would also turn today's reported backward thresholds above 1 (6.23 or 17.6 on some pairs) into None, which then needs a new representation. A principled bracket exists instead:
- Each point's efficiency is a ratio of two moments that are linear in μ, so each point has a closed-form zero, μ_i = -T_out(0)/T_out'(μ).
- Wherever each point's efficiency is decreasing, the path average's first root lies between the smallest and largest μ_i over the zone.
- Bracket there; no ceiling and no fallback are needed.

The proposal to keep the 'can only lose' law for backward drive is also wrong: it fails backward too, at Σ = 110 deg (by up to 4.7e-5). Delete it, or state it for the regime it was measured in, with that regime named.

title: As the shaft angle goes to 0 there are three wrong regimes before parallel: refusal, 100 % efficiency with no zone, and a cancellation-prone sliding ratio. Closed forms exist.
claim:
is_crossed sends any nonzero angle to the screw model. The screw model then:
(a) computes sliding_ratio = sqrt(1 - 2k cos S + k^2), which cancels catastrophically. It returns 0 and refuses AxesAreParallel below about 1e-7 deg.
(b) solves the contact normal by dividing by sin S. It picks the mesh branch by an 8-way search accepted within 1e-6*a, and places the line through an ill-conditioned 3x3 Cramer solve. Below about 5e-4 deg the branch offset exceeds the tolerance and the path is None.
(c) with no path, falls back to the pitch-point efficiency (which tends to 1), reports contact ratio 0, and sets flank_interference to [true, true].
F84's closure measured the seams at 0.01 deg only.
evidence: Probe 'sigma0': 17/43, helix 20, face 30, zero clearance. At S = 0 (line contact): eta 0.983694, pmax 364.09. At 1e-12 and 1e-9 deg: ERR 'parallel axes: a worm stage needs crossed shafts...'. At 1e-6 and 1e-4 deg: eps 0, eta 1.000000 both ways, lim Face. At 1e-2 deg: eps 1.6637, eta 0.983869, which is correct. Python branch_offset.py for the same pair: the branch offset is 7.5e-6 mm at 1e-3 deg, 1.8e-4 at 3e-4, 5.3e-4 at 1e-4 and 20 mm at 1e-6, against a tolerance of 3.2e-5. The solved normal's error grows from 6e-14 to 1.1e-8. Probe 'tiny': the sqrt sliding ratio is off by 1.2e-5 at 1e-4 deg, 1.2e-3 at 1e-5 and 0.20 at 1e-6, then refused. Probe 'normal': contact_normal() equals [sin a_n, -cos a_n cos b1, cos a_n sin b1] to 2.8e-14 at every shaft angle and pressure angle tried. It does not depend on S at all.
proposal:
Replace the solves with closed forms:
- sliding_ratio = |sin S / cos b2|, and the sliding direction cosines on the two velocities are sin b1 and -sin b2. The tangential balance is then (+-cos a_n cos b_i + mu s_i), continuous through S = 0, so Screw::new needs no AxesAreParallel.
- normal = [sin a_n, -cos a_n cos b1, cos a_n sin b1], with the flank as a sign.
- At the reference distance the line of action is P + s n, with P = [r1, 0, 0]. Tangency parameters are foot(P, n, O_i, a_i), whose denominator is cos^2 b_b,i.
- At another distance a, displace the line by delta, solved from u1.delta = 0, u2.delta = (a - a_ref)(u2.x), n.delta = 0. It is exactly 0 at a = a_ref, and its only ill-conditioning is the physical slide of about da/S.
This deletes mesh_branch, its 1e-6 tolerance, the 8-line loop, solve3 and its 1e-12. path_eff.py demonstrates it: the anchored closed-form construction reproduces the crate's eps 1.8338 and eta 0.684302.
validation: Sweep S logarithmically over 1e-12..1 deg at zero clearance. The path exists at every point, eps tends to eps_a/cos^2 b_b, eta tends to the parallel balance, and there is no refusal for S != 0. Keep the existing 90 deg and parallel-limit gates bit-for-bit (within 1e-13).

verdict.reason:
Every mechanism holds:
- The sqrt cancellation.
- The AxesAreParallel refusal below about 1e-7 deg.
- The division by sin Σ in contact_normal.
- The ill-conditioned Cramer solve (det ∝ Σ), which pushes the branch offset past the 1e-6·a tolerance near 2e-4 to 5e-4 deg. Acceptance is erratic there: 3e-4 passes, and 2e-4 and 5e-4 fail.
- The missing path, which falls back to pitch-point efficiency near 1, eps 0 and flank_interference [true, true].

The closed forms are right:
- n = [sin α_n, -cos α_n cos β1, cos α_n sin β1] satisfies both constraints exactly, since n·a2 = -cos α_n sin β2 = -sin β_b2.
- |v_s| = |sin Σ / cos β2|, because cos²β1 + cos²β2 - 2 cos β1 cos β2 cos(β1+β2) = sin²(β1+β2). The worst error over 10^4 random pairs was 4.4e-16.

Severity is low. The whole affected range is below 5e-4 deg (under 2 arcseconds), which no designer enters on purpose; the value of this finding is the simplification (it deletes mesh_branch, its tolerance and the sin Σ division), not the exposure.
verdict.evidence:
Mode f3, 17/43, +20 deg helix, 30 mm faces, zero clearance:
- Σ = 0: line contact, eps 4.758, η 0.983694.
- Σ = 1e-12, 1e-9 and 1e-7 deg: ERR 'parallel axes'.
- Σ = 1e-6, 1e-5 and 1e-4 deg: eps 0, Face, η 1.000000 both ways, travel [0, 0].
- Σ = 3e-4 deg and above: eps 1.6637, η 0.983868.

Mode f3sr, relative error of the sqrt form against sin Σ/cos β2: -3.5e-9 at 1e-2 deg, 1.2e-5 at 1e-4, -1.2e-3 at 1e-5, -0.198 at 1e-6, then refused.

A Python replica of mesh_branch (notes/verify-crossed-worm/branch.py) gives these branch offsets against a tolerance of 3.19e-5:

| Σ (deg) | Offset | det |
|---|---|---|
| 1e-2 | 1.75e-7 | -6.7e-5 |
| 1e-3 | 7.5e-6 | not recorded |
| 5e-4 | 3.6e-5 | not recorded |
| 2e-4 | 1.16e-4 | not recorded |
| 1e-4 | 5.3e-4 | not recorded |
| 1e-6 | 4.15 | -6.7e-9 |

The normal's error against the closed form grows from 8.9e-13 to 2.1e-9 over the same range.

shape.rs:3869 maps a missing path to flank_interference [true, true].
verdict.proposal_note: The proposal is sound. The line through P along the closed-form n at the reference distance needs no branch search, and foot()'s denominator becomes cos² β_b. Say explicitly that the displaced-line solve at a ≠ a_ref stays ill-conditioned as Σ → 0: that is the physical slide of about Δa/Σ, not a numerical defect. Also say that dropping AxesAreParallel from Screw::new relies on the sin Σ/cos β2 form. Keep the Σ = 0 dispatch to the line model (is_crossed), because the point model at Σ → 0 with Δa ≠ 0 slides where the line model rotates, which is the documented seam.

title: 'No stress depends on the face width' is false, yet it is the stated licence for shipping worm proportions
claim: crossed.rs says a worm's length and a wheel's face width 'enter no stress in this crate', so a recommendation 'cannot distort an answer', which is 'what makes it admissible where a K_v is not'. reference.md:1052/1082 and state.md:391 repeat it. But the rating takes max(ellipse, line) with line_length = min_i b_i/cos(b_b,i), and it rates at single-pair bounds of the face-clipped zone. reference.md:1134-1138 itself says the line term governs at small shaft angles. The only gate is 4 mm against 40 mm on the shipped worm, where neither mechanism binds.
evidence: Probe 'wormface', shipped worm 1/40: wheel face 0.2 mm gives pmax 7278.9 MPa, 0.5 mm gives 4657.5, and 1 mm or more gives 3376.1. Thread length 2 mm gives 3400.85. Probe 'face', 17/23 at 90 deg, faces 12 / 3 / 0.7 / 0.1 mm: pmax 1091.1 / 1122.3 / 1096.0 / 2862.5.
proposal: Restate it: the face widths enter the rating through the line term and the zone they clip, and a sensibly proportioned worm is insensitive to them. Justify the proportions by what they are: labelled inputs, whose effect on the rating is shown. Replace the equality test with a law: pmax is independent of b while the ellipse governs and the zone is tip-limited, and non-decreasing as b shrinks past either bound.
validation: Two tests: one asserts independence inside the regime; the other asserts the stress rises below the width where the line term or the zone clip binds (0.5 mm on the shipped wheel).

verdict.reason:
The categorical statements are false:
- crossed.rs:78-83 'enter no stress in this crate ... cannot distort an answer'.
- reference.md:1052 'A crossed pair has no stress that depends on its face width, so nothing about strength can size it'.
- reference.md:1082.
- state.md:392-393.
- train/mod.rs:679-680 'a point contact's peak pressure does not depend on it at all'.
- The on-screen strings train_note_wheel_width and train_note_worm_length ('changes no stress').

The face enters the rating twice: through line_length = min b_i/cos β_b,i in max(ellipse, line), and through the single-pair bounds of the face-clipped zone. The doc on the test itself (crossed.rs:549-557) already concedes the second. For the shipped worm at 90 deg the practical conclusion holds: nothing moves for a wheel face of 1 mm or more. But the general crossed-pair statement is materially false at small shaft angles with ordinary faces, where the line term governs and σ ∝ 1/√b exactly as on a parallel pair.
verdict.evidence:
Mode f4, shipped worm 1/40, wheel face:

| Wheel face (mm) | pmax (MPa) |
|---|---|
| 0.1 | 10202 |
| 0.2 | 7278.90 |
| 0.5 | 4657.48 |
| 1, 2, 4.69, 40 | 3376.09 |

Worm length 2 mm gives 3400.85.

Stronger evidence (mode f4b), 17/43 at +20 deg helix, 0.02 mm clearance:
- Σ = 2 deg: faces 5 / 10 / 20 / 40 mm give pmax 852.5 / 602.8 / 531.5 / 531.5 MPa.
- Σ = 5 deg: faces 5 / 10 give 837.4 / 729.7.
- Σ = 0.5 deg: faces 30 / 16 / 12 / 2 give 351 / 481 / 530 / 1360.
- At 10 deg and above, faces of 5-40 mm give identical pressures.
verdict.corrected_claim: The face widths enter a crossed rating through the line term, which governs below about 5-10 deg of shaft angle at ordinary faces, and through the zone they clip. On a worm at 90 deg, with faces of 1 mm or more, neither binds. So the worm proportions are harmless in practice, but 'no stress depends on the face width' is false for crossed pairs in general. The same false claim appears in train/mod.rs:679-683 and in the two UI strings.
verdict.proposal_note: Restate the claim in all six places, including the UI strings in all five catalogues. In the line-governed regime the premise of the gear.face_width_as_entered policy ('nothing about strength can size it') also fails; see the missed item. Replace the equality test with the two-regime law the auditor proposes.

title: The worm proportions are misattributed and partly mis-transcribed; two of them are geometry the crate could compute from its own tip radii
claim: Wheel face: the code uses b2 = 2 m_x sqrt(q+1), capped at 0.67 d1, and calls both 'BS 721 ... two statements from the same source'. RoyMech's BS 721 gives only b ~ 2m sqrt(q+1). That is the chord of the worm tip circle at the reference line, 2 sqrt(r_a1^2 - r1^2) with an addendum of m_x. MITcalc's CSN rule is 0.75 (1+2/q) d1 = 0.75 d_a1 for z1 < 4 and 0.67 d_a1 for z1 >= 4. The AGMA 0.67 figure caps the EFFECTIVE width used in a rating, and it is on the worm's diameter. Worm length: MITcalc gives (11 + c z2) m_x as CSN, not 'DIN/CSN'. Its DIN form is geometric, L = sqrt((d_e2/2)^2 - (a - d_a1/2)^2). Other sources use (12.5 + 0.09 z2) m for z1 = 3-4. The step in c at z1 = 4 is a rule of thumb, stated as if it were a fact.
evidence: wormstage: the wheel face is 4.690 mm, which is 0.67 x 7.0, so the misattributed cap is what binds on the canary. CSN's cap would be 0.75 x d_a1 = 6.75 mm, the recommendation 2 x 1.0104 x sqrt(7.93) = 5.69 mm, a 21 % change. The worm length of 13.539 mm matches MITcalc's CSN formula exactly. Sources: mitcalc.com/doc/gear4/help/en/gear4.htm; roymech.org/Useful_Tables/Drive/Worm_Gears.
proposal: Replace the table with the geometric forms, evaluated from the members' own tip radii: b2 = 2 sqrt(r_a1^2 - r1^2), and b1 = 2 sqrt(r_a2^2 - (a - r_a1)^2) (DIN's chord). They follow the designer's addendum, depend on no z1 step and need no source table. If the CSN/BS/AGMA figures are kept, offer them as named alternatives, each attributed exactly (CSN 0.75/0.67 d_a1; BS 721 2m sqrt(q+1); AGMA effective width <= 0.67 d_m). Update reference.md:1074-1077 and the golden corpus deliberately.
validation: Test that the chord identity holds at the default addendum: 2 sqrt(r_a1^2 - r1^2) == 2 m_x sqrt(q+1) exactly when r_a1 = r1 + m_x. Check homogeneity in the module. Cross-check one MITcalc worked example. Rerun check_golden and expect the wormstage face row to move.

verdict.reason:
The misattributions are confirmed from the sources:
- RoyMech's BS 721 material gives only 'b_a = Effective face width of worm wheel. About 2.m √(q+1)'.
- The '0.67 d1' appears only in RoyMech's 'AGMA method' section, as the effective face width inside the AGMA tangential-load rating ('actual face width, but not to exceed 0.67 d1').
- MITcalc gives (11 + c z2) m_x under ČSN only; its DIN form is geometric, L = ((de2/2)² - (a - da1/2)²)^0.5.
- The ČSN wheel face is 0.75 (1+2/q) d1 = 0.75 d_a1 for z1 < 4 and 0.67 d_a1 for z1 ≥ 4.

So 'Two statements from the same source' (crossed.rs:126) is false, and the on-screen strings 'per BS 721 convention' and 'per DIN/ČSN convention' misattribute.

The crate's own rationale for the cap is also geometrically wrong: 'past about two thirds of the worm's reference diameter the wheel's outer corners are beyond the thread'. The thread reaches the wheel's reference line over the chord 2√(r_a1² - r1²), which is 5.66 mm on the shipped worm, wider than the 4.69 mm cap.

The chord identity is exact: 2√((r1+m_x)² - r1²) = 2 m_x √(q+1), giving 5.68977 by both routes.

The 'mis-transcribed' part is not established. The crate names BS 721, not ČSN, for b2, so 0.67 d1 is a misattributed and misapplied AGMA rating limit, not a mis-copied ČSN coefficient. Also, of the two 'geometry the crate could compute' only the BS 721 face is literally a chord of the crate's tips. The worm length the crate ships is ČSN's non-geometric formula; only DIN's alternative is geometric.
verdict.evidence:
From the probe:
- The wormstage golden output has wheel face 4.690 = 0.67 × 7.0, so the cap binds.
- The BS formula gives 2 × 1.01036 × √7.9282 = 5.690.
- The chord at the crate's actual addendum, which is in m_n (r_a1 = 4.5, r1 = 3.5), gives 5.657.
- ČSN (z1 < 4) gives 0.75 × d_a1 = 0.75 × 9 = 6.75.
- Worm length 13.5389 = (11 + 0.06·40) × 1.010363, the ČSN formula exactly.

Sources: https://www.mitcalc.com/doc/gear4/help/en/gear4.htm (the ČSN and DIN formulas for b1 and b2) and https://roymech.org/Useful_Tables/Drive/Worm_Gears.html (the Nomenclature entry for b_a; 0.67 d1 under 'AGMA method of Designing Worm Gears').

UI: strings_en.toml:385-386. Docs: reference.md:1074-1077.
verdict.corrected_claim: The wheel-face cap 0.67 d1 is the AGMA rating's limit on effective face width, not a BS 721 statement and not a physical face recommendation. The worm-length formula is ČSN, not DIN/ČSN. Both errors reach the screen. BS 721's 2m√(q+1) is exactly the chord of the worm tip circle at the wheel's reference line when the addendum is m_x, so it can be computed from the members' own tips. DIN's worm length is likewise a chord (per MITcalc, without a factor 2).
verdict.proposal_note:
Two cautions on the proposal:
- The proposed b1 = 2√(r_a2² - (a - r_a1)²) carries a factor 2 that MITcalc's DIN form does not show. Check the source before attributing it to DIN.
- For the crate's cylindrical (non-throated) wheel both chords still describe an enveloping wheel. On the shipped worm the length chord is 17.98 mm and the face chord 5.66 mm, while the modelled contact needs 2.76 / 0.41 mm. Replacing the table with chords swaps one enveloping-wheel convention for another.

The cleaner fix is the related finding's: make the automatic crossed face come from the modelled zone, and keep the conventions only as explicitly attributed options (BS 721 2m√(q+1); ČSN 0.75/0.67 d_a1; ČSN (11 + c z2) m_x). The AGMA 0.67 d1 belongs to an effective-width rating the crate does not perform, so drop it. Correct the on-screen strings in all five catalogues, and move the golden output deliberately.

title: A cylindrical-wheel (point-contact) model is sized with enveloping-wheel conventions while its own zone of action gives the answer
claim: The proportions describe an enveloping (throated) wheel wrapping the worm, as crossed.rs:90-97 admits. The crate models a cylindrical involute wheel with point contact, whose zone and axial travel it already computes exactly (CrossedPath::axial_travel, face_widths_for). So the automatic worm faces are a rule of thumb about a different machine, hidden behind 'automatic'. By the owner's rule, estimates should be explicit user-visible options.
evidence: Shipped worm: recommended widths 13.539 / 4.690 mm, while the modelled contact needs 2.760 / 0.410 mm for eps = 1 (probe 'wormface'). The whole tip-limited zone travels less than 3 mm along the worm. Probe 'wormshift': with a wheel shift of 0.25-1.0 the continuity width grows to 4.19 / 1.41 mm; the proportions do not move.
proposal: Make the automatic face of any crossed member, worm or not, the width that holds the whole tip-limited zone. That is 2 x max|zone end - c_i| x sin(b_b,i), computed about the member's own mid-plane, which follows shift and clearance. Keep the worm conventions as an explicit 'enveloping-wheel proportions' option with its source. This also removes the only place the worm bit changes a number (shape.rs:3156), so a worm becomes a label.
validation: Law: at the automatic faces, limited_by == Tips (up to 1e-12) for every crossed preset and a shift/clearance grid. The worm bit then changes no figure except the names.

verdict.reason: The substance is right. The worm faces are enveloping-wheel conventions applied to a cylindrical, point-contact model. The premise crossed.rs gives for shipping them is stale: lines 88-97 say the crate 'does not derive that zone (docs/reference.md#crossed-axes, open)', but CrossedPath::face_widths_for, axial_travel and limited_by_face now derive and apply it. Three parts of the finding do not hold. (a) 'Hidden behind automatic' is overstated. The automatic value carries a note naming its source (strings_en.toml:385-386, 'automatic uses {width} mm per BS 721 convention'), and the input can be edited. (b) One evidence figure is wrong. The auditor says the tip-limited zone travels 'less than 3 mm along the worm'; it travels 4.98 mm. (c) The proposal is unsafe as written, because the zone-only width is narrower than the Hertz patch and so raises the rated stress. No reported stress is wrong at the shipped proportions, so the defect is conceptual and documentary, not a wrong number.
verdict.evidence:
Probe probes/verify-crossed-worm-b, mode f6.
- Shipped worm 1/40, d1 7: faces 13.539 / 4.690 in use (the recommendation). face_width_for_continuity [2.7603, 0.4099]. axial_travel [4.9807, 0.7189]. limited_by Tips. pmax 3376.09 MPa.
- Axial centre gives 0.1066 / -0.6829; the wheel's widths grow with its shift. Continuity width at x2 = 0.25 / 0.5 / 1.0: [2.94, 0.58] / [3.13, 0.75] / [4.19, 1.41]. The proportions do not move.
- The auditor's own formula for the tip-zone widths, 2·max|zone end − c_i|·sin β_b,i, gives [5.240, 0.772] on the shipped worm. At those faces ε stays 1.814 (Tips), but pmax rises to 3679.35 MPa (+9.0 %) and the patch is truncated to 0.779 mm. The ellipse is 1.581 mm long.
- The same construction on worm 2/41 d16: widths [5.31, 0.68], pmax 2066.83 → 2522.53 MPa (+22 %).
- Wheel-face sweep at 13.539 worm: pmax is unchanged at 3376.09 down to 1.0 mm, and rises below the patch length: 4657 MPa at 0.5 mm, 7279 at 0.2.
- The worm bit changes a number only at shape.rs:3156 (the other uses are 374 is_worm_thread, 733 member_names and arrangements.rs:838 family), so 'the only place' holds.
- reference.md:1063-1066 records the opposite decision for crossed gear pairs: 'an automatic face on a crossed gear pair stands at its box ... because the alternative — a face that grows with every helix the designer tries — was a width nobody had asked for'.
verdict.corrected_claim: The worm's automatic faces are enveloping-wheel conventions (13.54 / 4.69 mm on the shipped worm), while the modelled cylindrical contact needs 2.76 / 0.41 mm for ε = 1 and 5.24 / 0.77 mm to hold the whole tip zone. The documented reason for using published practice ('this crate ... does not derive that zone', crossed.rs:88-97) is stale. The convention is labelled on screen and editable, and at the shipped widths it changes no reported stress.
verdict.proposal_note: Do not set the automatic face to the zone width alone. PointBuilt::rate bounds the contact line by min_i(b_i / cos β_b,i), so a face narrower than the ellipse raises the rating: +9 % on the shipped worm and +22 % on 2/41, which moves the golden worm figures. A model-derived automatic width must satisfy b_i ≥ max(2·max|zone end − c_i|·sin β_b,i, 2a_patch·cos β_b,i) over every load case, or it must be kept as a reported floor. Extending it to crossed gear pairs reverses the documented decision at reference.md:1063. That decision's argument is weak but should be argued explicitly, not overridden silently. The minimum fix is to rewrite crossed.rs:88-97 to say that the zone is derived and that the proportions are a deliberate enveloping-wheel convention, sized well above the model's floor.

title: The rationale for reporting no bending on a worm rests on claims that are false for the standards and for the crate's own wheel
claim: (1) 'The tooth measured would not be the tooth loaded ... a worm wheel's tooth is ... throated'. The crate's wheel is an ordinary involute helical gear, the profile it generates; the throated wheel is what it does NOT model. (2) 'Worm gearing's rating standards rate durability, not bending, so no published bending allowable exists'. ISO/TS 14521 (and ISO/TR 14521:2010, which lists tooth breakage) and DIN 3996 rate tooth-root strength as a shear stress, tau_F = F_tm2/(b_2H m_x) Y_eps Y_F Y_gamma Y_K, against a tabulated tau_Flim x Y_NL. BS 721 rates wheel bending through its stress factor sigma_bm. The crossed helical gear pair, which is two plain helical gears, gets no bending figure either.
evidence: MITcalc gear4 documentation quotes 'tF = Ftm2 / (b2H * mx) * Yeps * YF * Yg * YK' and 'tFG = tFlim * YNL' against DIN 3996:2019 and ISO/TS 14521:2020. RoyMech's BS 721 page gives 'M b = 0.0018 X b.2 sigma bm.2 m l f.2 d 2'. The ISO/TR 14521:2010 scope covers 'wear, pitting, worm deflection, tooth breakage and temperature'.
proposal: Rewrite the rationale to its one defensible reason: a point load on a wide tooth needs an effective-width convention. Then, in line with the owner's rule, offer that convention as an explicit, labelled feature: an ISO/TS 14521-style root shear figure for the wheel, with b_2H and Y_F read from the crate's own generated profile, off by default and named as the standard's. Leave the canary untouched.
validation: Check one worked example from ISO/TS 14521 Annex or DIN 3996. The new figure must not change any existing output unless it is enabled.

verdict.reason: Two of the three stated reasons are wrong or inconsistent with the crate. Reason 1 describes a throated wheel, but the crate's wheel is the involute helical tooth it generates: corrections.md 4.5.1 says 'nothing here throats anything', and reference.md 'Not built' lists the enveloping wheel. Reason 1 also cannot apply to a crossed helical pair, which gets no bending figure either. Reason 3 says rating standards 'rate durability, not bending, so no published bending allowable exists'. That is true of AGMA's worm practice but not of DIN 3996 / ISO/TS 14521 (tooth-root shear stress τ_F against τ_Flim·Y_NL) or BS 721 (a bending stress factor). It is also internally inconsistent: every other member's bending is checked against generic material allowables, not published gear σ_Flim. Brass C360's fatigue allowable is itself 'estimated, 0.30 × UTS' (materials_default.toml:85). Reason 2 and the effective-width argument hold: a point load on a wide tooth needs an effective-width convention that multiplies a stress. state.md:616 already states only that reason and needs no change. The decision stands on it, so no number is wrong.
verdict.evidence:
- rationale.md:888-899 read: 'A worm wheel's tooth is the envelope of the worm thread: throated ...' and 'Worm gearing's rating standards rate durability, not bending, so no published bending allowable exists'.
- rationale.md:905-909: '... which is why no standard rates it analytically either'.
- The crossed members are built as ordinary rack-cut Tooth members. BuiltMember::Rack is used for both, and shape.rs:3205-3212 skips the bending section only because the mesh is not a line contact.
- materials_default.toml:85: Brass C360 fatigue_allowable 115 MPa, basis 'estimated'.
- The standards content (DIN 3996:2019 / ISO/TS 14521:2020 tooth-root τ_F = F_tm2/(b_2H m_x)·Y_ε·Y_F·Y_γ·Y_K; BS 721 bending stress factor) could not be re-fetched: web tools hit a session limit. It matches the published scope of those standards as known, and the auditor's quoted MITcalc and RoyMech formulas.
verdict.proposal_note: The rewrite should keep reason 2 and the effective-width argument. Drop reason 1, and correct reason 3 to say that DIN 3996 / ISO/TS 14521 rate wheel root strength by a convention (b_2H, Y_F for a throated wheel) and that this project declines it. Treat the optional ISO/TS 14521-style feature with care: taking Y_F and b_2H from the crate's cylindrical profile and pairing them with the standard's τ_Flim is exactly the uncalibrated partial set that rationale.md#no-isoagma-correction-factors refuses. If offered at all, it should be the standard's method whole, labelled as assuming an enveloping wheel, with τ_Flim data the library does not have (Brass C360 is not a wheel bronze). Leave shape.rs:3205's comment, which rests on the defensible reason.

title: ZA/ZN claims overreach: the fixed-normal property fails for them, and '1-15 %' is a sampled band on a non-conjugate pairing
claim: The rationale says 'The type touches contact stress and nothing else'. The script's docstring says 'nothing at all except contact stress', and that supporting all three worm types 'would be a parameter rather than a branch'. But the whole path construction, the rack law for a shift and the backlash projection rest on n.a = sin b_b being constant over the flank. That holds only for the involute helicoid. The ZN/ZA figure pairs those worms with an involute wheel, which rationale.md:877-881 itself says is not conjugate. The 1-15 % spans only the sampled lead angles, 4.8-19.5 deg, while multi-start worms reach 25-45 deg.
evidence: zn_normal.py (the script's own surfaces, d1 7, gamma 8.21 deg): n.z along the flank, from r 2.56 to 4.44, varies by 5.2e-13 for ZI, 1.33e-2 for ZN and 1.04e-2 for ZA, about 1.3 deg of normal tilt. worm_flank_curvature.py output: ZN -0.89 % at 4.78 deg rising to -14.80 % at 19.47 deg; no case above 19.47.
proposal: State it as: ZI is the only type the model is exact for; ZA/ZN would change the path, the shift law, the play and the curvature, and would need a conjugate wheel. Present the percentage as 'a ZN worm on an involute wheel, non-conjugate, at the pitch point, over 5-20 deg of lead', or remove it. Remove 'DESIGN 5' (a document that no longer exists) from both scripts.
validation: Extend the script's compare() to lead angles of 30 and 40 deg and assert the monotone trend it claims. Add an assertion that ZI's n.z spread is below 1e-10 and ZN's above 1e-3, so the distinction is gated.

verdict.reason: The claim holds and is stronger than stated. On the fixed normal, I built an independent closed-form ZA (Archimedean) flank, with no code from the tool. n·â varies along the flank, equals sin β_b1 only at the pitch radius, and tilts 1.60° from r 2.56 to 4.44. Everything path-based rests on n·â being constant: the line of action, ε, the rack law for a shift and the backlash projection. So 'the type touches contact stress and nothing else' holds only at the pitch point. On the percentage, running the tool's own compare() beyond its sample shows '1-15 %' is just the sampled band 4.8-19.5°. The deficit keeps growing past it, and the non-conjugate ZN/involute pairing then breaks down (negative relative curvature). The band ships to users in 5 languages and in the golden output. One minor evidence error: the auditor's 'about 1.3 deg of normal tilt' is 1.6° (ZA) and about 2.0° (ZN).
verdict.evidence:
- notes/verify-crossed-worm-b/za_indep.py, closed-form ZA normal, d1 7, γ 8.21°. n·â = 0.922855 at r 2.56, 0.930054 at 3.5 (= sin β_b1 0.930054), 0.933244 at 4.44. The tool's ZI spread is 5.2e-13; ZN 1.33e-2, ZA 1.04e-2.
- worm_flank_curvature.py as shipped (exit 0, no assert): ZN −0.89 % at γ 4.78° up to −14.80 % at 19.47°, with nothing sampled above that.
- notes/verify-crossed-worm-b/zn_steep.py, the tool's compare() with z1 6, z2 40: ZN −11.1 % at 20°, −21.2 % at 25°, −37.9 % at 30°. At 35-45° the relative curvature is negative and p0 = 0 (ZA from 40°).
- The same 20° lead gives −11.1 % here against −14.8 % for the 4-start 12 mm case, so the figure is not a function of lead angle alone.
- '1–15 %' appears in strings_{en,de,pt,zh-Hans,zh-Hant}.toml (train_zn_worm_s_contact_stress_1), in gear-cli main.rs:3174/3228, in golden worm_1_40_7_90.txt:40, and at reference.md:1087 and state.md:673.
- 'DESIGN 5' appears at crossed_path.py:32 and worm_flank_curvature.py:25; docs/ has no such document.
verdict.proposal_note: Sound. Besides qualifying the band, the user-facing string should either drop the percentage or say 'at the pitch point, lead angles up to 20°'. It currently shows on every worm regardless of lead. Asserting a monotone trend at 30-40° would fail, because the pairing breaks down (negative relative curvature). Assert instead that the deficit exceeds 15 % above about 21°, or restrict the claim.

title: crossed_path.py cannot fail, derives the contact ratio from a copy of the crate's construction, and keeps the two-sided zone the crate abandoned in F83
claim: The script contains no assert and always exits 0. normal_direction, tangent_line, foot and the reach formula copy the crate's algebra, so its eps = 1.777921670 is not 'from the surfaces' as screw.rs:2195-2200 and state.md:182 say. Only checks 1, 2 and 4 read the surfaces, and check 4 only at the pitch point. Its contact_ratio uses band (t - rho, t + rho): both sides of each tangency point, the reading F83 rejected. It agrees with the crate only where neither tangency point binds. The docstring's 'Four common tangent lines ... exactly one' contradicts its own output (eight, two).
evidence: Ran it: exit 0, no assertion. two_sided.py: 9/37 at 90 deg, beta1 20, addendum 2, gives 3.161 by the script's reading against 1.829 one-sided (the crate's rule). Shipped worm with addendum 2.5: 4.285 against 4.269. It takes about 7.7 s including nix startup.
proposal: Make it a gate: assert every residual and exit non-zero on failure. Measure the zone off the surfaces: at N points s along the line, place each flank through P + s n (place_on) and check its own normal agrees with n. Read r(s) from the surface and compare with each tip. Take the one-sided zone. Add fixtures where one-sidedness binds (the 9/37 case) and where the contact is off-centre (shift, clearance). Fix the docstring. Run it in CI next to validate_dxf.py.
validation: Point the script at a deliberately broken copy (for example the two-sided rule reinstated in a worktree) and check that it fails.

verdict.reason: All sub-claims reproduce. (1) The script has 0 asserts and exits 0 ('grep -c assert' = 0; run: exit 0). (2) normal_direction, tangent_line, foot and the reach are line-for-line the crate's algebra: screw.rs contact_normal, tangent_line, foot and reach. The only surface-derived checks are 1/2 (the helicoid's own normal law) and 4, and check 4 places the flanks only at the pitch point. Check 5 (conjugacy) and check 6 (ε and its limit) use the construction alone. So screw.rs:2195-2197 ('reads the line of action off them by numerical differentiation') and state.md:182 ('reaches the line of action through differential geometry') misdescribe it. (3) contact_ratio uses band (t − ρ, t + ρ), the two-sided reading that F83 replaced (history/audit.md Phase 8: 'The zone runs one way from each tangency point now'). The script would therefore have agreed with the pre-F83 fault. (4) The docstring's 'Four common tangent lines ... exactly one' contradicts check 3's own printout: 'Eight lines ... Two are the path'. The quoted ε = 1.777921670 is held by a hard-coded constant in the Rust test, so the crate cannot drift silently from it. The independence claimed for the zone is what fails.
verdict.evidence:
- Ran nix develop -c python tools/crossed_path.py: exit 0 in about 8.5 s. Output section 3 lists 8 lines, 2 of them at 0.00000 mm.
- Two-sided (script) against one-sided (the crate's rule, screw.rs:176-184), using the script's own geometry(): 9/37 at Σ 90, β1 20, addendum 2 gives 3.16099 vs 1.82915. Shipped worm with addendum 2.5 gives 4.28526 vs 4.26851. They are identical wherever no tangency point binds, e.g. 17/23 at 45/45: 1.777921669561576 both.
- check_tangency: `pitch = np.array([g1['r'], 0, 0])` is the only point at which flank normals are taken.
verdict.proposal_note: Sound. For the surface-measured zone, use the helicoid parameter u ≥ 0 (the involute exists on one side of the base cylinder) to get one-sidedness from the surface itself, not by copying the crate's rule. Otherwise the new check shares the rule it is meant to test. Adding it to CI costs about 8 s under nix develop. flake.nix:211-216 would then describe what it gates.

title: Parametrise the screw pair by helix angles indexed by member, not by the worm's diameter and lead angle
claim: ScrewParams takes starts, wheel_teeth and worm_pitch_diameter. Screw::new then recovers gamma1 = asin(z m_n/d) and stores both helix angles and both lead angles, with worm-named fields. The shape already holds the helix: it builds d1 = z m/cos(beta1), which Screw::new turns back through asin (a round trip the test at crossed.rs:1136-1139 concedes costs rounding). Consequences: a spur FIRST member is refused as WormTooThin although the physics is symmetric; there are two errors (WormTooThin, FirstMemberIsADisc) for the one condition |beta_i| < 90 deg; and 'worm'/'wheel' vocabulary sits in the universal model. beta2 = S - beta1 is recomputed at six call sites although it is a field, and axis_2 = [0, sin S, cos S] is built in six places.
evidence: Probe 'tiny': 961 of 1600 samples were refused, partly the beta1 -> 0 end where cos(beta1) rounds to 1 and sin(gamma1) = 1 exactly. crossed.rs:1189-1196 asserts the spur-first refusal as intended. grep: 'shaft_angle_rad - self.worm_helix_angle_rad' appears at screw.rs:689, 752, 880, 1025 and 1413.
proposal: Target shape: ScrewParams { normal_module, normal_pressure_angle_rad, shaft_angle_rad, teeth: [u32; 2], helix_rad: f64 (beta1; beta2 = S - beta1), profile_shifts }. Screw stores helix: [f64; 2], pitch_diameter: [f64; 2] = z_i m_n / cos(beta_i), lead: [Option<f64>; 2] (None at beta = 0), and closed-form sliding and normal. Provide axis(i) and helix(i) accessors. The worm's diameter is converted once, at the shape level, as beta1 = acos(z1 m_n/d1), refused there when d1 <= z1 m_n. Errors reduce to NotPositive and HelixAtRightAngle(member). Migration: keep the old constructor as a thin adapter for one commit, move the callers (shape.rs screw_of, the CLI worm command), then delete it.
validation: Every existing screw test ports unchanged in meaning. New law: swapping member labels (and mirroring the shaft angle) leaves eta, eps and pmax invariant to 1e-12, including a spur member first.

verdict.evidence:
Probe probes/verify-crossed-worm-b.
- Mode tiny: {AxesAreParallel: 961 (Σ 1e-16 to 5.75e-7 deg), ok: 639}.
- Spur first: Err(WormTooThin). Mirror order: Ok, lead 144.51 mm, axial module 2.0.
- Mode f10: with_first_helix(0) at Σ 30 → Screw(WormTooThin).
- Mode f10 and sign: with_first_helix(−10) at Σ 30 → screw β1 10.0000, β2 20.0000, d2 24.4761, while the members are cut at −10 / 40 with d2 30.0244 (see missed).
verdict.proposal_note: Two changes to the law. (1) Make it direction-aware: swapping labels exchanges η_forward and η_backward, and locking thresholds likewise, so assert η_fwd(a→b) = η_bwd(swapped). (2) Add a sweep over signed β1 ∈ (−90, 90) \ {0}, asserting that the screw's helices equal helix[m.a] and helix[m.b] and that the built members' pitch radii sum to the screw's reference distance. That law fails today (see missed). AxesAreParallel (Σ = 0) should stay as an error or be documented as unreachable, since the shape routes Σ = 0 to a line contact. Five string catalogues change with the error keys.

title: No-contact policy differs by contact kind: a line contact refuses; a point contact reports eps 0, a pitch-point efficiency, a pitch-point rating and both flanks fouled
claim: Line: ContactPath::new(..).ok_or(TrainError::NoContact). Point: path None becomes 'a contact ratio of nought, said by the mesh'. The efficiency then falls back to Screw::efficiency (the pitch point), locking friction to the pitch-point form, rate() to pitch-point curvature, and flank_interference to [true, true]. So a mesh whose teeth never meet, or whose path construction failed numerically, reports an efficiency and a contact stress for a contact that does not exist. That feeds the train's flow.
evidence: Probe 'sigma0' at 1e-4 deg: eps 0 with eta 1.000000 both ways and pmax 319.94, from a pitch-point Hertz patch. Code read at the cited lines.
proposal: Pick one rule and apply it to both kinds. Either refuse (NoContact) as the line contact does, or report 'no contact' as an explicit state in which efficiency and stress are absent (Option) rather than borrowed from another model. The empty face-bounded zone from the first finding goes through the same path.
validation: Law: no mesh reports a finite efficiency or contact pressure while its contact ratio is 0. Build fixtures for both kinds.

verdict.reason: Reproduced with teeth that genuinely cannot touch, not only the near-parallel numerical failure. A 17/23 crossed pair at 90° with 2-3 mm clearance (addendum 1 each) solves and reports ε 0, a pitch-point efficiency of 84.3 % both ways, pitch-point locking thresholds, 1517 MPa contact stress and interference on both flanks. The same pair on parallel axes is refused NoContact. The worm at 3 mm clearance reports 62 % efficiency, 3376 MPa and a 'self-locking' note. There is one more wrong output: with no zone, PointContact.limited_by is set to Face (shape.rs:2767, zone.map_or(ZoneLimit::Face, ..)), though no face limited anything. The documented policy contradicts the code: corrections.md:532 says a mesh with no path of contact 'is refused now, as it is on every mesh'. The only reasoning offered for the point-contact exception is the bare assertion at shape.rs:2902-2905. The fallback efficiency also enters the flow: cut.sliding and at_rest come from BuiltMesh::efficiency at shape.rs:2486-2492.
verdict.evidence:
Probe probes/verify-crossed-worm-b, mode f11.
- Crossed 17/23 90° clearance 2: eps 0, lim Face, eta 0.843090/0.843090, lock 0.93969/0.93969 (= cos α_n·cot 45°, the pitch-point form), pmax 1517.30 = pitch, interf [true, true], only note mesh.contact_ratio_below_one. Parallel 17/23 at clearance 2: ERR NoContact.
- Worm clearance 3: eps 0, eta 0.621270/0, pmax 3376.09, notes [self_locking, contact_ratio_below_one].
- σ 1e-4° (17/43, β_add 20°, clearance 0.02): eps 0, eta 1.000000/1.000000, pmax 319.94, interf [true, true], which matches the auditor.
verdict.proposal_note: Prefer refusal (TrainError::NoContact at shape.rs:2906). It matches the line contact and corrections.md:532, and needs no boundary type change. Explicit Option fields for efficiency and pressure would ripple through MeshReport, the flow and five catalogues. Before switching, run the relief sweeps and the golden corpus: search trials call build, and a trial that had no zone was accepted before and would be refused after. The near-parallel regime (σ ≈ 1e-4°) would then refuse rather than report 100 %. That is better, but its real fix is the closed forms of crossed-worm finding 3. Fix the Face label for no zone at the same time.

title: contact_ratio and locking_friction hold different quantities on the two contact kinds, including a -1.0 sentinel, so both jump at S = 0
claim: The one MeshReport field contact_ratio is eps_gamma (transverse plus overlap) on a line contact and zone/p_bn on a point contact. locking_friction is a computed value on a point contact, where a negative number means 'friction helps', but the literal -1.0 on every line contact, meaning 'never'. A designer turning the shaft angle from 0 sees both jump, although F84 promises 'the same rows with the numbers moving'.
evidence: Probe 'sigma0', 17/43, helix 20, face 30: at S = 0, eps 4.740 and locking -1/-1; at 0.01 deg, eps 1.664 and locking -2.582/+2.581.
proposal: Use two named fields for the two measures (for example points_along_line and lines_across_face), filled for whichever kind can compute them, with the headline chosen by one documented rule. Make locking_friction a Directional<Option<f64>> (None = no threshold within the model), or compute it for line contacts with the same exact balance (contact::Contact) along the parallel path. The parallel_limit test shows that balance agrees with the first-order integral to O(mu^2).
validation: Shaft-angle sweep: every field is continuous at 0 or explicitly None on one side, and there are no sentinels (grep for Directional::of(|_| -1.0)).

verdict.reason: The numbers reproduce, but most of the claim describes a seam the project documents on purpose, and that seam is real rigid-body physics. At S = 0 the contact is a line; at any S != 0 it is a point, so the count of tooth pairs changes measure. Renaming the field does not remove that jump. The docs do not 'promise' continuity: the same reference.md paragraph that says 'the same rows with the numbers moving' then tabulates 'contact ratio | not compared | a different measure'. The next paragraph explains why a line contact's threshold is 'never'. The MeshReport field docs (train/mod.rs:216-247) say the same. What does hold is narrower. locking_friction encodes 'nothing locks this way' as any negative number: on a point contact that is a computed root, on every line contact the literal -1.0. Every consumer reads only the sign, so the magnitude of a negative value means nothing anywhere.
verdict.evidence: Probe verify-crossed-worm-c 'sigma0' (17/43, helix +20, face 30, clearance 0.02, 2 N·m). At S=0: eps 4.740205, eta 0.983896/0.983896, lock -1/-1. At +0.01 deg: eps 1.643928, eta 0.984070/0.984033, lock -2.582485/+2.581083. At -0.01 deg the signs swap (+2.581083/-2.582485). The consumers: TrainPanel.svelte:489 `v > 0 ? v.toFixed(4) : t("ui.train_locking_never")`, and the row is shown only `{#if m?.point}` (TrainPanel.svelte:1169), so the -1 is never displayed. shape.rs:2700 checks `threshold > 0.0`. gear-cli main.rs:3059 prints 'no friction locks it this way'. CrossedPath::locking_friction (screw.rs:1219) already returns Directional<Option<f64>>, and PointBuilt::locking_friction (shape.rs:2513-2522) collapses the None back into the negative pitch-point value.
verdict.corrected_claim: MeshReport::locking_friction encodes 'no friction locks the pair this way' as a sign, not as a type. A point contact carries a negative computed pitch-point root; every line contact carries a literal -1.0 (train/mod.rs:483). Every consumer (the panel, the near-locking note, the CLI) reads only whether the value is > 0. Directional<Option<f64>>, the type CrossedPath::locking_friction already returns, would state 'never' without a sentinel. The contact_ratio jump (4.740 to 1.644 at 0.01 deg) and the locking jump reproduce exactly. Both are the documented line-to-point seam of the rigid-body model, not a representational defect.
verdict.proposal_note: Do not compute a line contact's threshold with the exact balance. The docs argue that a mu near 2.5 to 5 is outside anything the model describes, and that argument is sound. It also applies to the +2.58 a 0.01 deg point contact reports now, so the consistent fix is None ('never, within the model') on both kinds, not a new number on the line. Splitting contact_ratio is optional and cosmetic. If it is done, note that the normal-plane count eps_alpha/cos^2(beta_b) can be computed on a line contact too. That field could then be filled on both kinds and be continuous at S = 0, with eps_gamma line-only.

title: A crossed mesh's efficiency is computed at the early (pre-rating) face widths, but its zone, contact ratio and locking friction at the final ones
claim: cut() computes each mesh's efficiency from early_width, which is the proportion or the box value. A member that is also on a line mesh is later widened by that mesh's rating (widths = own.resolve(max(line asks, recommended))). The point report and PointBuilt::locking_friction then use final_width. When the face clips the zone, the reported locking threshold is not the friction at which the reported efficiency reaches 0, which the code's own rule forbids.
evidence: Traced in code; not probed (it needs a member meshing both a crossed and a parallel mate with an automatic face that clips the zone).
proposal: Evaluate the zone-dependent figures once, at one width set. Either state that the efficiency is at the pre-rating width and report the zone and threshold at that width too, or iterate once: the flow is linear in the per-mesh efficiencies and the widths change only through a max.
validation: Fixture: a wheel meshing a worm and a spur gear, automatic face, narrow enough that the zone is clipped. Assert that efficiency(locking threshold) == 0.

verdict.reason: Reproduced, not just traced. cut() takes each mesh's efficiency at early_width (shape.rs:3190-3193), and the flow is written from it. The point report's zone, contact ratio and locking threshold use final_width (shape.rs:3495, 3857-3864). The two differ only for a member that is on both a point mesh and a line mesh and has an automatic face. That shape can be reached from the panel, since Edit::AddGear adds a gear meshing any gear. The mismatch is small but breaks the rule stated in the CrossedPath::locking_friction doc: a quoted threshold must be the friction at which the quoted efficiency reaches zero.
verdict.evidence: Probe verify-crossed-worm-c 'early': crossed 17/43, first member face fixed at 30 mm, second member automatic with box value b, then AddGear on member 1 on a new axis, loaded body 1 to body 3. (1) Shaft angle 90, b = 1: final widths [30, 4.300, 4.300]. The report gives eps 1.815162 (Tips), lock 1.334266/0.654922 (both at 4.30 mm), but eta 0.838351/0.828910, which is exactly the b = 1 mm figure (its zone is Face-limited, eps 0.628474, lock 1.339307/0.657879). With the face pinned at 4.30: eta 0.837926/0.828392. (2) Shaft angle 60, b = 0.5: the reported eta 0.904362 is taken along a face-clipped zone (eps 0.527), while the reported eps is 1.715619 (Tips-limited); pinned at the final width, eta is 0.903215. (3) Shaft angle 90, box 30 mm with automatic narrowing to 1.07: the reported eta 0.837926 is the full-zone figure beside a reported eps 0.675 (Face); pinned at 1.07, eta is 0.838343.
verdict.proposal_note: The first option, reporting the zone and threshold at the early width, would make the reported eps and its 'below one' note describe a face the gear is not cut to, while the stress is rated at the final width. The better fix is to evaluate the efficiency, zone and threshold at the final width and re-run the flow once when a point mesh's efficiency moved. The width reaches the efficiency only through a face clip, so this rarely triggers. Also, the flow is a linear solve for given efficiencies, but its answer is not linear in them. Iterating means re-running solve_parts' flow after rate(), which crosses the cut/rate split, so budget M rather than S. The validation fixture exists in outline in the probe above.

title: Two comments give the contact point's speed along the line of action as r_b/cos(beta_b) per radian; it is r_b cos(beta_b)
claim: Rotating an involute helicoid by d_theta is the screw motion equivalent to translating it along its axis by -(r_b/tan b_b) d_theta. Its displacement along n is then r_b cos(b_b) d_theta. Per tooth that gives 2 pi r_b cos(b_b)/z = p_bn, the pitch the code rightly divides by. The comments' r_b/cos(b_b) would give p_bt/cos(b_b), which is not p_bn.
evidence: Derivation above. The identity cos(a_t) cos(b_b) = cos(a_n) cos(b) confirms r_b cos(b_b) 2pi/z = pi m_n cos(a_n) = normal_base_pitch().
proposal: Correct both comments to r_b cos(beta_b) and say once that p_bn = 2 pi r_b cos(beta_b)/z is the tooth-to-tooth spacing along the line.
validation: None needed beyond the existing contact-ratio tests. Optionally assert p_bn == 2 pi r_b cos(b_b)/z for both members.

verdict.reason: Both comments say the contact point advances at r_b/cos(beta_b) per radian. The true rate is r_b cos(beta_b). The code's arithmetic divides by p_bn = pi m_n cos(alpha_n) = 2 pi r_b cos(beta_b)/z, which is right, so only the comments are wrong. reference.md:295 states it correctly: 'a flank advances along the common normal by one normal base pitch per tooth'. The conclusion at screw.rs:1168 (uniform in s is uniform in time) still holds.
verdict.evidence: screw.rs:619-620 reads 'the contact point advances along this line at `r_b/cos β_b` per radian of its member's rotation'. screw.rs:1168-1169 reads 'advances along the path at a constant rate, `r_b/cos β_b` per radian'. I checked this independently in notes/verify-crossed-worm-c/pitch.py, which parametrises an involute helicoid (m_n 1, alpha_n 20, beta 20, z 17), rotates it by 1e-4 rad and solves for where it meets the fixed line along its normal. It advances 7.98739 per radian; r_b cos(beta_b) = 7.98739 and r_b/cos(beta_b) = 8.90748. Per tooth, 2 pi r_b cos(beta_b)/z = 2.95213 = p_bn exactly, against 3.29220 from the comments' rate.

title: Stale, misplaced and self-historical comments in the crossed code and its tools
claim:
Examples:
- screw.rs:6-7: 'the worm stage and a crossed-axis spur stage will both use it' (future tense; stages are retired).
- :549-551: 'DESIGN docs/reference.md'.
- :573-575: 'the ... audit identified as the one thing gating five ... gaps'.
- :622-630: 'What it does not yet bound: the face width ... is the next step', and :1257 'Reported rather than applied'. limited_by_face and face_widths_for exist.
- :2121-2123: an orphan doc for efficiency_rises_with_the_lead_angle is glued onto the_path_of_contact_passes_through..., whose doc says 'four lines'.
- :2183-2194: the doc of the_contact_ratio_approaches_... is merged into the_construction_reproduces_the_surfaces_derivation.
- contact.rs:633-635: 'arrives ... (milestone 7, step 5)'.
- contact.rs:675-678: the 'Three-component vector helpers' doc is attached to struct Contact.
- crossed.rs:80 cites 'the appendix'.
- Both Python tools cite 'DESIGN 5'.
- Many test docs narrate history ('used to', 'an earlier draft', 'the old worm entry point').

validation: tools/check_doc_links.py is still green. A grep for 'will both use it|milestone|DESIGN 5|not yet bound|four lines' is empty.

Is exactly one of them the line of action?') contradicts that script's own check at line 185-186 ('Eight lines ... Two are the path'), and it is the script corrections.md:367 credits with finding the eight. The test doc at screw.rs:2124-2130 likewise says 'the four lines'. contact.rs:633-635 promised the crossed version would 'build a different axis_2 for the same function'. That did not happen: production crossed code slips through Contact::slip, and contact::sliding_velocity has no production caller.
verdict.evidence: screw.rs:6-7 is in the future tense. screw.rs:549-551 reads 'and DESIGN docs/reference.md#crossed-axes says why'. screw.rs:573-575 reads 'the construction that the docs/reference.md#crossed-axes audit identified'. screw.rs:622-630 says 'using it to *bound* the zone is the next step', yet limited_by_face (screw.rs:922) and face_widths_for (screw.rs:974) exist. screw.rs:1256 says 'Reported rather than applied'. At screw.rs:2121-2123 the orphan efficiency doc sits above the_path_of_contact_passes_through..., whose doc says 'four lines'. The_contact_ratio doc is merged into the_construction_reproduces_the_surfaces_derivation, and the_contact_ratio_approaches_... at screw.rs:2235 has no doc. contact.rs:675-678 shows the helper doc rendering as the first paragraph of struct Contact. crossed.rs:80 cites 'the appendix', which is in docs/history/design-record.md. Both tools say 'DESIGN 5'. Grep finds 'used to' or 'earlier draft' about 20 times across screw.rs, crossed.rs and contact.rs.
verdict.proposal_note: Some of the history is the only statement of what a test guards, for example screw.rs:2204-2206 ('that the two were once quoted as one figure is why this test exists'). Rewrite those as the present-tense guard instead of deleting them. Also note that crossed.rs:76-81's claim ('A worm's length and a wheel's face width enter no stress in this crate ... bit-identical peak pressure') is false as well as stale. The probe for finding 13 gives pmax 2974.9 MPa at a 1 mm face against 2540.0 at 4.3 mm. That is covered by the auditor's separate face-width/stress finding, so fix both together.

title: Note thresholds for near-locking (0.8 x threshold) and low efficiency (eta < 0.5) are unnamed literals, and the second fires forward-only on point contacts
claim: 'static_friction > 0.8 * threshold' and 'efficiency.forward < 0.5' decide which warnings a designer sees. They are not named, documented or user-visible. The low-efficiency note is asked forward only, and only of crossed meshes, and its English embeds a rule of thumb: 'which usually limits a crossed-axis stage before stress does'.
evidence: grep finds neither number in docs/.
proposal: Name both as constants with a sentence of justification in reference.md, or better, as margins stated in the note (report the ratio static_mu/threshold and let the reader judge). Ask the efficiency note in both directions and for every mesh kind.
validation: check_strings stays green. A unit test fires each note at the named boundary.

verdict.reason: Both triggers are unnamed literals and appear nowhere in docs/. The low-efficiency note is asked forward only, and only on point contacts. In a train, a mesh's 'forward' is its member order, not the direction a case drives it, which contradicts the project's own 'a mechanism has no forward' rule (rationale.md#direction-is-the-readers-not-the-mechanisms). The probe also shows two effects the auditor did not: mirror-image pairs get different notes, and the note co-fires with the locking note.
verdict.evidence: shape.rs:2700 is `static_friction > 0.8 * threshold` and shape.rs:2709 is `m.efficiency.forward < 0.5`; grep finds neither factor in reference.md, rationale.md or state.md. Probe verify-crossed-worm-c 'notes' (17/23 at 90 deg): with the first helix at 9 deg, eta is 0.0000/0.6412 and the notes are forward_locking plus low_efficiency 'percent 0.0'. That sentence reads '0.0 %: most of the input becomes heat' on a pair that cannot be driven at all. The mirror pair at 81 deg gives eta 0.6412/0.0000 and only self_locking. strings_en.toml:142 embeds the rule of thumb 'which usually limits a crossed-axis stage before stress does', which also uses the retired 'stage' vocabulary.
verdict.proposal_note: Asking the note backward on every mesh would add noise to every worm, whose backward efficiency is routinely low or locked and already has its locking note. Ask it in the direction(s) the enabled load cases actually drive the mesh (c.directions[k]), and not in a direction already reported as locked. Name the 0.8 as a constant with one sentence in reference.md. The note already carries both mu and the threshold, so the reader can judge the margin.

title: Duplicated computations inside screw.rs and the point rating
claim:
- enum Flank {Driving, BackDriving} is a 1:1 relabelling of Drive, matched twice.
- flank_curvature re-derives alpha_t with its own atan instead of plane::transverse_pressure_angle, and returns beta_b, which the caller discards (let _ = (beta_b_1, beta_b_2)).
- rulings() builds the pitch normal a second time, with the opposite sign convention from contact_normal().
- patch_at calls line_pressure and elliptical_contact, then hertz::peak_pressure, which calls both again.
- axial_rate recomputes sin(b_b) from beta where |n.a_i| is already at hand.
- normal_module() recovers m_n from m_x cos(gamma) instead of storing it.
evidence: Read at the cited lines.
proposal: Delete Flank and use Drive. Have one fn normal(flank) that is the single source for the rulings and the path. Give hertz a function that returns the governing patch (pressure, length, width, which model). Read sin(b_b) as |n.a_i|. Store m_n.
validation: All existing tests pass unchanged, and the golden corpus is byte-identical.

verdict.reason: Every item holds when read at its line, with one correction. rulings() builds the other flank's normal, not the negative of contact_normal(): the y and z components are negated and x is kept. The skew is the same either way. The duplication is still real, and rulings' version is the closed form. contact_normal gets the same vector through the base helix angles, a square root and a division by sin(Sigma), which is the near-parallel weakness another finding reports. normal_module() recovering m_n as m_x cos(gamma) is harmless (rounding only) and the least worth changing.
verdict.evidence: Flank {Driving, BackDriving} (screw.rs:1345) is a private relabel of Drive: it is mapped from Drive at screw.rs:332-335 and 521-524 and matched at 472-475. flank_curvature (screw.rs:1471) computes `(alpha_n.tan() / cos_beta).atan()`, which is plane::transverse_pressure_angle verbatim (plane.rs:40-41). Its beta_b result is discarded at screw.rs:1416 (`let _ = (beta_b_1, beta_b_2);`). rulings' n_hat is [sin a, cos a cos b1, -cos a sin b1]. contact_normal reduces symbolically to [sin a, -cos a cos b1, cos a sin b1], using sin(beta_b) = sin(beta) cos(alpha_n) and beta2 = Sigma - beta1. patch_at (shape.rs:2568-2572) calls line_pressure and elliptical_contact, then peak_pressure (hertz.rs:274-305), which calls both again and makes the same line-or-ellipse choice a second time. axial_rate (screw.rs:1021-1028) recomputes sin(beta_b) from beta, while axial_travel in the same impl (screw.rs:1259-1270) uses n·a_i for the same quantity, and member_base(i).1 is a third source.
verdict.proposal_note: The validation should not require a byte-identical golden corpus for the axial_rate and normal replacements. They change rounding in quantities the corpus prints to 9 digits (contact ratios), so review any check_golden diff for size instead. Make the single normal(flank) the closed form. That removes contact_normal's sqrt and sin(Sigma) division as well as the duplication.

title: Tolerances chosen by feel in the crossed construction, and a fixed quadrature count
claim:
- mesh_branch accepts a residual below 1e-6 x max(a, 1). The finding on the shaft angle going to 0 shows this is what fails first.
- solve3 refuses |det| < 1e-12 in absolute terms.
- least_distance_lead_angle has an exact-90-deg branch at |S - 90| < 1e-12, and 1e-9 bracket insets.
- PATH_SAMPLES = 2048 is a trapezium count justified by a convergence test at two fixtures. The locking Brent multiplies it by every iteration.
evidence: Constants read at the cited lines. branch_offset.py shows the 1e-6 criterion binding at 3e-4 deg.
proposal: The closed-form line removes the first two. For the quadrature, either use Gauss-Legendre on the smooth integrand with an a-posteriori error estimate, or an adaptive rule to a stated tolerance, so the count follows from a tolerance rather than a number. The 90-deg branch can go: Brent at 90 agrees with (z1/z2)^(1/3) to its tolerance.
validation: Keep the_path_average_has_converged as a law on the chosen rule (error below tolerance). Run the typing-speed test.

verdict.reason: Every literal cited is where the finding says it is, and my own probe of the crate backs up each point. (1) The 1e-6·max(a,1) branch test in mesh_branch (screw.rs:856) is what fails first as Σ→0. It fails intermittently rather than at a clean threshold, which is worse than the finding says: the conditioning noise rises roughly like 1/sin Σ and crosses the fixed bar back and forth. (2) The trapezium count of 2048 is far more work than needed. Gauss-Legendre with 8 nodes reaches the 400k-sample reference to 1e-14 on every fixture I tried (both drive directions, four pairs). Trapezium at 2048 gets only ~3e-10, and each locking-friction Brent costs 1.36 ms. (3) The exact-90° branch in least_distance_lead_angle (screw.rs:437) is redundant. Brent 2e-12 away from 90° differs from the closed form by exactly slope×offset (7.2e-13 = 0.36×2e-12), so dropping the branch changes nothing a user could see. One narrower point: solve3's |det|<1e-12 is not a units error, because its rows are unit vectors (u1, u2, n) and the determinant is dimensionless and bounded by 1. It is still a threshold picked by hand.
verdict.evidence:
Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-crossed-worm-1 (release build):
- 17/43 pair with β_add = 20°: path_of_contact is Some at Σ = 1e-3°, None at 5e-4°, Some again at 3e-4°, then None at 1e-4, 1e-5 and 1e-6°. Screw::new returns AxesAreParallel at 1e-7° and 1e-9°.
- Error against a 400k-sample trapezium reference (μ = 0.06): z17/23 Forward trap2048 3.1e-10, trap256 2.0e-8, GL4 4.4e-11, GL8 6.2e-15; z1/40 Backward trap2048 5.2e-10, GL8 2.0e-14; z4/60 Forward GL8 2.0e-15. Timing: efficiency(2048) 79 µs, locking_friction(2048) 1.36 ms.
- least_distance_lead_angle(1, 40, 90° ± d) against atan((1/40)^(1/3)): d ≤ 5e-13 gives 0 (branch taken); d = 2e-12 gives ∓7.19e-13; d = 1e-10 gives ∓3.60e-11. Linear in d, so there is no jump at the branch edge.
- screw.rs:1329 solve3 takes rows [u1, u2, n], all unit vectors (tangent_line, screw.rs:1287-1295).
verdict.proposal_note: Replace the fixed trapezium with a fixed low-order Gauss-Legendre rule (8–16 nodes). The integrand is smooth and analytic on the zone, and GL8 already sits at round-off. That also retires SEARCH_SAMPLES = 256 (auto.rs:1597) and its 'an eighth of the points buys that sixty-four times over' argument: one rule then serves the rating and the search, and each locking Brent is ~250× cheaper. Keep the_path_average_has_converged, but restate it as a law on the new rule (GL n against GL 2n, both below a stated tolerance). Also fix the doc pointers: PATH_SAMPLES (shape.rs:2645) and SEARCH_SAMPLES (auto.rs:1591) both send the reader to `train::crossed` for the convergence test, but the test lives in screw.rs's tests. For mesh_branch and solve3, the closed-form line from the sibling finding (index 3) is the right fix. A wider tolerance only moves the noisy band.

title: English error text in gear-core uses retired 'stage' words, and the catalogue copy has drifted from it
claim: TrainError's Display writes 'parallel axes: a worm stage needs crossed shafts, and a parallel pair is a spur stage'. The catalogue says 'a worm stage needs non-parallel shafts'. That is two texts for one key, both with vocabulary the graph refactor retired, and English inside gear-core against rule 2. The probe hit this message for a nonzero shaft angle of 1e-9 deg.
evidence: Probe 'sigma0' output, and the lines cited.
proposal: Delete the English Display text for Screw errors (or all of TrainError) in favour of the Note key and its catalogue entry. Reword the catalogue entry without 'stage'. Once the closed forms remove AxesAreParallel, delete the key entirely.
validation: check_strings stays green, and the gear_io strings test fires every remaining screw error.

verdict.reason: The drift and the retired vocabulary are real. The claim that Display breaks rule 2 is a documented exception: docs/rationale.md:59-61 says 'Their Display impls remain, for the CLI and for Debug; what changed is which of the two the browser sees.' That exception still deserves questioning on its merits. The CLI already builds the English catalogue (gear-cli/src/main.rs:281, words() → Catalogue::english()), so a second English text in gear-core is a second copy that can and did drift. The drift is also worse than the finding says. The four translations (de, pt, zh-Hans, zh-Hant) translate the *Display* sentence ('...crossed shafts, and a parallel pair is a spur stage'), while strings_en.toml:197 is the shorter 'a worm stage needs non-parallel shafts'. So English and the other four languages say different things for one key. strings_en.toml:142 (low_efficiency) also still says 'crossed-axis stage'.
verdict.evidence: Probe prints TrainError::Screw(AxesAreParallel) Display: 'parallel axes: a worm stage needs crossed shafts, and a parallel pair is a spur stage' (train/mod.rs:1740-1743). strings_en.toml:197: screw_axes_are_parallel = "a worm stage needs non-parallel shafts". strings_de.toml:109: "parallele Achsen: eine Schneckenstufe braucht gekreuzte Wellen, ein paralleles Paar ist eine Stirnradstufe" (this matches Display, not en). pt:110 and zh-Hans/zh-Hant:105 also match Display. Screw::new returns AxesAreParallel at Σ = 1e-7° and 1e-9° (probe), so the message is reachable at a nonzero angle.
