Six scenarios, smallest input first:
1. Out of range: Train::alone(&arr::pair([17,43]), 2.0, 3000.0), then load_cases[1].duty = Intermittent{360°, at: 3 or 99, 10 actuations}, then solve_train.
2. Held body: the same pair with at: 0 (ground).
3. Hold edit: Train::alone(planetary(12,30,72,3)) with its default duty (25° × 1000 at the carrier, body 2). Then t.edit(Edit::Hold(2)), t.edit(Edit::Release(3)), and a declared Reacted load at 3.
4. Remove edit: Train::chained([pair(17,43), pair(20,40)]) with the duty at body 3. Then t.edit(Edit::Remove(Piece::Member(3))).
5. Document: to_toml of scenario 1's train with "at = 2" changed to "at = 99" in the duty table, then gear_io::train::from_toml, then solve_train.
6. Still port: a planetary with the ring released. Loads are the sun given at n rpm, the ring given at 0 rpm (torque automatic), and the carrier derived. The duty is 360° × 10 at the ring, and I ran it at n = 3000, 300 and 30.
repro.observed:
All four parts of the claim reproduce, and the verdict's extra route (drop_orphans) does too.

(1) Out of range panics. at=3 panics with "index out of bounds: the len is 3 but the index is 3" at crates/gear-core/src/train/mod.rs:4527:36. at=99 panics the same way. Nothing refuses the port: load entries are checked against the open ports as TrainError::LoadPort (mod.rs:4346), but `speeds[port]` is indexed unchecked. A panic in the wasm build is a trap. I inferred that and did not execute it.

(2) Document route (new evidence). from_toml accepted the file with the duty at 99 (duty read back as Intermittent{at: 99}) and the solve then panicked at mod.rs:4527. So one hand-edited or corrupted file crashes the solve, and with it the app.

(3) Held or ground body gives silent zeros. With at=0 the case reports solved=true, notes=[], and cycles {0,0} on both gears. With at=2 it gives 26 and 10. Those are correct: the output makes 10 turns, and 10·43/17 = 25.3 rounds up to 26 on the pinion.

(4) The panel's Hold edit leaves the duty behind. After Edit::Hold(2) the duty is still Intermittent{at: 2}. The case solves with notes=[], and all three members report 0/0 cycles while they turn at 3000, −1200 and −500 rpm. Before the edit they reported 1250, 167 and 209.

(5) The panel's Remove edit grounds the duty. Removing member 3 returns Ok, and drop_orphans (conditions.rs:349-352) rewrites the duty to at: 0. Both remaining gears then report 0/0 cycles with no note, where they reported 352 and 139 before. set_duty (conditions.rs:1152-1157) is another route: it seeds at=GROUND for a case with no loads.

(6) A still sweep port gives a count that depends on rpm. With a 360° × 10 sweep at the ring, the sun reports 77,118 cycles at 3000 rpm, 7,689 at 300 and 746 at 30. The same sweep at the carrier gives 180, 181 and 180. I derived the count by hand from the `unit` fallback (mod.rs:4413-4438, 4527). unit[sun] = n and unit[ring] = 1, because a speed of 0 is weighted ±1. unit[carrier] = n/7 + 6/7. The sun's turns against the carrier are therefore (6/7)(n−1)·10 per sweep, and with 3 planet contacts the count is 30·(6/7)(n−1). That gives 77,117.1 → 77,118 at 3000, 7,688.6 → 7,689 at 300, and 745.7 → 746 at 30, matching the output exactly. The answer adds an rpm to a unit weight of ±1, so it has no physical meaning. The correct answer is that the case says so: the ring does not turn, so a sweep measured there is undefined.

Severity: I re-judge this as medium rather than high. The rating takes no life factor from the cycle count. A pair with 2.5e8 counted cycles and the same pair with 0 give identical min_face_width (bending 0.8953, contact 8.483) and identical stresses. So the silent zeros and the rpm-scaled counts corrupt a figure that is reported but does not feed the verdict. They are not unconservative. That figure is still what a designer would compare against S-N data, and ordinary panel edits (Hold, Remove) reach it with no note.

The panic is the most serious part. It needs a document or wasm JSON naming a body that does not exist, which the panel's own edits did not produce: drop_orphans grounds the duty rather than leaving it out of range. from_toml does accept such a document, though, so a hand-edited file crashes the solve.
repro.note:
The ledger's proposal is right, with these additions.
- Validate the duty port wherever load ports are validated in solve_train. Refuse a port that is not an open port of the train as TrainError::LoadPort or a new DutyPort, and make from_toml and the wasm entry points run the same check.
- When speeds[port] == 0, emit a case note and give no cycles (cycles: None). Remove the `unit` fallback for cycle counting: its entries mix rpm with ±1.
- Train::hold should move a duty at the held body to the case's reacted port, using the rule set_duty already applies.
- drop_orphans, and set_duty on a case with no loads, should not silently write GROUND. Either refuse the edit or leave a state the solve reports.

A law that would catch all of this: for every preset and every body b (and b = 0, and b = max+1), a fatigue case with its duty at b either refuses, or carries the note, or counts non-zero cycles on every loaded member, and never panics. Also, after any Hold or Remove edit, every fatigue case either counts cycles or says why not.

One side observation: `gear-cli trainfile [path]` treats path as an output and overwrites it. Its "[path]" help reads like an input, which is how I overwrote my own notes file. That is a small usability point.

title: Reversal rule: 'more than one mesh' flags a pinion driving two gears, and under a reversing duty a planet's or idler's contact count is wrongly halved
claim: always_reverses(i) = meshes_of[i].len() > 1. The Reversal doc says 'a planet always does'. A gear driving two mates loads the same flank in both meshes and is not reversed, yet it gets the note, and with the switch on its fatigue bending allowable is cut to 0.7×. A planet or idler, by contrast, has its two flanks loaded by its two mates on every turn. Under a reversing duty each flank still sees one engagement per turn, but loaded_cycles halves contact for every member.
evidence: Probe `split` (pinion 20 meshing 40 and 50, non-reversing duty): member 0 carries gear.reversed_bending_uncorrected. Probe `planet rev=true` (12/30/72, 3 planets): planet cycles bending 30, contact 15. By flank bookkeeping (forward: flank A from the sun, B from the ring; back: B from the sun, A from the ring) contact should be 30.
proposal: Derive reversal per member per case from the flow. A member's root reverses when the torques its meshes put on it (on_members per mesh, already computed at mod.rs:4561) have opposite signs, or when the duty reverses. Where the member's own meshes already load both flanks (opposite signs), do not halve contact on a reversing duty. Pass a per-member flag in CaseLoad instead of the structural guess.
validation: Tests: the split-drive pinion reports no reversal note; a line(20,31,20) idler and every planet do; under a reversing duty the planet's contact equals its bending count, while a sun's is half. Hand-count flank engagements on the three presets.

verdict.reason: Holds on both counts. `always_reverses = meshes_of[i].len() > 1` (shape.rs:3373) is a structural stand-in for 'a planet or an idler'. A pinion that drives two gears loads the same flank in both meshes: same rotation, driver in both. Yet it gets gear.reversed_bending_uncorrected, and with the switch on it is judged against the 0.7× allowable. The reversing-duty branch of loaded_cycles halves contact for every member. For a member whose two meshes already load opposite flanks (a planet or idler), each flank sees one engagement per turn whichever way it runs, so contact should equal bending.
verdict.evidence: `split` (pinion 20 meshing 40 and 50, non-reversing duty): member 0 carries gear.reversed_bending_uncorrected, though both of its meshes are driven from it. `planetrev` (12/30/72, sweep at the carrier, 360°×10): with a non-reversing duty the planet (member 1) shows bending 24, contact 24, which is correct (72/30·10, paths_seen 1 for a replicated planet). With a reversing duty it shows bending 30, contact 15. Flank count: forward, flank A from the sun and B from the ring; back, B from the sun and A from the ring. Each flank therefore sees every turn, 30 under the per-actuation ceil, not 15. The sun's halving to 90 of 180 is correct.
verdict.proposal_note: Deriving reversal from the signs of the torques the member's meshes put on it (per mesh, per case) is the right generalisation: it covers idlers, planets and split drives with one rule. Carry a per-member, per-case 'both flanks loaded' flag. Contact halves only when the duty reverses and that flag is false. Also update the Reversal doc (mod.rs:2590 'A planet always does'), which should state the flank rule rather than the planet.

title: A statically indeterminate train (twin idlers) is refused, but its path is still reported with efficiency 0 (reads as self-locking) and backlash 0
claim: paths_of's `flowing` maps any flow refusal to (0.0, 0.0), and `coefficient` maps a non-unique play to 0. So a path whose flow is Undetermined gets efficiency 0 both ways, which Directional::locked (<= 0) reads as self-locking, and backlash 0,0,0. Every case of the train is refused as TRAIN_LOAD_SHARED, and that note advises 'hold one end only', which does not apply when the indeterminacy is two internal paths between one input and one output.
evidence: Probe `twin`: pinion 20 driving gear 40 through two 25-tooth idlers in parallel. Both cases solved=false, note train.load_shared. The path 1->2 is still reported: ratio 2, efficiency {0,0}, circulation {0,0}, backlash all 0.
proposal: Make paths_of return Option per figure. A refused flow gives efficiency None (or omits the path with a note), never 0, so that 0 keeps one meaning (locked). Do the same for play when System::play is not unique. Give Undetermined-with-one-reaction its own key (e.g. train.paths_parallel, 'the load divides between parallel paths in proportion to stiffness'), separate from load_shared. List twin-path (dual-countershaft) trains in docs/state.md as unsupported, or share equally where paths are symmetric, as replicated planets already do.
validation: Law: a path's efficiency is 0 only when Directional::locked agrees with a flow that solved and a mesh that locks; brute-force over presets plus the twin fixture. Strings law for the new key.

verdict.reason: Holds. `flowing` maps any flow refusal to (0.0, 0.0) (mod.rs:3426) and `coefficient` maps a non-unique play to 0 (mod.rs:3465). Directional::locked is `<= 0`, and the panel's lockedWays mirrors it (TrainPanel.svelte:475-480). A twin-idler train therefore shows 'turns neither way' and play 0,0,0. Its case note, train.load_shared, reads 'held at both ends … hold one end only', although only one end is held. I lowered severity to medium: the cases themselves are refused, and the configuration is outside the model's stated boundary. The defect is that the path row gives false figures where it should say it is unknown.
verdict.evidence: Re-ran `twin` (pinion 20 to gear 40 through two parallel 25-tooth idlers; held []; case loads: body 1 given, body 2 reacted). Both cases solved=false with note train.load_shared. Yet the path 1->2 is reported: ratio 2, eff {0,0}, circ {0,0}, backlash all 0. strings_en.toml:155: load_shared = "held at both ends: … hold one end only, or let a self-locking mesh hold it".
verdict.proposal_note: Make a path's figures Option, or drop the path with a note, so that 0% keeps the single meaning 'locks'. A separate key for 'the load divides between parallel paths inside the train' is right. Splitting equally by symmetry would be a hidden rule of thumb unless it is exposed as a user-visible option, which is the project's stated rule. Documenting it as unsupported is the minimal fix.

title: Duplicate entries at one body are accepted: two given speeds at the same port are summed (6000 rpm from two 3000s)
claim: solve_parts refuses entries at non-ports but not two entries at one body. Each given speed drives its body with the 'other' given ports grounded, and here the other is the same body, so each contributes a full motion and the speeds add. For torques, the last entry silently wins.
evidence: Probe `dup`: pair with loads [given(1,2,3000), given(1,2,3000), Reacted(2)] gives solved=true, body 1 speed 6000, body 2 speed -2372.09 (= -6000/2.529). An earlier-session probe (load and reacted at the same body) gives case_nothing_drives.
proposal: Refuse a case with two entries at one body, next to the LoadPort check (TrainError::LoadPort or a new DuplicateEntry { case, body }), or merge them on load in gear-io. The panel's edits never produce this; a TOML file or wasm JSON can.
validation: Negative fixture in the TOML reader and a unit test on solve_train.

verdict.reason: Reproduced independently. solve_parts (mod.rs:4345) refuses entries only at non-ports. Nothing in solve_parts, gear-io/src/train.rs or conditions.rs refuses two entries at one body. In the driver loop (mod.rs:4426-4449) each duplicate grounds 'the others', which is its own body, then drives itself at one turn, so each duplicate adds a full motion. For torques, the known[g] assignment (mod.rs:4475-4484) lets the last entry win. relieve_case happens to hide the speed case by turning the second speed derived, but solve_train does not run relief, so a TOML file or wasm JSON solved directly gives the wrong answer.
verdict.evidence: Probe verify-train-mod-b-2 on pair [17,43]. [given(1,2,3000), given(1,2,3000), Reacted(2)] gives solved=true, body1 speed 6000, body2 -2372.09, no note. [given(1,2,3000), Load{at 1, torque fixed 5, speed auto}, Reacted(2)] gives body1 torque 5: the last entry wins silently. [given(1), Reacted(2), Free(2)] is accepted, Reacted wins. After relieve_case, the duplicate's speed turns auto and the solve reads 3000. grep for duplicate/twice in gear-io/src/train.rs and conditions.rs finds no guard.
verdict.proposal_note: Refusing in the core, next to the LoadPort check, is the better of the two proposals: it covers the wasm path as well as the reader. Add TrainError::DuplicateEntry { case, body } (or reuse LoadPort), plus a catalogue key if it crosses. Merging in gear-io alone would leave wasm JSON unguarded.

title: Over-given speeds are reported as 'short by 4294967295 speeds'
claim: When more speeds are given than the mobility, driving one with the others grounded is inconsistent, so determined = false and `short` is usize::MAX. The note TRAIN_CASE_UNDERDETERMINED then renders 'motion undecided: 4294967295 more speed(s) to give'. The case actually has too many speeds, not too few.
evidence: Probe `overspeed`: pair, load 1 given 3000 rpm and load 2 speed given -1000 gives note {key: train.case_underdetermined, short: 4294967295}.
proposal: Tell the two apart: count given speeds against case_mobility(); if it is over, emit a new key train.case_overdetermined { over }, and keep underdetermined for short > 0. Never format usize::MAX.
validation: Unit tests for both notes; strings law for the new key.

verdict.reason: Confirmed, and wider than stated. On a pair with both ends' speeds given, `short` falls back to usize::MAX, which is clamped to u32::MAX and formatted as 4294967295. This happens even when the two speeds agree exactly with the ratio: a consistent over-specification is refused and worded as too few speeds. On a differential (planetary with the ring released, m=2), three given speeds give determined=false while short=0, because driving all three ports at one turn is a consistent rigid rotation. The note then reads 'motion undecided: 0 more speed(s) to give'. Both messages are wrong, and the catalogue text ('... or one fewer port to leave free') does not fit an over-given case either.
verdict.evidence: Probe: pair, given(1, 3000) plus speed fixed -1000 at 2 gives {key: train.case_underdetermined, short: "4294967295"}. Pair with 4300 and -1700 (-4300·17/43, exactly consistent) gives the same note. Planetary(12,30,72,3) after release(3) (held [], mobility 2), with speeds given at 1, 2 and 3, gives {short: "0"}. Code: mod.rs:4453-4462, `.map_or(usize::MAX, ...)` and `u32::try_from(short).unwrap_or(u32::MAX)`. strings_en.toml:153.
verdict.proposal_note: Count given speeds against case_mobility() and emit case_overdetermined { over = given - m } when it is over. Keep case_underdetermined only for short > 0 with every given speed individually determined. The test should include the differential's short=0 path and the consistent-ratio pair.

title: Docs say an unmentioned chain end is reacted; the code treats every unmentioned port as free
claim: LoadCase::loads says 'The chain's two ends, where the case does not load them, are *reacted*'. LoadRole says 'the chain's two ends are reacted, every other open port is free'. The code reacts only ports declared Reacted (mod.rs:4360-4364), which is what solve_train's own doc says ('a port it does not mention is free').
evidence: Code at mod.rs:4360: `filter(|&s| declared(s, LoadRole::Reacted))`. Probe `freeport` (declared=false): a case with only a load at 1 on a pair is not reacted at 2.
proposal: Rewrite both doc comments to 'a port the case does not mention is free; a reaction is declared', and delete the 'chain's two ends' default.
validation: check_doc_links still passes; a unit test that an unmentioned end reports BodyRole::Free.

verdict.reason: The code reacts only declared Reacted ports (mod.rs:4360-4364), and solve_train's doc (mod.rs:4146) says an unmentioned port is free. LoadCase::loads (mod.rs:2819-2826) and LoadRole (mod.rs:2839-2841) still describe a 'chain's two ends are reacted' default that no code implements. The same contradiction sits inside a single paragraph of docs/reference.md: line 2737 says 'A port the case does not mention is free.', while lines 2747-2753 say 'The two ends it does not load are **reacted** ... Every other open port the case does not load is **free**'. It is doc-only (the code is self-consistent and fresh cases write Reacted explicitly), so low rather than medium.
verdict.evidence: Probe: pair with only given(1, 0.1, 3000) reports body 2 as BodyRole::Free and the note train.load_not_reacted, so it is not reacted. grep shows no code that supplies a default Reacted. gear-io strings.rs:1167/1417 and fresh cases write Load::declared(end, Reacted) explicitly. docs/reference.md:2737 against 2747-2753.
verdict.proposal_note: Also fix docs/reference.md:2747-2753, which the finding missed: delete the 'two ends it does not load are reacted' sentences and keep 'A port the case does not mention is free' once.

title: A free port declared in so many words counts differently in relief from an unmentioned (default) free port
claim: LoadRole's doc says an entry may 'say the default in so many words'. But relieve_case_toggles counts declared Free entries in `reacted` (!is_load) and unmentioned free ports not at all. The same physical case therefore keeps or loses its given torque depending on whether the free port is written.
evidence: Probe `freeport`: pair with load 1 (torque 0.1 given) and output unmentioned: relief turns the given torque automatic, and the solve says case_nothing_drives. With Free(2) declared, the torque stays given and the solve says load_not_reacted (the lock question).
proposal: Pick one meaning. Either state that a declared Free is the lock question and not the default (fix LoadRole's doc), or count torques as loads + reacted − m everywhere and ask the lock question by the case's shape (a given torque with no reaction), independent of how the free port is written.
validation: Law: relief and solve are invariant under adding or removing Load::declared(p, Free) for any unmentioned open port p.

verdict.reason: The behavioural difference is real, but it is deliberate and documented where it is decided. relieve_case_toggles' comment (mod.rs:3690-3697) and docs/reference.md:2764-2765 both say a declared free port counts as the reaction it declines to be, so that a given torque beside it stands and the lock question is asked on purpose. The argument holds: counting unmentioned ports as reactions would raise relief's torque limit on every multi-port train and weaken it. solve_train itself treats declared and unmentioned free identically: before relief both give load_not_reacted. What is actually wrong is LoadRole's doc (mod.rs:2839-2842), which says an entry may 'say the default in so many words', implying a declared Free is equivalent to silence. It is not. A secondary, real consequence: an unmentioned end silently turns the designer's given torque derived, and the case then reports case_nothing_drives rather than the more informative load_not_reacted.
verdict.evidence: Probe: pair, given(1, 0.1, 3000), nothing at 2. Before relief the note is load_not_reacted. After relieve_case the torque is auto=true and the note is case_nothing_drives. With Free(2) declared, the torque stays given and the note stays load_not_reacted. Code: mod.rs:3698-3699, `reacted = c.loads.iter().filter(|l| !l.is_load()).count()`.
verdict.corrected_claim: LoadRole's doc says a declared Free restates the default, but relief deliberately (mod.rs:3690-3697, reference.md:2764) counts a declared Free as a reaction and ignores an unmentioned free port. So the doc is wrong, not the rule. As a side effect, an unmentioned free end lets relief turn the only given torque derived, and the case then reports nothing_drives instead of load_not_reacted.
verdict.proposal_note: Take the proposal's first option: rewrite LoadRole's doc to say a declared Free is the lock question, not the default. Do not adopt the invariance law, which contradicts a sound deliberate rule. Optionally, stop relief from turning the last given torque derived when no reaction is declared at all, so that the solve asks the lock question rather than saying nothing drives.

title: Seed rounding to 1e-4 absolute is written three times and loses small figures
claim: Derived figures are seeded as (v·1e4).round()/1e4: a fixed decimal-place display rounding in the core, written at three sites. For small torques the seed is wrong by a large fraction, and it becomes the given value if the designer toggles the box to given.
evidence: Probe `seed`: pair at 3e-5 N·m: derived torque 7.4626e-5 is seeded as 0.0001 (+34%).
proposal: One helper `fn seed(v: f64) -> f64` rounding to significant figures (e.g. 6), not decimal places, used at all three sites. Or store the unrounded value and let the formatter round.
validation: Test: seeding then toggling to given leaves solve_train's figures unchanged within 1e-6 relative, across torques 1e-6..1e6.

verdict.reason: There are three sites of `(v * 1e4).round() / 1e4`: mod.rs:3661 (torque), mod.rs:3664 (speed) and mod.rs:2359 (relieved_from). The seed becomes the given value once toggled. Absolute rounding to four decimal places is a relative error that grows without bound as the magnitude falls. The rounding is intentional ('to the digits they saw', mod.rs:2346-2348) and matches the panel's `Number(computed.toFixed(4))` at web/src/TrainPanel.svelte:1814. So it is a fourth copy of the same constant, in TypeScript, and the display loses the same digits.
verdict.evidence: Probe, pair [17,43] with the output torque derived. Input 3e-5 N·m: seeded 0.0001, actual 7.4626e-5 (+34%). Input 1e-3: seeded 0.0025, actual 0.0024875 (+0.5%). Inputs 2 and 1234.57 are exact to 1e-4. The speed seeds are -1186.0465 against -1186.046511.
verdict.proposal_note: The core and the panel must change together. If the core rounds to N significant figures while TrainPanel.svelte:1814 keeps toFixed(4), the seed no longer equals 'the digits they saw'. Better: one `seed(v)` helper to significant figures in the core, with the panel formatting to the same significant figures from a core-provided precision. Or store unrounded and let a single formatter round. Since rule 1 puts number policy in Rust, the precision should be one named constant there.

title: per_tooth rebuilds the whole kinematic system once per member per path on every solve, for a figure only the harness reads
claim: PathReport::per_tooth is serde-skipped ('the panel shows none of it'), yet paths_of calls train.system_counting once per member for each path on every solve_train, including every wasm solve and both solves of a preview. It is also a finite difference (the ratio at z+1, a jump), which is correctly documented as such.
evidence: Code at mod.rs:3437-3456; the serde(skip) and ts(skip) at 3920-3921. The known flaky wall-clock test (every_search_is_quick_enough_to_type_over) is the budget this spends from.
proposal: Move per_tooth out of PathReport into a separate `pub fn ratio_per_tooth(train, parts, path) -> Vec<Option<f64>>` that the harness and Alone call. Also backward = forward / forward[b] on a one-motion path, so motion_from(b) and the backward[a]==0 check are redundant; the backlash closure also recomputes coefficient() three times per mesh.
validation: The golden corpus is unchanged (the harness still prints per_tooth); time a 16-gear line solve before and after.

verdict.reason: per_tooth is computed on every solve_train for every path (mod.rs:3437-3456, 3525), and it is serde- and ts-skipped (mod.rs:3920-3921). The consumers are the harness (gear-cli kinematics.rs:453, graph.rs:109), Alone.ratio_per_tooth, and the shape.rs/mod.rs laws. Its cost is small, though: a worktree toggle that returns early shows 5-20% on small presets and nothing measurable on a long line, where the 2^M flow dominates (reported separately under kinematics-flow and lens-performance). The claim that the flaky wall-clock test's budget is what per_tooth spends from is overstated. That test times solve_preset with searches on, which run for milliseconds, while per_tooth takes microseconds. The architectural point stands: a harness-only figure lives on the solve path. The backlash closure does call coefficient() three times per mesh via Backlash::banded (mod.rs:162-165), since the band points share one coefficient.
verdict.evidence: Worktree with an env toggle that makes per_tooth return early, release build, 5-solve average. Planetary: 238 µs against 194 µs. Ravigneaux: 66 against 58. Wolfrom: 38 against 36. Line of 2: 83 against 71. Line of 8: 3.34 ms against 2.83 ms. Line of 16: 778 ms against 782 ms (unchanged, flow-dominated). every_search_is_quick_enough_to_type_over (mod.rs:9997) times solve_preset with set_search(true).
verdict.corrected_claim: per_tooth, a harness-only figure, is computed on every solve, including wasm and both solves of a preview, at a cost of roughly 5-20% of a small preset's solve and negligible on long trains. Moving it out is a cleanliness gain more than a performance one. coefficient() is evaluated three times per mesh where once would do.
verdict.proposal_note: Moving it to a separate function that the harness and Alone call is reasonable. Hoist coefficient(k, read, from) out of the banded closure (compute a Vec once per path, then multiply by play[band]). Do not cite the wall-clock test as the motivation.

title: Train::arranged sends every non-load entry, Free included, to the output
claim: arranged moves each is_load entry to input and every other entry to output, whatever its role. A case with a declared Free input (the back-driving 'free' variant) ends up with its Free entry at the output. solve_alone then picks the first non-load entry as the path end even when it is Free, while paths_of only counts Reacted entries, so the path lookup silently falls to None.
evidence: Code at mod.rs:3140-3144 and 3222 (`find(|l| !l.is_load())`) against 3392 (`l.role == LoadRole::Reacted`).
proposal: In arranged, move only Load entries to input and Reacted entries to output, and leave Free entries where they are (or drop them). In solve_alone, match the reaction with `l.role == LoadRole::Reacted`.
validation: Unit test: arranged on a case with a declared Free input keeps it Free at the input; solve_alone finds the path.

verdict.reason: The code reads as quoted, but the failure described does not follow from it, and no caller can reach it. Every caller of `arranged`/`arranged_as` applies it to a fresh `Train::alone`, whose two cases are exactly [Load at input, Reacted at output] (mod.rs:3120-3122, 2936-2943). I grepped all 20+ call sites: no Free entry exists when `arranged` runs. Under the finding's own scenario the lookup still works. `arranged` puts every non-load entry at `output`, so `find(|l| !l.is_load())` in `solve_alone` returns `output` whether it lands on the Free entry or the Reacted one. The ends come out (input, output), and `paths_of` wants that same pair from the Reacted entry. The probe confirms the ratio is found. The only case that gives None has a Free entry and no Reacted entry. There `paths_of` wants no path whether or not `arranged` ran, so `arranged` is not the cause. The narrower point that holds: the doc says every case is "reacted at `output`", but roles are left as they are. A case with Load+Free comes back with no reaction, and a case with Load+Free+Reacted comes back with two entries at one body.
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-train-mod-b-3 on pair([17,43]). Loads [(1,Load),(2,Free),(2,Reacted)] after arranged(&[],1,2) give ratio Some(-2.529), the same as the plain alone train. Loads [(2,Load),(1,Free)] become [(1,Load),(2,Free)] after arranged and give ratio None. That is the expected answer for a case with no reaction: paths_of (mod.rs:3390-3392) wants Load→Reacted pairs only. Call sites: edits.rs:907, gear-cli main.rs:236/3382, planetary.rs:41, arrangements.rs:968/1046/1383, shape.rs:4418/5024/5048/5122/5620/5769/5989/6054, mod.rs:4912/4943/4982/11316/11350. All are on Train::alone output.
verdict.corrected_claim: `Train::arranged` rewrites only where each entry sits, not its role, so it does not fully keep its documented promise ("loaded at input and reacted at output"). A case with a Free port and no reaction stays unreacted, and a Free entry beside a Reacted one lands on the same body. No caller passes such a case, and the path lookup in `solve_alone` does not fail as a result.
verdict.proposal_note: The simplest fix that keeps the doc true: have `arranged` rebuild each case's loads as `[the first is_load entry moved to input, Load::declared(output, Reacted)]`, keeping the kind, duty and figures, and drop any other entries. `solve_alone` can match `role == Reacted` for tidiness, but that changes no answer after `arranged`.

title: The case's first-load accessors (torque/speed/set_*) read a declared reaction when it is listed first
claim: LoadCase::torque(), speed(), set_torque(), set_speed() and set_port() act on loads.first(), which can be a Reacted or Free entry whose figures are unread. set_torque on such a case writes a figure nothing reads and reports success.
evidence: Code at mod.rs:2986-3015; 20 call sites across the crates.
proposal: Act on the first entry with is_load(), or remove the accessors in favour of explicit indexing (the panel already names loads by index through CaseFreedom).
validation: Unit test with a case whose first entry is Reacted.

verdict.reason: The hazard is as described: `torque()`, `speed()`, `set_torque()`, `set_speed()` and `set_port()` act on `loads.first()` whatever its role. But the claim of 20 call sites across the crates overstates the reach. Every call site is test code: the gear-core sites are all at mod.rs lines ≥ 5026, inside the #[cfg(test)] module that starts at 4639, and the gear-io site is train.rs:591, inside #[cfg(test)] from 461. gear-wasm and gear-cli call none of them. So no production path reads a Reacted entry's unread figures through these accessors. The real finding is a public production API that only tests use, whose name ("the first load") suggests a load when it means the first entry. Every test that uses it builds the case with the Load first, so nothing is wrong today.
verdict.evidence: grep for `.set_torque(|.set_speed(|.set_port(|.torque()|.speed()` over crates/: mod.rs:5026,5163,5821,5926-5928,6036,6284,7294,7307,7521,8815,8855,9502,10572,10620,10877,10912,11012,11031 and gear-io train.rs:591. `grep -n '^#\[cfg(test)\]'` gives mod.rs:4639 and gear-io train.rs:461. The constructors ultimate/fatigue/back_driving (mod.rs:2936-2975) all put the given Load first.
verdict.corrected_claim: Only tests use LoadCase's first-entry accessors. They are pub production API that act on `loads.first()` whatever its role, and their docs say "the first load". Nothing in production misreads through them, but a future caller could.
verdict.proposal_note: CLAUDE.md's rule is that what nothing reads goes. Delete the five accessors, or move them into the test module as helpers, and have the tests index `loads[0]` (or `loads.iter().find(Load::is_load)`) directly. The one gear-io test (train.rs:591) becomes `loads[0].speed.manual`. Pointing them at the first `is_load()` entry keeps dead production API alive.

title: FaceSources::width_for jumps from a vanishing ask to the given width at exactly zero
claim: With sources enabled, the width follows the asked width as it tends to 0 with the load, then at exactly 0 returns `given`: the output jumps. The comment defends this (an unsolvable case gives zero asks), but the clash is between 'unsolved' and 'unloaded'.
evidence: Code at mod.rs:2553-2557 and the comment at 2531-2534.
proposal: Filter unsolved cases out of `asks` upstream: an unsolved case asks nothing (None). Then return want whenever at least one enabled rating returned Some, even when it is 0, and `given` only when none did. Also trim the history paragraph ('used to come out zero') in favour of the rule.
validation: Test: a solved case at torque → 0 gives width → 0 continuously; an unsolved case leaves the width at its box.

verdict.reason: I reproduced the jump. On pair([17,43]) with the face width set to automatic (default FaceSources: bending ultimate and fatigue on), the width scales linearly with torque down to 4.5e-13 mm at 1e-12 N·m. At exactly 0 N·m it jumps to the box's 10 mm. The comment at mod.rs:2531-2534 makes 'unsolved' and 'unloaded' the same thing via `want == 0.0`, and that is the source. The proposal is unsafe as written, though. Returning `want` when it is 0 gives a member of zero width, and the doc comment at 2515-2519 and docs/state.md:746 record that a zero width makes every rating infinite or NaN. So the proposal would turn the jump into a degenerate gear at zero load. A face width that tends to zero is also a problem of its own (see missed).
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-train-mod-b-3. With face_width.auto = true, T=2 gives 0.8953 mm, T=1e-3 gives 4.4765e-4, T=1e-6 gives 4.4765e-7, T=1e-12 gives 4.4765e-13, and T=0 gives 10.0, with no notes at any torque. Code at mod.rs:2553-2557: `if want == 0.0 { given } else { want }`. shape.rs:3461-3473 floors the ask only by `for_overlap(i)`, which is 0 on straight teeth (reference.md:472).
verdict.proposal_note: Filtering unsolved cases upstream (so they ask None) is right. But returning 0 for a solved zero-load case produces a zero-width gear, which the rating divides by. The continuous fix needs a floor that holds at zero load: a stated minimum automatic width, for example a user-visible b_min/m_n proportion or the box value as a floor, shown as a note when it governs. Then width = max(floor, ask) is continuous through T=0 and never degenerate. Whether unsolved cases with no ask fall back to the box or to the floor should then be one rule.

title: Exact kinematics overflows i128 on a 9-pair chain whose answer is ~1e14; the case is then misreported as underdetermined
claim: System::solve absorbs every structural row before any condition, and Ratio::checked_add cross-multiplies full denominators. In a chain of fixed-axis pairs the intermediate RREF entries grow about 4.5 decades per stage and pass i128 (1.7e38) at 9 stages of 17/43 or 13/61, and at 11 of 19/23. The answer itself is only (43/17)^9 ≈ 4e3, with numerator and denominator near 1e14. solve_parts maps every Err from motion_in (Overflow, Conflicts) to `determined = false` and emits TRAIN_CASE_UNDERDETERMINED with short = 0, so the user is told the case lacks a speed when the train is fully determined. ratio.rs:26-28 says 'i128 holds any train anyone will build', and the only overflow test (train/mod.rs:7746) uses 4e9-tooth gears.
evidence: probe probes/kinematics-flow/src/bin/pairs.rs: n 8 → Ok(6975757441/11688200277601); n 9 motion from input → Err(Overflow), while the same system driven from the output returns Ok(-502592611936843/118587876497). So the failure depends on elimination order, not on the size of the answer. pairs2.rs, 9 × pair([17,43]): Train::motion Ok, but solve_train case note `train.case_underdetermined {short: "0"}`, paths 0. Main probe: 10 × pair([17,43]) and 14 × pair([17,19]) show case 0 unsolved with case_underdetermined while case 1 (back-driving) solves. Python emulation notes/kinematics-flow/ratio_emu.py reproduces the crate's order exactly: cur 17/43 OVF at 9, 19/23 at 11. The same with conditions absorbed first: 17/43 fine to 23 stages, 13/61 to 20. lcm-based add: 17/43 fine to 12.
proposal: (a) Stop hiding the reason: at train/mod.rs:4432 match Err(Refusal::Overflow) → push ERROR_TRAIN_OVERFLOW (or TrainError::Overflow), Err(Conflicts(b)) → an overdetermined note naming b, and keep case_underdetermined for Ok(non-unique) only. (b) Make overflow unreachable for realistic trains. Either (i) absorb the unit condition rows (Ground/Drive) before the structural rows in System::solve; they are single-entry rows and eliminate whole columns, and conflict naming still works because a structural row can only conflict through the RHS. Or (ii) replace the incremental RREF with fraction-free Bareiss elimination over i128, whose intermediates are bounded by minors (Hadamard), or with a small bigint. (c) Pre-cancel gcd(den_a, den_b) in checked_add. (d) Correct the ratio.rs:26 claim to state the actual limit.
validation: New law in kinematics tests: a chain of N pairs z1/z2 for N up to 20 with z in 12..97 returns the exact product (z1/z2)^N whichever end is driven. A solve_train test that a 12-pair chain has a path and no case_underdetermined note. Keep the 4e9-tooth test for real overflow, and assert it now raises the overflow note rather than underdetermined.

verdict.reason: Reproduced exactly. It happens only at 9 or more fixed-axis stages with coprime counts, and every train of realistic depth I tried solves: 3 to 6 chained planetary sets 23/31/85, 3 to 5 Wolfroms 17/[53,55], and a 6-pair chain of mixed coprime counts. So the overflow is an edge case. The misreported reason and the silently dropped path are the real defect: a train whose header ratio solves shows a case called underdetermined with short 0, and no path.
verdict.evidence: Probe probes/verify-kinematics-flow-1 bin pairs calls System::motion_in directly on n × pair([17,43]). n=8 from the input gives Ok(6975757441/11688200277601). n=9 from the input gives Err(Overflow), while from the output it gives Ok(-502592611936843/118587876497). n=10 behaves the same. Bin pairs2 runs solve_train. [17,43] n=9 and n=10, and [19,23] n=11 and n=12: Train::motion is Ok (for example -502592611936843/118587876497), case 0 is unsolved with note train.case_underdetermined {short:"0"}, case 1 (back-driving) solves, and paths is 0. [20,40] solves up to n=20 because its denominators stay small. The cause is at train/mod.rs:4433-4441, where `_ => determined = false` swallows Err(Overflow) and Err(Conflicts). paths_of's motion_from (mod.rs:3401-3406) drops the path with .ok()? and gives no note. ratio.rs:26-28 ('i128 holds any train anyone will build') is false as written.
verdict.proposal_note: Parts (a), (c) and (d) are sound. Part (b)(i) would break a stated behaviour. motion_in's `first` exists so that the condition that conflicts is the one named, and check_parts refuses a part at the hold that locked it. If the conditions are absorbed before the structural rows, a locked train conflicts on a structural row (its reduced right-hand side becomes non-zero), and solve() reports that as NoMotion without naming any condition. The auditor's note that 'conflict naming still works' is wrong. Two ways keep the naming: solve conditions-first to get the answer, and replay in the current order only when a conflict appears; or keep the order and make the arithmetic hold, with Bareiss fraction-free elimination or a small bigint. Cancelling gcd(den_a, den_b) in checked_add (c) is cheap and worth doing, but by the auditor's own emulation it only moves 17/43 from 9 stages to 12.

title: Power flow enumerates 2^M direction assignments over the whole train's meshes: seconds at M=14-16, no bound on M, silent wrap at M≥32
claim: flow::solve loops `for assignment in 0..(1u32 << m)` and, for each assignment, runs an O(bodies·M²) float elimination. M is the number of meshes in the whole train, because one flow is solved across all parts. solve_train calls it per case and 3 times per path (running forward, backward, and at rest). Time therefore doubles per added mesh, and offers, previews and relief multiply it again. There is no guard on M. In release or wasm builds `1u32 << 32` has no overflow check and wraps to 1, so at M ≥ 32 only the all-forward assignment would be tried, silently. CLAUDE.md rule 3 says 'A full train solve is microseconds'.
evidence: probes/kinematics-flow (release): flow::solve alone on a chain: M=10 8.7 ms, M=15 422 ms, M=18 2.0 s, M=20 11.2 s. solve_train: ravigneaux([18,30],[22,18],62,3) x1 M=4 1.8 ms, x2 M=8 21.6 ms, x3 M=12 265 ms, x4 M=16 5688 ms. 7 simple sets (M=14) 1762 ms. 4 meshed-planet sets (M=12) 315 ms. 'all presets but crossed' (M=10) 96 ms. Polynomial alternative, tested against a mirror of the crate's algorithm (notes/kinematics-flow/fp2.py, fp4.py): solve the lossless system, take each mesh's direction from the sign of its driver power, re-solve with loss, repeat until the directions are stable. Result: identical efficiency and every shaft torque (to 1e-9) in 147,000/147,000 cases over simple, Wolfrom, compound, meshed, Ravigneaux, hula, Simpson and chains with η 0.5-0.999, converging in 1 solve (142,383) or 2 (4,617). fp4 (η 0.9-0.999 plus worms with backward η ∈ {0, -0.2, 0.2}): 392,000/392,000 agree. With extreme inputs (fp3: η 0.3-1, 15 % negative or zero directions) it agreed in 376,034/392,000. Every disagreement was a case where every consistent flow had efficiency 0 (locked), and the iteration cycled instead of finding it.
proposal: Replace the enumeration with the fixed-point: directions from the lossless flow's power signs (sign 0 keeps the previous choice), re-solve under those directions, stop when stable (≤ M+1 iterations), then apply the existing consistency and loss filters. Fall back to enumeration only when the iteration cycles or ends inconsistent (the self-locking case), and restrict that fallback to the connected parts whose meshes changed direction (series parts decouple through their shared bodies' torques), capping it with an explicit refusal note above, say, M=20. Use u64 or checked_shl at minimum. Rewrite the flow.rs header (lines 10-19) and remove 'microseconds' from CLAUDE.md or state the measured figure in docs/state.md.
validation: Keep the enumeration as a test oracle: a property test over every preset, every chained pair of presets and random η (including self-locking), asserting the new solve returns the enumeration's efficiency, directions and shaft torques. A timing law: a 7-set chain solves in under 50 ms. The existing flow tests (Pennestrì on every arrangement, the locked pair) must pass unchanged.

verdict.reason: flow::solve enumerates `for assignment in 0..(1u32 << m)` over every mesh in the whole train (flow.rs:223). paths_of calls it per case and again for each path direction and at rest. I measured the exponential growth myself. Even moderate trains take milliseconds, not the 'microseconds' in CLAUDE.md. Nothing bounds M, and in release or wasm builds `1u32 << 32` wraps to 1, so at 32 or more meshes only the all-forward assignment is tried. The fixed-point proposal is supported by the auditor's data (fp2/fp4 agreed in every case, and a fallback is needed for locked cases, as fp3 shows).
verdict.evidence: Release probe bin dual, solve_train on chained ravigneaux([18,30],[22,18],62,3): x1 (M=4) 1.3 ms, x2 (M=8) 13.3 ms, x3 (M=12) 153 ms, x4 (M=16) 2913 ms. Bin sets: 3 chained planetary sets 3.4 ms, 6 sets (M=12) 93 ms. The auditor's notes/kinematics-flow/out_fp2.txt and out_fp4.txt show agree = cases, with no fallbacks, over the swept families. flow_study's earlier run without a fallback found 7113 compound and 2115 Ravigneaux cases where the plain fixed point returned nothing, so the fallback is essential, not optional.
verdict.proposal_note: Keep the enumeration as the fallback and as a test oracle, as proposed. The fallback cannot be dropped: the auditor's own flow_study shows the unaugmented iteration fails on locked cases. A cheaper first step, independent of the fixed point, is to solve the flow per connected component of meshes that share no unknown torque (series parts decouple through a known shaft torque), which turns 2^(ΣM) into Σ2^(M_i). lens-architecture #7 proposes the same. Use checked_shl, or refuse above a stated M, in any case.

repro.reproduction:
I ran a release-build probe crate against the public API: /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/repro-kinematics-flow-1/src/main.rs, binary /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probe-target/release/probe_repro_kinematics_flow_1, with modes `time`, `wrap` and `train`.
(1) `time`: calls flow::solve on an idler chain of M external meshes on ground, with η 0.98 forward and 0.97 backward, driven from the far end so every mesh runs Backward. It also calls solve_train on arr::ravigneaux([18,30],[22,18],62,3) chained 1 to 4 times, with an ultimate case and a back-driving case.
(2) `wrap`: the same chain at M = 32, 33, 40 and 64, driven forward and in reverse.
(3) `train`: solve_train on N chained arr::pair presets alternating [17,19] and [19,17] so the ratio stays near 1, for N = 4, 32 and 33, with LoadCase::ultimate and LoadCase::back_driving.
How I know the correct answer: power in a series chain of simple meshes loses a factor η at each mesh, so the efficiency is Π η. That is 0.97^M for the reverse-driven chain, and it is symmetric for the pair chain. The crate's own N=4 result matches this, which confirms that closed form is the right oracle.
repro.observed:
Exponential time (release):
- flow::solve alone, reverse chain: M=8 0.45 ms, M=10 2.3 ms, M=12 12.2 ms, M=14 60 ms, M=16 267 ms, M=18 1234 ms. That is about 4.6x per 2 meshes, i.e. about 2^M.
- The efficiency is correct at every M up to 18 (for example M=18: 0.577951263 = 0.97^18).
- solve_train on Ravigneaux chains: x1 (M=4) 1.4 ms, x2 (M=8) 12.3 ms, x3 (M=12) 140 ms, x4 (M=16) 2851 ms.

Silent wrong answer at M ≥ 32. Release builds have no overflow check, so `1u32 << m` (flow.rs:223) keeps only the low 5 bits of m:
- The chain driven forward at M=32, 33 and 64 gives the right answer (0.523883140 = 0.98^32), because assignment 0 is the only one tried.
- The same chain driven in reverse returns Err(Inconsistent) at M=32, 33, 40 and 64. The closed form says 0.377307551 at M=32.
- M=40 took 3.4 ms against 0.02 ms at M=32: 1<<40 is masked to 1<<8, so 256 assignments are tried. That confirms the masking.

The fault reaches the train level through solve_train:
- 4 pairs (M=4): both paths have efficiency 0.918177 in each direction, and both cases solve. 0.918177 = η^4, with η taken from the 32-pair forward result.
- 32 pairs (M=32): path 1->33 gives 0.505138 forward but 0.000000 backward. Path 33->1 gives 0 forward. The back-driving case reports solved=false with the note `train.load_not_reacted`. The correct backward efficiency is 0.505138, since the pairs are symmetric, as the 4-pair case shows. The note tells the user something false.
- 33 pairs: the same result.

Nothing refuses a large M, and no note is raised. In a debug build (which is what the tests run) the same shift would instead panic with a shift overflow, so no test can see the release/wasm behaviour. I did not create any worktree.
repro.note:
Confirmed on both counts.
(a) The time is exponential in the number of meshes across the whole train. It is already seconds at M=16 with realistic presets (four Ravigneaux sets), and offers, previews and relief multiply it further. CLAUDE.md rule 3's "a full train solve is microseconds" is false beyond the smallest trains: 1.4 ms at M=4.
(b) At M ≥ 32, release/wasm returns wrong results silently. The back-drive efficiency comes out as 0 and a false "load not reacted" note is raised, where it should be 0.505.

Severity stays high. The wrong answer needs 32 or more meshes, which is uncommon but has no guard. The exponential time already hurts at 12-16 meshes, and the UI edits and dry-runs trains interactively.

Two fixes, the minimal one first:
- Minimal: use u64 or checked_shl and refuse above a stated M with a note.
- Proper: split the flow into connected components that share no unknown torque, turning 2^ΣM into Σ2^M_i. Or use the fixed-point on lossless power signs, with enumeration kept as the fallback for locked cases and as a test oracle.

A regression test must run in release mode or call the component splitting directly; a debug-mode test only panics.

title: A refused flow or play solve is reported as efficiency 0 and backlash 0: dual-countershaft trains read as self-locking with zero play
claim: paths_of's `flowing` maps any flow::Refused to (0.0, 0.0). `coefficient` maps any play refusal to 0.0. A redundant mesh loop, such as two layshafts sharing the input and output gears (twin-countershaft truck transmissions) or a doubled mesh, makes the flow Undetermined (load sharing is statically indeterminate). It also makes System::play return NoMotion for every mesh in the loop, because a unit play in one row contradicts the parallel row. The path then shows efficiency 0.000 % both ways, indistinguishable from a self-locking drive, circulation 0, and backlash that silently drops every mesh in the loop. Both quantities are well defined here: identical branches give the branch efficiency, and the play of parallel identical branches is that of one branch.
evidence: probes/kinematics-flow/src/bin/dual.rs (input 17 meshes 43 on each of two layshafts, 19 on each layshaft meshes output 41). Single layshaft: ratio 5.458204, eff 0.968084/0.968084, backlash fwd 0.058901° bwd 0.321491°. Dual: same ratio, eff 0.000000/0.000000, backlash 0.000000°/0.000000°, case note train.load_shared. loop.rs (the output pair doubled on one layshaft): eff 0.000000, backlash fwd 0.018050° against the true 0.058901°, so the output mesh's play is dropped entirely and backlash is understated by 69 %.
proposal: Make PathReport's efficiency, circulation and backlash Option (or carry a note) and set None with a stated reason (train.load_shared / a new 'mesh loop' note) instead of 0.0. Keep the (0,0) value for a genuine locked flow only. For play, detect NoMotion per mesh and either say the loop's play is not additive or compute it: the play of a loop is the minimum over its branches, which the System can produce by solving each spanning tree with the loop's redundant rows removed and taking the minimum. For the flow of identical parallel branches, a minimum-norm (equal-share) solution gives the efficiency that holds for any share when the branches' η are equal. Offer that as an explicit, labelled assumption rather than silently choosing.
validation: Test: the dual-countershaft train reports an efficiency equal to the single-layshaft one (or None plus the note, never 0.0), and backlash not below the single-branch figure. A law over every preset with one mesh doubled: path backlash is never less than without the doubling.

verdict.reason: The numbers reproduce exactly. One correction: the case is not silent. It carries train.load_shared and is marked unsolved, so 'indistinguishable from self-locking' overstates it at case level. Even so, the path still prints 0 % efficiency and 0° (or understated) backlash as figures. The note's text blames the user's holds ('held at both ends ... hold one end only'), which is not the cause, because a redundant mesh loop has no second hold to remove. The backlash understatement in the doubled-mesh case is a silent wrong number.
verdict.evidence: Probe bin dual (input 17 to 43 on each layshaft, 19 to 41 output). With one layshaft: ratio 5.458204, efficiency 0.968084/0.968084, backlash 0.058901°/0.321491°. With two layshafts: same ratio, efficiency 0.000000/0.000000, backlash 0.000000/0.000000, case solved false, notes [train.load_shared]. Bin loop (output pair doubled on one layshaft): backlash forward 0.018050° against the true 0.058901°, and 0.098522° against 0.321491° backward, with row_play identical for meshes 1 and 2. Code: mod.rs:3418-3431 maps any flow::Refused to (0,0). mod.rs:3458-3465 maps play Err(NoMotion) to 0.0. mod.rs:4500-4503 pushes TRAIN_LOAD_SHARED for Refused::Undetermined. strings_en.toml:155 reads 'held at both ends: ... hold one end only'.
verdict.corrected_claim: For a train with a redundant mesh loop (twin countershafts, a doubled mesh), the case is refused with train.load_shared, whose words blame a double hold that is not there. The path still reports efficiency 0 and circulation 0 as if they were figures. Its backlash silently drops every mesh in the loop: 0 for the twin layshaft, and 69 % understated for a doubled output mesh.
verdict.proposal_note: Make efficiency, circulation and backlash Option, or suppress the path while its case is refused; that is the minimal fix. Add a distinct 'redundant mesh loop' note instead of reusing load_shared. For play, the minimum over the loop's spanning trees is correct for rigid bodies, but an equal-share flow is a hidden assumption and must stay an explicit, opt-in label, as the auditor says.

repro.reproduction:
Probe crate /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/repro-kinematics-flow-2 (public API: arrangements::Builder, Train::chained, chain_ends, LoadCase::ultimate(i,o,2.0,3000.0), solve_train with gear_io default library). Run: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probe-target /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/gc <probe dir> cargo run --offline -q --bin dual (and --bin loop).
Smallest input: module 1. An input gear of 17 teeth meshes 43 on a layshaft, and 19 on that layshaft meshes an output of 41 (input and output coaxial). Bin `dual` adds a second identical layshaft (17-43 and 19-41 again) with its own centre distance. Bin `loop` instead doubles the 19-41 pair on the same layshaft. No worktree was created.
repro.observed:
Single layshaft: ratio 5.458204, efficiency 0.968084/0.968084, backlash fwd 0.058901 deg, bwd 0.321491 deg, case solved, no notes. The per-mesh row_play is identical for every mesh in every variant: [~0, 0.029232, 0.058609].
Twin layshaft: same ratio 5.458204, but efficiency 0.000000/0.000000, backlash fwd 0.000000 and bwd 0.000000, case solved=false, notes [train.load_shared].
Doubled output mesh: efficiency 0.000000/0.000000, backlash fwd 0.018050 deg (should be 0.058901) and bwd 0.098522 deg (should be 0.321491). That is 69 % understated, silently: the path figure carries no note of its own.
How the correct values are known, without sharing code:
(a) Rigid bodies and parallel identical branches: the output can turn until the tightest branch closes, and identical branches close together. So the loop's play equals one branch's play, the single-layshaft 0.058901 deg. Every branch's η is the same, so the efficiency is 0.968084 whatever the load share.
(b) The doubled-mesh figure is exactly the single-branch figure with the output mesh's term removed. The two terms should stand in the ratio (r41/r43)(19/41) = 19/43 = 0.4419, and the numbers give 0.018050/(0.058901-0.018050) = 0.018050/0.040851 = 0.4419. So the 0.018050 left is the input mesh's reflected play, and the output mesh's term was dropped.
Cause confirmed in code:
- mod.rs:3419-3434: `flowing` has `.map_or((0.0, 0.0), ...)` on flow::solve, so a Refused (here Undetermined) becomes efficiency 0 and circulation 0.
- mod.rs:3458-3465: `coefficient` has `system.play(k,&c).and_then(Result::ok).map_or(0.0, ...)`, so a mesh inside a loop, whose play is NoMotion, contributes 0.
- strings_en.toml:155: load_shared reads "held at both ends: ... hold one end only, or let a self-locking mesh hold it". This train has only one hold, so the advice cannot be followed.
repro.note:
Fully reproduced, with the reviewer's correction confirmed: the case is not silent (solved=false plus train.load_shared). I re-judge severity as medium rather than high. The ratio is right and the case carries a refusal flag. The efficiency 0 also sits beside that flag, so it is misleading but flagged. Two defects remain. First, backlash is a wrong number with no flag of its own: 0 for twin countershafts, and 69 % low for a doubled mesh. Second, the note's advice (hold one end only) is wrong for a redundant mesh loop, which has no second hold to release. Twin-countershaft gearboxes are a real design, so this is reachable. The doubled mesh between the same two bodies is more contrived.
Fix, in order of minimum effort:
1. Make PathReport efficiency, circulation and backlash Option, set to None when flow::solve is Refused or any mesh's play() is NoMotion. Never map either to 0.0.
2. Add a distinct note key for a redundant mesh loop (5 × strings_*.toml), separate from train.load_shared.
3. Optionally compute the loop's play as the minimum over spanning trees: drop one redundant row per loop, solve, take the minimum.
Test to add: the twin-layshaft train's path backlash is either None or at least 0.058901 deg, and its efficiency is either None or 0.968084, never 0. Law: over every preset, doubling any mesh never lowers the path backlash.
