With everything pinned and D typed (just = D), relief frees only x_s. The planet-ring mesh then has D, x_p and x_r all given, and the solve fails with the wrong message, 'the gears cannot mesh: module, pressure angle or helix differ'. Probe -d (rebuilt; output identical to the pre-crash file): 18 of 122 'everything pinned, then one box typed' cases fail across the presets (Planetary, Compound, MeshedPlanets, Layshaft, Planocentric). For example, MeshedPlanets with D1 typed: x2 is the only unknown for both mesh 1 and mesh 2, so D1 is not reached.
proposal: Replace the counted groups for the geometric relations with structural rank. Declare each relation (one per mesh: its distance, clearance, size and the shifts it can move) as a row, and each input as a column. A state is admissible when a maximum bipartite matching covers every row with an automatic column (Hopcroft-Karp, or Kuhn at these sizes; probe -d's sdr() is a working sketch). Relief: while the matching is short, turn automatic the least-precious given input (in the declared precedence, `just` last) that lengthens it. Keep the distance-and-clearance, module and always_automatic rules as they are; they are genuine count rules. This makes the result independent of group order by construction, because it asks one global question.
validation: Strengthen every_input_relief_leaves_given_is_honoured_by_the_solve to probe -d's form: from every preset with everything pinned, for every freedom f, nudge f, relieve with just = f, solve, and require the typed value to equal the solved figure (1e-6) with no part.distance_not_reached or part.clearance_negative notes. Also sweep every order of the groups returned by freedoms() and require identical toggles.

verdict.corrected_claim: Relief counts each mesh relation as its own FreedomGroup, and the state it leaves is not what the solve can close. There are two different mismatches. (a) A later mesh's group lists as absorbers shifts of the first mesh, such as x_sun for the planet-ring mesh (absorbers() at shape.rs:591). Such a shift can close the later mesh only through an automatic distance. When the distance is given, one automatic shift is counted by both groups. This is a real Hall-condition failure. Example: Planetary with D typed leaves D, C, x_p, x_r and pd_ring given and only x_s automatic. Both groups pass, and the ring mesh is not reached. (b) The auditor's headline example (x_s pinned, then D typed) is not 'two relations, one unknown' as relief models it. The size entry is automatic there, so a matching with size as a column (the auditor's own sdr(), which includes the readings entry) admits the state: E1 takes size, E2 takes x_p. It fails because the solve sizes the helix only for a mesh whose two shifts are both pinned (helix_angles, shape.rs:821-837). The relation model's size unknown is wider than what the solve does. The proposal as written, bipartite matching with size in each relation's columns, fixes (a) but still accepts (b).
verdict.reason: I confirmed the failures, but the diagnosis and the proposal cover only one of the two mechanisms. The existing law every_input_relief_leaves_given_is_honoured_by_the_solve (mod.rs:7938) only nudges boxes left given after relieved(None). It never types an automatic box with `just`, so it cannot see either mechanism. The failures are loud: part.distance_not_reached and part.clearance_negative are raised, or a misleading Mesh(Incompatible) 'module, pressure angle or helix differ'. They are not silent wrong answers, so the severity is lowered to medium.
verdict.evidence: My rerun of probe -d (notes/verify-train-mod-a-1/d.txt): 18 of 122 'everything pinned, then one box typed' cases fail. Examples: Planetary 'typed Distance(0)' with given [D, C, x1, pd2, x2] gives distance_not_reached and clearance_negative, with x_s the only automatic shift. MeshedPlanets 'typed Distance(1)' gives distance_not_reached. My rerun of probe a: '12/30/72 + x_s pinned, + D pinned' has given D, C, x_s, x_r with no size reading given. The planet-ring nominal is 21.063 against 21.225 asked, and x_p = -0.064 was spent on the sun mesh. Printed groups: [[D],[x_s],[x_p],[C],[readings]] given<=4 and [[x_p],[x_r],[x_s]] given<=2. Seven of the 18 cases are finding 3's layshaft and compound helix/pd cases rather than this mechanism.
verdict.proposal_note: Make the relation columns exactly what the solve can use: D, C, and the mesh's own two shifts. Include the group's size only where the solve would size it (both of that mesh's shifts given and nothing stated). Otherwise extend helix_angles/the plan to solve the size jointly. Better still, derive relief from the solve's plan (roles given/free/reaches/absorbs) so the two cannot diverge. Test with the auditor's validation law, which types every automatic box with `just` and requires no distance/clearance note and an honoured value. That law catches both mechanisms, whatever the implementation.

title: Size readings of mesh groups that are not first on their distance are in no group, so a typed helix is silently ignored and a typed pitch diameter makes the solve refuse
claim: The only exclusivity entry for a mesh group's readings (each member's helix and pitch diameter, and the overlap) is pushed inside the first-mesh-on-a-distance group (order.push(entry(readings_for(k))) when n == 0). A Layshaft's second and third pairs, and a Compound's second pair, share distance 0 with the first pair but are separate mesh groups, so their readings are never grouped. Several readings can stand together. helix_angles then takes the last reading per member, and two members of one mesh can state different helices.
evidence: Probe -d (out/d_rerun.txt). Layshaft: typing Member(2, Helix) = 1.0 comes back as 0.00000 with no note; the helix is disregarded because Member(2, PitchDiameter) also stands. Typing Member(2|3|4|5, PitchDiameter) gives the error 'the gears cannot mesh: module, pressure angle or helix differ'. The same holds on Compound, Member(2|4). The comment at shape.rs:4066 says a later mesh gives on nothing but its absorbers, because 'the size ... move[s] every mesh on the distance together'. That is false when the later mesh is in its own mesh group: a layshaft pair's size moves only that pair.
proposal: Declare the size entry once per mesh group, independent of distances: a group {entry(readings of the group)} with given_at_most = 1 as far as exclusivity goes. Let each relation row reference that group's size column. In the matching formulation of the previous finding this is simply one column per mesh group.
validation: Law: after relief, at most one reading per mesh group stands, over every preset and arrangement (the idempotence law checks this only inside declared entries). Probe -d's Layshaft and Compound helix and pitch-diameter lines must pass.

verdict.reason: freedoms() (shape.rs:4048-4081) pushes entry(readings_for(k)) only when n == 0, meaning only for the first mesh on a distance. readings_for(k) (shape.rs:998) returns the readings of k's own mesh group. A Layshaft's pairs 2-3 and 4-5, and a Compound's second pair, are separate mesh groups that sit second or third on distance 0, so their helix and pitch-diameter readings are in no entry at all, and several can stand together. helix_angles picks the last reading (readings().rev(), shape.rs:806), so a typed helix loses to a pitch diameter that is also given. It does so silently, with no note, which is why the severity stays high. The comment at shape.rs:4066-4071 ('the size ... move every mesh on the distance together') is false for a later mesh in its own mesh group: that pair's size is an independent unknown for its own relation.
verdict.evidence: My rerun of probe -d: 'Layshaft: typed Member(2, Helix) = 1.00000, solve came to 0.00000; notes []', with Member(2, PitchDiameter) and Member(2, Helix) both left given. The same holds for members 3, 4 and 5, and for Compound members 2 and 4. Typing Member(2|3|4|5, PitchDiameter) on the Layshaft, or 2|4 on the Compound, gives 'the gears cannot mesh: module, pressure angle or helix differ': two members of one mesh state different helices. The probe-a output also shows the correct behaviour when only the helix is given: 'layshaft: member 2 helix given 10 ... helices [0,0,10,-10,0,0]'.
verdict.proposal_note: Emitting a readings-exclusivity group per mesh group (given_at_most 1) fixes the silent ignore. In addition, the later pair's own relation should list its group's size as a column, because it is a genuine unknown for that pair. That ties this finding to finding 2's corrected model.

repro.reproduction:
I built a probe crate against the public API at /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/repro-train-mod-a-3/src/main.rs; its output is in /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/repro-train-mod-a-3/out.txt. For each of the Spur (the control), Layshaft and Compound presets it starts from `Preset::build()`. It then types a value the way the panel does: set `manual`, set `auto = false`, call `relieved(Some(that freedom))`. It solves with `solve_alone(&Train::alone(s, 10.0, 1000.0), &default_library())` and prints what is still given, each member's helix and pitch diameter, and the notes. The inputs start from defaults, not from the probe -d state where everything was pinned.

Smallest inputs:
(A) Silent ignore. Type Member(i, PitchDiameter) = z·m_n/cos 15°, then type Member(i, Helix) = 10. Here i = 0 on Spur and i = 2 on Layshaft and Compound.
(B) Refusal. Type Member(2, Helix) = 10, then type the mate's PitchDiameter = z·m_n/cos 20°. The mate is 1 on Spur, 3 on Layshaft and 4 on Compound.
repro.observed:
(A) Silent ignore. The Spur control does the right thing. Relief turns the earlier pitch diameter back to automatic, leaves only Member(0, Helix) given, and the solve gives helices [10, −10] with pitch diameters 17.2623 / 43.6633. The Layshaft and Compound do not. Both Member(2, PitchDiameter) and Member(2, Helix) stay given, and the solve returns 15°, not the 10° just typed. Layshaft gives helices [0,0,15,−15,0,0] and d2 = 42.4463. Compound gives [0,0,15,0,15] and d2 = 61.0813. In both cases there are no notes other than the Compound's usual part.planets_share_load_equally. With 20° in place of 15° the Compound behaves the same way: the solve comes to 20° (d2 = 62.7865) after helix = 10 was typed.

(B) Refusal. The Spur control relieves the earlier helix, leaves only Member(1, PitchDiameter) given, and solves at [−20, 20]. On the Layshaft, Member(2, Helix) and Member(3, PitchDiameter) both stay given. On the Compound, Member(2, Helix) and Member(4, PitchDiameter) both stay given. Both solves refuse with "the gears cannot mesh: module, pressure angle or helix differ". On the Compound the mate's 20° pitch diameter typed alone solves fine ([0,0,20,0,20]), so the refusal is caused only by the two readings standing together. On the Layshaft, 20° typed alone is refused as undercut, which is a separate matter; the "cannot mesh" error in (B) is a different refusal.

Both readings also stand when they agree (pitch diameter for 10°, then helix 10). That is harmless in value, but it breaks the rule that relief leaves one reading per mesh group.

How I know what is correct:
- The Spur runs the same code path and shows the intended behaviour.
- The docstring on `Shape::relieved` (train/mod.rs:2296-2300) says the solve should not "accept an input and quietly disregard it". Case (A) does exactly that.
- Checked by hand from d = z·m_n / cos β: 59/cos 15° = 61.081, 41/cos 15° = 42.446, 59/cos 20° = 62.787, 59/cos 10° = 59.910. So the reported diameters are the 15° or 20° values, not the typed 10°.

Cause, as the ledger states: `freedoms()` at shape.rs:4061-4066 pushes `entry(readings_for(k))` only when n == 0. The later groups on distance 0 (Layshaft members 2-3 and 4-5, Compound members 2 and 4) get no exclusivity entry. `helix_angles` (shape.rs:803-815) then takes the last reading per member through `readings().rev()`, and the pitch diameter is pushed after the helix, so the pitch diameter wins. Two members of one mesh can each state their own helix.
repro.note:
Severity re-judged: high, kept. It is reachable from the default presets in two ordinary keystrokes, with nothing pinned beforehand. A value the designer has just typed is disregarded with no note, which the relief contract explicitly promises never to do. The other order gives a refusal that relief exists to prevent.

It affects every preset that has a second mesh group on a shared distance. I checked Layshaft and Compound. Hand-built graphs may have more.

Validation law to add: after `relieved`, at most one Helix/PitchDiameter/Overlap reading stands per mesh group, swept over every preset and every arrangement. The Spur, Layshaft and Compound (A) and (B) cases above make good fixtures.

I created no worktree; only the probe crate and the notes directory were written, both under /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit.

title: Thickness-coefficient groups are per mesh, but the rule runs along the whole chain of meshes: a sun and a ring can both stay given, and the planet then breaks the ring mesh's rule depending on mesh order
claim: k_b = 2 − k_a across an external mesh and k_ring = k_pinion across an internal one. In a connected mesh group the coefficients therefore have one degree of freedom, but relief allows one given per mesh. With k_sun and k_ring both given, thickness_mods() gives the planet whichever mesh it visits first, and the other mesh's rule is broken with no note. The result also depends on the order the meshes are listed in.
evidence: Probe train-mod-a. With the ring's k given at 1.05, typing the sun's at 1.1 (just = sun) leaves [(given 1.1), (auto), (given 1.05)] and thickness_mods() = [1.1, 0.9, 1.05]: the planet-ring mesh runs at k_p = 0.9 against k_r = 1.05, where the rule requires them equal. With all three given, relieved(None) on the preset leaves only the ring given, giving [0.95, 1.05, 1.05]. The same set with its two meshes swapped leaves sun and ring given, giving [1.1, 1.05, 1.05]. So the relief outcome depends on mesh order, against the 'whatever order' claim at mod.rs:2317.
proposal: Emit one ThicknessMod group per mesh group: order = the group's members, given_at_most = 1, automatic_at_most = len. The `just` member stays, and the rest follow through thickness_mods(). This is a tree for every preset. If a cyclic mesh group is ever allowed, check it is consistent there. Also make thickness_mods() traverse in a canonical order (BFS from the given member) instead of mesh order.
validation: Law: after relief, every mesh's rule holds on thickness_mods() (k_a + k_b = 2 external, k_a = k_b internal) to 1e-12, over every preset and every start state, and permuting shape.meshes leaves toggles and thickness_mods unchanged.

verdict.reason: freedoms() emits one ThicknessMod group per mesh with given_at_most 1 (shape.rs:4086-4096). The rule chains through a mesh group, so sun and ring can both stay given. thickness_mods() (shape.rs:1047) then propagates in mesh order, and the first mesh to reach the planet wins, so the other mesh's rule is broken with no note. A mesh-order swap changes which members relief leaves given, which contradicts the 'whatever order the groups come in' doc (mod.rs:2313).
verdict.evidence: My rerun of probe a: 'ring k given then sun typed: [(false,1.1),(true,1.0),(false,1.05)] -> resolved [1.1, 0.9, 1.05]'. The planet-ring internal mesh needs k_p = k_r, but it has 0.9 against 1.05. 'sun mesh first: all k given, relieved(None) leaves given [2] -> [0.95,1.05,1.05]' against 'ring mesh first: ... leaves given [0, 2] -> [1.1,1.05,1.05]'. In the second, 1.1 + 1.05 ≠ 2 breaks the external rule, and the outcome depends on mesh order.
verdict.proposal_note: One group per mesh group is right for the tree-shaped presets. The law should also sweep permutations of shape.meshes.

title: The pitch-diameter reading loses the helix hand and clamps a diameter below z·m to a straight tooth with no note
claim: The reading's helix is acos((z m_n / d).clamp(-1, 1)), which is always ≥ 0. A left-hand member that pins its pitch diameter (the 'pin what you see' flow, relieved_from) turns right-hand, and every mate flips with it. A diameter below z m_n clamps to β = 0 and reports d = z m_n with no clamp note. That breaks rule 5 ('clamp ... and say so').
evidence: Probe -c: pair 17/43 with_first_helix(-15). The solve gives helices [-15, 15] and pd 17.5997. Pinning pd = 17.5997 (the value shown, rounded to 1e-4) gives helices [15.00006, -15.00006]: the hand has flipped. Pair 17/43 with pd = 15 < z·m = 17 reports pd 17.000, helix 0, with no part or gear notes.
proposal: Carry the hand: Reading.helix = sign·acos(z m_n / d), where sign is the member's current hand, i.e. the sign of its helix_angle.manual, or +1 when that is 0. A separate hand input would be cleaner, and would also let a diameter state a size without a hand. Refuse d < z m_n as no shape (rule 5's refusal branch), or clamp it and raise a gear clamp note naming the diameter.
validation: Law: for every member with β ≠ 0, pinning its pitch diameter to its reported value leaves helix_angles() unchanged to the precision of the value pinned, sign included. A test that pd < z m_n gives a refusal or a note, never a silent change.

verdict.reason: The reading at shape.rs:3991-3997 is acos((z·m_n/d).clamp(-1,1)), which is always ≥ 0, so it carries no hand, and d < z·m_n clamps to β = 0 with no note. I reproduced both. Severity is lowered from high: for a lone pair, flipping every hand is a mirror image with identical ratings. It does, however, reverse axial thrust and the drawn hand, and in a multi-group train (such as a layshaft whose pairs' hands are chosen to balance thrust on the shared shaft) it flips one group and not the other. The silent clamp breaks rule 5.
verdict.evidence: My rerun of probe -c: 'left hand -15: helices [-15.0, 15.0] pd 17.5997' becomes 'pd pinned to what it showed: helices [15.000059934612164, -15.000059934612164]'. 'pd 15 < z m = 17: pd reported 17.000 helix 0.0000; part notes []; gear notes []'.
verdict.proposal_note: Carrying the sign of the current helix is the minimal fix. Refusing d < z·m_n is more consistent with rule 5 than clamping, since no helix yields that diameter: the input describes no shape. A diameter so close to z·m_n that it rounds is still reachable at a small β.

title: The overlap box shows mesh 0's ratio but the core reads it at the group's narrowest face, so pinning what the box shows moves the helix
claim: Reading::overlap takes given_width(group), the minimum face over every member of the mesh group, so the ratio is enforced on the group's narrowest mesh. The panel displays reports[meshes[0]].line.contact_ratios.overlap, and relieved_from seeds from that figure. With a narrow ring, the value shown and the value enforced belong to different meshes.
evidence: Probe -c: planetary with sun and planet at 10 mm and the ring at 6 mm, helix given 18.3101°. The box shows 1.0000 (mesh 0), while mesh 1 is at 0.6000. Pinning the shown 1.0 on the group's meshes (just = Overlap(0)) moves the helix to 31.5740°. Asking 1.0 on mesh 0 alone gives reported overlaps [1.667, 1.0].
proposal: Make the group's overlap one core figure: the minimum ε_β over the group's meshes, which is what the reading enforces. Expose it where Figure/solved figures are built (ShapeResult::figure(Freedom::Overlap(k)) returns the group minimum), and have the panel show that figure instead of computing reports[meshes[0]]. This also takes an engineering choice out of the TypeScript (rule 1).
validation: Law: for every preset with every width given, pinning Overlap to the figure the core reports leaves helix_angles() unchanged to 1e-4 relative.

verdict.reason: Reproduced with my own probe. The size reading of a mesh group (shape.rs:3997-4010) takes Overlap(k) from the group's first mesh and turns it into a helix at given_width(group), which is the least face width of every member in the group (shape.rs:970-975). The panel shows reports[meshes[0]].line.contact_ratios.overlap (TrainPanel.svelte:1937). That figure is mesh 0's own ratio at its own width. Pin-what-you-see seeding uses the same figure: relieved_from takes Train figure(Freedom::Overlap(k)), which is meshes[k].line.contact_ratios.overlap (mod.rs:4118-4121). So when the ring is narrower than the sun and planet, the number shown and the number enforced belong to different meshes, and pinning the shown number moves the design.
verdict.evidence: Probe verify-train-mod-a-2 (bin probe_verify_train_mod_a_2), planetary(12,30,72,3) with sun and planet at b=10 and the ring at b=6. With the helix given as 18.3101°, the box shows ε_β(mesh0)=1.0000 and mesh 1 is at 0.6000. Pinning the shown 1.0 on every mesh of the group and relieving with just=Overlap(0) moves the helix to 31.5740° (the box stays automatic). Asking 1.0 on mesh 0 with the ring at 20 or 10 gives 18.3101° and overlaps [1.0, 1.0]. With the ring at 6 it gives 31.574° and overlaps [1.667, 1.0]. Check: sin⁻¹(1.0·π·1/6)=31.57°, sin⁻¹(π/10)=18.31°.
verdict.proposal_note: Either direction of unification works. Reporting the group minimum as the figure (the proposal) matches what is enforced and serves as a floor for every mesh. The alternative is to read the size at mesh 0's own width, which matches what is shown but leaves the narrow mesh below the asked ratio. The group minimum is the better choice. Figure(Overlap(k)) is also used by the relief law's signature, so change it in the core and not only in the panel.

title: The overlap-to-helix relation jumps at its limit: ε_β just below b/(π m) gives an 87° helix, exactly at the limit is a misleading refusal, and above it the helix drops to 0
claim: helix_for_overlap accepts sin β up to and including 1 (0.0..=1.0). At sin = 1 the helix is 90°, which is no gear, and the solve refuses with a message about base circles. Above the limit the reading is None and the helix falls back to its box (0°), with a note. The output therefore runs 70° → 87° → error → 0° as the ratio rises through the limit, and nothing warns while it approaches.
evidence: Probe -c: pair 17/43, both faces 10 mm, m = 1. Overlap 3.0 gives helix 70.47° (pd 50.9). 3.18 gives 87.47° (pd 385.4) with no note. 10/π = 3.18310 gives ERROR 'no such gear pair: the profile shifts require the base circles to overlap'. 3.2 gives helix 0.000° with part.overlap_unreachable.
proposal: Make the admissible interval half-open, sin < 1. Beyond it, choose one behaviour: refuse with the overlap_unreachable key as an error, or clamp to the largest helix the mesh accepts (the same bound the helix box's admissible range carries) and keep the note. Never fall back to the box's stale manual value. That fallback is where the jump comes from.
validation: A sweep of ε_β across b/(π m_n): the helix is monotone non-decreasing, or the ratio is refused, with no drop back to the box value and no error from an unrelated key.

verdict.reason: The discontinuity is real. The helix runs to within a hair of 90° with no note, exactly at the limit the solve fails with an unrelated error, and above the limit the helix drops to 0 with part.overlap_unreachable. Two details are wrong. (1) The fall-back is not to 'the box's stale manual value'. Relief turns the helix entry automatic when the overlap is given, so the helix falls to its automatic value (0). With the helix box's manual value set to 25 the result is still 0.000°. (2) The proposal's 'clamp to the largest helix the helix box's admissible range carries' has no finite target: admissible_ranges gives helix_angle Bound::strictly(-90,90) (auto.rs:698), and a helix typed directly at 89.9° is accepted with no note. The deeper gap is that nothing in the train bounds or notes a near-90° helix from any reading. The overlap path is one way in.
verdict.evidence: Probe bin seven: pair 17/43, both faces 10, m=1. ε_β 3.0→70.47°, 3.18→87.47° (pd 385), 3.183→89.55° (pd 2157), lim−1e-9→89.9986° (pd 678202), all with no notes. At exactly 10/π: ERROR 'no such gear pair: the profile shifts require the base circles to overlap'. At lim+1e-9, 3.2 or 4.0: helix 0.000, pd 17, note part.overlap_unreachable. The results are identical with the helix box's manual value at 0 or at 25. Helix typed 87 or 89.9 directly: accepted, no notes. helix_for_overlap at mod.rs:2150-2153 uses (0.0..=1.0).contains(&sin).
verdict.corrected_claim: The ε_β→helix reading admits sin β = 1 (a 90° helix, which fails later with an unrelated base-circle error) and approaches it with no warning. Past b/(π m_n) the helix falls to its automatic value (0°) with overlap_unreachable. The output therefore jumps from about 90° to 0°. No part of the train bounds or notes a near-90° helix, whichever reading produced it.
verdict.proposal_note: Make the interval half-open. Past the limit, keep the note but make the behaviour one continuous rule. The honest choice is to refuse: say overlap_unreachable and stop there. A clamp has no finite angle to clamp to unless the project states a maximum helix as a user-visible input, and rule 5 would require stating that bound. Separately, consider a note for any helix whose pitch diameter exceeds a stated multiple, or for β past a stated bound, whichever reading produced it.

title: The relief law checks that a given input is read, not that it is honoured, and only relieves with just = None
claim: every_input_relief_leaves_given_is_honoured_by_the_solve passes when a nudged input changes any figure. A distance that is read but not reached (with distance_not_reached raised) still counts as honoured. The test only relieves from all-pinned with just = None, which is not how the panel relieves. relief_is_idempotent_from_any_start checks each group's count, which the defects above satisfy.
evidence: All four relief defects above pass the existing suite (679/679 green at HEAD). Probe -d, the stronger form (nudge f, relieve with just = f, require value typed == value solved and no distance or clearance notes), fails 18 of 122.
proposal: Add the law in probe -d's form, and a group-order permutation law (see the relief-architecture finding). Keep the current law as the cheap structural half.
validation: Before the fix, run the new law in a worktree at HEAD and see it fail on the 18 recorded cases; after it, see it pass.

verdict.reason: The law's only assertion is that some figure moved (mod.rs:8009-8012). It starts from settled = pinned.relieved(None) and nudges each given input without relieving again with just = f. A given input that is read but not reached therefore passes. I reproduced the auditor's stronger probe at HEAD: 18 of 122 'pin everything, type one box, relieve with just' cases fail, while the suite passes. The failures are Layshaft and Compound helix/pitch-diameter readings ignored or erroring, distance_not_reached on Layshaft, Planetary, Compound and MeshedPlanets, and the Planocentric clearance. They belong to findings 2-5 and 10, which shows the law does not detect them.
verdict.evidence: Probe bin d (a copy of train-mod-a-d) output: '18 of 122 ... cases fail'. Examples: 'Layshaft: typed Member(2, Helix) = 1.00000, solve came to 0.00000; notes []'; 'Planetary: typed Distance(0) = 21.24528 ... notes [part.distance_not_reached, part.clearance_negative]'; 'Planocentric: typed Clearance(0) = 0.03000, solve came to 0.02000; notes []'. The law's code is at mod.rs:7938-8016.
verdict.proposal_note: 'No distance or clearance notes' is too strict as the pass condition. Some such notes are legitimate physical outcomes and not relief faults. Example: 'Planocentric: typed Member(0, Shift)=0.05 ... notes [part.clearance_negative]', where the tips hold the distance open. State the law as: after relieve(just=f), f's typed value is the solved figure, or a note names both the asked and the reached value. Otherwise it will fail on physics rather than on relief.

title: settle's stated order independence is false, and a walk that does not converge returns silently
claim: The doc says '# Settled, whatever order the groups come in' and that the answer 'never [depends] on the order the toggles happened to be turned in'. Groups share entries, and each fixes itself greedily, so group order decides which entry is relieved. The pass loop is capped at toggles + 1 and returns whatever it holds if it has not converged; no debug_assert or error. The comment at mod.rs:2412, 'The planetary set reaches the second pass: its clearance is alone in its group with none allowed automatic', describes a group that no longer exists. No declaration has automatic_at_most 0; the second pass is reached now only through always_automatic on a crossed mesh's overlap.
evidence: Trace, with a planetary set fully pinned and just = None. In declared order, group 1 relieves D and group 2 then relieves x_p, leaving a valid state. Probe train-mod-a's 'all pinned, D +0.1, just None' shows D and x_p freed, as traced. In reverse order, group 2 relieves x_p first and group 1 is then at 4 ≤ 4 and keeps D, leaving the over-determined state of the relief-architecture finding. The thickness mesh-order probe shows the same kind of dependence directly. grep of automatic_at_most over the crate finds declarations only at shape.rs:4082/4095/4112 and mod.rs:2220/2231, none of them 0.
proposal: Once matching replaces the counts, state the actual invariant: the result depends only on the declared precedence and `just`. Replace the bounded loop with a loop that terminates by construction (each step turns one input and strictly increases the matching, or restores a count), or at least debug_assert!(!moved) after the cap. Delete the stale planetary example.
validation: The group-permutation law; a debug assertion that the walk converged, run under the whole suite.

verdict.reason: Three parts. The code's result depends on group order, and I measured it. The claim that a non-converging walk returns silently is true of the code (no assertion after the bounded loop at mod.rs:2325-2334), but in my runs the walk always converged. The stale planetary comment is confirmed. In a worktree I copied relieved() with the groups reversed and ran it over every preset (plus the hula), from all-pinned, with just = None and each mentioned freedom. The results differ in 173 of 322 cases. In every case the reversed result is itself a fixed point of forward relief, so the relief rules admit more than one settled answer and group order picks one. All 644 walks converged, so the heading's literal claim, 'Settled', holds for reversal; the result is what is not order-independent. 'Never on the order the toggles happened to be turned in' is about toggle history, and I have no evidence against it. The planetary comment at mod.rs:2422-2426 is stale. A Preset::ALL sweep of freedoms() finds groups with given_at_most 0 or automatic_at_most 0 only in Worm and Crossed ([[Overlap(0)]], always_automatic). The planetary clearance sits in distance_and_clearance (automatic_at_most 1 of 2).
verdict.evidence: notes/verify-train-mod-a-2/group_order.txt: 'TOTAL 322 DIFFS 173 NONCONV 0'. Examples: preset 1 just None, 'only rev [Member(0, ThicknessMod)]; rev stable fwd? true'; preset 5 just Distance(0), 'only fwd [Member(1, Shift)], only rev [Member(0, Shift), Member(0, ThicknessMod)]'. Probe bin nine: only 'Worm/Crossed: given<= 0 auto<= 1 order [[Overlap(0)]]'.
verdict.corrected_claim: relieved() always settled in the sweep, but its answer depends on the order in which freedoms() lists the groups. Reversing that order changes which inputs stay given in 173 of 322 all-pinned relief calls, and both answers are fixed points. The doc heading 'Settled, whatever order the groups come in' implies more than holds, and no test permutes the groups. The loop has no convergence assertion. The planetary second-pass example describes a group that no longer exists; only crossed-mesh overlap groups reach that pass among the presets.
verdict.proposal_note: Add a group-permutation law. My probe's relieve_in(rev) is a ten-line harness to start from. Add debug_assert!(converged) after the loop. Replace the planetary example with the crossed-overlap case. Making relief order-independent needs a global rule (matching or a declared precedence across groups). That is finding 2's redesign, not a doc change.

title: Relief clamps Clearance on a distance sized by its tips without releasing it, so a typed clearance is silently replaced (Planocentric)
claim: When an automatic distance is sized by tip room (sized_by = Some), the clearance is a floor, not a figure the solve honours. Relief still leaves Clearance given, and the solve reports the clearance it came to, which differs, with no note. The test suite skips exactly this case (tips_hold → continue).
evidence: Probe -d: Planocentric with everything pinned, Clearance typed 0.03: the solve comes to 0.02 with no notes. The test at mod.rs:7985-8006 excludes this case on purpose.
proposal: When sized_by is Some for a distance, either note the clearance that was overridden (key and values: asked, reached), or have freedoms() turn Clearance(d) automatic through always_automatic while the tips size it. The first keeps relief a pure function of inputs.
validation: Probe -d's Planocentric line passes: either the value is honoured or a note names both numbers.

verdict.reason: Reproduced, but part of the mechanism is misdescribed. On this internal mesh, clearance = nominal − running (sign −1), so a larger clearance shortens the distance until the tips cross. The tips bound the clearance from above: it is a ceiling, not a floor, and the test comment at mod.rs:7986 ('the clearance is a floor the mesh clears') is also wrong on this point. The shipped Planocentric preset already sits exactly at that ceiling (clearance 0.02, sized_by Some(0)). Every clearance typed above 0.02 is discarded and reported as 0.02 with no Note, whether relief used just = None or just = Clearance(0). It is not wholly silent: the panel annotates the distance box 'held open by mesh k' from DistanceReport.sized_by (TrainPanel.svelte:762). The clearance box carries no annotation, and no Note exists for the core's other readers.
verdict.evidence: Probe bin ten, Planocentric all pinned. Typed clearance 0, 0.01 or 0.02 → reached 0, 0.01, 0.02 with sized_by None. Typed 0.025, 0.03, 0.05 or 0.1 → running 1.73418 and clearance 0.02000, sized_by Some(0), notes [], identical for just None and just Clearance(0). The shipped preset's own report is clearance 0.02, sized_by Some(0).
verdict.corrected_claim: On an internal mesh whose distance the tips size, a typed clearance above the tip-limited value is replaced by that value with no Note. The shipped Planocentric preset sits at the limit, so any clearance larger than the default is ignored. The panel annotates only the distance box. The tips cap the clearance; they do not set a floor, and the relief-law test's comment mis-states this.
verdict.proposal_note: Prefer the note: say the asked value and the reached value, since that keeps relief a pure function of inputs. Correct the test comment ('floor' → 'ceiling on this internal mesh'). Once the note exists, drop the tips_hold skip from the relief law in favour of 'honoured or noted'.

title: GearResult repeats params: profile_shift, addendum and helix_angle are bit-identical to params.*, and MemberFacts' reason for them is stale
claim: GearResult::of copies f.params.addendum and f.params.helix_angle into their own fields, and profile_shift comes from MemberFacts, whose doc says it differs from params 'for a hula gear'. The hula stage has been retired and the two now always agree. lead_angle (90 − |β|) and pitch_diameter are one-line functions of params.
evidence: Probe -c over every preset, with the search on and off: max |GearResult.profile_shift − params.profile_shift| = 0, addendum 0, helix 0. Consumers read the duplicates: web/src uses .profile_shift in 9 places and .addendum in 9; gear-cli uses .profile_shift in 40 places.
proposal: Drop GearResult.profile_shift, addendum and helix_angle, plus MemberFacts.profile_shift, and read params.* (the wire type keeps params). Keep pitch_diameter, lead_angle and lead as derived outputs if the panel prefers not to compute them; they are engineering numbers, so rule 1 keeps them in Rust. Regenerate the bindings and update the readers.
validation: check_bindings, npm run check, and check_golden with no numeric diff.

verdict.reason: GearResult::of (mod.rs:1502-1518) copies f.params.addendum and f.params.helix_angle into their own fields. profile_shift comes from MemberFacts.profile_shift, which the only constructor (shape.rs:3780) fills with x[i]. params comes from built.members[i].params(), built through params_at(i, x[i], ...), which sets profile_shift: x (shape.rs:1115-1118). No guard rewrites profile_shift in tooth.rs or gear.rs. The two are therefore equal by construction, and the doc 'for a hula gear is the layout's, not the parameters'' (mod.rs:1469-1470) is stale. Measured difference over every preset, with the search on and off: 0 for all three fields. The consumer counts in the evidence are inflated: grepping web/src outside wire for GearResult's .profile_shift/.helix_angle finds a handful of reads (TrainPanel.svelte:1426 g?.helix_angle, 1509 g?.profile_shift); most hits are input or params fields. This does not change the finding.
verdict.evidence: Probe output: 'max |GearResult.x - params.x| 0e0, addendum 0e0, helix 0e0'. Code at mod.rs:1507-1512 and shape.rs:3780-3781.
verdict.proposal_note: Removing the fields changes the wire and the golden output format (gear-cli prints .profile_shift in about 40 places). Expect check_golden text churn even with no numeric diff, so regenerate with --write only after checking the diff is pure renaming. Keep lead_angle, lead and pitch_diameter in Rust as outputs, per rule 1.

title: Broken intra-doc links in scope, pointing at renamed or deleted items
claim: rustdoc cannot resolve kinematics::System::play (268), ToothOutline::rim_support (740), Loading::for_cases (912; no such function), minimum_profile_shift (1118), TrainError::note (1711), stated_helix (2073; the function is Shape::helix_angles) or always_given (2225; no such function). Reading::helix, a public item, links to the private overlap_notes (2083). check_doc_links.py does not check rustdoc links, so none of these fail a gate.
evidence: Salvaged notes/train-mod-a/cargo_doc.txt and cargo_doc_private.txt, captured at this HEAD (scope.rs is byte-identical): 'warning: unresolved link to `Loading::for_cases` --> crates/gear-core/src/train/mod.rs:912:11', and so on for each.
proposal: Fix each link: crate::kinematics::System::play, crate::strength::ToothOutline::rim_support, delete the for_cases sentence (MemberRating.cases doc), crate::auto path for the minimum shift, crate::note::Explain::note, Shape::helix_angles, and delete the always_given clause. Add RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links' cargo doc --no-deps to CI.
validation: cargo doc with broken_intra_doc_links denied is clean.

verdict.reason: Every cited link is unresolved or crosses into a private item, and no gate checks rustdoc links. The auditor missed one more in the same file (`Port` at mod.rs:2804), and the problem runs crate-wide: 37 broken or private-item links across 17 files.
verdict.evidence: Salvaged notes/train-mod-a/cargo_doc_private.txt was captured in a worktree at HEAD (its worktree-at-crash.diff is empty). It lists unresolved links at mod.rs:268, 740, 912, 1118, 1711, 2073, 2225 and 2804, plus 'public documentation for `helix` links to private item `overlap_notes`' at 2083. I checked the targets by grep. kinematics.rs:462 `pub fn play` exists, but the path is not in scope. strength.rs:505 `rim_support` is a trait method, so it needs the full path. mod.rs:809 `Loading` exists but has no `for_cases`. auto.rs:106 `minimum_profile_shift` exists but needs `crate::auto::`. `note` is `Explain::note` (note.rs:415), which rustdoc cannot reach as `TrainError::note`. There is no `stated_helix`, and the function is shape.rs:802 `helix_angles`. There is no `always_given`. `Port` is not a type: conditions.rs has `Ports` and `PortBody`. Across the crate, `grep -c 'unresolved link|links to private' cargo_doc_private.txt` = 37, spread over auto, contact, gear, mesh, metrology, outline, screw, shaper, strength, tooth and train/{conditions,groupings,mod,offers,pair,shape,wiring}. Neither flake.nix nor .github/workflows/ci.yml runs `cargo doc`.
verdict.corrected_claim: Nine intra-doc links in train/mod.rs are broken: the eight listed plus `Port` at 2804 (the auditor's list stopped at 2225). One more, at 2083, is public-to-private. The crate as a whole has 37, and none is gated.
verdict.proposal_note: Adding `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links -D rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links' cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items` to CI means fixing all 37 links, not just the ones in scope. Also fix `[`Port`]` at mod.rs:2804 (it should probably be `PortBody` or plain text).

title: Much of the prose in scope is the history of retired stage types, not a description of the code
claim: The doc comments repeatedly explain what 'three stage types', 'the spur stage', 'a hula stage' or 'the pair stage' used to do: ContactRatios::of ('written out once per stage type'), Backlash::banded ('written out four times'), MeshReport ('A set's sun_planet/planet_ring and a hula stage's two pairs ... a pair's one mesh is on its own result', which is false now), ContactPatch::line ('an epicyclic set applies ... a pair evaluates each case'), Bending, MemberFacts ('Three stage types built a GearResult'), FreedomGroup ('It was three functions in TypeScript'), and TrainError's Display ('a worm stage needs crossed shafts, and a parallel pair is a spur stage'). Rationale belongs in docs/rationale.md and history in docs/corrections.md, and CLAUDE.md says each thing is said once.
evidence: Read directly at the lines listed. The MeshReport and ContactPatch sentences describe per-stage structure that shape.rs replaced.
proposal: Cut each to what the item is and the invariant it keeps, and move any history not already in docs/corrections.md there by finding number. Rewrite the two Display strings in graph vocabulary.
validation: check_doc_links and a reading pass.

verdict.reason: Two of the cited passages are now false descriptions of the code. The rest are history presented as rationale. Keeping the reasoning next to the code is the project's deliberate style (CLAUDE.md defends the prose-to-code ratio), but paragraphs that only recount how many stage types once repeated something describe code that no longer exists. They also cut against 'each thing said once', since docs/corrections.md already records that history.
verdict.evidence: mod.rs:196-198 (MeshReport) says 'a pair's one mesh is on its own result'. It is not: every mesh, a pair's included, is in `TrainResult.meshes` by graph index (shape.rs:3815ff builds a `LineMesh` per k). mod.rs:411-414 (ContactPatch::line) says 'an epicyclic set applies [the square root] ... a pair evaluates each case and passes one'. The only caller is shape.rs:3832, which passes `scaled[k].1` (shape.rs:3292, the same scaling for every mesh), so no pair or set branch exists. The Display text at mod.rs:1742 ('a worm stage needs crossed shafts, and a parallel pair is a spur stage') uses stage vocabulary, and so does the catalogue's `screw_axes_are_parallel = "a worm stage needs non-parallel shafts"` (strings_en.toml:197). The auditor did not name the catalogue line. `grep -c 'stage type'` counts 16 occurrences in train/mod.rs and 23 in gear-core as a whole.
verdict.corrected_claim: The MeshReport and ContactPatch::line docs describe per-stage structure that no longer exists, and are wrong. The ContactRatios::of, Backlash::banded, MemberFacts and FreedomGroup paragraphs are accurate history whose 'why' could shrink to a single sentence. The stage wording appears both in TrainError's Display and in the catalogue string screw_axes_are_parallel (×5 languages).
verdict.proposal_note: Fix the two false sentences first. Rewrite screw_axes_are_parallel in all five catalogues along with the Display (or delete the Display, per finding 14). Trimming the historical paragraphs is a style call; where one is cut, cite its finding number in docs/corrections.md rather than paraphrasing it.

title: TrainError's Display carries a second English wording of every error, beside the string catalogue
claim: There are about 80 lines of English in gear-core (rule 2) for the CLI and Debug. It repeats the strings_en.toml text, and has already drifted into stage vocabulary. ScrewError's messages are written out here instead of on ScrewError. gear-cli already depends on gear-io, so it could render Explain::note() through the English catalogue.
evidence: mod.rs:1712-1788. docs/rationale.md:60 keeps Display 'for the CLI and for Debug'. The argument is convenience, which a derive(Debug) plus the catalogue in the CLI would cover just as well.
proposal: Have gear-cli print gear_io::strings::render(&e.note(), "en"). Replace the Display impls with a one-line key dump, or remove them and rely on Debug. Then rule 2 holds without an exception.
validation: check_golden: the CLI's error lines change once, in wording only. Record them with --write after review.

verdict.reason: The claim holds and the documented justification is weak. CLAUDE.md states rule 2 without exceptions, but gear-core carries a second English rendering of every TrainError (plus MeshError, MeasurementError and EditRefused). Its wording has already drifted from the catalogue. The CLI already renders notes through `gear_io::strings::Catalogue::english()` and could render errors the same way. One correction to the rationale: 'for Debug' is wrong, because Debug is derived and does not use Display. The real constraint is that `impl std::error::Error` (mod.rs:1790, mesh.rs:780, metrology.rs:759) needs a Display. So Display cannot simply be removed: it can become a one-line key dump.
verdict.evidence: mod.rs:1712-1788 contains 20 `write!` arms of English. The ScrewError texts are written inline there, and screw.rs has no Display for ScrewError, only `note()` with keys (screw.rs:195-201). There is drift: Display says 'a worm stage needs crossed shafts, and a parallel pair is a spur stage', while strings_en.toml:197 says 'a worm stage needs non-parallel shafts'. The CLI prints errors with Display at main.rs:709, 1238, 1630, 1658, 1697, 1742, 1767, 1929, 3186, 3301 and 3337 ('train did not solve: {e}'), but renders notes with `words().render(note)` (main.rs:281-282, 795ff). docs/rationale.md:59-61 reads: 'Their `Display` impls remain, for the CLI and for `Debug`'. Other Display impls with English: mesh.rs:766, metrology.rs:748, edits.rs:171.
verdict.proposal_note: Keep `impl Display`, since `std::error::Error` requires it, but make it `write!(f, "{}", self.note().key)` or key plus values. Switch the CLI's `{e}` sites to `words().render(&e.note())`. Apply the same change to MeshError, MeasurementError and EditRefused so the rule has no exception anywhere. Check that `TrainError::InPart` still renders its cause through the note. Correct docs/rationale.md:59-61. Record the CLI golden diffs with --write, which counts as a write, so only after review.

title: relieved_from rounds a seeded figure to 1e-4 in the core, and so changes the design it pins
claim: `a.manual = (v * 1e4).round() / 1e4` hard-codes the panel's display precision in Rust for every unit: mm, degrees, and dimensionless shift and k. Pinning a box therefore moves the design by up to half a unit in the fourth decimal. A pitch diameter of 17.5997 pinned changes the helix by 6e-5°. The docs call this 'to the digits they saw', but the digits are the panel's choice (num(x, 4)) and are stated a second time here.
evidence: Probe -c: helix 15.0 → 15.000060 after pinning the rounded pd. mod.rs:2362.
proposal: Seed the exact figure. If the panel wants the box to read rounded, it rounds for display, which it already does. Otherwise state the precision once per Freedom next to the unit table and use it from both sides.
validation: Law: relieved_from followed by a solve reproduces every figure to 1e-12 relative.

verdict.reason: The rounding is deliberate and tested (`a_box_relief_pins_is_seeded_from_its_figure` asserts 0.1235). It exists so that a pinned box shows the digits the designer saw. It still has the cost the finding describes, and my probe found a sharper consequence: pinning a box moves a quantity the designer did not touch, and it can carry a design sitting exactly at a limit across that limit. The precision is also written twice. TrainPanel.svelte:1814 shows an auto figure as `Number(computed.toFixed(4))` and the core rounds with `(v * 1e4).round() / 1e4`, so if either changes they silently disagree. The rounding is an absolute 1e-4 for every unit, mm, degrees, and dimensionless shift or k alike.
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-train-mod-a-3 runs every preset and every toggle. It flips the toggle, calls `relieved_from`, and compares the solve against the same shape with the pinned inputs seeded exactly. Out of 39 pins, touching Clearance pins Distance. On Spur the clearance the designer had moves from 0.0200000 to 0.0200475, and the mesh's minimum backlash goes from -2.2e-14 (exactly zero: running clearance equal to the tolerance) to 0.000233. On Compound the pinned distance 20.999928 → 20.9999 moves the clearance to 0.0199719, and the minimum backlash goes from 0.0 to -9.70e-5, a sign change (binding at the tolerance end). On Worm the clearance moves by 0.2%. On Crossed the path backlash moves by 3.4e-4 relative. No note fired or vanished in any of these cases (note sets were identical), so the sign change passes silently.
verdict.proposal_note: The finding says 'the panel rounds for display, which it already does'. That is inaccurate. TrainPanel.svelte:1814 shows a *given* box's `a.manual` raw (`computed === undefined ? a.manual : ...`) and rounds only computed figures, so seeding exactly would make pinned boxes show 15 digits unless the panel also rounds given values for display. There are two clean options. (a) Seed the exact figure in the core and have the panel format every box, given or automatic, with one display precision. (b) Keep rounding for what-you-see-is-what-you-get, but move it to the one place that defines the display precision: the panel rounds the figures before sending them, or the core exports the constant. Option (a) meets the owner's 'pinning changes nothing' ideal and needs a law: relieved_from followed by a solve reproduces every figure to about 1e-12 relative. The existing test's 0.1235 assertion would then change to the exact value.

title: Backlash::banded's nominal-as-candidate reasoning is sound, but the per-member band's own minimum can sit below the nominal on both sides without saying so
claim: The three-point min/max is correct for a per-mesh band, including a shared distance where the sun mesh and ring mesh cancel (planetary reports 0.04172 at all three points, which matches). Its doc then argues about the path-level stationary case, which banded no longer serves: the path is built from row_play. Once the path uses per-distance extremes (first finding), banded is only the per-mesh band, and the planetary paragraph belongs to the path.
evidence: Probe -b: Planetary reported and recomputed [0.04172, 0.04172, 0.04172]. Wolfrom, Compound and Planocentric rows fall (internal) and are ordered correctly by the min/max.
proposal: Once the path construction is fixed, move the 'set carries one of each' paragraph to backlash_at, and keep banded's doc to the per-mesh rule.
validation: Documentation only.

verdict.reason: The premise is wrong. `Backlash::banded` still serves the path: `backlash_at` (mod.rs:3467-3483) calls `Backlash::banded(0.0, 1.0, 1.0, |t| ...)` to sum `coefficient(k, read, from) * row_play[k][band]` over every mesh. That is exactly the 'set that carries one of each, referred to one body' case the paragraph describes. The paragraph is therefore where it belongs, and moving it to backlash_at would separate the argument for why the nominal is a candidate from the function that takes all three points. The title's 'without saying so' is also wrong: the doc says outright that 'both ends of the band sit *below* the nominal' and that 'the nominal is therefore a candidate for either end'. For the per-member use (shape.rs:3560-3572, one mesh, its own distance) play is monotone in distance, so the per-member band cannot sit below the nominal on both sides at all.
verdict.evidence: mod.rs:3467 `let backlash_at = |read: Body, from: Body| -> Backlash { Backlash::banded(0.0, 1.0, 1.0, |t| { let band = if t < 0.0 {0} else if t > 0.0 {2} else {1}; row_play.iter().enumerate().map(|(k, play)| coefficient(k, read, from) * play[band]).sum::<f64>().to_degrees() }) }`. Per-member use: shape.rs:3567 `super::Backlash::banded(built.meshes[k].running, tolerance_minus, tolerance_plus, |a| (play_of(k, a) / z).to_degrees())`, which covers a single mesh.
verdict.proposal_note: There is a real, smaller point nearby (see missed): backlash_at pushes three precomputed values through banded's distance arithmetic by passing a fake nominal of 0 and a fake band of ±1, then decoding the sign of t back into an index.

title: No-shape gear inputs panic or produce huge outputs instead of being refused (rule 5)
claim: Neither gear-core nor the wasm boundary checks GearParams for inputs that describe no shape. teeth 0, module 0, module NaN, thickness_mod NaN, profile_shift NaN, and pressure_angle exactly 0 panic in Gear::profile ('range start index 1 out of range for slice of length 0'). A panic in wasm is a trap. Meanwhile solve_gear returns Ok and export_dxf returns a 15.6 MB drawing (pressure angle 90: 20.6 MB). module -1 and helix 90° are accepted as geometry: helix 90 gives a tip radius of 1.4e17 mm. The only gate is the TypeScript validate() against Rust-supplied bounds, which rule 5 does not count as the core refusing.
evidence: Ran the existing probe binaries /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probe-target/release/probe_primitives (mode guards, Tooth::new then Gear::new(..).profile(50)) and probe_primitives_wasm (all three wasm entry points). Results: 'module 0: PANIC', 'teeth 0: PANIC', 'pa 0: PANIC', 'k NaN: PANIC', 'x NaN: PANIC', 'module NaN: PANIC'. wasm: 'module 0 gear_profile PANIC', 'module 0 export_dxf ok len 15601615', 'pa 0 export_dxf ok len 15601615', 'pa 90 export_dxf ok len 20617731', 'helix 90: ... ra 1.388e17'. resolved_params (lib.rs:656) returns req.params unchecked. pa 0 with k=1 fails because thickness_shift computes π·0/(4·tan 0) = 0/0 = NaN.
proposal: Add GearParams::check(&self) -> Result<(), Note> in params.rs. It refuses the no-shape conditions docs/reference.md#input-ranges already states: module ≤ 0 or non-finite; teeth == 0; |β| ≥ 90°; pressure angle ≤ 0 or ≥ 90° or non-finite; k outside (0,2) or non-finite; any non-finite shift, addendum, dedendum or root radius. Each gets an error.* key. Call it at the top of Tooth::new, Gear::new (or make them return Result), and in the wasm resolved_params, so that every entry point (solve_gear, gear_profile, export_dxf, and train members through the shape) refuses the same way. Reuse the Bound values from auto::ranges_at_shift, so the bounds are still written in one place.
validation: A law test sweeping each field to 0, a negative value, NaN, ±inf and its open bound: every entry point returns Err with a catalogue key and never panics. check_wasm.sh probes for gear_profile and export_dxf with module 0 and teeth 0. The strings test covers the new keys.

verdict.reason: Reproduced with my own probe (probes/verify-primitives-a, mode guards). On the single-gear path (Tooth::new, Gear::new(..).profile, gear_io::gear_to_dxf, and so the wasm solve_gear/gear_profile/export_dxf and gear-cli show/dxf), nothing refuses an input that describes no shape. This contradicts rationale.md#clamp-rather-than-refuse-and-say-so, which names 'a module of zero' as refused. Two corrections to scope. (1) The train path does refuse these inputs, though for misleading reasons: for a pair([17,43]), module 0 and module -1 give InPart{NoContact} ('the teeth never contact'), pa 0 and pa 90 give Mesh(OutsideInvoluteDomain), and teeth 0 gives Wiring(MemberWithoutTeeth). (2) Reach is limited. GearPanel.onInput writes tab.params only when validate() passes, so the gear panel never sends an out-of-bound value. JSON cannot carry NaN or inf, so the non-finite cases reach only direct Rust callers, the CLI and TOML documents (TOML does allow nan and inf).
verdict.evidence: Probe output (notes/verify-primitives-a/guards.txt): 'module 0: profile PANIC' / 'dxf ok len 15601615'; 'module NaN: profile PANIC'; 'teeth 0: profile PANIC' / 'dxf ok len 920765'; 'pa 0: ... st=NaN ... profile PANIC' / 'dxf 15601615'; 'k NaN', 'x NaN': profile PANIC; 'pa 90: dxf ok len 20617731'; 'helix 90: ra=1.388155e17'; 'module -1: ra=-7.987387e0 ... clamp.tip_capped_pointed radius -11.0197'. The panic site is gear.rs:564 `r_full.extend_from_slice(&r[1..])` on an empty half-profile ('range start index 1 out of range for slice of length 0'). `gear-cli show 0` panics at crates/gear-core/src/gear.rs:564:44. wasm resolved_params (lib.rs:656) returns req.params unchecked. Train probe (notes/verify-primitives-a/train.txt): 'train module 0: Err InPart { part: 0, cause: NoContact }', 'train pa 0: Err ... OutsideInvoluteDomain', 'train teeth 0: Err ... MemberWithoutTeeth(0)'.
verdict.proposal_note: Making Tooth::new and Gear::new return Result touches hundreds of call sites and tests. A lighter route reaches the same guarantee: (a) add GearParams::check(&self) -> Result<(), Note>, built from auto::ranges_at_shift's invariant Bounds, and call it at every boundary: wasm resolved_params, gear-cli argument parsing, gear-io document load, and Shape's member validation, so that a train refuses module 0 with that key rather than 'no contact'; (b) make Gear::profile return an empty outline instead of panicking when a half-profile is empty. Note also that the bound 0 < α < 90° is not where 'no shape' begins: every α above arctan(π/(4 h_f)) (32.1° at h_f = 1.25) already produces a self-intersecting outline (see missed). A check limited to the documented bounds would leave that region admitted.

title: thickness_shift uses the unguarded pressure angle while the geometry uses the guarded one
claim: The tooth guard raises the pressure angle to 0.5° (tooth.rs:402), but transverse_thickness takes x_s from params.thickness_shift(), which reads the raw params.pressure_angle, and multiplies it by the guarded tan α. The thickness modification is therefore mis-scaled for 0 < α < 0.5°, and NaN at exactly α = 0 with k = 1. The UI accepts 0 < α (the bound is open), so 0.3° is a legal input. auto::ranges_at_shift repeats the same mix, so the bounds the UI shows are affected too.
evidence: tooth.rs:833-834: `let x_thick = params.profile_shift + params.thickness_shift(); let mut st = m * (PI / 2.0 + 2.0 * x_thick * an.tan()) / beta.cos();` where `an` is the guarded angle. params.rs:105: `let an = self.pressure_angle.to_radians();`, unguarded. Worked example at α = 0.3°, k = 0.9: x_s(0.3°) = −0.314/(4·0.005236) = −15.0 against −9.0 at the guarded 0.5°. That gives s = π/2 + 2·(−15.0)·tan 0.5° = 1.309 m instead of the intended k·π/2 = 1.414 m, 7.4% thin.
proposal: Give thickness_shift the angle it is to be used with: `pub fn thickness_shift_at(&self, alpha_n: f64) -> f64`. Better, move the pressure-angle guard into params.rs as `fn guarded_normal_pressure_angle(&self) -> (f64, Option<Note>)` and have thickness_shift, Tooth, tool_wanted_by and the three copies in auto.rs all call it (see the separate finding on the five copies).
validation: A test: for α in {0.1°, 0.3°, 0.49°} and k in {0.9, 1.1}, the generated rack thickness equals k·π/2·m at the guarded angle. Plus α = 0, k = 1 no longer produces NaN.

verdict.reason: transverse_thickness (tooth.rs:833-834) takes x_s from params.thickness_shift(), which uses the raw pressure angle (params.rs:104-106), and multiplies it by the guarded tan α_n. Below 0.5°, the tooth's thickness modification is therefore not k·πm/2. The UI admits 0 < α < 0.5° because the bound is open at 0. The same mix appears in auto.rs:308 (admissible_profile_shift) and auto.rs:678 (ranges_at_shift), and in Mesh::new (mesh.rs:270-276: x_thick from the raw angle, g1.alpha_n guarded). So the tooth, its mesh and its bounds are consistently wrong together rather than inconsistent with each other. At α = 0 exactly with k = 1, x_s = 0/0 = NaN.
verdict.evidence: Probe mode thickness (z = 40, x = 0, m = 1, target k·π/2): 'pa 0.3 k 0.9: st/m = 1.308993 want 1.413717 rel err -7.408e-2' (matches the auditor's -7.4%); 'pa 0.1 k 0.9: rel err -4.445e-1'; 'pa 0.1 k 1.1: +3.636e-1'; 'pa 0.49 k 0.9: -2.268e-3'; 'pa 0.5 and above: rel err +0.000e0'. 'pa 0: ... st=NaN' in guards.txt.
verdict.proposal_note: The single guarded-angle accessor in params.rs is the right fix. Every reader of thickness_shift (tooth.rs:833, auto.rs:308/678, mesh.rs:746, gear.rs:922/936, ring.rs:244/1032, shape.rs:522/1175/1359) must switch together, or the mesh's inv α_w relation and the tooth stop agreeing. ring.rs:218 applies no pressure-angle guard at all, so a ring and pinion below 0.5° would then sit at different angles. Decide whether the ring takes the guard too.

title: Two guards fire without a note, contradicting the Clamps contract
claim: params.rs:188 promises that every guard that fires appends a note. Two do not. The tip-above-base-circle floor (`ra.max(rb*(1+TIP_ABOVE_BASE_FRACTION))`) and the fillet floor (`rho.max(MIN_FILLET_MODULES*m)`) change the geometry silently. The fillet floor also swallows a NaN root radius, because f64::max ignores NaN.
evidence: Probe mode guards, Tooth::new: 'addendum -5: ([], ..., ra 7.9873872846676095, ..., rb 7.987387276680222)'. The tip was forced to rb·(1+1e-9) and no note was pushed. 'root_radius -1: ([] ...)' and 'root_radius NaN: ([] ...)': the round was floored to 1e-9·m, again with no note.
proposal: Push notes at both sites: a clamp.tip_raised_to_base key (new) and clamp.fillet_raised (new), or refuse, once the check from the first finding exists, since a negative or NaN radius and a tip below the root describe no shape. Also fix params.rs:189, which still says 'human-readable note'; notes are keys now.
validation: Extend the strings 'fire every note' test to both keys. A property test: whenever Tooth's ra or tip_round differs from the value computed from the inputs, clamps.any() is true.

verdict.reason: Both floors change the geometry with no note, against the Clamps doc at params.rs:185-189, which also still says 'human-readable note'. The tip floor is not a tolerance that no design is near. When the addendum puts the tip below the base circle, `ra.max(rb*(1+1e-9))` (tooth.rs:471) moves the tip by millimetres without a word. The fillet floor (tooth.rs:922/925) also absorbs a negative or NaN root radius, because the `rho > rho_cap` comparison is false for NaN and f64::max drops NaN.
verdict.evidence: Probe guards.txt: 'addendum -5: Tooth ok ra=7.987387e0 rb=7.987387e0 ... clamps=[]' (asked tip r + m(-5) = 3.5 mm, delivered 7.99 mm). 'root_radius -1: rho=1.000000e-9 ... clamps=[]'. 'root_radius NaN: rho=1.000000e-9 ... clamps=[]'.
verdict.proposal_note: Do not note the fillet floor when the asked root radius is exactly 0. A sharp rack is a legal input with its own threshold (ShiftRange::sharp_rack_undercut), and flooring 0 to 1e-9·m is the degeneracy tolerance the guard doc describes. The proposed property test ('whenever tip_round differs from the input, clamps.any()') would therefore force a note onto every sharp-rack gear. Compare against the floor instead. Refuse a negative or non-finite root radius, or a tip below the root circle, through finding 0's check. Note a tip raised from between the root and base circles as a clamp.

title: Ratio::checked_add overflows i128 long before the answer does
claim: checked_add forms n1·d2 + n2·d1 over d1·d2 without first cancelling gcd(d1,d2). In the kinematics elimination, the train is refused with Overflow when its exact ratio needs only about 51–67 bits of 127. Henrici's gcd-first addition, which gives the same unique normalised result, moves the refusal out to where the answer itself approaches 127 bits. cmp_checked has the same pattern.
evidence: Probe probe_primitives mode overflow builds a chain of n compound meshes through kinematics::System::motion with the current code. 'primes~60-400: n=10 refused Overflow; exact answer needs 66.5/67.3 bits'. '17/43 repeated: n=14 refused; 57.2/76.0 bits'. 'small primes 11..: n=11 refused; 51.4/75.0 bits'. The same probe against the saved worktree with Henrici addition (worktree-at-crash2.diff, ratio.rs), run as release/probe_primitives_wt: 'primes: n=17 refused; exact answer needs 119.6/120.8 bits', '17/43: n=24; 98.1/130.2 bits', and 'small primes' solved all 29 stages. RATIO_NAIVE=1 on the same binary reproduces the n=10/14/11 refusals.
proposal: Replace checked_add with Henrici's form: `let g = gcd(self.den, other.den); let (d1, d2) = (self.den / g, other.den / g); let t = self.num.checked_mul(d2)?.checked_add(other.num.checked_mul(d1)?)?; let g2 = gcd(t, g); Self::new(t / g2, (self.den / g2).checked_mul(d2)?)` (g2 ≥ 1, since g ≥ 1). In cmp_checked, compare num1·(d2/g) with num2·(d1/g). Results are bit-identical, because Ratio is normalised and unique.
validation: A property test over random reduced fractions: Henrici add equals the naive add wherever the naive one succeeds. The overflow probe as a test: a chain of k prime-count meshes solves whenever the product of its tooth counts fits in 126 bits. cargo nextest and check_golden unchanged.

verdict.reason: Reproduced independently, and the fix checked in a worktree. checked_add (ratio.rs:136-140) multiplies whole denominators. The kinematics elimination therefore refuses with Overflow when the exact answer needs 51 to 67 bits. Henrici's gcd-first form moves every refusal out to where the answer is near 127 bits. The suite also enshrines the spurious refusal. train::tests::a_conflict_a_missing_shaft_and_an_overflow_are_each_named (train/mod.rs:7730-7746) builds six pairs with teeth (4e9+k, 4e9+1+k). Their ratio telescopes to 4e9/(4e9+6) = 2e9/(2e9+3), a 31-bit answer, yet the test asserts TrainError::Overflow and its doc calls these 'tooth counts whose product outgrows an exact ratio'. With Henrici addition that train solves and the test fails. The auditor's validation claim that 'cargo nextest [is] unchanged' is therefore wrong. Severity stays medium: power trains rarely reach 10 stages, but prime-count multi-stage trains (orreries, clock trains) do, and the refusal is labelled as the answer being too big when it is not.
verdict.evidence: Probe mode overflow, current code: 'primes: n=10 REFUSED Overflow; exact answer needs 66.5/67.3 bits'; '17/43: n=14 REFUSED; 57.2/76.0'; 'small primes: n=11 REFUSED; 51.4/75.0'; '17/53,19/61,23/47: n=13 REFUSED; 55.5/74.6'; 'add 1/2^64 + 1/(3*2^63): None (exact = 5/(3*2^64), fits)'. Worktree with Henrici checked_add, same probe: primes n=17 (119.6/120.8 bits), 17/43 n=24 (98.1/130.2), mixed n=22 (94.1/126.2), small primes all 30 solved, 1/2^64 + 1/(3·2^63) = Some(5/55340232221128654848). The gear-core nextest run on that worktree: 602/604 passed. Failures: a_conflict_a_missing_shaft_and_an_overflow_are_each_named ('left: None, right: Some(Overflow)' at train/mod.rs:7746), plus the known wall-clock test every_search_is_quick_enough_to_type_over.
verdict.proposal_note: Apply the Henrici form as proposed. In the same change, rewrite the overflow test so its answer genuinely needs more than 127 bits: distinct large primes that do not telescope, for example six pairs of distinct primes near 4e9. Correct its doc comment. Otherwise the gate keeps asserting the artefact. cmp_checked has no production caller (only its own test), so delete it rather than fix it (see missed).

title: Tol's 'relative' tolerance is absolute for every |x| < 2.25, and the two solvers read x_tol differently
claim: The Tol doc says the relative term 2ε|x| makes 'the same settings mean the same thing on a root of 1e-3 and one of 1e+3'. With the default x_tol = 1e-15, the absolute floor exceeds 2ε|x| wherever |x| < 1e-15/(2·2.2e-16) ≈ 2.25. That covers every angle in radians, every roll parameter below 2.25, and the dimensionless travel coordinates. A root of 1e-3 is therefore held to about 5e-13 relative, a root of 1e3 to 4.4e-16. The floor is also used differently: Brent stops on half the bracket ≤ 0.5·x_tol + 2ε|b| (bracket ≤ x_tol + 4ε|b|), Newton on step < x_tol + 2ε|x|. Finally, the Tol parameter is varied at exactly one of 26 call sites, hertz.rs:433 with an unexplained 1e-14 in ln κ.
evidence: solve.rs:87 `let tol1 = 2.0 * f64::EPSILON * b.abs() + 0.5 * tol.x_tol;` against solve.rs:191 `step.abs() < 2.0 * f64::EPSILON * x.abs() + tol.x_tol`. grep for 'Tol {' and 'Tol::default' across crates: every production site passes Tol::default() except hertz.rs:433-436 (x_tol 1e-14). Logged real solves (sum_cli.txt) show the effect: returned roots up to 296 ulp from the f64 sign crossing at tooth.rs:630 and 213 at ring.rs:545. Harmless physically (under 1e-13 mm), but not what the doc says.
proposal: Make the floor scale-free and the same in both solvers. Drop the Tol struct and parameter, and use tol1 = 2ε·|x| + ε·max(|lo|,|hi|)·2^-? , or simply 4ε·max(|b|, bracket_scale), where bracket_scale = max(|lo|,|hi|). That keeps termination at a root of exactly 0 and removes the unit dependence. Keep MAX_ITER as a private const. If hertz genuinely needs 1e-14, say why in hertz.rs; otherwise it takes the default. Rewrite the Tol doc to state the rule actually implemented.
validation: The existing a_large_root_converges test, extended to scale 1e-6 with the assertion that the relative error is < 8ε at every scale (it currently passes only because its threshold is 1e-14). The solver-site log (the brent/newton wrapper from worktree-at-crash.diff) re-run: max ulps-to-crossing ≤ 4 at every site. check_golden: expect a few last-digit moves; the diff is the question.

verdict.reason: The Tol doc (solve.rs:18-23) and reference.md#root-finding say the relative term makes the settings 'mean the same thing' at every magnitude. With x_tol = 1e-15, the absolute floor dominates 2ε|x| for |x| < 2.25. Brent's stopping bracket is x_tol + 4ε|b| (tol1 = 2ε|b| + 0.5 x_tol against half the bracket). Newton's is step < x_tol + 2ε|x|, the usual NR zbrent/rtsafe conventions. For Brent the effect is larger than the auditor states: on (x/r)^3 - 1 its returned root has relative error 1.8e-7 at r = 1e-9 and 1.4e-10 at r = 1e-6. Newton stays within 1 ulp because its final error is far below its last step. hertz.rs:433 is the only production site with a non-default Tol (1e-14), and nothing says why 1e-14. The physical effect at the crate's actual root magnitudes is negligible (≤ 1e-15 absolute), so this is a documentation fault.
verdict.evidence: Probe mode tol: 'r=1e-9: brent rel err 1.78e-7 (860334265 ulp) newton rel err 2.07e-16 (1 ulp) | brent stop width/r 1.00e-6'; 'r=1e-6: brent rel err 1.42e-10'; 'r=1e-3 ... r=1e6: 0 ulp both'. solve.rs:87 `let tol1 = 2.0 * f64::EPSILON * b.abs() + 0.5 * tol.x_tol;` against solve.rs:191 `step.abs() < 2.0 * f64::EPSILON * x.abs() + tol.x_tol`. grep 'Tol {' finds only solve.rs:267 (test) and hertz.rs:433.
verdict.proposal_note: The suggested floor, 4ε·max(|b|, max(|lo|,|hi|)), is not scale-free in the useful sense and loosens many current solves. A small root in a wide bracket, for example the pointed-tooth roll on [0, POINTED_TOOTH_MAX_ROLL = 50] with a root near 0.3, would stop at 4.4e-14 instead of about 1.1e-15, some 40 times looser. Better options: (a) keep the solver and correct the doc to state the rule actually implemented (a 1e-15 absolute floor, relative above |x| ≈ 2.25), or (b) have each site pass its variable's natural scale (module for a length, 1 for an angle) as x_tol = ε·scale. Give hertz a one-line reason for 1e-14 or the default. Keep max_iter settable, because the exhaustion test (solve.rs:267, 'stingy') depends on it.

title: brent/newton_bracketed return None for 'no root' and for 'failed' alike, and callers turn it into a value
claim: The module promises that a failed solve makes 'the caller report the geometry as impossible'. In practice the one None covers three different outcomes: not bracketed, a non-finite f mid-solve, and iterations exhausted. strength.rs uses brent as a test for whether a root exists (92% of calls at :735 are unbracketed on purpose), so a NaN failure on the flank would silently drop that candidate from the form factor. shaper.rs:450 `.unwrap_or(floor)` and ring.rs:568 `.unwrap_or(0.0)` turn a failed solve into a number, which is exactly the best effort the module says never happens.
evidence: Outcome counts from the instrumented run (sum_cli.txt): strength.rs:735 {'unbracketed': 3981, 'end_zero': 337, 'tol': 31, 'zero': 1}; ring.rs:545 {'unbracketed': 272}; shape.rs:1490 {'unbracketed': 67}; screw.rs:1230 {'unbracketed': 24}. Code: shaper.rs:450 `brent(angle_at, floor, p.cutter_tip_radius, Tol::default()).unwrap_or(floor)`; ring.rs:568 `brent(over, s_j, 0.0, Tol::default()).unwrap_or(0.0)`.
proposal: Return `Result<f64, SolveError>` with `enum SolveError { NotBracketed, NonFinite, Exhausted }`. Callers that ask whether a root exists match NotBracketed and propagate the other two. The two unwrap_or sites should either prove that the fallback is the limit value (and say so in a comment) or propagate. Migration: add brent_checked/newton_checked returning Result, move the 26 sites over one file at a time, then delete the Option versions.
validation: A test per error variant (the existing exhaustion and unbracketed tests, plus a NaN in the interior). A mutation check: make strength.rs's flank condition return NaN at one interior point and confirm the new API surfaces an error where today the rating silently changes.

verdict.reason: The API conflation is real, and the module doc's line that a failed solve makes 'the caller report the geometry as impossible' (solve.rs:9-14) is contradicted by callers that map None to a value. There are more of them than the auditor lists: shaper.rs:450, ring.rs:568, tooth.rs:601-604, 626-629 and 689-697. No wrong answer is demonstrated, though, and the non-bracket arms are practically unreachable with finite inputs. The auditor's own log of more than a million real solves (sum_cli.txt) records only 'tol', 'zero', 'end_zero' and 'unbracketed', never a non-finite or exhausted outcome. Bisection fallback makes 200 iterations unreachable in f64. shaper.rs:450 is bracketed by construction (angle_at(floor) ≥ 0 is checked first, and angle_at(tip radius) = -1), so its unwrap_or(floor) fires only on NaN input. ring.rs:566-568 is never reached by the suite (it is uncovered in uncovered_lines.txt, and it is the path of the known UNFIRED clamp.ring_fully_filleted). A NaN mid-solve comes only from non-finite inputs, which is finding 0's domain.
verdict.evidence: sum_cli.txt outcome columns: strength.rs:735 {'unbracketed': 3981, 'end_zero': 337, 'tol': 31, 'zero': 1}, shaper.rs:450 {'tol': 4142, 'zero': 37}, no site with a non-finite or exhausted outcome. Coverage: 'crates/gear-core/src/ring.rs: ... 566-568' uncovered. solve.rs:54/128/152/196 return None on non-finite f, the same value as not bracketed (solve.rs:64).
verdict.corrected_claim: brent and newton_bracketed return one None for not-bracketed, non-finite and exhausted, and five call sites turn None into a fallback value, which contradicts the solve.rs module doc. With finite inputs, though, only 'not bracketed' is reachable, and none of the fallbacks has been shown to produce a wrong answer.
verdict.proposal_note: Migrating 26 sites to Result<f64, SolveError> costs M for a hypothetical gain. Cheaper and sufficient: close finding 0, so non-finite residuals cannot arise from inputs. Rewrite the solve.rs doc to say None means 'no root in the bracket, or the residual was not finite'. At each fallback site add a one-line comment giving the limit the fallback stands for (shaper.rs:450: bracketed by construction; tooth.rs:689: monotone θ). If a typed error is wanted, it earns its place only at strength.rs:725/735, where 'no tangency on this curve' is the signal.

title: The solve inventory and inverse-involute docs are stale: 26 solver sites not ten, #2 is Brent, the bare scheme diverges at 74° not 60°
claim: (a) rationale.md claims 'Ten scalar solves ... none with a tuning parameter'. Production code has 26 brent/newton call sites (gear.rs:1137; tooth.rs:456,604,630,689,708; shaper.rs:450; ring.rs:545,568; involute.rs:63; hertz.rs:429; auto.rs:146,366,744,755,842; strength.rs:688,725,735; contact.rs:534; shape.rs:860,959,1490,1695; screw.rs:454,1230), plus two fixed-count bisections (metrology.rs:200, gear.rs:1119). Several carry tuning literals (hertz 1e-14; bracket-growth factors 1.4, 1.5, 2; caps 40/60/64/80; shape.rs:860's 89°). (b) Row #2, 'Tip radius for a given tip width — Newton, analytic ds/dr', is two Brent solves in auto.rs:744-755. (c) solve.rs:6, involute.rs:48, reference.md:30 and corrections.md:423 say seed+Newton 'reaches machine precision in two to four steps up to roughly 60° but diverges above it'. Measured, it takes 5 steps at 50–60° and converges up to 72° (9 steps), leaving the domain from 74°. involute.rs:97's own test comment says 75°.
evidence: grep 'brent(\|newton_bracketed(' over crates/gear-core/src with test-module line numbers checked (strength tests from 1914, auto from 1932, shape from 4192, screw from 1496, gear from 1146). notes/primitives/newton_div.py (plain Python, the crate's seed): '50 5 steps', '60 5 steps', '65 6', '70 7', '72 9 steps', '74 left domain at step 1 (x=1.69)', '75 left domain', '80 left domain'.
proposal: Regenerate the rationale table from the call sites: one row per purpose, the method, and any literal the site carries. Better, have tools/ list solver call sites and check_doc_links (or a new check) fail when the count drifts. Correct the divergence sentence to 'five steps to 60°, and leaves the domain from about 74°' everywhere, or drop it in favour of the test that holds it.
validation: check_figures, with the new numbers tagged to a gear-cli or test output. A grep-based count check in tools/.

verdict.reason: All three parts hold. (a) The inventory is out of date and its 'none with a tuning parameter' is false. (b) Row #2 is Brent, not Newton. (c) The bare seed+Newton scheme converges up to 73.2°, not 60°. One detail is off: the auditor's '5 steps at 50–60°' counts the step that only confirms convergence. Counted to within 2 ulp it is 3 steps at 20–40° and 4 at 50–60°, so the docs' 'two to four steps' is roughly right on the count and wrong only about where the scheme diverges.
verdict.evidence: grep 'brent(\|newton_bracketed(' over gear-core/src (solve.rs excluded) gives 26 production sites, all above each file's test module: tooth.rs 456,604,630,689,708; involute.rs 63; gear.rs 1137; shaper.rs 450; strength.rs 688,725,735; screw.rs 454,1230; ring.rs 545,568; auto.rs 146,366,744,755,842; hertz.rs 429; contact.rs 534; shape.rs 860,959,1490,1695. Among the purposes not in the rationale table are the pointed-tooth roll, the eccentric amplitude, the shaper round boundary, the pointed shift, the round ceiling, the screw turning point, locking friction, efficient_split, the helix for a target distance and tip room.
