title: Search constants and tolerances with no stated origin, and one 'at the floor' tolerance written three ways
claim: Search::SHIPPED scan=12 and starts=2 carry no rationale. resolution, budget and first_step do. The sizing rounds cap of 3 and the 'moved' test `resolution * 1e-3` are unexplained. 'The shift is at its floor' uses 1e-12 in member_is_buildable and in the shifts_for_efficiency pre-filter, while the tooth's undercut flag uses compat::SAME_SHIFT = 1e-9. shape.rs:1700 uses `e + 1e-9` and train/mod.rs:1254 `asked - 1e-12`.
evidence: Read at the cited lines; params.rs:292-304 defines SAME_RACK/SAME_SHIFT = 1e-9 as the crate's named tolerance for this question.
proposal: Use compat::SAME_SHIFT everywhere a shift is compared with a floor. Derive scan from resolution and the box, e.g. the smallest scan whose spacing is below the narrowest constraint feature, or document it as a measured trade-off with the sweep that set it. Replace the rounds cap by a convergence condition (held distance moved < resolution) plus a guard, and state the guard.
validation: cargo nextest run; check_golden unchanged, or a diff that is explained.

verdict.reason: Some of the sub-claims hold and some do not, and the headline ('one at-the-floor tolerance written three ways') mixes three different questions. (a) Neither scan=12 nor starts=2 has a reason for its value in its field doc. But the struct doc (auto.rs:1623-1636) calls all five fields effort parameters that are 'gated rather than tuned', and the_search_is_converged_not_budgeted (train/mod.rs:5608) runs Search::refined(3), which scales scan and starts. So there is a stated origin: the gate. What is really wrong with scan is that it decides feasibility, which contradicts the struct doc's 'raising any of them may only sharpen an answer'. That is the auditor's finding 0, not this one. (b) The rounds cap of 3 does have an explanation, at shape.rs:1872-1874: 'Three at most; the second usually moves nothing and the third never has'. It is empirical, and reaching the cap is silent. (c) The 'moved' test (shape.rs:1914) is unexplained, and its units do not match: it compares held running distances in mm against search.resolution*1e-3, where resolution is in modules of shift. (d) The 1e-12 at auto.rs:1021 is a real literal beside compat::SAME_SHIFT=1e-9. For an Absorbed member the floor is minimum_profile_shift(...).with_cutter_radius (pair.rs:117), which is the same x_min that Tooth::undercut reads (tooth.rs:479-481). So the same question is asked at two tolerances, and the tighter one wins. I found no reachable case where they disagree. The auto.rs:1507 site is inside shifts_for_efficiency, which only tests call (callers at auto.rs:2764/2850/2876 and train/mod.rs:5253/5279 are all in test modules). (e) shape.rs:1700 `e + 1e-9` is not a shift floor. It leans an axis distance in mm. Its comment, 'by the solver's own tolerance', is false: brent's tolerance is 2ε|b| + 0.5·x_tol (solve.rs:88, x_tol=1e-15 at solve.rs:38), about 1e-14 mm at 40 mm (also reported as lens-magic-numbers #14). (f) train/mod.rs:1254 `asked - 1e-12` is the flag for a clamped addendum, not a shift floor; a test repeats it at train/mod.rs:9687. This overlaps lens-magic-numbers #9 and shape-a #11.
verdict.evidence: I read auto.rs:1657-1721 (Search fields and docs), shape.rs:1867-1920 (rounds loop), solve.rs:35-42 and 88-90 (brent tolerance), pair.rs:106-119, tooth.rs:479-481, params.rs:292-304 and train/mod.rs:1237-1257. I checked callers with grep: shifts_for_efficiency has no production caller, and the gear-cli comment at main.rs:1542 saying it is 'the only command that drives' it is itself stale, since shifts_report builds arr::pair and solves the shape.
verdict.corrected_claim: Several literals in the search and sizing code have no stated origin. The rounds loop's 'moved' tolerance `search.resolution * 1e-3` (shape.rs:1914) compares mm against a shift resolution in modules. The 1e-9 lean at shape.rs:1700 is described as 'the solver's own tolerance', but brent's is about 1e-14. member_is_buildable (auto.rs:1021) uses 1e-12 where Tooth::undercut uses compat::SAME_SHIFT for the same x_min comparison on absorbed members; the effect is cosmetic, and no misfire is reachable. scan=12 and starts=2 are justified only by the convergence gate, and the field docs should say so. The rounds cap is explained, but it fires silently.
verdict.proposal_note: 'Derive scan from the narrowest constraint feature' cannot be implemented, because that width is unknown until after the sweep. The feasibility problem belongs to finding 0: seed starts at the box ends searchable_shift returns and at the floor, rather than refining the grid. 'Replace the rounds cap by a convergence condition plus a guard' describes what the code already does. The actual fixes are: scale the tolerance by module (e.g. m_n·resolution) or use brent's own tolerance; emit a note or debug assertion when the cap is hit while still moving; use compat::SAME_SHIFT in member_is_buildable; and at shape.rs:1700 either return the bracket end on the clear side or step with f64::next_up until room ≥ 0, with the comment corrected.

title: The pointed-tooth roll is solved three ways; the tip-width ceiling builds a whole tooth per candidate
claim: The same relation, ψ_b = inv α_point (u_point = tan α_point), is solved by brent in addendum_for_tip_width, by newton_bracketed in Tooth::new, and is also exactly involute::inv_inverse(ψ_b). addendum_asked constructs a full Tooth (profile, fillet, clamps) only to read r, r_b and ψ_b, which are closed-form from the params. It does so for every search candidate, before the real tooth is built.
evidence: auto.rs:744-749 and tooth.rs:455-462 solve psi_b − inv_from_roll(u) = 0 on [0, POINTED_TOOTH_MAX_ROLL]; involute.rs:51 inverts inv directly, with a bracketed Newton.
proposal: Add one function, pointed_roll(psi_b) = inv_inverse(psi_b).map(f64::tan), used by both. Give addendum_for_tip_width a signature taking (r, r_b, ψ_b, m, x), or a lightweight 'TransverseTooth' computed from GearParams without generating the profile, and call it from addendum_asked.
validation: Existing addendum_for_tip_width tests plus a law that the pointed radius from Tooth::new and from the shared function agree to 1e-12 over z, x, α. Measure search time before and after.

verdict.reason: The unification half is confirmed and is broader than stated. The cost half is real but negligible, and it overstates what Tooth::new does. Over 466 capped, non-severed teeth (z 3–150, α 14.5–30°, x −0.5–1, β 0/20°, h_a=4), Tooth::new's pointed-capped ra matches rb·hypot(1, tan(inv_inverse(ψ_b))) to 4.0e-16 relative. addendum_for_tip_width(g, 0) matches to 4.3e-16. So three solvers (newton_bracketed at tooth.rs:456, brent at auto.rs:744, inv_inverse) give one answer. There is a fourth site: ring.rs:297 already uses inv_inverse(−ψ_b) for the ring's pointed radius, and its comment (ring.rs:289-291) says 'Closed form through the same inv⁻¹ everything else uses, and it mirrors Tooth's pointed-tooth clamp'. That is false of Tooth, which solves the same relation by hand. On cost: Tooth::new computes only scalars, a junction solve and a severing check, with no profile, in 0.35–0.6 µs. On 9/37, addendum_asked accounts for 793 of 1563 Tooth builds in one search (10.8 ms), so removing it saves about 0.3–0.5 ms (≈3–4%). On Compound it is 14,219 of 20,272 builds in 396 ms (≈1.5–2%). The case for the change is one statement, not speed. One irony supports it: member_is_buildable's doc (auto.rs:1006-1008) argues that building a tooth twice per candidate is 'a cost a search pays a thousand times over', and addendum_asked does exactly that. This overlaps primitives #8 and lens-magic-numbers #10.
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-auto-search-c/probe_main.rs printed 'F13: 466 capped teeth: Tooth::new ra vs inv_inverse: rel 3.997e-16; addendum_for_tip_width(0) vs inv_inverse: rel 4.299e-16' and 'Tooth::new 0.35–0.60 us each'. Severed teeth were excluded because their ra is later set down (differences up to 0.89 appear otherwise). A worktree counter (worktree.diff) gave 'pair[9, 37]: 10.8ms, tooth builds 1563, of which addendum_asked 793' and 'Compound: 395.7ms, tooth builds 20272, addendum_asked 14219'.
verdict.corrected_claim: The pointed-tooth roll u − atan u = ψ_b is solved by newton_bracketed in Tooth::new (tooth.rs:456) and by brent in addendum_for_tip_width (auto.rs:744). inv_inverse gives the same answer to 4e-16, and ring.rs:297 already uses it for the internal case, with a comment that wrongly says Tooth does the same. addendum_asked builds a Tooth per new search candidate, which is about half of all Tooth builds, but that is 2–4% of search time.
verdict.proposal_note: A lightweight ψ_b must reproduce Tooth::new's pressure-angle guard and transverse_thickness's clamps (tooth.rs:823-845), or ψ_b will differ on thin or thick teeth. Reuse transverse_thickness rather than rewriting the formula. Make pointed_roll(ψ_b) = inv_inverse(ψ_b).map(f64::tan) the one function, used by Tooth::new, addendum_for_tip_width and (negated) the ring. Keep POINTED_TOOTH_MAX_ROLL's semantics in mind: inv_inverse searches to π/2 − 1e-12, while the tooth stops at u=50. Both agree because ψ_b < inv(atan 50) ≈ 48 for any buildable tooth, but the law test should include the largest ψ_b the guards admit.

title: searchable_shift bisects a piecewise-linear bound, re-running the undercut solve on every evaluation
claim: The root-round ceiling ρ_max(x) = 0.95·min(m(h_f − x), ρ_fit(x)) is piecewise linear in x (w_tip is linear, so ρ_fit is too). The doc admits this and chooses bisection to avoid stating it twice. Each residual evaluation calls admissible_ranges, which calls admissible_profile_shift, which calls minimum_profile_shift (a bracketed solve in the capped-tool regime), even though only root_radius.max is read.
evidence: Read of ranges_at_shift (auto.rs:676-685) and searchable_shift (819-849).
proposal: Have ranges_at_shift expose the root-radius ceiling as a function of x in its linear form, returning slope and intercept for each branch, from the same expressions it uses now, so there is still one statement. Then searchable_shift solves two linear equations and takes the smaller root. Failing that, give searchable_shift a narrow helper, root_radius_ceiling(p), that skips the undercut solve.
validation: A law: for random (z, α, ρ, h_f, x_s) the closed-form ceiling matches the bisected one to 1e-12. check_golden unchanged.

verdict.reason: The ceiling is piecewise linear, and the bisection does re-evaluate everything each time. The auditor's reason is wrong, though, and the true closed form is simpler than proposed. w_tip does not change with x in the ordinary regime: dst/dx = 2m·tanα_n/cosβ = 2m·tanα_t exactly cancels d(−2·b_d·tanα_t)/dx = +2m·tanα_t, because shifting moves the rack out without changing its tip land. So ρ_fit is constant, and below the shallow-cut threshold the ceiling is x_c = h_f − ρ·m_t/(0.95·m) = h_f − ρ/(0.95·cosβ). Only for x ≥ h_f − 0.05, where the tool is deepened and b_d is fixed at 0.05·m, does ρ_fit fall linearly. Train members are always concentric (shape.rs:1027 sets angular_shift 0), so these two pieces are the whole of it. searchable_shift's own doc ('both terms are linear in x') is equally loose. On cost: brent needs 11 evaluations on average (max 24), about 54 µs per call, once per free member per solve rather than per candidate. That is about 1% of a pair search, so there is no performance case. Each evaluation does run 3× admissible_profile_shift (a minimum-shift step plus a pointed-threshold brent at auto.rs:366) and, in the shape, at(x)'s addendum_asked Tooth with two brents, all discarded except root_radius.max. The documented reason for bisecting (not stating the rule twice) is a legitimate concern, but the owner's goal of 'closed form where possible' outweighs it, and the concern can be met.
verdict.evidence: Probe (notes/verify-auto-search-c/probe_main.rs) over z∈{5..60}, α∈{14.5,20,25}, h_f∈{1,1.25,1.4}, ρ∈{0.05..0.45}, β∈{0,15,30}, k_s∈{1,1.1} printed: 'F14: 2079 cases agree to 2.220e-16; w_tip variation in ordinary regime 6.661e-16 mm; evaluations per call mean 11.0, max 24', and 'searchable_shift: 53.5 us per call'. Code read at auto.rs:655-707 and 819-849.
verdict.corrected_claim: searchable_shift finds the root-round ceiling by brent (about 11 evaluations of the full admissible_ranges) although it has a two-piece closed form. Below the shallow cut, w_tip and ρ_fit do not depend on x, so the ceiling is x ≤ h_f − ρ/(0.95·cosβ) (when 0.95·ρ_fit ≥ ρ·m_t). Above it, b_d = 0.05·m and ρ_fit falls linearly. This matches the bisection to 2e-16. The cost is negligible, so the issue is closed form versus numeric solve, plus a doc that misdescribes the terms.
verdict.proposal_note: Returning a slope and intercept for each branch from ranges_at_shift is more structure than needed. Add one function, e.g. root_round_shift_ceiling(p) -> Option<f64>, written from the same b_d, w_tip and FILLET_FRACTION_OF_MAX, and gate it with a law that ranges_at_shift's root_radius.max evaluated at the ceiling equals p.root_radius, so forward and inverse forms cannot drift. Correct the doc so it no longer says ρ_fit is linear in x.

title: Union-find written twice in shape.rs; state.md still describes per-stage objectives
claim: asking_members and search_components each define the same inner `fn find` with path compression. docs/state.md:487-489 says 'The spur pair, the planetary set and the hula stage each have their own free variables and their own objective over one shared search'. There is now one objective (the product over meshes) in one shape solve.
evidence: Read at the cited lines.
proposal: Have search_components compute components once and derive asking_members from them, or hoist one small union-find helper. Rewrite the state.md sentence to describe the shape's one search, its coordinates and its components.
validation: cargo nextest run; check_doc_links.

verdict.reason: The duplication and the stale state.md sentence both hold, and the stale sentence is worse than reported. One small correction: only search_components' find (shape.rs:2060-2072) compresses paths; asking_members' (shape.rs:1996-2002) does not. Both union the same relation: meshes on an unheld distance, and meshes sharing a Free member. asking_members uses every Free member, while search_components uses only the asking free ones, but that gives the same partition on every component that asks. So one mesh partition could produce asking, free and the axis components. mesh_groups (shape.rs:1087) is a third union-find in the file (shape-a #15, lens-architecture #11). In docs/state.md:487-489, besides the per-stage objectives, the next clause, 'a crossed pair's shifts are placed by the constraints alone, since the search is the parallel-axis mesh's', is also false. trial_efficiency scores point contacts through CrossedTrial (shape.rs:2259), reference.md:766-778 says crossed pairs are searched, and crossed.rs has the_optimiser_reaches_a_crossed_pair_by_its_own_mesh.
verdict.evidence: I read shape.rs:1987-2119 and state.md:478-491. A worktree probe of crossed([17,43], 5°) with set_search(true) chose x=[0.4345, 0.8494] rather than the floor, so crossed pairs are searched.
verdict.corrected_claim: asking_members and search_components each hand-write a union-find over the same mesh relation, and only the second compresses paths. docs/state.md:487-489 describes per-stage objectives and says crossed pairs are not searched; both are stale.
verdict.proposal_note: Compute one mesh partition first. Then asking = partition contains a mesh with search; free = Free members in asking partitions; and the axis components are the partitions' axes. This removes the second union-find instead of hoisting a helper. Rewrite state.md's sentence to say: one product-over-meshes objective, searched per component in sum and division coordinates, over line and point contacts alike.

title: The search's answer does not depend on friction: the objective is purely geometric
claim: With the line-contact efficiency model, η is linear in µ at fixed geometry, so argmax over shifts does not depend on µ. MeshTrial/CrossedTrial take friction and evaluate η at it, but the choice they drive is µ-free (at least for line contact). This is a law worth stating and testing, and it means the chosen shifts can be cached across µ edits.
evidence: probe_continuity, µ from 0.03 to 0.12 in 41 steps on 9/37, 17/43 and 7/40: identical shifts at every step. η falls by exactly 6.531e-4 per 2.25e-3 of µ on 9/37.
proposal: State it in the MeshTrial doc. Optionally have the parallel-axis objective be the geometric loss integral (1−η)/µ. Check whether the crossed (screw) efficiency is also µ-linear before generalising.
validation: Law test: for presets with search on, shifts_at is bit-identical at µ=0.04 and 0.12.

verdict.reason: This holds only for a component with a single line-contact mesh and μ > 0. The general claim, and the proposal to cache across μ edits, are wrong. Line contact gives η = 1 − μ·L(geometry) (contact.rs:436), so for one mesh the argmax does not depend on μ. I reproduced that: Spur, Planocentric and pairs 9/37, 7/40, 17/43 and 12/29 are identical to ≤ 6e-16 for μ between 0.01 and 0.3. But the shape maximises the product ∏(1 − μ_k·L_k) over a component's meshes, which depends on μ at second order when μ is uniform and at first order when meshes have different μ (every mesh has its own sliding_friction). Point contacts (CrossedTrial, the exact force balance) are not linear in μ. At μ = 0 the objective is identically 1 and the answer is whatever the tie-break gives.
verdict.evidence: Worktree test probe_mu_independence (notes/verify-auto-search-c/worktree.diff), max shift change against μ=0.08, with search on. Uniform μ: Idler 4.71e-4 at μ=0.3; Compound 1.11e-3 at μ=0.01/0.02/0.2 and 3.32e-3 at μ=0.3; MeshedPlanets 4.43e-3 at μ=0.2/0.3. μ alternating (0.03, 0.15) per mesh: Idler 2.21e-2, Wolfrom 2.08e-2, Compound 4.21e-2, MeshedPlanets 4.68e-2, Layshaft 2.21e-3. crossed([17,43], 5°): 1.88e-2 at μ=0.12 and 3.70e-2 at μ=0.2. μ=0: Spur moves by 0.69 module, MeshedPlanets by 3.06, and 9/37 returns [0.5085, 0.0673] (how=Chose) against [0.6746, 0.7332] at μ=1e-9.
verdict.corrected_claim: For a search component with one line-contact mesh and μ > 0, the chosen shifts do not depend on μ, because η is affine in μ. For components with several meshes (a product of efficiencies, with per-mesh μ) and for crossed or worm point contacts, the choice depends on μ, by up to 0.047 module on shipped presets with unequal friction and 0.037 on a 5° crossed pair. At μ = 0 the search is degenerate.
verdict.proposal_note: Do not cache chosen shifts across μ edits. That is wrong for multi-mesh components and crossed meshes. The proposed law ('bit-identical at μ = 0.04 and 0.12 for presets') is a weak gate: on every preset the second-order dependence at those two values happens to fall below the walk's step, so it would pass while the property fails at 0.3, and ulp-level differences (4.4e-16 on Spur) make 'bit-identical' fragile. State the law for single line meshes only, with a tolerance of Search::resolution. Scoring line meshes by their geometric loss L = (1−η)/μ is worth doing for a different reason: it removes the μ = 0 degeneracy (see missed).

title: Meshed-planet and other triangle closures are never checked: an unbuildable set solves as valid
claim: Where three axes are joined pairwise by distances (central to P1, central to P2, P1 to P2 in a meshed-planet or Ravigneaux set), the three distances must satisfy |r1 - r2| <= d12 <= r1 + r2 for the carrier to hold the axes at all. Neither the plan nor anything else in train/ checks this, so geometrically impossible sets are solved and reported with a ratio, layouts marked clearance_ok and no note.
evidence: Probe probes/shape-a2 (the public API, solve_alone on arrangements::meshed_planets(24,[18,18],zr,3)). zr=96: distances [21.02, 38.98, 18.02], so |38.98-21.02| = 17.96 <= 18.02, which is fine. zr=120: distances [21.02, 50.98, 18.02], so |50.98-21.02| = 29.96 > 18.02, which is impossible. It still returned ratio -4.0, layouts [(1, 16.41, true), (2, 68.30, true)] and only 'planets_share_load_equally' notes. zr=150: 65.98 vs 18.02, also accepted, ratio -5.25. grep -i 'triangle|law of cosines' over train/ finds nothing. LayoutReport only checks neighbours on the same axis, so it never sees the angle between P1 and P2.
proposal: Give the solve a positional closure. For every cycle of distances in one frame (found from the axis graph: a spanning tree plus back edges), place the axes: in a carrier frame, the carried axes by radius and phase angle. For three axes, compute the angle from the law of cosines, cos phi = (r1^2 + r2^2 - d12^2)/(2 r1 r2), and refuse with a named TrainError (e.g. AxesCannotBePlaced { distances }) when |cos phi| > 1. Longer cycles are over-constrained: report the closure residual as a note. With the positions known, extend LayoutReport to check the tip gap between instances of different planet axes (P2 of set j against P1 of set j+1), which is currently unchecked.
validation: A law over every preset and arrangement that each solved shape's distances admit a planar placement. Include a negative fixture, meshed_planets(24,[18,18],120,3), that must be refused. Cross-check the placement angle against tools/train_kinematics.py for the Ravigneaux preset.

verdict.reason: The behaviour is real, but it is a gap the project already documents, not an undiscovered bug. docs/state.md:636 ('Two carried axes placed round the carrier ... nothing checks the three form a triangle, and the planet-clearance layout places one axis's planets without the other's ... a layout that does not close is a fault this tool does not yet name') and state.md:1194 list both the missing triangle check and the missing cross-axis layout check. Being documented does not settle it: rule 5 in CLAUDE.md says to refuse input that describes no shape at all, and an unclosable triangle is such an input. Still, 'critical' overstates a gap the project has written down.
verdict.evidence: Reproduced with probe probes/verify-shape-a-1 (solve_alone on arrangements::meshed_planets(24,[18,18],zr,3)). zr=96: distances [21.02, 38.98, 18.02]; the triangle closes, and the law of cosines gives phi = 2.94 deg, so even the shipped preset is nearly collinear. zr=110: [21.02, 45.98, 18.02]; |45.98-21.02| = 24.96 > 18.02, impossible, yet ratio -3.583 and layouts ok. zr=120: 29.96 > 18.02, ratio -4.0, layouts [(1,16.41,true),(2,68.30,true)]. zr=150: ratio -5.25. The only notes in every case are planets_share_load_equally. grep for triangle/placement in train/ finds nothing.
verdict.corrected_claim: The known and documented residual (state.md:636) is real, and it is a silent solve of geometry that cannot exist. A meshed-planet or Ravigneaux set whose three distances violate |r1-r2| <= d12 <= r1+r2 solves, and it reports a ratio, clearance_ok layouts and no note (e.g. meshed_planets(24,[18,18],110 or 120,3)). Rule 5 argues for refusing it, so the documented deferral does not hold up.
verdict.proposal_note: The law-of-cosines placement is right for the triangle. Refuse only when |cos phi| > 1 (rule 5); a longer over-constrained cycle should be refused on its closure residual too, not merely noted. When it lands, delete or update the state.md:636 row and the state.md:1194 sentence. The shipped preset sits at phi ~ 2.9 deg (P1 and P2 almost radial), which is worth a sanity look at the same time.

title: The plan's role assignment depends on mesh order: a valid given distance is reported unreached with negative clearance
claim: On a given distance, the second loop of plan_held assigns roles for 'both free' meshes without checking whether either member already got a role from an earlier mesh in the same loop. It also never re-runs the one-free propagation afterwards. A member marked Settled or Reaches by mesh j is overwritten by mesh j+1, and closed() then computes the earlier mesh from a shift that later changes, so that mesh misses the held distance.
evidence: Audit test audit_plan_order (notes/shape-a/shape_audit.rs, run1.log). Axes A and B, with p(21) and r(22) on A and q(30) on B; meshes p-q and r-q on distance 0, held at 26.2 mm; r-s(25) on distance 1. Mesh order [p-q, r-q]: roles [Reaches(0), Reaches(1), Free, Free], and q's Settled is overwritten by Reaches(1). Mesh 0 then runs at 26.2778 against 26.2 held. The notes are part.distance_not_reached (asked 26.18, reached 26.2578) and part.clearance_negative (overlap 0.0578 mm). The same graph in order [r-q, p-q]: both meshes at 26.2, clearance 0.020, p shift 0.6506 against 0.7429. In that order role[q] is Settled even though q is also the Reaches member, which also gives trial_efficiency's undercut floor (Decided) the wrong role.
proposal: Replace the two loops with one constraint-graph pass per held distance. Unknowns are the free members; each mesh is an edge with the linear equation x_a + sign*x_b = S_m. In each connected component, pick the root as the member in the most meshes (ties to the lowest index). It stands Settled, or becomes a search variable (see the Settled finding). BFS from the root gives every other member Reaches(edge). An edge between two already-decided members is a closure check, recorded in the Plan so closed() verifies it and reports distance_not_reached only when it genuinely fails. Roles are then assigned once and never overwritten.
validation: A law that permuting shape.meshes, and permuting members within a mesh where the kind allows it, leaves every shift, running distance and note unchanged, swept over every preset plus ferguson-like fixtures with a member in several meshes on a given distance. The fixture above must close in both orders.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading the code and by running it. In plan_held, the second loop (shape.rs:1274-1296) looks only at in_meshes counts for meshes left unplanned by the first loop. It never re-checks whether a member was decided earlier in the same loop, so it overwrites a role and never re-runs the one-free propagation. closed() then computes the earlier mesh's reach from a value the later divide changes. Rated medium, not high: the notes fire loudly, and the topology (one gear meshing two gears on one axis at one given distance) is unusual. The graph edits make it reachable, though, and the result depends on mesh order, which breaks a basic invariance.
verdict.evidence: My own worktree test (notes/verify-shape-a-1/vsa1.rs, v1_order): p(21) and r(22) on axis A, q(30) on B, r-s(25) on a second distance, distance 0 held at 26.2. Order [p-q, r-q]: roles [Reaches(0), Reaches(1), Free, Free], nominals [26.2578, 26.18], clearance -0.0578, notes distance_not_reached and clearance_negative. Order [r-q, p-q]: roles [Reaches(1), Settled, Free, Free], but q is 0.0923, set by the divide, so 'Settled' is a mislabel. Both nominals are 26.18 and p is 0.6506. Orders [q-p, q-r] and [q-r, q-p] (members swapped within a mesh) are also valid but give a different design: q 0.0 Settled, p 0.7429, r 0.1846. At held 26.3 the same pattern appears: order 0 overlaps by 0.0998 mm. So three different answers come from four orderings of one graph.
verdict.proposal_note: The constraint-graph BFS is sound. Also require invariance under swapping a and b within a mesh (orders 2/3 above differ from order 1 even where both close). The law should compare shifts, not only notes.

title: Searching one mesh changes the shift division of meshes that did not ask to be searched
claim: closed() divides a both-free mesh's sum with divide_shift_sum only when the free vector is empty, which is a global switch. Once any component is searched, place() passes a full vector, so every non-asking mesh whose first member is Free takes that member at its floor and hands the whole sum to the second. This contradicts MeshInput::search ('a component none of whose meshes asks keeps its undercut shifts') and lowers the efficiency of the meshes left alone.
evidence: Audit test audit_search_couples_components: layshaft (20,40)+(30,30)+(35,25), distance given at 30.5 mm with clearance 0.02. No search: shifts [0.2537 x6], mesh efficiencies [0.98569, 0.98710, 0.98678]. search=true on mesh 1 only: shifts [0.0, 0.5075, 0.2535, 0.2540, 0.0, 0.5075], efficiencies [0.98501, 0.98710, 0.98618]. Meshes 0 and 2 were not asked, yet their division moved from equal to floor-and-rest and they got worse. Mesh 1, the one that asked, barely changed.
proposal: Make closed take free: &[Option<f64>], Some only for members the search actually moves, and apply the divide rule per mesh whenever member a is Free and free[a] is None. place() then writes Some only for free[j] indices. This also removes the global 'free.is_empty()' mode.
validation: A law that toggling search on mesh k leaves every shift outside k's search component bit-identical, swept over every preset with each mesh toggled in turn.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. In closed() (shape.rs:1363), the equal division of a both-free sum on a held distance is gated on free.is_empty(). Once any component is searched, place() builds a full vector from settled = asked.settled (the undercut floor, shape.rs:1723). Every non-asking mesh then takes its first member at the floor and gives the rest of the sum to the second. This contradicts the MeshInput::search doc (shape.rs:228-231: 'a component none of whose meshes asks keeps its undercut shifts'). The efficiency lost is small, about 7e-4 on a mesh, so medium rather than high.
verdict.evidence: v2_search_couples: layshaft (20,40)+(30,30)+(35,25), distance fixed at 30.5, clearance 0.02. No search: shifts all 0.2537, eff [0.98569, 0.98710, 0.98678]. search on mesh 1 only: shifts [0.0, 0.5075, 0.2535, 0.2540, 0.0, 0.5075], eff [0.98501, 0.98710, 0.98618]. search on mesh 0 only: meshes 1 and 2 change to [0.0, 0.5075] and [0.0, 0.5075], eff 0.98652 and 0.98618, both worse than unsearched. On an automatic distance all meshes form one component, so the coupling there is by design and not this bug.
verdict.proposal_note: The Option-per-member form is right. The same free slice is also passed through sized() / room_at, so change its semantics there too. The law should also cover a tip-sized (held-by-sizing) distance, where the 'None if sized' fallback path runs.

title: A Settled member is a real degree of freedom the search never moves; search=true reports NotAsked
claim: On a given distance, a free member in more meshes than its mate (a planet) becomes Role::Settled at its undercut floor. The component still has one degree of freedom (move the planet, let sun and ring reach), but chosen_at only searches Role::Free members, so with every mesh asking for efficiency the answer is the floor and the result says NotAsked.
evidence: Audit test audit_settled_hides_a_freedom: planetary 12/30/72, distance given at its own running value + 0.1, ring shift automatic. Roles [Reaches(0), Settled, Reaches(1)]. With search off or on: how NotAsked, shifts [0.2341, 0.0, 0.2774], efficiency 0.977792. Moving the planet by hand with the distance kept: +0.1 gives 0.977972, +0.2 gives 0.977836, -0.2 gives 0.976423. There is an optimum near +0.1 the search cannot reach.
proposal: When the member's component asks to be searched, give the root of each held-distance component (the member the plan now calls Settled) Role::Free and a Coordinate::Own axis over its searchable interval. Keep Settled only for components that do not ask. Once the plan is a constraint graph (previous finding) this is one line: the root's role is Free-if-asking.
validation: A test that on the planetary preset with a given distance and search on, the chosen efficiency is at least the best of a manual sweep of the planet shift, and how == Chose.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. With a given distance and the ring shift automatic, the planet is Role::Settled (shape.rs:1288). chosen_at gathers searchable members only from Role::Free (shape.rs:1757-1759), so free is empty and the result is NotAsked even with search set on every mesh. One degree of freedom remains, and moving it by hand improves efficiency. The gain is small (about 2e-4), but the result misreports 'not asked' to a designer who asked.
verdict.evidence: v3_settled: planetary 12/30/72, distance fixed at automatic+0.1 (21.2453), ring shift automatic. Search off and on both give roles [Reaches(0), Settled, Reaches(1)], how NotAsked, shifts [0.2341, 0.0, 0.2774], eff 0.977792. Planet shift by hand, distance kept: -0.2 gives 0.976423, +0.05 0.977923, +0.10 0.977972 (best), +0.15 0.977943, +0.2 0.977836, +0.3 0.977390. No notes change across the sweep.
verdict.proposal_note: Making the component root Free when its component asks is right. Its interval must be the one inside which both reaching mates stay admissible; otherwise the search spends trials on points where trial_efficiency returns None. Also fix the Decided role passed to undercut_bound for the member that becomes searched.

title: An automatic clearance's hidden manual value decides the shifts
claim: With the distance given and the clearance automatic, given_running is None, so the plan closes the distance as if it were automatic. running_of and build still open every mesh by clearance.manual, the value in a box the panel shows as automatic, so the absorbed shift and the resulting backlash depend on a number the designer cannot see.
evidence: Audit test audit_auto_clearance_stale_manual: planetary 12/30/72, distance fixed at 21.19528, clearance {auto: true, manual: s}. s=0: nominal [21.1453, 21.1453], ring shift -0.1491, reported clearance 0.0499. s=0.1: nominal [21.0437, 21.2437], ring -0.2540, clearance 0.1515. s=0.3: nominal [20.8308, 21.4308], ring -0.4620, clearance 0.3645, first-mesh backlash 2.54 against 0.37. The running distance is identical in all four. TrainPanel.svelte:769-773 renders the clearance as an auto field showing dres?.clearance, so the manual value stays hidden in state.
proposal: Decide what an automatic clearance means and state it once. Suggested: with the distance given and clearance automatic, the shifts close every later mesh to the first mesh's nominal, which is the zero-clearance absorb (run_at with 0). The reported clearance is then running minus nominal, equal on every mesh. Never read clearance.manual while clearance.auto is set. Implement it as a clearance_used(d) helper that returns 0 (or a named default) when auto, and use it in running_of, build and closed.
validation: A law that, over every preset, changing clearance.manual while clearance.auto is set changes no output bit.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is confirmed, and it is worse than stated. It only arises where a distance carries two or more meshes: on a pair the hidden value changes nothing. Relief makes the state reachable from the panel, because touching the clearance spares it and pins the distance. At the shipped hidden value 0.02 the automatic clearance gives the ring mesh negative backlash. The proposal as written (zero-clearance absorb, nominals equal) would itself give the ring mesh an interference.
verdict.evidence: v4_auto_clearance: planetary 12/30/72, distance fixed at automatic+0.05 (21.19528), clearance {auto:true, manual:s}. s=0: nominal [21.1453, 21.1453], ring -0.1491, backlash [0.368, -0.147], note clearance_negative overlap 0.0499. s=0.02 (the default manual): nominal [21.1253, 21.1653], backlash [0.514, -0.089], clearance_negative overlap 0.030. s=0.1: reported 0.1515, backlash [1.097, 0.145]. s=0.3: reported 0.3645, backlash [2.543, 0.723]. With the clearance given at 0.02: nominal [21.1753, 21.2153], backlash [0.148, 0.060], no warning. On pair([17,43]) at a fixed distance, s=0 and s=0.3 give identical output. relieved(Some(Freedom::Clearance(0))) on a set with clearance auto leaves clearance auto and distance given. The panel's toggle (TrainPanel.svelte:1840-1850) seeds manual only when turning auto OFF, so the last typed value stays hidden. The reported clearance is running - nominal[0] only, so the internal mesh's different gap is never shown in the clearance field.
verdict.corrected_claim: On a distance with two or more meshes (any set), a given distance with an automatic clearance closes the later meshes to the first's nominal ± 2·clearance.manual, a value the panel hides. The reported clearance is the first mesh's alone, and the other mesh runs at a different gap, which is negative (interference, clearance_negative) at the shipped hidden 0.02 when the distance is given a little over the automatic one. Pairs are unaffected.
verdict.proposal_note: Do not take 'zero-clearance absorb' (nominals equal). That is the s=0 row above, which interferes on the internal mesh. The consistent meaning is one derived clearance c shared by every mesh on the distance. The first mesh's shifts fix c = running - nominal_0, and each later mesh reaches kind.nominal_of(running, c): the reach path closed() already uses for a held distance, with c in place of clearance.manual. Never read clearance.manual while auto is set. Also update docs/reference.md:420-426, which still says a set's clearance is always given (see missed).

repro.reproduction: Probe crate at /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/repro-shape-a-4/src/main.rs, run against the public API with solve_alone(Train::alone(shape, 20, 1000)). Smallest input: arrangements::planetary(12,30,72,3); distances[0].distance = Auto::fixed(21.195279), which is the automatic running distance 21.145279 plus 0.05; distances[0].clearance = Auto::automatic(s). Only s, the manual value of a clearance marked automatic, changes between runs. Control 1: the same with the clearance given at 0.02. Control 2: pair([17,43]) at a fixed distance, s = 0 and s = 0.3. Independent check at /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/repro-shape-a-4/nominal.py. It uses mpmath, the textbook involute centre-distance equation (inv α_w = inv α + 2 tan α Σx/Σz, a = m Σz cos α / (2 cos α_w), with the internal form for the ring) and the shifts the solve reported. It shares no code with the crate. No worktree was created.
repro.observed:
The running distance is 21.195279 in every run. The panel's clearance field is automatic, so it shows the reported clearance. Every one of the following changes with the hidden s:

| s (hidden) | planet shift x | nominals (ext / int) | reported clearance | backlash, deg (sun-planet / planet-ring) | note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | -0.149050 | 21.145343 / 21.145343 | 0.0499 | 0.368 / -0.147 | clearance_negative |
| 0.02 (preset's shipped value) | -0.170059 | 21.125279 / 21.165279 | 0.0700 | 0.514 / -0.089 | clearance_negative |
| 0.1 | -0.254015 | 21.043745 / 21.243745 | 0.1515 | 1.097 / 0.145 | none |
| 0.3 | -0.462002 | 20.830800 / 21.430800 | 0.3645 | 2.543 / 0.723 | none |
| given 0.02 (control) | sun 0.403971, planet -0.223325 | 21.175279 / 21.215279 | 0.0200 | 0.148 / 0.060 | none |

- **What the code does:** it closes the internal mesh to the external nominal ± 2·s. The mechanism is in shape.rs: given_running (line 625) returns None when the clearance is automatic, while lines 841, 1206, 1354 and 2855 still read clearance.manual. The planet's shift absorbs the difference.

So ticking the clearance to automatic and typing a distance gives exactly the s = 0.02 row: a hidden 0.02 decides the shifts, and the result is an interfering ring mesh.

What would be correct: the verifier's rule, one clearance c shared by every mesh on the distance. The first mesh fixes c = running − nominal₀, and each later mesh reaches kind.nominal_of(running, c). The s = 0 row, which is the ledger's original proposal, gives equal nominals, and the internal mesh then interferes by 0.0499.
repro.note:
Confirmed as the verifier's corrected claim, with one correction to the ledger's wording. The shift that moves is the planet's (member 1), not the ring's: the preset fixes the ring's shift at 0, and both the ledger and the verdict label the moving value "ring". - **Against high:** every reported figure is geometrically true for the shifts chosen (independently recomputed), and the interference case does raise part.clearance_negative. The designer is warned, not misinformed.

Fix: add a clearance_used(d) helper. Under auto it returns the derived clearance c = running − nominal₀; otherwise it returns manual. Use it at shape.rs:841, 1206, 1354 and 2855.
