It should also check that every mesh on a distance reports the same signed gap. Also update docs/reference.md:420-426.

title: tip_clearance = 0 is a hidden mode switch: going from 0 to 1e-9 moves the distance, turns a refusal into a solve, and contradicts its own doc
claim: sized() treats tip_clearance > 0.0 as 'a gap asked is a distance asked'. It then walks inward below the shifts' own distance to the least distance at which the tips clear. At exactly 0 the shifts' distance stands unless the tips cross, and where the shifts' closure fails it refuses. Distance::tip_clearance's doc says the automatic distance is 'what the shifts leave or what the tips need, whichever is larger', which the code does not do for a gap > 0.
evidence: Audit test audit_tip_clearance_scan. planocentric 20/28: gap 0 gives e=3.980000, sized_by None, ring x=0.0000; gap 1e-9 gives e=3.971973, sized_by Some(0), x=-0.0040. The distance moved inward by 0.008 mm, smaller than the shifts' own. 20/32: 5.980 to 5.814. planocentric 12/13 through 12/24: gap 0 gives Err(Mesh(OutsideInvoluteDomain)), gap 1e-9 solves (e.g. 12/13 at 0.850534). push_distance gives a fresh internal distance a gap of 0.0 when the shape has no distance yet, so a graph-built internal mesh starts on the refusing side.
proposal: Make the rule one continuous function: e = the least distance in the involute domain at which room(e) >= gap, with gap >= 0 and no 'asked' flag. Whether that may go below the shifts' own distance is one explicit rule applied at every gap, including 0. If the 'no gap asked, keep the shifts' distance' behaviour is wanted, expose it as Option<f64> (None = not asked) so the mode is visible, and fix the field doc to say what the code does.
validation: A continuity law: for each internal preset, e(gap) is continuous and non-decreasing in gap on [0, 0.5], including at 0+, and success does not depend on gap = 0 versus 1e-9.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. sized() (shape.rs:1585) switches mode on tip_clearance > 0.0, and the comment says so on purpose ('A gap asked for is a distance asked for ... With no gap asked the shifts' own distance stands'). The field doc at shape.rs:274-278 ('whichever is larger') contradicts the code. The step at 0+ is a real discontinuity, and so is the refuse-versus-solve flip. The mode is deliberate, but it is a hidden flag on a float, contrary to the owner's continuity goal.
verdict.evidence: v5_tip_gap: planocentric 20/28 (preset gap 0): gap 0 gives e=3.980000, sized_by None, x=0. Every gap from 1e-12 to 0.3 gives e=3.971973, sized_by Some(0), x=-0.0040, so the distance moves inward, below the shifts' own. 20/32: 5.980 to 5.814218. 12/13: gap 0 gives Err(Mesh(OutsideInvoluteDomain)), 1e-12 gives e=0.850534. 12/18: Err, then e=3.030014. 30/33 and 30/31 are already tip-sized at 0 and show no step. For 20/28 the same e holds for every gap up to 0.3, so the root is set by the crossing margin, not by the asked far gap: tip_room's room is min(far_gap - asked [mm], tip_margin [deg]) with -1.0 on interference (shape.rs:1538-1545). arrangements.rs:462 gives a fresh distance gap 0.0.
verdict.proposal_note: Option<f64> (None = not asked) is the lower-risk fix and keeps the golden outputs. A single continuous rule would move every planocentric at gap 0. Either way, rewrite the Distance::tip_clearance doc. Also note that in the gap>0 mode the inward walk drives the crossing margin (degrees, with no asked value) to zero, so the designed distance leaves the tips just touching where their circles cross. A continuous rule needs an asked crossing margin too, not only a far gap.

title: A distance at a tiny non-zero angle breaks the point-contact model (refused at 1e-9 degrees, eps 0 and efficiency 1 at 1e-6)
claim: The line/point choice is an exact float compare (angle != 0.0). Just above zero the screw model is numerically degenerate: at 1e-9 degrees it refuses with AxesAreParallel, and at 1e-6 degrees it returns a contact ratio of 0.0000 and an efficiency of exactly 1.00000. From 1e-3 degrees it is smooth. Its limit also differs from the line contact in efficiency (0.98513 against 0.98499) and peak pressure (1753.6 against 1764.2 MPa). The contact-ratio count difference is documented; these breakdowns are not.
evidence: Audit test audit_crossed_to_parallel, arrangements::crossed([20,40], sigma).with_first_helix(15). sigma 0: line, a=31.078285, eps 2.3662, eff 0.98499, p_max 1764.2. sigma 1e-9: Err(Screw(AxesAreParallel)). sigma 1e-6: point, eps 0.0000, eff 1.00000/1.00000, p_max 1625.9. sigma 1e-3: eps 1.6393, eff 0.98513, p_max 1753.6.
proposal: Put one named threshold in screw.rs, e.g. PARALLEL_BELOW_DEG, chosen from where the screw model's conditioning is lost (measure it: the smallest sigma at which eps and efficiency agree with the 1e-3 values to 1e-6). Make kind_of, is_crossed and the screw constructor use it, so a near-parallel angle is treated as the line contact, and say so with a Note. This needs agreement with the crossed-worm auditor, who owns screw.rs.
validation: A sweep of sigma over 10^[-12, 1] degrees asserting eps and efficiency are finite, non-degenerate, and within a stated tolerance of the sigma=0 line values once below the threshold.

verdict.reason: The degeneracy is real, but the finding places it in the wrong range and misses the cause. It also counts as undocumented a limit gap that docs/reference.md already records as a seam. Cause 1: Screw::new computes sliding_ratio = sqrt(1 - 2k cos Σ + k²), which loses everything to cancellation near parallel. It comes out exactly 0 for every Σ ≤ 5.6e-7°, and the result is AxesAreParallel. Cause 2: path_of_contact_at's branch test (offset < 1e-6·a_ref) works on a tangent-line construction whose residual grows like 1/Σ. At Σ ≤ 3.2e-4° it rejects every branch and the path is None. The report then gives ε = 0, and the efficiency silently falls back to the pitch-point formula, whose sliding vanishes, so it reads 1.000000. The breakdown reaches 3.2e-4°, not just 1e-6° as claimed; everything is smooth only from 5.6e-4°. The limit mismatch in efficiency and p_max is already recorded: reference.md's limit table says efficiency meets only 'first order in μ' and peak pressure within '5 %'.
verdict.evidence: My worktree sweep over crossed([20,40],σ).with_first_helix(15), σ = 10^(k/4)°. Every σ ≤ 5.623e-7 gives Err(Screw(AxesAreParallel)). Every σ in [1e-6, 3.162e-4] gives ε 0.00000, η 1.000000 and p_max ≈1629.7. From 5.623e-4 up: ε 1.63926, η 0.985134, p_max 1753.64. Instrumenting the code: at σ = 1e-7° the computed sliding is 0, while the cancellation-free sqrt((1-k)² + 4k·sin²(Σ/2)) gives 1.807e-9 and agrees with the original to 1e-5 wherever the original is valid. The tangent-line offset is 1.06 mm at 1e-6°, 1.4e-4 at 1e-4° and 1.6e-5 at 5.6e-4°, against a tolerance of 3.1e-5. The efficiency fallback is shape.rs:2491 (`zone.and_then(...).unwrap_or_else(|| p.screw.efficiency(mu, d))`).
verdict.proposal_note: A threshold that swaps in the line contact near Σ = 0 would not remove the discontinuity. It moves a jump of the documented seam's size (ε 2.37 against 1.64, which are different measures) to the threshold. Better to fix the conditioning where it breaks: (a) in screw.rs:249, use sliding_ratio = sqrt((1-k)² + 4k·sin²(Σ/2)), which is exact and free of cancellation, so only Σ == 0 is refused; (b) make the tangent-line branch test scale with the construction's conditioning (a residual relative to 1/sin Σ), or pick the branch by sign rather than by residual; (c) never replace a missing path with the pitch-point efficiency without saying so, and raise a Note when the path is None. A sweep law over σ ∈ 10^[-9, 1]° asserting ε > 1 and |η - η(1e-2°)| < 1e-4 would hold all three.

title: A malformed document (index out of range) panics in the core instead of being refused
claim: Nothing validates a Shape's indices (mesh a/b into members, member body into bodies, body axis into axes, distance axes, couplings). gear_io::train::from_toml on a file with one mesh index set to 99 panics in Shape::mesh_groups. The wasm import at gear-wasm lib.rs:972 calls it, so a hand-edited or corrupted file traps the page instead of producing a refusal.
evidence: probes/shape-a with notes/shape-a/good.toml and bad.toml, which differ only in 'b = 1' vs 'b = 99' at line 587. good.toml loaded (adjusted false). bad.toml: panic at shape.rs:1091:24, 'index out of bounds: the len is 7 but the index is 99'. Audit test audit_malformed_graph: a mesh member out of range panics in graph.rs:236, and a body on a missing axis panics at shape.rs:457. A distance axis out of range and a member body not listed are refused, but with misleading messages ('mesh 1 is not a mesh this shape has', 'axes are not fixed in one frame').
proposal: Add Shape::validate() -> Result<(), ShapeInvalid> that checks every index and the structural invariants (the ring is b of an internal mesh, or normalise by swapping; count >= 1; at most one Distance per unordered axis pair; a coupling's two bodies distinct and listed). Call it in from_toml, in every wasm entry that deserialises a Train, and at the top of solve_train. Give each variant a catalogue key.
validation: A fuzz-style test mutating each index field of every preset's TOML to out-of-range values, asserting from_toml or solve_train returns Err and never panics.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. from_toml calls shape.relieved(), which indexes without checks, so a document with one mesh index out of range panics inside gear-core. That breaks the workspace rule 'A calculation engine must not panic' (Cargo.toml:26), and gear-wasm's own test says a bad file 'comes back as a reason, not a panic'. One overstatement: web/src/core.ts:597-602 wraps import_train in try/catch, so the page shows an opaque 'unreachable' error rather than dying. A trapped wasm instance does not unwind, though, so later calls on it are not guaranteed.
verdict.evidence: Re-ran probes/shape-a: good.toml and bad.toml differ only in 'b = 1' vs 'b = 99' (diff confirms line 587); bad.toml gives 'PANIC in from_toml'. Re-ran audit_malformed_graph in my worktree. A mesh member out of range panics at graph.rs:236:19 (len 3, index 99), and a body on a missing axis panics at shape.rs:457:39. A distance axis out of range is refused as 'mesh 1 is not a mesh this shape has'. A member body not listed is refused as 'axes are not fixed in one frame'. A duplicate distance is refused as 'below the base-circle limit', and axis count 0 solves. Existing tests (a_bad_geartrain_file_comes_back_as_a_reason, rejects_malformed_input_instead_of_panicking) cover only parse-level errors.
verdict.proposal_note: Validate once, where a Shape enters from outside: Shape::validate() in from_toml and in each wasm entry that deserialises a Train. Everything past that point can then keep its direct indexing. A check at the top of solve_train would repeat it on every keystroke for shapes the core built itself. The validation should also cover count >= 1 and at most one Distance per axis pair (a duplicate currently gets a misleading refusal, and count 0 solves).

title: A mesh's frame is decided per member, so one sun gear meshing two carriers' planets (a Simpson) is refused
claim: frame_of_member returns the first carrier found among a central member's mates, and Wiring::frame requires both members of a mesh to have the same per-member frame. A central gear meshing planets on two different carriers therefore fails on its second mesh with NoCommonFrame, even though each mesh has a well-defined frame (its planet's carrier).
evidence: Audit test audit_simpson_common_sun: one sun gear meshing p1 (carrier 1) and p2 (carrier 2). Frames: mesh 0 Ok(2), mesh 1 Ok(2), mesh 2 Err(NoCommonFrame(2)), mesh 3 Ok(4). With two sun gears on one body instead, all four meshes are Ok.
proposal: Make the frame a property of the mesh: frame(k) = the carrier of whichever member's axis is carried, provided the other member's axis is that carrier's axis or also carried by it, else ground. Store it in MeshSpec (or compute it in Wiring from the mounts' axes), and drop Mount::axis_fixed_in. edits.rs:379 is the one other caller and should ask the mesh as well.
validation: The Simpson fixture above solves and gives the textbook two-speed ratios, checked against tools/train_kinematics.py. Every preset still yields identical frames.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is as described: a sun meshing planets on two carriers gets NoCommonFrame on its second mesh. It is a deliberate, documented limitation, though, and a kinematically exact workaround exists. wiring.rs:33-39 says: 'The one thing this cannot express is a member central to two different carriers ... If one arrives, the field becomes a list'. The auditor's own fixture shows that two sun gears on one body solve with every frame Ok. Physically, a common sun meets its two planet sets on different axial stretches of its face, so two members on one body is arguably the more faithful rating model anyway. The editor refuses it cleanly and gives no wrong answer: add_on_new_axis returns WrongFamily for a mate that is not in ground (edits.rs:379). What holds is narrower: the doc's premise 'No arrangement in scope has it' is outdated now that the graph editor lets a designer build any train, and the refusal names no workaround.
verdict.evidence: Re-ran audit_simpson_common_sun: meshes 0 and 1 are Ok(2), mesh 2 is Err(NoCommonFrame(2)), mesh 3 is Ok(4). With two sun members on one body all four are Ok. frame_of_member (shape.rs:431-452) takes the first carrier found among the mates. frame_of_member also feeds the tooth-cycle count (shape.rs:3747) and first_speed (shape.rs:3882).
verdict.proposal_note: Storing the frame on the mesh alone is not enough. Tooth cycles (shape.rs:3747) and a member's speed against its frame (shape.rs:3882) are computed per member, and a sun central to two carriers has two engagement frequencies, so its cycles would have to be summed per mesh. Cheaper and accurate: keep the model, have the WrongFamily/NoCommonFrame refusal text point to 'two gears on one body', and update wiring.rs's 'no arrangement in scope' sentence.

title: Two given distances in one helix group size its helix twice; the solve refuses with an opaque 'Incompatible' and relief does not repair it
claim: helix_angles sizes the helix separately for every mesh with both shifts pinned and a given distance. A mesh group has one helix, so two such meshes in one group produce contradictory helices, and propagation silently keeps the first. The build then refuses with MeshError::Incompatible. The relief walk treats the group's one size entry as satisfying each mesh's relation separately, so it frees only the middle distance and the refusal remains.
evidence: Audit tests audit_two_sized_helices_in_one_group and audit_two_sized_relieved. line(&[20,30,25,35]).size_free(), all shifts fixed at 0, distances 0 and 2 given (25.5, 30.5): helices [11.139, -11.139, 10.182, -10.182], so member 1 is -11.139 and member 2 is +10.182 across an external mesh that needs opposite hands of equal size. Result: Err(Mesh(Incompatible)). After relieved(None): shifts auto [false, false, false, false], distance auto [false, true, false], and the solve is still Err(Mesh(Incompatible)).
proposal: Count the helix once per mesh group in the relief: freedoms() should emit one relation per mesh but make the group's size entry satisfy at most one of them (e.g. a FreedomGroup per mesh group with given_at_most = number of meshes - 1 over that group's pinned-distance relations). In helix_angles, size from the group's first qualifying mesh only, and emit a named refusal (e.g. TrainError::SizeOverConstrained { meshes }) if another mesh in the group would ask for a different helix.
validation: Extend every_input_relief_leaves_given_is_honoured_by_the_solve to line shapes with two or more pinned distances in one group, and to size_free shapes.

verdict.reason: Reproduced exactly. helix_angles (shape.rs:821-875) sizes every mesh that has both shifts pinned and a given distance, and it skips a mesh only when one of that mesh's own members already has a helix, never when its group does. Two such meshes in one helix group therefore get contradictory helices: member 1 at -11.139 and member 2 at +10.182, across an external mesh that needs equal and opposite. The build refuses with an opaque Mesh(Incompatible). relieved(None) leaves all four shifts, distances 0 and 2, and the size standing, so the relieved shape still fails. That breaks the stated contract that relief leaves only what the solve can honour. The relief law every_input_relief_leaves_given_is_honoured_by_the_solve (mod.rs:7938) sweeps only presets, and no preset has two pinned distances in one helix group, so nothing tests this.
verdict.evidence: Worktree run of audit_two_sized_helices_in_one_group. d0 25.5 / d2 30.5 gives helices [11.139, -11.139, 10.182, -10.182]; d2 31.0 gives [.., 14.45, -14.45]; d0 25.2 / d2 30.2 gives [6.85, .., 6.26, ..]. All three are Err(Mesh(Incompatible)). audit_two_sized_relieved: shifts auto [false; 4], dist auto [false, true, false], clr auto [false; 3], and the solve is still Err(Mesh(Incompatible)).
verdict.proposal_note: Sensible. In helix_angles, skip the sizing when any member of the mesh's group already has a helix, not only the mesh's own two members. Then the second pinned distance meets a NoCommonDistance-style refusal rather than Incompatible, and relief must count a group's size once against all its distance relations. Add a line(&[20,30,25,35]) case with two pinned distances to the relief law.

title: A stated pitch diameter below z*m silently becomes a 0 degree helix
claim: The pitch-diameter reading is acos((z*m/d).clamp(-1,1)). A diameter below z*m, which no helix can give, clamps to straight teeth with no note, against rule 5 ('clamp rather than refuse, and say so').
evidence: Audit test audit_pitch_diameter_below_floor, pair([12,40]) at m=1 with first diameter 3, 11.9 and 12: helix [0,0] and notes [] in each case. 12.5 gives 16.26 degrees and 14 gives 31.00 degrees.
proposal: When z*m/d > 1, raise a Note (e.g. key member.pitch_diameter_below_reference, values asked and floor) from the reading, and carry it into the part's notes the way params guards are.
validation: A test that d < z*m yields the note and d >= z*m does not; gear_io::strings then requires the catalogue entry in all five languages.

verdict.reason: The clamp is as described. In the core, d < z·m, and also d = 0, silently becomes 0° with no note on a parallel mesh. But the panel shows the pitch-diameter box only for worm members (TrainPanel.svelte:729: `pitchDiameter: isWormMember ? mem.pitch_diameter : undefined`), and on a crossed/worm mesh d ≤ z·m is refused as Screw(WormTooThin), not clamped. The silent case is reachable only through a TOML file, the API or the harness (with_first_diameter). A negative diameter is refused, but as Mesh(OutsideInvoluteDomain), a key that names the wrong cause.
verdict.evidence: Worktree runs. pair([12,40]).with_first_diameter(d) for d in {0, 1e-9, 3, 11.9, 12}: helix [0,0], notes 0; d = -12, -24 and -30 give Err(Mesh(OutsideInvoluteDomain)). worm(1,30).with_first_diameter(d) for d in {0.5, 0.99, 1.0}: Err(Screw(WormTooThin)); 1.01 gives helix 8.07°. Code: shape.rs:3994-3998 `(z1 / m.pitch_diameter.manual).clamp(-1.0, 1.0).acos()`.
verdict.proposal_note: Keep one reading, and make d ≤ 0 a refusal with its own key rather than OutsideInvoluteDomain. A note for 0 < d < z·m is consistent with rule 5, but that value is 'no shape' (no helix gives it), so by the same rule it arguably belongs among the refusals. Either way, the parallel and crossed paths should give the same answer for the same bad diameter, where today one clamps silently and the other refuses.

title: The tip-sizing walk and the solver brackets are full of unnamed tolerances and step constants
claim: Several constants are chosen by feel or written twice. The relative agreement 1e-9*max(|p|,1) appears twice (closed and build). absorb falls back to a +/-5.0 shift window. sized uses a 1% initial step, x1.5 growth, 40 and 80 iteration caps, 1e-12 and 1e-6 domain nudges and a 1e-9 'lean'. chosen_at runs 3 rounds and uses a 'moved' test of search.resolution*1e-3, which compares a dimensionless shift resolution with a distance in mm. The parallel helix bracket is [0, 89] degrees, size_reaching nudges by 1.000_001 and 1e-9 and grows for 60 doublings, and the teeth cache clears past 4096. The 'near self-locking' note fires at 0.8 x threshold and 'low efficiency' below 0.5; these are rules of thumb that are not user-visible and not in docs/.
evidence: Read at the listed lines. grep over docs/*.md finds no statement of the 0.8 or 0.5 note thresholds.
proposal: Name each one in one place with its reason: an AGREE_REL constant shared by closed/build, a TipWalk struct for the sizing walk, a distance tolerance in mm derived from the solver's Tol for the rounds test (not resolution*1e-3), and the absorb fallback taken from admissible_ranges or refused rather than +/-5. Make the two note thresholds explicit inputs of the report (or at least document them in docs/reference.md next to the self-locking section).
validation: check_golden unchanged after naming (pure refactor). For the rounds tolerance, audit_search_rounds shows the re-sized distance agrees to 4e-15 mm, so any tolerance of 1e-9 mm or more keeps behaviour.

verdict.reason: Most items check out, but several of the 'by feel' constants are justified where they stand, and one is a naming issue with no behavioural effect. Confirmed: the relative tolerance 1e-9·max(|p|,1) appears twice in production (shape.rs:1404 closed, shape.rs:2872 build), plus five more copies in tests. The rounds test at 1914 compares plan.held, which is distances in mm (a Vec<Option<f64>> per distance, shape.rs:1214), against search.resolution·1e-3, a dimensionless shift resolution (auto.rs:1717, 1e-3). The units are mixed, although the result is a benign 1e-6 mm. The 0.8×threshold near-locking note and the <0.5 low-efficiency note (shape.rs:2700, 2709) appear nowhere in docs/. The ±5.0 fallback (1479-1480) applies only when admissible_ranges gives no bound. Justified where they stand: the 1e-9 'lean' at 1700 ('by the solver's own tolerance'), the 1.000_001 floor nudge and the 4096 cache cap, each commented. The 0.8 and 0.5 thresholds govern only advisory notes, and those notes print the friction and the threshold, so the user sees the numbers but not the trigger.
verdict.evidence: Read shape.rs:1404, 1479-1480, 1620 (`* (1.0 + 1e-6)`), 1638 (`* 0.01`), 1700, 1876 (`for _ in 0..3`), 1914, 2700, 2709, 2824 and 2872. A grep of docs/*.md for 0.8, 'near ... lock', 'low efficiency' and '50 %' finds no statement of either note threshold. strings_en.toml:139-142 hold the note texts.
verdict.proposal_note: Priority order: (1) one shared AGREE_REL for the two production 1e-9 comparisons; (2) replace resolution·1e-3 with a tolerance in mm (it moves no answer); (3) state the 0.8 and 0.5 note triggers in reference.md next to self-locking, or better, have the note state its trigger. Wrapping the tip walk's step constants in a struct is cosmetic and low value.

title: absorb runs a bracketed Newton even when the absorber is not in the first mesh, where a closed form exists
claim: When the absorbing member has coefficient 0 in the first mesh (e.g. a ring absorbing after sun-planet), the target running distance is fixed. The absorber's shift then follows in closed form from shift_sum_reaching (the involute inverse, or the linear rack law on crossed shafts), exactly as the reaches branch in closed() already does. Only a member in both meshes (a planet) needs a root find.
evidence: absorb (lines 1416-1498) always builds a bracket, calls pull_in and then newton_bracketed. closed() lines 1350-1390 solve the same one-mesh relation in closed form via shift_sum_reaching.
proposal: In absorb, if coefficient(first) == 0, compute the target as running_of(first, x) mapped to nominal with kind.nominal_of, call shift_sum_reaching(m, nominal), and solve linearly for x_i. Keep Newton only for a member in both meshes. That shrinks the bracket, pull_in and fallback code to the one case that needs it.
validation: Bit-level or 1e-12 agreement of every preset's shifts before and after (check_golden), plus a test that a ring absorber's shift matches shift_sum_for directly.

verdict.reason: Holds. An absorber that sits in only one of the two meshes (a sun or a ring behind a sun-planet mesh; the layshaft's and compound's later-pair absorbers) leaves the other mesh's running distance fixed, so its shift follows from shift_sum_reaching plus one linear step. I built that closed form in a worktree test and it matches absorb() to at most 4.4e-15 on every one-mesh absorber in the presets and on the set's sun and ring absorbers. The Newton only earns its place for an absorber in both meshes (the planet). I also raised the severity from low to medium, because the Newton path changes behaviour as well as being slower. With a one-sided bracket, absorb falls back to the member's admissible profile-shift range, or a hard-coded +/-5. That caps the answer, so the solve refuses cases that have a shift. Neither the planet absorber nor the reaches branch in closed() has this cap.
verdict.evidence: Worktree test (diff saved at /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-shape-a-3/worktree.diff). Closed form vs absorb: layshaft absorbers 2 and 4, diff 9.2e-16; wolfrom absorber 2, 1.4e-15; compound absorber 4, 6.8e-16; planetary(12,30,72,3) with the sun absorbing, 2.4e-15; with the ring absorbing, 4.4e-15. Planet absorbers show coefficients cf=1, cm=1, which is the both-meshes case. Then planetary(12,30,72,3), sun and planet given at settled+dx, ring automatic. At dx=0.6 the closed form gives 1.81112 and absorb gives the same. At dx=0.7 the closed form gives a ring shift of 2.11246, and the planet-ring mesh then runs at 22.300774, exactly the sun-planet distance. absorb returns None because the ring's admissible range is -2.13..1.94 (shape.rs:1470-1476), and solve_alone refuses with 'no profile shift brings the meshes to one axis distance; these tooth counts cannot be assembled'. It refuses the same way at dx 0.8 to 2.0.
verdict.proposal_note: Generalise the proposal to an absorber in exactly one mesh on either side: coefficient 0 in `first`, or coefficient 0 in `m`, since absorbers() allows the first mesh's members while it is closed alone. Agreement will be within about 5e-15, not bit-level, so validate with check_golden and a 1e-12 law rather than bit equality. The change also removes the admissible-range cap and the +/-5 fallback for these absorbers. That is a behaviour change, and a welcome one, but it must be deliberate. An out-of-range shift should then go through the member builder's clamp-and-note, as the reaches branch already does ('a shift past what its cutter reaches is a part that says so through its clamps'). Add a test that the pushed-ring case above solves with a note instead of refusing.

title: The data model says one thing several ways: helix three ways with last-wins, per-group module stored per member, overlap duplicated by the panel, ring position by convention
claim: The model is not fully normalised. (1) A group's helix can be stated as a member's helix_angle, as its pitch_diameter, or as the first mesh's overlap, and helix_angles resolves conflicts by 'the last reading given' in list order. (2) module and pressure_angle are per-group quantities stored per member and kept equal by share() writing manual; normal_module() reads manual, which is only right after share(). (3) MeshInput.overlap is one number per group that the panel writes into every mesh of the group. (4) The ring must be MeshInput.b by convention: a ring as a gives kind_of == None, and absorbers and tooth_sum then silently treat it as external (map_or(1.0)), giving 'no profile shift brings the meshes to one axis distance'. (5) Distance allows duplicate entries for one axis pair (first wins), and axial_clearance is 'of the first axis's members', so its meaning depends on the order of Distance.axes while distance_of accepts either order.
evidence: Read at the listed lines. Audit test audit_malformed_graph: swapping a/b on the planetary's internal mesh is refused as 'no profile shift brings the meshes to one axis distance'; a duplicate distance is silently shadowed.
proposal: Target shape: a MeshGroup record, derived from the graph but holding module, pressure angle and one Size enum {Helix(Auto<f64>), PitchDiameter(member, f64), Overlap(f64)}, keyed by the group's lowest member so it survives edits, replacing the three per-member fields and the per-mesh overlap. Make MeshInput order-free by deriving the ring side (kind_of returns the ring's index). Key distances by unordered axis pair (validate uniqueness), and make axial_clearance name its axis. Migration: keep the current fields as serde input only, fold them into the group record in from_toml, and bump gear-io's change log.
validation: A round-trip law: every preset and every corpus file converted into the new model gives identical outputs (check_golden, check_wasm). A law that permuting mesh a/b or distance axes changes nothing.

verdict.reason: Each fact checks out on reading, but two of the five items are guarded, one is misread, and the proposed rebuild is out of proportion. (1) Three readings of one helix with last-wins resolution: relief keeps at most one reading per group, and every file is relieved on load (gear-io/src/train.rs:369-375). The helix_angles comment states this. Last-wins only reaches an unrelieved shape built in code, and that ordering is a deliberate fallback. (2) Module and pressure angle per member, written by share(): the doc says the solve shares before it reads. I found no wrong output, only fragility. (3) Is misread. MeshInput.overlap is deliberately per mesh: every mesh's overlap is a floor under its own automatic face width, and only the group's first mesh reads the helix (shape.rs:3610-3620 'the group's first mesh reads the size, every mesh's is a floor'). Only the panel collapses it to one number. (4) and (5) are real latent hazards, reachable only from a hand-written TOML file or code. With the ring as `a`, kind_of returns None and the refusal message is wrong. A duplicate distance is shadowed first-wins. The core's own constructors cannot produce either: push_mesh swaps the ring to `b` (arrangements.rs:430), and edits keep one distance per pair.
verdict.evidence: shape.rs:806-822 (last-wins with its comment); gear-io/src/train.rs:369-375 (relieved on load); shape.rs:100-117 and 1941-1965 (share before read); shape.rs:3610-3620 and the test at shape.rs:5547 (per-mesh overlaps 0.8 and 1.2 honoured); arrangements.rs:430 (push_mesh normalises the ring to b); edits.rs:834, where well_formed checks 'distance stated twice' but is #[cfg(test)] only and never checks the ring side. The auditor's log /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/shape-a/run1.log:155-157: the ring-first case is refused 'no profile shift brings the meshes...'; the duplicate case is refused by the shadowing entry's 1 mm distance ('below the base-circle limit').
verdict.corrected_claim: Two input invariants the solve relies on are never checked on input: the ring is MeshInput.b, and one Distance per unordered axis pair. A hand-written file that breaks either one gets a misleading refusal, or its duplicate entry silently shadowed. The helix, module and overlap representations are guarded by relief and share() and carry documented roles; overlap in particular is per mesh on purpose.
verdict.proposal_note: The MeshGroup/Size-enum migration is heavy, and as proposed it would lose the per-mesh face-width floor that overlap carries. A cheaper fix covers (4) and (5): promote edits.rs's well_formed (today #[cfg(test)]) to a production check at every entry that takes a graph (from_toml, and the wasm solve and edit entries), and add 'ring is b' to it. Alternatively, normalise the mesh on load with push_mesh's swap. Give each refusal a named key. Make axial_clearance name its axis, or define it as the lower-indexed axis's, which is independent of order. Leave the helix-reading design alone, or at most move the last-wins fallback behind the relief invariant as a debug_assert.

title: The thickness rule 'at most one given per mesh' does not bind a chain; the documented invariant is not what relief keeps
claim: Member::thickness_mod says the two k's of a mesh sum to 2 and 'relief keeps it so'. The FreedomGroup is per mesh, so a chain with k given on both ends keeps both, and propagation leaves the middle mesh summing to 1.9. The geometry stays consistent (the equivalent shift enters the shift sums), so the answer is not wrong; the stated invariant is.
evidence: Audit test audit_thickness_chain: line(&[20,30,25]) with k0=1.2 and k2=1.1 given, k1 automatic. After relief: given [(true,1.2),(false,1.0),(true,1.1)], thickness_mods [1.2, 0.8, 1.1], and mesh 1 sums to 1.9. Clearances [0.020, 0.020].
proposal: Either make the thickness freedom per mesh group (given_at_most 1 over the group, like module), or rewrite the doc to say the mate rule is the default for automatic members only and that a given k on both members of a mesh is honoured as a backlash choice.
validation: The relief law then covers it: every_input_relief_leaves_given_is_honoured over a chain fixture.

verdict.reason: Holds, and it is worse than stated. The thickness FreedomGroup is per mesh (shape.rs:4088-4097), so in a chain with k given at both ends, relief keeps both, and the automatic middle member follows only one mesh. The Member::thickness_mod doc (shape.rs:172-177, 'the two sum to 2 ... and relief keeps it so') is therefore false. Beyond the auditor's claim, which mesh the middle member follows is decided by the order of the mesh list. Reversing the mesh list of the same graph changes the middle gear's k from 0.8 to 0.9: the same train cut two ways depending on file order. So there is a behaviour defect as well as a stale doc.
verdict.evidence: Worktree test sa3_thickness_order: line(&[20,30,25]) with k0=1.2 and k2=1.1 given and k1 automatic, then relieved(None). The given flags stay [(true,1.2),(false,1.0),(true,1.1)]. thickness_mods() gives [1.2, 0.8, 1.1] in mesh order and [1.2, 0.9, 1.1] with s.meshes reversed. The propagation loop at shape.rs:1053-1075 takes the first mesh in list order that reaches an unset member.
verdict.proposal_note: Prefer the first option, with the relation stated per connected run: a given k fixes every member its meshes reach, so allow at most one given k per mesh group (given_at_most 1 over the group, like module). That removes both the false invariant and the order dependence. Rewriting only the doc would leave the order dependence in place. Add a law that permuting mesh order leaves thickness_mods unchanged.

title: Three hand-written union-finds in one file, two of them over the same mesh relation
claim: mesh_groups, asking_members and search_components each implement union-find (one with path compression, two without). asking_members and search_components build the same mesh relation (meshes on an automatic distance, meshes sharing a free member) in slightly different ways, which invites the two to disagree about what a component is.
evidence: Read at the listed lines. asking_members unions meshes sharing any Free member. search_components unions through search axes, which are Free members that ask.
proposal: One small DisjointSet in a util module. Compute the component relation once as a Plan method, fn components(&self, plan) -> Vec<MeshComponent>, and derive both asking_members and the search components from it.
validation: Existing laws plus an assertion that each search component's meshes are exactly one asking component.

verdict.reason: Holds, and the count is five, not three. shape.rs has three hand-written union-finds: mesh_groups (a closure, no compression, root = min), asking_members (no compression) and search_components (full path compression). graph.rs has two more: graph_of at line 64 and Shape::parts at line 234 (one-step compression). parts' first step, members joined by meshes, is the same relation as mesh_groups. asking_members and search_components build the same component relation, the second restricted to free members that ask. They agree today because the asking filter keeps whole components, but that equivalence is not asserted anywhere.
verdict.evidence: grep 'fn find' in crates/gear-core/src gives train/graph.rs:64, train/graph.rs:234, train/shape.rs:1996 and train/shape.rs:2060, plus the closure at train/shape.rs:1090. Read shape.rs:1993-2044 (asking_members) and 2051-2110 (search_components).
verdict.proposal_note: Put one DisjointSet in a small crate-private module and use it at all five sites, not only the three in shape.rs. Let mesh_groups be derived from the same member-mesh relation that Shape::parts starts from.

title: Comments cite retired code and narrate history
claim: absorb's doc says it is 'a bracketed Newton, as `planetary::solve` absorbs into the planet', but no planetary::solve exists (grep of train/planetary.rs and planetary.rs finds no fn solve). About ten comments explain behaviour by the retired stage types ('the hula's own solver', 'what one switch on the stage used to mean', 'it was the stage's until the stage went'). A reader without the history cannot use them.
evidence: grep -n 'stage|hula's own solver|used to|retired' in shape.rs lines 1-3100 lists the lines given.
proposal: Drop the planetary::solve reference. Restate each historical comment as the present reason (e.g. line 1863: 'searching held-distance components apart is the same optimum at a fraction of the trials'), and leave the history to docs/corrections.md.
validation: check_doc_links still passes; a review read.

verdict.reason: Holds. No planetary::solve exists anywhere in the crate: grep finds only the comment itself at shape.rs:1414. The history-narrating comments are present at the cited lines (82, 1582, 1756, 1863, 1872, 1973, 2189, 2344, 3023), and there are more past line 3100: the 'which used to be a field on the type' impl doc near line 3930, and the 'It was one relation per *distance*...' paragraph in freedoms(). Line 1872's 'Three at most; the second usually moves nothing and the third never has' is also a dated measurement standing in for the reason behind the literal 3.
verdict.evidence: grep -rn 'fn solve' in crates/gear-core/src/planetary.rs and train/planetary.rs returns nothing. grep 'planetary::solve' returns only shape.rs:1414. The awk/grep over shape.rs lines 1-3100 lists 82, 1582, 1756, 1863, 1872, 1973, 2189 and 3023.
verdict.proposal_note: When rewording line 1872, also give the round limit a stated reason, or replace it with a convergence test (stop when the sized distance moves by less than the solver tolerance) with a cap, rather than a count recorded from observation.

title: chosen_at, sized, plan_held and helix_angles are 100-220-line functions mixing several concerns
claim: chosen_at (1717-1934, about 217 lines) holds the fallback, interval building, coordinate transform, box, placement, components, rounds and assembly. sized (about 143 lines) holds two bracket walks. plan_held about 110 and helix_angles about 105. Their closures capture the enclosing state, which is part of why the plan-order and search-division bugs above were hard to see.
evidence: Line counts from the reads.
proposal: Split chosen_at into SearchSpace::new(plan, free, intervals) (coordinates, box, place), search_components and a rounds loop. Split sized into one sizing per distance returning Option<(f64, usize)>, with the two walks as one bracket_monotone(room, from, dir) helper. The helix-sizing loop in helix_angles becomes a size_from_distance(k) function.
validation: Pure refactor: nextest, check_golden and check_wasm unchanged.

verdict.reason: The line counts check out exactly, and sized() does hold two hand-rolled bracket walks with feel-chosen constants. The claim that the long closures are why earlier bugs were hard to see is conjecture, and I discount it. The refactor itself is sound and behaviour-neutral as proposed.
verdict.evidence: Measured by brace matching: chosen_at is shape.rs:1717-1934 (218 lines), sized 1568-1711 (144), plan_held 1222-1332 (111), helix_angles 802-905 (104). sized's walks at 1631-1690 use step 0.01*from, growth 1.5, iteration caps of 40 and 80, a 1e-12 step floor and a 1e-9 lean. room_at re-plans (plan_held) on every evaluation.
verdict.proposal_note: When extracting bracket_monotone, state its constants once, derived from the involute domain's floor and `reach` (already computed at 1640) instead of the 40/80 iteration caps. The helper could then serve helix_angles' and size_reaching's bracketing too.

title: chain_on on an emptied train reads a stale body-list index: panic, or case entries on the wrong bodies
claim: lay() returns the new shape's input and output as positions in shape.bodies. In the k==0 branch, chain_on merges the input with the first parked body, then reads body(self, output) at the old position. When the emptied train still lists a parked body, the merge shortens the list. The output position then points past the end (panic) or at the wrong body. The emptied train still lists parked bodies after removing the planet axis of a Planetary, Wolfrom or Planocentric: drop_bare keeps a body a case names, and drop_orphans returns early when there are no members. lay's doc assumes the opposite: 'which no merge with a body nothing lists reorders'. The comment 'so the second is read afresh' is also wrong: it re-reads the body's number, but at a position that has already moved.
evidence: probe repro3/repro8. Wolfrom, then Remove(Axis(1)), which offers() lists as allowed, leaves bodies [(1,0)] with cases [(1 Load),(2 Reacted)]. Then offers(Target::Train) panics: 'index out of bounds: the len is 2 but the index is 2' at conditions.rs:1198:67, backtrace chain_on <- Train::edit <- Train::offers. Insert Spur, Worm or Crossed at None panics the same way. Insert Idler gives a case reacted at 3 and a headline path 1->3 with ratio -1.4706, against 1->2 at 2.5294 for a fresh Idler: the idler shaft is reported as the output. Insert Layshaft gives path 1->3 at -2.5294 instead of 1->2 at 2.3662. Planocentric, then Remove(Axis(1)), leaves bodies [(1,0),(2,0)]. Then Insert Spur gives bodies [(2,0),(1,0),(3,1)] and cases [(2 Load),(1 Reacted)]: roles swapped, both on the input shaft, the spur's output in no case, and paths None. The same happens for every preset (repro4: 'DIFFERENT' for all 10). The random walks hit the panic from 5 different edit sequences. In wasm a panic traps the instance.
proposal: Make the emptied state match lay's assumption, rather than patching indices. When an edit leaves the shape with no members, Train::edit clears it to Shape::default(): no bodies, no axes, no distances. The cases stay parked by number, as drop_orphans already intends. Then no parked body is listed, a merge never shortens the list, and chain_on's k==0 branch is correct as written. Belt and braces: have lay() return body numbers instead of list positions, and have chain_on map them through a renumber map that merge/prune return, so no position is read after a merge.
validation: A new law in offers.rs: for every preset P and every removal offered on it that leaves no members, offers(Target::Train) does not panic. For every preset Q, Insert{Q, at: None} then gives the same cases and holds as chain(&[Q]), with each parked load and reaction at Q's conventional input and output. Extend the_cases_survive_an_emptied_train_and_take_the_next_preset_conventionally, which already empties a Planetary via Remove(Axis(1)) at mod.rs:7325 and stops one step short, with a chain_on of a Spur.

verdict.reason: Reproduced independently with my own probe. The mechanism holds as described. lay() returns list positions (conditions.rs:1236, `(at + input - 1, at + output - 1)`). In chain_on's k==0 branch (1197-1208), the first merge renames the parked listed body onto the new input and dedups `shape.bodies`, which shortens the list. `body(self, output)` then indexes a stale position. lay's doc says 'no merge with a body nothing lists reorders', but here the parked body is listed: drop_bare keeps a body a case names (1120-1141), and drop_orphans returns early on an empty shape (341-346). Remove(Axis(1)) is offered unrefused on Planetary, Wolfrom, Planocentric, Compound and MeshedPlanets.
verdict.evidence: Probe probes/verify-edit-ops-1 (f0). Wolfrom then Remove(Axis(1)) leaves bodies [(1,0)] with cases [(1 Load),(2 Reacted)]. After that, offers(Target::Train) PANICS, and so do Insert Spur and Insert Worm at None. Insert Idler solves, but its headline path is 1->3 at -1.4706 against 1->2 at 2.5294 for a fresh Idler, so the idler shaft is taken as the output. Planocentric then Remove(Axis(1)) leaves bodies [(1,0),(2,0)]. Insert Spur then gives bodies [(2,0),(1,0),(3,1)] and cases [(2 Load),(1 Reacted)]: both entries sit on one shaft, and path is None against a fresh (1,2,-2.5294). The same holds for Idler and Worm. Planetary and Compound, emptied, come out correct: nothing stays listed, or the listed body is the one merged second. The existing test at mod.rs:7325 empties a Planetary and stops before a chain_on.
verdict.proposal_note: Adopt the primary fix: clear the shape to Shape::default() whenever an edit leaves no members. It restores lay's stated precondition and keeps the parked cases, which drop_orphans already leaves alone. The 'belt and braces' half, where lay returns body numbers and merge returns a renumber map, is worth doing too. Once the list can no longer hold a parked body, it is optional.

repro.reproduction:
Probe crate /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/repro-edit-ops-0/src/main.rs uses only the public API. The smallest input: `Train::chained(vec![Preset::Wolfrom.build()], chain_ends case)`, then `t.edit(Edit::Remove(Piece::Axis(1)))`. `t.offers(Target::Axis(1))` lists this removal with refused=None. Then call `t.offers(Target::Train)`, or `t.edit(Edit::Insert{shape: Preset::Spur.build(), at: None})`. Run with: CARGO_TARGET_DIR=/home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probe-target /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/gc /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/repro-edit-ops-0 cargo run --offline -q.

I also ran it on the compiled payload. I ran wasm-bindgen --target nodejs on target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/wasm/gear_wasm.wasm into notes/repro-edit-ops-0/pkg, then ran notes/repro-edit-ops-0/trap.cjs. That script sets the default train's shape to the "wolfrom" preset, calls edit_train {graph:{remove:{axis:1}}}, then calls offers {at:"train"} and edit_train insert spur at null.

I checked what is correct in two ways that do not share the chain_on code. A fresh `chain(&[Q])` of the same preset is one. Hand ratios from the tooth counts are the other: Idler 17→25→43 gives +43/17 = 2.5294. Layshaft 17/43 then 29/31 gives (43·29)/(17·31) = 2.3662.
repro.observed:
Wolfrom, emptied: bodies [(1,0)], held [], cases [[(1 Load),(2 Reacted)]], 0 members.
- offers(Train) panics with "index out of bounds: the len is 2 but the index is 2" at conditions.rs:1198:67 (`train.shape.bodies[entry].body` in chain_on's k==0 branch). Insert Spur panics the same way.
- Insert Idler raises no error but is wrong. Case [(1 Load),(3 Reacted)], headline path 1→3 at −1.4706 (= −25/17, the idler shaft). A fresh Idler gives 1→2 at +2.5294 (= 43/17).
- Insert Layshaft gives path 1→3 at −2.5294 (= −43/17, the layshaft). The fresh value is 1→2 at 2.3662.

Planocentric, emptied: bodies [(1,0),(2,0)]. offers does not panic, but every insert is wrong.
- Insert Spur gives bodies [(2,0),(1,0),(3,1)] and cases [(2 Load),(1 Reacted)]. Both case entries land on the one new input shaft, the spur's output 3 is in no case, and paths is None. The fresh Spur gives (1,2,−2.5294).
- Idler and Layshaft come out the same way (paths None).

In wasm, both offers and edit_train throw "RuntimeError: unreachable", so the panic traps the instance. A later defaults() call on the same instance still answered in node.
repro.note:
Confirmed by execution, native and in the shipped .wasm. The mechanism matches the ledger. lay() returns list positions. The first merge in chain_on's k==0 branch dedups `shape.bodies`, because the emptied train still lists a parked body: drop_bare keeps it, since a case names it, and drop_orphans returns early when there are no members. `body(self, output)` then reads a stale index, which runs past the end (Wolfrom) or lands on the wrong body (Planocentric, Idler/Layshaft on Wolfrom).

Severity stays high:
- the trigger is an edit the core itself offers as allowed;
- the panel's next offers(train) call then traps;
