evidence: grep: ShaperCut is constructed only in ring.rs:408 and by equivalent_to_rack in tests.
proposal: If wanted, add a cutter choice to GearParams (rack or pinion cutter with z_c, h_a0, ρ_0). The unified RollingCorner makes the rack κ = 0 of the same input, so no branch is needed. Otherwise, say in the header that the external shaper exists as the limit instrument only.
validation: The same envelope gates as the ring, run on external shaper-cut teeth.

verdict.evidence:
- grep 'ShaperCut::': constructed only at ring.rs:408 and ring.rs:452 (fallback), and by equivalent_to_rack at shaper.rs:552-857, inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests from line 532.
- ShaperCut's methods (shaper.rs:148-485): new, reference_centre_distance, corner_centre_at, trochoid_at, trochoid_point_and_tangent, trochoid_curvature_radius, and private helpers. There is no junction, limit or outline.
- corrections.md:440: 'this crate's external gear is rack-cut'.
verdict.corrected_claim: ShaperCut computes the fillet (trochoid) of an external workpiece correctly, but only as the test instrument for the rack limit. No tooth, outline, strength or metrology path exists for a shaper-cut external gear, and nothing in GearParams or the train can ask for one. The header table in shaper.rs reads as if the case were supported.
verdict.proposal_note: The cheap part is to relabel the table row 'external gear, shaper — the fillet only, as the rack limit's instrument (tests)', and to make equivalent_to_rack #[cfg(test)] or pub(crate). The real feature belongs with lens-unification #2 (one tooth generated by one tool of signed pitch curvature), not with a new GearParams field bolted onto Tooth.

title: The profile jumps at the severing threshold (physical, but unflagged as a discontinuity)
claim: At the shift, dedendum or thickness where the fillets first meet on the centreline, r_a drops by 1.3–2.6 mm and u_j becomes NaN. This is correct: the part above the neck detaches. But it is the one place the profile is discontinuous in its inputs, and the searches over shift read r_a.
evidence:
sweep_out.txt (earlier run, 20,000-step sweeps):
- z=5 in x: r_a jumps 1.584 at x = −0.5397
- z=8 in x: 1.300 at x = −0.9551
- z=8 in h_f: 2.55 at h_f = 2.4836
- tooth-form-2 `cont`, z=5 in k: 0.968 at k = 0.1976

No other jump appears in x, root round, addendum, pressure angle, dedendum, helix angle or thickness modification.
proposal: None to the geometry. Make sure every search that reads r_a treats severed as infeasible rather than as a small r_a, and state the jump in reference.md#the-generated-profile.
validation: A law that no auto search returns a severed tooth.

verdict.reason: The geometry part holds, and I checked it independently. At the severing threshold r_a, r_j, s_j and theta_a jump and u_j becomes NaN. This is the physical detachment. Across 3.6M teeth it is the only jump in the profile along x. Two parts do not hold. (1) 'Unflagged' is wrong: every severed tooth carries clamp.tooth_severed and the panel shows ui.gear_severed. strength.rs refuses to rate it. reference.md:125-128 documents the truncation, and corrections.md:577 with tests/geometry_laws.rs:254-270 records that tip and root stop being exact where the profile is truncated. (2) Half the proposal is already implemented: member_is_buildable (auto.rs:1022) refuses `tooth.severed` unconditionally, even with 'no undercut' off, and every search objective passes through MeshTrial/CrossedTrial::efficiency (auto.rs:1189, 1237; shape.rs:2208-2270). It is also redundant in practice, because the other refusals already reject every severed member I tried. What survives is a wording fix and an advisory threshold the shift range does not publish (reported under missed). A related regime is already reported as lens-numerical-robustness #3: just above the threshold, for z >= 9, the junction lies above the tip (r_j > r_a on 142,882 of the 3.6M swept teeth).
verdict.evidence:
Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-tooth-form-f12 bisects the thresholds to 1e-13, at m=1 with default params. Jump in r_a along x: z=3 at x=-0.15200: 1.839; z=4 at -0.34987: 1.707; z=5 at -0.53959: 1.569; z=6 at -0.69751: 1.459; z=7 at -0.83404: 1.368; z=8 at -0.95505: 1.288; z=9 at -1.06423: 1.219; z=10 at -1.16403: 1.156. Along other inputs: z=8 in h_f at 2.483571: 2.537. z=5 in k at 0.197665: 0.962. z=5, x=-0.5, in rho at 0.23125: 1.595. z=5, x=-0.54, in beta at 1.2514 deg: 1.569. Along the addendum there is no threshold. At m=3 the z=8 jump is 3.865, so the jump scales with the module and '1.3-2.6 mm' is an m=1 figure. After severing r_a is below r_b in every case (z=10: 3.68 < 4.70; z=8 h_f: 2.46 < 3.76), so no involute is left.

Independent swept-rack check: notes/verify-tooth-form-f12/sweep_check.py builds the rack from m, alpha, h_f, rho and x only and shares no code with the crate. At z=5, x = threshold - 1e-5, the rack cuts the tooth centreline away over [1.387345, 1.396]. The lower edge equals the code's r_a to 4.8e-14 mm, and material survives on the centreline above that band up to the tip at 2.96, so the upper part is an island cut free. At threshold + 1e-5 nothing below r_a is removed; the least clearance is 8.3e-6 mm, and 1.66e-3 mm at +2e-3, so the neck closes continuously. z=8 gives the same result, with the lower edge equal to r_a to 2.6e-14 mm.

Other jumps: 60,000-step x sweeps over z=5-14, alpha 14.5/20/25 and beta 0/30 (3.6M teeth) in ra, rf, r_j, theta_a, theta0, rho and st. There are 144 steps larger than 30 times their neighbours, all at severing flips, and 0 elsewhere.

Search gate: I used Cut::Pinned to bypass member_is_buildable and ran 305,000 severed pinions (z 3-12, 100 shifts below each threshold) against wheels (z 12-200, x -1..2). Of the 189,825 meshes and paths that built, none passed MeshTrial's remaining refusals, even with min_contact_ratio 0. For a severed tooth flank_ends gives junction = tip (tooth.rs:286-291). shifts_for_efficiency with no undercut floor, for z1 4-10 against z2 20/40/80, chooses pinion shifts of +0.43 to +0.73, at least 1 module above any severing threshold. The existing law every_preset_chooses_a_member_that_can_be_cut (train/mod.rs:10145) asserts !severed, but its presets never approach severing.

Wording: reference.md:125-126 ('the cutter has removed the whole tooth'), tooth.rs:202 ('removed the tooth entirely') and tooth.rs:638-640 all describe removing the whole tooth. The swept check shows the cutter removes only a band at the neck; the stump below it survives and the part above falls away.
verdict.corrected_claim: At the severing threshold (in x, h_f, k, rho or beta) the tip radius drops from the addendum asked for to the neck, about 1.2-1.8 modules along x, 2.5 along h_f and 1.0 along k. The neck lies below the base circle, and r_j, s_j and theta_a jump with it. The jump is physical: the two fillets meet on the centreline and the part above falls away. It is the only jump in the tooth profile, and it is already flagged: a clamp note, the panel's severed line, and a strength refusal. Every search refuses a severed member through member_is_buildable, and the other mesh refusals would refuse it anyway. What is missing is precise wording in the docs, plus a severing threshold in the published shift range (see missed).
verdict.proposal_note: Geometry: no change, agreed. The search half of the proposal is already implemented and enforced twice over. A law that no search returns a severed tooth would only restate the member_is_buildable check, and the presets could never fail it on severing, so it is not worth adding. The documentation change is worth making, but as a correction rather than a new statement. Replace 'the cutter has removed the whole tooth' in reference.md:125-126, tooth.rs:202 and tooth.rs:638-640 with: 'the two fillets cross on the centreline, so the tooth is cut through there and what lies above falls away; r_a becomes the radius of the lower crossing, below the base circle in every case measured, so no involute remains; this is a drop of about 1.2-1.8 modules from the addendum asked for, flagged by clamp.tooth_severed'. Quote the jump in modules, not mm. The more useful change is to announce the threshold before it is crossed; see the missed item.

title: Gear tab box text goes stale: setKind and neighbouring edits change params without updating the box, so the gear drawn and exported is not the one the boxes show
claim: `raw` (the text in each FIELDS box) is set once from tab.params when the panel mounts and is written again only by onInput and sizeByThrow. setKind resets every parameter the new kind hides to its default (dedendum and root_radius for internal; angular_shift and index_offset for non-eccentric) but leaves raw alone. After a round trip of kinds, the box shows the old typed text while params, and so the solve, the drawing and the DXF, hold the default. The same happens with `errors`: a value refused against a bound keeps its error, and params keep the old value, even after another field moves the bound so that the typed text would now be valid.
evidence: grep 'raw' GearPanel.svelte: writes only at L122 (onInput) and L189 (sizeByThrow off). setKind (state.svelte.ts:267-278) does `tab.params = {...tab.params, [f.key]: fallback[f.key]}` for fields outside the kind. Scenario: external tab, type dedendum 1.4 (params 1.4, raw '1.4') -> internal (params.dedendum = 1.25, field hidden) -> external: the box shows 1.4 and the solve uses 1.25 (default read from p6: dedendum 1.25). App.svelte keys the panel by tab id, so nothing remounts it.
proposal: Stop holding a second copy of the value. Keep raw text only while the box has focus, or while its text does not parse: derive the displayed text from tab.params[f.key] unless an unparsed draft exists for that key, and clear the draft whenever params[f.key] changes from outside (an $effect keyed on the param, or clear all drafts in setKind). Recompute `errors` as $derived from the drafts and the current bounds instead of storing them. Better still, this becomes the single NumberBox component proposed in the decomposition finding.
validation: A component test (vitest + @testing-library/svelte): type dedendum 1.4, switch kind to internal and back, and assert the input's value equals String(tab.params.dedendum). Type an out-of-bound shift, raise teeth so it becomes admissible, and assert the error clears and params take the typed value.

verdict.reason: Holds as stated. `raw` is seeded once from tab.params when the panel mounts (GearPanel.svelte:37-39). Only onInput (L122) and sizeByThrow (L189) write it. setKind (state.svelte.ts:267-278) resets dedendum and root_radius (kinds external/eccentric, core.ts:395,402) and angular_shift and index_offset (eccentric only) in tab.params, and leaves raw alone. App.svelte:91 keys GearPanel on workspace.selected.id, so a kind change does not remount the panel. When the hidden field comes back, its input renders value={raw[f.key]}, which is the old text, while `request` is built from tab.params, which holds the default. `errors[key]` is recomputed only on that key's own input, so an error survives a change in the bound it was checked against. The only other writer of params is Workspace.adopt, which makes a fresh tab and so a fresh mount. That path is fine.
verdict.evidence: grep: raw written only at GearPanel.svelte:122 and :189. setKind at state.svelte.ts:267-278 writes `tab.params = {...tab.params, [f.key]: fallback[f.key]}`. The defaults() gear params are dedendum 1.25, root_radius 0.38 and angular_shift 0 (read from the wasm defaults()). Two concrete paths: dedendum external -> internal -> external, and angular_shift eccentric -> external -> eccentric. In both the box shows the typed text and the solve, drawing and DXF use the default.
verdict.proposal_note: The fix is right: derive the displayed text from params unless a draft for that key exists, clear drafts in setKind, and make `errors` a $derived. The proposed validation assumes vitest and @testing-library/svelte, but web/package.json has no test framework at all. Adding one means new devDependencies, which changes the fixed-output hash `nix build .#web` checks over package-lock.json, plus a new CI row. Either budget that, or cover this with a pure-TS draft/params reducer that tsc and a small node script can test.

repro.reproduction:
I ran the real GearPanel.svelte against the real wasm core in jsdom, working on a copy of web/. The project was not touched: no worktree, no files written in it. Setup: /home/user/gearcalc/web was copied with rsync to /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/repro-web-0/web, its node_modules copied, and vitest, jsdom and @testing-library/svelte installed there with --no-save. The testing-library render could not be used because its .svelte.js file is not compiled under node_modules, so the test mounts through svelte's own mount(). ResizeObserver and canvas getContext are stubbed. The wasm is loaded with initSync, then loadCore() and workspace.initialise() run. The test is test/stale.test.ts in that directory. Run it with: cd /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/repro-web-0/web && nix develop /home/user/gearcalc -c npx vitest run test/stale.test.ts. It fails 4 of 4. Each test asserts what a fixed panel would show.
Smallest input (default gear: m=1, z=9, dedendum 1.25): type 1.4 in the Dedendum box, set Type to Internal, then back to External.
repro.observed:
1. Dedendum, external -> internal -> external. After typing, the box shows 1.4 and params.dedendum is 1.4. On internal, params.dedendum is 1.25 (setKind reset it). Back on external, the box shows "1.4" but params.dedendum is 1.25. The solve, drawing and DXF use 1.25: root diameter 6.5 mm, where the box's 1.4 would give 6.2 mm. Independent check: d_f = d - 2(h_f - x)m, so the difference is 2(1.4 - 1.25)(1) = 0.3 mm. It scales with the module, so at m = 5 it is 1.5 mm, and the export carries it silently.
2. angular_shift, eccentric -> external -> eccentric (eccentric is developer-mode only, so developer.enabled was set true). The box shows "0.1" and params.angular_shift is 0.
3. Stale error. Typing addendum -0.5 is refused (min -0.271) and params keep 1. Profile shift 0.5 then lowers the core's bound to -0.771, so -0.5 is now admissible. The field still carries the error, params stay 1, and the one label says both "above -0.771: tooth must have height" and "must be at least -0.2713832022347944". That contradiction is on screen.
4. Reverse case (a step beyond the ledger). With dedendum 1, root radius 0.5 is accepted (max 0.572). Setting dedendum back to 1.25 drops the max to 0.448. params keep 0.5 and no error is shown. The wasm solve accepts rr=0.5 and emits only clamp.tooth_undercut, a note that is about undercut, not the root radius.
Correct behaviour, the test's oracle: each box's text equals String(tab.params[key]) unless there is an unparsed draft, and the error state follows the current ranges. Cases 1 and 2 are wrong against that directly. Cases 3 and 4 are wrong against the core's own reported ranges.
repro.note:
Confirmed by execution, and the claim holds in full. Severity: high for the kind round trip. The boxes silently disagree with the geometry being drawn and exported, and that path is open to every user through the Internal kind (the eccentric path needs developer mode). The drawing does show the truth, which only partly softens this. The stale error (case 3) is medium: the refusal is visible, but it is wrong and contradicts the bound printed next to it. Case 4 is new: an accepted value is left outside a bound that later tightens, with no error shown. The proposed fix covers it if `errors` is derived from params plus drafts against the current ranges, rather than only from drafts.
On the ledger's validation: component tests do work here with vitest, jsdom and a plain svelte mount. The obstacle the verdict raised stands, though: adding devDependencies changes package-lock.json and therefore the `nix build .#web` fixed-output hash. The alternative of a pure-TS reducer test also stands.
Everything is in /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/repro-web-0/web: test/stale.test.ts (the repro), test/ranges.test.ts (a probe of which inputs move which bounds) and vitest.config.ts. No worktree was created.

title: Clearing or half-typing the train's addendum sends NaN, which fails the whole train request at the boundary
claim: boundedNumber writes `e.currentTarget.valueAsNumber` directly. That is NaN for an empty box, a lone '-', or any unparsable text. JSON.stringify writes NaN as null and serde refuses it, so solveTrain returns ui.train_boundary_failed with an English serde message. ports, groupings, flows and names all come back empty, and the flow list, the case rows and the gear names disappear while the designer types. The `finite()` guard at L397-406 exists for exactly this and says so ('A box cleared keeps the number it held'), but boundedNumber, the addendum's row, does not use it. Because editTrain also reports a boundary failure as success (see the editTrain finding), every Offers click on such a train silently does nothing.
evidence: Probe p1: setting shape.members[0].gear.addendum = NaN and calling solve_train gives 'bad train request: data did not match any variant of untagged enum Either at line 1 column 1349'. L1765: `oninput={(e) => set(e.currentTarget.valueAsNumber)}`. Every other plain number row goes through `bind:value={get, finite(set)}`.
proposal: Route boundedNumber through the same guard: `oninput={(e) => finite(set)(e.currentTarget.valueAsNumber)}`, or better, the shared NumberBox. Also make core.ts refuse to send a non-finite number: a replacer in JSON.stringify that throws on NaN or Infinity, so the fault is caught on this side and named.
validation: A unit test on the row: dispatch input events with '', '-' and 'abc', and assert gear.addendum is unchanged and solveTrain(...).failure is null.

verdict.reason: Holds. The boundedNumber snippet uses `oninput={(e) => set(e.currentTarget.valueAsNumber)}` (TrainPanel.svelte:1765). The `finite()` guard is not applied there, although its own comment (L397-403) describes this exact failure. valueAsNumber is NaN for an empty box, and for a lone '-', which comes up mid-typing because the addendum may be negative. JSON.stringify writes NaN as null, and serde refuses it. solveTrain (core.ts:768) then returns the catch branch, which empties ports, groupings, flows and names. It recovers on the next valid keystroke, so this is transient, which is why the severity is medium rather than high. I did not verify the editTrain part, which depends on a separate finding.
verdict.evidence: My node probe against web/src/wasm/gear_wasm.js: shape.members[0].gear.addendum = NaN -> 'THROW bad train request: data did not match any variant of untagged enum Either at line 1 column 1349'. JSON.stringify({a:NaN}) -> '{"a":null}'. Every other plain number row uses `bind:value={get, finite(set)}` (for example L1723 in numberField).
verdict.proposal_note: The one-line fix `finite(set)(valueAsNumber)` is sufficient and matches the file's own convention. A JSON.stringify replacer that throws on non-finite numbers is a good belt-and-braces addition, and it should raise a catalogued ui key, not English.

title: Material override box: clearing it writes an override of 0 (Number('') = 0), a comma silently restores the library value, and an unsolved box shows a made-up 0
claim: `property()` parses with `Number(e.currentTarget.value)`. For type=number, value is '' when the box is empty, and also when the text is unparsable in the browser's locale (for example '1,5' in an English-locale Chrome). Number('') is 0, which is finite, so clearing the box sets the override to 0 and un-greys it. An elastic modulus of 0 makes the train fail with error.train_no_contact, a message about contact rather than about the empty box. Separately, `value={override ?? used?.value ?? 0}` shows 0 as the material's value whenever neither an override nor a library or solved value is known, which is a number nobody computed.
evidence: Probe p1: material_overrides.elastic_modulus = 0 gives failure {key:'error.train_no_contact', part:1}. Code L1051-1053: `const v = Number(e.currentTarget.value); gear.material_overrides[key] = Number.isFinite(v) ? v : null;`
proposal: Treat an empty box as 'no new number yet' and leave the stored override as it was, as finite() does elsewhere. Clearing an override already has its own control, the × button. Parse with valueAsNumber. Show '' rather than 0 when nothing is known.
validation: A component test: clear the E box and assert the override is unchanged and there is no failure; type 2e5 and assert the override is 2e5; with no library match, assert the box is empty.

verdict.reason: The main claim holds. Number('') is 0, so clearing the box writes an override of 0 and un-greys it, and E = 0 fails the train with error.train_no_contact. A blank `used` shows a greyed 0, against the panel's own BLANK convention (L390-396). The second claim is wrong: a comma does not 'silently restore the library value'. For type=number the browser sanitises unparsable text to value '' (Chrome and Firefox both do this), so '1,5' in an English locale also gives Number('') = 0 and an override of 0. The `Number.isFinite(v) ? v : null` branch is effectively unreachable from this input.
verdict.evidence: TrainPanel.svelte:1049-1053: `value={gear.material_overrides[key] ?? used?.value ?? 0}` and `const v = Number(e.currentTarget.value); gear.material_overrides[key] = Number.isFinite(v) ? v : null;`. Probe: material_overrides.elastic_modulus = 0 -> failure {key:'error.train_no_contact', part:1}.
verdict.corrected_claim: Clearing the box, or typing text the browser cannot parse (such as '1,5' in an English locale), writes an override of 0, because value is '' and Number('') is 0. The train then fails with an unrelated contact error. The null (restore) branch is unreachable, and a box with no known value shows a made-up greyed 0.
verdict.proposal_note: Use valueAsNumber with the same finite() guard as the other rows, so a NaN leaves the override as it was. The × button is the way to restore. Render BLANK when neither an override nor a used value exists.

title: The internal-gear (ring) tab validates and annotates its inputs against an external gear's ranges
claim: `result = solve(request)` always solves params as an external gear, even when the tab is internal. onInput validates every field with `boundFor(f.key, result.ok.ranges)`, and notesFor/boundNote/shiftNote print those ranges under the ring's fields (undercut, sharp-rack undercut, pointed, addendum minimum). RingSummary carries no ranges, so the ring has no bounds of its own to show. A ring input the ring model accepts is refused, and the numbers printed under the ring's profile shift describe a different part. (The train panel does this right: it deliberately shows no shift bound for a shaper-cut member, TrainPanel.svelte:1548-1551.)
evidence: Probe p6: the external solve at z=60 gives profile_shift bound [-2.130, 1.942] and undercut -2.450. solve_ring with z=60 returns ok for x = -1.5, -0.8, 0.8, 1.5 and 2.5. The ring tab would refuse 2.5 ('at most 1.942') and keep the previous shift. An internal tab also runs an unneeded external solve on every change.
proposal: Have solve_ring return `ranges: Ranges`, built from what limits a ring (base circle, the cutter's reach, the generation limit; docs/reference.md#internal-gears). Make `bounds` a $derived picking ring.ok.ranges or result.ok.ranges by kind, and compute `result` only when not internal. Until the core reports ring ranges, show no bound for internal tabs rather than the external one, as the train panel does.
validation: A wasm probe step: solve_ring's ranges.profile_shift contains every x the ring solve builds without a refusal, over a sweep. A component test: an internal tab at z=60 accepts x=2.5.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is right: an internal tab validates and annotates against the external solve's ranges (GearPanel.svelte:125, 47, 89, 106), and RingSummary carries no ranges. The stated consequence is wrong, though. x = 2.5 at z = 60 is not an input the ring model accepts: solve_ring returns ok only because it clamps, reporting clamp.ring_space_capped, clamp.ring_space_closed and clamp.cutter_no_tip_corner. The upper end of the external bound, 1.942, matches the ring's own space cap at z = 60 (history/audit.md F54). The real fault runs the other way. The external bound admits shifts the ring clamps: at z = 60 the ring is clamp-free (ignoring 'ungenerated') only on [-0.80, 1.94], while the tab admits [-2.13, 1.94]. At z = 30 the ring is clamp-free only on [0.10, 0.68] (tip raised to the base circle below that, space closed above), while the tab still admits [-2.13, 1.94]. The note under the ring's shift also prints rack concepts, 'undercut' and 'sharp-rack undercut' (-2.450 at z = 60), that do not exist for a ring. The documents disagree on this. corrections.md:559 and F54 say admissible_profile_shift 'already bounds a ring'; state.md:634 says the rack's range is not a ring's, and the train card deliberately shows none. The measurement supports state.md.
verdict.evidence: Node probe of solve_gear and solve_ring at 0.01 steps with the default cutter (20 teeth, addendum 1.25, tip_round 0.2): z=60, external bound [-2.130, 1.942], ring clamp-free [-0.80, 1.94]. z=30, same external bound, ring clamp-free [0.10, 0.68]. z=100, ring [-1.63, 1.94]. At z=60, x=-1.5 gives clamp.ring_tip_raised, ring_space_closed and ring_flank_fillet_gap, all inside the external bound. At x=2.5 the ring is clamped (space capped and closed, no tip corner).
verdict.corrected_claim: On an internal tab the shift bound and its annotations are an external gear's. They admit shifts the ring's own cut clamps (much of the range at small ring tooth counts; on z=30, [-2.13, 0.10) and (0.68, 1.94]) and print rack-only thresholds (undercut, sharp-rack undercut) under a ring field. The upper end coincides with the ring's space cap only at larger tooth counts. The claim that inputs the ring model accepts are refused is not supported, because the cited x = 2.5 is clamped.
verdict.proposal_note: The interim step, showing no bound for an internal tab as the train card does, is right. When solve_ring gets ranges, derive them from the ring's own guards in Ring::cut_by_at_virtual_z: the ra_min (base circle or pointed) clamp gives the lower end, and the space cap and rf_max closure give the upper. The validation should be 'no clamp inside the range', not 'solve_ring returns ok', since solve_ring clamps rather than refusing. Also correct corrections.md:559 and F54's statement that admissible_profile_shift bounds a ring.

title: Gear tab boxes bound straight to numbers turn null when cleared: raw English serde errors, and clearing the throw box switches the input mode
claim: Mate teeth, mate shift, eccentric throw, cutter teeth, addendum and tip round, pin diameter and chord tolerance use plain `bind:value` on type=number. Svelte 5 binds an empty box as null. mate.teeth or cutter.teeth null, or any decimal, fails serde, and the results column prints the raw message ('bad gear request: invalid type: null, expected u32 at line 1 column 279'), English and uncatalogued. tab.eccentricThrow = null is the representation of 'amplitude is the input', so clearing the throw box to type a new number flips the mode: the box turns into the disabled computed one under the cursor.
evidence: node_modules/svelte/src/internal/client/dom/elements/bindings/input.js:287 `to_number(value) { return value === '' ? null : +value; }`. Probe p6: mate teeth null -> THROWS 'invalid type: null, expected u32'; mate teeth 43.5 -> THROWS 'floating point `43.5`, expected u32'. Probe p3: ring with cutter teeth null -> THROWS 'bad ring request: invalid type: null, expected u32'. GearPanel L400: `byThrow = tab.eccentricThrow !== null`.
proposal: Use one NumberBox for every numeric input, with draft text, parsing, an integer flag and a bound from the core. Keep the mode in a boolean field (throwIsInput) separate from the number, so no value doubles as a mode. In the wasm entry points, turn serde failures into a Note key (for example error.request_malformed with the field path) so nothing English reaches the screen.
validation: Component test: clear each of these boxes and assert no request fails and the mode is unchanged. Probe: a malformed request returns a catalogued key.

verdict.reason: Mostly holds. Svelte 5 binds an empty number box as null (node_modules/svelte/.../bindings/input.js:287-288, `value === '' ? null : +value`). Null in mate.teeth, mate.profile_shift, cutter.teeth or cutter.addendum (and tip_round, the same f64 field shape) makes the request throw an uncatalogued English serde message, printed raw at GearPanel.svelte:574 and :645. Clearing the throw box sets tab.eccentricThrow = null, and `byThrow = tab.eccentricThrow !== null` (L400) flips the mode under the cursor. The list overreaches on two fields: pin diameter and chord tolerance do not fail when null. The gear request drops a pin diameter <= 0 or null, solve_ring takes a null pin_diameter as None, and a null chord_tolerance is accepted by both entry points.
verdict.evidence: Node probe: mate teeth null -> 'bad gear request: invalid type: null, expected u32'. mate shift null -> 'expected f64'. cutter teeth null -> 'bad ring request: invalid type: null, expected u32'. cutter addendum null -> 'expected f64'. chord_tolerance null -> ok for both gear and ring. pin_diameter null for a ring -> ok.
verdict.corrected_claim: Clearing the mate teeth, mate shift, cutter teeth, cutter addendum or tip round box sends null and shows a raw English serde error. Clearing the throw box flips the eccentric sizing mode. The pin-diameter and chord-tolerance boxes clear without error: null is read as 'none' or accepted.
verdict.proposal_note: Keeping the mode in its own boolean, separate from the number, is the right structural fix. The same finite() guard the train panel already uses is a smaller first step. Turning serde failures into a Note key in gear-wasm fits rule 2.

title: Train integer inputs (teeth, planet count, cutter teeth, actuations) accept fractions and negatives, which fail the whole train at the boundary
claim: finite() passes any finite number, so 17.5 or -5 teeth, or 2.5 planets, reach serde as a u32 and the train comes back as ui.train_boundary_failed with the serde text. The lists, ports and names blank out. `min="1"` on two of these inputs is a bound written in TypeScript, and the browser does not enforce it on typed text.
evidence: Probe p3: teeth 17.5 -> 'invalid type: floating point `17.5`, expected u32'; teeth -5 -> 'invalid value: integer `-5`, expected u32'; axis count 2.5 -> 'expected u32'; teeth 0 -> error.train_wiring (a proper note).
proposal: Give the NumberBox an integer flag, as FieldSpec.integer already does on the gear tab: a non-integer draft shows ui.validation_not_a_whole_number and is not written. Take the bound from the core (GearResult.ranges.teeth exists; add one for axis.count) and drop min="1".
validation: A component test typing 17.5 and -5 into the teeth box: the train still solves and the box shows the whole-number note.

verdict.reason: Holds. finite() lets any finite number through, so 17.5 or -5 teeth, 2.5 planets, or a fractional actuations count (a u32, mod.rs:2747) reaches serde as a non-integer and the whole train fails at the boundary, blanking the lists. `min="1"` does not stop typed text. The effect is transient and needs deliberately non-integer input, so low rather than medium. Teeth 0 comes back as a proper note (error.train_wiring). Axis count 0 solves with failure=null on the default pair's second axis, so zero passes silently there as well.
verdict.evidence: Probe: teeth 17.5 -> 'invalid type: floating point `17.5`, expected u32'. teeth -5 -> 'invalid value: integer `-5`, expected u32'. axes[1].count 2.5 -> 'expected u32'. count 0 -> ok, failure null. TrainPanel.svelte:834, 906 (numberField, which uses finite at L1723), 1356 and 1366.
verdict.proposal_note: An integer-aware guard (Number.isInteger(v) && v >= 0) in the TS layer is input sanitation, not engineering. The admissible bound (>= 1 teeth, >= 1 planets) should come from the core's ranges, per rule 1, as proposed.

title: Rule 1: the gear tab's mate is created with 43 teeth written in TypeScript
claim: freshTab writes `mate: { teeth: 43, profile_shift: 0, internal: false }`. GearTabDefaults (gear-wasm defaults()) carries params, cutter, pin_diameter, chord_tolerance, reference_circles and eccentric_throw, but no mate. This is exactly the class docs/corrections.md rows 494 and 571 record closing ('the boundary's own defaults'), and the eccentric centre-distance profile a designer reads is computed against this mate.
evidence: GearTabDefaults.ts fields: `params, cutter, pin_diameter, chord_tolerance, reference_circles, eccentric_throw`. grep in gear-wasm/src/lib.rs finds 43 only inside test requests (L2125, L2154, L2178).
proposal: Add `mate: MateRef` to GearTabDefaults in gear-wasm, and pin it in the boundary-defaults canary that row 571 describes. freshTab reads d.mate.
validation: check_bindings shows the new field; the canary fails if the default moves; grep web/src for the literal 43 finds nothing.

verdict.reason: This holds as stated. A fresh gear tab's mate tooth count is a literal typed in TypeScript. It is the same class of fault corrections.md closed for the eccentric throw, and the row that pinned the boundary's own defaults listed the tab's tooth count, the pin diameter and the throw, but left out the mate. The mate is only read in eccentric mode, so the effect is limited to the centre-distance profile and the throw seed there. That is why the severity is low, even though it breaks a stated rule.
verdict.evidence: web/src/state.svelte.ts:147 `mate: { teeth: 43, profile_shift: 0, internal: false },` sits inside freshTab, beside d.params, d.pin_diameter and d.cutter, which all come from defaults(). crates/gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:1106-1122: GearTabDefaults has params, cutter, pin_diameter, chord_tolerance, reference_circles and eccentric_throw, and no mate. The eccentric_throw field's own doc says 'a number the application shows is a number Rust decided'. GearPanel.svelte:370 binds the value into a visible field (tab.mate.teeth), and GearPanel.svelte:152 sends it as the request's mate in eccentric mode. corrections.md row (~l.571) lists the boundary's own defaults without the mate.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposal is sound. MateRef already exists as a wire type in gear-wasm (lib.rs:69/82), so adding `mate: MateRef` to GearTabDefaults and pinning it in the existing boundary-defaults canary is a small change.

title: Rule 1: diameters from radii, mm to µm, and fraction to percent are computed in TypeScript
claim: `2 * s.variation.tip_radius[0]` and `2 * root_radius` make diameters, and `1e3 * s.variation.drive_pitch_error`, index errors, sinusoid_error and sinusoid_backlash convert mm to µm in the panel. docs/rationale.md#no-engineering-calculation-in-typescript says 'so is a diameter'. The wire units also disagree: ToleranceOut.tooth_to_tooth and .total are printed as µm with no conversion, and their generated type states no unit, while the Variation fields are mm and converted. pct() multiplies by 100.
evidence: GearPanel L723: `range(n(2 * s.variation.tip_radius[0]), n(2 * s.variation.tip_radius[1]))`. L742: `um(1e3 * s.variation.drive_pitch_error)`. L822: `um(s.tolerance.tooth_to_tooth)`, no factor. wire/wasm/ToleranceOut.ts documents no unit.
proposal: Have Variation and CentreProfile carry what is displayed (tip_diameter and root_diameter ranges, and pitch errors in the unit shown), or have the core state each field's unit in its doc so ts-rs carries it. Delete every `2 *` and `1e3 *` from the panels. Document ToleranceOut's unit.
validation: grep -nE '[0-9]e[0-9]|\b2 \*' web/src/*.svelte finds nothing; the golden corpus prints the diameters and they match the gear-cli figures.

verdict.reason: The diameter part holds. rationale.md#no-engineering-calculation-in-typescript says in so many words 'so is a diameter', and GearSummary already sends diameters for the uniform gear, so the panel doubling the eccentric Variation radii is both a Rule 1 breach and inconsistent with its own sibling rows. The unit part is overstated. GearSummary's generated doc states 'Lengths are millimetres, angles degrees, composite errors micrometres', so ToleranceOut's unit is documented at the struct that carries it, just not on the field. mm-to-µm and fraction-to-percent are changes of display unit, which is arguably the 'TypeScript formats it' the rule allows. They are a softer consistency point, not an engineering calculation.
verdict.evidence: GearPanel.svelte:723 and :728 use `2 * s.variation.tip_radius[0]` and `2 * s.variation.root_radius[...]`. web/src/wire/wasm/GearSummary.ts:33-40 already carries pitch_diameter, base_diameter, tip_diameter and root_diameter. docs/rationale.md:30 says '**A default is one of those numbers**, and so is a diameter'. GearSummary.ts:16 says 'Lengths are millimetres, angles degrees, composite errors micrometres.' gear-core/src/gear.rs:653-677 documents the Variation fields in mm. The 1e3 factors are at GearPanel 742, 744, 749, 751, 776 and 782. TrainPanel.svelte:410 has pct = 100*v.
verdict.corrected_claim: The eccentric gear's tip and root diameter ranges are doubled from radii in GearPanel.svelte (L723, L728). That breaks rationale.md's explicit 'so is a diameter', while the uniform gear gets diameters from the core. The mm-to-µm and ×100 conversions are display-unit formatting with documented units (GearSummary doc: composite errors in µm, Variation in mm). The mixed wire units within one summary are a minor inconsistency, not an undocumented unit.
verdict.proposal_note: Add tip_diameter and root_diameter ranges to Variation, matching GearSummary. Putting a per-field unit doc on ToleranceOut is harmless. Do not require every 1e3 or 100 factor to be removed. A single display-unit decision is enough: either every error field crosses in µm, or the panel owns the unit change and says so.

title: Engineering judgements repeated in TypeScript: locking, contact ratio below 1, idle, internal mesh, crossed, a weak basis
evidence: groupings.rs:242 `let idle = |p: Option<f64>| p.is_some_and(|p| p < 1e-9);` against TrainPanel L168 `(...power_through ?? 1) === 0`. Probe p7: the two rules agree on all ten presets today, because an idle layshaft ratio is exactly 0.0. TrainPanel L1120 `class:warn={r.transverse < 1}`.
validation: grep for '<= 0', '< 1', '=== 0' and '!== 0' on core values in web/src finds none. A core law: MeshCase.idle equals the flow's Idle rows for every case of every preset.

verdict.reason: The copies exist, but most are TypeScript reading a documented encoding, not re-deriving a rule. locksAt reads the documented sign convention of locking_friction ('Negative means ... no friction locks it'). The contact-ratio warn only adds a colour beside a core note. The 'weak' basis is a styling choice over an enum. lockedWays is a one-line mirror of Directional::locked (`<= 0.0`), and the panel's comment admits it. Two items are real second copies. First, idleInCase uses `=== 0` on power_through, while groupings.rs uses `< 1e-9` on the same normalised figure, so the Centres list and the Flow list use different rules. They agree today only because idle meshes come out exactly 0. Second, internalOn re-derives 'internal' from members' ring cutters, while the core already marks an internal mesh by `MeshReport.tip_room` being non-null, documented as 'None for an external one'.
verdict.evidence: groupings.rs:242 `let idle = |p: Option<f64>| p.is_some_and(|p| p < 1e-9);` against TrainPanel.svelte:166-168 `(... power_through ?? 1) === 0`. mod.rs:319 documents power_through as normalised by the case's input power, so the 1e-9 is relative. That is not a scale bug, but it is a second epsilon. TrainPanel.svelte:419-424 internalOn; wire/core/MeshReport.ts:111 'Where an internal mesh's tips are, and None for an external one'. contact.rs:273 `Directional::of(|d| *self.get(d) <= 0.0)` against TrainPanel.svelte:477 `[e.forward <= 0, e.backward <= 0]`. mod.rs:240-247 documents locking_friction's sign convention.
verdict.corrected_claim: Two panel predicates duplicate core rules and can disagree with them. The idle chip in the Centres list uses exact zero against the flow's 1e-9. internalOn re-derives mesh kind that MeshReport already exposes through tip_room. lockedWays is a trivial mirror of Directional::locked. The remaining items read documented encodings and are not separate rules.
verdict.proposal_note: Keep it minimal. Add `idle: bool` to MeshCase from groupings' single rule, or name the 1e-9 as a constant and cross it. Key the panel's internal check off `tip_room !== null`, or add `internal` to MeshReport. Crossing `locked` as Directional<bool> is cheap. There is no need for Basis::weak or a `crossed` flag. `angle !== 0` on a user input and an enum match on basis are not engineering judgements.

title: Display precision is fixed decimals chosen in TS, and turning auto off rounds the solved value to 4 decimals, which loses precision at the default 0.1 N·m scale
claim: autoNumber shows `Number(computed.toFixed(4))` and, when auto is switched off, seeds `a.manual = shown`. That rounds to 4 absolute decimals. A derived torque of 3e-5 N·m, which is 0.1 N·m through a 3000:1 train at the shipped defaults (0.1 N·m, 30,000 rpm), becomes a given torque of 0.0000 = 0. A derived 1.234e-4 becomes 1e-4, an 18 % change. Readouts are likewise absolute: torque num(v,4), stresses 1 decimal, lengths 3-4. strings.svelte.ts:80 says 'how many decimals a quantity deserves is a judgement about the quantity, made where the model is', which the panels contradict about 100 times. The comment at TrainPanel L1847-1848 says the gear tab's throw and amplitude seed the same way, but GearPanel L184-189 seeds full precision.
evidence: TrainPanel L1814 and L1849 as quoted. GearPanel L184: `tab.eccentricThrow = cp.sinusoid.amplitude` (unrounded). defaults: LoadCase::ultimate(input, output, 0.1, 30_000.0) (gear-wasm lib.rs:1175).
proposal: Seed the manual value with the full solved value, not the rounded display, and fix the comment. For display, either (a) the core ships a display precision (significant digits) per quantity kind in Defaults, used by one fmt(v, kind) helper, or (b) switch to significant figures via Intl.NumberFormat(language(), {maximumSignificantDigits}) so small magnitudes keep their digits. Option (a) keeps the judgement in Rust, as Rule 1 and the Note doc ask.
validation: Test: with a computed torque of 3e-5, turning auto off leaves manual === 3e-5. A readout of 1.234e-4 shows 4 significant digits.

verdict.reason: This holds. autoNumber shows `Number(computed.toFixed(4))`, and when auto is switched off it seeds `a.manual = shown`, so a derived torque below 5e-5 N·m becomes a given torque of 0, and one near 1e-4 loses up to half its value. The adjacent comment's claim that 'the gear tab's throw and amplitude do the same' is false. GearPanel's sizeByThrow seeds `cp.sinusoid.amplitude` at full precision. autoNumber is used for load torques (TrainPanel.svelte:961-964, `load.torque.auto ? (at?.torque ?? null)`), so the rounding reaches inputs. The quoted 3000:1 scenario has the direction backwards: a reduction multiplies torque. Small derived torques still come from speed-ups, or from the 0.02 N·m fatigue default through a ratio of order 100 or more. The display half is also fair: rationale.md:46-50 puts rounding in the core, and the panels choose absolute decimals.
verdict.evidence: TrainPanel.svelte:1814 `{@const shown = computed === undefined ? a.manual : computed === null ? null : Number(computed.toFixed(4))}`. TrainPanel.svelte ~1849 `if (!v && a.auto && shown !== null) a.manual = shown;`, with the comment '...the gear tab's throw and amplitude do the same.' GearPanel.svelte:184-185 `tab.eccentricThrow = cp && !isUnavailable(cp) ? cp.sinusoid.amplitude : defaults().gear.eccentric_throw;` (unrounded). Number((3e-5).toFixed(4)) === 0. gear-wasm lib.rs:1177 `LoadCase::fatigue(input, output, 0.02, 30_000.0)`.
verdict.proposal_note: Seeding with the full value is a one-line fix, together with the comment. For the display, significant figures (Intl.NumberFormat with maximumSignificantDigits, in the app's language) fix the small-magnitude loss without a new wire field. A core-shipped precision per quantity kind is heavier and only needed if the owner wants the decimals judgement in Rust.

title: Numbers are formatted in mixed locales: toLocaleString beside toFixed, inputs follow the browser, html lang stays 'en'
claim: count() uses `toLocaleString()` with no locale, which is the browser's locale, not the app's language. Every other figure uses toFixed with '.', and the core's Note values use '.'. In a de-DE browser the cycles column reads '1.000.000 / 1.000.000' beside '0.1234' torques, so the dot means two things in one table. Number inputs parse and display in the browser's locale, whatever the app language. setLanguage never updates document.documentElement.lang, so a German catalogue is announced as English (screen readers, hyphenation). Typing '1,5' in an English-locale browser leaves input.value empty, and the gear tab answers 'required', which is misleading.
evidence: L409 `v.toLocaleString()`; L407 `v.toFixed(digits)`. grep documentElement in web/src finds no match. index.html `<html lang="en">`.
proposal: One formatter module: `fmt(v, kind)` = Intl.NumberFormat(language(), precision from the core). Use it for every readout, including count(), and pass the same locale to the core if Notes are to agree, or decide explicitly that the app is '.'-decimal everywhere and make count() use that too. In setLanguage set `document.documentElement.lang = code`. Where the empty-text case is ambiguous, show 'not a number in this format' rather than 'required'.
validation: A test under a de-DE Intl: the cycles and torque cells use one decimal separator; switching the language changes document.documentElement.lang.

verdict.reason: Each part checks out. count() uses toLocaleString() with no locale, so it follows the browser, not the app language. Every other readout uses toFixed, which always prints '.'. setLanguage (core.ts:475-486) never sets document.documentElement.lang, and index.html hard-codes lang="en". GearPanel's onInput answers 'ui.validation_required' whenever input.value is empty, and a number input the browser cannot parse reports an empty value, so a malformed entry reads as 'required'. The effect is cosmetic or accessibility-level only; no computed value is wrong.
verdict.evidence: TrainPanel.svelte:409 `const count = ... v.toLocaleString()`, used at :1264 for cycles. TrainPanel.svelte:406-410 num/pct/n all use toFixed. `grep -rn documentElement web/src` returns nothing. web/index.html:2 `<html lang="en">`. core.ts:475-486 setLanguage sets the code, the storage and the catalogue only. GearPanel.svelte:126 `const err = text.trim() === "" ? t("ui.validation_required") : validate(f, v, b);`.
verdict.proposal_note: The smallest consistent fix is to decide on '.' decimals throughout, to match the core's Note values, and make count() use a fixed locale or a plain grouping, plus set documentElement.lang in setLanguage. Moving every readout to Intl with the app locale would make panel figures disagree with Note values, which the core formats with '.', unless Notes change too. Say so explicitly if that route is taken. The input-validity case can be detected with `e.currentTarget.validity.badInput`.

title: English and unit literals outside the catalogue: 'Fine'/'Standard', 'Unnamed', 'mm/s', 'mm', '°', file-name fallbacks; the catalogue has duplicate unit keys
evidence: grep '"Fine"\|Unnamed' web/src: GearPanel 532 and 819, Sidebar 134 and 154. strings_en.toml: gear_mm (301) and train_mm (486) are both 'mm'; gear_unnamed (343) and train_unnamed (635) are both 'Unnamed'; there is no fine or standard key.
proposal: Add ui.tolerance_scale_fine/_standard (or render the ClassRef through a Note) and ui.unit_mm, ui.unit_um, ui.unit_mm_s, ui.unit_deg. Delete the per-panel duplicates and the '°' special case. Use the unnamed keys in Sidebar. Extend check_strings.py to flag capitalised string literals and bare unit literals in .svelte markup and TS outside comments.
validation: The extended check_strings.py fails on the current tree and passes after the change.

verdict.reason: The English literals are real i18n defects. 'Fine'/'Standard' appear twice with no key. The Sidebar prints 'Unnamed' although ui.gear_unnamed and ui.train_unnamed exist and are used elsewhere in the panels. File-name fallbacks are English. check_strings.py only matches `"ui.…"` keys, so none of this can fail it. The unit part is weaker. 'mm', 'µm', '°' and 'mm/s' are language-independent symbols in all five shipped catalogues (en, de, pt, zh-Hans, zh-Hant). Writing them literally is not an i18n bug, only an inconsistency: some units go through keys (two keys, gear_mm and train_mm, for one symbol) and some are literal. A check that flags every bare unit literal would add noise.
verdict.evidence: GearPanel.svelte:532 and :819 `{... scale === "fine" ? "Fine" : "Standard"}`. Sidebar.svelte:134 and :154 `{tab.name || "Unnamed"}`, while GearPanel.svelte:307 and :326 and TrainPanel.svelte:1998 use t("ui.*_unnamed"). strings_en.toml:301 `gear_mm = "mm"`, :486 `train_mm = "mm"`, :343 and :635 both 'Unnamed'. TrainPanel.svelte:1724 `unit === "°" ? "°" : unit ? t(unit) : ""`. tools/check_strings.py:56 matches only `"(ui\.[A-Za-z0-9_]+)"`.
verdict.corrected_claim: The JGMA scale names and the sidebar's 'Unnamed' are untranslated English beside existing or missing catalogue keys, and file-name fallbacks are English. Unit symbols are language-neutral. They are inconsistent (duplicate gear_mm/train_mm keys, some literal, a '°' special case) but not mistranslated.
verdict.proposal_note: Add ui.tolerance_scale_fine and ui.tolerance_scale_standard, and use the existing *_unnamed keys in the Sidebar. For units, choose one convention: either all literal SI symbols, deleting gear_mm/train_mm and the '°' special case, or one shared ui.unit_* set. Extending check_strings.py to capitalised literals in markup is reasonable. Flagging bare unit literals is not.

title: The material provenance marker shows the basis's first English letter, so 'datasheet' and 'derived' both show 'd'
claim: `{used.basis[0]}` prints the first character of the Basis enum value: overridden->o, datasheet->d, derived->d, chart->c, estimated->e. A datasheet value and a derived value are marked identically, the letters are English initials in every language, and there is no title or tooltip to decode them. The marker's only job is to show where a number came from.
evidence: Basis.ts: `"overridden" | "datasheet" | "derived" | "chart" | "estimated"`. TrainPanel L1064-1066 as quoted.
proposal: Add one catalogue entry per basis: a short mark (ui.basis_mark_) plus a title (ui.basis_) in all five languages. Render `{t(mark)}`.
validation: check_strings passes, and the rendered markers for datasheet and derived differ.

verdict.reason: Holds as stated. TrainPanel.svelte:1064-1065 renders `{used.basis[0]}` with no title. The library contains a real collision: materials_default.toml has 28 datasheet values and 1 derived value (brass Poisson's ratio, per the file's header note), and both show 'd'. `overridden` can never show, because an override takes the × branch at L1057. The harness already tells the two apart: gear-cli main.rs:2391-2397 tags Derived as 'D' and Datasheet as 'd'. So the panel is less precise than the harness, and it shows English initials in every language. Severity is low: the `.weak` class already colours chart and estimated values, and the collision affects one value in the shipped library.
verdict.evidence: web/src/TrainPanel.svelte:1064 `{used.basis[0]}`. Count of `basis = "..."` in materials_default.toml: datasheet 28, estimated 10, chart 1, derived 1. crates/gear-cli/src/main.rs:2393-2397 maps Datasheet->'d', Derived->'D'. grep finds no basis strings in strings_en.toml.
verdict.proposal_note: Also put `used.note` in the title where it is present. Value carries a provenance note, e.g. reversed_bending_allowable's '0.7 x the one-directional allowable...' in material.rs:176, and the library's estimated values carry notes too. Showing it is the point of the marker. The mark itself can be a catalogue entry, as proposed. No `overridden` mark is needed, because that branch never renders.

title: editTrain reports a boundary failure as success, and relieveTrain/relieveCase fail silently
claim: editTrain returns null (no refusal) whenever the thrown message does not start with 'ui.'. Offers.make then closes the menu, clears the preview and calls made(), which moves the selection as if an edit had been made, though nothing changed. With a train holding NaN or a fractional tooth count (see the earlier findings), every edit fails this way with no message. relieveTrain and relieveCase also swallow every error.
evidence: core.ts L822-823: `return message.startsWith("ui.") ? message : null;`. Offers L91-95: `refusal = editTrain(...); if (refusal !== null) return; over = null; open = null; made?.(o.edit, meshes);`
proposal: Return a union { ok } | { refused: key } | { failed: detail }. Offers shows ui.train_boundary_failed for `failed`, and does not call made(). Relief can do the same, or at least console.error.
validation: A unit test with a stubbed edit_train that throws a non-ui error: made is not called and a message is shown.

verdict.reason: The mechanics hold. editTrain (core.ts:817-823) returns null for any thrown message that does not start with 'ui.'. Offers.make (Offers.svelte:88-96) then closes the menu and calls made(). A non-'ui.' error really can reach this path. edit_train_impl (gear-wasm lib.rs:1557) maps a serde failure to its own message, and a train holding NaN (JSON.stringify writes null into an f64) or a fractional tooth count fails deserialisation that way. The consequences are milder than stated. made() only clears the selection when the edit was a remove, selects min(a,b) when it was a join, and selects nothing for an add, because the mesh count has not moved. So the real harm is a silent no-op with the menu closing and no message. The swallowing is documented ('swallowed as before', core.ts:815; 'a click is not the place to discover a broken boundary', core.ts:674-675). That argument is weak, though: solveTrain already turns the same failure into ui.train_boundary_failed with its detail (core.ts:772-783), so a key for this case already exists.
verdict.evidence: core.ts:822 `return message.startsWith("ui.") ? message : null;`. Offers.svelte:91-95. TrainPanel.svelte:250-253 made(). gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:1557 `serde_json::from_str(input).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?`. core.ts:780 already uses `ui.train_boundary_failed` with `detail`.
verdict.proposal_note: The smallest fix needs no new union type. Return `ui.train_boundary_failed` (with the detail) in place of null, so Offers shows it through the existing refusal path and does not call made(). Relief can log the failure or do the same. The root cause is the inputs that let NaN or a fraction into the train, and fixing that removes most of the ways to reach this path.

title: The gear tab's adopt list runs a full train solve per train tab just to read member names
claim: memberRefs(train) calls solveTrain(train), which does every part's cut, search, flow and rating, to read `names`. Its own doc says the names need no geometry. GearPanel renders it once per train tab when the panel mounts, and again in the onchange handler. Train solves cost 3-7 ms each on the presets, and a searched hula was once 70 ms a keystroke (corrections.md row 408), so ten open trains is a noticeable pause every time a gear tab opens.
evidence: members.ts: `const names = solveTrain(train).names;`. Probe p2: solve_train takes 2.7-7.4 ms per preset.
proposal: Add a cheap wasm entry point, member_names(shape), backed by Shape::member_names (and list it in tools/wasm_boundary.json with a probe step), or have solve_train's topology half available separately. memberRefs calls that.
validation: check_wasm with the new probe; a timing sanity check in wasm_probe.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. memberRefs (members.ts:81-82) runs the full solveTrain only to read `names`. The wasm side computes names before any solve (gear-wasm lib.rs:839 `req.train.shape.member_names()`), so a cheap entry point is straightforward. GearPanel calls memberRefs once per train tab when rendering the adopt list (L308), and once more on change (L301). I did not re-measure the per-solve cost in wasm. The auditor's native timings are plausible, and the cost grows with the number of tabs. There is also a correctness side-effect nobody noted: when solveTrain fails at the boundary it returns `names: []` (core.ts:790). Every gear is then labelled 'Gear N', and `adoptable: names[index]?.role !== "worm"` becomes true for a worm, so the doc's claim that names 'arrive whether or not the train solved' fails on exactly that path.
verdict.evidence: members.ts:82 `const names = solveTrain(train).names;`. gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:839 `let names = req.train.shape.member_names();`. core.ts:790 fallback `names: []`. GearPanel.svelte:301, 308.
verdict.proposal_note: A `member_names` entry point needs a row in tools/wasm_boundary.json and a probe step in wasm_probe.mjs (check_wasm fails otherwise). A cheaper alternative is to cache names per train tab from the solve TrainPanel already makes, although the gear panel may render when no train panel has solved. The entry point is the cleaner fix and also closes the worm-adoptable fallback.

title: Load-case edits are split: add_case and duty go through the core, removeCase and setRole mutate in TypeScript
evidence: L287 `tab.train.load_cases.splice(i, 1)`. L327 `c.loads.push({ at: b.body, role, torque: { auto: true, manual: 0 }, speed: { auto: true, manual: 0 } })`.
proposal: Add TrainEdit variants `remove_case: number`, `set_role: {case, body, role}` and `enable: {case, on}`, done by Train methods (the fresh load's placeholders then come from Rust) and followed by relieve_case inside the core. Add a wasm_probe step for each.
validation: The existing case laws, extended to remove_case and set_role over every preset: the result keeps the case within the train's mobility.

verdict.reason: The removeCase and setRole parts hold, and removeCase has a consequence stronger than the finding says. The core's rule for bodies (conditions.rs, doc above drop_bare at ~1112-1120) counts a case entry as a reason for a bare body to exist. Removing the only case that names a parked body in TypeScript therefore leaves a body the core's own rule would drop. That is exactly the 'what else has to change' the CLAUDE.md rule is about. setRole pushes `{auto:true, manual:0}` in TypeScript. The zeros are placeholders under auto, and relieveCase then runs (TrainPanel.svelte:329), so relief does happen, but the fresh entry's shape is decided outside the core. The 'enabling a case flips c.enabled and asks for no relief' part is refuted. Relief keeps a case's loads within the train's mobility, and `enabled` changes no load. Train has no other field that refers to a case's enabled state (the struct fields are load_cases, reversed_bending, shape, held). No rule applies there.
verdict.evidence: TrainPanel.svelte:287 `tab.train.load_cases.splice(i, 1);`. TrainPanel.svelte:327 the push with `manual: 0`, then L329 `relieveCase(...)`. TrainPanel.svelte:2053 `c.enabled = v;`. conditions.rs:1112-1120 'A hold or a case's entry is a reason' for a body to stay. mod.rs:3540-3568 Train fields.
verdict.corrected_claim: removeCase and setRole edit the train in TypeScript and bypass core rules. removeCase can leave a body that only the removed case named, which the core's drop_bare rule would take away. setRole's fresh entry is shaped in TypeScript. The enable toggle needs no rule.
verdict.proposal_note: Add `remove_case` (it calls drop_bare afterwards) and `set_role` as TrainEdit variants, each with a wasm_probe step. Leave `enabled` a plain field.

title: The wire uses mixed conventions for 'none' and for numbering
claim: Axis.carried_by uses 0 for 'the ground', but AxisGroup.carried_by uses null. The panel tests both: `(carried_by ?? 0) !== 0` at L241, `!== null` at L536, `!== 0` in members.ts. TrainFailure.part is numbered from one, while every other index on the wire (parts, meshes, members, PartReport position) is 0-based, and the panel subtracts 1 at L2116.
evidence: Generated types as cited; TrainFailure's doc says 'numbered from one'.
proposal: Pick one convention per concept: carried_by as Option<body> in both, or 0 in both; failure.part as a 0-based index into `parts`. Regenerate the bindings and drop the -1 and the `?? 0` checks.
validation: check_bindings and npm run check pass; the golden corpus prints the harness's own numbering, unaffected.

verdict.reason: Both inconsistencies are real and generated from Rust. Axis.carried_by is a usize with GROUND=0; its doc even records that it used to be an Option. groupings.rs:47/123 turns the same fact back into `Option<usize>` with `(carried_by != GROUND).then_some(..)`. The panel handles both forms: `(… ?? 0) !== 0` at L241, `!== null` at L536, and `!== 0` in members.ts:34. TrainFailure.part is made 1-based on purpose in gear-wasm lib.rs:864 (`u32::try_from(*part + 1)`), and the only consumer subtracts 1 (TrainPanel.svelte:2116). Every other part or mesh index on the wire is 0-based. Nothing in the documents argues for the +1.
verdict.evidence: web/src/wire/core/Axis.ts `carried_by: number`; wire/core/AxisGroup.ts `carried_by: number | null`; crates/gear-core/src/train/groupings.rs:123; crates/gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:864; TrainPanel.svelte:2116 `showPart(failure.part! - 1)`.
verdict.proposal_note: Prefer the stored convention (0 = ground) for AxisGroup too, since Axis cannot change without breaking the stored-file compatibility its doc describes. Drop the `+ 1` at lib.rs:864 and the `- 1` at L2116 in the same commit, then run check_wasm --write, because its recorded payloads may include `part`.

title: TrainPanel.svelte (3,079 lines) should be split, and the panels' four number-input paths should become one component
evidence: Structure grep: 20 {#snippet} blocks; the style runs from L2182 to L3079; 24 grid-template-columns declarations; the parsing lines are cited in the earlier findings.
validation: Every numeric input in web/src goes through NumberBox (grep type="number" finds matches only in NumberBox.svelte). Component tests for NumberBox cover empty, '-', a fraction in an integer box, out-of-bound text and auto seeding.

verdict.reason: The measurements hold. TrainPanel.svelte has 3,079 lines: script 1-502, style 2182-3079, 21 {#snippet} blocks (not 20), and 24 grid-template-columns declarations. The identical `1fr auto var(--field-box) var(--unit-cell)` template appears at L2242, 2245, 2248 and 2615, and in GearPanel:947. The four parse paths exist. GearPanel.onInput (L121-129) uses draft text and validation. The numberField and raw inputs use `finite` (L404) through bind. The auto-number snippet uses `valueAsNumber` with no guard (L1765), so a cleared box writes NaN. property() uses `Number(v)`, where Number('') === 0, so clearing a material box writes an override of 0 (L1052-1053). Integer boxes such as gear.teeth (L1366) accept fractions. One supporting claim is wrong: 'Snippets cannot be shared with GearPanel.' The installed Svelte is 5.56.9, and Svelte 5.5 and later can export top-level snippets from `<script module>` when they close over no instance state. Sharing is therefore constrained, not impossible. Components are still the better vehicle for a stateful NumberBox. The direction, one NumberBox component, is sound and matches the owner's one-model goal.
verdict.evidence: wc -l: 3079 TrainPanel.svelte, 1004 GearPanel.svelte; `grep -c {#snippet` = 21; TrainPanel.svelte:1765 `oninput={(e) => set(e.currentTarget.valueAsNumber)}`; L1052 `const v = Number(e.currentTarget.value);`; L404-405 `finite`; GearPanel.svelte:121-129; node_modules/svelte version 5.56.9.
verdict.corrected_claim: TrainPanel is 3,079 lines with 21 snippets and about 900 lines of CSS. Its numeric inputs parse four different ways, two of which write a wrong value (NaN, or 0 for an empty box) into the train. Snippets could be exported from `<script module>`, but a stateful NumberBox component is the right unification.
verdict.proposal_note: Do step 1 first (NumberBox with draft text, a finite guard, an integer flag and a core-supplied bound) and port property() and autoNumber onto it right away, because those two carry live bugs. Splitting the snippets into files is lower value and can follow. The validation grep `type="number"` only in NumberBox.svelte is a good gate. Keep the core-supplied bounds, because rule 1 forbids writing any bound in TypeScript.

title: Dead or stale code: Library.names, the data-theme CSS blocks, about 50 unused type imports, a stale duplicate doc comment
evidence: A grep for each export's uses in web/src: 'library.names' has no match. state.svelte.ts L375-376. A grep for data-theme and dataset.theme finds matches only in app.css.
proposal: Delete Library.names and the stale comment. Either add a theme control or remove the two data-theme blocks and narrow the comment. Replace the two type lists with `export type * from './wire'` (TS 5) and import only what core.ts uses.
validation: npm run check passes; the bundle size is unchanged or smaller.

verdict.reason: Every item holds as stated. Library.names has no reader: the only `.names` uses in web/src are `result.names` and `solveTrain(train).names`. Trains.remove carries two doc comments, and the first contradicts both the code and the second. Nothing in web/src or index.html sets data-theme or dataset.theme, so the :root[data-theme=dark|light] blocks and the color-scheme comment that argues for them (app.css:16-21) are dead. core.ts imports 75 wire types (lines 14-89). About 50 of them appear nowhere except the re-export list at lines 91-168, so they are unused imports and the two lists are kept in step by hand.
verdict.evidence: state.svelte.ts:375-376 reads `/** Deleting the last tab leaves a fresh one, as for gears. */` followed by `/** Deleting the last tab leaves none; the main panel offers a new one. */`, and the body does not create a tab. state.svelte.ts:422 is `get names()`, which nothing calls. A grep for data-theme finds only app.css:19, 81, 98 and 114. The dark palette is also written twice verbatim, once in the media query at 81-95 and again at 98-112. I ran a Python count of each name imported at core.ts:14-89 over the rest of the file: most occur exactly once, and that once is the export list. tsconfig has verbatimModuleSyntax and TS is ^5.6, and wire/index.ts exists, so `export type * from "./wire"` is available.
verdict.proposal_note: `export type *` also re-exports wire types the current list leaves out. That is harmless because they are type-only. If the data-theme blocks are removed, collapse the duplicated dark palette into the media query and drop the comment at app.css:16-21 about the explicit attribute. Keep the `color-scheme: light dark` line.

title: Accessibility gaps: segmented controls and list selections announce no state, the viewport has no keyboard or touch zoom
evidence: Code as cited. Viewport handles onwheel, onpointerdown, onpointermove, onpointerup and onpointercancel only.
proposal: Give the segmented controls role=radiogroup, with role=radio and aria-checked on each button, or aria-pressed. Add aria-current="true" to selected rows. Add role="img" and an aria-label to the canvas, +/- and arrow-key handlers, and two-pointer pinch zoom through zoomAbout.
validation: svelte-check a11y warnings stay at zero; manual check with a screen reader and on a touch device.

verdict.reason: The segmented buttons (duty at 882/885, case role at 948-954, grouping at 2148) show their state only through class:on. Selected flow rows use class:sel, with no aria-current or aria-selected. The canvas has no role or label and handles only wheel and pointer events, with touch-action:none, so touch users cannot zoom. index.html has a fixed lang="en", and nothing sets documentElement.lang. While checking I found a related defect the finding does not mention: the pointer handlers track a single lastX/lastY and do not key on pointerId. A second finger's pointerdown resets them, so a two-finger touch makes the drawing jump instead of zooming (added under missed).
verdict.evidence: Viewport.svelte:181-186 has handlers only for onwheel, onpointerdown, onpointermove, onpointerup and onpointercancel. Line 212 sets `touch-action: none`. onDown (79-84) overwrites lastX and lastY for any pointer. TrainPanel.svelte:882, 948 and 2148 carry `class:on=` with no aria attribute. index.html:2 is `<html lang="en">`. A grep for documentElement.lang finds nothing.
verdict.proposal_note: aria-pressed on each button is the smallest change and matches Switch. Pinch zoom needs a pointerId→position map in any case, and that map also fixes the jump bug. Set document.documentElement.lang wherever setLanguage runs.

title: No front-end tests, and nothing enforces Rule 1 in TypeScript
claim: The web package has no test runner; `npm run check` is type-checking only. rationale.md says Rule 1 is 'Enforced by: defaults, bounds and strings all crossing from Rust'. That keeps them from being duplicated, but nothing detects a number typed into .ts or .svelte: the mate's 43, the 2* and 1e3* conversions and the TS judgements were all found by reading. The corrections ledger records this class more than once (rows 443, 494, 571, 604, 684).
evidence: package.json scripts: dev, build, preview, check; devDependencies include no test framework. tools/ has no TS literal scan.
proposal: (1) Add vitest with @testing-library/svelte, with tests for the pure helpers (outside, validate, notes, offers.sections, assignLeaves, the formatter) and for NumberBox, and run it in CI beside npm run check. (2) Add tools/check_ts_numbers.py: flag numeric literals other than 0, 1 and -1 in web/src script and markup, excluding comments, CSS, step= and array indices, against a short commented allowlist, and put it in CI.
validation: Run the new scan on the current tree: it must flag state.svelte.ts:147 and GearPanel.svelte:723 and 742. Run the vitest cases against the current code: they must fail on the bugs above.

verdict.reason: web/package.json has only build, dev, preview and check scripts, and no test framework. tools/ has no scan of the TS side. rationale.md:37-39 says Rule 1 is enforced by defaults, bounds and strings crossing from Rust, but that stops duplication, not a new literal. The cited literals exist. state.svelte.ts:147 has `mate: { teeth: 43, ...}`, a tooth-count default that the wire Defaults type does not carry, which is a live Rule 1 violation. GearPanel.svelte:723/727 double radii into diameters, and 742/745 scale mm to µm by 1e3. corrections.md:494 records that one such case was found 'by sweeping the front end for engineering numbers rather than by anything failing', which supports the claim that only reading finds them.
verdict.evidence: cat web/package.json shows no test dependency. grep 'mate' web/src/wire/wasm/Defaults.ts finds nothing, so the 43 is TS-only. My rough scan of web/src script and markup, with comments, strings and <style> stripped, finds 121 numeric literals other than 0 and 1: 67 in TrainPanel, 18 in GearPanel, 16 in Viewport, 9 in core.ts, 8 in Offers and 3 in state.svelte.ts. A commented allowlist is feasible at that size.
verdict.proposal_note: The literal scan (part 2) is the direct, cheap enforcement of Rule 1. Do it first and put it in CI. For the cited cases, the fix is to have the core send the diameters and the mate default so that the literals go, not to allowlist them. vitest (part 1) adds npm devDependencies, which changes package-lock.json and so the fixed-output hash in `nix build .#web`, and it tests only pure helpers that the wasm probe partly covers already. It is worth doing but has lower value than part 2.

title: Friction can be typed negative, and the core then reports a mesh efficiency above 1 beside a path efficiency of 0
claim: The sliding and static friction rows are plain numberFields with no bound, so a designer can enter μ < 0. The core accepts it: the mesh reports forward efficiency 1.207 at μ = -1 and 1.010 at μ = -0.05, the path reports 0, and no note is raised. The panel shows '120.7 %' on the mesh and '0 %' on the path.
evidence: Probe p4: mu -1 gives mesh {forward:1.2069, backward:1.2069}, path {forward:0, backward:0}, notes []; mu -0.05 gives mesh 1.0103, path 0; mu 0 gives 1 and 0.99999999; mu 0.05 gives 0.9897 both.
proposal: The core should return a Bound for each mesh input (sliding_friction and static_friction ≥ 0, min_contact_ratio > 0, and so on), as GearResult.ranges does for gear inputs, and refuse or clamp μ < 0 with a Note. The panel shows the bound through FieldRow like every other bounded field.
validation: A core law: for every preset and μ in a sweep including negatives, mesh efficiency lies in [0, 1] or the solve carries a refusal note. A panel test: -1 shows the bound note.

verdict.reason: I reproduced it against the shipped wasm. Negative sliding friction yields a mesh efficiency above 1 and a path efficiency of exactly 0, with no mesh note, no train note and no failure. Nothing in gear-core, gear-io or gear-wasm bounds sliding_friction or static_friction. The friction fields are plain numberFields (TrainPanel.svelte:673-674) with no bound. The path's 0 is the more serious half: it is a wrong answer given silently. Under Rule 5 a negative coefficient describes nothing physical, so it should be clamped to 0 with a note, or refused.
verdict.evidence: notes/verify-web-4/p.mjs, run with node against web/src/wasm, varies sliding and static friction on the default train, which starts at 0.08 and 0.16. Sliding -1 gives mesh forward/backward 1.20688 and path 0/0, with notes [] and []. Sliding -0.05 (static 0.05 or -0.05) gives mesh 1.01034 and path 0/0, with no notes. Sliding 0 gives mesh 1 and path 0.9999999999999999. Sliding 0.05 gives 0.98966 for both. The only negative-sign handling for friction is in screw.rs:362 and shape.rs:2702, which concern the locking threshold and not the input. The same unbounded field also arrives through TOML import.
verdict.proposal_note: The minimal fix is in the solve (shape.rs, where the mesh efficiencies are computed around 3196): clamp μ<0 to 0 and emit a Note, per Rule 5, or refuse. The Bound for the panel can then be sent from the core, as GearResult.ranges already does. The proposed law (every preset, μ swept through negatives, mesh efficiency in [0,1] or a note present) is the right regression gate.

title: Minor duplicate or global state: the popup width is written in TS and CSS; import and adopt errors outlive their tab; defaults() is cloned for every preset label
claim:
The three items:
- Offers positions its preview with `POP = 320` while its CSS says `min(20rem, …)`: 320 px only at a 16 px root, and narrower on phones.
- trains.importError and workspace.adoptError are app-global, so a failed import shows in every train tab until the next successful import.
- names.preset and names.family call defaults(), a structuredClone of the full defaults including every preset shape (0.3-0.5 ms per call in probe p2), for every menu entry and label.
evidence: Code as cited; probe p2 'defaults clone 0.27-0.55 ms'.
proposal: Measure the popup (getBoundingClientRect after mount) or read a CSS variable. Put import and adopt errors on the view of the tab that caused them, or clear them on tab switch. Add a read-only `presetInfo()` in core.ts that returns the cached presets and families without cloning.
validation: Visual check at a 12 px root and on a phone width; switching tabs clears a stale error.

verdict.reason: Two of the three items hold as small inefficiencies or points of hygiene, and the popup item is narrower than stated. POP = 320 does duplicate `min(20rem, calc(100vw - 16px))`, but the default root is 16px (app.css sets 15px on body, not on html), so the two agree at default settings. On phones the placement is already safe: `beside` is false and `left` is clamped to 8, so the narrower CSS width still fits. The mismatch matters only when a user has enlarged the root font size, where the popup can be wider than 320 px and overflow the right edge when placed beside. importError is cleared only by a successful import, and a failed import creates no tab, so the error stays on every train tab. adoptError likewise shows on every gear tab. names.preset and names.family call defaults(), which structuredClones the full defaults (38 kB of JSON, 10 presets) three times per preset entry.
verdict.evidence: Offers.svelte:70 has `const POP = 320` and 285 has `width: min(20rem, calc(100vw - 16px))`. app.css:122-132 has `body {... font-size: 15px}`, and no html font-size is set. state.svelte.ts:343/359/370 show importError set on failure and cleared only on success. TrainPanel.svelte:214-217 is where the three defaults() calls per preset happen. offers.ts:69/130-131 call n.preset and n.family per offer. My measurement (notes/verify-web-4/c.mjs) is 0.27 ms per structuredClone(defaults), about 8 ms per add-menu render at 10 presets.
verdict.corrected_claim: The popup width is written twice, in TS (320) and CSS (20rem). They disagree only when the root font size is not 16px, not on phones. The import and adopt errors are app-global and persist across tabs until the next success. The preset and family labels clone the full defaults three times per preset offer, about 8 ms per render.
verdict.proposal_note: For the popup, set the width as a CSS variable (--pop-width) and read it with getComputedStyle, or measure the popup after mount. For the errors, clear them on tab switch or give them a dismiss control; attaching them to a tab does not fit a failed import, which creates no tab. For the labels, a non-cloning read-only accessor for the presets and families in core.ts is correct.

title: Graph indices are never validated: any train entry point, and import_train on a hand-edited file, panics, and a carried-by cycle allocates without bound
claim: A Train or Shape deserialises with any integer in mesh.a/b, body.axis and axis.carried_by, and nothing checks them afterwards. Shape::parts, Shape::relieved and everything built on them index these fields directly. An out-of-range index panics (a wasm trap). A carried_by that names a body on the same axis, or any carrier cycle, makes the loop 'A carried axis brings its carrier's' (graph.rs:288-299) push the same axis forever. gear_io::train::from_toml runs relief straight after parsing, so a hand-edited .toml file traps inside import_train rather than being refused with a reason.
evidence: Default spur train with shape.meshes[0].b=5: solve_train, offers, preview_edit, edit_train, relieve, relieve_case and adopt_member each throw RuntimeError 'unreachable'.
