Natively the panic is 'index out of bounds: the len is 2 but the index is 5' at shape.rs:1091:24 (relieved) and graph.rs:236:19 (parts). bodies[1].axis=7 panics at graph.rs:291:40. axes[1].carried_by=2 (the body on that same axis): the native run was OOM-killed at a 2 GB memory cap (exit 137); in wasm it traps after 0.4-2.3 s, having grown linear memory towards 4 GB. Round-tripping each of these through export_train and then import_train gives 'IMPORT REFUSED: RuntimeError unreachable' for all three (importtrap2.mjs). An out-of-range held or load index, by contrast, returns error.train_no_such_body cleanly.
proposal: (1) Fix the loop now: push the carrier's axis only if it is not already in `axes` (`if !axes.contains(&a)`), which also bounds it on any cycle. (2) Add Shape::validate() -> Result<(), ShapeError>, where ShapeError has a note() naming the bad piece and index. It checks mesh.a/b < members.len(), every member.body is in bodies, body.axis < axes.len(), distance axes < axes.len(), carried_by is GROUND or a listed body, carriers are acyclic, couplings name listed bodies, and held and load `at` are listed bodies. (3) Make an invalid graph unrepresentable: #[serde(try_from = "RawShape")] on Shape (and Train), so serde_json and toml both refuse at parse time with that note. Every entry point and from_toml then inherits the check with no per-call code.
validation: A law over every preset: for each index-carrying field, set it to len, len+5, self and a two-axis cycle, then call each train entry point natively under catch_unwind with a watchdog. Each must return Err or a failure note, never panic, and terminate. Add a step to tools/wasm_probe.mjs that imports a TOML with a carried_by cycle and records the refusal.

verdict.reason: Holds as stated. Nothing validates the graph's indices after deserialisation; there is no validate/try_from anywhere in train/, gear-io/src/train.rs or gear-wasm. from_toml (gear-io/src/train.rs:360) goes straight to relieved() -> shape.relieved(None), so a malformed file traps inside import_train. The carried_by loop at graph.rs:288-299 plainly cannot end on a self-carrier: axes[1].carried_by = the body on axis 1 makes axis_of_body return 1, 1 is pushed, k reaches it and pushes 1 again, forever. The panel's own edits are validated by the core, so the realistic ways in are a hand-edited or corrupted .toml and a developer calling the boundary. That still breaks rule 5 ('Refuse input that describes no shape at all'), and in the browser the cycle grows memory towards 4 GB.
verdict.evidence: Re-run against the built pkg (notes/verify-wasm-boundary-1/t0.mjs). mesh[0].b=5: solve_train throws RuntimeError unreachable, and export then import_train also throws RuntimeError unreachable. bodies[1].axis=7 does the same on both. held=[99] comes back cleanly as error.train_no_such_body. Given the machine's crash history, I did not run the carried_by cycle; graph.rs:288-299 shows the unbounded push directly. The only guard is dedup after the loop, which the loop never reaches.
verdict.proposal_note: (1) and (2) are sound. For (3), serde try_from on Shape covers JSON and TOML input but not shapes built in code. Keep validate() as a public fn and call it from solve_train/relieved too, or debug_assert it in Shape::apply's transact, so the edit laws also exercise it. Check the carrier-acyclicity rule against how GROUND (0) is encoded in carried_by.

repro.reproduction:
Probe crate /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/repro-wasm-boundary-0 (src/main.rs), built through gc, binary /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probe-target/debug/probe_repro_wasm_boundary_0 <case>. Every case uses the public API only. The base is Train::alone(&arrangements::pair([17,43]), 100.0, 1000.0), which has axes=2, bodies=[(1,ax0),(2,ax1)], members=2, meshes=1 and carried_by=[0,0]. One field is changed, then solve_train(&t, &default_library()) runs under catch_unwind. The same train is written with gear_io::train::to_toml and read back with from_toml, which is import_train's native path. Smallest inputs:
- `mesh2`: meshes[0].b = members.len() = 2 (off by one).
- `mesh`: meshes[0].b = 5.
- `axis`: bodies[1].axis = 7.
- `cycle`: axes[1].carried_by = 2, the body that sits on axis 1 (a self-carrier). In a file this is a single line, `carried_by = 2`, at line 92 of notes/repro-wasm-boundary-0/cycle.toml, which the probe wrote with `tomlcycle`. It was run with `ulimit -v 1000000` and `timeout 30`.
The unmodified base returns Ok on both paths, which is the control.
repro.observed:
What happened:
- **meshes[0].b=2 (and =5):** solve_train panics at graph.rs:236:19 with "index out of bounds: the len is 2 but the index is 2" (5 for the second input). from_toml panics at shape.rs:1091:24, inside relief (mesh_groups), with the same message.
- **bodies[1].axis=7:** both solve_train and from_toml panic at graph.rs:291:40 with "the len is 2 but the index is 7".
- **axes[1].carried_by=2:** the process aborted after 1.6 s with "memory allocation of 1073741824 bytes failed" at the 1 GB address-space cap. That is not a catchable panic: catch_unwind does not help, and the process dies. The cause is the loop at graph.rs:288-299. axis_of_body(2) returns 1, so 1 is pushed, k reaches it and pushes 1 again, and the Vec doubles without bound. The sort/dedup after the loop is never reached.

What is correct: every one of these files describes no shape at all, so rule 5 (CLAUDE.md) requires a refusal with a reason. The same entry points already do that for a bad hold (error.train_no_such_body, as the verifier observed). from_toml returns Result<_, TrainError::Parse> for input that does not match the schema, but here it never returns. Checking against the code:
- mesh a/b index members directly (graph.rs:246, shape.rs:1091).
- body.axis indexes axes (graph.rs:291).
- There is no validate or try_from anywhere on Shape or Train. carried_by only has the ground_if_null deserializer (shape.rs:118-124).

The claim holds exactly as stated, natively. I did not re-run the wasm trap or the 4 GB growth: the verifier's t0.mjs already shows RuntimeError unreachable for the first two, and the native abort shows the cycle's mechanism.
repro.note:
Severity re-judged from high to medium. The failure is loud: a panic or abort, never a silently wrong number. It needs malformed input, meaning a hand-edited or corrupted .toml, a stale stored train, or a developer calling the boundary, because the panel's own edits are validated by the core. Against that:
- It breaks rule 5.
- It breaks from_toml's documented contract that a document that is not a geartrain comes back as TrainError::Parse.
- In the browser the cycle case can hang the tab while memory grows. An off-by-one is enough to trigger it, which makes it the worst of the set.

On the proposal:
- **(1) is correct and minimal.** Change graph.rs:293-295 to `if let Some(a) = axis_of_body(carrier) { if !axes.contains(&a) { axes.push(a); } }`. This bounds the loop at axes.len() on any cycle.
- **GROUND encoding:** GROUND = 0 (kinematics.rs:118) and train bodies are numbered from 1, so the `carrier != GROUND` test is sound. A carried_by that names no listed body (e.g. 99) returns None and is skipped in this loop, so a validator should refuse that case explicitly.
- **(2)/(3):** add Shape::validate(). Use serde(try_from) on Train and Shape so both JSON and TOML refuse at parse time. Also call validate() at the top of solve_train and relieved, so shapes built in code are covered too.
- **Regression tests:** use the four probe cases above as a law over every preset: for each index field, try len, len+5, a self-carrier and a two-axis carrier cycle, and expect Err or a note, never a panic, and termination.

title: A trap poisons the wasm instance permanently, loses the panic message, and several wrappers swallow it silently
claim: wasm32-unknown-unknown panics abort to an 'unreachable' trap, and there is no panic hook, so the message and location are lost. Each trap leaks the shadow-stack frames and the call's allocations. After roughly 760-1000 traps, every call to every entry point, valid ones included, fails with 'memory access out of bounds' until the page is reloaded. Answers stay bit-identical until then. The web layer never re-instantiates. Several wrappers catch and discard the failure: profile and ringProfile return null (blank viewport), offersAt returns [], previewEdit returns null, relieveTrain and relieveCase return, and editTrain returns null for any message not starting with 'ui.'. The lib.rs module doc promises that 'Anything that can fail returns a reason rather than a number'.
evidence: poison3.mjs, alternating a trapping call with a good solve_gear and solve_train and comparing the answers: 'train after 1000 traps a good call threw: memory access out of bounds' and 'profile after 764 traps a good call threw: memory access out of bounds'. The answers matched until that point. offers and preview_edit run on hover, so a train that traps reaches that count through ordinary use.
proposal: (a) In core.ts, route every entry point through one wrapper. On WebAssembly.RuntimeError it re-instantiates from the cached WebAssembly.Module (initSync) and surfaces ui.train_boundary_failed with the panic text, never swallowing it. (b) In lib.rs, install a std::panic::set_hook once from a #[wasm_bindgen(start)] fn. It writes the PanicInfo (message and location) to a thread_local, and a `last_panic()` entry point, or the wrapper's error path, reads it. (c) Finding 1's validation makes the known panics unreachable; (a) and (b) cover the rest.
validation: A node test: 5000 trapping calls, then a good call must still return the recorded answer, and the surfaced error must contain the Rust panic location.

verdict.reason: The mechanism holds: there is no panic hook (grep finds no set_hook or wasm_bindgen(start) in gear-wasm), a trap loses the message, and the instance is poisoned after a fixed number of traps. core.ts swallows failures in profile, ringProfile, relieveTrain, relieveCase, previewEdit, offersAt and editTrain (for non-'ui.' messages). The comments call these swallows deliberate ('a defect on this side of the boundary ... swallowed'), but that argument assumes a failure can only be a JSON-shape defect, and a Rust panic is not one. It is also why the poisoning is invisible. I set severity to medium rather than high because ordinary panel use cannot reach 1000 traps: an import that traps is refused, and the train never gets into the panel. Reaching it needs another panic bug in a train the panel holds. It is defence in depth.
verdict.evidence: notes/verify-wasm-boundary-1/t1.mjs alternates the mesh b=5 solve_train (trap) with a good solve_train and compares each answer to the reference. Answers are bit-identical through 999 traps; then 'after 1000 traps good call threw: memory access out of bounds'. core.ts:528-535 (profile returns null), core.ts:708-715 (relieveTrain returns), core.ts:815-823 (editTrain returns null unless the message starts with 'ui.'), core.ts:834-844 (previewEdit returns null) and core.ts:851-856 (offersAt returns []).
verdict.proposal_note: Re-instantiating from a cached WebAssembly.Module on any WebAssembly.RuntimeError is the part that fixes the poisoning, and it is cheap. Read the panic hook's thread_local before re-instantiating, or the message is lost with the old memory. The hook works under panic=abort, since hooks run before the abort.

title: The ring tab's 'smallest tooth count' ignores profile shift, and its formula is written twice (served copy in lib.rs, tested copy in a ring.rs test)
claim: smallest_tooth_count computes ceil(2 h_a cos(beta) / (1 - cos(alpha_t))) from addendum, pressure angle and helix only. Its doc says 'the fewest teeth this design could have had and still cleared its own base circle'. The ring's tip is at r - (h_a - x) m, so the true bound is z > 2 (h_a - x) cos(beta) / (1 - cos(alpha_t)). Any shifted ring gets a wrong number. The formula is also written twice: lib.rs derives alpha_t itself, while the ring.rs test uses plane::transverse_pressure_angle. The core test checks its own copy, not the one served.
evidence: ringsmall.mjs, module 1, 20 deg, h_a=1, default cutter. x=+0.5: the tab reports 34, but the core's clamp.ring_tip_raised first fires at z=16 (z=17 is clean); the corrected formula gives 1/0.06031=16.6, so 17. x=-0.3: the tab reports 34, yet z=34 itself fires clamp.ring_tip_raised, and z=44 is the first clean count; the corrected formula gives 2.6/0.06031=43.1, so 44. The only lib.rs test (lib.rs:2310) asserts 34 at x=0.
proposal: Add Ring::smallest_tooth_count(params) in gear-core/src/ring.rs, derived from the same tip-radius expression Ring::cut_by uses, so it cannot diverge from the clamp. Delete lib.rs:554-561 and the formula in the ring.rs test. RingSummary calls the core function.
validation: Extend the_smallest_ring_follows_the_design_rather_than_a_rule_of_thumb into a law over a grid of x in [-0.5, 0.8], h_a, alpha and beta: building at z_min raises no CLAMP_RING_TIP_RAISED, and building at z_min - 1 raises it.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by derivation and by running it. Ring::cut_by sets ra = r - m(h_a - x) (ring.rs:275) and clamps to rb (ring.rs:278-303), so the base-circle bound is z >= 2(h_a - x)cos(beta)/(1 - cos(alpha_t)). lib.rs:554-561 omits x. The duplicate is real too: lib.rs derives alpha_t inline, the ring.rs:1244 test uses plane::transverse_pressure_angle, and the core test checks its own copy rather than the one served. The figure exists to tell a designer which margin they are on, and it is wrong for every shifted ring, by 2x in one direction.
verdict.evidence: notes/verify-wasm-boundary-1/t2.mjs, module 1, 20 deg, h_a=1, default cutter. The tab reports smallest_tooth_count=34 at every x. At x=0.5, z=16 fires clamp.ring_tip_raised and z=17 does not; the formula with x gives 16.58 -> 17. At x=-0.3, z=34 and z=43 fire it and z=44 does not; with x it gives 43.11 -> 44. At x=0.3, z=23 fires and z=24 does not; with x it gives 23.21 -> 24.
verdict.proposal_note: Moving the function into ring.rs, next to the ra expression, is right. When h_a - x <= 0 the threshold is <= 0: return 1, as .max(1.0) already does, and state that. The doc should also say the count is the base-circle bound only. At the same counts ring_flank_ungenerated and, on large rings, the pointed-tip bound can still fire, so 'fewest teeth this design could have had' overstates it.

repro.reproduction:
I ran the `.wasm` the browser loads: the gear_wasm pkg built from sources that have not changed since 2026-09-24, loaded through `solve_ring`. The script is /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/repro-wasm-boundary-2/sweep.mjs, run with `nix develop /home/user/gearcalc -c node sweep.mjs`. It covers h_a in {1, 0.8}, α in {20°, 25°}, β in {0°, 30°} and x in {-0.5, -0.3, 0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.8}. For each design it walks z upward from 3 and finds the first z whose result carries no `clamp.ring_tip_raised` (the core's own check that the tip has not dropped below the base circle), then compares that z with the `smallest_tooth_count` the ring tab shows.

**Smallest input:** module 1, α = 20°, h_a = 1, β = 0, default cutter, x = +0.5. The tab says 34, but z = 17 builds clean and z = 16 clamps.

**How the correct value is known:** a closed form written in JS, sharing no code with the Rust. The tip is at r − (h_a − x)m and the base circle at r·cos α_t, so the tip clears the base circle when z > 2(h_a − x)cos β / (1 − cos α_t). The same condition appears in ring.rs:275-303, where it sets `ra = r - m*(addendum - x)`.
repro.observed:
The tab's figure never moves with profile shift, and it was wrong in 20 of the 24 designs swept. It was right only at x = 0.

For h_a = 1, α = 20°, β = 0, the tab shows 34 at every x. The first z that builds clean is:

| x | first clean z |
|---|---|
| -0.5 | 50 |
| -0.3 | 44 |
| 0 | 34 |
| 0.3 | 24 |
| 0.5 | 17 |
| 0.8 | 7 |

The other designs behave the same way:
- **h_a = 0.8:** the tab shows 27; the truth is 44 / 37 / 27 / 17 / 10 for x = -0.5 to 0.5.
- **α = 25°:** the tab shows 22; the truth is 33 / 28 / 22 / 15 / 11 / 5.
- **β = 30°:** the tab shows 23; the truth is 34 / 29 / 23 / 16 / 12 / 5.

The closed form with x matched the core's clamp in every case. The one exception is h_a = 0.8, x = 0.8, where the formula gives 1 and the scan started at z = 3.

The error runs both ways:
- **Negative shift:** the tab gives a count that is too small. At x = -0.3 it says 34, yet a 34-tooth ring would be clamped, and 44 is the first clean count. A designer who trusts it builds a ring the core has to repair.
- **Positive shift:** the tab is too strict, by up to 5× at x = 0.8 (34 against 7).

The duplicate formula is confirmed too. lib.rs:554-561 (`smallest_tooth_count`) derives α_t inline and has no x term. The test at ring.rs:1244 recomputes its own copy through `plane::transverse_pressure_angle`, and it and the only lib.rs test check x = 0 alone, so no test runs the served function with a shift.
repro.note:
I re-judge severity as medium, not high. The shown figure is wrong for every shifted ring, sometimes by a factor of several, and in the unsafe direction when x < 0. But it is advice only: the geometry is still clamped and reported correctly through `clamp.ring_tip_raised`, so nothing downstream (outline, strength, DXF) is computed from the wrong count.

The ledger's proposal stands:
- Add `Ring::smallest_tooth_count` in gear-core/src/ring.rs, built from the same tip-radius expression as `cut_by`. Have `RingSummary` call it, and delete the lib.rs copy and the formula copied into the test.
- Make the test a law over a grid of x, h_a, α and β: z_min builds with no `CLAMP_RING_TIP_RAISED`, and z_min − 1 raises it. Where h_a − x ≤ 0 the bound is 1.
- Change the doc to say this is the base-circle bound only, since `ring_flank_ungenerated` and the pointed-tip bound can still fire.

I made no worktree and no probe crate, so there was nothing to clean up. The only files written are under /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/repro-wasm-boundary-2/.

title: The over-pins range around an eccentric gear is computed in the boundary, silently skips seats that fail, and depends on whether tooth 0 seats
claim: lib.rs builds PinsOut.around by looping over_pins_at over every start and ignoring errors (`if let Ok`), taking the nominal at start 0. best_span_around, the core's equivalent for span, refuses unless every position measures. Its doc says 'a span that can only be taken at some angular positions is not a measurement of the gear'. So two policies answer one question, and the looser one lives outside gear-core. Whether the tab shows a number at all is decided by whether the arbitrary tooth 0 seats the pin. The panel sends out-of-range pins to Rust (it only checks > 0), so this path is live. Separately, the endpoints of pin_diameter_range_around are verdict flips, and the panel wraps them as an inclusive Bound, a bound decided in TypeScript.
evidence: Eccentric gear z=23, x=0.2, angular_shift=0.5; published pin range [1.35917, 3.03441]. d=0.999*lo: start 0 seats, 21 of 23 positions measurable, and solve_gear returns a nominal and around [24.126, 24.420] with no flag. d=0.99*lo: 17 of 23 measurable but start 0 fails, so the result is unavailable (error.measure_pin_too_small). d=lo and d=hi exactly: 21 of 23 measurable, yet GearPanel.svelte:209 builds the bound with exclusive_min and exclusive_max false.
proposal: Add metrology::over_pins_around(gear, d, count) -> Result<(OverPins, [f64; 2]), MeasurementError>, requiring every start and returning the failing seat's error, as best_span_around does. lib.rs calls it and its loop is deleted. Publish the pin range as a gear_core::auto::Bound with exclusive ends, crossing as ranges.pin_diameter, so the panel stops constructing one.
validation: Law: over_pins_around is Ok exactly when d lies strictly inside pin_diameter_range_around, over eccentric and concentric gears. Over-pins with index_offset rotated by one tooth gives the same verdict.

verdict.reason: Holds. lib.rs:357-374 takes the nominal from over_pins_at(start 0) and folds the range over `if let Ok` seats. best_span_around (metrology.rs:609) requires every position and says why. So two policies answer one question, and the looser one sits in the boundary. Running it shows the silent subset produces a discontinuity. The TS-built Bound (GearPanel.svelte:209) is real but minor: the ends are 64-halving bisection midpoints, so inclusive versus exclusive differs by an ulp. The real issue is that a pin outside the published range gets a number.
verdict.evidence: notes/verify-wasm-boundary-1/t3.mjs, z=23, x=0.2, angular_shift=0.5, range [1.359166, 3.034407]. At d=0.99*lo the result is unavailable (error.measure_pin_too_small). At d=0.995*lo and 0.999*lo, below the published range, you get a nominal and around [24.091, 24.399] and [24.126, 24.420] with no flag. At d=lo*1.0001, inside, around[0] drops to 24.104 from 24.134 at d=lo: the low end jumps as the seats that had been dropped start to measure. With index_offset 0..3, around[0] moves between 24.091 and 24.126 at the same d.
verdict.proposal_note: over_pins_around in metrology.rs, with every-start-or-error, mirrors best_span_around exactly. The boundary loop and its `if let Ok` then go. Move the exclusive flags into Rust along with the Bound, but that is cosmetic next to the silent subset.

title: The DXF's reference circles are the raw tooth's, not the gear the panel quotes
claim: export_dxf_impl passes Tooth::new(params) to gear_to_dxf. That function draws the outline from Gear::new(gear.params), which is correct, but takes the pitch, base, tip and root circles from the raw tooth. The summary quotes Gear::mean(), the tooth rebuilt by the shared cutter. For an eccentric gear the drawing's root reference circle therefore disagrees with the panel and matches neither the mean nor the cut root.
evidence: dxfcircles.mjs, z=23, 25 deg, x=0.2, angular_shift=1.0: summary pitch/base/tip/root 11.5 / 10.4225 / 12.5 / 10.45; DXF circles 11.5 / 10.4225 / 12.5 / 10.7; the cut root varies over [9.459, 11.45].
proposal: Change gear_io::gear_to_dxf to take &gear_core::gear::Gear and draw the circles from gear.mean(), the tooth summarise quotes. export_dxf_impl builds Gear::new(resolved) once and passes it.
validation: Test in gear-wasm: for an eccentric gear, the DXF CIRCLE radii equal solve_gear's pitch/base/tip/root radii. python3 tools/validate_dxf.py still passes.

verdict.corrected_claim: On an eccentric gear whose shared tool cuts deeper than its own dedendum (or trims tips), the DXF's construction-layer root (and possibly tip) reference circle is the raw Tooth::new value, not Gear::mean(), which the summary quotes. The outline itself is correct. It only occurs for the eccentric kind, which is developer-only in the panel (core.ts:295 developer: true), and only when the dedendum is shallower than some tooth needs. With the default dedendum 1.25 the circles agree.
verdict.reason: The mechanism is exactly as stated (lib.rs:708 Tooth::new; dxf.rs:119-127 draws circles from gear.r/rb/ra/rf while the outline goes through Gear::new). But it only fires under a narrow condition the finding does not state, on a developer-mode kind, and on the construction layer. Hence low.
verdict.evidence: notes/verify-wasm-boundary-1/t4.mjs. With dedendum 1.25, addendum 1: summary and DXF agree (10.45) at angular_shift 0 and 1. With the auditor's addendum 0.8, dedendum 1.0, index_offset 1: angular_shift 0 gives 10.7 for both; angular_shift 1 gives summary root 10.45 but DXF 10.70.
verdict.proposal_note: Passing &Gear and drawing from gear.mean() is right, and it also removes the second Gear::new that gear_to_dxf makes internally.

title: Five error shapes cross the boundary, and English sentences and a Rust Debug dump reach the user
claim: Errors come back as: 'bad gear|ring|train request: <serde>'; a bare serde message (adopt, relieve, relieve_case, edit, preview, offers); a catalogue key as the message, which editTrain tells apart with startsWith('ui.'); the Debug format of TrainError (relieve_case: 'Wiring(0, NotAMesh(0))'); and English prose written in lib.rs. The unreachable-throw prose ('a centre-distance throw of X mm is not reachable with this mate - a larger tooth-count difference ...') is reachable by typing a large throw, and GearPanel shows it in whatever language is selected. That contradicts the catalogue rule the rest of the boundary follows (TrainOutcome's doc explains why a failure must be a Note).
evidence: run.log: relieve_case with mesh a=b gives 'Wiring(0, NotAMesh(0))'; relieve_case with no library gives 'missing field `library`'; solve_gear with throw=1000 gives the English sentence; adopt with member 99 gives 'the train has no member 100'. GearPanel.svelte:452 passes result.error into FieldNote.
proposal: One contract: a JsError means the request was not valid JSON for its type (a developer fault). Everything a designer can reach comes back as a Note in the payload. Concretely: GearSummary gains `throw_refused: Option<Note>` (key ui.gear_throw_unreachable, value throw), or solve_gear returns {ok} | {refused: Note}. relieve_case maps TrainError through e.note(). Adopt's two refusals become notes on AdoptOutcome.failure. editTrain gets a typed {refused: key} instead of sniffing the message. Five catalogue entries.
validation: A lib.rs test drives every *_impl through its designer-reachable refusals and asserts that each comes back as a Note whose key is in the English catalogue. The existing strings firing test then covers the translations.

verdict.reason: The five shapes exist as described: 'bad X request:' prefixes (lib.rs:564, 630, 834), bare serde messages (adopt, relieve_case, edit), a catalogue key sniffed by startsWith('ui.') in core.ts:821, Debug output `{e:?}` for TrainError in relieve_case (lib.rs:1501), and English prose in lib.rs:660-677 and 1385-1389. The throw prose reaches the user through GearPanel.svelte:452 FieldNote in any language, but only on the eccentric kind, which is developer-only. relieve_case's Debug text is swallowed by relieveCase and never shown. The finding misses the more reachable English: import_train and import_materials return TrainError/toml Display text (lib.rs:972-979), which Sidebar.svelte:120 and TrainPanel.svelte show verbatim to a designer importing a bad file.
verdict.evidence: lib.rs:1501 `.map_err(|e| format!("{e:?}"))`; lib.rs:671-676 English format!; lib.rs:1385 'the train has no member {}'; core.ts:821 `message.startsWith("ui.")`; GearPanel.svelte:452 shows result.error; state.svelte.ts:411-414 and Sidebar.svelte:119-120 show a library import error string.
verdict.proposal_note: The one-contract proposal is sound. Extend it to the two file imports: wrap the parser's own message (inherently English, with line and column) as a value inside a keyed Note such as ui.import_unreadable {detail}, so the sentence around it is translated.

title: The generated-bindings check cannot see request shapes: seven request types and TrainEdit are hand-written in TypeScript, and unknown fields are silently ignored
claim: check_bindings.sh regenerates only the types that derive TS. It is transitively complete for outputs and for GearRequest, RingRequest and TrainRequest, because a TS-derived struct forces TS on its fields. AdoptRequest, RelieveRequest, RelieveCaseRequest, EditRequest, TrainEdit, PreviewRequest and OffersRequest derive no TS, and languages() builds its rows with json!. core.ts writes these shapes by hand, TrainEdit as a full copy of the Rust enum, so a Rust rename type-checks green. No request struct uses deny_unknown_fields, although the TOML document types do, so a misnamed optional field silently falls back to its default. The library field is called 'materials' (optional) in three requests and 'library' (required) in relieve_case, which is why core.ts calls defaultLibrary() on every case relief.
evidence: The probe sends {train, library} to solve_train at wasm_probe.mjs:131, 264 and 265, where the field is `materials`. The library is dropped and the default used, which is invisible only because the two libraries are equal. run.log: 'solve_train unknown field' and 'solve_gear unknown field' both return ok. web/src/wire/wasm has 20 files and none is a request type for those six entry points.
proposal: Derive TS (export_to wasm/) on the seven request types and TrainEdit, and replace the json! row in languages_impl with a #[derive(Serialize, TS)] LanguageEntry. Import them in core.ts and delete the hand-written TrainEdit. Add #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] to every request struct. Name the library `materials: Option<MaterialLibrary>` everywhere, and fix the probe's three calls.
validation: In a worktree, rename a request field in Rust: check_bindings plus npm run check must fail. A probe call with a misspelt field must come back refused, recorded in wasm_boundary.json.

verdict.reason: Holds as stated. The seven request structs in crates/gear-wasm/src/lib.rs (AdoptRequest 1338, RelieveRequest 1451, RelieveCaseRequest 1489, TrainEdit 1544, EditRequest 1550, PreviewRequest 1608, OffersRequest 1650) derive only Deserialize, with no TS. web/src/wire/wasm holds 20 files and none of them is one of these. core.ts:809-812 is a hand copy of the TrainEdit enum. That contradicts the header check_bindings.sh writes into wire/index.ts: "Nothing here is written by hand. core.ts used to carry a copy of every one of these". No struct in lib.rs uses deny_unknown_fields, although params.rs, material.rs, ring.rs and train/mod.rs do. The library field is `materials: Option` in AdoptRequest, PreviewRequest and TrainRequest, and `library` (required) in RelieveCaseRequest; core.ts:710 calls defaultLibrary() on every relief because of that. wasm_probe.mjs:131, 264 and 265 send `{ train, library }` to solve_train, and that field is dropped without a word. One partial mitigation: check_wasm runs the hand-written probe, so renaming a *required* field or a TrainEdit variant in Rust does fail there. An optional field, and core.ts's copy, are not covered by any gate.
verdict.evidence: grep 'deny_unknown' crates/gear-wasm/src/lib.rs finds no match. ls web/src/wire/wasm lists AdoptOutcome, Adopted, ClassRef, CutterRef, Defaults, GearRequest, GearSummary, GearTabDefaults, MateRef, Maybe, PinsOut, PresetEntry, PresetFamilyEntry, RingRequest, RingSummary, SpanOut, ToleranceOut, TrainFailure, TrainOutcome, TrainRequest and nothing else. In notes/wasm-boundary/results.json, 'solve_train unknown field' ({materails: ...}) comes back status OK, and so does 'solve_gear unknown field' ({pin_diamter}). wasm_probe.mjs:131 reads `w.solve_train(JSON.stringify({ train: t, library }))`, and lib.rs:755 reads `pub materials: Option<gear_core::MaterialLibrary>`.
verdict.proposal_note: Sound. Before adding deny_unknown_fields, check that no UI object carries extras. GearPanel's GearRequest and RingRequest literals match their fields exactly, and `tab.mate` must stay exactly {teeth, profile_shift, internal}. Also ts-type RelieveRequest and OffersRequest, and have core.ts annotate each JSON.stringify argument with the generated type (as solveTrain already does with TrainRequest), so npm run check sees the shapes. relieveCase, editTrain and previewEdit swallow every error. Without that change a rename degrades to silent no-ops rather than type errors.

title: The figures a fresh load case starts at are two copies of the same literals, and the tab defaults live in the boundary rather than the core
claim: defaults_impl writes LoadCase::ultimate(.., 0.1, 30_000.0) and fatigue(.., 0.02, 30_000.0). apply_edit's AddCase writes (0.1, 30_000.0) and (0.02, 30_000.0) again, with the comment 'The figures a fresh case starts at are the shipped train's'. Nothing ties the two together. UI_SEED=5 mm face width, teeth 9, pin 1.75 mm and throw 0.1 mm are engineering defaults in the boundary crate, invisible to gear-cli and the core suite. reference_circles: true duplicates REFERENCE_CIRCLES_BY_DEFAULT. pin 1.75 mm and throw 0.1 mm are absolute, not scaled by module.
evidence: lib.rs:1175-1177 against 1576-1577. The test the_defaults_this_boundary_invents_are_the_ones_it_shipped asserts the literals of defaults_impl only, not add_case.
proposal: Add CaseKind::fresh_figures() -> (torque, speed) in gear-core; both sites call it. Move the tab defaults into one gear-core constructor (for example gear_core::defaults::gear_tab() and Train::fresh()) that the boundary serialises. REFERENCE_CIRCLES_BY_DEFAULT is used at line 1161.
validation: Test: edit_train add_case on the default train yields a case whose figures equal defaults.train.load_cases[0] and [2].

verdict.reason: lib.rs:1175-1177 writes ultimate(.., 0.1, 30_000.0) and fatigue(.., 0.02, 30_000.0). apply_edit at lib.rs:1575-1578 writes the same pairs a second time, under the comment 'The figures a fresh case starts at are the shipped train's'. Nothing ties the two together. the_defaults_this_boundary_invents_are_the_ones_it_shipped asserts only the defaults_impl literals (lib.rs:2853-2866). The probe does record the add_case output in tools/wasm_boundary.json, so a change to one copy would show up as a change-detector diff, but nothing would flag the two copies disagreeing. UI_SEED, teeth 9, pin 1.75 mm and throw 0.1 mm are UI starting values in the boundary crate. That is still Rust, so it does not break rule 1. Pin 1.75 mm is about 1.75·m at the default m = 1 and does not scale with module. It is only a starting value, and the panel shows the admissible pin range beside it. reference_circles: true (lib.rs:1161) duplicates REFERENCE_CIRCLES_BY_DEFAULT (lib.rs:123).
verdict.evidence: sed -n 1170-1180 and 1570-1580 crates/gear-wasm/src/lib.rs. grep in the wasm tests finds no add_case assertion. tools/wasm_probe.mjs:151-153 records add_case only as data.
verdict.proposal_note: The smallest fix is a gear-core `LoadCase::fresh_figures(kind) -> (torque, speed)`, or a `Train::fresh_case(kind)` without figures, used by both sites. Moving the gear-tab starting values into gear-core is optional, since they are UI seeds and not engineering. The pin default could be expressed as a multiple of module, or left as it is with a comment. Also use REFERENCE_CIRCLES_BY_DEFAULT at lib.rs:1161.

title: check_wasm's coverage gate reads exports by grepping source for an exact attribute line
claim: The exported set is taken from `grep -A2 '^#\[wasm_bindgen\]$'` followed by `pub fn`. An entry point written #[wasm_bindgen(js_name = x)], with more than one attribute between, or in another module escapes the gate. The set the payload actually exports is available in the build.
evidence: Script text at check_wasm.sh:108-110. The d.ts produced by the same run lists 'export function' for every entry.
proposal: Read the exports from the built module: node -e with WebAssembly.Module.exports on the optimised wasm (minus memory and __wbindgen_*), or the `export function` lines of the generated gear_wasm.d.ts. Compare that list with `called`.
validation: In a worktree, add #[wasm_bindgen(js_name = probe_me)] pub fn x(); the gate must fail.

verdict.reason: check_wasm.sh:108-110 takes the exported set from `grep -A2 '^#\[wasm_bindgen\]$' lib.rs | sed -n 's/^pub fn .../p'`. Today it finds all 23, and `#[must_use]` between the attribute and the fn is tolerated. A `#[wasm_bindgen(js_name = ...)]` attribute, a second module, a macro-generated entry, or three or more attribute lines would each escape the gate silently. The built artifacts list exports independently of how the source is written.
verdict.evidence: The grep pipeline on the current tree gives 23 unique names, and there are 23 '^#[wasm_bindgen' lines. crates/gear-wasm/src holds only lib.rs, so the gap is latent. web/src/wasm/gear_wasm.d.ts has 24 'export function' lines: the 23 entries plus initSync.
verdict.proposal_note: If the d.ts is used, drop wasm-bindgen's glue (initSync and the default init) as well as __wbindgen_*. WebAssembly.Module.exports on the optimised module is the cleanest source.

title: The 23 entry points could be about 12, and 23 near-identical wrappers could be one generic helper
claim: Six entry points are static data: version, defaults, languages, default_materials, resolve_language, and strings per language. version, languages and the default library could ride on defaults. Each keystroke calls solve_gear and gear_profile separately, each re-parsing and rebuilding Gear::new. Every train entry point re-deserialises the whole train. Each entry is written as a `_impl` plus a wasm wrapper with its own map_err text, which is where the five error shapes came from.
evidence: lib.rs has 23 #[wasm_bindgen] fns, each with a hand-written pair. GearPanel.svelte:250-253 calls profile and ringProfile beside solve and solveRing.
proposal: Add a generic `fn json<Rq: DeserializeOwned, Rs: Serialize>(input: &str, f: impl FnOnce(Rq) -> Rs) -> Result<String, String>` and write each entry as one line. Fold version, languages and default_materials into Defaults. Optionally add `profile_points: Option<usize>` to GearRequest and RingRequest so one call returns the summary and the outline. Keep the train verbs separate: they are distinct questions, and one dispatch enum would only move the match.
validation: tools/check_wasm.sh --write diff limited to the removed entries; npm run check green.

verdict.reason: The per-entry boilerplate is real: 23 wasm wrappers, each a hand pair of `_impl` plus `map_err(|e| JsError::new(&e))`. A generic `json` helper would shorten them, and version, languages and default_materials could ride on defaults. The claim of 'about 12' is not supported, though. strings(language), resolve_language(tag), the import/export pairs, the three train verbs and the DXF exports are distinct questions. Folding the three static ones and merging the two profile calls into solve leaves about 18. The per-keystroke cost of calling solve_gear and gear_profile separately is two Gear::new builds, microseconds in a pure boundary. That is a tidiness issue, not a performance one.
verdict.evidence: lib.rs has 23 `#[wasm_bindgen]` fns and 54 map_err sites. GearPanel.svelte:247-254 derives outline = profile(request, 600) separately from result = solve(request). strings and resolve_language take arguments, so they cannot be folded into defaults().
verdict.corrected_claim: The 23 wrappers could share one generic JSON helper. About three static-data entries (version, languages, default_materials) could fold into defaults, and the two profile calls could be merged into solve_gear/solve_ring as an option: about 18 entry points, not 12. This is a modest cleanup with no correctness or performance stake.
verdict.proposal_note: Folding default_materials into defaults also removes the need for core.ts:710's defaultLibrary() re-parse per relief, if relieve_case takes `materials: Option` (see finding 6). Keep `strings` per language: shipping every catalogue inside defaults would inflate the first load.

title: Stale or misplaced documentation at the boundary
claim: The default_materials doc comment (lib.rs:992-997) sits above solve_ring's, so the generated .d.ts gives solve_ring both texts and default_materials none. The languages doc (906-912) is attached to resolve_language_impl. The Cargo.toml description says 'three functions' (there are 23). solve_train's doc says 'The third of the three entry points', which is history. The module doc's 'Anything that can fail returns a reason' is not true of the traps.
evidence: web/src/wasm/gear_wasm.d.ts:272-284 shows 'The material library the tool ships with ... Derived geometry for one internal gear' on solve_ring, and gear_wasm.d.ts:32 has default_materials undocumented.
proposal: Move each comment onto its fn, update the Cargo description to 'JSON in, JSON out', delete the 'third of three' sentence, and scope the module-doc claim until findings 1 and 2 land.
validation: Regenerated d.ts shows each doc on its own function; check_doc_links passes.

verdict.reason: Confirmed in both the source and the generated d.ts. The default_materials doc (lib.rs:992-997) sits directly above solve_ring's doc, so gear_wasm.d.ts:273-285 gives solve_ring both texts, and default_materials (d.ts:32) has none. The 'languages this build ships' doc (lib.rs:906-912) is attached to resolve_language_impl, while languages()'s own doc says 'See [`languages_impl`]', which points at an undocumented fn. Cargo.toml says 'three functions', against 23. solve_train's doc says 'The third of the three entry points docs/rationale.md#the-stack planned', which is history. One sub-claim is overstated: the module doc's 'Anything that can fail returns a reason' sits in a paragraph about measurements (span, pins, tolerance class) returning Maybe::Unavailable rather than a number. It is not a claim about panics, so it is inaccurate only in its broad first sentence.
verdict.evidence: grep -B12 'export function solve_ring' web/src/wasm/gear_wasm.d.ts shows 'The material library the tool ships with ... Derived geometry for one internal gear.' lib.rs:1248 has `#[wasm_bindgen] pub fn default_materials` with no preceding doc. crates/gear-wasm/Cargo.toml:3 reads 'Thin by design: three functions, JSON in, JSON out.'
verdict.proposal_note: Move the languages doc onto languages_impl, or onto languages() itself and drop the 'See' link. Rewording the module doc's first sentence to 'A measurement that cannot be made returns a reason' fixes it without waiting on other findings.

title: The eccentric gear's mate silently inherits this gear's addendum, dedendum, root radius and thickness factor
claim: eccentric_mate builds the mate as Tooth::new(GearParams { teeth, profile_shift, angular_shift: 0, index_offset: 0, ..req.params }), so it copies thickness_mod, addendum, dedendum and root_radius. MateRef's doc justifies sending less by saying the mate shares module, pressure angle and helix 'by definition'. thickness_mod is not shared by definition, and it changes a zero-backlash centre distance. This is an assumption the user cannot see or change.
evidence: Code reading at lib.rs:638-644. I did not measure how much centre_profile reads the mate's thickness.
proposal: Either state the assumption in MateRef's doc and the panel note, or add thickness_mod (default 1) to MateRef and build the mate with it. Better still, move eccentric_mate into gear-core beside centre_profile.
validation: Test: centre_profile with the mate's thickness_mod at 1 and at 0.95 differs by the amount the zero-backlash relation predicts.

verdict.reason: eccentric_mate (lib.rs:636-651) builds the mate with `..req.params`, so it copies thickness_mod, addendum, dedendum, root_radius and helix. Only thickness_mod reaches centre_profile_of, through `x_mate = profile_shift + thickness_shift()` at gear.rs:922. Addendum, dedendum and root radius do not enter, and neither does the helix hand, since same_rack_as ignores it and mt and alpha_t come from this gear. So the real exposure is thickness_mod, which is not shared 'by definition'. Its own doc says 'Two gears in mesh must sum to 2 for zero backlash', and copying it makes the sum 2k instead of k+1. The gear tab exposes a thickness modification field, and the panel's mate note reads 'shares module, pressure angle and helix', so the user cannot see this assumption.
verdict.evidence: Probe probes/verify-wasm-boundary-2, z = 20 at angular_shift 0.3 against a z = 40 mate, m = 1. At k = 0.95 with the mate at 1.0: mean commanded distance 29.884072, amplitude 0.30986. With the mate copying 0.95: mean 29.770343, amplitude 0.32007. So the mean moves by 0.114 mm and the throw by 3.3 %. At k = 0.98 the mean moves 0.044 mm and the throw 1.2 %. At k = 1 the two agree exactly.
verdict.proposal_note: Add `thickness_mod` (serde default 1.0) to MateRef and build the mate with it, rather than only documenting the assumption. A mate with nominal thickness is the neutral reading, and the error is first-order in (1 − k). resolved_params' throw inversion uses the same mate, so it is fixed by the same change.

title: Chord tolerance is clamped and replaced without a note, and has no published bound
claim: Ring and gear outlines raise chord_tolerance to MIN_RELATIVE_TOLERANCE * r_f and replace a non-finite or non-positive value with the default, without raising a clamp note (rule 5). The panel's only bound is an HTML min=0. Very small tolerances produce DXF strings of 20-150 MB that the tab builds in memory.
evidence: run.log: export_dxf with chord 1e-9, 1e-12 and 1e-300 gives 20.8 / 21.8 / 21.8 MB (the floor bites silently); export_ring_dxf with chord 1e-12 gives 151,719,047 bytes in 6.2 s.
proposal: Publish chord_tolerance as a Bound in the ranges, with its floor, and push a clamp note when the floor or the fallback is applied.
validation: Test: outline at 1e-12 carries clamp.chord_tolerance_raised; the panel shows the bound.

verdict.reason: The sizes reproduce, but the auditor names the wrong cause. The relative floor is not what caps the output. MAX_SUBDIVISION_DEPTH = 14 (outline.rs:49) does, and it stops subdividing without saying so. That breaks the contract in the doc comment, 'accurate to chord_tolerance millimetres'. The non-positive/NaN fallback to the default is also silent, as claimed. The proposed Bound at 1e-12·r would be useless as a UI bound.
verdict.corrected_claim: Asking for a tighter chord tolerance than the outline can meet goes unreported. Subdivision stops at MAX_SUBDIVISION_DEPTH = 14 (2^14 chords per curve, outline.rs:49 and 88). Below about 1e-10 mm for the default 9-tooth, m=1 gear, the returned outline no longer meets the tolerance requested, and there is no note. Output size is bounded per curve, not per part: it grows about as 6·2^14·z vertices, so a 60-tooth ring at 1e-9 mm is already 99 MB and a many-toothed ring can exhaust the tab's memory. The relative floor MIN_RELATIVE_TOLERANCE·r (5.5e-12 mm here) hardly ever binds before the depth cap does. The gear path takes it on r_a (gear.rs:613) and the ring path on r_f (outline.rs:265), while its doc comment says 'relative to the tip radius'. A value of 0, a negative or NaN silently becomes DEFAULT_CHORD_TOLERANCE. The panel's input has only min=0, and 0 turns into the 1 um default without a word.
verdict.evidence: My own run of the auditor's wasm pkg (notes/verify-wasm-boundary-3/t.mjs, r.mjs). export_dxf, default gear (z=9, m=1, r_a=5.5 mm): chord 1e-3 → 29,686 B / 3 ms; 1e-6 → 794,073; 1e-8 → 8,008,743; 1e-9 → 20,844,224 / 386 ms; 1e-10, 1e-11, 1e-12 and 1e-300 → 21,838,721 each. The size is identical from 1e-10 down, and the relative floor (5.5e-12) is not active at 1e-10 or 1e-11, so the plateau is the depth cap. export_ring_dxf, z=60: 1e-3, 0 and -1 → 108,460 B each (the silent fallback); 1e-9 → 99,001,975 B / 1.9 s; 1e-12 → 151,719,047 B / 2.7 s. Code: outline.rs:88 `if sagitta <= tolerance || depth >= MAX_SUBDIVISION_DEPTH { out.push(...) }` gives no signal. outline.rs:59-63 doc says 'relative to the tip radius'; ring.outline uses self.rf. GearPanel.svelte:548 has `min="0"` only.
verdict.proposal_note: A UI Bound at 1e-12·r does nothing useful: the practical limit is the depth cap, and it depends on z and curve length. Better: (1) have outline() report the tolerance it achieved, meaning the largest sagitta left where the cap stopped, and raise a note (e.g. clamp.chord_tolerance_unmet) when that exceeds the request. Raise another when 0/negative/NaN was replaced. The DXF entry points need a result type with notes for this, since today they return a bare String. (2) Bound the total work by a vertex budget instead of a per-curve depth, or derive the depth from the tolerance and the curve length. (3) Use one radius for the relative floor, the largest radius of the part, and fix the doc comment. Nothing is needed in TypeScript beyond showing the note.

title: centre_profile branches on angular_shift == 0.0 exactly
claim: At exactly 0 the answer is unavailable (ui.gear_concentric_has_no_profile), while at 1e-300 it is a flat profile. The branch lives in the boundary rather than the core.
evidence: Code reading.
proposal: Move the decision into gear_core::gear::Gear::centre_profile. Either return the constant profile for zero variation, with the panel rendering a point, or decide on variation().eccentricity == 0 in one place.
validation: centre_profile is continuous as angular_shift goes to 0.

verdict.reason: The discontinuity is real and I measured it. At angular_shift = 1e-300 the core's answer is bit-identical to the answer at 0 (x + 1e-300·cos θ == x in f64): a flat profile with mean 26.000000000000004 mm. At exactly 0 the boundary throws that away and gives a note that does not even state the one constant distance. The readout loses a number at one point. The exact-zero test sits in gear-wasm, while the only other concentric test is in the core (gear.rs:621 `varying = angular_shift != 0.0`), so there are two sites. That one is a representation choice (exact arc against subdivided curve) and is geometrically continuous. The phase is well defined at zero amplitude too (0°), so nothing undefined was being guarded.
verdict.evidence: notes/verify-wasm-boundary-3/c.mjs, default gear with mate {teeth:43, x=0}. angular_shift=0 → {"unavailable":{"key":"ui.gear_concentric_has_no_profile"}}. angular_shift=1e-300 → commanded all 26.000000000000004, sinusoid {mean 26.000000000000004, amplitude 0, phase 0}, sinusoid_backlash [0,0]. lib.rs:939 `if params.angular_shift == 0.0 { return Maybe::Unavailable{...} }`. Test lib.rs:2155-2160 pins the refusal. The panel shows the section only in the eccentric tab (GearPanel.svelte:693, 757).
verdict.proposal_note: Returning the flat profile at zero is the simpler fix: delete the branch and the string key in all five catalogues, and change the wasm test at lib.rs:2155 to assert amplitude 0 and range[0]==range[1]. One caution: GearPanel.svelte:183 (sizeByThrow) seeds eccentricThrow from defaults().gear.eccentric_throw when centre_profile is unavailable. Without the refusal, turning 'size by throw' on at zero shift would seed a throw of 0 instead. That is arguably right (no jump), but check that amplitude_for_throw(0) returns 0 and that the toggle stays useful. Moving the same refusal into the core, the proposal's other option, keeps the discontinuity and only relocates it.

title: points_per_tooth is an unbounded usize from JavaScript
claim: -1 from JavaScript becomes 4294967295 and traps on allocation; 2^31 traps after 2.7 s. The panel passes 600, so this is reachable only by a caller other than the panel.
evidence: run.log: gear_profile with n=-1 traps in 0 ms; with n=2147483648 it traps in 2664 ms.
proposal: Take u16, or clamp in Gear::profile and Ring::profile.
validation: Probe step with n=-1 returns an error.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. wasm-bindgen converts a JS -1 to usize 4294967295, and gear_profile and ring_profile trap with RuntimeError 'unreachable' (capacity overflow or allocation failure) instead of returning a JsError. The only caller is core.ts, which passes the fixed 600 from GearPanel.svelte:253, so the panel cannot reach it. After a trap the module still works: solve_gear and gear_profile succeed afterwards. Large legal values are slow but do not trap: n=1e6 gives 18M floats in 0.7 s.
verdict.evidence: notes/verify-wasm-boundary-3/p.mjs and t.mjs. ring_profile n=-1, 4294967295 and 2^31 → RuntimeError unreachable in 0-2 ms. gear_profile n=-1 → RuntimeError unreachable. Afterwards solve_gear returns 2853 chars and gear_profile(…,600) returns 10604. gear_profile n=1e5 → 1,799,804 values / 84 ms; n=1e6 → 17,999,804 / 719 ms. n=0..3 give 308 values, because gear.rs:561 and ring.rs:828 floor per-tooth points at (n/2).max(8).
verdict.proposal_note: Taking u16 at the boundary is enough and costs nothing. A better fix is to drop the argument: the screen profile would be drawn to a chord tolerance, as the export outline is, or at a resolution the core picks. Then the core has one way to say how finely an outline is drawn, not a point count in one path and a chord tolerance in the other, and the literal 600 leaves core.ts's caller. If the count stays, clamp it in Gear::profile/Ring::profile beside the existing .max(8) floor, so a count that is too large cannot be passed either.

title: The load-sharing note quotes '-24% to +15%'; sweeping the band gives +33 % to -74 %, and the rating jumps a third at ε = 2
claim: mesh.load_sharing_out_of_band tells the user the extrapolated result 'can vary from -24% to +15%', and state.md says the same. Those figures are the extremes of four hand-picked cases, not of the band. Across equal spur pairs they are exceeded several-fold. Separately, the shared rating is discontinuous at the band edge: bending stress falls by a third as ε crosses 2.
evidence: Probe bins sharing/sharing2/edge (probes/gear-io) use the exact rating closure of tests/notes.rs. The four test cases give +0.2357, +0.1563, +0.1169 and -0.1517, which is where 24/15 come from. The sweep z=20..150 step 5, h_a=1.0..1.5 step 0.025 changed 403 figures, all at ε>=2 (0 in-band changes, so the band edge is right). Largest relief +33.3 % at z=20, h_a=1.375, ε=2.006; largest increase -73.6 % at z=150, h_a=1.5, ε=2.759. Fine step at z=20: h_a 1.3700, ε=1.99979, σ_F 49.978 MPa both ways; h_a 1.3710, ε=2.00099, unshared 49.964 against shared 33.309 (-33.3 %) in one step. tests/notes.rs never reads the catalogue text, so the message can drift freely; it asserts the four-case extremes fall in (0.15,0.35) and (-0.30,-0.05), a bound that records where its sample stopped. Its module doc still names the retired key `stage.load_sharing_out_of_band`. The de/pt/zh messages carry an older, different wording ('measured between a 24 % relief and a 15 % increase').
proposal: The core rates the member both ways already, so drop the fixed band figure. Have the note carry this mesh's own change, e.g. `.number("change", 100*(shared/unshared-1), 1)`, rendered as 'load sharing at a virtual contact ratio of {ratio} is out of band: it changes this figure by {change} % against the unshared rating'. Update all five catalogues. Delete the four-case magnitude assertion in tests/notes.rs, or replace it with a law: the note's {change} equals 1 - shared/unshared for every mesh that raises it. Correct state.md's 'from a 24 % relief to a 15 % increase' to the swept range, or remove it. Report the ε=2 jump to the contact/strength owners. The ramp should reach the unshared value continuously at ε→2⁺ (the share at the single-pair boundary must tend to 1), or the jump must be documented in state.md with its size (−33 % at z=20).
validation: Law test: for a sweep over z and h_a, the note is raised if and only if ε≥2, and its {change} equals 1−shared/unshared exactly. Continuity law: |σ_shared(ε=2+δ) − σ_unshared(ε=2−δ)| → 0 as δ→0. check_figures (or an extension of it) confirms no catalogue message states a fixed percentage.

verdict.reason: The main claim holds. The quoted '-24% to +15%' is the extreme of the four cases in tests/notes.rs, and a sweep of the band far exceeds it. Two parts of the finding do not hold as written. (1) The proposal says the core 'rates the member both ways already'. It does not: Bending::of (train/mod.rs:741-757) calls bending_section_shared once, with the model the designer chose. A per-mesh {change} needs a second sweep with LoadSharing::None when the note fires. That is cheap, but it is new work. (2) The step at ε=2 is real, but it is not 'a boundary the physics does not have'. For rigid teeth the single-pair zone really does vanish at ε=2. Just below 2, the swept maximum is full load at the vanishing plateau. Just above, no point carries more than RAMP_MAX=2/3, so the figure falls by exactly 1/3 by construction. A stiffness-based share without load-induced contact extension shows the same jump. Forcing the share to tend to 1 as ε→2⁺ would invent behaviour. The right fix is to state the jump and its size (exactly 1/3 of the figure, from RAMP_MAX). docs do not state it today: state.md:524 and reference.md only say that below the band nothing changes.
verdict.evidence: My copy of the auditor's probe (probes/verify-gear-io-1, bin sharing) gave the same four test cases: +0.2357, +0.1563, +0.1169, -0.1517. The sweep z=20..150, h_a=1.0..1.5 gave '403 cases where sharing changes the figure; relief max +0.3332, increase max -0.7361' (z=150, h_a=1.5). The edge probe at z=20: h_a 1.3700, ε=1.99979, 49.9784 both ways; h_a 1.3705, ε=2.00039, unshared 49.9710, shared 33.3139 (d=+0.3333). contact.rs:869-870 has RAMP_MAX=2/3, and load_share at d=1 with ε→2⁺ gives t→1, so share→2/3. The stale figure appears in more places than the finding lists: strings_en.toml:137; de/pt/zh-Hans/zh-Hant (same 24/15, longer wording, not an older figure); train/mod.rs:719-720, Bending::note's doc ('from a 24 % relief to a 15 % *increase*'); state.md:730-732; reference.md:2847-2848 ('up to a quarter in either direction'); state.md:1019-1021 ('re-measured at 12–24 %'). tests/notes.rs:4 names the retired key `stage.load_sharing_out_of_band`. The test never reads the catalogue, and its bounds (0.15..0.35, -0.30..-0.05) only cover the four sampled cases.
verdict.corrected_claim: Every place that quotes the out-of-band effect as '-24 %..+15 %' or 'up to a quarter' is wrong. That is five catalogues, the Bending::note doc, state.md at two places and reference.md. A sweep of equal spur pairs reaches a 33 % relief (by construction, just above ε=2) and a 74 % increase (z=150, h_a=1.5). The rating steps by exactly 1/3 at ε=2, which is inherent to the ramp once the single-pair zone vanishes. That step is not documented.
verdict.proposal_note: Either drop the fixed figures everywhere or replace them with this mesh's own change. The per-mesh change needs a second bending_section_shared(…, LoadSharing::None) call inside Bending::of when out_of_band. Nothing computes it today. Do not change the ramp to force continuity at ε=2. Document the jump in state.md: at ε→2⁺ the maximum share drops from 1 to RAMP_MAX, so the figure falls by 1 − RAMP_MAX = 1/3. Replace the four-case magnitude test with a law on the note's {change}. Also fix the stale key name in the notes.rs module doc.

title: One root arc per tooth in every rack-cut gear and ring DXF is not the root circle: its bulge ends at the first fillet sample, not the junction
claim: On the leading side of each tooth the root vertex is pushed with bulge_for(half_pitch − θ0). But `subdivide` pushes only each chord's far end, never t=0, so the next vertex is the first fillet sample rather than the fillet junction. The 'exact' root arc is laid over the wrong endpoints, making an arc of the wrong radius about a point off the axis. The trailing side is correct, because the fillet walk ends at the junction. So the dxf.rs claim that the root arcs 'remain exact circular arcs' is false for half of them, and the junction point is never written.
evidence: ezdxf bulge_to_arc on `gear-cli dxf 17 0.2 0.001` gives 17 arcs, one per tooth, running from r=7.45000 to r=7.45194 with arc radius 12.6833 and centre 5.2361 mm off the origin. The other 34 are concentric. Helical z=17: R=12.95. Ring z=60 (probe gear-io-dxf): R=45.17, centre 13.94 off. Distance from the true junction (rf, θ0) to the drawn arc (rootdev.py): 1.076e-3 mm (gear) and 1.570e-3 mm (ring) at tolerance 1e-3, both over it. It is 7.39e-3 at tolerance 0.01 and 2.67e-2 at tolerance 0.1, both inside. outline.rs's `only_the_tip_and_root_arcs_carry_a_bulge` checks the radius of the bulged vertex, not of the vertex the arc ends at, so it cannot see this.
proposal: In Tooth::emit_root (side<0, concentric branch) and in Ring::outline step 1, push the junction vertex `pt(rf, −θ0)` (Ring: `pt(self.rf, −theta_root)`) as a line vertex right after the bulged root vertex, so the fillet subdivision starts from it. Equivalently, change `subdivide`'s contract to take the start point explicitly. Adjust the whole-number-of-teeth vertex-count expectations.
validation: Replace the bulge test with the law that matters: for every bulged segment (v_i, v_{i+1}), the arc centre from (v_i, v_{i+1}, b_i) lies on the axis within 1e-9, and both endpoints are at r_f or r_a within 1e-9. Run it on external, helical, ring and severed gears. The same check in validate_dxf.py (next finding) proves the file.

verdict.reason: The code reads exactly as described. Tooth::emit_root's concentric side<0 branch pushes (rf, −half_pitch) with bulge_for(half_pitch − θ0). The next call, subdivide(&f_minus, 1.0, 0.0, …), pushes only interior points and the t=0 end. It never pushes t=1, which is the fillet's root end (rf, −θ0). So the bulge is laid between the space centre and the first fillet sample. The severed branch explicitly pushes pt(rf, −θ0), and the displaced branch's subdivide ends at the junction, so both are right. Ring::outline step 1 has the same defect: its f_minus subdivide runs 0→1 from s_root and never emits t=0, and when there is no fillet the flank subdivide also starts past u_j. The trailing side ends at the junction and is correct.
verdict.evidence: I exported `gear-cli dxf 17 0.2 0.001` and read it back with ezdxf bulge_to_arc. GEAR_PROFILE has 1122 vertices: 34 concentric arcs and 17 off-axis ones. Example: endpoints r=7.450000 and 7.451937, arc radius 12.6833, centre 5.2361 mm from the origin. The cause is at outline.rs:129-137 (bulge pushed), 214-219 (subdivide 1→0 omits t=1) and 289-307 (ring). The test only_the_tip_and_root_arcs_carry_a_bulge (outline.rs:659-672) checks only the radius of the bulged vertex, so it cannot see this. dxf.rs:27-30 claims the root arcs 'remain exact circular arcs'.
verdict.proposal_note: Follow the severed branch's pattern: push Vertex::line(pt(rf, −θ0)) after the bulged vertex, and in the ring push pt(rf, −theta_root). This adds one vertex per tooth, so update the vertex-count expectations and golden outputs. Replace the bulge test with the arc-centre-on-axis law.

title: The CI DXF check cannot catch a wrong bulge, contrary to its own comment, and never sees a ring or an eccentric gear
claim: The comment on the radius checks says they are 'the part that would catch a wrong bulge'. They cannot catch a single sign-flipped arc: a flipped root arc bows outward and a flipped tip arc inward, both stay inside [root, tip], and the endpoints still reach both circles. The area and periodicity checks are also too loose to see it. CI runs the check on one external spur gear only, so ring_to_dxf, which ships through gear-wasm export_ring_dxf, and eccentric gears are never read back by an independent parser.
evidence: flip.py negated one bulge (the first root half-arc, 0.001893) in g17.dxf: validate_dxf.py reports 'all checks passed'. Negating all 51 arcs fails only because the minimum radius comes out 7.449893 against 7.45000, a 0.1 µm margin. The 12.68 mm off-axis root arcs of the previous finding pass the script too. gear-cli has no ring DXF command (gear-cli help), and ci.yml:114 exports only `dxf 17 0.2 0.001`.
proposal: In validate_dxf.py, for every bulged segment compute the arc with ezdxf.math.bulge_to_arc and require its centre within 1e-9 of the origin and its radius equal to --root or --tip within 1e-9. Add a 'the outline passes through the fillet junction' check only if the CLI can print that point. Add a `gear-cli dxf-ring [z] [cutter z] [tol]` subcommand (a COMMANDS row) and a second CI invocation with a ring (root > tip, clockwise bore, rim circle present). Fix the comment.
validation: Gate-the-gate: run the new script on g17_flipone.dxf and on the current (pre-fix) g17.dxf; both must fail. Run it on the fixed export; it must pass.

verdict.reason: The gap is real, but it is narrower than the finding says. validate_dxf.py passes an outline whose root arcs are centred 5 mm off-axis (finding 1), and CI never reads back a ring or an eccentric gear. The comment 'This is the part that would catch a wrong bulge' is overstated. But the claim that the script 'cannot catch a single sign-flipped arc' is false in two of the three positions per tooth. A flipped tip arc fails the periodicity check, and a flipped trailing root half-arc fails the min-radius check. Only the leading root half-arc, the one finding 1 already makes wrong, evades. The finding also misreads the margin. The flipped root arc dips 1.07e-4 mm = 107 nm below the root circle, against TOL = 1e-6 mm (validate_dxf.py:37), so the margin is 100x, not '0.1 µm'. The periodicity catch is thin, though: 8.8 µm against a 5 µm threshold.
verdict.evidence: On my own g17.dxf, the unmodified file prints 'all checks passed'. Flipping bulge #0 (the leading root half, -0.00189) also passes. Flipping #1 (the tip, index 32) gives 'FAIL outline is periodic in one tooth pitch (worst 8.80e-03 mm)'. Flipping #2 (the trailing root, index 65) gives 'FAIL every point within [root, tip]: 7.449893..9.700000' and 'FAIL root arc reaches the root circle exactly'. ci.yml:113-116 runs only `dxf 17 0.2 0.001`. gear-cli has one dxf COMMANDS row (main.rs:503-507) and no ring export. ring_to_dxf ships through gear-wasm export_ring_dxf (lib.rs:614, 1024).
verdict.corrected_claim: validate_dxf.py cannot see an arc whose endpoints lie between the root and tip but whose centre is off the axis. It passes today's 17 off-axis root arcs, and a sign flip of those same arcs. Flipped tip arcs and flipped trailing root arcs are caught, the tip only narrowly by periodicity. The script's comment overstates what it checks. CI reads back only one external spur gear, never a ring or an eccentric gear.
verdict.proposal_note: The centre-and-radius law per bulged segment is the right check, and it subsumes the flip cases. For the ring, a `gear-cli dxf-ring` COMMANDS row also adds a golden output, which is fine. For eccentric gears the circle check would need the displaced envelopes (finding 3) first.

title: An eccentric gear's DXF draws its tip and root reference circles on the axis, although the outline is displaced by e
claim: gear_to_dxf draws circles of radius tooth.ra and tooth.rf centred on the origin whatever the angular shift. Per params.rs and the panel's own string (gear_tip_root_envelopes_pitch_base_circles), an eccentric gear's tip and root envelopes are displaced by e = m·angular_shift (strictly a limaçon), while only the pitch and base circles stay on the axis. The exported construction layer therefore shows teeth running through the tip circle, and a blank turned to it would be too small.
evidence: Probe gear-io-dxf, z=30, m=1, angular_shift=0.3: outline vertex radius 13.4515..16.3000 mm and vertex centroid (−0.166, 0). The DXF circles are 13.75, 14.0954, 15.0 and 16.0, all at (0,0,0) (audit.py on ecc30.dxf). The teeth cross the drawn tip circle by 0.30 mm, and the blank diameter is 0.6 mm short.
proposal: Draw the pitch and base circles at the origin as now. For the tip and root, emit the envelope the gear actually has: either a CIRCLE at centre (e, 0) of radius ra and rf (the displaced-circle approximation, with its e²/2ρ departure stated), or an LWPOLYLINE of the limaçon r(θ) = ra + e·cos θ. Pass the circles to outline_to_dxf as (centre, radius) rather than bare radii so the writer stays kind-agnostic. At e=0 it collapses to today's output bit for bit.
validation: Law: for every export, max over outline vertices of |v| equals the maximum of the drawn tip envelope within the chord tolerance, and the same for the root minimum. Run over angular_shift ∈ {0, 0.1, 0.3} and assert the e=0 file is byte-identical to today's.

verdict.reason: gear_to_dxf passes &[gear.r, gear.rb, gear.ra, gear.rf] as bare radii, and outline_to_dxf draws each as a circle at the origin. The outline itself comes from Gear::new(params) and is displaced by e = m·angular_shift, toward +x, where x(θ) peaks at θ=0. params.rs:45-48 and the panel string say the tip and root envelopes are displaced and the pitch and base circles are not. The construction layer therefore contradicts the gear's own documentation. It is on by default (REFERENCE_CIRCLES_BY_DEFAULT) in export_dxf_impl.
verdict.evidence: Probe bin ecc (probes/verify-gear-io-1), z=30, m=1. At shift 0: outline r 13.7500..16.0000; circles at (0,0) with r 15, 14.0954, 16, 13.75. At shift 0.3: outline r 13.4515..16.3000, and the same four circles, all at (0,0). The teeth cross the drawn tip circle by 0.30 mm. Code: dxf.rs:119-129.
verdict.proposal_note: Pass (centre, radius) pairs to outline_to_dxf. The limaçon polyline is exact, and the displaced circle departs by only e²/2ρ (about 3 µm here), which the UI already states. Either is acceptable if the departure is stated. At e=0 the output must stay byte-identical, which the golden `dxf 17 0.2 0.001` checks.

title: The train reader accepts NaN in every float field, and a NaN input is then misreported by the solve
claim: from_toml deserialises with no finiteness check, so `nan` or `inf` (legal TOML) passes in all 29 float fields. The solve then answers as if something else were wrong: a NaN axis distance is refused as 'below the base-circle limit', and a NaN or inf torque solves with σ_F = 0 and the note 'nothing drives this case'. Rule 5 says refuse input that describes no shape. A NaN describes no shape, and the refusal should name the field.
evidence: Probe probe_gear_io: '29 of 29 float fields accept nan' (list includes distance/manual, module/manual, face_width/manual, addendum, sliding_friction, tolerance_plus, …). 'NaN distance: imported (adjusted=false), solve -> Err("part 1: the axis distance is below the base-circle limit")'. Probe bin presets: 'torque NaN: solve OK, stress Some(0.0) … notes ["train.case_nothing_drives"]', and the same for inf.
proposal: After parsing and before relief in from_toml and convert, walk the document (a `fn non_finite(&Train) -> Option<path>`, or serde `deserialize_with = finite` on an `f64` newtype used by Auto<f64> and the plain fields). Refuse with a new TrainError::NotFinite { field }, crossing as a catalogue key (e.g. error.document_value_not_finite {field}).
validation: Law test: for every float path in the every-preset document (the probe's traversal), replacing it with NaN, inf or -inf gives a refusal that names that path. Every finite value still round-trips bit-exact.

verdict.reason: from_toml does no finiteness check, and TOML's nan/inf literals deserialize into every f64 field. The solve then gives a misleading reason: a NaN distance is refused as 'below the base-circle limit', and a NaN or inf torque is treated as 'nothing drives'. This goes against rule 5's 'refuse input that describes no shape' with a named cause. Severity is lower than claimed. TOML is the only route, since JSON across the wasm boundary cannot carry NaN, and it takes a hand edit writing nan or inf. Nothing crashes, and the answer is refused or zeroed, not a plausible wrong number.
verdict.evidence: Main probe: '29 of 29 float fields accept nan' (the full list includes distance/manual, module/manual, torque/manual, …) and '== NaN distance: imported (adjusted=false), solve -> Err("part 1: the axis distance is below the base-circle limit")'. Presets probe: 'torque NaN: [manual = nan] solve OK, stress Some(0.0) … notes ["train.case_nothing_drives"]', and the same for inf. Finite floats round-trip bit-exact (0 of 7 tricky floats differ). The module doc's 'What is not checked on import' section (train.rs:~288) does not mention finiteness.
verdict.proposal_note: A serde `deserialize_with` on the Auto<f64> and plain fields catches it at parse time with the TOML path in the error, and needs no separate traversal. Cross the refusal as a catalogue key, not as English, per rule 2 applied to the boundary. Keep the refusal in gear-io, since only TOML can produce the value.

title: The material reader accepts E <= 0, ν outside (-1, 0.5) and negative allowables; the solve then blames the teeth
claim: materials::from_toml checks only for an empty library and duplicate names. The sanity test (every_material_carries_physically_sane_values) runs on the shipped library only, so a hand-edited library, which the spec invites, is not checked at all. A zero or negative modulus, or ν = 1.2, imports, and the train solve then fails with 'the teeth never come into contact', which sends the user to the geometry.
evidence: Probe bin matlib: 'E = 0: accepted; solve Err part 1: the teeth never come into contact'. The same holds for E = −190000 and for ν = 1.2. Negative fatigue, NaN ultimate and density = −1 all import without complaint.
proposal: Move the sanity rules from the test into from_toml as refusals naming the material and field: density > 0, E > 0, −1 < ν < 0.5, allowables > 0, all finite (MaterialError::Implausible { material, field }). Keep the default-library test as a call to the same validator. Cross the refusal as a catalogue key rather than as English (see the next finding).
validation: Law: for each material and each numeric field of the default library, setting it to 0, −1, NaN or ν=0.6 is refused and names both. The shipped library still parses.

verdict.reason: The misattribution is confirmed. materials::from_toml checks only for an empty library and duplicate names. E=0, E<0 and ν=1.2 all import, and the solve then reports 'the teeth never come into contact', which points the user at the geometry. The sanity test covers only the shipped library. The proposal puts the check in the wrong place, though. A library also reaches the solve as JSON from the panel through gear-wasm, which has a material box and export_materials_impl(library_json). A check inside gear-io's TOML reader misses that path. The validator belongs to MaterialLibrary or Material in gear-core, called by the TOML reader, the wasm entry points and the default-library test.
verdict.evidence: Probe bin matlib: 'E = 0: accepted; solve Err part 1: the teeth never come into contact', and the same for E = -190000 and nu = 1.2. 'fatigue = -330', 'ultimate = nan' and 'density = -1' were all accepted. The solved member uses '4340 Hardened Steel', so the fatigue and ultimate edits (made to other entries) did not reach it. That shows acceptance, not their effect on the answer. materials.rs:50-62 is the whole of the validation.
verdict.corrected_claim: No path that brings a material library in, whether the TOML reader or JSON over wasm, checks the physical values. An implausible modulus or Poisson ratio is misreported by the solve as a contact-geometry failure.
verdict.proposal_note: Put `MaterialLibrary::check() -> Result<(), Implausible{material, field}>` in gear-core/material.rs and call it from gear-io from_toml, from the gear-wasm entry points that take a library, and from the default-library test. Its refusal crosses as a catalogue key. Do not duplicate the rules in the test.

title: gear-io's own error messages (library and train import) reach the panel in English in all five languages
claim: MaterialError and gear-io's TrainError implement Display with English sentences ('material library contains no materials', '...two materials named {n}', 'geartrain file is not valid: …'). gear-wasm passes e.to_string() across, and the panel shows it as importError/error verbatim. A German or Chinese user importing a bad file gets English. (The train-mod-a audit reported the same for gear-core's TrainError; this is gear-io's own pair.)
evidence: wasm lib.rs:961 `gear_io::from_toml(toml_text).map_err(|e| e.to_string())`; lib.rs:972 does the same for trains. core.ts importLibrary/importTrain return `e.message`; state.svelte.ts:410-414 assigns it to `this.error`.
proposal: Give both error enums a `note(&self) -> Note` (keys error.library_empty, error.library_duplicate_name {name}, error.document_not_valid {detail}, error.library_implausible {material}{field}). Pass the Note across the boundary as the other refusals do, and render it through the catalogue. The toml crate's own parser message can ride in {detail}, since it is the parser's text rather than ours.
validation: gear_io::strings' fire-every-note sweep gains cases that fire each new key. A panel check in any language shows no English prose on a failed import.

verdict.reason: The English is real, but the finding makes the two halves sound alike and they are not. Library import: MaterialError::Empty and DuplicateName are sentences we wrote, and the Sidebar shows them with no translated wrapper at all, so that half fully holds. Train import: gear-io's TrainError has only Parse and Serialise, both wrapping the toml/serde parser's own English. The panel already wraps it in a translated ui.train_import_failed. So the only English we wrote there is a redundant 'geartrain file is not valid:' prefix, which duplicates the translated 'Import failed:'. The proposal also names a key, error.library_implausible, for an error variant that does not exist.
verdict.corrected_claim: The material-library import shows gear-io's own English (MaterialError::Empty and DuplicateName, via e.to_string()) raw in Sidebar.svelte:120, with no catalogue key in any language. The train import is already wrapped by the translated ui.train_import_failed. There the only English of our own is the 'geartrain file is not valid: ' prefix, which repeats the wrapper. The rest is the toml/serde parser's text, which no catalogue can translate.
verdict.evidence: Probe probes/verify-gear-io-2 printed 'material library contains no materials' and 'geartrain file is not valid: TOML parse error at line 1, column 8 ... invalid type: integer `1`, expected a string'. gear-wasm lib.rs:960-972 uses map_err(|e| e.to_string()). Sidebar.svelte:119-120 renders {library.error} bare. TrainPanel.svelte:1987 renders t("ui.train_import_failed", { reason: trains.importError }). materials.rs:20-29 has 4 variants and no Implausible. train.rs:305-311 has only Parse and Serialise. The same fault for gear-core's TrainError was closed in corrections.md:525; this pair was not.
verdict.proposal_note: Give MaterialError a note() with keys for Empty {} and DuplicateName {name}, plus a detail-carrying key for Parse. Wrap library errors in a translated 'library import failed: {reason}' as the train side already is. For TrainError, drop the English prefix and pass the parser detail as {reason}. Leave out library_implausible: no such variant exists.

title: An unknown key at the train document's root is silently dropped; the module doc says every struct refuses one
claim: TrainDocument derives Deserialize without #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], so `zz_unknown = 1` or a stale top-level field loads silently. The module doc states 'Every struct the document is made of says deny_unknown_fields now'. The refusal test covers [train.shape], a member and [train], but not the root.
evidence: Probe probe_gear_io inserted an unknown key at each table path of the every-preset document. Every path is refused except the root ('true <root>').
proposal: Add #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] to TrainDocument. Extend a_field_the_shape_no_longer_has_is_refused_and_named with a root-level case. Better still, make the test traverse every table of the serialised document, as the probe does, so a new struct cannot miss the attribute.
validation: The traversal test: an unknown key inserted at every table path is a parse error that names it.

verdict.reason: TrainDocument derives Deserialize without deny_unknown_fields, so an unknown key at the document root is accepted silently. The same key under [train] is refused. The module doc (train.rs:265) says every struct of the document refuses one. The practical risk is small: the root has only two fields, and 'name' is required, so a misspelt name is still refused as a missing field. What is silently dropped is only an extra root key.
