verdict.evidence: train.rs:297-302 shows `#[derive(Clone, Debug, Serialize, Deserialize)] pub struct TrainDocument` with no serde attribute. My probe (probes/verify-gear-io-2) printed 'root unknown accepted: true' and '[train] unknown accepted: false'. The test a_field_the_shape_no_longer_has_is_refused_and_named (train.rs:664) injects only under [train.shape], a member and [train].
verdict.proposal_note: The one-line attribute plus a root case in the test is enough. The table-traversal test is a good addition because it stops a new struct from missing the attribute.

title: Defaulted fields read old files through live constants, so changing a default silently re-means every older file; the doc says refusal is the rule
claim: The heading says a file written before a shape change 'will be refused … a document read with a field quietly defaulted is a document that describes a different gearbox'. Yet 16 fields default when absent (held, role, reversed_bending, carried_by, min_planet_clearance, couplings, tip_clearance, material_overrides, no_sharp_tip, no_undercut, pressure_angle, ring, load_sharing, min_contact_ratio, overlap, search). Each is justified as 'what every older file meant', but that meaning is supplied by default_planet_clearance() = 0.3, DEFAULT_MIN_CONTACT_RATIO = 1.2 and GearParams::default().pressure_angle = 20. Change any of those and every older file changes meaning silently, and no test pins it. There is no format version to tell the reader which meaning a file was written under. The doc also still says 'Two changes so far:' above 24 entries.
evidence: Probe probe_gear_io, 'omitted key still accepted (defaulted)': the 16 paths listed. The writer always writes every field (text_equal on every preset), so only hand-written or older files hit the defaults.
proposal: Add `format = N` at the document root, written on every export. The reader accepts absent fields only for format < N, filling them from constants frozen in gear-io (e.g. `const V_ABSENT_MIN_CONTACT_RATIO: f64 = 1.2`), not from gear-core's live defaults. At the current format every field is required, which is what the writer already produces. Move the 24-entry migration narrative out of the module doc into docs/ as a table of format → change, and fix 'Two changes so far'.
validation: Test: a golden file per older format in tests/data reads to the same solved figures after any change to gear-core's defaults (perturb DEFAULT_MIN_CONTACT_RATIO in a worktree and watch the old-file test stay green while a current-format file without the field is refused).

verdict.reason: The doc contradictions hold. The heading says a changed file 'will be refused'. It says 'Two changes so far' above 25 entries. It says 'No compatibility shim, deliberately', yet 16 fields carry serde defaults, which is a shim, and some of them read live gear-core constants (DEFAULT_MIN_CONTACT_RATIO, default_planet_clearance()=0.3, GearParams::default().pressure_angle). The exposure is overstated, though. Every one of these defaults was added before 'The train is one graph', which is the last migration entry, and a staged file is refused unless it goes through `gear-cli convert`. The writer also writes every defaulted field. So no file this tool wrote as a graph ever reaches a default. Only hand-written omissions and the one-shot `convert` of stage-era files (Staged deserialises Vec<Shape>, so Shape's defaults apply there) read through live constants. A format-version scheme is out of proportion to that exposure.
verdict.corrected_claim: Two problems. First, train.rs's module doc contradicts itself: it says refused, 'Two changes so far' over 25 entries, and 'no compatibility shim' beside 16 serde defaults. Second, three of those defaults (min_contact_ratio, min_planet_clearance, pressure_angle) read live gear-core constants, not values frozen to the file format. Changing those constants would silently change what `convert` makes of a stage-era file, and what a hand-written graph file that omits them means. Tool-written graph files are not affected: they carry every field.
verdict.evidence: My probe: min_contact_ratio, min_planet_clearance, load_sharing and search are each written 3 times in a 2-preset document, and pressure_angle and overlap are written as [train.shape.members.pressure_angle] tables. With every min_contact_ratio line deleted, the file loads with 1.2. shape.rs:84-99 and 206-240 show the defaults tied to live values (default_min_contact_ratio returns super::DEFAULT_MIN_CONTACT_RATIO; default_pressure_angle uses GearParams::default()). train.rs:23-27 says 'will be refused … Two changes so far'. train.rs:176-179 says 'No compatibility shim, deliberately'. train.rs:241-253 makes the graph entry last, with staged files refused unless converted.
verdict.proposal_note: Cheaper and closer to the owner's goals than `format = N`. Make the graph format require every field, as the writer already produces. Move the defaults onto the stage-era reader only (a Staged-specific shape, or fill-ins in convert) and write them as literals frozen in gear-io with a comment. Then gear-core's constants can move without re-meaning anything. Separately, rewrite the module doc's heading and 'Two changes so far', and move the 25-entry migration narrative to docs/ as a table.

title: zh-Hant catalogue contains five Simplified characters
claim: Traditional text carries 际 (should be 際) in part.planets_share_load_equally and ui.gear_what_teeth_reach_short_2e_odd, 属 (屬) in error.screw_axes_are_parallel, 点 (點) in ui.gear_flank_fillet_junction, and 机 (機) in ui.gear_zero_backlash_at_each_tooth.
evidence: zh_cc.py (OpenCC s2t over every zh-Hant value) flags those five plus 布/面/合. 分布, 面 and 合 are correct Traditional usage, so those three are OpenCC false positives. zh-Hans has no Traditional characters.
proposal: Replace the five characters. Add a check (tools/check_strings.py or the Rust test) that runs a small list of Simplified-only characters, or OpenCC with an allowlist, over zh-Hant.
validation: The new check fails on the current file and passes after the fix.

verdict.reason: All five occurrences are present: 际 twice, 属, 点 and 机, which in Traditional are 際, 屬, 點, 機. The catalogue already uses the Traditional forms elsewhere (際 and the others appear 7 times). A scan with my own list of Simplified-only characters found no other Simplified-only character. Nothing in check_strings.py or strings.rs checks the script.
verdict.evidence: grep over strings_zh-Hant.toml: line 43 '實际輪系', line 105 '属於直齒級', line 186 '交点', line 252 '實际達到', line 253 '机構'. grep -c '[際屬點機]' gives 7. tools/check_strings.py and crates/gear-io/src/strings.rs have no Hant/Simplified check.
verdict.proposal_note: A short deny-list of Simplified-only characters in the Rust strings test is enough and has no false positives. OpenCC with an allowlist adds a dependency and, as the auditor saw, misfires on 布/面/合.

title: Terminology for one concept varies within a language (contact ratio, ring, load, ground, port, profile shift, torque)
claim: The same term is translated inconsistently, so a reader cannot tell a label from its note. zh-Hant: contact ratio is 接觸比 on the panel, 重合度 in mesh.contact_ratio_below_one and 重疊比 for the minimum. Ring is 內齒輪 (10) and 內齒圈 (7), and gear_kind_internal reads the tautology '內齒輪（內齒輪）'. Load is 負荷 (14) and 載荷 (4). Ground: de uses 'Gestell' on the panel but 'Masse' (electrical earth) in error.train_load_port, zh uses 机架 on the panel but 地 (earth) in the error, and pt uses 'Terra' (electrical) in both. pt: ring is 'anular' in notes and 'coroa' in the add menu, and 'coroa' is also the worm wheel and the rim. Profile shift is 'correção' (12) and 'deslocamento' (3). Torque is 'Torque' (BR) on the panel and 'binário' (PT) in train.case_nothing_drives. Port is 'eixo' (which is also 'axis', 47 uses) and 'porta'. de port is 'Welle' and 'Anschluss'.
evidence: term counts: zh-Hans 内齿圈 17 / 内齿轮 1; zh-Hant 內齒圈 7 / 內齒輪 10; pt anular 10 / coroa 10, correção 12 / deslocamento 3; zh-Hant 負荷 14 / 載荷 4. keys.py dumps for ui.train_contact_ratio, ui.train_min_contact_ratio, mesh.contact_ratio_below_one, error.train_load_port, ui.train_ground and ui.gear_kind_internal.
proposal: Fix one term per concept per language: zh-Hant 接觸比 (or 重合度) everywhere, 內齒圈 for ring (gear_kind_internal → '內齒輪（內齒圈）'), 負荷 or 載荷 throughout; ground = Gestell / 機架 / estrutura fixa (not Masse / 地 / Terra); pt anular for ring, correção de perfil for shift, one of torque / binário. Add a glossary table at the head of each catalogue, and a check_strings step that greps each glossary entry's English term and requires the chosen translation in the same key.
validation: The glossary check passes. Re-run term.py and each concept yields one term per language.

verdict.reason: The recounts reproduce the substance, with small count differences. zh-Hant shows 接觸比 on the panel (8), 重合度 in the note (1) and 最小重疊比 for the minimum. It has 內齒輪 11 and 內齒圈 7, and gear_kind_internal reads '內齒輪（內齒輪）'. It has 負荷 17 and 載荷 5. For ground, de uses Gestell on the panel but Masse in train_load_port, zh uses 机架/機架 on the panel but 地 in the error, and pt uses Terra in both. pt uses coroa for the ring in the add menu (475-495), for the worm wheel (444) and for the rim (61), and anular 9 times. pt profile shift is correção 12 and deslocamento 3. pt torque is 'Torque' on the panel and binário in case_nothing_drives. de port is Welle 11 and Anschluss 1. The catalogue headers say the text is machine-translated and unreviewed, which explains these but does not excuse them.
verdict.evidence: grep over each catalogue for the keys train_contact_ratio, train_min_contact_ratio, contact_ratio_below_one, train_load_port, train_ground, gear_kind_internal, case_nothing_drives and train_torque, plus the term counts above.
verdict.proposal_note: A glossary check keyed on English terms appearing in the same key is fragile: English prose paraphrases, and 'ring' matches inside other words. A per-language list of forbidden variants is simpler and cannot misfire, for example zh-Hant 重疊比/重合度 and 內齒輪 except in gear_kind_internal; pt 'binário' and 'Terra'; de 'Masse'.

title: The pt catalogue mixes pre- and post-reform spelling although its header says it follows the Acordo Ortográfico
claim: The header says the translation uses 'a grafia do Acordo Ortográfico', yet pre-reform forms remain: 'contacto' ×6, 'rectos', 'recto', 'accionar', 'exacta'. The post-reform forms appear 33 times ('contato' ×13, 'reto' ×9, 'acionar' ×9, 'exata/exato' ×2). The panel shows 'Razão de contato' next to 'Razão de contacto mínima'. 'adelgaçamento' (thinning) for undercut is also doubtful; 'rebaixamento' or 'interferência de corte' is the usual gear term.
evidence: Word counts over strings_pt.toml with grep -oi; ui.train_contact_ratio against ui.train_min_contact_ratio.
proposal: Normalise to the AO forms (contato, reto, acionar, exato), and have a pt-speaking reviewer settle the undercut term. Add the pre-reform forms to a forbidden-word list in the catalogue check.
validation: The forbidden-word check passes; the two contact-ratio labels read identically.

verdict.reason: The mix is real. The panel shows 'Razão de contato' beside 'Razão de contacto mínima', and 'rectos', 'accionar' and 'exacta' are genuinely pre-AO. But 'contacto' is not a pre-reform form. The consonant is pronounced in European Portuguese, so AO90 keeps 'contacto' as the PT-PT spelling beside Brazil's 'contato'. The fault is PT-PT and PT-BR variants mixed, against the header's own promise to pick one form. The counts are also slightly off: 'recto' does not occur on its own, only 'rectos' once. I cannot settle whether 'adelgaçamento' is the right term for undercut with the means available.
verdict.corrected_claim: strings_pt.toml mixes European and Brazilian variants of one word: contacto ×6 (lines 69, 70, 395, 409) against contato ×13, and binário against Torque. The header (lines 18-19) promises one form wherever the norms diverge. It also keeps three genuinely pre-AO spellings: rectos (47), accionar (71) and exacta (119). The undercut term needs a native reviewer.
verdict.evidence: grep -n -o -w over strings_pt.toml: rectos:47, contacto:69,69,70,70,395,409, accionar:71, exacta:119. Line 344 is train_contact_ratio = "Razão de contato" and line 395 is train_min_contact_ratio = "Razão de contacto mínima". Header lines 18-19: 'com a grafia do Acordo Ortográfico; onde as normas europeia e brasileira divergem, foi escolhida a forma mais reconhecível em ambas'.
verdict.proposal_note: Pick one variant, PT-BR 'contato' being the majority form already, and add a forbidden-word list. Do not call 'contacto' pre-reform in the list's comment: it is the valid post-AO European form.

title: Engineering figures typed into message text duplicate code constants and doc figures that no check compares
claim: ui.train_note_min_contact_ratio says '1.2 is the typical design minimum', a copy of DEFAULT_MIN_CONTACT_RATIO = 1.2. ui.train_zn_worm_s_contact_stress_1 says '1–15 %', a copy of state.md/rationale.md's measurement. mesh.load_sharing_out_of_band carries '-24% to +15%' (shown wrong above). check_figures.py scans docs/*.md, *.html and README.md only, so none of these can be caught drifting, and rule 1 (the number shown is Rust's) is broken by prose.
evidence: check_figures.py:128-130 globs only docs/ and README. grep of digits in strings_en.toml.
proposal: Make each a placeholder the core fills: {default} from DEFAULT_MIN_CONTACT_RATIO, sent across in gear-wasm's defaults, and a {low}/{high} pair for the ZN/ZI band from a named constant, or better, the ZN figure computed for the worm on screen. Alternatively extend check_figures.py to the five catalogues so a figure there must be printed by the code.
validation: grep for digits in strings_*.toml values finds only unit symbols and standard names (ISO 6336-3, JGMA 116-02, BS 721).

verdict.reason: The duplication is real, but only the 1.2 is a code constant the prose copies. The two measured bands are copies of prose figures in the documents, and nothing checks or generates those either. Part of the proposal cannot be built: there is no ZN model to compute a figure from.
verdict.corrected_claim: ui.train_note_min_contact_ratio hard-codes '1.2', a copy of DEFAULT_MIN_CONTACT_RATIO (train/mod.rs:1855). It will drift silently if the default moves. The note is shown beside that very field (TrainPanel.svelte:682). The ZN '1–15 %' and the load-sharing '24 % / 15 %' figures are measurements that are also written as untagged prose in state.md:673/732, rationale.md:873, reference.md:1087 and the comment at train/mod.rs:720. check_figures.py only checks marked blocks, and none of these copies carries a marker. So the catalogues are no more exposed than the documents: the figures have no generator anywhere.
verdict.evidence: Output of grep: strings_en.toml:496 '1.2 is the typical design minimum', plus the same in de, pt and both zh files. mod.rs:1855 `pub const DEFAULT_MIN_CONTACT_RATIO: f64 = 1.2`. state.md lines 665-740 carry no figures marker near either band; the markers are at 186/199/200/847/860 only. The panel reads the note at TrainPanel.svelte:682 and the ZN note at :1225. In the English '-24% to +15%', the sign agrees with state.md's '24 % relief to 15 % increase'.
verdict.proposal_note: Pass the 1.2 through a {default} placeholder filled from gear-wasm's defaults. That is cheap and right. For the ZN band, 'computed for the worm on screen' is not possible: rationale.md:866-871 says the crate models only ZI, because the analytic curvature shortcut exists only for the developable flank. Extending check_figures.py to the catalogues does nothing on its own, because no command prints these figures. Either give the bands one named source, such as a tool script or a figures-by-test tag, or accept them as documented measurements. The note may also be conflating two things: '1.2 is the typical design minimum' is a claim about practice, while the default is a choice. If the text keeps the claim, it should say the default follows it rather than restate the number.

title: A script subtag loses to a region subtag in the language resolver: zh-Hans-HK resolves to Traditional
claim: Language::resolve marks a zh tag Traditional if any subtag is hant, tw, hk or mo. An explicit script, which BCP 47 says is decisive, does not override the region, so 'zh-Hans-HK' and 'zh-Hans-TW' (both real browser tags) get zh-Hant.
evidence: Code: `rest.iter().any(|p| matches!(*p, "hant" | "tw" | "hk" | "mo"))` with no check for 'hans'. The test table has no mixed script-and-region case.
proposal: Decide by the script subtag when present (hans → Simplified, hant → Traditional), and fall back to the region only when no script subtag is given.
validation: Add ('zh-Hans-HK','zh-Hans'), ('zh-Hans-TW','zh-Hans') and ('zh-Hant-CN','zh-Hant') to a_language_tag_resolves_to_the_catalogue_it_names.

verdict.reason: Holds as stated, and the code contradicts its own doc comment: strings.rs:58 says 'the script is what decides'. The resolver can be reached from the browser: core.ts:497 passes navigator.language to resolve_language (gear-wasm lib.rs:1244).
verdict.evidence: strings.rs:87-90: `rest.iter().any(|p| matches!(*p, "hant" | "tw" | "hk" | "mo"))`. For 'zh-hans-hk' the exact match fails, 'hk' is in rest, so it returns zh-Hant. The test table (strings.rs:370-396) has no case where the script and region disagree. 'zh-Hant-CN' already resolves correctly to Hant because 'hant' is present, so the only failing tags are zh-Hans-{TW,HK,MO}.
verdict.proposal_note: Implementation: `let script = rest.iter().find(|p| matches!(**p, "hans"|"hant"));` then `match script { Some(&"hant") => Hant, Some(_) => Hans, None => region rule }`. Add zh-Hans-HK, zh-Hans-TW and zh-Hant-CN to the test table.

title: The 4340 hardened steel's fatigue estimate keeps the figure its own note calls optimistic, without a size and sign in state.md
claim: fatigue_allowable = 750 MPa (0.5 × UTS) comes with a note saying 'Treat as optimistic … the true figure is plausibly nearer 700 MPa'. Rule 6 wants a known bias written with its size and sign. Here the direction (optimistic, about +7 %) is known and the default still takes the non-conservative end. Everything else in the file checks out arithmetically.
proposal: Either use the 700 MPa the note argues for, with basis 'estimated' and the reasoning kept, or keep 750 and record '+7 % (optimistic) on 4340 hardened fatigue' in state.md's bias list.
validation: The state.md bias list names every 'estimated' allowable whose note states a direction.

verdict.reason: The finding holds and understates the case. state.md:745 does list the entry ('Hardened 4340's fatigue allowable is the weakest number in the library'), but with no size or sign, which rule 6 requires. Worse, the classical rule the note cites (Shigley/Mischke) sets S_e' = 0.5·S_ut only for S_ut ≤ 1400 MPa and a flat 700 MPa above that. At this temper's S_ut of 1500 MPa, the rule gives exactly 700 MPa, not 'plausibly nearer 700'. The shipped 750 departs from the rule the note names, on the non-conservative side, by +7.1 %.
verdict.evidence: materials_default.toml:62: fatigue_allowable = 750, basis 'estimated', note '0.5 × UTS … Treat as optimistic … endurance ratio … falls away above roughly 1400 MPa UTS … nearer 700 MPa'. UTS = 1500 MPa per ultimate_allowable's note. 750/700 = 1.071. The annealed cross-check (0.5×690 = 345 against 330 published, 4.5 %) is correct. state.md:745 is one line with no figure.
verdict.proposal_note: Prefer the first option: 700 MPa, basis 'estimated', note 'Shigley's S_e' = 0.5 S_ut, capped at 700 MPa above S_ut = 1400 MPa'. That is the stated convention applied in full rather than a guess. Then state.md:745 can drop the entry or say the cap is the estimate. Keeping 750 would need '+7 % over the capped classical estimate' written into state.md, and nothing argues for 750 over the rule.

title: No check compares ui.* placeholders with what the panel passes
claim: every_placeholder_is_a_value_the_core_supplies skips ui.* keys, and check_strings.py checks only that each key exists and is used. A ui message whose {name} the .svelte call does not pass would render with a brace in it and pass CI.
evidence: uiph.py over web/src: 403 t("ui.…") call sites checked and all consistent today. The only flag, TrainPanel.svelte:1894, passes a typed {a,b} object. check_strings.py has no placeholder logic (grep).
proposal: Add the uiph.py comparison to check_strings.py: for each t("ui.k", {…}) literal, the object's keys must equal the message's placeholders. Typed pass-through objects need an allowlist or a TS type derived from the catalogue.
validation: Temporarily rename a placeholder in strings_en.toml; the check must fail.

verdict.reason: The gap is real. every_placeholder_is_a_value_the_core_supplies skips keys starting with 'ui.' (strings.rs:516). check_strings.py (81 lines) has no placeholder logic. Mismatches between translations and English are caught (strings.rs:354), but mismatches between the panel and English are not. I re-scanned independently and found every call site consistent today, so the finding is about a missing gate, not a live bug. A missing value leaves '{name}' visible (the test at strings.rs:458), so the failure would show on screen rather than crash.
verdict.evidence: My own scanner (notes/verify-gear-io-3/uiph.py) matched 401 t("ui.…") sites. The 19 it flagged are all false positives from property access inside the value expressions: `num(m?.backlash[e].nominal,5)`, `{ mate: gear }`, `{ name: role, number }`. Checked by reading TrainPanel.svelte:1161/1256/2096, offers.ts:48, members.ts:68 and GearPanel.svelte:227. So a regex check is fragile, as this shows.
verdict.proposal_note: Parse object literals properly rather than by regex. Capture the top-level keys of the literal: a key followed by ':' at brace depth 1, or a shorthand identifier. A naive key regex produces false positives, as my scan showed. The more robust alternative is the one the finding mentions: generate a TS type mapping each ui key to its placeholder names from the catalogue, and let npm run check enforce it. That also covers non-literal arguments.

title: Small inaccuracies in gear-io comments and test names
claim: (a) dxf.rs:93 says coordinates are written 'with enough digits to round-trip a double'. `{:.12}` fixed decimals is not a round trip: a 100 mm coordinate keeps 15 significant digits. Harmless at 1e-12 mm, but the claim is wrong; either say '1e-12 mm' or write `{value:?}`. (b) train.rs:27 says 'Two changes so far:' above 24 entries. (c) `the_sweep_fires_most_of_the_catalogue` asserts all notes fire (its own doc says 'all, not a fraction'); rename it every_note_fires_or_is_in_unfired. The UNFIRED doc is mostly the history of entries that left, which belongs in corrections.md. (d) error.screw_axes_are_parallel still says 'a worm stage', and de/pt/zh say more than the English ('a parallel pair is a spur stage'), so the translations are not of this message. (e) clamp.ring_flank_ungenerated supplies {tip} but the message never uses it; it could state the band 'flank from {tip} to {limit} mm'. Also observed_values accumulates names without deduplicating ('tip' ×49).
evidence: Read at the cited lines. A temporary test in the worktree listed supplied-but-unused values: only clamp.ring_flank_ungenerated: tip. drift.py: error.screw_axes_are_parallel changed in English after all four translations.
proposal: Apply the five wording fixes. Make observed_values collect into a BTreeSet. Add the supplied-but-unused check (every value a fired note carries appears in its English message, or is listed as deliberately unshown) beside the existing supplied-but-missing check.
validation: cargo nextest run -p gear-io; the new check passes after (e) is resolved.

verdict.reason: All five points hold on re-reading. They are wording fixes except the supplied-but-unused check. Each is checked in the evidence below.
verdict.evidence: (a) dxf.rs:93-97: the comment says 'enough digits to round-trip a double', but the code is format!("{value:.12}"). A 100 mm coordinate gets 15 significant digits; a round trip needs 17. (b) train.rs:27 says 'Two changes so far:'. grep counts 24 '//! - ' entries from line 29 to 241. (c) strings.rs:1575 is `fn the_sweep_fires_most_of_the_catalogue`, while its doc at 1566 says 'The sweep fires every key there is … Asserted as *all*'. The UNFIRED doc (1597-1640) spends about 30 of 44 lines on entries that left. The ring_addendum_clamped story is already told nearly word for word in docs/corrections.md:573, so it is said twice. (d) Commit 830ebf3 changed the English to 'a worm stage needs non-parallel shafts', but de/pt/zh still translate the old 'parallel axes: … a parallel pair is a spur stage'. 'Stage' is also stale vocabulary since the stages retired. (e) ring.rs:481-483 supplies .number("limit") and .number("tip"), while all five messages use only {limit}. observed_values extends a Vec per firing (strings.rs:589-591), so it repeats names.
verdict.proposal_note: For (d), stop saying 'stage': a mesh built on a distance at an angle is the model now, so write something like 'the shafts are parallel; a crossed or worm mesh needs non-parallel axes', and retranslate all four. For (c), move the history to corrections.md, which already has it, and keep only the live entry with its evidence. For (a), writing `{value:?}` gives the shortest string that round-trips. DXF readers accept it, but it can print exponent form for tiny values ('1e-7'). A DXF parser reads that, but check it with validate_dxf.py, or just correct the comment to 'to 1e-12 mm'.

title: Root arc on the minus side of every tooth (external and ring) is bulged to the wrong end point: not concentric, off by 1.1-3x the tolerance
claim: `emit_root(side=-1)` pushes the arc's start (rf, -half_pitch) carrying bulge tan((half_pitch-theta0)/4). The fillet is then walked by `subdivide`, which emits interior and end points but never the start. So the arc's end vertex (rf, -theta0) is never emitted. The bulge meant for a 0.0076 rad arc gets applied to a chord that ends at the first fillet vertex, 3.4x further round. Ring::outline has the same omission (fillet walked from t=0 without its start). The severed branch alone pushes the vertex explicitly (lines 181-184), which shows the intent. The module's 'tip and root arcs stay exact' is therefore false on half the root arcs of every exported gear.
evidence: Probe `junction` mode, z17 default: v0 = (r 7.250000, ang -0.184800, bulge 1.8928e-3), and the next vertex is (r 7.252185, ang -0.171233), a fillet point. trochoid_at(0) = (7.25, 0.177228) is never emitted on the minus side, while the plus side ends correctly at 0.177228. Ring z43: v0 at -0.073060, then 22.747919 at -0.068123, while space_starts_at = 0.069563. Deviation from the true curve (dense independent reference, arcs flattened with their true centre): z17 1.22x/1.26x/1.09x at tol 1e-2/1e-3/1e-4; z9 undercut 1.20-1.22x; z30 rr.1 2.71x at 1e-3; z30 rr.2 m3 2.98x; ring z43 1.44/1.53/1.20x; ring z90 1.59/1.70/1.36x. Worst arc-centre offset from the axis: 22 mm (z17), 48 mm (z43), 84 mm (ring z90). After inserting pt(rf, -theta0) (ring: pt(rf, -theta_root)) after each tooth's first vertex (probe `fixed` mode): every external and ring case lies within 0.60-1.06x of the tolerance, and arc centres sit at 1e-13..3e-10 mm from the axis.
proposal: In `emit_root` for the constant-root case with side < 0, push `Vertex::line(pt(rf, -theta0))` after the bulged start vertex, and delete the now-duplicate explicit push in the severed branch. In `Ring::outline` step 1, push `pt(rf, -theta_root)` after `start`. The better fix removes the bug class: see the unification finding (one walker over `sections()` where every section emits its own end point and an arc section is one bulged vertex).
validation: Tighten `the_outline_meets_the_tolerance_it_was_given` to `ratio <= 1.1` at every tolerance (measured max after the fix: 1.06). Replace its concentric-arc shortcut with true point-to-arc distance (see the test-gap finding). Add a law over all externals and rings: for every bulged span, both endpoints lie at the same radius as the gear circle it represents, and bulge == tan(Δangle/4). The current code fails that law on every tooth. Re-record the golden DXF outputs.

verdict.reason: Holds as stated. The code does what the finding says, and my own measurements agree with the auditor's numbers. I rate it medium rather than high: the absolute stray stays within a few times the tolerance asked for (worst 4.2x). But every exported gear breaks the module's single promise ('the tip and root arcs stay exact'; reference.md:143; state.md:575 'DXF with exact arcs'). On the minus side of every tooth it also leaves a tangent kink at mid-space where the true curve is smooth.
verdict.evidence: Code as read: outline.rs:130-141, `emit_root(side<0)` pushes (rf,-half_pitch) with bulge tan((half_pitch-theta0)/4). Step 2 then walks `subdivide(&f_minus, 1.0, 0.0, ..)`, which by its own doc (outline.rs:65-67) 'emits the interior and end point, not the start', so (rf,-theta0) is never emitted. Ring::outline has the same gap at outline.rs:289-304. Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-gear-outline, mode `junction`, z17 default at 1e-3: v0 is (r 7.250000, ang -0.184800, bulge 1.8928e-3) and v1 is (r 7.252185, ang -0.171233), a fillet point, while trochoid_at(0) = (7.25, 0.1772282). The v0->v1 arc has radius 12.9955 mm, its centre sits 5.75 mm off the axis, and its tangent at v0 is 0.0192 rad off the root circle's. The plus-side root arc v73->v74 is exact: centre 1.9e-14 mm off, radius 7.25. Ring z43: v1 at -0.068123 where the space starts at 0.069563, centre 9.39 mm off. Independent true deviation (arcs flattened on their true centres; dense 20000-point-per-section reference; notes/verify-gear-outline/dev.txt), as-is then fixed: z17 1.22/1.26/1.09x -> 0.78/0.94/1.00x; z9 x-0.2 1.24/1.24/1.13x -> 0.87/0.99/0.98x; z30 m3 at 1e-4 2.86x -> 1.00x; ring z43 1.44/1.53/1.20x -> 0.75/0.94/0.98x; ring z90 1.59/1.70/1.36x -> 0.98/0.82/0.96x. Worst centre offsets: z17 22.4 mm, z43 47.6 mm, ring z90 83.8 mm. On bulged spans alone (arcs.txt): up to 2.95x on z17 at 1e-5, 3.18x on z30 m3 x-0.3 at 1e-4, 4.16x on z12 m10 at 1e-6. The error scales with the tolerance and is never large in absolute terms. The shipped CI DXF (`gear-cli dxf 17 0.2 0.001`) read back with ezdxf: 17 of 51 bulged spans have centres 5.24 mm off the axis (arccheck.py).
verdict.proposal_note: I tested the proposal in a detached worktree (fix_and_tighten.diff). Changes: push `pt(rf,-theta0)` after the bulged start in emit_root's constant case, push `pt(rf,-theta_root)` in Ring::outline step 1, and delete the explicit push in the severed branch. With those, the whole workspace suite passes except the known wall-clock test, and the outline test's own metric falls to at most 0.9993x on all nine of its gears at every tolerance. Deleting the severed-branch push has a second benefit. With a varying root, emit_root(-1) already ends on that point, so the push duplicates a vertex today: z5 x-0.8 dx0.1 exports 10 zero-length segments, one per severed tooth on top of finding 8's one per mid-space. Goldens to re-record: dxf_17_0.2_0.001. meshsweep_60_20_0.8 and hulasweep_18_0.25 may also change, because gear-cli's roll_pair flattens both outlines at 1e-5; I did not verify this. The unified section walker is the durable cure, but the three-line fix stands alone.

title: The outline tolerance test was loosened to fit the root-arc bug, and its arc distance cannot see it
claim: `worst_deviation` measures any bulged span as `|r_p - r_a|`, with no angular extent and no real arc centre. So a wrongly bulged, non-concentric arc passes, and any reference point near rf matches some root arc anywhere on the gear at almost zero distance. The doc attributes the measured 2.5x to 'a curved flank's true worst deviation is larger than its midpoint sagitta … most so on an undercut tooth'. That diagnosis is wrong: the excess is the missing vertex. The thresholds (`r <= 3.0`, `ratio[2] <= 1.4`) record where that bug sat. `only_the_tip_and_root_arcs_carry_a_bulge` checks only the start vertex's radius. The ring test checks vertices only, and its closure check `gap < 2*pitch_arc` holds by construction.
evidence: With the vertex fixed, lines stay at 0.60-1.06x and arcs are exact (probe `fixed`). So nothing about undercut flanks needs 3x. The test's own table shows z9/z17 undercut at 2.51/2.70x at 1e-2, the same cases the probe traced to the root arc (worst on arcs 1.20-1.30x at r = rf + 0.02 mm). The ring test at outline.rs:411-421 compares vertices only, and every vertex of the bad arc does lie on the curve.
proposal: Compute the distance to a bulged span as the true distance to the arc it encodes: centre from chord and bulge, clamped to its angular extent. Tighten to 1.1x at every tolerance and drop the separate convergence threshold, which a correct scheme meets trivially. Extend `only_the_tip_and_root_arcs_carry_a_bulge` to assert both ends of every bulged span lie on the same gear circle and the bulge matches their angular separation. Give the ring the same `worst_deviation` law as the external gear, not the vertex-only check, and drop the vacuous gap assertion.
validation: Before the fix, the tightened test must fail on the current code (it does: 1.2-3.0x); after it, it must pass. Run it in a detached worktree as CLAUDE.md's rule 5 of testing asks.

verdict.reason: The substance holds, with two small corrections. First, the thresholds were not 'loosened': 3.0 and 1.4 were set when the test was written (commit 8c716c0, previous audit F69), just above values the defect produced. Second, the metric did register the defect, as the inflated 2.5x, because the fillet stretch the missing chord leaves uncovered gets matched to nothing close. Its bulge branch `|r_p - r_a|` cannot see a non-concentric arc and does not bound angular extent. The previous audit's F69 closure named the mechanism 'a re-entrant flank's worst deviation exceeds [the midpoint sagitta]' (docs/history/audit.md:1493-1497), and so does the test doc (outline.rs:529-531). That mechanism is refuted: the whole excess is the missing vertex.
verdict.evidence: I reproduced the test's own `worst_deviation` in the probe (mode `testmetric`, notes/verify-gear-outline/testmetric.txt). It matches the doc table exactly: z9 x-0.2 2.511/1.806/1.112, z17 x-0.2 2.699/1.840/0.994, z43 x0.4 0.628/0.927/0.986. z9 x0 at 1e-4 reads 1.331, which is what the 1.4 convergence bound accommodates. The excess is not about undercut: z43 x-0.2, not undercut, reads 1.23/1.33x. After the vertex fix, all 27 cells read at most 0.9993x. The worst points before the fix all sit on the minus side next to rf (e.g. r 3.0819 vs rf 3.05 at ang -0.2777). Rule-5 check in a worktree (tightened_on_unfixed.diff): tightening to 1.1 fails on current code ('z9 x-0.2: [2.51, 1.81, 1.11]') and passes with the fix. `only_the_tip_and_root_arcs_carry_a_bulge` (outline.rs:656-672) tests only the bulged vertex's own radius, which is rf on the bad span. The ring test (outline.rs:411-421) checks vertices, which lie on the curve by construction. Its `gap < 2*pitch_arc` holds whenever the last vertex is within two pitches of the first.
verdict.proposal_note: Replace the concentric shortcut with the true point-to-arc distance. That is right, and needed: with the vertex fixed, the current metric passes, but it would still pass a wrongly bulged arc. The 1.1 bound is itself a threshold read off a measurement, which CLAUDE.md's testing rule 3 discourages. Stronger: make the subdivision stop only when the chord is within tolerance at t = 1/4, 1/2 and 3/4. The test can then assert <= 1.0x at the points the scheme promises, with a stated margin for between-sample error, and it also covers the S-bends that finding 5 exposes. Also correct the F69 paragraph in docs/history/audit.md, or add a correction row, since its stated mechanism is wrong.

title: `a_rings_outline_refines_when_asked_to` measures an external gear, never the ring
claim: The test builds `Ring::cut_by(..)` and then measures `crate::gear::Gear::new(g.params).outline(..)`: an external gear with the same parameters. Ring::outline's refinement is never tested. Its tolerance floor also differs (relative to rf, not ra).
evidence: outline.rs:451-452: `let coarse = crate::gear::Gear::new(g.params).outline(1e-2).len(); let fine = crate::gear::Gear::new(g.params).outline(1e-5).len();` where `g` is the Ring.
proposal: Use `g.outline(1e-2)` and `g.outline(1e-5)`. Better still, fold it into a ring `worst_deviation` law at three tolerances.
validation: The corrected test calls Ring::outline, and a mutation of Ring::outline's tolerance (e.g. `tol * 4`) must turn it or the deviation law red.

verdict.reason: The unit test measures an external gear, not the ring. Two parts of the claim do not hold. 'Ring::outline's refinement is never tested' is false for the project's checks as a whole: the golden corpus (tools/check_golden.sh) catches a moderate mutation of the ring's tolerance, though no Rust test does. And the floor is not a different rule. A ring's rf is its outermost radius, as ra is an external gear's, so both floors are relative to the largest radius.
verdict.evidence: outline.rs:451-452 build `crate::gear::Gear::new(g.params)` from the Ring's params, so the test measures a z60 external gear. Worktree mutation: `4.0 * chord_tolerance...` and then `100.0 *` in Ring::outline. `cargo nextest run -p gear-core -p gear-io` stays green apart from the known timing test (644/645 at 100x). The corpus reacts, though: at 4x, `gear-cli meshsweep 60 20 0.8` changes 4 lines against tools/golden/meshsweep_60_20_0.8.txt and `hulasweep 18 0.25` changes 4 lines. At 100x, meshsweep flips to 'THE TEETH FOUL'. The path is gear-cli/src/main.rs:1000-1001, where roll_pair flattens ring.outline(1e-5). For a ring rf > ra (ring.rs `outline` floor `MIN_RELATIVE_TOLERANCE * self.rf` and the annulus check `r >= ra && r <= rf` at outline.rs:432), so the floor is the outermost radius either way.
verdict.proposal_note: Point the test at `g.outline(..)`. Better, fold it into a ring version of the true point-to-arc deviation law (finding 1), so the Rust suite and not only the corpus gates the ring's tolerance.

title: λ's 'unavoidable error' holds only at a fixed axis distance; at the commanded (zero-backlash) distance λ=0 is exactly conjugate both ways
claim: The docs say a gear with varying thickness 'cannot be exactly conjugate both ways', that λ scales the drive error by |1-λ| and the coast error by |1+λ|, that λ=0 is minimax, and that 'λ=1 is exactly conjugate forward'. That is true only for single-flank running at a fixed axis distance. The feature's own operating model is different: `CentreProfile.commanded`, `sinusoid_backlash`, `amplitude_for_throw` and the crank it sizes have the mate following the zero-backlash distance a_w(x_k). At that distance both flanks touch, and by symmetry the mate's phase is set by the tooth's seat alone. So λ=0 gives zero transmission error on both flanks, and any λ≠0 adds λ(ψ̄-ψ_k)·r_b to both. The `Variation.drive/coast_pitch_error` fields are valid inspection figures (flank-seat spacing), but their docs present them as the transmission error a reversing drive sees.
evidence: Independent check, notes/gear-outline/conjugacy.py: numerical contact closure of a z43 mate onto each flank of tooth k of a z24, Δx=0.25 gear, with no line-of-action formula. Output (conjugacy.out), TE range over teeth k=0..12 on the base circle. Fixed distance: λ=0 drive 171.0 / coast 171.0 µm; λ=0.5 85.5 / 256.5; λ=1 0.00 / 342.0, which reproduces the documented |1∓λ| law. Commanded distance a_w(x_k): λ=0 drive 0.00 / coast 0.00; λ=0.5 85.5 / 85.5; λ=1 171.0 / 171.0.
proposal: State the two operating modes explicitly in reference.md#angularly-varying-profile-shift and rationale.md. Fixed distance (single flank, backlash varying by 2Δa·tanα): the |1∓λ| trade-off. Following distance (double flank, the mode `centre_profile` and the crank serve): λ=0 exact both ways, λ harmful. Retitle the Variation pitch/index errors as inspection quantities (flank-seat spacing), not transmission errors, and remove 'λ=1 buys a one-way component' from their docs. If λ has no use in the following mode, consider withdrawing it as an input (rule: a toggle nothing needs goes), or report a TE figure per mode.
validation: A law in gear.rs tests: with a mate at `centre_profile(..).commanded[k]`, close the drawn outlines on each flank (the 'gated twice' outline-closing machinery already exists) and assert zero phase variation across k at λ=0, and a variation of λ·max|ψ̄-ψ_k|·r_b at λ≠0.

verdict.corrected_claim: The documented trade-off assumes a fixed axis distance, and the documents never say so. That covers drive error |1-λ| against coast |1+λ|, 'λ=0 is the minimax', and 'λ=1 is exactly conjugate forward'. The feature's own commanded-distance output (CentreProfile, the crank throw) assumes the mate follows a_w(x_k). In that mode, at each tooth's own commanded position, the mate's phase is the tooth's seat. So λ=0 gives zero per-position error on both flanks, and λ≠0 adds λ(ψ̄-ψ_k)·r_b to both. λ=1 is then not exactly conjugate forward: it carries a once-per-revolution error equal to λ=0's fixed-distance index error. λ=0 is not 'exactly conjugate both ways' in continuous meshing either. Within each tooth's contact the drive error is r_b[(1-λ)ψ_j - ψ(θ)], which at λ=0 leaves a tooth-frequency residual about one adjacent seat step in size (~22 µm p-p at z24, Δx 0.25, m1). With contact ratio above 1, no axis-distance schedule removes it, so the documents' 'cannot be exactly conjugate both ways' is true in general.
verdict.reason: Per position, the auditor's calculation is right: the numeric closure in notes/gear-outline/conjugacy.py agrees with my derivation. The headline overclaims, because the exactness holds only at the sampled instants. The consequence is real and user-facing: the λ field's note tells a user that λ=1 is exact forward. That is false in the mode for which the same panel reports a commanded profile and crank throw.
verdict.evidence: Derivation. For involutes of one base circle at axis distance a, a flank seated at base angle d_j meets its mate at phase r_b·d_j + C(a) on the drive side and r_b·c_j - C(a) on the coast side. C(a) is the backlash law's half-term: rationale.md's 'mesh-phase coefficient is exactly half the backlash'. Zero backlash at tooth k fixes C(a_k) = -r_b ψ_k + const. With d_k = 2πk/z + λψ̄ + (1-λ)ψ_k and c_k = 2πk/z + λψ̄ - (1+λ)ψ_k, both flank errors at a_k equal -λψ_k·r_b + const. That is zero spread at λ=0 and λ(ψ̄-ψ_k)r_b at λ≠0. It matches the auditor's numeric closure (conjugacy.out: commanded λ=0 0.00/0.00; λ=1 171.0/171.0 µm), and at fixed a it reproduces |1∓λ| (171/171, 85.5/256.5, 0/342). For continuous running with a(θ) tracking ψ(θ), the drive error on tooth j is r_b[(1-λ)ψ_j - ψ(θ)]. Across one pitch at quadrature that varies by r_b·(2tanα/z)·Δx·2sin(π/z) = 11.28·0.0303·0.25·0.261 ≈ 22 µm, so λ=0 is exact only at the samples. With overlapping contact intervals, zero error on both flanks for all θ forces C constant, so a fixed distance, so uniform thickness: the 'cannot be both ways' statement survives. Where the claim reaches the user: strings_en.toml:312 'cannot be conjugate both ways ... 1 is exact forward, twice the error in reverse'; gear.rs:32-44 and 666-678; reference.md:1667-1677; rationale.md:1088-1103.
verdict.proposal_note: Do not withdraw λ. At a fixed axis distance λ=1 is exactly conjugate forward in continuous meshing, which no λ achieves in the following mode, so the input has a real use. State both modes in reference.md, rationale.md and the UI note. At a fixed distance: the |1∓λ| trade-off. When the mate follows the commanded profile: λ=0 is best on both flanks and λ≠0 adds λ(ψ̄-ψ_k)r_b to both, with a tooth-frequency residual about one adjacent seat step in size whatever λ is. Phrase the proposed law per position (closure at commanded[k]). Do not assert continuous exactness.

title: `sinusoid_backlash` leaves out the kind's sign: negated for an internal mate
claim: The documented law is j_t = σ·2a′(inv α′ − inv α_w), with σ = −1 for internal because separating the centres of an internal pair closes it. `centre_profile_of` computes `j = 2.0 * fit * (inv(alpha_actual) - inv(alpha_ideal))` without σ, although `sigma` is in scope. For an eccentric pinion in a ring (reachable from the gear tab through `eccentric_mate`), every position's slack and interference are swapped. The panel's warn class (`p.sinusoid_backlash[0] < 0`) and range are read from the wrong end. The only test asserts the range straddles zero, which a negated range also does.
evidence: Probe `sigma` mode, z20 Δx=0.2. External mate z43: reported [-1.7522e-3, 1.7850e-3], law gives [-1.7522e-3, 1.7850e-3], agreeing. Internal mate z60: reported [-2.7784e-3, 2.8595e-3], law gives [-2.8595e-3, 2.7784e-3], exactly negated.
proposal: Multiply by `sigma` (`let j = sigma * 2.0 * fit * (...)`), or better, call the mesh module's own backlash function so the law has one site.
validation: Add an internal case to `a_simple_crank_cannot_follow_the_ideal_profile` that asserts, position by position, that j has the sign of σ·(fit − ideal). Also assert it against `Mesh` backlash evaluated at the fit distance.

verdict.reason: Holds exactly as stated: the backlash law is written a second time without σ. The visible effect is small, so I rate it low rather than medium. Only the range reaches the panel. It is swapped end for end, understating interference by the range's asymmetry, about 5-7% in the cases I ran. The panel's warn class does not depend on the error either: the fitted residual always straddles zero, so `sinusoid_backlash[0] < 0` holds whatever the sign.
verdict.evidence: gear.rs:1006 reads `let j = 2.0 * fit * (inv(alpha_actual) - inv(alpha_ideal));`, with `sigma` in scope at gear.rs:903. The documented law is j_t = σ·2a′(inv α′ − inv α_w) (reference.md:272-284), and Mesh::backlash multiplies by `self.kind.sign()` (mesh.rs:354). Probe mode `sigma` (notes/verify-gear-outline/sigma.txt) evaluates Mesh::backlash at each tooth's fitted distance; each Mesh's own a_w equals commanded[k] exactly. z20 Δx0.2 against external z43: reported [-1.7522e-3, 1.7850e-3], Mesh [-1.7522e-3, 1.7850e-3]. Against internal z60: reported [-2.7784e-3, 2.8595e-3], Mesh [-2.8595e-3, 2.7784e-3]. z20 in ring z60 at Δx0.5: reported [-18.57, 19.94] µm against true [-19.94, 18.57] µm. It is reachable: gear-wasm lib.rs:636-651 `eccentric_mate` builds MeshKind::Internal when `mate.internal`. The only tests (gear.rs:2022; gear-wasm lib.rs:2140) use an external mate and check only that the range straddles zero.
verdict.proposal_note: Routing through Mesh::backlash needs a built Mesh per tooth, and centre_profile_of deliberately builds no gears so that amplitude_for_throw stays cheap. Instead, factor the law into one free function in mesh.rs, e.g. `backlash_at(kind, a_ref, alpha_t, alpha_w, a_actual)`, and have Mesh::backlash and centre_profile_of both call it. Test: an internal case asserting, position by position, that j matches Mesh::new(tooth_k, mate, Internal).backlash(fit_k). Also consider reporting the offset a crank needs so that it never interferes (from min j). Because the warn always fires, it carries no information.

title: The smoothstep root displacement folds the eccentric fillet at admissible inputs, and the export then strays 4.6x the tolerance
claim: The fillet is displaced by r → r + w(t)·Δ(angle), with t = (r_j − r)/(r_j − r_f) and w = t²(3−2t). The drawn radius's derivative along the fillet is 1 − Δ·w′(t)/span, which goes negative (the fillet folds back in radius) whenever |Δ| > (2/3)(r_j − r_f). A small shared tip round makes the fillet short, and Δ reaches m·Δx·|cos θ − cos θ_k| across a space. This happens at admissible amplitudes, including the showcase case in corrections.md 4.10. The midpoint-sagitta subdivision then misses the sharp turn the fold creates.
evidence: Probe `fold2`: min d(r_drawn)/dr on the fillet = −2.13 (z23 α25 x0.2 Δx1 ded1 add0.8 λ1; shared ρ = 0.0475), −1.50 (same at λ0), −0.20 (z24 Δx1 rr0.02), −1.91 (z24 Δx2 rr0.38), −3.51 (z24 Δx2 rr0.02). Admissible Δx max is 5.17/5.375 for these. Mild cases stay positive (z24 Δx0.25-0.5: 0.83-0.94). The export of the first case (probe `ecc`, `diag`) deviates 1.44x/3.61x/4.56x at tol 1e-2/1e-3/1e-4, not converging, and the worst segment (v559→v560, r 11.1838→11.1117) cuts across the turn at r 11.1755.
proposal: Displace along a monotone parameter that spans the whole run from the flank junction to mid-space: the fillet's trochoid parameter s joined to the root arc's angle, normalised by arc length, rather than radius over the fillet alone. That spreads Δ over a much longer run. Then state and enforce the non-fold condition: max |Δ|·w′/L < 1. Where it would still fail, clamp and raise a Note (rule 5). The flank is untouched by any choice, since w = 0 there. Longer term, derive the fillet as the envelope of the tool corner under rolling plus radial motion, which rationale scopes out.
validation: Law over a grid of (z, Δx up to admissible max, ρ, λ): the drawn radius is monotone from the flank junction to mid-space on every tooth, modulo the envelope's own slope. Then the outline's worst deviation is ≤1.1x the tolerance on eccentric gears too, using the true point-to-segment reference already in the probe.

verdict.reason: The fold and the export stray both reproduce. The fold is worse than the finding says: the drawn fillet dips below the root envelope at its own angle, a notch no hob can leave, in the showcase configuration two tests already build. One nuance on cause: the strongest fold I found exports within tolerance at 1e-4, so the fold does not always produce the stray. Every case over tolerance had a fold, and concentric gears with the same small tip round stay within tolerance. The stray therefore comes from the displaced fillet's sharp S-turn defeating a midpoint-only sagitta test.
verdict.evidence: Probe mode `fold` reimplements Gear::displacement: every Gear::outline vertex at 1e-5 lies on the reimplementation to 1e-8 mm. The partial slope 1 - Δ·w′(t)/span, minimum over all fillets: z23 α25 x0.2 Δx1 ded1 add0.8 λ1 (ρ 0.0475) -2.130; same at λ0 -1.505; z24 Δx1 rr0.02 -0.200; z24 Δx2 rr0.02 -3.513; z24 Δx0.5 +0.865; z24 Δx0.25 +0.942. Admissible Δx is 5.17 and 5.38. Actual radius reversal along the fillet: 0.053 mm (z23 λ1) and 0.073 mm (z24 Δx2). Mode `notch`: the drawn fillet goes below root_at(its own angle) by 0.0489 mm (z23 λ1, tooth 3) and 0.0700 mm (z24 Δx2 rr0.02); the mild cases never do. Export against the dense drawn curve, truth-to-outline with bulges flattened (fold2.txt, fold.txt): z23 λ1 1.44/3.61/4.59x at 1e-2/1e-3/1e-4, worst in the fillet (e.g. tooth 3, r-rf 0.041, r_j-r 0.010); z23 λ0 1.34/1.38/2.66x; z24 Δx1 rr0.02 1.20/6.14/1.005x; z24 Δx2 rr0.02 1.33/1.11/1.00x; no-fold z24 Δx0.5 0.995/1.105/0.999x and Δx0.25 0.999/1.002/1.000x. Concentric controls with the same tool rounds (ρ 0.02, 0.0475; mode `smallrho`) stay at or below 0.99x once the root-arc vertex is fixed. No test checks the drawn fillet against the envelope: `no_tooth_leaves_the_envelope_it_belongs_to` (gear.rs:2052) checks each tooth's rf and ra only, and gear.rs:2147-2170 checks root_at(seat) only.
verdict.proposal_note: Beyond the reparametrisation, add two laws. The drawn fillet never goes below root_at(angle), and its radius is monotone from junction to root apart from the envelope's own slope. Run them over a grid up to the admissible Δx with small ρ. Separately, a quarter-point sagitta check in `subdivide` (see finding 1) would bound the export error whatever the fillet's shape, so the tolerance promise stops depending on the displacement being well behaved. If the reparametrised displacement can still fold at extreme Δx/ρ, the rule-5 clamp with a Note is the right fallback.

title: With λ≠0 the root 'reach' can fall short of a tooth's own fillet, and the outline crosses itself
claim: `root_reach` meets the neighbour at the midpoint between the two seats, `half_pitch + λ(ψ_a − ψ_b)/2`. `corrected` then maps the root arc [θ0, half_pitch] linearly onto [θ0, reach]. When reach < θ0 the root runs backwards over the tooth's own fillet, and the outline and DXF cross themselves. `admissible_angular_shift` does not account for λ.
evidence: Probe `invert`, a sweep of z ∈ {9,12,17,24,40}, Δx ∈ {0.25..1.5}, λ ∈ {±0.5, ±1}, rr, x ∈ {0, 0.3}, limited to Δx ≤ admissible: 24 of 480 cases have reach − θ0 < 0. Examples: z17 Δx1.5 x0.3 λ±1 (admissible 3.83): −2.48e-3 rad at the undercut teeth 12-14, raw-vertex polygon crossings = 6 against 2 at λ=0. z9 Δx1.5 λ±1: −2.34e-2 rad. Probe `where`: the λ-only crossings sit at r 6.3-7.8 mm, rel-angle ±0.17-0.18 rad, i.e. at mid-space on undercut teeth.
proposal: Meet the neighbour at the midpoint of the free gap between the two fillet feet (seat_k + θ0_k and seat_{k+1} − θ0_{k+1}), not between the seats. When that gap is negative the neighbours' fillets overlap: trim both at their intersection and raise a per-tooth Note, as a severed tooth already does, rather than drawing an inverted root.
validation: Law: over the probe's sweep, every drawn root arc runs forward (reach ≥ θ0 or the trim note fires), and the outline has zero self-crossings (a segment-intersection check like the probe's `crossings`).

verdict.reason: Reproduced exactly, at inputs inside every bound the core publishes, and only when λ≠0. The drawn root runs backwards into the tooth's own fillet, and both the DXF outline and the screen profile cross themselves. The proposal's first half would change nothing, though: θ0 is the same on every tooth of a gear, so the midpoint of the free gap between the fillet feet is the same point as the midpoint between the seats. Only the second half (trim where the fillets overlap, with a note) fixes it.
verdict.evidence:
Probe probes/verify-gear-outline-b, modes reach2 and whyadm (outputs in notes/verify-gear-outline-b/).
- Auditor's examples reproduced: z17 Δx1.5 x̄0.3 λ±1 gives reach−θ0 = −2.482e-3 rad; z9 gives −2.336e-2 rad.
- Both are inside admissible_ranges: shift window [−0.656, 0.442], amplitude bounds 3.83 and 2.06.
- Their root radius 0.38 is above its bound 0.0475, but the core clamps it to exactly that (mean.rho = 0.0475 either way), and the margin is identical at rr = bound.
- Over 1477 cases inside every bound (z 9–60, Δx 0.25–1.75, x̄ ∈ {−0.3, 0, 0.3}, λ ∈ {0, ±0.5, ±1, ±2}): 70 invert, 0 of them at λ=0.
- λ=±1 examples: z9 Δx0.75 x̄0 is −6.13e-3 rad (19.9 µm at rf), with 2 proper crossings in both Gear::outline and Gear::profile against 0 at λ=0. z9 x̄−0.3 Δx1: 38 µm. z12 Δx0.75: 3.1 µm. z17 x̄−0.3 Δx1: 1.8 µm.
- Crossings sit 1e-3 to 7e-3 rad from the seat midpoint, at r 6.3–7.8 mm (z17 Δx1.5 x̄0.3 λ1).
- θ0 spread across one gear's teeth is ≤ 4.3e-16 relative. Algebraically ac = mπ/4 + depth·tanα_t + ρ(1/cosα_t − tanα_t), which has no x in it.
- Default gears at λ=1 first invert at Δx = 0.53 (z9), 1.71 (z17), 1.79 (z24).
- The gated case in the_root_of_one_tooth_meets_the_next (z23, Δx1, λ ≤ 2) keeps a margin ≥ 3.96e-3, which is why it passes.
verdict.proposal_note:
reach < θ0 is exactly the condition that neighbouring fillet feet overlap (free gap = 2(reach − θ0)), so 'meet at the midpoint of the free gap' is the current rule restated. Two fixes work:
1. Trim both fillets at their crossing and raise a per-tooth note (Rule 5).
2. Publish a closed-form λ bound in admissible_ranges: |λ| ≤ 2(π/z − θ0) / max_k |ψ_b,k − ψ_b,k+1|. Today Ranges has no index_offset bound and the UI field has none.
Either way, add a law on the drawn geometry: no proper self-crossing of Gear::profile or of the flattened Gear::outline for eccentric gears at λ ∈ {±0.5, ±1}.

title: Rings have their own profile and outline walkers; the 'one assembly, one outline path' claim is false
claim: gear.rs says every gear in the crate comes through it and that 'there is one outline path … Gear::profile'. In fact Ring::profile is the z-fold replication gear.rs says it replaced. Ring::outline is a second hand-sequenced seven-step walker. Tooth::tooth_outline hand-codes `Tooth::sections()`'s order a second time, independently of the uniform sampler. The missing-vertex bug sits exactly in this duplication. Gear only ever cuts external teeth with a rack, so an eccentric ring can be neither built nor drawn. state.md's 'An eccentric ring … The core supports it' holds only for `centre_profile`'s arithmetic.
evidence: ring.rs:827-846 replicates one half-profile z times at 2πk/z. outline.rs has two walkers (158-247 and 250-354) with parallel steps 1-7. Gear::new calls Tooth::cut_by (rack) only. The wasm always calls centre_profile with MeshSide::First (lib.rs:944).
proposal: Introduce one tooth-form trait implemented by Tooth and Ring: sections as `Arc{r, θ0, θ1}` or `Curve{f, t0, t1}`, plus psi_b, rf, ra and theta0. Make `Gear<T>` the assembly and write one outline walker over sections. Each section emits its own end vertex, an Arc emits one bulged vertex, and a Curve is subdivided. Gear::profile becomes the same walker with uniform sampling. Migration: (1) write the walker for Tooth and prove it bit-identical to tooth_outline plus the missing vertex; (2) move Ring onto it and delete Ring::outline and Ring::profile; (3) generalise Gear over the form, which gives eccentric rings for free. Correct state.md:628 meanwhile.
validation: Existing concentric bit-identity test (`a_concentric_gear_is_drawn_exactly_as_it_always_was`) for Tooth, plus the same for Ring against its current profile. The strengthened arc and tolerance laws run over both kinds. The ring DXF golden stays identical, apart from the fixed vertex.

verdict.reason: Every structural claim holds. Rings are replicated and drawn by their own two walkers. The external gear's export walker hand-codes the section order a second time. Gear can only build rack-cut external teeth. The doc claims ('the only place', 'one outline path', 'The core supports it') are false. gear.rs even contradicts itself: its module doc says there is one outline path, and its Gear::outline doc calls that 'the second place a gear gets drawn'.
verdict.evidence:
- ring.rs:827-846: Ring::profile replicates the half-profile at 2πk/z.
- outline.rs:250-354 (Ring::outline) and outline.rs:158-247 (tooth_outline) are each seven hand-written steps, separate from Tooth::sections() (tooth.rs:725).
- Rings go around Gear entirely: wasm ring_profile (lib.rs:1014) and gear-io's ring_to_dxf (dxf.rs:143) call Ring::profile and Ring::outline.
- Gear::new calls only Tooth::tool_wanted_by and Tooth::cut_by (gear.rs:174, 196, 207).
- wasm centre_profile passes MeshSide::First only (lib.rs:944).
- gear.rs:604 calls Gear::outline 'the second place a gear gets drawn'; gear.rs:48 says 'one outline path … Gear::profile'.
- rationale.md:1065 repeats 'every gear in the crate is drawn through it'.
- state.md:628 ('A UI decision rather than a limit'): the core can only compute a commanded distance for a Gear placed at MeshSide::Second. It cannot build, draw, export or report the variation of a ring-form eccentric member.
verdict.proposal_note:
- Gear::profile is sampled by arc-length allocation (allocate_by_arc_length), not uniformly, and a_concentric_gear_is_drawn_exactly_as_it_always_was pins that arithmetic. A unified walker must reproduce it or re-baseline deliberately.
- 'Eccentric rings for free' is overstated. Each of these needs a ring reading: root_at/displacement (the root moves outward on an internal gear), the one-tool rule for a shaper Cutter, admissible_angular_shift, and variation()'s seats (a ring's ψ is a space's).
- Cheapest first step: make every section emit its own end vertex in both walkers. That alone fixes finding 0 for externals and rings.

title: Eccentric export emits z zero-length segments (one per tooth, including across the closure)
claim: For a varying root, `emit_root(side<0)` pushes curve(1.0), the mid-space point, before subdividing. The previous tooth's `emit_root(side>0)` already ended on that same point, and the last tooth's ends on v[0]. So every eccentric outline carries z duplicate vertices, i.e. zero-length segments. Some CAD importers reject or flag them.
evidence: Probe `ecc`: dup=24 for z=24 at every tolerance (segments shorter than 1e-9 mm). Concentric gears: dup=0.
proposal: On side < 0, do not push curve(1.0). Let the previous tooth's end (or the polyline's closed flag, for tooth 0) supply it. For tooth 0, start the walk at the fillet junction instead.
validation: Law: no two consecutive vertices (cyclically) closer than 1e-9·ra, on concentric and eccentric gears.

verdict.reason: Reproduced: exactly z zero-length segments on every non-severed, non-pointed eccentric gear, closure included, and none on the concentric ones checked. There is also one more per severed tooth on an eccentric gear, from a second duplicate the auditor missed. The claim that CAD importers reject such segments cannot be checked here.
verdict.evidence:
- Probe mode dup: z24 Δx0.25 has 24 segments < 1e-12 mm at tolerance 1e-2, 1e-3 and 1e-4 (closing segment 1.1e-14 mm). z17 Δx0.5 has 17; z23 Δx1 λ1 has 23; concentric z17 and z24 have 0.
- Cause: outline.rs:149-151 pushes curve(1.0), the mid-space point, on which the previous tooth's subdivide already ended (outline.rs:154).
- Extra case: the severed branch (outline.rs:181-184) pushes pt(rf, −θ0) right after emit_root's varying subdivide (outline.rs:152) ended on that same point. z9 x̄−0.3 Δx1 is admissible, has severed teeth 4 and 5, and carries 12 zero-length segments.
- tools/validate_dxf.py does not check for zero-length segments.
verdict.proposal_note:
- Dropping the side<0 push is enough for every tooth, tooth 0 included: the polyline is closed, and tooth z−1's trailing root supplies the shared mid-space point. 'Start tooth 0 at the fillet junction' is unnecessary.
- A cleaner single rule: emit_root(side<0) always emits its own end vertex (the fillet foot) in both branches, and the severed branch's explicit push is removed. That also restores finding 0's missing root vertex.
- The proposed law ('no consecutive vertices closer than 1e-9·ra') will also fail on every pointed tip until finding 9 is fixed.

title: The outline does not clamp a pointed tooth's theta_a ≥ 0 as the profile does, leaving round-off bowties
claim: `sample_section` uses `theta_a.max(0.0)`, but `tooth_outline` uses the raw `theta_a` for both the bulge and the tip vertex. On 40% of teeth capped as pointed, theta_a is −1e-16 rad. The flanks then cross at the tip, a self-intersection of about 1e-15 mm, and the tip span is a degenerate bulged arc.
evidence: Probe `tip`: 380 of 941 pointed-capped teeth (z 6..60, x 0.3..2.07) have theta_a < 0, worst −4.5e-15 mm. z17 x1.4: theta_a = −1.67e-16. The `where` probe finds crossings on those teeth at the tip radius (j−i = 2).
proposal: Use `self.theta_a.max(0.0)` in the outline. When it is 0, emit the tip as a single vertex with no bulge.
validation: Law: no self-crossings on any concentric outline across the pointed-tip range; no bulged span with chord < 1e-12.

verdict.reason: The bowtie is real in memory, but it is the lesser half of the problem. Every pointed-capped tooth emits a degenerate tip span, whichever sign θ_a's round-off takes. In the 12-decimal DXF the bowtie vanishes into a zero-length bulged segment. The proposed .max(0.0) does not remove the degenerate span in the ~40% of cases where θ_a rounds positive.
verdict.corrected_claim: On a pointed-capped tooth θ_a is round-off (±1e-16 rad) rather than 0. The outline therefore emits a ~1e-15 mm bulged tip span on every such tooth, which the 12-decimal DXF writes as a zero-length segment with a '-0.000000000000' bulge. When θ_a rounds negative (40% of cases) the two flanks also cross by ~1e-15 mm in the in-memory outline.
verdict.evidence:
- Probe mode tip over z 6..59, x̄ 0.3..2.07: 941 pointed-capped teeth. θ_a < 0 on 380, > 0 on 382, exactly 0 on 179; |θ_a|·ra ≤ 4.46e-15 mm.
- 138 sampled outlines carry 2303 segments < 1e-12 mm, about one per tooth.
- z17 x1.4: tip span 3.6e-15 mm, bulge −8.3e-17.
- Proper crossings between segments i and i+2 of the raw vertices: 6 at z17 x1.4, 3 at x1.8, 0 at x1.2 (θ_a is −5.6e-17 there too).
- dxf.rs:97 writes {:.12}, so both tip vertices print identically, and dxf.rs:478-479 still writes the nonzero bulge.
verdict.proposal_note: Make the cap exact in Tooth::build_with_z: when CLAMP_TIP_CAPPED_POINTED fires, set θ_a = 0.0 and u_tip = u_point, as check_severed already sets θ_a = 0.0. Then have the walker skip the tip vertex and its bulge when θ_a == 0, as the severed branch does. Gear::profile already drops a zero-length TipArc section in allocate_by_arc_length, so the two drawings then agree.

title: `corrected` identifies the root arc by exact float equality `r == g.rf`
claim: The docs say 'No section needs identifying: the rules are functions of where the point is'. Yet `corrected` stretches a point's angle only when its radius equals rf exactly, bit for bit. It works because the root arc is sampled at literally `self.rf`, and trochoid_at(0) happens to return rf exactly. Any change to how either is evaluated silently disables the stretch.
evidence: gear.rs:389 `let tt = if r == g.rf {`. Probe `junction`: trochoid_at(0) = (7.25, 0.1772…), equal to rf only by construction.
proposal: Pass the section identity (or the root-arc parameter) from the walker, as the unified section walker would do naturally, rather than inferring it from the radius.
validation: Existing continuity laws (`the_root_of_one_tooth_meets_the_next`, `the_root_runs_continuously…`), plus a test that perturbs rf by one ulp in the sampler and still passes.

verdict.reason: The float-equality identification is real, and it contradicts the 'no section needs identifying' comment. But 'silently disables the stretch' holds only for the export path. The screen path is gated by a test. The trochoid_at(0) remark is wrong but harmless.
verdict.corrected_claim: corrected identifies the root arc by bitwise r == rf. The screen path is guarded: breaking the stretch fails the_root_runs_continuously_round_an_eccentric_gear. The export path is not: a one-ulp change to the radius emit_root samples at removes the stretch from the DXF, and no test fails. trochoid_at(0) plays no part: its radius differs from rf by an ulp on 2.3% of teeth, with no effect, because the foot maps to along = 0 either way.
verdict.evidence:
Worktree mutations:
- (a) `if false && r == g.rf` in corrected: the_root_runs_continuously_round_an_eccentric_gear FAILS (plus only the known timing test).
- (b) outline.rs:147 changed to `pt(self.rf * (1.0 + f64::EPSILON), th)`: gear-core + gear-io + gear-wasm pass 674/675 (only the known timing test fails). A probe test on the z23 Δx1 λ1 export shows coincident seam vertices falling from 23 to 1, i.e. 22 mid-space seams now open by λ(ψ_k − ψ_k+1), the ~0.009 rad the root_reach doc quotes.
- Why no test sees it: the export continuity check skips λ≠0 (gear.rs:2382-2385), and the_root_of_one_tooth_meets_the_next checks root_reach arithmetic, never drawn vertices.
- trochoid_at(0).0 == rf bitwise on only 13190 of 13500 teeth (worst 2.6e-16 relative). Harmless: the foot's θ is ac/r = θ0 exactly, so along = 0 either way.
verdict.proposal_note: Give Gear a root_point(k, side, along) used for every root-arc sample in both emit_root and Gear::profile (the arc-length allocator already knows which section each sample came from), and keep corrected for generated curves. Gate the export by a seam-coincidence law at λ≠0 rather than relying on a one-ulp mutation.

title: Misattached and stale doc comments in gear.rs, outline.rs and rationale.md
claim: Nine doc problems in gear.rs, outline.rs and rationale.md. (1) `displacement`'s whole doc (what is corrected, why the fillet moves, smoothstep) is fused into `root_reach`'s doc block. `displacement` has none, and root_reach's rustdoc opens with an unrelated essay. (2) 'distinct teeth ⌈z/2⌉+1' is wrong for odd z: it is ⌊z/2⌋+1. (3) The outline.rs module doc contrasts with `Tooth::profile`, which does not exist. (4) `emit_root` carries `tooth_outline`'s doc ('One tooth's vertices … The loop above …', a loop that no longer exists), and `tooth_outline` has none. (5) A test doc says reference.md tabulates the 62.6/93.9/125.2 µm figures, marked [verified]; they are only in rationale.md, unmarked. (6) rationale.md names `eccentric.rs`, which is now gear.rs. (7) rationale.md says an eccentric gear is 'assembled out of `Gear`s', which should be `Tooth`s. (8) DEFAULT_CHORD_TOLERANCE is 'chosen from that table rather than picked as a round number', but 1 µm is not in JGMA 116-02; it is a round number below its 5 µm.

proposal: Move the displacement doc onto `fn displacement` and the tooth-outline doc onto `tooth_outline`. Correct ⌈z/2⌉ to ⌊z/2⌋ in both places. Fix the Tooth::profile, eccentric.rs and 'Gear's' names. Point the test doc at rationale.md, or move the table into reference.md where check_figures can see it. Reword the default-tolerance rationale honestly: a round figure five times finer than the tightest grade.
validation: tools/check_doc_links.py; `cargo doc` shows each doc on its own item; a unit assertion `distinct_teeth() == z/2 + 1` for odd and even z.

verdict.reason: All eight listed items hold; the auditor wrote 'nine' but lists eight. The same pattern occurs in more places than the auditor found.
verdict.evidence:
- (1) gear.rs:309-345 is displacement's doc running straight into root_reach's at 346; fn displacement (404) has no doc. Its 'tt is its angle from the tooth's own centreline' is also wrong: displacement takes the absolute angle seat + tt.

- (5) The tabulated figures with [verified] are in docs/history/design-record.md:2480-2487. rationale.md:1098-1099 has only 62.6 and 125.2. reference.md has none of them.
- (6) rationale.md:1065 names `eccentric.rs`.
- (7) rationale.md:1112 says 'assembled out of Gears'.
- (8) The minimum tooth_to_tooth in jgma_116_02.csv is 5 µm (fine grade 0), so 1 µm is a round number below it, not a value read from the table.
verdict.proposal_note:
- Add the extra broken links from (3): tooth.rs:324, dxf.rs:35, gear.rs:255.
- For (5): the provenance is the superseded design record, which CLAUDE.md says nothing points at. State the table in reference.md#angularly-varying-profile-shift with a figures tag, rather than pointing code at history.

title: The tolerance floor is set by feel and silent; the depth cap is what actually binds
claim: MIN_RELATIVE_TOLERANCE = 1e-12·ra is described as where 'double precision cannot resolve' the sagitta. That is about 1e-11 mm on a 10 mm gear, far below any CAD resolution, so a tolerance typed as 1e-9 is accepted and every span runs to MAX_SUBDIVISION_DEPTH = 14. The test pins 400k-1.2M vertices at 1e-18. The panel input is `min=0 step=0.0005` with no upper bound on fineness. The clamp and the non-positive fallback raise no Note (rule 5). The floor is written twice, relative to ra for Gear and to rf for Ring.
evidence: Vertex count scales as tol^-1/2 (count.txt: z17 has 226 per tooth at 1e-4). Extrapolated, 1e-9 gives about 70k per tooth, over 1M for z17, against the 16384-per-curve cap. `an_unreachable_tolerance_stays_bounded` asserts 400,000..1,200,000 vertices for one default gear.
proposal: Derive the floor from what an export can mean, e.g. 1e-6 mm (1 nm) absolute, or a relative 1e-9 with the reasoning written down. Clamp in one function in outline.rs that both Gear and Ring call, and return a Note when it clamps or falls back. MAX_SUBDIVISION_DEPTH then becomes a pure safety stop that no reachable input hits.
validation: A test that the floor fires a Note, and that at the floor every span terminates on sagitta rather than on depth (count below spans × 2^14).

verdict.reason: The core claim holds, and the floor turns out to be completely inert rather than just set by feel. I replicated `subdivide` span for span in a probe. The replica's vertex count equals `Gear::outline`'s exactly on five gears across 1e-3..1e-18 (one z200 case at 1e-9 is 260 of 6.3M off, from rotation rounding). Where the stop falls: the depth cap binds first at 1e-9 mm on every gear tested (z17 m1, z9 x-0.2, z43, z17 m5, z200). At 1e-9 on z17 m1, 9,188 of 60,852 spans per tooth end on depth rather than sagitta, and the fillets are already at 16,384. From 1e-10 down, nearly every span ends on depth. The floor (1e-12·ra, about 9.5e-12 mm here) sits 2-3 decades below that. Removing it changes the 1e-18 count from 1,113,908 to 1,114,146 (+0.02%) on z17, and not at all on z9, z43 or z200. It is argued from double precision rather than pure feel, but the argument is off: coordinate resolution is about ε·ra ≈ 2e-15 mm, about 3.7 decades below the floor, so the floor sits neither at the precision limit nor where the work is actually bounded. The other claims check out. The floor is written twice: gear.rs:611-616 against `mean.ra` and outline.rs:264-268 against `rf`, the outermost radius in both, so the intent matches but the code is duplicated. Neither the fallback nor the clamp raises a Note, and `outline` returns a bare `Vec<Vertex>`. GearPanel.svelte:548 is `min="0" step="0.0005"` with nothing below it. The test pins 400k..1.2M at 1e-18 (measured 1,113,908). The auditor also understated the consequence. Below about 2e-9·m the promised tolerance is silently missed: the sagitta at the cap is 1.4-9.8x the tolerance at 1e-9 and up to 405x at the floor. The work is still unbounded on large gears (see missed). Severity stays low because it takes a sub-nanometre entry and an export click to reach.
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-gear-outline-c (modes tol, nofloor, dxf); outputs in /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-gear-outline-c/tol.txt, nofloor.txt, dxf.txt. z17 m1: 1e-8 -> 376,516 vertices, 0 spans ending on depth; 1e-9 -> 1,034,518, 9,188 of 60,852 spans/tooth on depth, worst sagitta at cap 1.97e-9; 1e-10 -> 1,106,904, 62,272 of 65,110 on depth (19.7x tol); 1e-12 and 1e-18 -> 1,113,908 each. Without the floor at raw 1e-18: 1,114,146 (z17), and identical counts for z9 (589,842), z43 (2,818,134) and z200 (13,107,600). z17 m5 at 1e-9: sagitta at cap 9.84e-9 (9.8x). gear.rs:613 `chord_tolerance.max(crate::outline::MIN_RELATIVE_TOLERANCE * self.mean.ra)`; outline.rs:265 `chord_tolerance.max(MIN_RELATIVE_TOLERANCE * self.rf)`; outline.rs:88 `if sagitta <= tolerance || depth >= MAX_SUBDIVISION_DEPTH`.
verdict.corrected_claim: The floor is inert. The depth cap (2^14 spans per curve) is the only thing that bounds the work, and it binds at about 1e-9 mm on a module-1 gear (tol/m below about 1e-9), 2-3 decades above the floor. Between about 2e-9·m and the floor the outline silently misses the tolerance asked: 1.4-9.8x at 1e-9 and up to about 400x at the floor. At 1e-9 about 15% of z17's spans end on depth, not every span; from 1e-10 down nearly all do.
verdict.proposal_note: Tie the floor to the tooth, not to ra. The cap binds per curve, and a curve's size is the module: z200 has ra = 100m, so 1e-12·ra is still 1e-10·m and inside the cap region. An absolute 1e-6 mm (1 nm), 5000x below JGMA's finest 5 µm, avoids the cap on every gear tested. At that floor z200 m1 gives 238k vertices, a 9.3 MB DXF and 250 ms, with no span ending on depth. For the cap to bind at 1e-6 mm would need a module around 1 m. Make it one clamp function in outline.rs that Gear and Ring both call. Send the bound to the panel from Rust (rule 1 counts a bound as an engineering number; today `min="0"` in the .svelte is the only bound), for example through the defaults or ranges payload, and report the effective tolerance when it clamps. Rewrite the comments that credit the floor with bounding the work (see missed). The auditor's validation is right: at the floor, zero spans end on depth, checked on the largest z and module the grid holds.

title: Polyline flanks cost 1.2-1.5x optimal chords, and arcs (bulges) would cut them 3-10x
claim: Dyadic bisection on midpoint sagitta is sound once the vertex bug is fixed (worst deviation ≤1.06x). It spends 1.23-1.50x the closed-form optimum of equal-sagitta chords, ∫√(κ/8tol)ds. Because the output format already carries bulges, the flank and fillet could be emitted as tangent-continuous arcs (biarcs) to the same tolerance. That gives far fewer entities, G1 continuity (a polyline kinks by about √(8·tol·κ) at every vertex), and what CAM wants for G2/G3.
evidence: Probe `count` (count.txt), flank segments against the optimal-chord count: z17 1.50/1.36/1.43x at 1e-2/1e-3/1e-4; z43 1.33/1.33/1.23x; z17 m5 1.38/1.40/1.38x. The estimated arc count for the same flank is 2-10 per flank against 6-106 chords. The fillet is the larger share (z17 at 1e-3: 21 fillet segments against 15 flank).
proposal: An optional `OutlineStyle::Arcs` using biarc fitting of the involute and trochoid (both have closed-form tangent and curvature: `flank_point_and_tangent` and `fillet_point_and_tangent` already exist on Ring). Check the error against the true curve by the same law. Keep chords as the default until a CAD import (SOLIDWORKS/ezdxf) has been checked.
validation: The same worst-deviation law, now point-to-arc, at 1.0x; the entity count reported; `validate_dxf.py` round trip; G1 continuity asserted at every arc joint.

verdict.reason: The numbers reproduce independently. I integrated ∫√(κ/8tol)ds numerically over 200k points for the flank and the fillet, and for the involute that matches the closed form √(r_b/8tol)·(2/3)(u_tip^{3/2}−u_j^{3/2}) to 0.1 segment. Flank segments against ceil(optimum): z17 1.50/1.36/1.43, z43 1.33/1.33/1.23, z17 m5 1.38/1.40/1.38 at 1e-2/1e-3/1e-4, exactly as reported. The fillet is 1.00-1.56, and it is the larger share (z17 at 1e-3: 21 fillet against 15 flank segments). The overhead is intrinsic to dyadic bisection on midpoint sagitta. The kink √(8·tol·κ) follows from h = √(8tol/κ) and turning angle κh. The arc estimate holds to order of magnitude. A single best-fit arc per span has error about 0.0080·|κ'|h³, which for the involute (κ' = −1/(r_b²u³)) gives N ≈ (0.0080·r_b/tol)^{1/3}(u_tip−u_j): z17 m1 at 1e-3 about 2.6 against 15 chords, z17 m5 at 1e-4 about 9.5 against 106, z200 at 1e-3 about 0.6 against 6. Biarcs are two arcs per span with a tangent constraint, so the real reduction is somewhat below that 3-10x. Tangent helpers exist both on Ring (ring.rs:680,690) and for Tooth (strength.rs:299,357), not only on Ring. The module doc says the flank and fillet "genuinely have no arc representation". That is true of exactness, but it does not rule out an arc approximation within the tolerance. This is a feature gap with no correctness impact, so info.
verdict.evidence: /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-gear-outline-c/chords.txt (probe mode chords). Example: `z17 m1 default tol 1e-3: flank segs 15 opt 10.9 (closed 10.9) ratio 1.36 | fillet segs 21 opt 13.5 ratio 1.50`; `z17 m5 tol 1e-4: flank segs 106 opt 77.0 ratio 1.38`. Every reader of the current file already takes bulges: tip and root arcs use them (outline.rs:13-17, reference.md:3036-3039).
verdict.proposal_note: Do not add `OutlineStyle::Arcs` alongside chords. That would be a permanent second path, a branch rule 4 and the one-model goal argue against.
