title: A carried_by self-loop or cycle makes Shape::parts allocate without bound (abort/OOM) — reachable from a file or a wasm payload
claim: The 'a carried axis brings its carrier's' loop pushes the carrier's axis onto `axes` without checking whether it is already there. If an axis is carried by a body on that same axis, or two axes carry each other, the loop never ends and the Vec grows until allocation fails. That is an abort, not a panic, so catch_unwind and wasm error handling cannot recover it. Nothing on the load path rejects such a train, and the test-only `well_formed` rejects only the one-axis self-loop, not a two-axis cycle.
evidence: repro `doc selfcarry` (Planetary+Spur with axes[0].carried_by = a body on axis 0) and `doc cycle` (axes[0].carried_by = the planet body, whose axis is carried by the carrier on axis 0): the train was written with to_toml and read back with from_toml, which printed `memory allocation of 2147483648 bytes failed` and aborted. The old probes `selfcarry` and `fuzzfile2` (`/shape/axes/0/carried_by +1`) gave the same. The watchdog log shows fuzzfile killed at 6.2 GB and 5.8 GB (14:18). Offered and raw edits never produce the state (0 'axis carried by a body on itself' hits over the walks), so only external input reaches it.
proposal: In Shape::parts, push the carrier's axis only when it is new: `if let Some(a) = axis_of_body(carrier) { if !axes.contains(&a) { axes.push(a); } }`. That makes the closure terminate on any input. Also refuse such a train at load time (next finding): the carried_by relation must be acyclic and no axis may be carried by a body on itself.
validation: A unit test in graph.rs: a shape with a self-carried axis and one with a two-axis cycle both return from parts() (with the one-line fix) and are refused by the validator. Re-run `repro doc selfcarry|cycle` under ulimit: it returns a parse/structure error instead of aborting.

verdict.reason: graph.rs:288-297: the closure pushes axis_of_body(carrier) with no membership check, and the `while k < axes.len()` loop walks over what it pushes. An axis carried by a body on itself, or any cycle in carried_by, makes the loop run forever. I reproduced it independently. The web panel imports train TOML through gear_io::train::from_toml (gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:972), so a corrupted file opened in the browser grows wasm memory until it traps. In wasm the panic-versus-abort distinction does not matter, because both kill the instance.
verdict.evidence: My probe (probes/verify-graph-ops-1, `doc self` and `doc cycle` on Planetary+Spur, whose axes' carried_by is [0,2,0]) sets axes[0].carried_by to a body on axis 0, or to the planet body on axis 1 (carried by body 2 on axis 0). It writes the train with to_toml and reads it back with from_toml. Under ulimit -v 3 GB both print `memory allocation of 4294967296 bytes failed` and abort. edits.rs:834 well_formed is #[cfg(test)].
verdict.proposal_note: The `!axes.contains(&a)` guard is the right minimal fix, and it also stops the duplicate work on legitimate carried chains. A load-time check (finding 1) should still refuse the cycle by name, because a cyclic carried_by has no kinematic meaning even when parts() terminates.

repro.reproduction:
Smallest in-memory input: take `Preset::Spur.build()`, which has 2 axes and bodies [(1, axis 0), (2, axis 1)] with carried_by [0, 0], and set `axes[0].carried_by = 1` (axis 0 is then carried by the body that sits on it). For a two-axis cycle, instead set `axes[0].carried_by = 2` and `axes[1].carried_by = 1`. Then call `Shape::parts()`.
- Probe: /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/repro-graph-ops-0 (`probe_repro_graph_ops_0 clean|self|cycle`, under `ulimit -v 2000000`).
- Written as a file, the change is one character. In the graph-format TOML (notes/repro-graph-ops-0/clean.toml against self.toml and cycle.toml), line 53 goes from `carried_by = 0` to `carried_by = 1`.
- Shipped release harness, legacy stage file: copy crates/gear-io/tests/data/elevation_drive_staged.toml and change line 152 from `carried_by = 0` to `carried_by = 1`. That gives notes/repro-graph-ops-0/staged_self.toml; staged_cycle.toml also changes line 157. Then run `/home/user/gearcalc/target/release/gear-cli convert staged_self.toml`.
- Browser payload: notes/repro-graph-ops-0/wasm.mjs and wasm2.mjs load the built web/src/wasm/gear_wasm_bg.wasm (built 7 minutes after HEAD's commit) with initSync and call `import_train` on the graph-format self.toml and cycle.toml.
- Fix check: in a worktree, add `if !axes.contains(&a)` before the push at graph.rs:293 and add a unit test that calls parts() on the self-loop and the cycle. The worktree has been removed.
repro.observed:
Without the fix:
- The probe on the unmodified Spur returns 1 part with axes [0,1], and from_toml gives Ok.
- With the self-loop or the two-axis cycle, `Shape::parts()` never returns and aborts with `memory allocation of 2147483648 bytes failed` (exit 134). No panic is raised, so catch_unwind cannot catch it.
- `gear-cli convert` (release build, legacy stage file): the clean file exits 0. staged_self and staged_cycle abort with `memory allocation of 4294967296 bytes failed` (exit 134). This path goes through gear_io::train::convert → graph_of → parts.
- Wasm `import_train`: the clean file returns OK in 9 ms. self.toml and cycle.toml throw `RuntimeError: unreachable` after about 3.2 s. At that point the instance's linear memory has grown from 2 MiB to 2050 MiB, and wasm memory never shrinks. In this run the instance still answered afterwards: two more clean imports returned OK, with memory still 2050 MiB. So in node the verifier's statement that "both kill the instance" did not hold. The cost was a 3 s freeze, 2 GiB held for the rest of the session, and an opaque "unreachable" error. On a memory-limited browser or phone, the growth itself could kill the tab.

What is correct, and how I know:
- The closure's own purpose ("a carried axis brings its carrier's") says it computes the set of axes reachable through carried_by.
- On any input, that set is at most self.axes.len() entries, so the loop must terminate.
- With the one-line membership guard, the closure computes exactly that. Self-loop and cycle both return 1 part with axes [0,1], the same as the clean train. The new unit test passes, and the whole workspace suite passes, 680/680 (679 plus the new test), so nothing legitimate depended on the duplicate pushes.
- With the guard in place, from_toml accepts both malformed files (Ok), and solve_train then refuses them cleanly with `InPart { part: 0, cause: Wiring(NoCommonFrame(0)) }`, a structured error rather than an abort.
repro.note:
Confirmed by execution on all three routes the ledger names: the public API, the shipped release gear-cli (`convert` on a stage file), and the built browser wasm (`import_train`). The smallest trigger is a Spur pair with one carried_by edited, so any train at all is exposed, not just epicyclic ones.

I re-judge severity as medium rather than high:
- Only a hand-edited or corrupted file reaches it. The offered edits cannot produce it, per the ledger's walks.
- No figure is wrong and no data is lost.
- In the browser the instance survived in my run. The damage there is a 3 s hang, 2 GiB held for the rest of the session and a meaningless error message.
- It is still a real robustness defect: it is an abort, not a panic, with a one-line fix.

Recommended fix, verified in a worktree: at crates/gear-core/src/train/graph.rs:293, write `if let Some(a) = axis_of_body(carrier) { if !axes.contains(&a) { axes.push(a); } }`, and add a regression test covering both the self-loop and the two-axis cycle.

The fixed build then loads such a file and refuses it only at solve time, as NoCommonFrame. That supports the companion proposal: the loader (gear_io::train::from_toml and convert) should refuse a carried_by relation that is cyclic or self-carried, naming it.

Process note: my first `git -C /home/user/gearcalc worktree add` used a relative path and so briefly created /home/user/gearcalc/wt/repro-graph-ops-0 inside the project. I found it and removed it: the worktree was removed and pruned, the wt/ directory deleted, and `git status` is clean again. No file under the project was edited.

Artifacts are in /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/repro-graph-ops-0/ (TOML inputs, wasm.mjs, wasm2.mjs) and in /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/repro-graph-ops-0 and repro-graph-ops-0-fixed. The fixed probe points at the removed worktree, so it will no longer build.

title: No structural validation of a train read from TOML or JSON: out-of-range indices panic in from_toml and solve_train
claim: from_toml deserialises and goes straight to `relieved`, and convert and every wasm entry that takes a Train deserialise and solve. No step checks that indices are in range. A hand-edited or corrupted file therefore panics, or aborts (previous finding), instead of being refused with a reason. The invariant set already exists as `edits::well_formed`, but it is #[cfg(test)] and only the edit laws run it. gear-io's claim that nonsense is 'refused with the parser's own message rather than a panic' holds only for syntax.
evidence:
repro `doc <case>` on Planetary+Spur, written with to_toml and read with from_toml, then solve_train:
- bodies[0].axis=99: from_toml panics 'index out of bounds: the len is 3 but the index is 99'.
- meshes[0].a=99: from_toml panics 'len is 5 but the index is 99'.
- duty.at=99: from_toml Ok, then solve_train panics 'len is 6 but the index is 99' at mod.rs:4527 (`speeds[port]`).
- load at 99, held 99, coupling [1,99], a distance to axis 99, a member on body 99: each is refused by name (LoadPort, NoSuchBody, Wiring).

The old fuzz table fz.out, over field ±{1,7,99}, counted panics: bodies/#/axis 39, meshes/#/a 19, meshes/#/b 21, duty/at 9, axes/carried_by 5 plus cycles.
proposal: Promote well_formed to a production `Train::check(&self) -> Result<(), Malformed>`, with a `Malformed` catalogue key so the reason crosses as words. Extend it to: every index in range (body.axis, member.body listed, mesh a/b, distance axes, coupling ends); carried_by acyclic and never a body on the same axis; every hold at a listed body; every case entry and every Intermittent duty.at at a listed body, or ground only on an empty train. Call it first in from_toml, convert, solve_train, edit_train, offers and preview_edit, returning the refusal.
validation: A fuzz law in gear-io over the same index fields (±1, ±7, 99) and carried_by cycles: from_toml returns Ok or Err, never panics or aborts, and a document that passes check solves or is refused by name. Port the existing fuzzfile probe as the test.

verdict.reason: from_toml parses and goes straight to relieved(), which reads the graph. No index validation runs on the load path or in solve_train. I reproduced each panic the auditor lists. The test-doc sentence at gear-io/src/train.rs:710 ('Nonsense is refused with the parser's own message rather than a panic') holds only for syntax. The only boundary test, `rejects_malformed_input_instead_of_panicking` in gear-wasm, covers solve_gear and export_dxf and no train entry.
verdict.evidence: probe `doc bodyaxis` (bodies[0].axis=99): from_toml panics 'index out of bounds: the len is 3 but the index is 99'. `doc mesh` (meshes[0].a=99): from_toml panics 'len is 5 but the index is 99'. `doc duty` (duty.at=99): from_toml Ok, then solve_train panics 'len is 6 but the index is 99' (mod.rs:4527 `speeds[port]`). `doc member` (members[0].body=99) is refused, but as Wiring(NoCommonFrame(0)), which names the wrong fault.
verdict.proposal_note: Promoting well_formed to a production Train::check is sound. It is cheap next to a solve, so calling it at every boundary (from_toml, convert, and each wasm entry that takes a Train) costs nothing. Keep one validator, so the test laws and the loader share the invariant set. A member on an unlisted body should be refused as such rather than as NoCommonFrame.

repro.reproduction:
Probe crate /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/repro-graph-ops-1 (binary probe-target/debug/probe_repro_graph_ops_1). `write Spur` emits the Spur preset alone with an ultimate and a fatigue case through gear_io::train::to_toml. That gives notes/repro-graph-ops-1/spur.toml: 2 axes, bodies 1 and 2, 2 members, 1 mesh. mk.py makes one-line hand edits of it (v_*.toml). `read FILE` runs from_toml and then solve_train, each under catch_unwind. The same files were then run through the real payload: a --target nodejs wasm built with the shipped tools/build_wasm.sh into notes/repro-graph-ops-1/pkg (target dir under the cache). run.cjs calls import_train followed by solve_train, the same sequence as web/src/core.ts importTrain. It then calls them on the unedited file again to check whether the instance survives. Smallest inputs, each a single edit, out of range by one:
(a) mesh `a = 0` -> `a = 2`, or `b = 1` -> `b = 2`.
(b) body 1 `axis = 0` -> `axis = 2`.
(c) both Intermittent duties `at = 2` -> `at = 3`.
(d) first axis `carried_by = 0` -> `carried_by = 1`: an axis carried by the body that sits on it.
Controls: held = [3], a load at 3, a coupling [1,3], a distance to axis 2 and a member on body 3.
repro.observed:
Native runs:
(a) from_toml panics at shape.rs:1091:24, 'index out of bounds: the len is 2 but the index is 2'.
(b) from_toml panics at graph.rs:291:40 with the same message.
(c) from_toml returns Ok (adjusted false). solve_train then panics at mod.rs:4527:36 (`speeds[port]`), 'len is 3 but the index is 3', and the same for 4, 7 and 99. When only the ultimate case's duty is edited, the solve is Ok: an ultimate case never reads its duty.
(d) Not a panic but an unbounded allocation. In Shape::parts (graph.rs:289-298), the loop 'A carried axis brings its carrier's' keeps no visited set, so it pushes the same axis forever. The process was OOM-killed (exit 137). Under `ulimit -v 2 GB` it aborted in 2.8 s with 'memory allocation of 2147483648 bytes failed'. That is an abort, which catch_unwind cannot catch.

In the wasm payload, (a), (b), (c) and (d) each throw `RuntimeError: unreachable` with no message. For (c) the throw comes from solve_train after import_train succeeded. The UI would therefore open the tab, and every re-solve of it would throw. For (d), import_train threw after 3.4 s with node RSS at about 2.1 GB. The instance was not poisoned: in every case, the unedited file imports and solves identically afterwards.

The controls are refused, but some under the wrong name:
- held 3 and coupling [1,3]: NoSuchBody{at:3}, correct.
- load at 3: LoadPort{case:0}, correct.
- distance to axis 2: InPart{Wiring(NotAMesh(0))}, the wrong name.
- member on body 3: Overdetermined{at:2}, the wrong name. The verifier saw NoCommonFrame for this case on a different preset.

Correct behaviour, by the file's own schema, which needs no second tool: the train lists 2 members, 2 axes and bodies 0..2. An index of 2 or 3 names nothing, and an axis carried by a body on itself is no shape at all. CLAUDE.md rule 5 says such input is refused, and gear-io/src/train.rs:710 says nonsense is 'refused with the parser's own message rather than a panic'. The file header says 'Editing this file by hand is expected.'
repro.note:
The finding holds. It is also slightly worse than the ledger says: the carried_by self-cycle is not only a panic. It is an unbounded Vec growth at crates/gear-core/src/train/graph.rs:289-298 that exhausts memory. Natively that is an uncatchable abort; in wasm it takes about 2 GB and 3.4 s before it traps.

I re-judge the severity as medium rather than high:
- No case gives a silently wrong number. Every failure is loud.
- The wasm instance survives the trap, so the next import or solve works.
- core.ts importTrain catches the exception and shows the message, though the message is only 'unreachable'.
- The cycle case, which can freeze a browser tab, is the high-severity part. Fixing it alone needs only a visited set, or a bound of axes.len() on that loop.

Proposal:
- Keep the ledger's plan: promote edits::well_formed to a production Train::check. Call it in from_toml and convert before relieved(), and at the top of solve_train, edit_train, offers and preview_edit.
- Add to the invariants: carried_by acyclic, and never a body on the axis it carries; mesh a/b and body.axis in range; duty.at on a listed body.
- Give the distance-to-a-missing-axis and member-on-a-missing-body cases their own refusals.

These variant files are the regression inputs: notes/repro-graph-ops-1/v_mesh_a_2.toml, v_body_axis_2.toml, v_duty_all_3.toml and v_carried_self.toml. The runner is notes/repro-graph-ops-1/run.cjs.

title: An offered remove empties a Wolfrom and leaves a case-named body listed; offers(Train) and Insert then panic at conditions.rs:1198
claim: When a removal takes every member, drop_bare keeps any body a case still names, together with its axis. drop_orphans meanwhile parks the cases, because the members are empty. The empty train therefore still lists a body, while parked() also counts that body as parked, since it is in no part. chain_on's k==0 branch then reads `self.shape.bodies[output]` by an entry index taken before the first merge. That merge dedups the leftover entry, the list shrinks, and the index is out of bounds. The same state means Planocentric, emptied and given a spur, ends with its reaction on a bare body coaxial with the input (total None).
evidence: repro `empty`: for each preset, cased with ultimate and fatigue cases at chain_ends, it takes the first unrefused offered Remove at the last axis. Wolfrom with Remove(Axis(1)) gives bodies [(1,0)], axes [0], members 0, and both cases at [1,2]. After that, `t.offers(Target::Train)` panics 'index out of bounds: the len is 2 but the index is 2', and so does Edit::Insert{Spur, None}. For Planocentric the insert succeeds: bodies [(2,0),(1,0),(3,1)], member bodies [2,3], cases load at 2 and react at 1 (a bare body), `total None`. The earlier walk (walk_s2.txt, walk 130) hit the same panic through offers at Train after [Planocentric, Worm] | Remove(Axis(1)) | Remove(Body(2)). In the panel, offers(Train) is what runs when nothing is selected.
proposal: Root cause: an empty graph should list nothing. In drop_bare, when `shape.members` is empty, clear bodies, axes, distances and couplings, so the cases alone carry the parked numbers, which is what drop_orphans and parked() already assume. Separately, make chain_on's k==0 branch robust: have `lay` return the laid bodies' numbers, have `merge` return (or apply) the renumbering it made, and look up the output by its (renumbered) body number instead of a stale entry index.
validation: A law over every preset: remove pieces through offers until the train is empty (every order the offers allow), then offers(Target::Train) does not panic, Insert of every preset succeeds, and the parked cases land on the new preset's conventional input and output (headline is Some and the train solves). The repro `empty` prints no panic and Planocentric's case reacts at the spur's output.

verdict.reason: I reproduced it through offered edits only. Emptying Wolfrom by the offered Remove(Axis(1)) leaves bodies [(1,0)] on one axis with no members and both cases at [1,2]. After that, t.offers(Target::Train) and Edit::Insert{Spur, at: None} both panic with 'index out of bounds: the len is 2 but the index is 2'. offers(Train) is what the panel asks with nothing selected, so the panel breaks on a state it offered. The mechanism holds as the finding describes it. drop_bare keeps a body a case names. drop_orphans returns early when members is empty. chain_on's k==0 branch then reads bodies[output] with an entry index from lay(), and the first merge has already deduplicated the list and shrunk it. Planocentric's variant also holds.
verdict.evidence: probe `empty`, Wolfrom: 'Remove(Axis(1)) -> [(1, 0)] axes 1 members 0 ... offers(Train) Err("index out of bounds: the len is 2 but the index is 2") insert spur Err(same)'. Planocentric: after emptying, bodies [(1,0),(2,0)]. After inserting a spur, bodies [(2,0),(1,0),(3,1)], cases load at 2 and react at 1 (both on axis 0, neither the spur's output), and solve gives cases solved [false,false]. Planetary and MeshedPlanets also leave a body listed ([(2,0)]) and survive only because the indices happen to fit.
verdict.proposal_note: Both halves are right. The root fix (an empty graph lists nothing, so drop_bare clears bodies, axes, distances and couplings when members are empty) removes the state. Making chain_on use body numbers rather than stale entry indices removes the fragility itself. The law should cover every preset emptied by every offered order, as proposed.

repro.reproduction: I ran a probe crate against the public API: /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/repro-graph-ops-2/src/main.rs, via `cargo run` through gc. For each preset it builds `Train::chained(vec![p.build()], ...)` with one ultimate case and one fatigue case at `chain_ends()`. It then applies the first unrefused `Edit::Remove` that `t.offers(Target::Axis(last))` offers, repeating until the train has no members. Last, it calls `t.offers(Target::Train)` and `Edit::Insert { shape: Preset::Spur.build(), at: None }`, each under catch_unwind. Smallest failing input: Preset::Wolfrom, then the one offered edit Remove(Axis(1)), then offers(Target::Train). Only offered edits are used, so this is two actions in the panel: pick Wolfrom, remove the planet axis, and with nothing selected the panel calls offers(Train).
repro.observed:
Wolfrom:
- Start: bodies [(1,0),(2,0),(3,0),(4,1)], held [2], cases load 1 / react 3.
- After the offered Remove(Axis(1)): bodies [(1,0)], axes 1, members 0, held [], and both cases at load 1 / react 2. Body 2 is not in the list; body 1 is still listed.
- offers(Train) then panics with "index out of bounds: the len is 2 but the index is 2", and Insert Spur panics with the same message.

Planocentric:
- After the offered Remove(Axis(1)): bodies [(1,0),(2,0)], members 0, with no panic.
- Insert Spur gives bodies [(2,0),(1,0),(3,1)]. Both cases load at 2 and react at 1, and both of those bodies sit on the leftover axis 0; the spur's second body, 3, is on axis 1.
- solve_train returns Ok with cases solved [false, false], so the train is silently broken.

Correct answer (control): a fresh Spur train, and a Spur emptied the same way (which leaves bodies []), both put the cases at the spur's input and output, (1,2), with solved [true, true].

Planetary, emptied: it leaves [(2,0)] listed. Insert still solves [true, true], only because the indices happen to fit, and the axes come out swapped: bodies [(1,1),(2,0)].

So the claim holds as stated. An empty graph still lists a body a case names. chain_on's k==0 branch then reads `bodies[entry]` with an entry index from `lay` that the first merge has made stale: it panics when the list shrinks past it, and otherwise merges the wrong body.
repro.note:
Severity stays high. The state is reached from a shipped preset by one offered edit. The panic is in offers(Target::Train), which the panel calls whenever nothing is selected, and in wasm a panic traps the module. The Planocentric variant is a silent wrong result: the train solves Ok, but its cases are unsolved and sit on a leftover bare axis.

What I checked and how I know the correct answer:
- The spur control shows where the cases should land.
- The same emptying on Spur leaves bodies [], and Insert then behaves correctly. This supports the proposal's root fix: when `shape.members` is empty, drop_bare should clear bodies, axes, distances and couplings.
- chain_on's k==0 branch should also look up input and output by body number, taken before the first merge or renumbered after it, not by an entry index. This lives at crates/gear-core/src/train/conditions.rs around lines 1195-1207: `let body = |train, entry| train.shape.bodies[entry].body` is used after `self.merge(...)`.

Probe: /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/repro-graph-ops-2. I created no worktree.

title: 'Add case' can write a case at bodies the train does not have, and even switched off it makes the whole solve fail
claim: fresh_case uses headline(), then chain_ends(), then parked bodies, and finally `(max_body+1, max_body+2)`. On a non-empty train with neither a headline nor chain ends, that fallback names two bodies that do not exist. solve_train validates every case's entries against the open ports, the switched-off ones included, so the whole train returns Err(LoadPort). This contradicts the doc (a fresh case 'switched off, so a case added at its default figures moves no rating') and TrainResult.cases ('the ones switched off too… so a panel can say whether one could be switched on').
evidence: repro `fresh3`, all steps offered: [Worm, Planetary, Compound] with cases, Remove(Mesh(0)) twice (the worm's load goes), then Insert Layshaft at body 1. That leaves open ports [1,5,6,8,9,10], headline None, chain_ends None, and fresh_case at [11,12] (max_body 10). solve_train was Ok(()) before the case, Err(LoadPort{case:2}) with the case added and switched off, and the same error with it enabled.
proposal: (a) fresh_case's last resort on a non-empty train should be two open ports: the first open port and the last open port in body order. The phantom pair should only be used for an empty train. (b) solve_train should not fail the train over a switched-off case: validate its ports into that case's TrainCase (solved=false plus a note naming the case) and keep the other cases' results. An enabled case at a non-port can keep its current refusal, or take the same per-case treatment.
validation: A law: for every train reachable by a seeded walk of offered edits, the case fresh_case returns names only open ports (or parked numbers on an empty train), and pushing it switched off leaves solve_train's Ok/Err unchanged. Re-run repro fresh3: the new case sits at open ports and the solve stays Ok.

verdict.reason: fresh_case's last fallback, (max_body+1, max_body+2), is reached on a non-empty train whenever headline() and chain_ends() are both None and nothing is parked. solve_train (mod.rs:4325-4347) checks every case's entries against the open ports, the disabled ones included, and returns Err(LoadPort) for the whole train. I reproduced it only through offered edits. It contradicts fresh_case's own doc ('switched off, so a case added at its default figures moves no rating'). I put severity at medium rather than high: the state needs a multi-part train with no chain ends, and deleting the case recovers it.
verdict.evidence: probe `fresh`: cased [Worm, Planetary, Compound]; Remove(Mesh(0)) twice (both offered); Layshaft inserted at body 1 (offered). Open ports are [1,5,6,8,9,10], headline None, chain_ends None. fresh_case gives [11,12] with enabled=false. solve_train is Ok(()) before the push and Err(LoadPort { case: 2 }) after it.
verdict.proposal_note: (a) is the fix that matters: two open ports on a non-empty train. It could use the first and last open ports, or the first open port and the last part's conventional output. (b) is a policy change to solve_train: reporting a disabled case's bad port inside its TrainCase is reasonable, but an enabled case at a non-port should keep its refusal so a mistyped file is not silently half-solved.

title: Load cases do not survive an edit round trip: removing the stage a case reacts at drops the reaction and grounds the duty
claim: chain_on moves every case entry and duty at the old chain end on to the new shape's output. The inverse edit, removing the stage just chained, does not move them back: drop_orphans deletes the reaction entry, with its given torque and speed, and sets an Intermittent duty to ground. A preset added and removed again therefore leaves the graph identical but every case unreacted. The 'every add undoes' law compares Shapes only, so it cannot see this.
evidence: repro `undo`: take a Spur with cases (load 1, react 2, duty at 2), Insert any parallel or skew preset or Wolfrom/Compound at None, and remove its axes through the edits. The graph comes back equal (`shape back true`), but the cases become [(1,Load)] with `duty at 0` (`cases back false`), and every case reports solved=false with 'train.load_not_reacted' (repro `zero`: Spur+Spur, Remove(Member(3))). This held for Spur, Idler, Layshaft, Worm, Crossed, Wolfrom and Compound.
proposal: Make the case edits symmetric. When a removal takes the body an entry names while members remain, re-seat the entry rather than drop it. The target is the surviving body the removed part was joined through, i.e. the body the part shared with the rest of the train, or chain_ends().1 when that is ambiguous. The entry keeps its role and figures, and an Intermittent duty at the same body follows it. Drop an entry only when there is nowhere to put it, and then raise a note.
validation: A train-level undo law beside every_add_undoes: for every preset p, Train(Spur, cased) → Insert p at None → remove p's pieces through offers, and assert load_cases equal the original field for field and the train solves with every case solved.

verdict.reason: chain_on moves case entries and the duty from the old chain end to the new output (conditions.rs:1207-1222). No removal moves them back. drop_orphans (conditions.rs:341-355) drops any entry at an unlisted body and sets an Intermittent duty to GROUND. Insert-then-remove therefore restores the Shape exactly and leaves every case unreacted. The every_add_undoes law compares shapes only, so it cannot see this.
verdict.evidence: probe `undo`: a cased Spur (load 1, react 2, duty 2). Insert Spur at None gives cases [(1,Load),(3,Reacted)] with duty 3. Removing the added axis restores the shape ('shape true') but not the cases: [(1,Load)] with duty Some(0) ('cases false'). Both cases then report solved=false with train.load_not_reacted. Wolfrom behaves the same. The Idler row of probe `empty` shows the same loss from an ordinary removal, with no undo involved: Remove(Axis(2)) drops the reaction, and the re-inserted spur's cases never solve.
verdict.proposal_note: The re-seating rule needs a precise target. The removed part's body that another remaining part still lists (the join body) is well defined when exactly one exists. Otherwise fall back to chain_ends().1 or to leaving the entry parked with a note. Dropping silently is the one choice that should go.

title: A fatigue duty measured at a held body or at ground silently counts zero cycles
claim: An intermittent duty's turns are `per[s]/per[port]` scaled, with 0.0 wherever the sweep body does not turn, and no note says so. Several paths put the sweep on a body that does not turn: Train::hold removes the case entries at a body but leaves duty.at there; drop_orphans sets duty.at to GROUND; set_duty on a case with no entries seeds GROUND. Every member of such a fatigue case then reports 0 bending and 0 contact cycles, which reads as a result, not a fault.
evidence: Old `duty` probe output: 'pair duty@ground: member 0 case 0 cycles bending 0 contact 0 … solved true notes []' and 'set duty@held ring: … cycles bending 0 … solved true notes []'. Also 'after hold(out 3): loads [(1, Load)] duty Intermittent { … at: 3 }'. repro `undo`/`zero`: after a removal, the duty is 'at: 0'. `grep DUTY note.rs` finds no note key for this case.
proposal: Treat duty.at as a case entry. hold() and join() move it to the case's first reaction (or clear it to the set_duty seed rule), and drop_orphans re-seats it with the reaction (previous finding). In solve, when an enabled fatigue case's sweep body has zero speed in both the case motion and the unit motion, emit a note (e.g. `train.duty_at_still`, naming the body) and report cycles as None rather than 0.
validation: A law: for every preset with a fatigue case, hold the duty body, or remove the stage it sits on, and assert either non-zero cycles or the note. Run check_strings and the five catalogues for the new key.

verdict.reason: In the turns computation (mod.rs:4516-4535), per[port]==0 yields 0.0 turns for every body. No note is emitted, and the case reports solved=true. The GROUND producers are real: drop_orphans sets duty.at=GROUND on any removal that takes the duty body (finding 4 reaches it through offered edits), and set_duty seeds GROUND on a case with no entries. hold() (conditions.rs:1052-1064) removes the load entries at the held body but leaves duty.at pointing at it.
verdict.evidence: probe `duty`: Spur+Spur fatigue case with the duty moved to body 0. solve_train is Ok, case 1 solved true with notes [], and every member reports cycles Some((0.0, 0.0)), against (445,445)/(176,176)/(176,176)/(70,70) with the duty at the output. Edit::Hold(out) on a cased Spur leaves cases [(1,Load)] with duty at 2, the held body. That particular train then refuses as Overdetermined, but the duty is left dangling all the same.
verdict.proposal_note: Report cycles as None, with a note naming the sweep body, when the sweep body turns in neither the case motion nor the unit motion. That is the robust part, because it covers every producer. The re-seating in hold, join and drop_orphans is the finding-4 fix and should share its rule.

title: Join keeps a load at a body it has just made held
claim: hold() removes every case entry at the held body because 'no case can say anything of it'. try_join/merge, however, maps a held body and a loaded body onto one number, dropping only Free entries, so an offered Join can leave a case entry at a held body. solve_train then refuses the train with LoadPort. The two rules for one invariant disagree.
evidence: Walk tallies (walk_s2.txt): 'case # entry at held body #' 237 hits, e.g. walk 0 ending '… | offer Join { a: 5, b: 1 }', where one body was held and the other loaded. LoadPort errors appear in the same walks' solve tallies.
proposal: At the end of merge, apply hold's rule: when the merged body is in `held`, retain only case entries not at it, and move a duty there to the case's reaction. Better still, factor that rule into one function that both hold and merge call.
validation: Extend the train-level well_formed (test-gap finding) with 'no case entry at a held body' and run it after every Join in the offers sweep.

verdict.reason: Reproduced independently. Try_join drops only Free entries and merge keeps one entry per body, so an offered Join between a held body and a reacted end leaves a case entry at a held body. Hold() removes every such entry. So the two rules for one invariant disagree. The solve error is not always LoadPort: in my repro it is Overdetermined.
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-graph-ops-2: Train::chained([Planetary, Planetary]) with case [(1 Load),(5 Reacted)], held [3,6]. Edit::Join{a:3,b:5} is offered (offers(Target::Body) lists it unrefused) and gives Ok. Afterwards held is [3,5] and the case is [(1 Load),(3 Reacted)]: a reaction at held body 3. solve_train then returns Err(Overdetermined { at: 5 }). On the same train, Edit::Hold(5) leaves the case as [(1 Load)]. Code: conditions.rs:910-913 (retain drops only LoadRole::Free) and merge's retain at ~937-946 (dedups but keeps).
verdict.corrected_claim: An offered Join of a held body with a loaded or reacted one leaves a case entry at a held body, and solve_train then refuses the train (Overdetermined in the two-set repro; LoadPort in other walks).
verdict.proposal_note: Factoring one 'drop case entries at held bodies' helper and calling it from hold and at the end of merge is right. But hold() itself does not move a duty measured at the held body, so 'move a duty there to the case's reaction' is a new rule for both paths, not hold's existing rule. Decide it once in the shared helper.

title: pub Train::hold / join / split skip the validation Edit::Hold / Edit::Join apply
claim: There are two public ways to hold or join. Edit::Hold refuses ground and unlisted bodies (NoSuchIndex); pub hold() accepts any number, and the train then fails with NoSuchBody at motion and solve. pub join() discards try_join's refusal (`let _ =`), so a fixture that joins two geared bodies silently builds a different train than it says.
evidence: repro `join`: `t.hold(99)` gives held [99] and then motion Err(NoSuchBody(99)); `Edit::Hold(99)` gives Err(NoSuchIndex). `t.join(1,2)` on a Planetary changes nothing, silently, where `Edit::Join{1,2}` gives Err(Geared). The walks' only HARD invariant hits ('hold at unlisted', 16 in walk_s2) all came through pub hold().
proposal: Make hold/join return Result<(), EditRefused> with #[must_use], validating as Edit does, and have Edit::Hold/Join call them. Alternatively make them pub(crate) and route gear-cli/kinematics.rs and the fixtures through Train::edit.
validation: cargo build of gear-cli and the tests: every existing call site either handles or unwraps the Result, so a fixture whose join is refused fails loudly.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. pub hold(99) records a hold at an unlisted body, and the error only appears later at motion. pub join(1,2) on a set changes nothing and says nothing, while Edit::Join returns Err(Geared). split has no Edit counterpart, so the title's mention of it is only about silent no-op returns: it returns `body` unchanged for a bad part or body. The finding is otherwise accurate. Callers: gear-cli/src/kinematics.rs:289-328, mod.rs tests 6789-7536, edits.rs tests 1346-1553, and internally chain_on (conditions.rs:1225) and Edit::Hold (conditions.rs:1296).
verdict.evidence: Probe output: `pub join(1,2) changed: false; Edit::Join: Err(Geared)` and `pub hold(99) held [99]; Edit::Hold(99) Err(NoSuchIndex); motion Err(NoSuchBody(99))`. conditions.rs:865-867: `pub fn join(&mut self, a, b) { let _ = self.try_join(a, b); }`.
verdict.proposal_note: If join returns Result, the test at edits.rs:1553 must change. It currently relies on the silent refusal (`t.join(a, b); assert_eq!(format!("{t:?}"), before, "refused")`) and should assert Err(Apart) instead, which is better. Keep an unvalidated internal hold primitive (pub(crate) or private) for Edit::Hold and merge to share, rather than validating twice. The simplest route is making hold/join/split pub(crate) and routing gear-cli kinematics.rs through Train::edit.

title: The suite has no train-level invariant law: conditions.rs's case and hold rules are unchecked, and set_duty has no Rust test
claim: well_formed checks the graph and holds but not case entries, duty.at, dense numbering or carried_by acyclicity. The laws that use it apply one edit to a fresh preset, never a sequence, and compare Shapes rather than Trains. Coverage confirms set_duty (conditions.rs:1148-1165) and chain_on's duty move (1219-1223) are never executed by the Rust suite; only the wasm probe's recorded output touches set_duty. drop_bare, drop_orphans and prune have no direct law. That is why the three bugs above (chain_on panic, phantom fresh case, dropped reactions) pass 679/679.
evidence: notes/uncovered_lines.txt: conditions.rs 1148-1150, 1152, 1155-1159, 1161, 1165, 1222-1223 uncovered. `grep -rn set_duty` outside conditions.rs finds only gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:1582. The random walker (probes/graph-ops/src/main.rs, 150 walks × 25 steps, offered plus raw edits) found the offers(Train) panic, phantom case entries and holds at unlisted bodies in under a minute.
proposal: (1) Extend well_formed to the train as in the validation finding, and share one implementation with the production check. (2) Add a seeded random-walk law to gear-core (template: probes/graph-ops/src/main.rs, which interleaves offered edits, fresh_case, set_duty, Release/Hold and Join), about 50 walks × 20 steps, kept under a few seconds. After each step assert the train-level well_formed, that offers(Target::*) and solve_train do not panic, and a JSON round trip. (3) Add the train-level undo law from the dropped-reactions finding.
validation: Run the new law against the current tree in a worktree and confirm it fails on the chain_on panic and the phantom fresh case, then passes once both are fixed.

verdict.reason: well_formed (edits.rs:834-887, cfg(test)) checks graph and holds only: no case entry, no duty.at, no dense numbering, no carried_by cycle. The offers laws build every train with no load cases at all, so no offered edit is ever checked against cases. set_duty's only caller is gear-wasm. The uncovered lines match. Finding 6's bug (a reaction left at a held body after an offered Join) is the kind this law would catch, and it passes the suite today.
verdict.evidence: offers.rs:247-262 trains(): `Train::chained(stages, |_| Vec::new())`, so an_offer_is_its_edit and every_edit_the_train_makes_is_offered never see a case. uncovered_lines.txt conditions.rs: 1148-1150,1152,1155-1159,1161,1165 (set_duty body) and 1222-1223 (chain_on duty move). `grep -rn set_duty crates` finds only conditions.rs:1148 and gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:1527,1582.
verdict.proposal_note: A cheaper first step than the random walk: give offers.rs trains() a case at chain_ends (ultimate plus fatigue with an intermittent duty), and extend well_formed with 'every case entry and duty.at at a listed body not held'. That alone catches finding 6 over every preset. Keep the seeded walk small and deterministic (fixed seed) so it stays a law and not a flaky fuzz.

title: graph_of does not keep a stage's body order when a stage shares two bodies with earlier stages in the other order
claim: The code comment says 'Each stage keeps the order it numbered its bodies in'. That holds only when a stage shares at most one body with earlier stages, or shares them in the same relative order. If a stage lists two already-listed bodies in reverse order, one graph list cannot satisfy both stages. The converted part then has its slots in the graph's order, and its conventional input and output (which chain_ends, check_parts' driven port and fresh_case read) are swapped relative to the stage. The fixtures of graph.rs's laws are all chains, so they never exercise this.
evidence: repro `order`: stages Spur [1,2], Planetary [3,4,5,(6)], then a Spur listing [5,1] (ring first). The stage reads input 5, output 1; after graph_of, part 2 has bodies [1,5] and reads input 1, output 5. Members, meshes and distances map correctly ([[0,1],[2,3,4],[5,6]]).
proposal: State the limit in the module and code comment: a stage re-joining two earlier bodies keeps the graph's order. When conversion reorders a stage's slots, have convert set `adjusted`, or add a note, so the user knows the conventional ends may read differently. Add this file shape to fixtures() with an assertion on the motion only.
validation: The new fixture passes a_file_of_stages_turns_as_its_graph_does, and a test asserts that `adjusted` is set, or that the note fires, for this construction.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. A stage that lists two earlier bodies in reverse order cannot keep its order in one list, so the converted part's slots follow the graph's order and its conventional input and output swap. Impact is limited: gear-io convert takes holds and loads from the file as written (train.rs:434-445), so only defaults read from conventional ends differ (chain_ends, a fresh case, a chain_on onward). The comment 'Each stage keeps the order it numbered its bodies in' (graph.rs:139) overstates this.
verdict.evidence: Probe order(): stage c bodies [5,1], in 5, out 1. After graph_of, part 2 has bodies [1,5], in 1, out 5. Parts' members [0,1],[2,3,4],[5,6] map correctly. chain_ends is None for this graph.
verdict.proposal_note: Stating the limit in the comment is the right size of fix. A note or `adjusted` flag for it is optional: in converted files, holds and cases are explicit, so the swapped conventional ends only change later default choices.

title: Ports' doc contradicts Shape::ports on the hula (order, and whether the wobble body is a port)
claim: conditions.rs lists the hula's ports as 'its crank, its output gear, its grounded gear' and says a body not in the list, 'a planet's, a wobble body's', is nobody's to couple. Shape::ports makes every non-replicated body a port in body order, and says explicitly that a hula's wobble body is one ('an orbiting port is a port'). arrangements::hula lists the bodies as carrier, grounded, output, wobble.
evidence: shape.rs:4165-4186 (ports = (1..=bodies.len()).filter(!replicated)) and its comment on the wobble body; arrangements.rs hula doc: 'Bodies: carrier, grounded gear, output, then the wobble body'.
proposal: Rewrite Ports::ports' doc to: 'every body that is not replicated, in body order — a pair's two members; a set's sun, carrier and ring; a hula's crank, grounded gear, output and wobble body. A replicated planet is nobody's to couple.'
validation: check_doc_links still passes; a reader's check against Preset::build(...).ports() for the hula builder agrees with the doc.

verdict.reason: Ports::ports' doc (conditions.rs:52-60) contradicts Shape::ports and reference.md on the hula. It gives the wrong order and says the wobble body is not a port. The probe gives hula ports [1,2,3,4] with held [2] (bodies: carrier, grounded, output, wobble), so the wobble body is a port. reference.md:2681-2684 agrees with the code. The contradiction goes further than reported: docs/corrections.md:648 still says the wobble body 'is no port now', and shape.rs:4168's own comment says the wobble body has 'four gears on it', but it has two (member bodies [4,4,2,3]).
verdict.evidence: Probe: `hula bodies [1, 2, 3, 4] ports Ports { ports: [1, 2, 3, 4], held: [2] }`, `hula members on bodies [4, 4, 2, 3]`. conditions.rs:54 'a hula's crank, its output gear, its grounded gear' and :59-60 'one not in it — a planet's, a wobble body's — is nobody's to couple'.
verdict.proposal_note: Also fix shape.rs:4166-4172. The wobble body carries two gears, not four. The parenthetical 'For a while a body on a carried axis was no port...' is history that belongs in corrections.md, where a row should record the reversal of row 648.

title: Default distance clearance, tolerances and mesh friction are literals in arrangements.rs, written three times; pair() and planetary() re-set what push_distance already set
claim: The shipped 0.02 mm running clearance and ±0.02 mm tolerance appear as bare literals in push_distance, and again in pair() and planetary(). There they are no-ops: each preset's first distance comes from push_distance with no earlier distance, so it already has those values. FRICTION (0.08, 0.16) is a private const in arrangements.rs, while the other file defaults (planet clearance 0.3, overlap, minimum contact ratio) are named functions in shape.rs.
evidence: arrangements.rs:461-464 `Auto::fixed(0.02)`, `0.02`, `0.02`; 674-676 and 757-759 repeat them on `distances[0]`; line() and epicyclic() build their distances through push_distance with like=None, so the values are already set.
proposal: Add `default_running_clearance()`, `default_distance_tolerance()` and `DEFAULT_FRICTION` beside default_planet_clearance in shape.rs, use them in push_distance/push_mesh, and delete the six redundant assignments in pair() and planetary().
validation: cargo nextest run plus tools/check_golden.sh with no diff, which proves the assignments were no-ops.

verdict.reason: The assignments in pair() and planetary() are no-ops. line() and epicyclic() build every distance through Builder::distance -> push_distance, and the first distance has like=None, so it already gets Auto::fixed(0.02) and ±0.02. The literal is written three times, plus once in prose in Builder's doc (arrangements.rs:33). One part of the argument is weaker: the shape.rs default_* functions exist as serde fallbacks for fields a file may omit, while clearance and tolerance are required fields. So 'move them beside default_planet_clearance' is not needed for consistency.
verdict.evidence: arrangements.rs:454-466 push_distance (like = self.distances.first()); 674-676 and 757-759 reassign the same values to distances[0]; line() at 296-307 and epicyclic() at 206-275 use Builder::distance (arrangements.rs:95-103). Distance's clearance and tolerance fields in shape.rs ~273-284 carry no serde default.
verdict.proposal_note: Delete the six no-op lines. Name the values once as consts beside FRICTION in arrangements.rs (e.g. RUNNING_CLEARANCE and DISTANCE_TOLERANCE, each with its unit and the reason for its value). They are preset defaults, not file fallbacks, so shape.rs is the wrong home unless they become serde defaults. pair()'s doc ('the tolerance band a pair ships with') should then point to the const. check_golden with no diff confirms the deletion.

title: Two definitions of 'a worm': worm_and_pair's worm is not worm()'s, and 7 mm is written twice
claim: worm() pins the worm's shift at zero, sets its root radius to 0, puts the helix boxes where 7 mm gives them (so relief pins a sensible value rather than zero, as its own comment warns), makes the face widths automatic and sets a brass wheel. worm_and_pair sets only `worm=true` and `pitch_diameter = 7.0`, so its worm keeps the shift search, a rack fillet, zero helix boxes and a steel wheel. The same worm-practice conventions are therefore stated once and silently skipped once, with the literal 7.0 in both.
evidence: arrangements.rs worm(): `thread.profile_shift = Auto::fixed(0.0)`, `thread.root_radius = 0.0`, helix = acos(starts/7); worm_and_pair(): only `distances[0].worm = true` and `members[0].pitch_diameter = Auto::fixed(7.0)`.
proposal: Factor the worm conventions into `fn worm_conventions(shape: &mut Shape, distance: usize, worm: usize, wheel: usize, d1: f64)`, called by both, with `const WORM_PITCH_DIAMETER_MM: f64 = 7.0`. Alternatively build worm_and_pair as `worm(..)` followed by an AddRatio/AddGear edit.
validation: Tests using worm_and_pair: the worm member's shift reads 0 and its root radius 0, and the golden corpus diff is explained by the conventions (a diff is expected here: it is a fixture change).

verdict.reason: The two builders do state worm conventions differently, and the literal 7.0 appears twice. A probe shows what that changes at the shipped counts. The worm's shift comes out 0 in both builders, because the automatic search lands on zero, so the difference in shift appears only once a distance is given. The face widths do differ: worm_and_pair keeps MemberGear's default Auto::fixed(10.0), so the worm-drive proportions the solve recommends are reported but never applied. worm_and_pair's own comment says the worm flag "gives the two their conventional proportions", and that is false for the face widths. The root radius (0.38 against 0), the wheel material (4340 steel against Brass C360) and the helix boxes (0 against acos(1/7)) also differ, as the finding says.
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-graph-ops-3 (Train::alone(..,2.0,3000.0).arranged(&[],1,2), shipped library). worm(1,40): m0 x=0 b=13.539 (rec 13.539); m1 x=0 b=4.690 (rec 4.690); eta fwd 0.61805. worm_and_pair((1,40),(17,43)): m0 x=0 b=10.000 (rec 13.539); m1 x=0 b=10.000 (rec 4.690); eta fwd 0.61805. arrangements.rs:707-736 sets the worm conventions. arrangements.rs:787-791 sets only worm=true and pitch_diameter=Auto::fixed(7.0). mod.rs:1310 has the default face_width Auto::fixed(10.0). The only uses of worm_and_pair are fixtures: arrangements.rs:1045, shape.rs:5840, mod.rs:6348 and gear-cli/src/kinematics.rs:196. It is not a menu preset.
verdict.proposal_note: The better route is the alternative: build worm_and_pair as worm(w.0,w.1) and then add the pair with the graph's own Edit (AddGear/AddRatio on the wheel's body). This makes the fixture the same construction a designer would make in the panel, and it leaves only one statement of the worm conventions. If you factor out a helper instead, also name the 7 mm as a const next to worm(). Expect a golden or kinematics diff only if gear-cli kinematics prints face widths or material; the ratio and efficiency do not move.

title: Preset::family duplicates Shape::family by hand; small inconsistencies in the builders
claim: Preset::family is a ten-arm match whose only check is a test asserting it equals `self.build().family()`, which is the rule itself. planetary() alone clamps `count.max(1)` and alone spells `i32::try_from(planet).unwrap_or(i32::MAX)` instead of the module's `external()`.
evidence: The doc comment 'the test below holds the two to each other'; planetary() body vs wolfrom/stepped/planocentric, which call external() and do not clamp.
proposal: Make it `pub fn family(self) -> PresetFamily { self.build().family() }` (cheap, and there are ten presets), and delete the match and its test. In planetary(), use external(planet) and drop the silent clamp, or apply the same clamp in epicyclic for every family.
validation: cargo nextest run; the menu order and families in the wasm `defaults` recorded output unchanged (check_wasm.sh).

verdict.reason: The duplication and the planetary() inconsistencies are real. But the test is not tautological, as the finding implies. It checks the menu's hand-written grouping against the shape's reading, so a preset whose shape stopped reading as its family (for example a Crossed preset built at angle 0) would fail it. Making family() = build().family() turns that check into something true by construction. That is a reasonable simplification: the grouping would then follow the shape automatically, and defaults() builds every preset anyway. The count.max(1) clamp is also redundant, because Shape::count_of already reads a zero count as 1 (shape.rs:463). The proposal's "delete the match and its test" is wrong about the test: every_preset_is_in_its_own_family_and_solves_conventionally also checks that every preset solves, so only its family assertion should go.
verdict.evidence: arrangements.rs:902-914 is the ten-arm match. arrangements.rs:1285-1295 is the test, which also asserts r.ratio is finite and nonzero for every preset. The only callers are gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:1185 and that test. arrangements.rs:741-742 has count.max(1) and i32::try_from(planet).unwrap_or(i32::MAX), whereas wolfrom, stepped and planocentric (lines 544, 573, 604) use external() and do not clamp. external() at line 471 has the same body. shape.rs:463 has count_of … self.axes[a].count.max(1).
verdict.corrected_claim: Preset::family duplicates Shape::family, and a test cross-checks the two (a genuine but avoidable check). planetary() alone clamps count and spells out external() inline; the clamp repeats what Shape::count_of already does.
verdict.proposal_note: Keep every_preset_..._solves_conventionally and remove only its family assert_eq. Drop count.max(1) in planetary() rather than moving it into epicyclic, since the shape already tolerates count 0 where it reads counts.

title: The panel's fresh-case figures are written twice in gear-wasm
claim: The shipped train's case figures (0.1 N·m / 30 000 rpm ultimate, 0.02 N·m / 30 000 rpm fatigue) are literals in `defaults` and again in apply_edit's AddCase arm, whose comment says 'the figures a fresh case starts at are the shipped train's'. A change to one leaves the other stale.
proposal: Add one `fn shipped_case_figures(kind: CaseKind) -> (f64, f64)`, better placed in gear-core beside LoadCase so the core owns the default under rule 1, and use it at both sites.
validation: check_wasm.sh with no diff.

verdict.reason: Both sites carry the same four literals. The AddCase comment says the figures are the shipped train's, and nothing ties them together. Rule 1 does not strictly require the constants to live in gear-core, because gear-wasm is Rust. Still, Train::fresh_case (conditions.rs:1094) already exists in the core and takes torque and speed as parameters, so the core owning the defaults there is the natural single home.
verdict.evidence: gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:1175 LoadCase::ultimate(input, output, 0.1, 30_000.0); :1177 LoadCase::fatigue(input, output, 0.02, 30_000.0); :1576 CaseKind::Ultimate => (0.1, 30_000.0); :1577 CaseKind::Fatigue => (0.02, 30_000.0). A test at lib.rs:2853 pins only the speed 30_000.0 of case 0.
verdict.proposal_note: Put the figures on CaseKind in gear-core, for example CaseKind::shipped_figures(self) -> (f64, f64), or have fresh_case take only the kind. Then use them in both the defaults() train and apply_edit. The comment above defaults' train at lib.rs:1165 ("The three loads a fresh train used to hold as fields") is refactor history of the same kind as finding 15 and could be rewritten as present tense at the same time.

title: conditions.rs comments carry refactor history and a pointer to the working handoff notes
claim: Several doc comments explain the present by the past. For example: 'It used to live on the stage… which is why…'; 'That is the handoff's point about mobility above one taken seriously', which points at geartrain-refactor-handoff.md, a root-level working note; '`solve_train` refused a train outright when any one stage would not close…'; and MotionReport 'crossed to the panel on every solve until it was asked…'. The present-tense rule each one carries is clear without the story, and the story belongs in docs/corrections.md or rationale.md.
evidence: The quoted lines at the given locations; the owner's goal is 'each thing said once' with 'no self-referential history'.
proposal: Keep one present-tense sentence per item (e.g. 'A body's role is a reading of a load case, not structure: two drives and one load, or one drive and two loads, are one kinematic object'). Move the history to docs/rationale.md#… with a link, and drop the reference to the handoff file.
validation: tools/check_doc_links.py passes; the comments read the same to someone who has never seen the stage types.

verdict.reason: All four quoted passages are there and explain the present by the past. docs/rationale.md already records the stage-type history (line ~1694: "Each arrangement was a stage *type* with a result of its own"), so the module doc repeats it. "The handoff's point" points at a working note in the repository root with no link. The same unlinked reference to the handoff also appears in train/wiring.rs:16 and kinematics.rs:159, which the finding did not list.
verdict.evidence: conditions.rs:8-12 ("It used to live on the stage — a planetary set carried an `Arrangement`…"); :25-26 ("That is the handoff's point about mobility above one taken seriously"); :146-148 ("`solve_train` refused a train outright when any one stage would not close…"); :707-709 ("It crossed to the panel on every solve until it was asked…"). geartrain-refactor-handoff.md:108 is "## 4. Mobility > 1". Handoff references in code: wiring.rs:16 ("The handoff this work answers proposes storing each mesh's frame") and kinematics.rs:159 ("the handoff this work answers is right that…").
verdict.proposal_note: Extend the proposal to wiring.rs:16 and kinematics.rs:159. Either state the argument in present tense or link to the rationale.md section that carries it. If the handoff file is to stay as a reference, check_doc_links.py should see a real link to it, not a prose mention.

title: Ring tab's 'smallest tooth count' ignores profile shift (computed in gear-wasm, not the core)
claim: `smallest_tooth_count` is documented as 'the fewest teeth this design could have had and still cleared its own base circle'. It computes ceil(2 h_a cos β / (1 − cos α_t)), which leaves out the profile shift. The ring's actual tip radius in ring.rs:278 is r − m(h_a − x), so the true bound is ceil(2 (h_a − x) cos β / (1 − cos α_t)). Because the formula sits in the boundary crate, no core law or golden output covers it.
evidence: A probe using Ring::cut_by with a 10-tooth cutter on default rack params: at z=17, x=+0.5 the tip clears the base circle (ra=8.0000 > rb=7.9874, no ring_tip_raised clamp) but the UI figure says 34. At z=40, x=−0.3 the core raises the tip (clamp.ring_tip_raised, ra=rb=18.7939) and the UI figure still says 34. With the shift included the formula gives 17 and 44, which matches the clamp exactly at z=16/17 and 40/44. The wasm test asserts only the unshifted case (x=0 gives 34).
proposal: Move the function into gear_core::ring as `Ring::smallest_tooth_count(params) -> u32` (or `ring::fewest_teeth`), using (h_a − x). Have the wasm read it. Delete the wasm copy.
validation: A law over a grid of x ∈ [−0.5, 0.8], β ∈ {0, 15, 30}°, h_a ∈ {0.8, 1.0}: at z = smallest the cut ring has no CLAMP_RING_TIP_RAISED, and at z = smallest − 1 it has one.

verdict.reason: The ring tab's 'smallest tooth count' leaves out the profile shift, so the panel shows a wrong figure for any shifted ring. The core's tip is ra = r − m(h_a − x) (ring.rs:278) and the tip clears the base circle when r(1 − cos α_t) ≥ m(h_a − x), which gives z ≥ 2(h_a − x)cos β/(1 − cos α_t). gear-wasm lib.rs:554-561 uses params.addendum alone. The figure is wrong in both directions: too pessimistic for x > 0 and too optimistic for x < 0. The doc comment at lib.rs:533 says 'this design', which includes its shift. The only test (lib.rs:2310) is the x = 0 case, and no golden output reaches the wasm crate. Severity is medium rather than high: the core's own clamp (CLAMP_RING_TIP_RAISED) still protects the geometry; only the advisory figure is wrong.
verdict.evidence: Derived from ring.rs:278 and r = z·m_t/2, rb = r·cos α_t. Computed at α = 20°, β = 0, h_a = 1: x = +0.5 gives 16.58, so 17 (panel shows 34); x = −0.3 gives 43.11, so 44 (panel shows 34); x = 0 gives 33.16, so 34 (matches the test). The wasm copy also re-derives α_t with its own atan expression instead of plane::transverse_pressure_angle, which ring.rs uses.
verdict.proposal_note: Put it in gear_core::ring next to the clamp and compute it from the same ra and rb expressions, so the clamp and the figure cannot disagree. The proposed law (no clamp at z = smallest, a clamp at smallest − 1) is right, but restrict it to the base-circle clamp. For large z the thickness clamp (ψ_b < 0, about 105 teeth) can fire independently. Also update the doc comment's formula.

title: Engineering defaults live in gear-wasm and are written twice (fresh-case figures, UI seeds)
claim: The shipped load-case figures are literals in the boundary crate: (0.1, 30_000.0) ultimate, (0.02, 30_000.0) fatigue, and 3.0 back-driving. They appear once in defaults_impl and again in apply_edit's AddCase, whose comment says they are 'the shipped train's'. Nothing ties the two copies together. The same crate also holds UI_SEED = 5 mm face width, the gear tab's 9 teeth, a 1.75 mm pin and a 0.1 mm throw. So the 'thin boundary' holds engineering numbers that the core's tests and golden corpus never see.
evidence: grep for 30_000.0 finds lib.rs lines 1175, 1177, 1576 and 1577, plus a test at 2853. Train::fresh_case(kind, torque, speed) in the core takes the figures as arguments, so the core has no default of its own.
proposal: Add gear_core::train::defaults (or arrangements::shipped) containing `Train::shipped()`, `LoadCase::fresh(kind, input, output)` with named constants (SHIPPED_ULTIMATE_TORQUE and so on), and a `GearTabDefaults` built in the core. Make defaults_impl and apply_edit one-line reads of these.
validation: tools/check_wasm.sh shows no diff in recorded answers. Add a core test that a fresh case of each kind equals the shipped train's case of that kind.

verdict.reason: Real part: the fresh-case figures (0.1 N·m / 30 000 rpm ultimate, 0.02 N·m / 30 000 rpm fatigue) are written twice in gear-wasm, in defaults_impl and in apply_edit's AddCase. Only a comment ties them together, and the one test (lib.rs:2853) checks the shipped train, not AddCase. The golden corpus cannot see them: the CLI and gear-io use different figures (2.0 N·m, 3000 rpm). Overstated part: this is not a breach of rule 1 (these are Rust numbers, not TypeScript), and the UI seeds (5 mm face-width seed, 9 teeth described as 'the specification's default tooth count, not the core's', 1.75 mm pin, 0.1 mm throw) are panel seeds. The boundary's defaults() is a defensible home for them, so moving them into gear-core is a choice, not a fix.
verdict.evidence: lib.rs:1175-1177 and lib.rs:1576-1577 hold the same literals. Train::fresh_case (conditions.rs:1094) takes torque and speed as arguments. grep for LoadCase::ultimate( shows gear-cli main.rs:1327 and strings.rs:1113 use 2.0 N·m at 3000 rpm, so check_golden never sees 0.1/30 000.
verdict.corrected_claim: The shipped load-case figures are duplicated between defaults_impl and apply_edit(AddCase) in gear-wasm with nothing but a comment tying them, and no corpus or core test reaches them.
verdict.proposal_note: The smallest fix is one `fn shipped_case(kind: CaseKind) -> (f64, f64)` (or named consts) in gear-wasm, read by both sites, plus a wasm test that AddCase of each kind equals the shipped train's case of that kind. Moving GearTabDefaults into gear-core is optional and not justified by this finding.

title: Five refusal channels cross the boundary; an edit refusal is detected by string-prefix sniffing
claim:
The same boundary returns refusals in five different ways:
1. solve_train returns a Note as data (TrainOutcome.failure).
2. edit_train throws a JsError whose message is a catalogue key, and core.ts detects it with `message.startsWith("ui.")`. rationale.md#no-english-in-gear-core says branching on message text was eliminated.
3. solve_gear, solve_ring and the DXF exports return free English text.
4. gear_profile, offers and preview_edit swallow errors into null or [].
5. The core has eight error enums (TrainError, MotionError, WiringError, MeshError, ScrewError, MeasurementError, EditRefused, flow::Refused). Each has two renderings, `Explain::note` and an English `Display`. EditRefused has no Explain, only a bare-string key(), and its keys are not note::key constants.
evidence: edit_train_impl maps an error with `e.key().to_string()` into a JsError; core.ts:825 tests `message.startsWith("ui.")`. resolved_params returns format!("a centre-distance throw of {:.4} mm is not reachable…"), and GearPanel.svelte:645 shows result.error as it comes. TrainError's Display (mod.rs:1712-1788) still says 'a worm stage needs crossed shafts, and a parallel pair is a spur stage', naming stage types that no longer exist.
proposal: Use one refusal type: `pub struct Refusal { note: Note, at: Option<PieceRef> }`. Implement `From<E> for Refusal` for every core error, and give EditRefused `Explain` with its keys in note::key. Every wasm entry point returns `{ok: T} | {refused: Refusal}` as data. JsError is kept only for a malformed request. Delete the English Display impls in gear-core. gear-cli renders a Note through gear_io::strings with the English catalogue. core.ts gets one generic `call()` that narrows the union.
validation: Extend gear_io::strings' 'fire every note' test to fire every EditRefused and every error variant. Add a wasm test that no entry point returns a string that is not JSON. The golden corpus diff on CLI error lines is reviewed once and recorded.

verdict.reason: Three specific points hold. (1) edit_train returns an EditRefused as a JsError whose message is its key, and core.ts:825 tells a refusal from a defect with message.startsWith('ui.'). preview_edit already carries the same refusal as data (Preview.refused: Option<Note>, preview.rs:22,90), so the two channels for one refusal disagree. (2) resolved_params sends English to the gear tab (see finding 3). (3) The TrainError Display for AxesAreParallel still says 'a worm stage … a spur stage' (mod.rs:1742), and strings_en.toml:197 screw_axes_are_parallel also says 'a worm stage'. The 'five channels / eight enums, each with two renderings' framing is inaccurate. MotionError, WiringError and flow::Refused have neither Display nor Explain; they fold into TrainError through From. ScrewError has Explain but no Display of its own. Only MeshError, MeasurementError and TrainError carry both, and EditRefused has key() plus Display. Channel 4 (offers, preview_edit and gear_profile return null on error) is the documented 'boundary broke' path: those entry points fail only on a malformed request, and preview carries its refusal as data. The prefix test branches on a namespace, not on wording, so it will not break under translation, unlike the four cases rationale.md describes.
verdict.evidence: core.ts:817-826 editTrain; edits.rs:155-168 key(); preview.rs:22,88-90; mod.rs:1742-1743; strings_en.toml:197; grep of impl Display/Explain in gear-core/src lists only metrology.rs, mesh.rs, screw.rs (Explain only), train/mod.rs and edits.rs (Display).
verdict.corrected_claim: edit_train sends a refusal through the exception channel and the UI tells it from a defect by a 'ui.' prefix, while preview_edit returns the same refusal as data. Gear-tab failures cross as English (finding 3). A stale 'stage' wording survives in TrainError's Display and in the English catalogue. The claimed eight-enum, two-rendering duplication does not hold as stated.
verdict.proposal_note: The narrow fix is enough: have edit_train return {train} | {refused: Note} as data, as preview does, and drop the prefix test. Give the gear-tab failures Notes (finding 3), and reword the stale 'stage' strings. Deleting every English Display in gear-core would break the CLI's error lines and the golden corpus for little gain. The CLI could render through gear_io::strings, but that is a separate and larger change.

title: Gear-tab failures reach a translated UI in English
claim: When a throw cannot be reached or no mate was given, and on a malformed request, the gear and ring tabs show an English sentence built in Rust with the number already formatted. A German or Japanese user sees English, and the string catalogues and check_strings.py cannot see these sentences.
evidence: resolved_params returns Err("a centre-distance throw is commanded against a mate — set the mate's tooth count") and Err(format!("a centre-distance throw of {:.4} mm is not reachable with this mate…")). core.ts `solve` wraps them as {error: e.message}, and GearPanel renders `{result.error}`.
proposal: Emit a Note (for example error.gear_throw_needs_mate, and error.gear_throw_unreachable with a `throw` number) through the Refusal channel proposed above. Add the five catalogue entries.
validation: The gear_io::strings firing test covers the new keys. A wasm test checks that an unreachable throw returns {refused:{note:{key}}}.

verdict.reason: The unreachable-throw sentence is a Rust-built English string with a pre-formatted number. core.ts wraps it as {error: e.message} and GearPanel renders it verbatim (GearPanel.svelte:574 for the ring, :645 for the gear), so non-English users see English, and check_strings and the catalogues cannot see it. It is reachable: in eccentric mode the panel sends a user-typed throw, and amplitude_for_throw refuses a large one. The other sentence ('commanded against a mate — set the mate's tooth count') cannot be reached from the panel: GearPanel.svelte:152-155 always sends the mate whenever it sends a throw, so that one is a defect-path message. ui.gear_export_failed also interpolates an English reason from the DXF path.
verdict.evidence:
lib.rs:656-679 resolved_params, whose two Err strings include format!("a centre-distance throw of {:.4} mm…"). core.ts:520-524 is solve's catch, which returns {error: e.message}. GearPanel.svelte:152-155 sends the mate together with any eccentric_throw, and GearPanel.svelte:645 renders

{result.error}

.
verdict.proposal_note: Only the unreachable-throw case needs a catalogue Note (with a `throw` value formatted in the core). The needs-a-mate case is a malformed request and can stay on the defect path. Carry the Note as data in the solve_gear result instead of through JsError.

title: Dense-index graph with renumbering on every removal; the UI re-derives the core's renumbering
claim: Axes, bodies (train numbers), slots (per-part numbers), members, meshes, distances, couplings and cases are all addressed by position. Every removal has to renumber every reference across the shape, holds, loads and duties (renumber, prune, drop_orphans, drop_bare, renumber_bodies, drop_bodies and others). Edit results do not say what was made or where things moved, so TrainPanel guesses. It selects `{ body: Math.min(edit.join.a, edit.join.b) }` after a join and clears the selection after any removal 'since the numbers after it have moved'. That puts a renumbering rule in TypeScript, and it goes wrong whenever prune shifts the kept body. There are also two numbering systems for one body (train number and part slot). They are translated through `port`, `slot`, `body_at` and `slot_if_any`, at more than 60 sites in conditions.rs, edits.rs, shape.rs and mod.rs.
evidence: renumber() maps a dropped body to GROUND via `map(b).unwrap_or(GROUND)`, so a member or carrier that still named a dropped body would silently land on ground. Only the invariant that prune checks every naming site prevents that, and prune checks bodies, holds and loads but not members or axes directly. TrainPanel.svelte:249-254 contains the selection guess.
proposal: Step A (no format change): have `Train::edit` return an `EditOutcome { made: Vec<PieceRef>, renumbered: Renumbering }`. Have edit_train return it, and make the UI's `made()` a lookup. Step B: add newtype indices (BodyId, SlotId, MemberIdx, MeshIdx, AxisIdx, DistanceIdx) that serialize as plain numbers, so the wire and file stay the same and the compiler separates body from slot. Step C (optional, format bump): give pieces stable ids that are never renumbered, which deletes prune and renumber.
validation: Existing laws every_add_undoes, a_removal_takes_what_goes_with_it_and_leaves_nothing_hanging and every_edit_the_train_makes_is_offered. A new law: for every edit on every preset, each piece named in `made` exists afterwards, and `renumbered` maps every surviving old index to the same piece (compared by content).

verdict.reason: Dense positional indices with renumbering after every removal are real. Returning what an edit made or kept (step A) is a sound, cheap improvement. The concrete defect claims do not hold. After a join the panel selects min(a,b), and the core's rule is exactly 'the lower number survives' (conditions.rs:910). merge gives up b's number and prune closes up only the numbers above it, so bodies below min(a,b) do not move. The TypeScript line is therefore a duplicated rule, not a wrong one. The one way it could go wrong is joining two bodies that only free loads name, which exists only on an empty train where drop_orphans has not run. Clearing the selection after a removal is a UI choice, not a renumbering rule. The renumber() unwrap_or(GROUND) concern is theoretical. Members name bodies that shape.bodies lists (renumber_bodies at shape.rs:404 maps members, carried_by and couplings together), and prune's 'named' test covers shape.bodies, holds and loads. A member on an unlisted body is already an invalid shape. The two numberings (train body and part slot) are deliberate: a part's kinematics is solved in its own numbering, which is what lets a preset be asked alone. The count of translation sites holds (about 98 across the four files, tests included).
verdict.evidence: conditions.rs:909-916 (the lower survives, then merge), conditions.rs:304-336 prune, shape.rs:404-419 renumber_bodies, TrainPanel.svelte:249-253 made().
verdict.corrected_claim: Edits do not report what they made or kept, so TrainPanel re-states the core's 'lower body survives a join' rule and the 'first new mesh is at the old count' rule in TypeScript. They agree with the core today but are not tied to it.
verdict.proposal_note: Step A (EditOutcome with made and kept pieces) is worth doing. Step B (newtype indices) is a reasonable safety gain. Step C (stable ids, a file-format bump) is a large redesign, and nothing here shows a defect that would justify it.

title: shape::rate is one 556-line function of ~20 nested closures; it also sizes face widths, so the cut/rate split is not 'geometry vs load'
claim: `rate()` covers, in one body: contact stress at a probe width, point-contact rating per case, the member rating, automatic face-width sizing (overlap floors, largest requirement across meshes), backlash rows and bands, distance and group notes, planet layout, and assembly of MeshReport and GearResult. Cut is documented as 'everything about it no load case moves', but face width is geometry, it is sized here from the flow's torques, and the reported ContactRatios.overlap is read at that load-sized width. solve_parts (358 lines) and chosen_at (184) are the next longest. Because the closures capture one another, no piece can be tested or reused on its own.
evidence: census.py longest functions: rate 556, solve_parts 358, chosen_at 184, groupings::flow 171, paths_of 150, graph::parts 147, offers::candidates 137. Inside rate, `let widths` is computed at about 3480, `mesh_widths[k]` feeds ContactRatios::of at 3817, while cut() computed each mesh's efficiency at `early_width` (3189).
proposal: Make the solve a pipeline of pure stages, each with its own output struct: `plan → search (Chosen) → build (Built) → cut (efficiencies, bending sections) → flow (CaseLoad) → size (Widths: per member, with the requirement that set each) → rate (MemberRating and ContactPatch per case) → report (MeshReport, GearResult, notes)`. Move the backlash rows and bands and the layout to their own functions taking (Built, Distance). Aim for no function over about 120 lines.
validation: A behaviour-neutral refactor: cargo nextest, check_golden and check_wasm with zero diffs. Add unit tests for `size` alone, e.g. a width a given overlap asks for equals width_for_overlap, and the largest requirement wins.

verdict.reason: The size claim holds and is understated: rate runs 3250-3907, about 657 lines by brace count; chosen_at is 217 lines and cut is 137. The body is a chain of closures that capture one another (on_a_line, early_width, face_of, point_contact, play_of, contact_at, final_width), so none can be tested alone. The architectural complaint that face width 'belongs in cut' is wrong. Width is sized from the flow's torques, the flow is written from the efficiencies that Cut computes, so width must come after the flow. The Cut doc ('everything no load case moves') is accurate because Cut does not store a width. For line contact, efficiency does not depend on face width at all (shape.rs:2484-2486), so the flow is unaffected. Reading the overlap ratio at the load-sized width is correct, since that is the width the gear gets.
verdict.evidence: Brace-matched lengths from a script over shape.rs: rate 3250-3907 (657 lines), chosen_at 1717-1934 (217), cut 3105-3242 (137). shape.rs:2482-2495 shows Line efficiency takes no face, while Point uses zone(face). shape.rs:3487-3514 sizes the widths and then computes rated_point at final_width.
verdict.corrected_claim: rate is one ~650-line function built from mutually capturing closures, which blocks unit testing of face-width sizing, backlash and reporting. Width sizing sits in rate because it depends on the flow, and that placement is correct.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposed pipeline order (cut, flow, size, rate, report) matches the dependency and is sound. Extract size_widths(&Cut, asks) -> Widths and the backlash rows first. The '120-line' target is a rule of thumb, not a requirement. See the missed item on efficiency at early width for point meshes.

title: train/mod.rs and shape.rs are grab-bags: inputs, reports, rating, relief, errors and solve in one file; impls scattered over 6-7 files
