claim: train/mod.rs defines, in about 4,640 production lines: mesh report types (ContactRatios, Backlash, MeshReport, LineContact, PointContact, ContactPatch, TipRoom), rating (Bending, Loading, Rated, MemberRating), member inputs (MemberGear, FaceSources), results (GearCase, GearResult, TrainCase, PathReport, TrainResult), the error (TrainError), relief (Freedom, MemberFreedom, Figure, Reading, FreedomGroup), load cases (LoadCase, Load, Duty, Turns, CaseLoad, Cycles), Train itself, and solve_train and paths_of. After those come 6,700 lines of tests. `impl Train` blocks sit in mod.rs (×2), conditions.rs (×3), offers.rs, groupings.rs and planetary.rs. `impl Shape` blocks sit in shape.rs (×3), edits.rs, arrangements.rs (×3), graph.rs (×2) and mod.rs. shape.rs:338-2360 is one impl mixing topology queries, helix readings, groups, the closure plan, the search and building. shape.rs imports 13 names from super (mod.rs), and mod.rs reaches back into shape, so the two are one unit split arbitrarily.
evidence: Top-level item listing of mod.rs (grep of pub struct/enum/impl). census.py counts: mod.rs 98 pub items and 196 pub fields, shape.rs 34 and 56. crossed.rs has 13 code lines and 1,829 test lines.
proposal:
Proposed layout for train/:
- model/ (inputs only): shape.rs with Axis, BodyOn, Member, MeshInput, Distance, Shape; train.rs with Train, LoadCase, Load, Duty, MemberGear, FaceSources.
- topology/: graph.rs (parts), wiring.rs, groupings.rs, names.rs (member_names), and components.rs (one union-find).
- solve/: plan.rs, search.rs, build.rs, cut.rs, flow.rs, size.rs, rate.rs, paths.rs, and mod.rs holding solve_train.
- report.rs: every *Report and *Result type.
- relief.rs
- error.rs
- edit/: edits.rs, offers.rs, preview.rs, the train-level edits from conditions.rs, arrangements.rs and defaults.rs.
- tests/: by topic (motion, flow, relief, edits, rating, presets).

Move the tests first, which is purely mechanical, then the types. Nothing changes in behaviour, and ts-rs export_to paths are explicit, so web/src/wire does not move.
validation: Every step is behaviour-neutral: nextest, clippy, check_golden, check_bindings (no diff) and check_doc_links (update CLAUDE.md's map in the same commit).

verdict.reason: The inventory holds as stated. train/mod.rs has production code up to its #[cfg(test)] at line 4639 and 6,724 lines of tests after it (11,363 lines in all). It defines report, rating, input, result, error, relief and load-case types, plus Train, solve_train and paths_of. `impl Train` blocks sit in mod.rs (x2), conditions.rs (x3), groupings.rs, offers.rs and planetary.rs. `impl Shape` blocks sit in shape.rs (x3, one running from 338 to about 2360), arrangements.rs (x3), graph.rs (x2), edits.rs and mod.rs:2241. shape.rs imports from super at lines 39-42, and mod.rs re-exports shape and refers to shape:: types in its reports. That is a real cycle. crossed.rs has 13 non-comment lines before its tests at 139, and 1,829 test lines. One small error: shape.rs imports 14 names from super, not 13. The cost is navigation and review in an 11k-line file, not correctness. CLAUDE.md's map exists precisely to offset it, which shows the cost is real.
verdict.evidence: wc -l train/*.rs: mod.rs 11363, shape.rs 6262, crossed.rs 1968. grep '^#[cfg(test)]' puts mod.rs:4639 and crossed.rs:139. The impl listings are as above. shape.rs:39-42 is `use super::{ContactRatios, Freedom, FreedomGroup, GearResult, Loading, MemberFacts, MemberFreedom, MemberGear, MemberRating, MeshReport, Ports, Reading, TrainError, PROBE}`. Only 10 path references to train/*.rs exist across docs, tools and web, so the move cost outside the crate is mostly CLAUDE.md's map. ts-rs uses export_to = "core/" (79 occurrences), so moving files leaves web/src/wire unchanged.
verdict.proposal_note: Doing the test move first is right, and it is cheap: #[cfg(test)] submodules like train/tests/{motion,flow,relief,edits,rating,presets}.rs keep access to private items, whereas integration tests under crates/*/tests would lose it. The split between model, topology and solve does not by itself break the shape.rs↔mod.rs cycle. The cycle goes only if the report and rating types (MeshReport, GearResult, MemberRating, Bending) move into a report.rs that both shape's solve and mod.rs depend on. Do that first among the type moves. crossed.rs should become a test module next to the screw tests, with `proportions` moved to screw.rs or arrangements.rs. Update CLAUDE.md's per-file table in the same commit, because it names these files as the map.

title: The flow and exact kinematics run over the whole train's meshes although the train already decomposes into parts
claim: solve_parts concatenates every part's meshes and couplings into one MeshFlow list and runs flow::solve once per case over all of them (2^M direction assignments). The exact kinematic system is likewise assembled over all bodies at once. Parts are defined as the pieces that close apart, and in a chain they touch only at shared bodies. Solving per part, or per block of parts that share more than one body, and composing through the shared bodies would bound the flow at Σ2^{M_k} instead of 2^{ΣM}, and would keep the exact rationals at one part's size. This is the architectural root of two findings kinematics-flow has already reported (i128 overflow on a 9-pair chain, and the unbounded 2^M search that wraps at M ≥ 32).
evidence: Probe timing (release build) for n chained spur presets: n=1 0.13 ms; n=4 0.9 ms; n=8 7.7 ms (256 assignments). At n=9 the case is refused as train.case_underdetermined with short="0", although Train::motion() at n=9 succeeds with exact speeds (−17/43, 289/1849, …). The flow loop is `for assignment in 0..(1u32 << m)` over every mesh and every coupling (couplings are pushed into the same list).
proposal: Build a block graph: nodes are parts, edges are shared bodies. Where a part meets the rest through one body (a cut vertex), solve its motion as a ratio against that body and its flow given that body's torque, then propagate along the tree. Only biconnected blocks (split-power loops) need a joint solve. Within a block, keep the current 2^M enumeration, and refuse with a named note above a documented M_max instead of wrapping.
validation: Reproduce every figure the kinematics fixtures and `gear-cli kinematics`/`graph` print (golden, zero diff). A chain of 30 spur pairs solves in under 5 ms with the exact ratio (43/17)^30. Pennestrì's η₀^w law still holds on every arrangement.

verdict.reason: Two parts of the claim hold. The flow enumerates 2^M over every mesh and coupling of the whole train (flow.rs:223 `for assignment in 0..(1u32 << m)`; mod.rs pushes every part's meshes and then every coupling into one list). The timings reproduce: n=1 0.14 ms, n=4 0.83 ms, n=8 7.73 ms. The claim fails on the other part. Whole-train assembly is not the root of the n=9 overflow. With the same whole-train System, `motion` (conditions absorbed in body order) solves n=9 and n=12 exactly, and it is `motion_in(&c, &[driver])`, the driver-first order solve_parts uses, that overflows. The overflow is intermediate growth: Ratio::checked_add cross-multiplies denominators without a gcd, and the elimination order matters. The exact answer (43/17)^n fits i128 up to n≈23, and body-order motion still overflows from n=16. So the kinematics half is an elimination and Ratio problem that kinematics-flow 0/9 and primitives 3 already locate precisely. The flow half is already reported with a better remedy (kinematics-flow 1, lens-unification 6, lens-performance 0). As an architectural observation, per-part composition is a valid but secondary route.
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-lens-architecture-2, release build, n chained pair([17,43]), ultimate case at chain_ends. Output: n=9 'solved=false notes=[train.case_underdetermined short=0]'; sys.motion(&c) → Ok(-0.000235952287559495 = -(17/43)^9) while sys.motion_in(&c,&[1]) → Err(Overflow); n=12 motion Ok(1.458e-5) / motion_in Overflow; n=16 both Overflow although 43^16 ≈ 1.3e26 < i128::MAX ≈ 1.7e38. solve_parts at mod.rs:4431-4455 maps a non-unique or erroring motion_in to `determined=false` and the note 'short=0'.
verdict.corrected_claim: The power flow's 2^M enumeration spans the whole train's meshes and couplings although parts are separable, which is already reported elsewhere. The i128 overflow at nine chained pairs does not come from assembling the whole train: the same whole-train system solves in body order and fails only in the driver-first order. Its cause is elimination order together with Ratio::checked_add growing without a gcd, and per-part solving is not needed to fix it.
verdict.proposal_note: The validation target cannot be met: (43/17)^30 has a 49-digit numerator (43^30 ≈ 1e49), beyond i128. No exact solve, per-part or not, can print it in the current Ratio type. Cheaper fixes come first: (1) name Refusal::Overflow instead of reporting 'underdetermined short=0'; (2) reduce by gcd in Ratio::checked_add/mul, and absorb unit condition rows before structural rows; (3) take mesh directions from the lossless flow's power signs and enumerate only the meshes that can lock or carry near-zero power (the fixed-point route in kinematics-flow 1 / lens-performance 0). That removes the exponential cost without a block-cut tree. Also leave lossless couplings out of the enumeration entirely. Decomposing into a block graph remains worth doing only if the fixed point proves insufficient on split-power loops.

title: The 'one seam' between line/point contact and rack/ring members leaks: 37 kind dispatches in shape.rs; a bevel pair would touch them all
claim: BuiltContact's doc says 'every question the solve asks of a mesh is answered here, once per model, and nothing above needs to know which it is holding'. Yet the rest of shape.rs dispatches on the model repeatedly: `.line()`, `BuiltContact::Line/Point`, `BuiltMember::Ring/Rack` and `ring.is_some()` appear in 37 production lines, about 20 of them outside the two enums' own impls. Examples: rate's report assembly (match &bm.contact → line_mesh_report or point_mesh_report), the worm recommendations in cut, bending only on line meshes, and on_a_line. BuiltMember duplicates the ToothOutline seam strength.rs already has for Tooth and Ring. Adding a bevel (intersecting axes) or a hypoid would mean a third variant in both enums and edits at every site.
proposal: Replace BuiltContact with `trait ContactModel { fn nominal(&self)->f64; fn efficiency(&self, a:&dyn ToothForm, mu, face)->Directional<f64>; fn play(&self, …); fn rate(&self, case:&CaseLoad, widths)->ContactPatch; fn sizes_face(&self)->bool; fn report(&self, …)->MeshContact }`, implemented for LineBuilt and PointBuilt. Replace BuiltMember with the ToothOutline/ToothForm trait, implemented by Tooth and Ring (as strength already does). Put the worm proportions behind `ContactModel::recommended_face`.
validation: Behaviour-neutral: golden, check_wasm and nextest with zero diff. Measure that kind-dispatch sites outside model impls drop to near zero. Adding a stub third model should compile by implementing the trait alone.

verdict.reason: The doc claim on BuiltContact (shape.rs:2434-2438: 'every question the solve asks of a mesh is answered here, once per model, and nothing above needs to know which it is holding') is false. The contact model is dispatched outside the enum's own impl at about 11 sites: the search trial at 2251/2259, the worm-width recommendation at 3153, bending only on line contacts at 3214, contact stress at 3305, point contact at 3337, the overlap floor at 3445, play at 3524/3537 and the report at 3813/3856. BuiltMember is dispatched outside its impl at 2219/2220, 3683, 3716 and 3843. The 37-line count mixes in `Member.ring.is_some()` on inputs (473, 474, 741, 1120, 1135, 1769, 4181) and construction sites (2803/2807, 2892/2911). Those are not leaks of the built-model seam. The claim that BuiltMember 'duplicates ToothOutline' is wrong: BuiltMember::bending already routes through ToothOutline (Bending::of(tooth…) / Bending::of(ring.as_ref()…)). Its other methods (as_gear, tip_radius, flank_ends, clamps, and the ring-specific reports) are questions ToothOutline does not ask.
verdict.evidence: sed shape.rs 2360-2500 shows BuiltMember/BuiltContact and their impls. The grep for `.line()|BuiltContact::(Line|Point)|BuiltMember::(Ring|Rack)|ring.is_some()` over lines 1-4189 lists the sites above. strength.rs has `impl ToothOutline for Tooth` (508) and `for crate::ring::Ring` (573). BuiltMember::bending calls super::Bending::of on each.
verdict.corrected_claim: BuiltContact's doc says nothing above the enum needs to know which contact model it holds, but about 11 sites in cut/rate (the search trial, bending, contact stress, point rating, overlap floor, play, report and worm width) match on it directly. BuiltMember has about 5 such sites. The seam is real but leaky. BuiltMember does not duplicate ToothOutline.
verdict.proposal_note: For a closed set of two or three models, a Rust enum with methods is as extensible as a trait. A bevel variant would have to implement every method either way, and a `dyn ContactModel` adds indirection and boxing for no gain. The cheaper fix is to move each out-of-impl match into a method on BuiltContact/BuiltMesh, such as play(), bending_contact_ratio() -> Option, contact_stress(), rate_point(), overlap_floor(), report() and recommended_face(). Then either make the doc true or reword it to say where the models differ by decision (no bending on a point contact). Do not replace BuiltMember with ToothOutline: the search's Cut::ByShaper and the ring-only reports genuinely need the Ring.

title: The TOML document is the internal struct's serde, unversioned; ~20 breaking changes are migrations in prose only
claim: TrainDocument is { name, train: gear_core::train::Train }, so any rename or move inside the core is a file-format break. The module doc lists about 20 breaking changes as hand-editing instructions ('Rename the field and add static_friction = 0.16…') over roughly 230 lines. There is no `format`/`version` field, so a reader cannot tell which instructions apply to a file. Only one migration (stages to graph) is automated (`convert`). The doc also says 'No compatibility shim, deliberately', while the core types carry 36 serde(default)/deserialize_with shims (such as ground_if_null for browser state that wrote null).
evidence: grep -c 'serde(default|deserialize_with' across gear-core gives 36 occurrences (shape.rs 10, mod.rs 16, …). grep for 'version' or 'format' in gear-io/src/train.rs finds no field. The same types are exported to TypeScript (79 ts-rs exports in web/src/wire/core), so one struct is three contracts: internal model, wire and file.
proposal: Add `format = N` to the document header. Write migrations as `fn migrate_vN(toml::Value) -> toml::Value`, applied in sequence on import (convert becomes one of them). Move the change log out of the module doc into docs/format.md, which describes only the current schema, with history moved to docs/history. Over time, give the document its own DTO in gear-io so core refactors stop being format changes.
validation: A corpus of one saved file per historical format, each importing to the train it meant, with figures equal to what `convert` produces today. `a_field_the_shape_no_longer_has_is_refused_and_named` still holds for the current version.

verdict.reason: TrainDocument is `{ name: String, train: gear_core::train::Train }` (gear-io/src/train.rs:298-302), with no version or format field. The module doc runs 233 lines from line 22 to 254 and holds 25 bullet-point change entries, most of them hand-migration instructions. It still opens with 'Two changes so far', which is stale. 'No compatibility shim, deliberately' (line 255) is contradicted by shims such as ground_if_null (shape.rs:118-124, 'as a browser's stored train wrote it while it was an Option'). The evidence count is overstated: gear-core carries 23 serde(default)/deserialize_with attributes (params 2, auto 2, material 1, train/mod.rs 9, train/shape.rs 9), not 36. The substance holds. A further point strengthens it: `convert` deserialises old staged files as `stages: Vec<Shape>`, the live Shape type (train.rs:395-403). The only automated migration is therefore itself coupled to the current internal struct, and the next Shape change will break it. The fixture test a_file_written_as_stages_is_refused_by_name_and_converts will catch that, but the remedy it forces is editing the old fixture, which defeats it, or freezing a copy of Shape.
verdict.evidence: gear-io/src/train.rs:298 is `pub struct TrainDocument { pub name: String, pub train: Train }`. `grep -c '^//! - '` over lines 22-254 gives 25. Line 27 reads 'Two changes so far:'. Lines 395-403 are `struct Staged { ... stages: Vec<Shape>, ...}`. grep of gear-core for `serde(default|deserialize_with` gives 23 lines. Related, already reported: gear-io 8 (defaults read old files through live constants), lens-docs-clarity 5 / ablate-features 10 (the 250-line change log), ablate-features 11 (shims).
verdict.proposal_note: The cheap, high-value part is `format = N` in the header, plus a refusal that names the version and points at `gear-cli convert`. Also move the change log out of the module doc; it duplicates other findings, so do it once. A full chain of toml::Value migrations for 25 historical formats is poor value for a tool with no installed base of files, and the owner's refuse-loudly stance is sound for the historical ones. Apply migrations only from the version field onward. To stop core refactors from being format breaks, freeze a small DTO for the staged format that `convert` reads, instead of reading the live Shape. Only then consider a document DTO for the current format.

title: Three records of one gear's inputs and three result pipelines (gear tab, ring tab, train member)
claim:
The same gear is described three ways:
- The gear tab uses GearParams (module, pressure angle, teeth, shift, helix, addendum, dedendum, root radius, k, angular shift, index offset) plus GearRequest extras, summarised into GearSummary.
- The ring tab uses GearParams plus CutterRef, summarised into RingSummary.
- A train member splits the same inputs over Member (module, pressure angle, k, ring cutter, pitch diameter) and MemberGear (teeth, shift, helix, addendum, dedendum, root radius, face, material), reported as GearResult.

As a result, the eccentric gear exists only on the gear tab, the ring's figures are computed twice (RingSummary against the train's ring handling), and adopt_member is a converter between the representations. Rule 4 ('a ring is a gear with a negative tooth count') is honoured in the mesh sign but not in the input or result types.
evidence: wasm solve_ring_impl builds RingSummary field by field from Ring. solve_gear_impl builds GearSummary via summarise() (about 130 lines). The train path builds GearResult in shape::rate. Member.ring: Option<Cutter> is the internal flag.
proposal: Converge on one `GearInputs` (the MemberGear fields plus module, pressure angle, k and cutter, each Auto where the train needs it, plus angular_shift and index_offset). Make the gear tab a one-member Shape, or a two-member Shape when a mate is given, solved by the train pipeline. GearSummary and RingSummary become projections of GearResult, which adds span, pins and tolerance. Retire solve_ring, ring_profile and export_ring_dxf into the gear entry points.
validation: A law: for every preset member, the gear tab's summary of adopt_member(member) equals the train's GearResult for it. The wasm answers recorded by check_wasm for the gear and ring tabs are reproduced.

verdict.reason: The 'three records' framing overstates the problem. GearParams is the one resolved record: the train resolves Member+MemberGear into GearParams and cuts with the same Tooth/Ring the tabs use (GearResult.params: GearParams; adopt_member returns result.members[i].params). Member/MemberGear differ legitimately: they carry Auto toggles and group roles (module and pressure angle stated once per mesh group, k per mesh) that a lone gear has no use for. The ring's figures are not 'computed twice' either: solve_ring_impl projects core Ring fields, and the train does not report them. What does hold is narrower. Rule 4 is broken at the boundary: the gear and the ring are two request types (GearRequest / RingRequest, both built on GearParams, the ring adding CutterRef), two summaries (GearSummary / RingSummary) and three pairs of entry points (solve_gear/solve_ring, gear_profile/ring_profile, export_dxf/export_ring_dxf), where the train's own input marks a ring as `Member.ring: Option<Cutter>`. The eccentric gear being gear-tab-only is a feature boundary, not a duplication.
verdict.evidence: gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:32 GearRequest { params: GearParams, pin_diameter, tolerance_class, chord_tolerance, reference_circles, working_depth, mate, eccentric_throw }; lib.rs:443 RingRequest { params: GearParams, pin_diameter, cutter: CutterRef, chord_tolerance, reference_circles }; solve_ring_impl at lib.rs:567-603 copies Ring fields into RingSummary. shape.rs Member has `pub ring: Option<Cutter>`. adopt_member_impl at lib.rs:1378-1420 returns `params: result.members[req.member].params` and the cutter. It converts nothing and only reads what the train already resolved.
verdict.corrected_claim: The gear and ring tabs are two parallel boundary pipelines over one GearParams: two requests, two summaries and three pairs of entry points. The train's own input marks a ring as an optional cutter on the same record. The train's Member/MemberGear is not a third copy; it is the Auto-toggled input form of GearParams.
verdict.proposal_note: Making the gear tab a one-member Shape solved by solve_train is overreach. The train pipeline needs materials and load cases, rates stresses the tab does not show, and cannot hold the tab's eccentric gear (angular_shift/index_offset). The smaller step removes the actual duplication: add `cutter: Option<CutterRef>` to GearRequest and one GearSummary with the ring-only fields optional (generation_limit, rim_radius, between_pins in place of over_two/three_pins), then retire solve_ring, ring_profile and export_ring_dxf (23 → 20 entry points, with the probe and web updated). The proposed law (adopt_member's params give the tab's summary equal to the train's GearResult) is a good addition either way.

title: Five hand-rolled union-find / connected-component routines
claim: graph_of, Shape::parts, mesh_groups, asking_members and search_components each write their own `find` and `union`, with three different path-compression variants (none, one-step, full). mesh_groups then groups in O(n²) by re-finding each group's root.
evidence: Code read at the listed lines.
proposal: Add one `DisjointSets` (new, union, find with full compression, components() -> Vec<Vec<usize>> in first-member order) in train/topology/components.rs, and use it at all five sites.
validation: A law over every preset, plus the graph harness's every-preset-after-every-other: parts, mesh_groups and search_components are identical before and after. Golden has zero diff.

verdict.reason: There are five hand-written disjoint-set routines: graph.rs:64 (one-step compression, graph_of over axes), graph.rs:234 (one-step, Shape::parts over members), shape.rs:1090 (no compression, a closure over &Vec, mesh_groups with union by min index), shape.rs:1996 (no compression, asking_members over meshes) and shape.rs:2060 (full compression, search_components over meshes plus axes). asking_members and search_components union the same relation (meshes on each automatic distance, plan.held[d].is_none()), so the same components are computed twice. mesh_groups regroups by calling find on each existing group's first member, which is O(n·groups). That is immaterial at train sizes, so the point is duplication, not speed. Partly reported before (shape-a 15: three in one file; auto-search 15: two).
verdict.evidence: Code read at graph.rs:55-100, graph.rs:225-260, shape.rs:1080-1110, shape.rs:1985-2020 and shape.rs:2050-2100. The compression variants are `parent[i] = r` (graph.rs), none (shape.rs:1090, 1996) and the full path loop (shape.rs:2066-2070).
verdict.proposal_note: A single DisjointSets is right. Its components() must return groups in first-member order, because parts, mesh_groups and every index the panel reads depend on that ordering; say so in its doc and hold it with the proposed before/after law. asking_members should consume search_components' (or a shared) mesh partition rather than rebuilding it. The new type fits in graph.rs or a small train/components.rs; the finding-6 directory layout is not required first.

title: TipRoom (pure ring geometry) lives in train/mod.rs and auto.rs reaches up into train for it
claim: TipRoom::at wraps ring::mesh_at, a ring, a pinion and a running distance. It knows nothing of trains. It is defined in train/mod.rs, and auto.rs (which CLAUDE.md says does not know what a shape is) calls crate::train::TipRoom. That is the only production dependency from a lower module into train/.
evidence: A code-only fan-out scan (comments stripped, test modules cut) finds auto→train as the single upward edge, at auto.rs:628.
proposal: Move TipRoom into ring.rs next to mesh_at, and re-export it from train for the report type.
validation: Compiles unchanged, check_bindings shows no diff (export_to explicit), golden has zero diff.

verdict.reason: Holds as stated, but the cited line is wrong. The only production upward edge from a lower gear-core module into train/ is auto.rs:1332 (`crate::train::TipRoom::at(ring, tooth, self.mesh.a_w).is_some_and(|t| t.tips_clear())` in MeshTrial::tips_are_clear), plus one use in auto.rs's test module at :2117. It is not at auto.rs:628, where admissible_angular_shift sits. TipRoom::at (train/mod.rs:579-589) is a thin map of ring::mesh_at, and tips_clear() is just `!self.tip_interference`, a copy of RingMesh::tip_interference.
verdict.evidence: A grep for `(crate|super)::train` in gear-core/src/*.rs (not train/) finds only auto.rs:1332 and 2117 as code; planetary.rs's matches are doc comments. train/mod.rs:546-605 defines TipRoom, and at() calls crate::ring::mesh_at. auto.rs:1932 opens the test module, so 2117 is test-only.
verdict.proposal_note: Moving TipRoom into ring.rs is fine: the ts-rs file name does not change. Its doc links to MeshReport::flank_interference and shape::Distance::tip_clearance would need the crate::train:: prefix. An even smaller fix gives the same answer: auto.rs can ask `crate::ring::mesh_at(ring, tooth, a_w).is_some_and(|m| !m.tip_interference)`, which is the same bit from the same function. The comment's point that the reader and the constraint must agree still holds, because both read RingMesh.

title: wasm surface: 23 hand-written entry points, each an _impl + JsError wrapper, mirrored by 23 hand-written try/catch wrappers in core.ts
claim: Each operation costs a Rust request struct, an _impl, a #[wasm_bindgen] wrapper, a line in tools/wasm_boundary.json, a probe step and a core.ts wrapper with its own error convention. Most take a train, sometimes a library, and return JSON, and several re-send the whole train and library for one question: relieve then solve on every change, offers asked twice per selection (Offers.svelte filters adds and verbs client-side).
evidence: lib.rs lines 723-1663: 23 wrappers. core.ts lines 518-863 has 20 wrappers, with the try/catch repeated in each.
proposal: Use one `#[wasm_bindgen] fn call(request: &str) -> String` over a serde-tagged `enum Request { SolveGear(GearRequest), SolveTrain(TrainRequest), EditTrain(..), … }` returning `{ok}|{refused}`. ts-rs generates the Request and Response unions, and core.ts has one `call<K>()`. Keep separate typed endpoints only for the Float64Array profiles. wasm_boundary.json and the probe list can then be generated from the enum.
validation: check_wasm still asserts that optimisation changes no answer, and records the same answers per request kind. The probe fails on a Request variant with no probe case.

verdict.corrected_claim: The counts and the repeated per-wrapper error handling hold, and the error conventions really do diverge. The costs attributed to hand-written wrappers mostly do not come from them. Re-sending the train and library is a consequence of rule 3 (pure calls, inputs are the only state), and a single dispatch function would not change it. The real, cheap-to-fix waste is that offers are computed twice per selected piece.
verdict.reason: lib.rs has 23 #[wasm_bindgen] items and core.ts has 19 catch blocks, with at least five error conventions: {ok}|{error}, null (profile, previewEdit), [] (offersAt), silent return (relieveTrain, relieveCase), and editTrain telling a refusal apart from a defect by `message.startsWith("ui.")` on a JsError string (core.ts:817-829). That last one is the real smell: a refusal travels as an exception message, not as a typed value. The offers duplication is real. TrainPanel.svelte:2173 and :2177 mount two <Offers> components over the same selected pieces, and each calls offersAt(train, g.target) and then filters adds against verbs client-side (Offers.svelte:46). Each call tries every edit on a copy, which lens-performance measured at 0.3-3 ms per piece. A tagged Request enum is a matter of taste. It would unify the error convention, but it does not remove the round-trips the finding cites.
verdict.evidence: `grep -c '#\[wasm_bindgen' crates/gear-wasm/src/lib.rs` gives 23. `grep -n catch web/src/core.ts | wc -l` gives 19. core.ts:817-829 shows editTrain's prefix test. TrainPanel.svelte:2173/2177 and Offers.svelte:41-49 show the double call. notes/lens-performance/offers.txt: offers over every member+body on a six-part chain totals 52 ms.
verdict.proposal_note: Do the two concrete fixes first; they are independent of the dispatch redesign. (1) Return a typed `{ok}|{refused: key}` from edit_train rather than a JsError whose message starts with 'ui.'. (2) Call offersAt once per selection in TrainPanel and hand both Offers strips the partitioned list. After that, a single `call(request)` entry is optional. It must keep check_wasm's per-entry probe coverage by making the probe exhaustive over the Request enum.

title: Part/slot lookups rebuild every part; a duplicated `_of(parts)` API exists to avoid it; `member()` panics
claim: Train::port, slot, member, ends_of, part_shapes and others each call self.parts(), which clones a sub-Shape per part, to answer a single index lookup. The parallel `motion_of(parts)`/`bodies_of(parts)` forms exist so that a caller holding the parts avoids recomputing them. `member(part, i)` indexes with `[]` and panics on a bad index in a pub API.
evidence: conditions.rs has 14 parts() calls; solve_parts, groupings and edits call it again.
proposal: Make parts a cached derived view built once per solve or edit (`struct Partition { parts, body_to_slots }`), passed explicitly. Parts become index sets over the train's shape instead of cloned shapes, which removes the slot/body translation. Return Option from member().
validation: Behaviour-neutral: golden and nextest. A micro-benchmark of offers() on a large train.

verdict.corrected_claim: The lookups do rebuild the parts, but the cost is immaterial. There are only two `_of(parts)` forms, both pub(crate). member() panics on a bad index exactly as slice indexing does.
verdict.reason: I timed Train::parts() in a probe against solve_train on Preset::ALL chains. parts() costs 0.3 us / 1.7 us / 6.9 us for 1 / 3 / 6 parts, against a solve of 82 us / 2.6 ms / 25 ms, so at most about 0.03% of a solve. The performance motive does not hold. The duplicated API is motion_of and bodies_of (conditions.rs:487, :833), both pub(crate); ends_of does not take parts. port, slot and member are fixture and harness lookups (gear-cli kinematics.rs, tests). member()'s `[]` panic is a documented fixture helper and behaves like indexing, but an Option would be more honest in a pub API. Turning parts into index sets over the shape is a large redesign that nothing measured justifies.
verdict.evidence: Probe verify-lens-architecture-3 (release): `n=1 parts() 0.3 us solve_train 82 us`, `n=3 parts() 1.7 us solve_train 2591 us`, `n=6 parts() 6.9 us solve_train 25192 us`. conditions.rs:211-246 holds port/slot/member. `grep -n 'fn [a-z_]*_of(' conditions.rs` finds ends_of(body), motion_of(parts) and bodies_of(parts).
verdict.proposal_note: Drop the Partition/index-set redesign. If anything, make member() return Option<usize> (or document the panic). The `_of` pairs can stay; they cost two one-line forwarders.

title: About 137 of 384 pub functions in gear-core are used only inside gear-core; odd shims like `index_pub`
claim: Every gear-core module is `pub mod`, and roughly a third of the pub functions are never referenced from gear-io, gear-wasm, gear-cli or the integration tests. The largest counts: mesh 16/26, auto 16/30, screw 16/26, train/mod 13/55, ratio 11/15, contact 8/21. PlanetaryShaft::index_pub is a pub alias of a private `index()` and is used only by tests.
evidence: A name-reference scan of pub fn names in gear-core against the text of the other crates and tests/. This is textual, so a few may be false positives.
proposal: Make the internal-only functions pub(crate), make `index` pub and delete `index_pub`, and turn on `unreachable_pub` as a warning in gear-core.
validation: cargo check of the whole workspace and `cargo doc`. A smaller pub surface is visible in `cargo public-api` if it is available.

verdict.corrected_claim: The counts reproduce, and index_pub is a dead shim used only from test code. The proposed `unreachable_pub` lint would not catch any of these functions, because every gear-core module is `pub mod`.
verdict.reason: My independent textual scan (gear-core src with test modules cut, against gear-io, gear-wasm, gear-cli and gear-core/tests) gives 144 of 450 `pub fn`/`pub const fn` unused outside the crate. The per-file figures match the finding exactly (mesh 16/26, auto 16/30, screw 16/26, train/mod 13/55, ratio 11/15, contact 8/21). index_pub (planetary.rs:62-66) is called only at planetary.rs:153-154, inside the #[cfg(test)] fn planet_speed, where the private index() is in scope anyway, and at kinematics.rs:1049 in its test module. rustc's unreachable_pub fires only for pub items not reachable from the crate root, and every item in a `pub mod` is reachable, so the lint stays silent. Several of the 'unused' functions are the natural API of a public type (Ratio's arithmetic, for one), so narrowing them is a style choice, not a defect.
verdict.evidence: planetary.rs:150 `#[cfg(test)]` precedes planet_speed, which uses index_pub at :153-154. kinematics.rs:730 opens the tests, and the use is at :1049. lib.rs:20-47 declares every module `pub mod`. The Python scan printed `450 144` and the per-file table above.
verdict.proposal_note: Delete index_pub. Make the test callers use a `pub(crate) const fn index` (or make index pub). For the wider narrowing, the tool is `cargo public-api` or a manual pass, not unreachable_pub. Keep the pub methods of types the harness or wasm handle.

title: Small API/naming inconsistencies at the crate seams
claim: gear_io::gear_to_dxf takes `&Tooth` but uses only `gear.params`, rebuilding a Gear, plus its four radii. The signature therefore invites the eccentric-as-concentric mistake corrections.md records. gear_io::train::TrainError has the same name as gear_core::train::TrainError, with unrelated meaning. EditRefused::key returns raw 'ui.*' strings instead of note::key constants, unlike every other refusal.
evidence: Code read at the listed lines.
proposal: Change the signature to `gear_to_dxf(&Gear, …)`. Rename the gear-io error to DocumentError. Put the edit-refusal keys in note::key, or into the Refusal channel proposed above.
validation: It compiles, and the DXF round-trip in validate_dxf.py shows no diff.

verdict.corrected_claim: The gear_to_dxf point is stronger than stated: it is an actual wrong output, not just an invitation to one (see the missed finding on eccentric reference circles). The TrainError name clash holds. The EditRefused point is refuted.
verdict.reason: gear_to_dxf (dxf.rs:119-128) draws the outline from Gear::new(gear.params) but the reference circles from the Tooth passed in, and every caller (gear-wasm lib.rs:708, gear-cli main.rs:2621) passes Tooth::new(params). For an eccentric gear, Gear's mean tooth is cut by the gear's common tool (gear.rs:207), so its rf differs from Tooth::new's by up to about 1.5 mm at m = 1 within the admissible Δx range. The DXF therefore disagrees with the panel, which quotes Gear::mean (lib.rs:692). gear_io::train::TrainError (Parse, Serialise) is re-exported at the gear_io root and shares its name with gear_core::train::TrainError, a different type. The EditRefused bullet is wrong on two counts. First, raw 'ui.' literals are the core's convention for interface words: arrangements.rs carries 13 of them for preset labels. Second, tools/check_strings.py scans crates/**/*.rs for such literals, so these keys are already checked against the catalogue. edits.rs:151-153 documents that a refusal is the interface's word, not a Note.
verdict.evidence: dxf.rs:119-128: `&gear_core::gear::Gear::new(gear.params).outline(..)`, `&[gear.r, gear.rb, gear.ra, gear.rf]`. Probe: z=6, x=0.5, Δx=0.8 gives Tooth::new rf=2.250000 and Gear::new(..).mean() rf=2.150000; z=10, x=0.5, Δx=2.225 (the admissible bound) gives a 1.525 mm difference. `grep -c '"ui\.'`: arrangements.rs 13, edits.rs 10. check_strings.py:28 includes `(ROOT / "crates").rglob("*.rs")`.
verdict.proposal_note: Change gear_to_dxf to take &Gear, taking circles from gear.mean() (Gear::mean exists at gear.rs:235), or to take &GearParams and build the Gear inside. Add a test that an eccentric gear's DXF root circle equals the summary's rf. Rename gear-io's error to DocumentError. Leave EditRefused::key as it is.

title: rationale.md says k₂ = 2 − k₁ is 'derived and the invariant is unwritable', but k is stored per member and both may be given
claim: Member.thickness_mod is an Auto on every member. thickness_mods() propagates only from given members to automatic ones and leaves two given members of a mesh as they are. The invariant is therefore writable, and is kept only by relief. Unpaired modification appearing as backlash is itself tested (mesh.rs:1476), so the storage is deliberate and the rationale sentence is stale.
evidence: thickness_mods(): `(Some(a), None)`/`(None, Some(b))` propagate, and `_ => {}` leaves both-given alone.
proposal: Rewrite the rationale paragraph to describe the actual rule: given on at most one member per mesh by relief, propagated along the mesh chain, with both-given read as a deliberate thinning that shows up as backlash.
validation: check_doc_links. The text is reviewed against thickness_mods.

verdict.reason: The rationale sentence is inaccurate, and the reality is worse than the finding says. k is stored per member (shape.rs:177). thickness_mods() propagates only into automatic members and ignores both-given (shape.rs:1060-1069). Relief allows at most one given per mesh (shape.rs:4088-4100), not per mesh group. In a planetary set, the sun and the ring can therefore both stand given after relief, and the planet's k then depends on mesh order, breaking one mesh's invariant silently. That also contradicts the shape.rs:173-176 doc comment ('relief keeps it so') and rationale.md:71-72 ('one stored k fixes all three').
verdict.evidence: Probe: Preset::Planetary, sun k=1.1 given, ring k=1.0 given, relieved(Some(Member(2, ThicknessMod))). The flags come back [given, auto, given] and thickness_mods = [1.1, 0.9, 1.0], so planet-ring = -0.1. With the two meshes swapped, thickness_mods = [1.1, 1.0, 1.0]. solve_train succeeds and emits only part.planets_share_load_equally.
verdict.proposal_note: Do not rewrite the rationale to bless the per-mesh rule; that would document an order-dependent answer. Change the relief group to one `given_at_most: 1` over every member of a mesh group (Shape::mesh_groups, which module and pressure angle already use). The rationale sentence then becomes true, and thickness_mods can never meet two givens in one component. If deliberate thinning on one side is wanted, expose it as its own input (for example a backlash allowance), not as a second k.

title: README claims gear-cli's module comment lists every command; that comment says it no longer does
claim: README tells readers the full command list is in main.rs's module comment. The list was removed from there because it went stale.
evidence: README.md:93-96: "`crates/gear-cli/src/main.rs` has all of them in its own module comment, next to the code. A third copy here was a third thing to keep in step". main.rs:9-13: "The list is [`COMMANDS`], and `help` prints it. It used to be written out here as well ... It had fallen out of step by eight of twenty-one." The story is told again in state.md:106-111.
proposal: Replace README.md:92-96 with one line: "`gear-cli help` lists every subcommand." Cut main.rs:9-13 down to "The command list is [`COMMANDS`]; `gear-cli help` prints it." Keep the one lesson, "a list next to the code is not kept in step by being next to it", as a single corrections.md entry.
validation: grep -n 'module comment' README.md returns nothing; check_doc_links stays green.

verdict.reason: README.md:93-96 still says main.rs 'has all of them in its own module comment'. main.rs:9-13 says the list was taken out of that comment and that `help` prints COMMANDS. state.md:104-111 tells the same story a third time. The claim holds as stated. It is a stale pointer, though, not a wrong number, so low rather than medium.
verdict.evidence: README.md:93-94: "`crates/gear-cli/src/main.rs` has all of them in its own module comment, next to the code." main.rs:9: "**The list is [`COMMANDS`], and `help` prints it.** It used to be written out here as well". state.md:106: "That was not always true. This paragraph used to name the harness's module comment instead".
verdict.proposal_note: The proposal is sound. Keep the 'proximity is not a mechanism' lesson in one place only: corrections.md, or the CLAUDE.md check-table rationale. Right now it appears in main.rs and state.md as well.

title: Three contradictory 'what to run before pushing' lists (README, state.md, CLAUDE.md)
claim: The three documents disagree about what CI runs and what to run before pushing.
evidence: README.md:73: `nix flake check  # everything CI checks: build, clippy, fmt, tests`. state.md:39: "`nix flake check` is not all of what CI runs", then state.md:44-45 "Before pushing, run all four." (its checks list omits check_units, check_wasm and validate_dxf). CLAUDE.md:179: "Before pushing, run everything the table marks \"yes\" — not a chosen subset", which is 13 checks. ci.yml runs check_units (line 95), check_wasm (105) and validate_dxf (111), none of which state.md lists.
proposal: Keep one list: CLAUDE.md's checks table, or better, a tools/check_all.sh that runs every CI step and that ci.yml also calls, so the list and CI cannot drift. README gets one line ("`tools/check_all.sh` runs what CI runs"). state.md 'Running it' drops its checks block and the "run all four" sentence. Delete the README comment "everything CI checks".
validation: A test or script diffs the `run:` steps in ci.yml against check_all.sh; grep 'run all four' returns nothing.

verdict.reason: Checked against ci.yml. It runs flake check, nix build .#web, check_doc_links, check_strings, check_bindings, npm run check, golden+figures, check_units, check_wasm and validate_dxf. README.md:73 calls `nix flake check` 'everything CI checks'. state.md:39-45 says it is not, then says 'run all four', and its checks block leaves out check_units, check_wasm and validate_dxf. CLAUDE.md:179 says to run all 13. That makes three disagreeing answers, and CLAUDE.md itself records two red builds from exactly this kind of drift.
verdict.evidence: ci.yml run steps at lines 39, 44, 51, 56, 62, 67, 82 (check_golden + check_figures), 95 (check_units), 105 (check_wasm), 111 (validate_dxf with --root 7.45 --tip 9.7 --base ... --teeth 17). state.md:48-58 lists bindings, doc_links, strings, golden, figures and npm check only.
verdict.proposal_note: A single tools/check_all.sh that ci.yml calls is the right mechanism. It has to carry validate_dxf's arguments, because CLAUDE.md's table gives `python3 tools/validate_dxf.py` with no arguments and that command is not runnable as written. It should also write to the cache dir rather than /tmp/gear17.dxf. CI splits steps for readable logs, so ci.yml can call check_all.sh per step (e.g. `check_all.sh units`) rather than as one monolith.

title: README's 'Nothing appears in two of them' is false; systematic restatement across README/CLAUDE.md/docs/code
claim: The same fact is written in 2-5 places, which is exactly the pattern corrections.md:26 ('One idea written down twice') says goes stale.
evidence:
Measured pairs:
- The four tooth.rs cautions: README.md:150-172 and CLAUDE.md:221-232.
- The Hertz half-space argument with the same numbers ('ρ₁ = ρ₂ = 10 and ρ₁ = 5.5, ρ₂ = 55 are the same contact'): rationale.md:1291 and strength.rs:1718, near verbatim. The 'ρ₁+ρ₂ is constant' step also appears at strength.rs:1724, strength.rs:1812 and reference.md:1177.
- The drive/coast mirror-image argument: mesh.rs:375 and rationale.md:1123.
- Layout tables: README.md:59-69, state.md:257-282 and CLAUDE.md:120-131.
- Standing rule 1: README.md:13-18, CLAUDE.md:44-47 and rationale.md:22.
- The crossed ε=1.777921670 / 1.758113579 comparison: README.md:203-216 and state.md:185-190.
- The 'nix flake check is not all' warning: state.md:39 and CLAUDE.md:160.
- 'Proximity is not a mechanism': state.md and main.rs twice.
proposal: Adopt the one-home rule below. Delete README's Layout, 'Notes for anyone changing the geometry' and 'Verification tooling' sections (their homes are CLAUDE.md and state.md). Delete state.md's Layout table (the map is CLAUDE.md). In code, keep each derivation once in reference.md, with the doc comment linking to its anchor (for example strength.rs:1711-1733 becomes two lines and a link to rationale.md#one-pressure-two-ratings...). Remove the ε comparison from README and keep it in state.md.
validation: A script tokenises sentences of ≥12 words across README, CLAUDE.md, docs/*.md and //, /// comments and reports near-duplicates (for example Jaccard over 5-grams >0.6). The count should go to about zero.

verdict.reason: The duplication is real and in places near verbatim. strength.rs:1714-1726 and rationale.md:1288-1296 share the 'ρ₁ = ρ₂ = 10 and ρ₁ = 5.5, ρ₂ = 55 are the same contact' passage almost word for word. The 'ρ₁+ρ₂ is constant' step appears in reference.md:1177, rationale.md:1296, strength.rs:1724 and strength.rs:1812. The four tooth.rs cautions are in both README:150-172 and CLAUDE.md:221-232. The ε comparison is in both README:203-216 and state.md:185-190. The layout tables are in README, state.md and CLAUDE.md. But the title overreaches. README:25 ('Nothing appears in two of them') and reference.md:10 speak only of the four docs/ documents. Most pairs cited involve README, CLAUDE.md or code comments, and those do not falsify that sentence. The only pairs that do falsify it are the ones inside the four docs, e.g. reference.md:1177 against rationale.md:1296 ('ρ₁+ρ₂ constant … peaks where equal … falls toward both ends'). Some code-to-doc duplication is also deliberate: CLAUDE.md treats the 1:1 prose:code ratio and the why-beside-the-code as the source of auditability.
verdict.evidence: Read strength.rs:1711-1733, rationale.md:1284-1298, reference.md:1176-1181, README.md:150-216, state.md:180-190 and 257-282, mesh.rs:373-379 and rationale.md:1123-1126. The mirror-image argument is near verbatim in the last pair.
verdict.corrected_claim: The same argument is often written in 2-4 places: README against CLAUDE.md or state.md, code doc comment against rationale.md, and in at least one case between two of the four docs (reference.md:1177 / rationale.md:1296). That last case makes the 'Nothing appears in two of them' sentence literally false. The README/CLAUDE.md/state.md restatements are the maintenance risk that corrections.md's 'one idea written down twice' names.
verdict.proposal_note: Deleting the README Layout section, the 'Notes for anyone changing the geometry' section and the Verification tooling section, plus state.md's layout table, is low risk. Cutting code derivations down to a link is less clear-cut. The strength.rs doc comment is where a maintainer changing contact rating reads, so prefer keeping the code copy short, one sentence plus a link, over deleting it. The proposed Jaccard 'count goes to about zero' target will flag legitimate short restatements, so use it as a warn-only aid, not a gate.

title: History narrated inside living text: 202 production comment lines, 14 'this paragraph used to say' passages
claim: Comments and living documents often describe what the code or text used to be, not what it is. That belongs to git and corrections.md.
evidence: hist.py over production code (test modules excluded): 13,861 comment lines, 202 with a history marker, concentrated in train/mod.rs (30), strength.rs (23) and auto.rs (21). Each marker usually opens a multi-line story, which puts the history share at roughly 6-9% of production comment. The 'three functions in TypeScript, one per stage type' story alone appears at mod.rs:2164, mod.rs:2306, gear-wasm lib.rs:1433, core.ts:655 and TrainPanel.svelte:51. Self-referential passages include CLAUDE.md:14 ('The first version of this paragraph said 1.5 to 1'), CLAUDE.md:182 ('the second red build this paragraph has cost'), state.md:106, 157 and 261 ('This paragraph used to name', 'This paragraph said "the last two"', 'This table named seven'), screw.rs:594 ('An earlier draft of this paragraph'), strength.rs:161 and reference.md:2079. state.md:17 says of itself 'the one file expected to be rewritten rather than amended', yet it has four narrated amendments.
proposal: Style rule: no 'used to / was once / stage type / an earlier version' in code comments, reference.md, rationale.md 'Decision' paragraphs, state.md or CLAUDE.md. A fault worth remembering gets one corrections.md log row, which the code may link to. Sweep with the regex in hist.py and rewrite each hit to its present-tense content (see the exemplars in patterns). Then add a warn-only check to tools/ that flags the phrases outside corrections.md and docs/history.
validation: hist.py reports ≤ 10 hits, each justified. check_doc_links is green. check_golden and nextest are unchanged, since this is comment-only.

verdict.reason: Re-running hist.py reproduces 202 hits in 13,861 production comment lines. But the regex is loose: 'It was ', 'had been', 'no longer', 'until the', 'retired'. In a 30-hit sample, about a third were not history narration, e.g. auto.rs:204 'the cutter no longer reaches', shape.rs:1248 'where it was asked', auto.rs:881 'until the two are level'. So roughly 130, not 202, are genuine. The self-referential passages are confirmed and are pure noise: CLAUDE.md:14, CLAUDE.md:182, state.md:106, state.md:157, rationale.md:724, screw.rs:594, strength.rs:161, contact.rs:398. So is the 'three functions in TypeScript, one per stage type' story, which appears at mod.rs:2164, mod.rs:2306, gear-wasm lib.rs:1432 (and its generated gear_wasm.d.ts:210), core.ts:655 and TrainPanel.svelte:51. A blanket ban goes too far, though. Many hits give the rejected alternative and why it was rejected, e.g. auto.rs:67 'It used to be a fixed 1 module — the classical rule', and auto.rs:1551 on the ±3-module sweep. That is rationale content the owner's goals value, and state.md:20-22 already argues against a literal word ban for this reason.
verdict.evidence: python3 notes/lens-docs-clarity/hist.py gives 202 hits, top files train/mod.rs 30, strength.rs 23, auto.rs 21. A seeded sample of 30 hits was classified by hand. grep for 'one per stage type' finds the five sites plus the generated .d.ts copy.
verdict.corrected_claim: About 130 production comment lines narrate past versions. The clearly removable class is (a) self-referential text ('this paragraph used to say', 'an earlier draft of this comment') and (b) stories about the retired stage type repeated at 4-5 sites. A 'was X, now Y' that states a rejected alternative and why it failed is legitimate rationale, and should be rewritten in the present tense ('a fixed 1 module, the classical rule, would …') rather than deleted.
verdict.proposal_note: Narrow the style rule to self-reference and to dead vocabulary ('stage type', 'card'), and rephrase rejected alternatives rather than remove them. A warn-only regex check will misfire on ordinary English ('no longer reaches'), as state.md:20-22 records happened before with 'now/still/currently'. If a check is added, match only 'this (paragraph|comment|table) (used to|said)' and 'earlier (draft|revision|version) of this'.

title: Terminology unsettled after the refactor: 'stage' (978 in code) vs part/preset/arrangement/shape/footprint, and no glossary
claim: Four overlapping nouns name a group of gears, and the one reader-facing definition is given in terms of the retired one.
evidence: Word counts, code/docs: stage 978/484, stages 160/48, part 453/191, preset 314/132, arrangement 175/80, shape 1235/211. In train/mod.rs, 25 of 404 'stage' hits are in production code and the rest are in tests. reference.md:2198 defines a preset as the thing 'whose footprint in the graph is what a stage was', and graph.rs:3 says parts 'are what a stage was', both addressed to a reader who has never seen a stage. Rationale has three overlapping sections: 'An arrangement is a "stage"' (159) says the word means an arrangement (worm stage, hula stage), while 'A stage is a preset's footprint, not a container' (263) and 'A train is one graph, and a part is how it falls apart' (216) restate each other ('nothing on screen is a part' is said in both). Headings still say 'One stage, one result' (1671, body about ShapeResult) and 'What a stage owes relief' (1941). No glossary exists; grep 'glossary|terminology' finds only state.md:568, which is unrelated. 'relief' is first used at reference.md:426, about 1,700 lines before its section.
proposal: Add a 'Terms' block at the top of reference.md with one line each for: train, shape (the graph), axis, body (port, slot), member, mesh, distance, coupling, part (derived solve unit), preset (a menu entry that lays pieces in), arrangement (the list a preset builds), family, hold, load case, load, path, relief/freedom, reading, mesh group. Decide once: 'stage' survives only in the fixed names 'worm stage' and 'hula stage' and in the legacy-file converter. Merge rationale 159, 216 and 263 into one section, 'Vocabulary: graph, part, preset'. Rename the headings at 1671 ('One shape, one result') and 1941 ('What a shape owes relief'), updating the ~15 code links (check_doc_links finds them). Rewrite reference.md:2198 and graph.rs:3 without 'what a stage was'.
validation: Every term in the glossary is defined before its first use: a script finds the first occurrence per term in reference.md. check_doc_links is green after the heading renames. Outside graph.rs/convert, gear-io's converter, tests and the two fixed names, grep -wci stage in production code goes under 20.

verdict.reason: reference.md:2198 defines a preset as 'whose footprint in the graph is what a stage was', and graph.rs:3 defines parts as 'what a stage was'. Both define current terms by a retired one. rationale.md has three overlapping sections. 159 'An arrangement is a "stage"' is actually about hula/eccentric naming. 216 and 263 both restate what a part is, using the same 'pieces that close, search and rate apart (`Shape::parts`)' phrase, and both say 'nothing on screen is a part' (lines 239 and ~281). The headings 1671 'One stage, one result' and 1941 'What a stage owes relief' describe the Shape machinery. Relief is used from reference.md:426 on, and no reference.md heading defines it anywhere, which is stronger than 'defined 1,700 lines later'. grep -wic 'stage' over crates/*/src gives 936 matching lines, which matches the order of magnitude claimed.
verdict.evidence: Read rationale.md:159-175, 216-230 and 263-285, reference.md:2195-2198, graph.rs:1-8, and grep '^#' docs/reference.md for 'relie' (no heading). The heading rename touches links such as gear-io/src/train.rs's `docs/rationale.md#what-a-stage-owes-relief`.
verdict.proposal_note: The glossary is worth it. Put it in reference.md's opening, which already sets out conventions at lines 12-14. Heading renames change anchors cited from code (e.g. gear-io train.rs), so run check_doc_links after renaming. Rationale 159 is a separate decision (naming the hula stage, 'drive' senses) and should not be merged into the graph/part/preset vocabulary section. Only merge 216 and 263.

title: gear-io/src/train.rs module comment is a 250-line changelog of file formats no reader accepts
claim: The module comment spends 291 lines, about 240 of them on migrations between intermediate schemas that are all refused anyway. It never states the current schema in one place.
evidence: train.rs:23-259 lists about 25 successive changes (working_depth→Auto, worm stage became a pair, loads became a list, constraints, `kind = "shape"`, shafts→bodies, ... 'The train is one graph'). Every intermediate format is refused by name, and `convert` (train.rs:422) reads only the last staged shape (StagedDocument, train.rs:406). The one current-schema description is a paragraph in reference.md:3056-3063. CLAUDE.md:143 tells contributors to append to 'gear-io/src/train.rs's change log' for every load-case change, so it will keep growing.
proposal: Replace the module comment with about 30 lines: inputs only; the name is part of the document; the current schema as a short annotated TOML example; that any other shape is refused by name (deny_unknown_fields) except `[[train.stages]]`, which `gear-cli convert` rewrites; and what is relieved and what is not checked on import. Move the change list to docs/history/file-format.md, or drop it since git keeps it. Change CLAUDE.md:143's instruction to 'update the schema example'.
validation: A doctest or unit test parses the annotated TOML example in the module comment with the reader, so the documented schema cannot drift. Existing refusal tests are unchanged.

verdict.reason: The module comment is 291 `//!` lines. Lines 23-~250 are a list of about 25 schema migrations. from_toml refuses every one of those formats, and `convert` reads only StagedDocument (train.rs:406-422). The only statement of the current schema is reference.md:3056-3063. The comment also contradicts itself: line 27 says 'Two changes so far:' and 3 + 21 + 1 = 25 bullets follow, a stale count of exactly the kind this project records as a fault. CLAUDE.md:143 does direct contributors to append to 'gear-io/src/train.rs's change log'.
verdict.evidence: awk count gives 291 //! lines. grep '^//! - ' over lines 41-239 gives 21 bullets, plus 3 before and the 'one graph' bullet. train.rs:27: "document that describes a different gearbox. Two changes so far:". train.rs:406-422: `struct StagedDocument`, `pub fn convert`.
verdict.proposal_note: Several bullets are the only prose that says what a current field means. For example, a load's `role` ("load"/"reacted"/"free") and a distance's `tip_clearance`. The replacement annotated TOML example has to carry those meanings, not just the field names. Keep the 'deny_unknown_fields is enforced, not assumed' paragraph in the present tense; it states a current invariant. Parsing the example with from_toml in a unit test is a good anti-drift gate.

title: Stale comment: MeshReport describes per-stage results the core no longer has
claim: The MeshReport doc says a set's `sun_planet`/`planet_ring` and a pair's 'own result' exist. They exist only in the harness's view in gear-cli.
evidence: mod.rs:194-197: "A set's `sun_planet`/`planet_ring` and a hula stage's two pairs are the same report ... a pair's one mesh is on its own result. This used to be the parallel-axis report only". grep shows `sun_planet` only in crates/gear-cli/src/main.rs:106-130 (the harness's Pair/Set view), and there is no `struct *Stage*Result|*PairResult` in the crates. mod.rs:467-468 likewise: "while there were such stages".
proposal: Replace the paragraph with: "Every mesh of every part is one of these, by the graph's mesh index." Delete the history sentence.
validation: Read-through; grep for sun_planet in gear-core returns nothing.

verdict.reason: The MeshReport doc names fields and per-stage result types that gear-core no longer has. `sun_planet`/`planet_ring` exist only as the harness's view in gear-cli, and there are no hula stages or pair results. The comment at line 467 is history too, but it also carries the reason the check sits inside `line_mesh_report` (so no caller has to remember it). Keep that reason and drop only the history.
verdict.evidence: crates/gear-core/src/train/mod.rs:194-197 reads: "A set's `sun_planet`/`planet_ring` and a hula stage's two pairs are the same report, which is why it is one type; a pair's one mesh is on its own result. This used to be the parallel-axis report only...".
