verdict.proposal_note: Line 194: replace the paragraph as proposed. Line 467: keep "asked here so that no caller has to remember to" and delete the clause about the stages.

title: Corrections log links bending faults to #contact-stress under opaque section numbers of a deleted spec
claim: The 'Where' column's link text is section numbers (4.3, 4.5.1, 4.7) from the removed brief. Several links point to the wrong section, which check_doc_links cannot catch because the anchors resolve.
evidence: Rows about the 30° tangent, parabola tangency on the fillet, ISO Y_S on a flank tangency, 'Rack-generated fillets keep q_s in range' and 'Helical bending measured Y_F on the transverse section' are all bending topics, and all link '[4.7](reference.md#contact-stress)'. reference.md has '## Bending' at line 1195. README.md:41 says the brief those numbers came from was removed.
proposal: Rewrite the Where column as topic links with readable text, for example [Bending](reference.md#bending), and re-target each row to its section.
validation: Manual pass, plus a check that no link text in corrections.md matches ^\d+(\.\d+)*$.

verdict.reason: The Where column's link text is section numbers from the removed brief, and the anchors are not consistent with those numbers. The same number points to many different anchors: '4.11' goes to 7 different anchors across 26 rows. Every bending row, and one efficiency row, links to #contact-stress, although reference.md has '## Bending' at line 1195. The cited line numbers are off by one or two: the bending rows are 356, 357, 358, 360 and 366, and the efficiency/sliding row is 361, as are later rows such as 439-441.
verdict.evidence: Running grep -o '\[[0-9.]*\](reference.md#...)' docs/corrections.md | sort | uniq -c gives '4.11' mapped to #bodies-and-constraints(2), #crossed-axes(1), #internal-gears(9), #the-graph(8), #the-hula-stage(1), #tooth-cycles(1) and #trains(3), and '4.7' to #contact-stress(13). Row 366, 'Helical bending measured `Y_F` on the transverse section', links [4.7](reference.md#contact-stress). reference.md:1092 is '## Contact stress' and 1195 is '## Bending'. README.md:41 says the brief was removed. Newer rows (for example corrections.md:454 and 659) already use the readable form [reference.md#internal-gears](reference.md#internal-gears).
verdict.proposal_note: Use the newer rows' own convention, a readable anchor as the link text, so the whole column is uniform. The check should also flag link text that is only a number, since check_doc_links resolves anchors but cannot judge where they point.

title: CLAUDE.md promises 'the tests that hold each' tooth.rs caution and names none
claim: The heading line promises test names; the list below it gives none. The README copy does name them.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:221 "Four in `tooth.rs`, and the tests that hold each:" is followed by items 1-4 with no test identifiers. README.md:156-172 names `legacy_clamp_still_shows_the_junction_step…`, `profile_is_bounded_from_both_sides_by_the_cutter` and `the_generated_profile_is_the_shape_the_cutter_would_leave`.
proposal: Keep the four cautions only in CLAUDE.md, each with its test name, and delete README's section.
validation: Each named test exists (grep in crates).

verdict.reason: It is true that CLAUDE.md:221 promises 'the tests that hold each' and then names none. But README is not the complete copy: it names a test only for item 1 and for the two simulations, not for items 2-4. More importantly, caution 4 is itself stale in both files. ShaperCut now caps an oversized tip round rather than refusing the tool (see missed). Moving the text into CLAUDE.md unchanged would carry that error with it.
verdict.evidence: CLAUDE.md:221-232 names no tests. README.md:163 names `legacy_clamp_still_shows_the_junction_step…` for item 1 only; the other names at README.md:173-178 are the two simulations. Tests that exist for each item: item 1, crates/gear-core/tests/regression.rs (legacy_clamp_…); item 2, tests/geometry_laws.rs:119 fillet_cap_guarantees_a_nonnegative_root_arc; item 3, tests/geometry_laws.rs:61 radius_is_monotone_and_theta_stays_in_the_half_pitch. For item 4, shaper.rs:154 says '**The round is capped, not refused.**', so no refusal test can exist.
verdict.corrected_claim: CLAUDE.md promises test names and gives none. README gives one of the four, and its item 4 (like CLAUDE.md's) describes behaviour the code has since reversed.
verdict.proposal_note: Name in CLAUDE.md: legacy_clamp_still_shows_the_junction_step…, fillet_cap_guarantees_a_nonnegative_root_arc and radius_is_monotone_and_theta_stays_in_the_half_pitch. Rewrite item 4 to say the round is capped to 95% of the largest that fits and reported, pointing at corrections.md:454. Keep the text in one place and have the other file link to it.

title: CLAUDE.md's train/ file map has lost its structure: 140-343-word cells and no 'does not know' column
claim: CLAUDE.md says the 'Does not know' column is the load-bearing one. The train/ table drops that column, and each of its rows is a paragraph of identifiers.
evidence: Word counts per row: conditions.rs 343, mod.rs 300, edits.rs 228, shape.rs 221, arrangements.rs 151, graph.rs 139. The gear-core table's rows average about 15-25 words in three columns. CLAUDE.md:59: "The load-bearing column is the last one." The edits.rs row also carries an anecdote ('how engaging a layshaft's other ratio lost the output'), which is also told at reference.md:2270, corrections.md:659 and edits.rs:747.
proposal: Use the same three columns as gear-core, capped at about 40 words per cell. For example, conditions.rs: 'Owns: holds, bodies and ports, the train's edits (join, hold, insert, chain_on). Does not know: geometry, or how a part is solved.' Move method inventories into each module's //! header, where rustdoc links check them. Drop anecdotes from the map.
validation: A test in check_doc_links flags any CLAUDE.md table cell over 60 words; every file in crates/gear-core/src/train is still listed.

verdict.reason: The train/ rows are paragraphs of identifiers, and the table drops the 'Does not know' column that CLAUDE.md:59 calls load-bearing. The gear-core table's cells are 4-25 words (planetary.rs 48). The edits.rs anecdote is also told in three other places. The proposal fits the owner's rule that each thing is said once.
verdict.evidence: awk word counts of column 2: mod.rs 296, conditions.rs 339, edits.rs 224, shape.rs 217, arrangements.rs 147, graph.rs 135, groupings.rs 100, offers.rs 87. The gear-core rows (CLAUDE.md:75-95) run 4-25 words, with planetary.rs at 48. The anecdote appears at CLAUDE.md:109, reference.md:2270, corrections.md:659 and edits.rs:747. The auditor's counts differ from mine by a few words because of tokenisation.
verdict.proposal_note: A 60-word gate in check_doc_links is a threshold rather than a law, which CLAUDE.md itself warns against; a reviewer's rule is enough. Deliberate absences are the useful content of the 'does not know' column (for example wiring.rs: no geometry; flow.rs: no geometry; preview.rs: decides nothing), and each module's //! already carries them.

title: CLAUDE.md opens with a 20-line parenthetical census history
claim: The first thing a reader of the map meets is four dated line counts and a correction of the paragraph's own earlier figure. It also names train/hula.rs, which no longer exists.
evidence: CLAUDE.md:14-33: '*(The first version of this paragraph said 1.5 to 1 ... It reads 16,100 / 12,900 / 5,000 at the tree the audit closed on, 17,100 / 13,600 / 5,100 ... `planetary.rs`, `hula.rs`, `pair.rs` and `crossed.rs` gave up 2,800 ...)*'. ls crates/gear-core/src/train/ has no hula.rs. The current line_census output (22,335 / 14,848 / 6,207, 0.94 to 1) matches the paragraph, so the figures are right. What is wrong is where they sit.
proposal: Replace lines 7-33 with: "Prose and code are about 1 to 1 (`tools/line_census.py` prints today's figures). Most of that prose is each model's argument and evidence; this file is how to find the right piece of it." The dated series belongs in commit messages.
validation: Read-through; line_census still runs.

verdict.reason: The main claim holds: a 20-line italic history of dated census figures, including a correction of the paragraph's own earlier value, is the first thing in the map. The census figures are current. But naming `hula.rs` is not an error: the sentence says it gave up lines between the four files, and deleting a file does that. The sentence that the ratio 'is not a target to reduce' has a purpose and should stay.
verdict.evidence: Running tools/line_census.py prints 22,335 / 14,848 / 6,207, 0.66 comment per line and 0.94 to 1, which matches CLAUDE.md:7-10 and 23. CLAUDE.md:27 reads "`planetary.rs`, `hula.rs`, `pair.rs` and `crossed.rs` gave up 2,800 between them", past tense and accurate. There is no train/hula.rs now.
verdict.corrected_claim: The dated census series and the self-correction are history that belongs in commit messages or state.md, not at the head of the map. The hula.rs mention is accurate history, not a stale reference.
verdict.proposal_note: Keep 'not a target to reduce' and the pointer to tools/line_census.py. Drop the dated series and the parenthetical about the earlier 1.5 figure.

title: reference.md, which says it 'states; it does not argue', carries history parentheticals and 'used to' prose
claim: reference.md breaks its own contract: at least 14 passages narrate past designs.
evidence: reference.md:1362 'One row that used to be here is gone ...' (a 6-line paragraph about an absent row). reference.md:2507-2513 '(Holds were once laid over each stage's conventions ... both words are gone.)'. reference.md:2548-2551 '(The chain used to be supplied by a rule ... then it was a list of couplings ...)'. reference.md:1383 'it was briefly untrue'. There are 14 grep hits for 'used to|was once|no longer|It was|became'.
proposal: Delete every parenthetical history in reference.md. Where the history is a real fault, make sure corrections.md has a row for it, and link it from reference.md if needed.
validation: grep -Ei 'used to|was once|were once|briefly untrue|once laid' docs/reference.md returns nothing.

verdict.reason: reference.md:7-10 promises it states and does not argue, and that 'Nothing appears in two of them'. Yet it narrates past designs at many places, several of which corrections.md already records (for example 2270 against corrections.md:659).
verdict.evidence: grep -nEi 'used to|was once|were once|no longer|It was|became|briefly untrue' docs/reference.md gives history hits at 451, 651, 727, 801, 1358, 1362, 1383, 2270, 2490, 2507, 2548, 2550 and 2703. Examples: 801 'They were once asked stage by stage...'; 2703 '(It was three lists — the speeds, the port bodies, the open ports...)'; 651 'That pair used to be answered at Σx = 1.6697 for 97.706 %'. Other hits are not history: 8 (the contract itself), 839, 1137, 2676 and 3163.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposed validation grep would fire on line 8 (the contract's own 'what was once wrong') and on present-tense uses such as 2676 'numbers the graph no longer has'. Scope it to exclude those, or review by hand. Before deleting 651 and 801, check that corrections.md has their rows (Σx 1.6697 interference; bounds per stage), because their figures are the evidence. Some passages, such as 399 and 649, also argue rather than state, which the same contract assigns to rationale.md.

title: Two stale standalone documents: the refactor plan/handoff (1,420 lines) and docs/history/design-record.md (4,408 lines, unreferenced)
claim: The plan says it is deleted once built, and it is built (every phase is marked done). Its measured baseline (train/mod.rs 8,499 lines, train/hula.rs 3,055) describes a tree that no longer exists. The design record has zero inbound references.
evidence: geartrain-refactor-plan.md:11: 'Both documents are working notes and are deleted once built'. Lines 875-974 say '*5a and 5b are done*', '*Phase 6 is done*', '*The clean-up pass, done*', '*The outliers pass, done*'. The handoff says 'Status: design only'. The plan's table has train/mod.rs at 8,499 lines; it is 11,363 today, and train/hula.rs no longer exists. The only code reference is kinematics.rs:308. grep 'design-record' outside docs/history finds nothing.
proposal: Delete both root notes. Rewrite kinematics.rs:308 to say what the fixture shows ('a part that does not close costs the whole train its answer; golden kinematics.txt:1474 records it'). Delete docs/history/design-record.md, since git is its provenance, and keep audit.md only while code cites F-numbers (35 mentions).
validation: check_doc_links green; grep for geartrain-refactor finds nothing.

verdict.reason: The root notes part holds. The two files come to 1,168 + 252 = 1,420 lines. The plan says 'Both documents are working notes and are deleted once built' (geartrain-refactor-plan.md:11), and its baseline table (train/mod.rs 8499, train/pair.rs 1441, train/planetary.rs 2711) describes a tree that no longer exists: mod.rs is 11,363 lines today, pair.rs 139, planetary.rs 47, and hula.rs is gone. Its residuals are already recorded elsewhere, so deleting it loses nothing: the positional conventional hold is in reference.md:2231 and 2500, the crossed pair missing from the oracle is in corrections.md:405, and the Ravigneaux planet-planet items are in state.md:636 and 756-763. Two parts of the claim are overstated. Not every phase is marked done: line 936 still reads 'Phase 7, the ablation half, in progress', which is stale rather than open. The handoff's 'design only' is its own inbound status, not a claim about the tree. The design-record part does not hold as proposed. Deleting docs/history/design-record.md goes against a documented decision with a real argument (its header, lines 10-14). The record says it holds reasoning the four documents only condense, such as the JGMA two-scale argument, and 'two-scale' occurs only there. It is also already excluded from the census and labelled 'nothing points here'. Git keeps it, but a reader would have to know to look. The first step should be to port or confirm each argument it names, then delete. The finding also misses a second pointer into the plan: corrections.md:668 cites '(Phase 3b)', which would dangle once the plan goes.
verdict.evidence: `wc -l`: plan 1168, handoff 252, design-record 4408, mod.rs 11363. `ls train/` has no hula.rs. The only pointers to the plan are `grep geartrain-refactor` hits at crates/gear-cli/src/kinematics.rs:308 and plan:8, plus corrections.md:668 'Retiring the lone stage (Phase 3b)'. Golden kinematics.txt:1474-1482 shows chain-unclosed reporting 'no answer: part 2: ...' while the graph still prints a total ratio of -4171/289. README.md:36-38 and state.md:280 both declare the design record kept for provenance on purpose.
verdict.proposal_note: Delete both root notes. Rewrite kinematics.rs:302-309 in present terms: the unclosed part costs the whole train its answer, and golden kinematics.txt records it. Replace 'Phase 3b' in corrections.md:668 with what it means ('retiring the lone stage'). For the design record, first check each argument it names (the JGMA two scales, the material survey, the crossed path, the λ minimax proof) against rationale.md and reference.md, port whatever is missing, and only then delete it.

title: 'milestone N' and 'Phase N' references to a deleted brief
claim: Milestone numbers refer to a brief that README.md:41 says was removed, so no reader can resolve them.
evidence: README.md:88 'have not moved since milestone 5'; shaper.rs:6 'curve milestone 8 needs'; contact.rs:634 '(milestone 7, step 5)'; main.rs:1283 'milestone 6's gate'; crossed.rs:43 'left a factor of two in this model for a milestone'.
proposal: Replace each with what it means, for example 'since the contact model was first built' or a version or commit; in crossed.rs just drop the clause.
validation: grep -rnw milestone outside docs/history returns nothing.

verdict.reason: Every cited reference exists and points at the brief that README.md:40-44 says was removed, so a reader cannot resolve it. The list is also incomplete. contact.rs:634 is worse than unresolvable: it promises a crossed-axis version of sliding_at 'with milestone 7, step 5' that never came, because the screw model has its own closed form (see missed). The docs/bending-check.html title block shows 'milestone 5' on a published page.
verdict.evidence: `grep -rni milestone` outside docs/history finds the auditor's sites plus several it missed: crates/gear-core/tests/metrology.rs:1 'Milestone 2's gate', crates/gear-core/src/ring.rs:1494 'Milestone 8's gate', crates/gear-core/src/train/crossed.rs:1324 'for a milestone', docs/bending-check.html:91 'milestone 5', docs/corrections.md:424 'would have gone live with milestone 9'. In corrections.md:371 and crossed.rs:43, 'for a milestone' means a span of time, which is harmless but vague.
verdict.proposal_note: Cover the missed sites as well. Use a date or commit, or name the capability ('once internal meshes had a path'). Drop the promise in contact.rs:633-635 rather than rewording it. Relax the validation grep for corrections.md, which is exempt as history, but not for bending-check.html.

title: Modules whose production code is a thin shell under long derivation prose (train/crossed.rs: 70-line header over ~70 lines of code)
claim: crossed.rs is 1,968 lines: 139 of production, 70 of them the module comment deriving backlash projection, then 1,830 of tests. The derivation belongs in reference.md#crossed-axes, and `proportions` could live in arrangements.rs beside `worm`.
evidence: grep '#[cfg(test)]' puts the test module at line 139. The header's own words: 'Not a stage of its own, and not a solve of its own ... What this module keeps is the worm's conventional proportions, the derivation below ..., and the tests'. pair.rs and planetary.rs in train/ describe themselves the same way ('this is what was left', 'No solve').
proposal: Move the derivation to reference.md (crossed backlash) and link it. Move `proportions` into arrangements.rs. Move the tests to crates/gear-core/tests/crossed.rs, or keep them in shape.rs's test module. Fold train/pair.rs's ShiftAsked into shape.rs or auto.rs. Keep train/planetary.rs's words as part of arrangements.rs. Then update CLAUDE.md's map.
validation: nextest count unchanged; check_golden unchanged; CLAUDE.md map lists every file.

verdict.reason: The measurements hold: the test module starts at line 139, lines 1-69 are the module comment, and the rest of the production part is `proportions`, about 10 lines of code under 60 of doc. But the claim that the derivation 'belongs in reference.md' misses that it is already there. reference.md:302-313 states j_n = j_axial sin β_b1 + 2Δa sin α_n, the separation-counts-twice and slide-counts-once argument, and the sin α_n identity. The rationale.md:715-716 measurement at 4 mm and 40 mm covers the proportions' claim too. So the real defect is duplication: the header should shrink to a link. Two parts of the proposal are poor. Moving `proportions` into arrangements.rs is the wrong home: that file is documented as 'knows nothing about solving', while `proportions` is read at solve time by shape.rs:3161-3169. screw.rs, beside the worm geometry, or auto.rs, beside other automatic values, would fit. Moving the tests to crates/gear-core/tests/ would need visibility widened, since they import super::super::shape internals (crossed.rs:142-151). Folding pair.rs (139 lines, all production, 10 outside uses of ShiftAsked) and planetary.rs (47 lines) into shape.rs, a very large file, trades a thin file for a bigger one. That is defensible but not clearly better.
verdict.evidence: `grep -n '#[cfg(test)]'` on crossed.rs gives 139, and pair.rs has none. reference.md lines 305-313 are quoted above. `grep proportions::` finds its only production callers at shape.rs:3161 and 3167. crossed.rs:80 says 'the appendix records the measurement', but no appendix exists in docs/*.md; the measurement is at rationale.md:715.
verdict.proposal_note: Reduce crossed.rs's header to a few lines linking reference.md#crossed-axes, and keep only what reference.md lacks (the 0.21 % parallel/crossed divergence at default clearance, if it is not there). Move `proportions` to screw.rs, not arrangements.rs. Keep the tests where they are unless shape internals become pub(crate). Fix the dangling 'the appendix'.

title: Doc comments much longer than their functions: 187 of 776 fn docs exceed the body, 67 by 3x
claim: Many long comments are legitimate derivations. A clear subset restates docs or tells history: mesh.rs:364 is 38 lines over a 1-line body (`angular_backlash/2`), strength.rs:1708 is 37 lines over 1 line, and wasm relieve/edit_train are 27-29 lines over 3.
evidence: ratio.py: 776 function doc blocks; comment longer than body in 187, at least 3× in 67. Examples: contact.rs:323 90/12, strength.rs:1311 61/11, gear.rs:309 58/11, mesh.rs:364 38/3, strength.rs:1708 37/3 (the latter restates rationale.md:1281-1316 nearly verbatim).
proposal: Apply the comment rule: at most one short paragraph of 'why', unless the item is itself a derivation with no home in reference.md. Otherwise link. Start with the 67 at 3x or more.
validation: Re-run ratio.py; count of ≥3× blocks under 25, each a derivation.

verdict.reason: The examples are real, and several restate a document. strength.rs:1708-1740 (ContactStress::governing) restates rationale.md:1281-1305 sentence by sentence, including the identical ρ₁=ρ₂=10 versus ρ₁=5.5, ρ₂=55 example. mesh.rs:364-400 (loaded_flank_phase) restates reference.md:315-318's mirror-axis argument. The wasm relieve doc tells history ('they used to live in the panel as three functions, one per stage type'). The headline counts, though, depend on the method. My own count, with doc lines preceding each production fn and a body of at least 1 line, gives 733 / 236 / 133, not 776 / 187 / 67, so the figures are not stable and the validation threshold of 'under 25' is a number chosen by feel. The metric is also skewed by design: every #[wasm_bindgen] entry point is a one-line wrapper over an _impl whose contract the doc states, and a one-line fn such as loaded_flank_phase carries a documented reason to exist as a named function (mesh.rs:390-397). Length is not the defect; restatement is.
verdict.evidence: My script at /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-lens-docs-clarity-3/docratio.py prints '733 236 133'. Its top entries are mesh.rs:402 (38/1), strength.rs:1746 (37/1), auto.rs:1057 (31/1), and gear-wasm lib.rs:1446 (29/1) and 1538 (27/1). The two passages were compared side by side as quoted in this session.
verdict.proposal_note: Frame the rule as one home per argument, not as a length ratio. Target doc blocks whose argument also appears in reference.md or rationale.md, and replace them with a one-line why plus a link. Keep the 'why a named function' paragraphs, which are decisions local to the code. Leave the wasm entry-point docs as the boundary contract, trimming only their history sentences. Drop the numeric validation threshold.

title: Verdict on 'the ratio is not a target to reduce': the argument does not survive; replace with a one-home rule
claim: The claim that the prose/code ratio 'is the reason the model decisions here are auditable' treats two different things as one: a model's reasons and evidence, which make it auditable, and restated history, which makes it harder to audit because the copies drift. The previous audit's reason for declining ('Reducing the prose. It is why the corrections log exists.') doesn't follow either: the corrections log would survive intact.
evidence: The project's top-ranked correction pattern, corrections.md:26, says 'A duplicated formula is a place where two answers can differ, and the copy nothing exercises is the one that is wrong'. The same holds for duplicated prose, as findings above show: README vs main.rs, state.md vs CLAUDE.md, CLAUDE.md vs README on the tooth.rs tests. History markers make up 6-9% of production comment. Unreferenced or stale standalone documents come to about 6,800 lines (design-record 4,408, refactor notes 1,420, plus the gear-io changelog of about 250).
proposal: Change CLAUDE.md:9-11 to: 'The ratio is not a target in either direction. What is a target is one home per fact: reasons and evidence stay beside the model or in rationale.md, history lives in corrections.md and git, and everything else links.' Expect the ratio to fall from 0.94 to about 0.8 as a side effect.
validation: line_census before and after; a duplicate-sentence script (see the restatement finding) reports about zero; no rationale entry loses its 'measurement that settled it'.

verdict.reason: The argument is sound and fits the owner's goals. The ratio statement (CLAUDE.md:9-11) confuses the volume of prose with auditability. The project's own top pattern (corrections.md:26-27, 'A duplicated formula is a place where two answers can differ') applies to prose, and this session confirmed three concrete prose duplicates: crossed.rs header versus reference.md:302-313, strength.rs governing versus rationale.md:1281-1305, and mesh.rs loaded_flank_phase versus reference.md:315-318. The closed audit's 'Reducing the prose. It is why the corrections log exists' (audit.md:510) is a non sequitur, since the corrections log is a separate document that a one-home rule would keep. Some numbers are off. The stale-document total is 4,408 + 1,420 + ~250 ≈ 6,080 lines, not 'about 6,800'. The 6-9 % history-marker share was not reproduced. The 'fall to about 0.8' is a guess. The census baseline itself is right: tools/line_census.py prints 22,335 / 14,848 / 6,207, with prose to code at 0.94.
verdict.evidence: The census output was quoted in this session. audit.md:510 '- **Reducing the prose.** It is why the corrections log exists.' CLAUDE.md:14-32, a 19-line paragraph narrating the ratio's history across branches, is itself the kind of history-in-a-map the proposal targets.
verdict.proposal_note: Adopt the one-home sentence. Also cut CLAUDE.md:14-32 to one line pointing at tools/line_census.py, since the per-branch history of the ratio belongs in git. Do not promise a target ratio.

title: Over-pins contact roll omits cos β_b: pin-validity range wrong on helical gears (doc and code agree, both wrong)
claim: The document and the code place the pin's contact point at roll `u_c = tan φ_M − σ d_p/(2 r_b)`. The seat equation next to it (`inv φ_M = … + d_p/(2 r_b cos β_b)`) is the correct over-ball relation, and consistency with it requires `u_c = tan φ_M − σ d_p cos β_b/(2 r_b)`. The contact radius therefore comes out too low on every helical gear, so the form-circle and tip checks — and with them `pin_diameter_range` (the bound the pin box shows) — are shifted.
evidence: notes/lens-docs-accuracy-2/ball.py builds an involute helicoid (m = 1, α_n = 20°, β = 30°, z = 17, d_p = 1.728) and places the ball centre by the crate's seat relation. The distance to the flank equals d_p/2 to 1e-13, so the seat relation is exact. The true nearest point has roll 0.424738 and radius 9.83066 mm. The code's formula gives roll 0.413541 and radius 9.79150 mm, 0.039 mm low. The cos β_b variant gives 0.424738, which matches the true point to 1e-8. metrology.rs:504 reads `let u_contact = phi.tan() - sigma * pin_diameter / (2.0 * rb);` while line 481 divides by `rb * beta_b.cos()`.
proposal: Change metrology.rs:504 to `phi.tan() - sigma * pin_diameter * beta_b.cos() / (2.0 * rb)` (β_b is already a parameter of `pin_seat`), and make the same change to reference.md:1414. Spur gears are unchanged (cos 0 = 1).
validation: Add a test that builds a helical gear, computes the contact by minimising the distance from the ball centre to the analytic helicoid (as ball.py does), and asserts the reported contact radius to 1e-9 over β ∈ {0, 15, 30, 45}°. Then run check_golden: any helical pin range that moves is expected to move.

verdict.reason: The claim holds, and I derived it again independently. An involute helicoid's normal lies in the plane tangent to the base cylinder, at β_b to the transverse plane. So the pin's radius d_p/2 along that normal projects to (d_p/2)·cos β_b along the transverse base tangent through the centre. The same projection gives the seat relation's d_p/(2 r_b cos β_b), which is correct. The contact roll must therefore be u_c = tan φ − σ d_p cos β_b/(2 r_b). The code drops cos β_b in the contact line but keeps it in the seat line. The contact radius feeds Space::seat's form and tip checks (metrology.rs:132-135), so the verdicts and pin_diameter_range move on every helical gear. Spur gears are unaffected.
verdict.evidence: metrology.rs:481 `sigma * (pin_diameter / (2.0 * rb * beta_b.cos()) - half_space)` against metrology.rs:504 `phi.tan() - sigma * pin_diameter / (2.0 * rb)`. The same pair is at reference.md:1413-1414. Hand check of the auditor's case (m=1, α_n=20°, β=30°, z=17, d_p=1.728): β_b = 28.02°, 1 − cos β_b = 0.1172, d_p/(2 r_b) = 0.0955, product 0.01119. That equals the auditor's roll gap 0.424738 − 0.413541 = 0.011197. Space::seat (metrology.rs:123-139) uses `contact` against `form` and `tip`, so the pin range is affected.
verdict.proposal_note: The fix is right: add `* beta_b.cos()` to line 504 and to reference.md:1414. Doc comment line 460 also needs the change. For a test, analytic nearest-point minimisation on the helicoid is enough. The golden outputs for helical over-pins and pin ranges will move, and that move is expected.

title: The 'ten scalar solves, everything else algebraic' inventory is far from complete, and two bisections bypass solve.rs
claim: rationale.md says 'Ten scalar solves … Everything else in the crate is algebraic — except one search'. reference.md says 'Every transcendental step in the crate routes through these two [solvers]'. Both are false. Row #2 ('Tip radius for a given tip width — Newton, analytic ds/dr') also does not describe the code: it runs Brent twice and uses no derivative.
evidence: Root-finder calls in production that the table does not list: contact.rs:534 `efficient_split`; auto.rs:366 (the pointed-tip shift); auto.rs:842 `searchable_shift` ceiling; tooth.rs:456 (the pointed-tooth roll, Newton — while auto.rs:744 solves the same quantity again by Brent); shape.rs:860 (helix for a target distance); shape.rs:959 `size_reaching`; shape.rs:1695 (tip sizing); shaper.rs:450 `largest_tip_round`; gear.rs:1137 `amplitude_for_throw`; screw.rs:454 `least_distance_lead_angle`; screw.rs:1230 `locking_friction`. Two fixed-count bisections that do not go through solve.rs at all: metrology.rs:192-212 (`pin_diameter_range`: a doubling walk to 64 steps, then 64 halvings) and verify.rs:726 (60 halvings). Brackets also carry unexplained literals: shape.rs:955-957 (1e-9) and screw.rs:452-453 (1e-9).
proposal: Regenerate the table from a grep of `brent(`/`newton_bracketed(` call sites: one row per quantity, with its method and bracket, and remove the claim 'everything else is algebraic'. Route the metrology pin bisection through `solve::brent` on a signed verdict residual (or state why a boolean verdict needs bisection, and name its 64). Solve the pointed-tooth roll once and share it between tooth.rs and auto.rs. Correct row #2 to Brent. Add a tools/ check (or a test) that counts solver call sites against the table so it cannot drift again.
validation: The grep count equals the table's row count, enforced by a check. After the pointed-tooth unification, the `addendum_for_tip_width` and Tooth tip-cap results are bit-identical across the geometry_laws grid.

verdict.reason: Both documents' claims are false. reference.md:47-48 says every transcendental step routes through the two solvers and that rationale.md holds the complete list. rationale.md:412-414 lists ten solves and says everything else is algebraic. A grep finds about 25 production call sites of brent/newton_bracketed. Many are absent from the table: contact.rs:534, auto.rs:366, auto.rs:744/755, auto.rs:842, tooth.rs:456, shape.rs:860/959/1490/1695, shaper.rs:450, gear.rs:1137, screw.rs:454/1230. Row #2 says Newton, but auto.rs:744-755 runs Brent twice with no derivative, and reference.md:251 repeats 'bracketed Newton'. The pointed-tooth roll is solved twice: Newton at tooth.rs:456 and Brent at auto.rs:744. metrology.rs:199 and verify.rs:726 are hand-written bisections outside solve.rs. No wrong answer results, so severity is low.
verdict.evidence: `grep -rn "brent(\|newton_bracketed(" crates/gear-core/src` output quoted above. auto.rs:744 `let u_point = brent(|u| g.psi_b - inv_from_roll(u), 0.0, POINTED_TOOTH_MAX_ROLL, ...)` against tooth.rs:456 `newton_bracketed(|u| psi_b - inv_from_roll(u), ...)`. metrology.rs:200 `for _ in 0..64`; verify.rs:726 `for _ in 0..60`.
verdict.proposal_note: Don't route pin_diameter_range through brent on a 'signed verdict residual'. Its doc comment (metrology.rs:176-182) gives a sound reason for bisecting a boolean: which condition binds differs by kind, so there is no single continuous residual. The same holds for verify.rs, where the instrument's predicate is geometric contact. Keep both bisections, and fix the documents to say that bracketed bisection on a verdict is a third method. The better target is sharing the pointed-tooth roll between tooth.rs and auto.rs, with one method. A grep-count check could instead stop the table from claiming completeness, e.g. by listing quantities per module.

title: root_radius is documented as normal modules but is multiplied by the transverse module
claim: params.rs says `addendum`, `dedendum` and `root_radius` are multiples of the normal module, and cites 0.38 as the ISO 53 basic rack, whose ρ_fP* is a normal-module coefficient. The tool is built with `rho = params.root_radius * mt` and the admissible range is divided by m_t. So a helical gear's cutter round is ρ*·m_n/cos β: 15.5 % larger than asked at β = 30°. That is neither the normal-plane round nor its true transverse curvature at the tip (ρ_n/cos²β, +33 %).
evidence: tooth.rs:918 `let mut rho = params.root_radius * mt;`; auto.rs:703 `Some((rho_max / mt).max(0.0))`; reference.md:163 `ρ ≤ 0.95 · min(b_d, ρ_max)/m_t`. Ellipse-curvature argument: stretching a normal-section circle of radius ρ by 1/cos β along the pitch line gives a vertex radius of ρ/cos²β. corrections.md:37 credits `Rack` of two lengths with removing a 'stray 1/cos β' on conversion, yet the inbound conversion here carries exactly that kind of factor.
proposal: Decide the coefficient's plane. Recommended: normal module (ISO): `rho_n = root_radius * m`, then either keep the transverse circle model with ρ_t = rho_n / cos²β (the vertex curvature) and state it as an approximation in state.md, or keep ρ_n and say so. Update params.rs, reference.md's table row and the admissible range together. If m_t is kept deliberately, change params.rs:8 to say 'transverse module for root_radius' and record the approximation, with its size and sign, in state.md.
validation: A helical test: fillet_curvature at the fillet root of a β = 30° gear with a sharp-bottomed space equals the chosen ρ expression to 1e-9. check_golden and check_figures show which helical bending figures move.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is right: tooth.rs:918 multiplies root_radius by m_t. It is a documented and deliberately unrepaired approximation, not an undiscovered one. state.md:689-699 records it with sign and size ('1/cos β larger than the normal round … 6 % at 20° … neither circle is it; sign stated, size stated, unrepaired'), per rule 6, and repeats it at state.md:1196. The same entry says no rating reads it, because bending uses the virtual spur with the normal round. reference.md:163 states the bound with /m_t, which matches the code. What remains wrong is the params.rs:8 doc comment, which lists root_radius among the normal-module coefficients. That comment contradicts the code and state.md.
verdict.evidence: params.rs:8-9 '`addendum`, `dedendum` and `root_radius` are multiples of the **normal** module'. tooth.rs:918 `let mut rho = params.root_radius * mt;`. state.md:689 '**The rack round is the coefficient times the *transverse* module** … A normal round's transverse section is an ellipse and neither circle is it; sign stated, size stated, unrepaired.'
verdict.corrected_claim: params.rs:8 wrongly says root_radius is in normal modules. The code scales it by the transverse module, a deliberate and documented approximation (state.md:689-699). The doc comment should say so and point to state.md.
verdict.proposal_note: Fix only the params.rs comment, e.g. 'root_radius is in modules and applied at the transverse module; see state.md'. Switching the plane is the separate, already-recorded decision in state.md:1196, and would move golden outputs and the worm's fillet cap.

title: The claim that every input bound sits exactly where the generator's guards clamp is false for pressure angle and dedendum
claim: reference.md says 'Every bound is closed form, and each sits exactly where the generator's own guards begin to clamp'. The pressure-angle range is strictly (0, 90)° while Tooth clamps anything ≤ 0.5° (CLAMP_PRESSURE_ANGLE_RAISED). The dedendum range is `−h_a < h_f < x + 0.9 r/m` while Rack::wanted_by clamps whenever h_f − x < 0.05 (CLAMP_DEDENDUM_RAISED). An in-range input is therefore clamped, with a note.
evidence: auto.rs:694 `pressure_angle: Bound::strictly(0.0, 90.0)`; the same function uses `.max(guard::MIN_PRESSURE_ANGLE_DEG)` internally (auto.rs:660-663). tooth.rs:401-408 clamps at 0.5°. tooth.rs:899-903 clamps bd at 0.05 m. The dedendum bound (auto.rs:702) has no x + 0.05 floor.
proposal: Either make the ranges report the guard (pressure angle min 0.5° exclusive-false; dedendum min max(−h_a, x + 0.05)), or reword reference.md to list which guards sit inside the displayed range and why. The first matches 'clamp rather than refuse, and say so' better, because the field then shows the true limit.
validation: A law over the tests/common grid: every input at its admissible bound ± ε produces no clamp note just inside the bound and a clamp note just outside it.

verdict.reason: The pressure-angle half holds. The range is Bound::strictly(0,90) (auto.rs:694), but Tooth::new clamps any α ≤ 0.5° with CLAMP_PRESSURE_ANGLE_RAISED (tooth.rs:401-408). The ranges code even applies .max(MIN_PRESSURE_ANGLE_DEG) internally (auto.rs:660-663). reference.md:165-168 also says the smallest pressure angle sits *inside* the shape's limit, which contradicts 'each sits exactly where the generator's guards begin to clamp' at reference.md:150-151. The dedendum half is a deliberate two-tier design, not an error. clamp.dedendum_raised marks a legal gear cut by a deeper hob, and the ranges deliberately run past it. That is argued at auto.rs:2307-2316 (a threshold, ShiftRange::shallow_cut, not a bound), with a recorded correction for when it was treated as a bound (a 62 % step as Δx left zero). The document's sentence is still too absolute about it.
verdict.evidence: auto.rs:694 `pressure_angle: Bound::strictly(0.0, 90.0)`. tooth.rs:401 `if an <= guard::MIN_PRESSURE_ANGLE_DEG.to_radians() {` … CLAMP_PRESSURE_ANGLE_RAISED. auto.rs:2307 'The dedendum note is not one of those clamps, and that is the two-tier distinction … the range deliberately runs past it'. auto.rs:315-319 'A threshold, not a bound'.
verdict.corrected_claim: reference.md:150-151 overstates the case. The pressure-angle range admits 0 < α ≤ 0.5°, which the generator clamps with a note, and the sentence contradicts reference.md:165-168. The dedendum-raised note inside the range is a deliberate threshold. The sentence should name it rather than the range being moved.
verdict.proposal_note: Do not raise the dedendum floor to x + 0.05. auto.rs:2307-2316 and ShiftRange::shallow_cut document why the range runs past the shallow-cut threshold, and a correction records the step that treating it as a bound caused. For the pressure angle, either make the bound min 0.5° (inclusive-exclusive per the clamp's `<=`), or reword reference.md to say the pressure-angle guard sits inside the physical bound the field shows.

title: The tip-width function s(r′) is called monotone decreasing, but its stated slope is positive at the base circle
claim: reference.md: 's(r′) = 2r′(ψ_b − inv α_{r′}) is monotone decreasing with ds/dr′ = 2(ψ_b − inv α_{r′} − tan α_{r′})'. At r′ = r_b that slope is 2ψ_b > 0, so s rises from the base circle to a maximum at tan α + inv α = ψ_b. The code's early exit, 'The tooth is at its widest where the involute starts' (`width(0) < min → None`), is therefore not exact either.
evidence: Derivative checked by hand: d(inv α)/dr = tan α / r, so ds/dr = 2(ψ_b − inv α − tan α). At z = 20, ψ_b ≈ 0.093, so the maximum sits near α ≈ 5°, r ≈ 1.004 r_b. Brent still brackets correctly whenever width(0) ≥ min, because the decreasing branch is then the only crossing.
proposal: Reword to 'decreasing above the radius where tan α + inv α = ψ_b, and unimodal from the base circle'. In code, either compare min_tip_width with the true maximum (closed form: tan α + inv α = ψ_b is one inv-type solve) or document why the base-circle value is a safe proxy (the margin is ~1e-3 relative).
validation: A unit test asserting width(u) increases for small u when ψ_b > 0 (documents the shape), and that addendum_for_tip_width returns Some whenever max width ≥ min.

verdict.reason: The derivative is right. d(inv α)/dr = tan α / r, so ds/dr = 2(ψ_b − inv α − tan α), which is 2ψ_b > 0 at r_b. So s is not monotone decreasing from the base circle, and the code's early exit and the auto.rs:711 comment ('strictly decreasing in r′') are wrong. I measured the maximum's excess over width(0) numerically: 0.14 % at z=20, x=0; 1.1 % at z=8, x=0.6; 0.016 % at z=100. Where width(0) < min ≤ max width, the function returns None although a radius with that width exists. Brent's bracket is otherwise sound, since only one crossing lies on the decreasing branch. The case matters only for a minimum tip width near the base-circle thickness, which is well beyond practical values, hence low severity.
verdict.evidence: Python: z=20 x=0: width(0)=1.75618, max=1.75872 at u=0.093. z=8 x=0.6: width(0)=1.99853, max=2.02123 at u=0.260. auto.rs:737 `// The tooth is at its widest where the involute starts.` / `if width(0.0) < min_tip_width { return None; }`. auto.rs:711-712 'strictly decreasing in `r'`'. reference.md:250-252 'monotone decreasing … so it is a bracketed Newton', though the code is Brent.
verdict.proposal_note: The maximum is at tan α + inv α = ψ_b, i.e. u + (u − atan u) = ψ_b in roll. That is one bracketed solve, or a closed-form seed plus solve. Bracket the Brent on [u_max, u_point] and return None only when width(u_max) < min. Fix reference.md:251 'Newton' to 'Brent' at the same time.

title: Stale figure: parabola vs 30° tangent Y_F range
claim: rationale.md says the construction is 'more conservative everywhere: +2.9 % to +13.7 % on Y_F'. The matrix it cites prints a parabola/tangent Y_F ratio of 1.006 to 1.312, mean 1.055, over the same 1521-design population. 'It' is also ambiguous: the preceding bullet is about the tangent.
evidence: `gear-cli matrix` (saved at notes/lens-docs-accuracy-2/matrix.txt), external section 5: 'Y_F parabola/tangent 1.006 .. 1.312 mean 1.055'. The Spearman ρ = 0.993410 in the same bullet list does still match.
proposal: Replace with the matrix figures (+0.6 % to +31.2 %, mean +5.5 %), name the construction explicitly ('the parabola is the more conservative…'), and tag the block `<!-- figures: gear-cli matrix -->` so check_figures holds it.
validation: tools/check_figures.py passes with the new tag, and fails if the matrix moves.

verdict.reason: I re-ran `gear-cli matrix`. Section 5 prints 'Y_F parabola/tangent 1.006 .. 1.312 mean 1.055' over 1508 designs rated by both. rationale.md:559 still carries '+2.9 % to +13.7 %', copied from the superseded docs/history/design-record.md:1772. 'It' is ambiguous after a bullet about the 30° tangent. The ratio > 1 means the parabola is the conservative one. The Spearman bullet is also slightly off: ρ = 0.993410 holds, but n = 1508, not the 1521 the bullet says.
verdict.evidence: notes/verify-lens-docs-accuracy-2-1/matrix.txt lines 11-13: '30° · Y_F only vs parabola · Y_F only rho = 0.993410 (n=1508)'. Lines 50-52: 'designs rated by both 1508 … Y_F parabola/tangent 1.006 .. 1.312 mean 1.055'. grep shows '13.7' only in rationale.md:559 and history/design-record.md:1772.
verdict.corrected_claim: The Y_F range is stale: the current figures are +0.6 % to +31.2 %, mean +5.5 %. The Spearman ρ is over 1508 designs, not 1521.
verdict.proposal_note: Tagging it `figures: gear-cli matrix` is reasonable. check_figures matches numbers at the document's precision, so write the figures as the command prints them (1.006, 1.312, 0.993, 1508) or as percentages it can match. check_figures' docstring says rationale.md is sometimes left ungated on purpose, but this bullet is presented as a current measurement, so gating it is right.

title: 'Every row of every table reports which bound stopped it' — no table or command does, and reference.md itself calls 17/43's optimum interior
claim: reference.md (Input ranges) says 'every row of every table in Efficiency reports which bound stopped it'. rationale.md says 'Every row of every table this project prints reports the sum landing on a bound rather than at a stationary point'. reference.md:639 says 17/43's optimum is interior ('nothing holds it there but the loss turning over'), and `gear-cli shifts` prints no bound column at all.
evidence: `gear-cli shifts 17 43` prints x1, x2, sum, eps and eta columns, with no bound. reference.md:639-645 contrasts an interior 17/43 with a constrained 9/37.
proposal: Delete both universal claims and keep the pair-specific statement (reference.md:639-649). Alternatively, add a 'bound' column to `gear-cli shifts` (the search knows which constraint rejected its neighbours) and record it in the corpus.
validation: check_figures/check_golden if the column is added; otherwise a grep that the phrase is gone.

verdict.reason: Both universal claims are contradicted by the documents' own worked example and by the harness. reference.md:639-645 says the 17/43 optimum is interior ('nothing holds it there but the loss turning over'). The sentence at reference.md:176-178 is wrong in two ways: 'the least-loss pair is always the one whose teeth barely reach' and 'every row of every table ... reports which bound stopped it'. rationale.md also contradicts itself: a few lines above the universal claim it says the optimum is 'as often at an end of the admissible interval', which is not 'every row'. The rationale citation is off: the sentence is at rationale.md:518, not :545.
verdict.evidence: `gear-cli shifts 17 43` prints x1/x2/sum/eps/eta fwd columns only, with no bound column. Its least-loss row is 0.4946/0.7620, Σx 1.2566, 98.488 %, and the axis-distance sweep peaks at that Σx with neighbours worse on both sides (98.485 % at 1.0294), so the optimum is interior. reference.md:176-178 reads: 'the loss falls monotonically with the length of the path, so the least-loss pair is always the one whose teeth barely reach, and every row of every table in [Efficiency] reports which bound stopped it'. rationale.md:518 reads: 'Every row of every table this project prints reports the sum landing on a bound rather than at a stationary point'. rationale.md:511-512 reads: 'the optimum is as often at an end of the admissible interval'.
verdict.corrected_claim: reference.md:176-178 (both 'always ... barely reach' and 'every row ... reports which bound') and rationale.md:518 state as universal what reference.md:639-645 shows is pair-specific: 17/43 is interior and 9/37 is bounded. No table reports a bound.
verdict.proposal_note: Prefer rewording over adding a column. The argument at reference.md:176-181 for not widening guards still holds when the optimum is only sometimes on a bound: 'it can move the answer onto a bound' is enough. Replace 'always ... barely reach' and 'every row ...' with 'where the optimum sits against a bound (9/37, below), widening the guard moves the answer'. Delete rationale.md:518-520 or reduce it to 'often, not always, so the whole thing is a search'.

title: Internal-gear generation limit and junction written with α_t where the code uses the shaper's cutting angle
claim: reference.md gives the generation limit as `√(r_b² + (a sin α_t)²)` and the junction as `… = a sin α_t + …`. The code uses `cut.centre_distance * cut.alpha_w.sin()`, the cutting pressure angle, which equals α_t only at zero shift (scale = 1). The same section defines `scale = a_cut/a_ref`, which moves the operating angle. `r_bw` in the junction formula is also undefined.
evidence: ring.rs:611 `f64::hypot(self.rb, self.cut.centre_distance * self.cut.alpha_w.sin())`; ring.rs:533 `self.cut.centre_distance * self.cut.alpha_w.sin() + r_bc * t_tan`.
proposal: Write both with `a_cut sin α_cut` (cos α_cut = a_ref cos α_t / a_cut), and define r_bw, or replace it with r_b of the ring.
validation: Reading check. Optionally, a ring test with a nonzero shift asserting that generation_limit differs from the α_t form.

verdict.reason: Ring::new builds its ShaperCut at a_cut, the operating geometry at −x (ring.rs:408-414). ShaperCut::new sets cos α_w = cos α_t / scale with scale = a_cut/a_ref (shaper.rs:186-200), so alpha_w equals α_t only at zero shift. generation_limit (ring.rs:611) and solve_junction (ring.rs:533) both use centre_distance·sin(alpha_w), not a·sin α_t. `r_bw` appears only once in reference.md (line 1583) and is never defined; the code uses self.rb, the ring's base radius. The rack-standing-in constructor (shaper.rs:510-520) does set alpha_w = α_t, but that path is not the ring's cut.
verdict.evidence: ring.rs:611: `f64::hypot(self.rb, self.cut.centre_distance * self.cut.alpha_w.sin())`. ring.rs:533: `self.cut.centre_distance * self.cut.alpha_w.sin() + r_bc * t_tan`. shaper.rs:186,192: `let scale = p.centre_distance / a_ref; let cos_aw = p.alpha_t.cos() / scale;`. `grep -n r_bw docs/reference.md` returns only 1583. reference.md:1548-1551 defines scale and says it is 'exactly 1 at zero shift'.
verdict.proposal_note: Write the two formulas as `a_cut sin α_cut` with `cos α_cut = a_ref cos α_t / a_cut` (the scale already defined at 1548), and replace r_bw with r_b. The 'differ by a sin α_t' prose at 1579 needs the same change.

title: Crossed shift law written with the radial shift x; the code (correctly) uses the thickness shift x + x_s
claim: reference.md: `a₀ = (d₁ + d₂)/2 + (x₁ + x₂) m_n`. The code feeds ScrewParams.profile_shifts with `shifts[i] + thickness_shift()` (shape.rs:522). The parallel section explicitly says its sums are over x + x_s; the crossed one does not, and by the document's own 'radial takes x, thickness takes x + x_s' rule it reads as radial.

proposal: Write `(x₁ + x_s1 + x₂ + x_s2) m_n` or add 'over the thickness shift, as on parallel axes'.
validation: Reading check.

verdict.reason: The code feeds the screw law with the thickness shift: shape.rs:522 `shifts[i] + thickness_shift()`, then screw.rs:272 `reference_distance + shift_sum * normal_module`. The document's own rule (reference.md:89-90: radial takes x, thickness takes x + x_s) makes `(x₁ + x₂) m_n` read as radial. The parallel section says outright that its sums are over x + x_s (reference.md:268-269); the crossed section (reference.md:934-941) does not. The derivation above the formula argues from a flank 'thickened by a shift', so the physics is the thickness shift and only the symbol is wrong.

title: The spur-only undercut reduction is stated as general
claim: 'With ρ = 0 it reduces to x_min = h_w − z sin²α_t / 2' holds only where r/m = z/2, i.e. β = 0. In general r/m = z/(2 cos β), giving x_min = h_w − z sin²α_t/(2 cos β). The tooth-count rule below it inherits the same restriction.
evidence: x_min = h_w − [ρ + sin α_t(r sin α_t − ρ)]/m with r = m z/(2 cos β).
proposal: Add '/cos β' or 'for a spur gear'.
validation: Reading check.

verdict.reason: The code takes r = m·z/(2 cos β) with m the normal module (auto.rs:117). Substituting ρ = 0 gives x_min = h_w − z sin²α_t/(2 cos β), and the tooth-count rule becomes z ≥ 2 h_w cos β / sin²α_t. The unqualified reduction is therefore spur-only. The same unqualified statement also appears in the auto.rs doc comment at :58, which the finding does not list. Both tests that pin it (auto.rs:2157 and :2193) use default spur params, so nothing exercises the helical form.

The test threshold at auto.rs:2172 uses `r = p.module * mid / 2.0` (β = 0).
verdict.corrected_claim: The reduction holds only at β = 0. The general form is h_w − z sin²α_t/(2 cos β). It is stated unqualified at reference.md:239 and at auto.rs:58.
verdict.proposal_note: Fix both locations. The 18/22-teeth table is correct as a spur (β = 0) statement and should say so.

title: 'Note::is(key), checked by the compiler' — it takes &str, and the crate's own test shows a mistyped key compiling
claim: corrections.md presents `Note::is(key)` as what makes text-matching unrepresentable, 'checked by the compiler'. The signature is `pub fn is(&self, key: &str)`, so any literal compiles; note.rs:437 asserts `!n.is("ring_addendum_clamp")`, a typo that compiles and returns false. Production callers do use `key::` constants, so this is a convention, not a type guarantee.
evidence: note.rs:398-400; grep of `.is(` finds only key:: constants in production.
proposal: Either make keys a newtype (`pub struct Key(&'static str)` with the constants as `Key`, and `is(&self, key: Key)`), which makes the claim true, or reword to 'by key constant, never by text'.
validation: With the newtype, `n.is("literal")` fails to compile (a compile-fail doctest).

verdict.reason: The signature does take &str, so the compiler checks nothing about a key passed to `is`. The guarantee is a convention: every production caller passes a key:: constant or a variable holding one (36 key:: call sites; params.rs:209 and shape.rs:5247 pass variables). The finding misreads note.rs:437, though. `!n.is("ring_addendum_clamp")` is a deliberate negative case asserting that a different key does not match, not a typo that slipped through. It still shows that an arbitrary literal compiles. What is enforced lies elsewhere: gear_io::strings fires every note and checks the catalogue both ways, which catches an unknown key raised by Note::new, but not a wrong key passed to `is`, which silently returns false.
verdict.evidence: note.rs:398: `pub fn is(&self, key: &str) -> bool`. note.rs:361: `pub fn new(key: &str)`. gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:335,342,373,596,936 build notes from bare `"ui.…"` literals. corrections.md:188: '*Now:* `Note::is(key)`, checked by the compiler'.
verdict.corrected_claim: 'Checked by the compiler' overstates it. Note::is takes &str, so a key passed as a literal is unchecked. Production code uses key:: constants by convention, and note.rs:437 is an intentional negative test, not a mistyped key.
verdict.proposal_note: A Key newtype would also have to cover Note::new, which gear-wasm calls with bare ui. literals that have no constants. Either give those keys constants too, or make `is` alone take the newtype. The cheaper fix is to reword corrections.md to 'by key constant, never by text'.

title: The crate still writes out the base pitch and the angular-play law inline, despite the 'one place' claims
claim: reference.md says the base pitch is `plane.rs`'s, in one place, and that angular play is 'one sentence for every mesh … mesh::angular_play'. shape.rs:3529 recomputes `PI * rack.mn * alpha_n.cos()` and :3532 writes `2π·slide/p_bn`, which is `angular_play × z` inlined. screw.rs:869 is a third copy of π m_n cos α_n.

title: The efficiency's 'independent numerical average' shares the helical cos β_b assumption and a looser tolerance than documented
claim: reference.md: 'Verified against a direct numerical average … over five meshes at three helix angles each, to 1e-10 relative.' The test divides its numeric average by the same `cos β_b` the closed form carries, so the helical factor is asserted on both sides rather than checked. The tolerance is 1e-9 absolute, not 1e-10 relative. The companion test `the_helical_efficiency_formula_reduces_exactly_at_zero_helix` pairs a spur path with a helical `g`, so its 'loss rises with helix' only restates the factor. Separately, `thickness_modification_equals_an_equivalent_profile_shift` compares two routes through the same `x + x_s` expression and cannot fail unless `thickness_shift()` is ignored altogether; the documented '4e-16' is not what it asserts (1e-14).
evidence: contact.rs:1729-1740: `numeric = 1 − mu·mean|ξ|·(1/rb1+1/rb2)/cos_bb`. tests/geometry_laws.rs:171-199.
proposal: Derive the helical factor independently: integrate μ·F_n·|v_s| over the contact lines of the helical face (F_n from torque and the flank normal, v_s from the two angular velocities at 3-D points) and divide by the input power. Assert the relative tolerance the document states. For k, check against a rack-generation measurement (verify.rs), which shares no algebra. Align the quoted tolerances with the asserted ones.
validation: Mutate the formula's cos β_b to 1 and confirm that the new test fails while the current one passes.

verdict.reason: The observations hold. The numeric side divides by the same `cos_bb` (contact.rs:1733-1735), so the helical factor sits on both sides of the comparison and is never measured. The test's own doc comment says it 'exercise[s] the cos β_b too', which overstates it. The tolerance is `< 1e-9` absolute, not the documented 1e-10 relative. The companion test fixes a spur path and varies only `g`, so its monotonicity restates the factor. The thickness test compares `x+x_s` against `x+x_s` (tooth.rs:833 vs the test's `profile_shift + x_s`), so it cannot catch an error in `thickness_shift()` itself; it only catches st ignoring it. It never checks the k-form `m(π/2·k + 2x tan α)` that the doc calls identical. It asserts 1e-14 where the doc says 4e-16, and it sweeps k over 5 values where the doc lists 3. The finding's validation step is wrong, though: if the closed form's cos β_b were mutated to 1, the current test would FAIL, because the numeric side keeps `/cos_bb`. So the current test does pin the implementation to the stated law. What it cannot catch is the law itself being wrong. I derived the law independently and it is correct. On parallel axes the relative angular velocity is axial, so the sliding velocity is perpendicular to the plane of action with magnitude ω_rel·ξ_t. Friction is μF_n with F_n = F_bt/cos β_b. Friction power over useful power therefore carries exactly 1/cos β_b. The gap is a test-independence and doc-accuracy issue, not a wrong answer.
verdict.evidence: contact.rs:1711-1747 read. The numeric side is `1 - mu*mean_abs_xi*(1/a.rb+1/b.rb)/cos_bb` and the assert is `(closed-numeric).abs() < 1e-9`. geometry_laws.rs:171-199 asserts `< 1e-14` on st of both routes. reference.md:86 says '4e-16', k ∈ {0.6,1.0,1.45}. tooth.rs:833-834: `x_thick = profile_shift + thickness_shift(); st = m(π/2 + 2 x_thick tan an)/cos β`.
verdict.corrected_claim: The efficiency test checks the closed form's averaging and its /ε_α bookkeeping against a numeric mean, but it takes the 1/cos β_b factor as given on both sides. The factor is physically correct (derivation above), yet no test measures it. The documented tolerances (1e-10 relative, 4e-16) do not match the asserted ones (1e-9 absolute, 1e-14). The thickness test is tautological with respect to x_s: it never compares against s_n = m(π/2·k + 2x tan α_n)/cos β.
verdict.proposal_note: A 3-D contact-line integration (effort M) is more than a textbook factor needs. The cheaper fix: (1) in the numeric average, compute the sliding velocity and the normal force from the gear axes directly (v_s = ω_rel·ξ_t, F_n = T/(r_b cos β_b) from the flank normal), or at least state in the doc that the factor is derived rather than measured. (2) Change the thickness test to compare `a.st` against the literal k-form `m(π/2·k + 2x tan α_n)/cos β`, which shares no x_s algebra. (3) Make the doc quote the tolerances the tests assert. The finding's validation (the mutant passes the current test) is wrong: the current test fails on that mutant.

title: The ring's smallest tooth count is computed in gear-wasm and ignores profile shift
claim: CLAUDE.md says all the mathematics is in gear-core and that the boundary is JSON in and JSON out. But the one engineering formula in gear-wasm, `smallest_tooth_count`, is `z > 2 h_a cosβ / (1 − cos α_t)`. It omits the ring's profile shift, while the core's own tip clamp uses `ra = r − m(h_a − x)`. It also ignores the thin-tooth limit the same clamp applies (ψ_b < 0). The gear tab shows this figure.
evidence: lib.rs:554-560: `let threshold = 2.0 * params.addendum * beta.cos() / (1.0 - alpha_t.cos());`, with no `profile_shift`. ring.rs:278: `let mut ra = r - m * (params.addendum - x);`, and the clamp CLAMP_RING_TIP_RAISED fires on that. The same formula is copied into the test ring.rs:1244, which only checks x = 0. Worked example at 20°, h_a = 1: x = −0.3 gives z_min = 2·1.3/0.0603 = 43.1, so 44, while the tab shows 34. x = +0.5 gives 17, while the tab shows 34. A designer who takes 36 teeth at x = −0.3 gets a clamped tip. It is the only trigonometry in gear-wasm outside its tests (grep of cos/sin/tan in non-test lib.rs lines 555-557).
proposal: Move the relation into gear-core, in ring.rs next to the clamp, as `Ring::smallest_teeth(params) -> u32`. It should include `(h_a − x)` and the ψ_b thickness limit, ideally by searching the smallest z at which `Ring::cut_by` raises no CLAMP_RING_TIP_RAISED, so the readout and the clamp are one rule. gear-wasm then calls it. Delete the copy in the test and have the test call the core function.
validation: Law: for a grid of (x, h_a, α_n, β, k), `Ring::cut_by` at the reported z raises no tip clamp and at z−1 it does. This is the existing test extended to x ≠ 0 and routed through the function the tab reads. Add a check_wasm probe with a shifted ring.

verdict.reason: The claim holds as stated. `smallest_tooth_count` (gear-wasm lib.rs:554-561) computes `2 h_a cosβ/(1−cos α_t)` from `params` and never reads `profile_shift`. `Ring::cut_by` places the tip at `ra = r − m(h_a − x)` (ring.rs:278) and raises CLAMP_RING_TIP_RAISED when `ra < rb`. So on any shifted ring the readout and the clamp disagree. The field's own doc comment (lib.rs:533-534) says 'the fewest teeth this design could have had and still cleared its own base circle', which is false once x ≠ 0. The only other copy is the test at ring.rs:1244, which sweeps x = 0 only, so no test covers the shift. I rated it medium rather than high: the figure is advisory, and the core clamp still names the problem on the gear actually built. The thin-tooth sub-claim is weaker than written. The ψ_b < 0 limit normally bites on large rings (about 105+ teeth at 20°), so it is an upper bound, not the smallest count. It enters the smallest count only through a large positive x or k.
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-lens-docs-accuracy-1-1 (Ring::cut_by with the default cutter, 20°, h_a = 1) printed the first z with no tip clamp. At x = −0.3 it is 44: z = 36 clamps (ra = rb = 16.9145) and z = 43 clamps. At x = 0 it is 34. At x = +0.5 it is 17: z = 17 gives ra 8.0000 against rb 7.9874, with no clamp. The wasm readout is 34 at every x. This matches the closed form `ceil(2(h_a − x)cosβ/(1 − cos α_t))`: 2·1.3/0.0603 = 43.1, so 44.
verdict.proposal_note: Moving it into gear-core is correct. It is an engineering number computed outside the core, which breaks rule 1 in spirit. The closed form is simple: `z_min = ceil(2(h_a − x) cosβ / (1 − cos α_t))`. Prefer it to searching z for the absence of CLAMP_RING_TIP_RAISED. That clamp also fires on the thin-tooth limit at large z, so the clamp-free set is a band, not a half-line. A 'smallest z with no clamp' search is well defined only if it starts from below. A more honest readout would give both ends of the band, the smallest and the largest tooth count, since ψ_b < 0 is the other end. Also note: x here is a user input. If the shape solves the ring's shift, the gear tab and the train would read different x's.

title: state.md says Y_S is applied; no rating applies it
claim: '`Y_S` and `Y_B` are applied and everything else is declined' (state.md:296). The Decided table repeats it: '`Y_S` and `Y_B` are the exceptions and are applied' (state.md:617). The rating uses Dolan–Broghamer K_f in place of Y_S. state.md:730 itself says 'nothing the train rates applies `Y_S`'.
evidence: strength.rs:1512 is the rating path: `section.bending_factor(RootStressModel::DolanBroghamer)`. RootStressModel::Iso6336, which is Y_S, is reached only from gear-cli/src/matrix.rs and from tests. The 'One bending model, and it is the NASA one' section of state.md says the same.
proposal: Rewrite both sentences. The notch factor is Dolan–Broghamer K_f, which replaced ISO's Y_S. Y_B, the rim factor, is applied when a rim is given. Y_β, f_ε and Y_DT are declined. The argument that a factor is kept unless it is half of a balanced pair then applies to Y_B alone, and K_f's own reason for replacing Y_S is argued under 'One bending model'.
validation: grep for RootStressModel::Iso6336 outside strength.rs, matrix.rs and the tests returns nothing, and the state.md sentences agree with that.

verdict.reason: The claim holds. state.md:296 and state.md:617 both say `Y_S` is applied. The rating calls `section.bending_factor(RootStressModel::DolanBroghamer)` (strength.rs:1512). `RootStressModel::Iso6336` is reached only from gear-cli/src/matrix.rs and from tests/bending.rs. state.md's own later text agrees with the code, not with those two sentences: line 730 says 'nothing the train rates applies `Y_S`', and the 'One bending model' table at line 827 records Y_S being replaced by K_f. The argument at 296-300 (Y_S is kept because it is not half of a balanced pair) is therefore arguing for a factor the tool no longer uses.
verdict.evidence: grep for RootStressModel::Iso6336 outside strength.rs returns only crates/gear-core/tests/bending.rs:216,357,459 and crates/gear-cli/src/matrix.rs:94,119,416. strength.rs:1512 reads `section.bending_factor(RootStressModel::DolanBroghamer)`. state.md:827: '| notch factor | ISO `Y_S`, fitted to the tangent section | Dolan–Broghamer `K_f`, fitted to this one |'.

title: A crossed pair is said to have no contact ratio; MeshReport gives one
claim: 'A crossed pair has none of it — its line of action slides rather than turning, so there is no such angle and no contact ratio to report' (state.md, 'Every parallel-axis mesh reports the same things'). Every mesh, crossed ones included, reports `contact_ratio`, and for a point contact it is measured along the line of action. The same list's hunting (`coprime`) and both-way efficiency are also reported for crossed meshes.
evidence: mod.rs:216-227: `contact_ratio` is documented as 'a point contact's along its line of action'. `gear-cli crossed 17 23 90` prints ε = 1.758113579. README and state.md themselves quote the crossed construction's ε = 1.777921670.
proposal: Say what a crossed mesh actually lacks: the operating pressure angle and the transverse/overlap split. Its contact ratio is the point contact's (see MeshReport::point), and its efficiency differs by direction.
validation: The sentence matches the fields that are Some or None on a crossed MeshReport in the `train mixed` golden output.

verdict.reason: The claim holds. `MeshReport::contact_ratio` is documented for both contacts (mod.rs:216-227: 'a point contact's along its line of action'). `coprime` and `efficiency` (a Directional) are fields on every MeshReport, crossed meshes included. The harness prints a contact ratio for a crossed pair. What a crossed mesh actually lacks is the `line: Option<LineContact>` block: `operating_pressure_angle` and the transverse/overlap `contact_ratios` live there (mod.rs, about lines 344-347 of the struct region). The state.md sentence ('no such angle and no contact ratio to report') is right about the angle and wrong about the ratio.
verdict.evidence: `gear-cli crossed 17 23 90` prints ε 1.758113579 in its table and 1.7581 in the 'least shift…' rows. MeshReport fields: coprime, contact_ratio, efficiency, locking_friction, sliding_ratio, cases, backlash, row_play, flank_interference, tips, notes, `line: Option<LineContact>` (operating_pressure_angle, contact_ratios) and `point: Option<PointContact>`. README.md:212-215 and state.md:188-190 quote the crossed ε themselves.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposed wording is good. It could also say that the headline sentence 'Every parallel-axis mesh reports the same things' is now true of every mesh for the shared fields, with only `line`/`point` differing.

title: The 1.1-million-case claim for the flow is 179,280 cases of the closed form
claim: 'that form never refused a driving input across **1.1 million** combinations, which `planetary::tests::a_driving_input_always_has_a_flow` still holds for the flow every path and case asks.' The test sweeps 179,280 combinations and calls `planetary::power`, the Pennestrì closed-form oracle. It never calls train/flow.rs.
evidence: The loops are zs 1..=119 step 2 (60 values), zr 1..=249 step 3 (83), 6 values of η0 and 6 arrangements: 60·83·6·6 = 179,280. The test's own floor is `checked > 100_000`. The body calls `power(i0, arrangement, 1.0, 1.0, eta0)`, which is crate::planetary.
proposal: Say '179,280 combinations of the closed form'. Say the flow is held to that form on every arrangement by flow.rs's and shape.rs's tests, and name them (e.g. every_arrangement_of_a_set_solves). Better still, have the test print its count so check_figures can tag the number.
validation: The count matches the loop product, and a named test that runs flow.rs against `power` exists.

verdict.reason: The named test does sweep 179,280 combinations (60 × 83 × 6 η0 × 6 arrangements), not 1.1 million, and it calls `crate::planetary::power`, the closed form, not flow.rs. So the sentence misdescribes what the test holds. The 1.1 million figure is not invented, though. Commit e725dd4 records a one-off sweep over the full grid, sun 1..119 × ring 1..249 × 6 η0 × 6 arrangements = 1,066,716, about 1.1 M. The standing test is a 1-in-6 subsample of that grid. The corrected claim is that the doc attributes a one-off 1.1 M sweep to a standing test that checks 179,280. The link from the closed form to the flow is a separate claim, held by other tests (flow.rs:463 `the_per_mesh_flow_is_pennestri_on_a_simple_set`, shape.rs:4422, mod.rs:6538).
verdict.evidence: planetary.rs:381-395: `(1..=119).step_by(2)` (60), `(1..=249).step_by(3)` (83), 6 η0 values, 6 arrangements. Python: 60·83·36 = 179,280. `git show e725dd4` message: 'refused never, across 1.1 million combinations — sun 1..119 against ring 1..249, eta0 from 0.999 down to 0.3, all six arrangements'. 119·249·36 = 1,066,716.
verdict.corrected_claim: state.md:791-794 attributes a one-off 1.1 M sweep (commit e725dd4, full grid 119 × 249 × 6 × 6) to `a_driving_input_always_has_a_flow`, which checks a 179,280-point subsample of that grid and calls the closed form `planetary::power`, not the flow. The flow is tied to the closed form by flow.rs:463 and shape.rs/mod.rs tests.
verdict.proposal_note: Keep both numbers honest: 'swept once over 1.1 million combinations (e725dd4); the test keeps a 179,280-point subsample of that grid standing, on the closed form, which flow.rs's `the_per_mesh_flow_is_pennestri_on_a_simple_set` holds the flow to'. The idea of having the test print its count is not worth the effort. The count is a loop product, so state the grid instead.

title: The hula crank is called a closed-form solve; it is a bracket walk plus Brent
claim: 'The hula stage reports that bound rather than acting on it — its crank offset is a closed-form solve on the tips, and an addendum moving with the shift would put an iteration inside it.' Since the hula solver retired, the tip-sized distance is found by growing steps (step = 1 % of the distance, ×1.5, at most 40 outward or 80 inward) and then `brent`. Every evaluation rebuilds a closed plan. The premise of the argument is false: the solve is already iterative.
evidence: shape.rs:1629-1690: 'Bracket the root by growing steps … then close in', with `for _ in 0..40` and `for _ in 0..80`, then `crate::solve::brent(room_at, lo, hi, …)` at 1693.
proposal: Either re-argue the decision on current grounds, for example that an addendum moving with the shift makes room_at non-monotone so the bracket is lost (and measure it), or apply the `no sharp tip` bound on the hula arrangement as on every other member and delete the exception. In either case remove 'closed-form'.
validation: If the bound is applied: every hula fixture in the golden corpus still solves, and hula_recorded moves only where the tip-width bound bites. If the exception is kept: a test showing the non-monotonicity the new argument claims.

verdict.reason: The premise is false, as the finding claims, and the situation is stronger than the finding says: the exception the sentence defends no longer exists in code. The tip-sized distance is found by a growing-step bracket (for _ in 0..40 outward, 0..80 inward) and then `brent` (shape.rs:1629-1693), not by a closed form. Each `room_at` evaluation builds the members through `Shape::params_at` (shape.rs:1115-1126). For every non-ring member, `params_at` applies `MemberGear::addendum_asked` at the trial shift, which is the `no_sharp_tip` bound (mod.rs:1236-1258). `tip_room` builds with params_at too (shape.rs:1530-1533). So the hula's wobble gears (external members) already have their addendum move with the shift inside the iteration, which is exactly what the sentence says the hula avoids. The only exemption is for rings, and it covers every ring, not the hula specifically. The sentence also still speaks of a 'hula stage', a type that has been retired.
verdict.evidence: shape.rs:1115-1126: `if self.members[i].ring.is_some() { return with_shift; } GearParams { addendum: self.members[i].gear.addendum_asked(&with_shift).used, ..with_shift }`. shape.rs:1530: `Tooth::new(self.params_at(m.a, x[m.a], helix))` inside tip_room. arrangements.rs:490-535: `hula()` sets no exception on no_sharp_tip (the default is true, mod.rs:1305). The sentence dates from commit 8cb9c12.
verdict.proposal_note: Neither option in the proposal is needed as a code change. The bound is already applied to the hula's external members, and rings are exempt uniformly. Just delete the sentence at state.md:449-452, or replace it with 'a ring's addendum is not held to a tip width, on any arrangement' if that exemption is what should be recorded. As a safeguard, a test could set a large min_tip_width on a hula's wobble gear and check that the addendum clamp note fires and the crank still solves.

title: The canary section contradicts itself and the bending section
claim: There are three errors. (1) 'Two figures have survived every refactor unchanged', followed at once by the strength canary moving twice and the worm canary several times. (2) 'The worm canary has moved four times', followed by a list numbered 1 to 5. (3) 'What it did to the numbers' says 'The strength canary moved once, deliberately: σ_F 69.2 / 63.4 → 74.3 / 63.8', while the canary table and README give 66.8 / 56.0 after two moves.

title: README says nix flake check is everything CI checks
claim: README Getting started says '`nix flake check` # everything CI checks: build, clippy, fmt, tests'. CI also runs nix build .#web, check_doc_links, check_strings, check_bindings, npm run check, check_golden, check_figures, check_units, check_wasm and validate_dxf. That is ten more. CLAUDE.md says 'nix flake check is **not** all of them', and records two red builds from a list shorter than CI's. state.md 'Running it' says 'Before pushing, run all four', and its tool block leaves out check_units.py, check_wasm.sh and validate_dxf.py: the omission CLAUDE.md records as costing a red build. ci.yml's own comments have the same drift: 'Everything CI needs to check: build, clippy --deny warnings, fmt, tests' above nine more steps, and deploy's 'the four consistency checks'.

verdict.reason: README.md:73 says '# everything CI checks: build, clippy, fmt, tests'. flake.nix:174-193 defines only four checks (build, clippy, fmt, test). ci.yml runs nine more steps after `nix flake check`: nix build .#web, check_doc_links, check_strings, check_bindings, npm run check, check_golden plus check_figures, check_units, check_wasm and validate_dxf. ci.yml has the same drift inside itself. Its comment above `nix flake check` reads 'Everything CI needs to check: build, clippy --deny warnings, fmt, tests'. Its deploy comment (line 141) lists 'the four consistency checks, the typecheck and the independent DXF read', which leaves out nix build .#web, check_units and check_wasm. docs/state.md:45 says 'Before pushing, run all four', and its tool block leaves out check_units.py, check_wasm.sh and validate_dxf.py. CLAUDE.md records exactly this omission (check_units) as the cause of a red build. state.md also says the mistake 'has cost one red build' while CLAUDE.md says two, a small inconsistency of its own. CLAUDE.md:162 (its checks table) is correct and should not be listed as a fault location.
verdict.evidence: Ran `grep -n 'everything CI\|all four\|four consistency'`: hits at README.md:73, docs/state.md:45 and ci.yml:141. Read flake.nix checks = {build, clippy, fmt, test}. Read the full ci.yml step list and state.md lines 29-58.

Note that CI runs the tools through `nix develop --command`, and the DXF step writes to /tmp, so the script should keep those semantics. Also fix the two ci.yml comments.
