proposal: Report ζ at both ends of the path per member in MeshReport, via one expression, one label ×5 and a readout on the mesh card. Optionally add `Objective::BalancedSliding` to auto::maximise (|ζ_1(start)| = |ζ_2(end)|) as a second, user-picked objective for the existing search.
validation: Against textbook values (Niemann/Winter tables for a 20° standard pair). Law: ζ_1 = 0 at the pitch point, and ζ_1(ξ)·ζ_2(ξ) relation 1/(1−ζ_1)+... identity: (1−ζ_1)(1−ζ_2) = 1 at every ξ.

verdict.reason: The gap is real: nothing in the core or the UI computes specific sliding. The closed form and the proposed law both hold. One supporting fact is wrong: the library has 5 polymers among its 8 materials (POM plus four PA grades), not 6. The '6 of 8' figure in the docs counts materials with no S-N data, which includes the brass. Two parts of the proposal are also imprecise, as the proposal note explains.
verdict.corrected_claim: Specific sliding ζ_i(ξ) = 1 − ω_jρ_j/(ω_iρ_i) is closed form from Mesh::curvature_radii and the tooth-count ratio, and it is not reported. MeshReport::sliding_ratio is a different quantity: pitch-point sliding over pitch-line speed, which is zero on parallel shafts. 5 of the 8 library materials are polymers.
verdict.evidence: grep for 'specific sliding' or 'specific_sliding' in crates, docs and web/src finds nothing. mesh.rs:543 gives curvature_radii(xi) = (rb1·tanα_w + ξ, rb2·tanα_w − ξ). MeshReport::sliding_ratio (train/mod.rs:248-256) is documented as 'exactly zero on parallel ones', so it is not ζ. materials_default.toml has 2 steels, brass C360, POM, PA6, PA6 GF30, PA GF50 and PA GF70. An independent Python check on a 17/43, m2, 20° standard pair (notes/verify-lens-feature-gaps-2/zeta.py) gives ζ1(A) = −9.954, ζ2(A) = 0.909, ζ1(E) = 0.607, ζ2(E) = −1.542, ζ = 0 at the pitch point, and (1−ζ1)(1−ζ2) = 1.0000000000000002 at every point.
verdict.proposal_note: Put ζ in LineContact, not in the shared MeshReport. On a point contact the sliding at the pitch point is not zero and the definition must be restated as |v_slide|/|v_rolling,i| through contact::sliding_velocity. Doing that would give one expression for both contacts. Write it with the signed ρ2 and signed z2 convention, not with magnitudes, so that an internal mesh needs no branch. auto::maximise takes a closure (auto.rs:1614), so it needs no `Objective` enum. A balanced-sliding objective belongs where shape.rs builds the closure, and it should be a user-visible choice beside efficiency.

title: Lubrication regime (film thickness, λ) fits the Hertz/contact data but only as an explicit fitted feature
claim: Every non-lubricant input to an EHL film estimate is already in the solve: the reduced radius along the path (curvature_radii), the load per unit length (F_bn/L), E*, the rolling speeds (body speeds from the motion times ρ_i), and κ for crossed pairs. What is missing is lubricant data (viscosity at oil temperature, pressure-viscosity α) and surface roughness per member. Dowson–Higginson and Hamrock–Dowson are regressions, which rationale.md's no-fits rule excludes from the mathematics. The owner's rule allows estimates as explicit user-visible features, as load sharing already is. μ is already a user input 'depending on lubrication', so a λ readout would tell the designer whether their μ is plausible.
evidence: The hertz.rs module doc rejects Hamrock–Dowson's κ fit for the solve. contact.rs:367 says μ depends on lubrication, speed, finish and temperature. No viscosity, roughness or film field exists (grep: 'viscos' and 'film' find nothing).
proposal: An opt-in mesh input `lubricant: Option<{η0 Pa·s, α 1/GPa}>` plus a per-member Ra. Report h_min(ξ) at the pitch point and at the single-pair points, and λ = h_min/√(Ra1²+Ra2²), labelled as Dowson–Higginson (line) or Hamrock–Dowson (point) with the fit named in the note. It changes no rating.
validation: Against Hamrock–Dowson's published worked example and an independent Python evaluation from tools/. Law: h_min is continuous across the line/point seam at Σ → 0 within the stated difference of the two fits, and that seam must be measured and recorded as the contact seams are.

verdict.reason: Accurate as stated. The solve has no viscosity, film or roughness field. The hertz.rs module doc and rationale.md reject Hamrock–Dowson's κ fit inside the mathematics. A film estimate is legitimate only as an explicit, labelled feature, which is what the proposal says. It is a feature idea, not a defect.
verdict.evidence: grep -i 'viscos|film|roughness' over gear-core/src, strings_en.toml and docs/*.md finds nothing relevant (the 'ra' hits are tip radii). hertz.rs:38-41 and rationale.md:462-468 refuse the κ fit. contact.rs:367-369 says 'μ is a mesh input ... depends on lubrication, speed, finish and temperature'. The only user-visible estimate today is LoadSharing::LinearRamp (contact.rs:935-948), which is the precedent the proposal cites.
verdict.proposal_note: Dowson–Higginson and Hamrock–Dowson hard-EHL fits do not apply to 5 of the 8 library materials. A polymer pair runs in the isoviscous-elastic (soft-EHL) regime, so the feature must choose the regime from the elasticity parameter (Hamrock–Dowson's regime map) or refuse polymers with a note. Viscosity depends on temperature, so η0 is meaningless without a temperature, which ties this to finding 8's thermal step. Write down the line/point seam as a known discontinuity between two fits. Do not hold it to a continuity law.

title: Power lost per mesh (W) and a thermal/tooth-temperature check are absent; for polymers temperature governs the allowable
claim: The flow already knows each mesh's loss in each case, but only ratios cross the boundary (efficiency, and power through over power in). The designer never sees watts dissipated, which is the input to any thermal decision. Six of the eight library materials are polymers quoted at 23 °C / 50 % RH. Polymer gear allowables fall steeply with tooth temperature (VDI 2736's central check), and there is no temperature input or estimate, so a POM or PA gear running warm is rated at room-temperature strength.
evidence: The strings have power-ratio labels only (train_circulation, train_mesh_power_through); grep finds no 'W', 'watt' or 'loss' readout. The materials TOML header states the polyamides are 'quoted CONDITIONED, at 23 °C'. grep finds no 'temperature' input anywhere in core or UI.
proposal: Step 1 (S): report each mesh's power lost in W per case, P·(1−η) with the power from the case's torque and speed, and the train's total, in Rust. Step 2 (M): an opt-in thermal estimate, labelled as one: ambient temperature, a housing or open-gear heat-transfer coefficient × area (user input) → steady oil/body temperature. For polymers, a VDI 2736-2 tooth-temperature estimate, shown beside the allowable with the note that the library value is at 23 °C. Step 3: a temperature column in the material data if it is ever sourced.
validation: Step 1: a law that the per-mesh losses sum to P_in − P_out for every preset and case (flow already balances). Step 2: VDI 2736's worked example evaluated independently in tools/.

verdict.reason: Step 1 holds exactly. flow.rs documents that each mesh's loss is (1−η) × mesh_powers × P_in, and every case carries a torque in N·m and a speed in rpm. Loss in watts is therefore one multiplication that only Rust may do (rule 1), and nothing reports it. The temperature half is true but overstated as a new discovery: rationale.md already names VDI 2736-2 as what would change the polymer allowables and says it is paywalled, so step 2 is blocked on a source, as the project records. A smaller related gap is confirmed: Material.condition ('conditioned, 23 °C / 50 % RH') crosses the wire and is never rendered, so the designer never sees the temperature an allowable is quoted at. Severity is low, not medium: no figure is wrong, and the missing thermal model is the project's own recorded limit.
verdict.corrected_claim: Per-mesh power loss in W is directly available (flow.rs:139-147 and 330-333: 'each mesh's loss is (1 − η) of it exactly') and not reported. No temperature model exists, and the state a polymer's allowable is quoted at (Material.condition) is never shown in the panel.
verdict.evidence: The en strings have only the ratio labels train_circulation and train_mesh_power_through (strings_en.toml:520-524), and no watt or loss readout. Load carries torque in N·m and speed in rpm (train/mod.rs:2874-2888), and CaseBody carries speed and torque. MeshCase::power_through is a ratio (mod.rs:311-326). grep -rni temperature over gear-core/src finds only the comment at contact.rs:368. rationale.md:1605: 'What would change this: ISO 6336-5 or VDI 2736-2, both paywalled'. web/src never reads `.condition`: grep finds only comments at TrainPanel.svelte:1034 and 1187-1197, and the material select at TrainPanel.svelte:1644-1645 shows m.name only.
verdict.proposal_note: Do step 1 (MeshCase::power_lost in W, and a train total per case). Use the law sum(loss) = P_in − P_out over the ports. It follows from the driving-side definition and should hold on every preset, circulating ones included. Put Material.condition beside the material's name on the card now, at no cost. Step 2 cannot be validated against VDI 2736's worked example without the paywalled standard, so record it under 'Decided, not pending' or 'Not built' with that reason. Do not build it from secondary sources.

title: No dynamic disclosure; a mesh-resonance ratio is derivable without K_v
claim: K_v is declined as population-calibrated, which is defensible. The mechanics under it are not calibrated: the resonance ratio N = n / n_E1, with n_E1 = (30000/(π z_1))·√(c_γ/m_red), is a single-DOF natural frequency from the reduced mass and the mesh stiffness. The crate can compute the reduced mass from density and geometry (the density is already a material field), and c_γ comes from the stiffness model or a user input. Reporting N and naming the resonance band as a note, with no stress factor, fits the 'say what is not modelled next to the number' rule.
evidence: grep: 'dynamic' has no hits in the core. `density` is carried per material (strings train_density, train_kg_m3) and is used for nothing a rating reads.
proposal: After the stiffness finding, or with c_γ as a labelled input: add MeshReport.resonance_ratio per case and a note `mesh.near_resonance` when 0.85 < N < 1.15 (ISO's main resonance band, cited as a band rather than applied as a factor).
validation: Against ISO 6336-1 Formula for n_E1 on a hand example. Law: N scales as n·z_1·√m_red, checked by doubling each input.

verdict.reason: The gap is real: nothing in the core concerns dynamics, and density feeds no rating. The claim that the result is 'derivable without calibration' is wrong on two counts. First, c_γ is not available. The crate has no stiffness model; state.md 'Worth doing next' lists a calibrated mesh-stiffness model as future work, and ISO 6336-1's own c′/c_γ is an empirical fit (q′ polynomial, C_M, C_R, C_B), which the no-fits rule excludes. Second, m_red in ISO's n_E1 comes from the gear bodies' polar inertias, J/r_b². The crate knows only the toothed rim, not the web, hub or shaft. The SDOF reading is also ISO's method for a single pair, not for trains or planetary sets. The main resonance band is also not a fixed 0.85-1.15: its lower bound N_S depends on load (N_S = 0.5 + 0.35·√(F_t·K_A/(b·100)) for light loads, otherwise 0.85).
verdict.corrected_claim: A resonance ratio could be reported only with c_γ and body inertia given as labelled user inputs (or as a solid-disc assumption stated as one), for a single pair. It is not derivable from what the solve holds today.
verdict.evidence: grep -rni 'dynamic|resonan|natural freq' over gear-core/src gives no hits. Density occurs only in material.rs and in a test fixture at train/mod.rs:1815; the UI shows it at TrainPanel.svelte:1655. contact.rs:943-946 calls LoadSharing a 'placeholder for a stiffness model'. state.md 'Worth doing next' lists 'A calibrated mesh-stiffness model'. rationale.md:580 declines K_v.
verdict.proposal_note: If this is done, make c_γ and each member's body inertia explicit inputs, not derived from density × rim. Report N for a lone pair only, and state the band as ISO's, with its load-dependent lower bound. Otherwise record it under 'Decided, not pending', next to K_v, as blocked on a stiffness model.

title: Ratio-per-tooth sensitivity is computed on every solve and never shown
claim: PathReport.per_tooth rebuilds the kinematic system once per member per path on every solve. It is marked serde(skip) and 'the panel shows none of it', although its own doc says it is 'what a designer choosing counts wants'. It is paid for in the solve that runs on every keystroke and delivered only to the harness.
evidence: mod.rs:3914–3920: '**Not sent**: the harness records it; the panel shows none of it.' Plus #[serde(skip)]. per_tooth closure at 3437 calls train.system_counting per member.
proposal: Either expose it (the natural home is a tooth-count sensitivity row on each gear card: ratio at z+1 and z−1, which also serves a target-ratio workflow) or compute it only on demand, through a harness-only entry or a flag on solve_train, so the interactive solve does not pay for it. Generalising it to numeric sensitivities (∂ output/∂ input by central difference on any input, cheap at µs solves) would give the uncertainty-propagation feature on one mechanism.
validation: If exposed: bindings and wasm probe record it. If made lazy: the corpus is unchanged and a timing comparison on the layshaft-then-compound fixture.

verdict.reason: per_tooth is computed on every solve and deliberately not sent. The cost is real but small. Measured by skipping the closure in a worktree, it is about 5-70 µs per solve: roughly 15-18 % on small parallel and epicyclic presets and about 1 % on crossed ones. 'dead-code' is the wrong category. The harness reads it (gear-cli kinematics.rs:453, graph.rs:109, golden tools/golden/kinematics.txt 'one more tooth'), Alone exposes it (mod.rs:3236), and a law tests it (mod.rs:11263). Keeping it core-side and off the wire is a documented decision (corrections.md:681). The remaining point stands: its own doc says a designer choosing tooth counts wants it, and the panel never shows it.
verdict.corrected_claim: PathReport::per_tooth is harness- and test-read, and not sent by decision. It costs about 15-18 % of a small parallel or epicyclic train's solve (about 60-70 µs) on every keystroke, and about 1 % on crossed ones. Either show it, which its doc argues for, or compute it on demand.
verdict.evidence: Timing probe against HEAD and against a worktree with `per_tooth: per_tooth(a, b)` replaced by an empty Vec. Best of 5 × 200 solves, release build: Spur 63.9→59.4 µs, Idler 188.7→167.6, Layshaft 393.1→323.3, Planetary 204.8→185.0, Wolfrom 265.4→245.2, Compound 401.9→355.9, MeshedPlanets 393.2→346.5, Worm 1696→1728 (noise), Planocentric 2513→2511. Output in notes/verify-lens-feature-gaps-2/timing.txt. Doc at mod.rs:3914-3920 ('Not sent: the harness records it; the panel shows none of it'). corrections.md:681 records the decision to skip.
verdict.proposal_note: Showing it is the better choice, per gear as 'ratio at z+1', for a target-ratio workflow. The absolute saving from making it lazy is tens of µs, not worth a flag on solve_train. The generalisation to numeric sensitivities is a separate feature and should not be sold as this finding's fix.

title: Bevel gears do not fit the screw model and break the 'sign is the mesh kind's' rule; face, hypoid and non-circular gears are XL
claim: Bevel geometry is conical (Tredgold's virtual cylindrical gear for tooth form and rating, ISO 10300), not a limit of the cylindrical screw/axode model: the screw model degenerates at a = 0. Kinematics would be cheap, since kinematics.rs needs only signed counts, but a bevel differential needs the two side-gear meshes to carry opposite signs relative to a common axis direction. The sign depends on axis orientation and which side of the apex each gear sits, not on MeshKind, which is the only source of sign by design (wiring.rs:40–47). The refactor handoff predicted this. Hypoid gears need the full crossed-axis conical geometry, face gears a new generation model, and non-circular gears break the constant exact-rational ratio every flow and kinematics law rests on.
evidence: MeshKind has External and Internal only, and wiring writes zb = m.kind.signed(zb). The handoff notes that 'Bevel side-gear pairs, face gears, and worm sets break it'.
proposal: If bevels are wanted: (1, M) give each axis a signed direction and derive a mesh's sign from the two axis directions and the apex side (a parameter replacing the MeshKind-only rule, with MeshKind remaining the parallel special case). This alone lets a bevel differential's motion, flow and efficiency be modelled with a user-given η. (2, XL) Conical tooth geometry and a rating via the virtual cylindrical gear, labelled as ISO 10300's approximation. Leave face, hypoid and non-circular gears out of scope and record them in 'Decided, not pending' with the reason (new generation mathematics, no constant ratio).
validation: Step 1: a bevel differential's Willis relation ω1+ω2 = 2ωc, and tools/train_kinematics.py extended with 3D rigid-body velocities.

verdict.reason: Accurate, and correctly marked info. MeshKind has only External and Internal. wiring.rs makes the sign the mesh kind's by design ('the fault has to be made unrepresentable'). A bevel differential's two side-gear meshes need opposite signs relative to one axis direction while both are 'external', and no MeshKind value gives that without mislabelling geometry. The screw model's crossed cylinders need a = r1 + r2 > 0, so it cannot become a bevel. Nothing in docs/ says bevel, hypoid, face or non-circular gears are out of scope: grep for 'bevel' finds only the withdrawn 'beveloid' reading in corrections.md:421-422. So the scope gap is undocumented, and recording it is warranted.
verdict.evidence: mesh.rs:49-56 (enum MeshKind { External, Internal }). wiring.rs:40-46 ('# The sign is the mesh kind's ... made unrepresentable rather than merely detectable'). geartrain-refactor-handoff.md:79: 'Bevel side-gear pairs, face gears, and worm sets break it. One stored field per mesh keeps bevel differentials in scope later'. grep -in 'bevel|hypoid|face gear|non-circular' over docs/*.md finds only corrections.md:421-422.
verdict.proposal_note: Signed axis directions plus apex side is the right parameter under rule 4, and it keeps the unrepresentability the wiring doc argues for. Do not reintroduce a free stored sign as the handoff suggested. Until then, add one row to state.md's 'Decided, not pending' or 'Not built' naming bevel, hypoid, face and non-circular gears and why.

title: Export is DXF only; SVG is a transcription of the bulge outline, STEP and a 3D view are large
claim: Vertex {x, y, bulge} converts directly to SVG path commands (bulge → arc radius chord/(2 sin(θ/2)), sweep from sign), so an SVG writer is under 100 lines in gear-io with the DXF writer's tests as the model. SVG serves laser cutting, documentation and the web. STEP needs B-spline or extruded-and-swept surfaces (a helical sweep for helical gears): L effort, high value for CAD users, whom DXF gives only a transverse section with no lead. A 3D view has no dependency on STEP and is L as well.
evidence: outline.rs:24–35 defines the bulge convention as 'a standard CAD construct'. The only export entry points are export_dxf and export_ring_dxf (gear_wasm.d.ts).
proposal: Add gear_io::svg::{gear_to_svg, ring_to_svg} beside dxf.rs, an `export_svg` wasm entry with its probe, and an 'Export SVG' button. Defer STEP. Tag the DXF export note that a helical gear's lead is not in the file.
validation: Read back with an independent SVG parser (e.g. svgpathtools in the venv): arc endpoints match the outline to 1e-9 mm, and area matches the DXF's (ezdxf) to the chord tolerance.

verdict.reason: Holds as stated. The only geometry exports are export_dxf and export_ring_dxf (crates/gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:737, 1024). Vertex {x,y,bulge} with bulge = tan(θ/4) (outline.rs:24-35) maps in closed form to an SVG elliptical-arc command: r = chord/(2 sin(θ/2)), large-arc flag = |θ|>π, sweep flag from the bulge's sign. gear_to_dxf/ring_to_dxf (dxf.rs:119-150) write a transverse section and carry no helix or lead. Neither dxf.rs, docs/reference.md#export-and-import (line 3036) nor the UI string gear_export_dxf='Export DXF' says that a helical gear's file is its transverse section only. So the small 'tag the note' part of the proposal is a real doc/UI gap too.
verdict.evidence: grep 'pub fn export_' crates/gear-wasm/src/lib.rs -> export_dxf, export_ring_dxf, export_materials, export_train only; grep -i 'helix|helical|lead|transverse' crates/gear-io/src/dxf.rs -> no match; outline.rs:26 'bulge is tan(θ/4) ... positive counter-clockwise'.
verdict.proposal_note: SVG's y-axis points down. The writer must either flip y (transform='scale(1,-1)') or invert the sweep flag, or every arc bows the wrong way. The validation should include a fixture where the difference is visible, such as an internal gear's bore. STEP is rightly deferred. A cheap first step is one sentence in reference.md#export-and-import and a field note on the export button: the DXF is the transverse section, and a helical gear's lead is not in it.

title: The geartrain has no drawing: a pair in mesh, or a set, is never seen
claim: The Viewport appears only in the gear tab, where it draws one gear. A train designer cannot see two members at their running distance and phase, which is where tip fouling, interference or an odd-looking shift is noticed. The only route is adopting a member into a gear tab, which shows it alone. The set drawing is 'Not planned', yet the placement it needs (planet phase for assembly) is already computed by Shape::assembly.
evidence: grep Viewport: GearPanel.svelte only. TrainPanel has lists and cards, no canvas. state.md:628: 'The viewport draws single gears; a set needs the carrier and N planets placed. Not planned'.
proposal: A mesh card's drawing: in Rust, a `mesh_profile(train, mesh)` entry returning both outlines placed (member b at the running distance, rotated by the closed-form phase that centres a tooth of a in a space of b, planets at their assembly angles for a replicated axis), drawn by the existing Viewport. No geometry is computed in TS, per rule 1. The set drawing is the same call over every mesh of a part.
validation: Law: at zero backlash the two outlines touch on the line of action and never overlap (polygon intersection area 0 within the chord tolerance). A planocentric fixture at its tip-clearing crank shows the tip gap equal to the reported tip_margin.

verdict.reason: There is a real gap: Viewport is used only in GearPanel.svelte, and TrainPanel has no canvas, so no train drawing exists. Two parts of the argument do not hold. (1) 'The placement it needs (planet phase for assembly) is already computed by Shape::assembly' is wrong. shape.rs:669 returns Option<(bool,bool)>, whether planets assemble equally spaced and whether simultaneously, and computes no angle or phase. (2) The claim that the drawing is where tip fouling or interference is noticed understates the numeric reporting. The shape already computes tip_interference and tip_margin (shape.rs:1540, arrangements.rs:1828-1860), and state.md:628 records the deliberate reason: 'nothing depends on it, and the set's numbers are all reported without it'. That reasoning is sound for correctness, so the drawing is a visual convenience, not a missing check. Medium overstates it.
verdict.evidence: grep -rln Viewport web/src -> web/src/GearPanel.svelte only (plus Viewport.svelte). shape.rs:669 'pub fn assembly(&self, axis: usize) -> Option<(bool, bool)>' ... 'Some((equal, simultaneous))'. state.md:628 '**Not planned** — nothing depends on it'.
verdict.corrected_claim: The train panel draws no mesh or set. Seeing two members at their running distance is a UI convenience the tool lacks. Fouling and interference are already reported numerically, and the planet placement angles are not computed anywhere: Shape::assembly only answers whether planets assemble. A drawing would need a new closed-form phase per mesh and per planet, not an existing result.
verdict.proposal_note: The mesh-drawing entry is sound and keeps rule 1 if the core returns placed outlines. The planet angles 2πk/N plus each planet's rotation phase must be derived fresh (φ_k = 2πk z_c/(N z_p) for the textbook simple set). They cannot be read off Shape::assembly, which would have to be extended or a sibling added. An eccentric/planocentric drawing also needs the crank angle.

title: All work is lost on reload or tab close, with no warning, and reload is the only way out of developer mode
claim: Tabs (gears and trains) live only in memory. The one stored key is the language. There is no beforeunload guard, so an accidental reload, back-navigation or tab close discards the whole session's design. The developer mode is 'left by reloading', so leaving it costs the user all open work. That is data loss in a plausible case. The stated reason, that copies in one browser should not cross, is met by sessionStorage, which is per tab, survives reload and never crosses to another copy.
evidence: grep beforeunload/sessionStorage/IndexedDB in web/src finds nothing. state.svelte.ts:36 says a view 'dies with the session, like everything here that is not the language'. rationale.md:2160 says 'A reload is the way out'.
proposal: Write the tabs' inputs (already the only state and already serialisable, since the train is TOML-exportable) to sessionStorage on change, debounced and wrapped in try/catch, and restore them on load, excluding the developer flag so a reload still leaves developer mode. Add a beforeunload prompt while any tab differs from its default. This is a UI-only change, with no engineering in TS.
validation: Playwright: edit a train, reload, and the same inputs and solved figures come back. A second tab opened fresh does not see them. Blocked storage still loads cleanly.

verdict.reason: Holds. No beforeunload, sessionStorage or IndexedDB exists anywhere in web/src. The only storage is localStorage 'gearcalc.language' (core.ts:459-482). state.svelte.ts:36 and :439-449 say tabs die with the session, and a reload is the way out of developer mode. It is worse than stated for gear tabs: a train can be exported to TOML (import_train/export_train), but a gear tab has no save route at all. Its only export is DXF, which cannot be read back, so a reload loses a gear design irrecoverably. No document argues that losing work on reload is desirable. The 'Two copies in one browser' rationale (state.md:71) is about nothing crossing between copies, and sessionStorage satisfies that. Severity is medium rather than high because trains can be saved to a file and a gear's inputs are few.
verdict.evidence: grep -n 'beforeunload|sessionStorage|localStorage|indexedDB' web/src -> only core.ts:464,482 (language). grep import_train/export_train -> core.ts only for trains; GearPanel.svelte has no import or document route. rationale.md:2155 'A reload is the way out, and a reload already returns everything else here to its default'.
verdict.proposal_note: Restoring tabs while leaving the developer flag unstored reintroduces the fault the developer mode's 'it only opens' rule exists to prevent (state.svelte.ts:445-449, rationale#a-hidden-input-is-still-an-input). A restored tab can be of kind 'eccentric', which the picker no longer lists after a reload. The restore must either convert or drop developer-only kinds, or re-enable developer mode when a restored tab needs it. rationale.md:2150-2160 and state.svelte.ts's comments then need rewriting, since the 'reload returns everything to its default' argument goes. Also note that a browser's 'Duplicate tab' copies sessionStorage, which is harmless here.

title: No undo; destructive edits apply on one click; the dry run is hover/focus-only and cannot be seen on touch
claim: A removal 'takes what goes with it' (a cascade), and it is applied by `onclick={() => make(o)}` at once. The only warning is the preview shown on mouseenter/focus, and a tap on a touch screen presses the button before any preview is visible. There is no undo, although the core guarantees every add undoes (the every_add_undoes law) and inputs are the whole state, so a snapshot stack is trivial.
evidence: Offers.svelte: onmouseenter/onfocus show the preview, onclick makes the edit, and make() clears the preview. grep undo/history in web/src finds nothing. The class:danger styling marks removals but does not confirm them.
proposal: Keep a bounded stack of prior train inputs per tab in state.svelte.ts (a structuredClone before each editTrain), bound to Ctrl/Cmd-Z and Ctrl-Shift-Z plus an Undo button beside the offers strip. On coarse pointers (matchMedia('(pointer: coarse)')), make the first tap on an entry show its dry run and the second tap apply it.
validation: Playwright: remove a mesh with a cascade, then undo, and the train serialises byte-identical to before. Touch emulation: the first tap shows the preview and does not edit.

verdict.reason: Holds. Offers.svelte's entry snippet shows the dry run on onmouseenter/onfocus and applies the edit onclick={() => make(o)}. make() calls editTrain at once and clears 'over'. On touch, focus and click fire in the same tap, so the preview is never seen before the edit. There is no confirm(), no pointer-coarse handling and no undo or history anywhere in web/src (the only 'undo' match is a CSS comment at TrainPanel.svelte:2655). class:danger only styles the entry. The core laws every_add_undoes/every_removal cover an edit's inverse on the graph, not a UI history. Since inputs are the whole state, a snapshot stack is straightforward.
verdict.evidence: web/src/Offers.svelte:88-99 (make), :110-121 (entry: onmouseenter/onfocus show, onclick make). grep -n 'confirm(|pointer: coarse|ontouch|undo' web/src -> only Viewport.svelte:183 onpointerdown for panning.
verdict.proposal_note: Snapshot the whole TrainTab.train, not only the shape: a removal also prunes holds and cases (drop_bare, prune). An undo that restores only the graph would desynchronise the holds and cases. The case editors (set_duty, fresh_case) and relief also mutate inputs, so the stack should hook every write to tab.train, not only editTrain.

title: Loads are stated as torque only; a power input is missing
claim: A load case takes torque (N·m) and speed (rpm). Designers commonly start from power and speed. Rule 1 forbids converting in TS, so the core would have to offer power as an alternative statement of the same load. It would be stored as the torque it implies, or as Auto-like 'given as power', so inputs remain the state.
evidence: The strings carry train_nm and train_rpm only; there is no kW or W label.
proposal: Add a load entry mode `Power(kW)` in LoadCase that the core resolves to torque = P/ω, reported as derived. At zero speed it is refused with a note (no torque from power at rest). Add one label ×5.
validation: Law: a power-stated case solves identically to its torque-stated equivalent (corpus-equal figures).

verdict.reason: Holds. Load stores torque: Auto<f64> (N·m) and speed: Auto<f64> (rpm) only (train/mod.rs:2874-2888). The only unit labels are train_nm and train_rpm (strings_en.toml:490, 608). The rationale 'Torque, not force, is what a Load stores' (rationale.md:829) argues against storing a force whose plane and radius are implicit. Power is as plane-invariant as torque, so that rationale does not forbid a power statement. Rule 1 does forbid converting in TS, so the gap must close in the core.
verdict.evidence: crates/gear-core/src/train/mod.rs:2882-2887 'N·m, given or derived ...' / 'rpm, given or derived ...'; grep -n 'kW|power' strings_en.toml -> only flow and circulation notes and 'Power through mesh', no input label.
verdict.proposal_note: A port's speed may itself be derived through the motion (Auto automatic). A power statement then resolves after the motion solve as T = P/ω with ω from the motion, which works because the motion precedes the flow in solve_train, but it should be stated. The zero-speed refusal must also cover a derived speed of nought, such as a held port. Relief (relieve_case) turns torque figures, so it must decide whether it turns P or T for a power-stated load. Record the choice in the load-case change log (gear-io/src/train.rs) per CLAUDE.md's load-case row.

title: No train synthesis: tooth counts for a target ratio (and a train-level multi-objective search) are absent
claim: The tool analyses a train the designer lays out, and the AddRatio edit sizes one mesh to a ratio. A designer's first question for a multi-stage reduction is which tooth counts give ratio R within a tolerance, under constraints on minimum teeth, hunting and a size budget. The exact rational kinematics (ratio.rs, i128) make this well posed: Stern–Brocot or continued-fraction enumeration for a chain of pairs, or a Willis closed form per epicyclic arrangement, then ranking by the existing per-path efficiency and size. auto::maximise is per mesh and in continuous shifts only.
evidence: No entry point takes a target ratio for a whole path. per_tooth, the one integer-sensitivity figure, is computed and hidden (see the per-tooth finding).
proposal: A harness command first (gear-cli synth R tol stages), then an 'offers' entry at a path: enumerate the admissible count sets by Stern–Brocot within tol, solve each candidate train (µs each), and return the Pareto set over |ratio error|, efficiency and total pitch volume, as offers with dry runs. There is no new mathematics beyond the enumeration.
validation: Known results: 2-stage ratios with the classical exact-ratio tables (e.g. Brocot's 1861 clock-train tables). Law: every returned train's path ratio is within tol and every set is non-dominated.

verdict.reason: The gap is real: no entry point, harness command or offer takes a target ratio for a path and returns tooth counts (grep for target/desired ratio finds nothing), and auto::maximise searches continuous shifts per shape. One premise misreads the code, though. Edit::AddRatio does not 'size one mesh to a ratio'. edits.rs:48-52 and add_ratio (edits.rs:523-560) copy the distance's first mesh onto a shared body and a new body, which adds a layshaft ratio with the same counts as the first. No edit sizes anything to a requested ratio.
verdict.evidence: crates/gear-core/src/train/edits.rs:48 '**Another ratio across a distance**: a gear on `shared` ... meshing a gear on a new body of the other, the two copying the distance's first mesh'; add_ratio clones self.members[on_shared] and self.members[alone].
verdict.corrected_claim: There is no ratio synthesis of any kind. Even AddRatio copies an existing mesh's counts rather than sizing to a target, so a designer must hand-iterate tooth counts to reach a path ratio.
verdict.proposal_note: Start with a harness command, as proposed. For an epicyclic path the admissible set must also pass Shape::assembly and the concentric distance closure, not only the ratio, or most candidates will fail at solve. Rank on explicit, user-visible objectives only: 'total pitch volume' is a new rule of thumb and must be named as one.

title: No production validation of 'no shape' inputs: the refuse half of rule 5 exists only in the gear tab's TypeScript
claim: The invariant bounds in ranges_at_shift are described as 'exactly one place any input limit is written down' (m>0, 0<α<90, z≥1, |β|<90, 0<k<2). They are enforced only by GearPanel.onInput, which does not commit an invalid value. Neither gear-core, gear-wasm nor the train panel refuses them. TrainPanel's `finite()` commits any finite number, and `class:invalid` only styles the field. So input that 'describes no shape at all' is never refused as such. It is built, clamped at random places, or refused later under an unrelated reason.
evidence: Probe prof/main (Tooth::new, Gear::new, Ring::cut_by): m=0 gives r=0 and only clamp.tooth_thickness_raised. m=-1 gives r=-8.5 with 6 clamps. β=90 gives r=1.39e17 with only clamp.fillet_capped. α=90 gives rb=0 with only clamp.fillet_capped. NaN module gives NaN everywhere with clamps=[]. Train sweep (notes/lens-errors-policy/train_degenerate.txt, 438 mutations over Spur/Planetary/Worm/Crossed) shows the same input refused under different keys. Module 0 gives error.train_no_contact (Spur), error.train_no_common_distance (Planetary) and error.screw_not_positive (Crossed). Pressure angle 0 gives error.mesh_outside_involute_domain (Spur), error.train_no_common_distance (Planetary) and error.screw_not_positive (Worm/Crossed). Pressure angle -21 gives error.train_no_root_section (Spur). Pressure angle 90 on Worm is accepted and rated with only mesh.forward_locking and mesh.low_efficiency. rationale.md:138 lists 'a module of zero' as refused.
proposal: Give the invariant bounds a production gate. Add `GearParams::refusal(&self) -> Option<Note>`, built from the same `Ranges` invariant part (module, pressure_angle, teeth, helix_angle, thickness_mod), with a new `error.input_out_of_range` key and values {field, bound}. Add the equivalents for a train member (face width > 0 where given, friction ≥ 0, planet count ≥ 1, cutter teeth ≥ 1, cutter tip round ≥ 0) as `Shape::refusal()`. Call it first in solve_gear_impl, solve_ring_impl, export_*_dxf_impl and Shape::cut, returning TrainError::Input{member, note} before any geometry. Keep the existing guards as the 'nearly cuttable' clamps. TrainPanel can then show the core's refusal instead of relying on HTML attributes. Migration: add the gate, then delete the scattered NotPositive/NoContact paths it makes unreachable (a coverage run will show them).
validation: Add a law that sweeps every numeric input of every preset (the probe's leaf walk) at 0, negative, 90° and NaN. Each result must be either Ok with only keys from a declared set, or Err(error.input_out_of_range) naming that field, never an unrelated key. Separately, a lone-gear law: for each field, a value outside the Ranges invariant bound returns the refusal from solve_gear.

verdict.reason: Nothing in gear-core, gear-wasm or gear-io gates the invariant bounds. Ranges (auto.rs:688-697) only reports them. GearPanel/core.ts `validate` enforces them in TypeScript for the lone-gear tab. TrainPanel's `finite()` (TrainPanel.svelte:404-406) commits any finite number, and `class:invalid` (lines 1364/1471/1491) only styles the field. solve_gear_impl and solve_ring_impl (gear-wasm lib.rs:685, 567) pass params straight to Gear::new / Ring::cut_by. The only early gate in the train is teeth==0 (TrainError::Wiring). I reproduced the evidence independently. A lone Tooth with m=0 gives r=0 and only clamp.tooth_thickness_raised. α=90 gives rb=5e-16 and only clamp.fillet_capped. β=90 gives r=1.39e17. A ring with z=0 and the default cutter is built (ra=0.47, rf=1.40), with the cutter clamped to 1 tooth. In the train (Spur): module 0 or -2 on both members gives error.train_no_contact. Worm with α_n=90 (and 89) solves OK with rated figures and only mesh/clamp notes, which is a wrong answer shipped rather than a wrong-key refusal. Severity is lowered from high: the NaN evidence cannot reach production (JSON carries no NaN and `finite()` filters it), the lone-gear tab does guard, and most train paths do refuse, albeit under the wrong key (that part is finding 3).
verdict.evidence: Probe probes/verify-lens-errors-policy-1 (main.rs and bin/tr.rs). m0: r=0 rb=0 ra=0 rf=0 clamps=[clamp.tooth_thickness_raised]. a90: rb=5.2e-16 clamps=[clamp.fillet_capped]. b90: r=1.388e17. Ring z=0 cutter=20: rf=1.4037 ra=0.4698 clamps=[ring_tip_raised, cutter_teeth_reduced, ring_space_closed, cutter_no_tip_corner]. Train spur module0: ERR error.train_no_contact. Worm pa90: OK keys=[clamp.fillet_capped, mesh.forward_locking, mesh.low_efficiency, mesh.self_locking]. rationale.md:138 lists 'a module of zero' as refused.
verdict.proposal_note: A gate placed at the Ranges invariant bounds would not catch the worm at α_n=89°, which is also rated, because Ranges admits up to 90° exclusive. The gate should refuse where the geometry stops existing (for example, no involute flank between the base and tip circles, or a severed tooth), not only at the open-interval ends. The 'face width > 0' clause needs a decision first. A face width of 0 currently solves OK with contact stress null, while -11 is refused as no_contact, so 0 already carries a meaning that the gate would remove. Keep the wasm error as a Note key rather than an English String (rule 2).

title: The ring cutter's centre distance silently falls back to reference centres, and the root radius jumps up to 1.13 mm inside the admitted range
claim: When the ring's radial shift drives the cutter–ring pair out of the involute domain, `operating_geometry(...).map_or(r - cutter_radius, ...)` quietly uses reference centres. At that boundary a_cut jumps from a_ref·cos α_t to a_ref. The root radius jumps outward, and past the boundary it no longer depends on the shift at all. No note names this. The only notes that appear are coincidental (ring_space_closed).
evidence: Probe ringx, default cutter (20 teeth), m=1. z=60: rf is 30.05728 at x=-0.818 and 31.18286 at x=-0.819, a jump of +1.126 mm. inv α_w = inv 20° + 0.0182x crosses zero at x=-0.819. z=43: rf is 22.06710 at x=-0.47, then 22.75000 at every x from -0.48 to -0.52 (+0.68 mm, then constant). The ring tab validates x against the external gear's Ranges (admissible_ranges gives [-2.13, 1.94] for z=43 and z=60, probe rng), so both values are accepted in the UI and flow into the ring's DXF.
proposal: At the domain edge, clamp the plunge to the last admissible cutter position (α_w → 0⁺: a_cut = a_ref·cos α_t, which is continuous) and push a new `clamp.ring_shift_beyond_cutter` note giving the shift that was honoured. Better still, give the ring its own admissible shift bound: the closed form x_min = −inv α_t·(z−z_c)/(2 tan α_n), from inv α_w = 0. Report it in RingSummary as `ranges` and validate the ring tab against it rather than against the external gear's ranges.
validation: Add a continuity law: sweep x through the domain edge for several (z, z_c) and require |Δrf| ≤ C·Δx (Lipschitz), and require the clamp note to fire exactly beyond x_min. A test that ring ranges.profile_shift.min equals the closed form.

verdict.reason: ring.rs:372-373 `operating_geometry(...).map_or(r - cutter_radius, ...)` falls back to reference centres when inv α_w < 0. The comment there acknowledges the fallback but gives no argument for it. The pair is geometrically impossible there (mesh.rs:138: 'the base circles would have to overlap'), so the fallback is neither a clamp nor a refusal. No note is specific to it. clamp.ring_flank_ungenerated and ring_tip_raised fire on both sides of the edge. The RingSummary carries no shift range of its own, so the ring tab validates x against the external gear's Ranges. I re-derived the domain edge in closed form, x_min = -inv α_t (z - z_c)/(2 tan α_n): -0.81899 for z=60 and -0.47092 for z=43, which matches where the jumps occur.
verdict.evidence: Probe sweep with the default cutter (20 teeth), m=1. z=60: rf 30.04385 at x=-0.8190, then 31.18206 at x=-0.8200 (Δ=+1.138 mm), falling only 0.0008 per 0.001 of x after that. z=43: rf 22.08938 at x=-0.4659, then 22.75000 flat for every x ≤ -0.4709 (Δ=+0.682 mm, and constant = r - r_c + r_tip). At the edge, a_w → a_ref·cos α_t, so a clamp there is continuous.
verdict.proposal_note: Clamping to α_w→0⁺ is continuous but cuts at a degenerate operating angle. It is worth stating that the honoured shift is x_min. Reporting x_min as the ring's own shift bound, and validating the ring tab against it, is the better half of the proposal. The same bound should feed the train's search and relief for ring members.

title: The documented examples of refusal are not refused: a cutter larger than its ring is clamped, and module zero is built
claim: rationale.md twice gives 'a pinion cutter larger than the ring it is to cut' and 'a module of zero' as input that is still refused. The code clamps the first: `cutter_teeth >= z` becomes `(z-1).max(1)` with clamp.cutter_teeth_reduced, justified at ring.rs:318 by 'Ring::cut_by reports rather than fails', which is a type-signature reason and not a rule-5 one. It builds the second.
evidence: ring.rs:322-326 (the clamp). Probe: z=0 ring shows clamp.cutter_teeth_reduced. Tooth::new with m=0 returns Ok-shaped output with only clamp.tooth_thickness_raised. Meanwhile MeshError::RingTooSmall refuses the same 'ring not larger' condition for a pinion (mesh.rs:259).
proposal: Decide one rule and make code and prose agree. Recommended: a tool no smaller than the workpiece ring describes no cut, so refuse it through the input gate in finding 1 (error.ring_cutter_too_large, values {cutter, ring}). Drop CLAMP_CUTTER_TEETH_REDUCED and its five catalogue lines. If clamping is kept instead, change both rationale paragraphs to say so and argue it.
validation: Run check_doc_links and check_strings after the key change. Add a law that Ring::cut_by with a cutter ≥ ring teeth is refused at every entry point (solve_ring, train cut).

verdict.reason: rationale.md:138-139 and 1635-1636 both name 'a cutter larger than the ring it cuts' and 'a module of zero' as refused. The code clamps the first: ring.rs:322-326 reduces cutter_teeth to (z-1).max(1) with clamp.cutter_teeth_reduced, even for z=0. It builds the second in Tooth/Gear/Ring and refuses it in the train only incidentally, as no_contact. The ring.rs comment's justification ('which of the two counts to give up is the designer's call') argues for refusing, not for picking one silently. MeshError::RingTooSmall refuses the same condition in a mesh, so the two paths disagree.
verdict.evidence: Probe: Ring z=43 cutter=50 gives rf=22.75, clamps=[clamp.cutter_teeth_reduced]. z=43 cutter=43 gives the same. z=20 cutter=20 builds with the cutter reduced. z=0 cutter=20 builds a ring of rf=1.40. Tooth m=0 builds with clamps=[clamp.tooth_thickness_raised].
verdict.proposal_note: Refusing requires Ring::cut_by to return a Result, or an input gate ahead of it (finding 0). Either way, rationale.md's examples should be re-checked against the code once the gate lands, so the prose names only refusals that actually happen.

title: Refusals name the wrong cause: 'the teeth never contact' now covers bad materials, non-positive face width and module zero
claim: The contact_stress/patch_at/contact_curvatures `None` is mapped to TrainError::NoContact. hertz.rs returns None for any non-positive modulus or width, so a material or a face width reaches the reader as 'the teeth never contact'. TrainError's own doc says this conflation was fixed. Likewise error.train_no_root_section blames undercut for a root lost to a zero dedendum or a negative pressure angle, and the test comment at shape.rs:4634 already calls that wording wrong. error.screw_not_positive is raised for a non-finite profile shift (screw.rs:254). error.screw_worm_too_thin advises reordering members for sin γ ≥ 1, which is a pitch diameter too small for the starts.
evidence: Probe mat: E=-1 → error.train_no_contact; E=0 → train_no_contact; ν=1 → train_no_contact. Train sweep: face_width -11 → train_no_contact (Spur, Planetary, Crossed). Module 0, -2 and 1e-6 on Spur → train_no_contact. Dedendum 0 on Spur member 0 → train_no_root_section. Worm pitch_diameter 0 → error.screw_worm_too_thin ('put the helical member first').
proposal: Once the input gate from finding 1 exists, most of these become unreachable. Map the rest to their own causes: TrainError::Material{name, field} (key error.train_material_invalid) for E*≤0; keep NoContact only for ContactPath::new == None; rename error.train_no_root_section to 'no root section is left to rate on this tooth' and drop the undercut wording in TrainError's Display. Give ScrewError a NonFinite variant, and reword worm_too_thin to 'the worm's pitch diameter is too small for its starts at this module'.
validation: Add a law over the degenerate sweep: every Err key is one of a declared per-field set, and NoContact appears only when ContactPath::new returned None. The strings test's fire-every-note covers the new keys.

verdict.corrected_claim: The mismatches between keys and causes are real: E≤0 (a material override typed in the panel), a negative face width, and module 0/-2 all refuse as error.train_no_contact; dedendum 0 on the 17-tooth member and α=-21 refuse as 'too undercut'; a non-finite shift is reported as 'not positive' (screw.rs:254). Two parts of the claim are overstated. TrainError's doc (mod.rs:1567-1572) says two *other* conflations were fixed (a common distance and the flow), not that no_contact is now used only for contact. The worm_too_thin wording ('no lead angle; put the helical member first') is accurate in the train's usual path, because shape.rs:529 derives d₁ = z m/cos β, so sin γ ≥ 1 happens exactly at β=0. It misleads only when a pitch diameter below z·m_n is typed. Also, ν=1 on one member does not refuse: that member is rated as rigid (contact 218 MPa).
verdict.reason: I reproduced most of the key mapping with my own probe. shape.rs:2563/2591/3322 map every `None` from hertz/contact_stress to NoContact, and hertz.rs:148-156 returns None for a non-positive E* or load, so a material fault reads as 'the teeth never contact'. The worm-message sub-claim holds only for a typed diameter.
verdict.evidence: Probe bin/tr.rs. spur E-1 (override on member 0): ERR error.train_no_contact. fw-11: ERR train_no_contact. module0 / module-2: ERR train_no_contact. ded0 on member 0: ERR train_no_root_section. pa-21: ERR train_no_root_section. worm pd0 and pd0.5: ERR screw_worm_too_thin. spur nu1 (one member): OK, contact_stress 218.44. strings_en.toml:194, 198, 202.
verdict.proposal_note: Most of this disappears once finding 0's gate and finding 5's material validation exist; do those first. Rewording worm_too_thin to mention only the diameter would make it wrong for the β=0 case the train actually reaches. It should name both causes: the worm member's helix is zero, or its pitch diameter is below starts × module.

title: An external member with no root section refuses the whole train, while a ring or a planet's other mesh is only noted
claim: shape.rs:3234 returns Err(NoRootSection) when an external member has no bending section in any line mesh. That discards the ratio, efficiencies, contact stresses and every other member's rating. The same missing figure on a ring, or on one of a planet's meshes, costs only that rating plus gear.bending_unrated_in_mesh. The test at shape.rs:4625-4640 argues that 'a stage that threw those away over one missing input would be deciding for the designer rather than informing them', and rationale.md:1638 says 'a part can be perfectly real while one question about it has no answer'. That is the argument against the remaining refusal.
evidence: Code read at shape.rs:3230-3237. Train sweep: Spur member 0 dedendum=0 → ERR error.train_no_root_section (nothing reported), while Planetary member 1 dedendum=0 → OK with gear.bending_unrated_in_mesh.
proposal: Delete the refusal loop. Let every member with all-None bendings carry a new `gear.bending_unrated` note (or reuse GEAR_BENDING_UNRATED_IN_MESH once per mesh) with bending_stress null. Remove TrainError::NoRootSection and error.train_no_root_section once nothing raises it.
validation: Change the existing ring-notch test into a law over all presets: forcing any one member's section to None leaves every other figure of the train equal to the unforced solve.

verdict.reason: shape.rs:3229-3237 refuses the whole shape when an external member on a line has no bending section in any mesh. A ring, or a planet rated on its other flank, costs only that figure. The comment gives no reason for the asymmetry, and rationale.md's 'A rating that cannot be taken costs the rating, not the stage' (and the shape.rs:4625-4640 test doc) argues against it on the merits. The cases that reach it are not severed teeth: in my probe the refused inputs (dedendum 0 on the 17-tooth member, α=-21) have a root section as a lone tooth (severed=false, root_section=true at 0.5), so the missing section comes from the train's load point, which is a rating question, not a question of shape.
verdict.evidence: Probe. Spur ded0 member 0: ERR error.train_no_root_section, with nothing else reported. Spur ded0 member 1: OK. Planetary ded0 on the sun (member 0): ERR. Planetary ded0 on member 1: OK with gear.bending_unrated_in_mesh. Lone Tooth z=17 ded=0: severed=false, root_section=true. Only z=3, x=-0.5 is severed.
verdict.proposal_note: Do not simply delete the refusal. A genuinely severed tooth (`Tooth::severed`) describes no shape and should still be refused, as its own key through the input gate of finding 0, not as 'no root section'. Only the rating-level absence should become a note.

title: The material library accepts unphysical constants, and a Poisson ratio of 0.7 silently raises contact stress by 34%
claim: gear_io::from_toml refuses only an empty library and duplicate names. It accepts E≤0, ν outside (-1, 0.5), negative allowables and negative density. These are materials that describe nothing, and they are then rated or refused under the wrong reason.
evidence: Probe mat (default library with one value edited, Spur preset). ν=0.7: imported, contact stress 206.99 MPa against 154.46 at 0.29, no note. Ultimate allowable -5: imported, rated, no note. Density -1: imported, rated. E=-1 or 0: imported, then solve fails with error.train_no_contact. ν=1: same.
proposal: In from_toml, after the duplicate check, validate each material: elastic_modulus > 0, -1 < poissons_ratio < 0.5, ultimate_allowable > 0, fatigue_allowable > 0, density > 0. Return MaterialError::Invalid{name, field}. Also cross it as a Note (error.material_invalid {name, field}) rather than English (see the finding on English at the boundary). Apply the same check to material_overrides on a member, in the input gate.
validation: A gear-io test perturbing each field of each shipped material to its bound and one ulp beyond: the bound itself is refused where the inequality is strict, and beyond it is always refused.

verdict.reason: gear_io::from_toml (materials.rs:50-62) checks only for an empty library and duplicate names, and import_materials_impl passes the result straight on. The finding understates how easy this is to reach: the train panel's per-member material overrides (TrainPanel.svelte:1049-1053, including poissons_ratio at :1657) commit any finite number, so no TOML import is needed. The project already knows the bounds, because materials.rs:119-137 asserts them for the shipped library only (density>0, E>0, 0.2≤ν<0.5, 0<fatigue<ultimate), but not for anything a user supplies.
verdict.evidence: Probe bin/tr.rs with overrides on the Spur preset. ν=0.7 on both members: OK, contact_stress 206.995 against 154.462 at base (ratio 1.340 = sqrt((1-0.29²)/(1-0.7²))), no note. ν=1 on one member: OK, 218.44 (the member is treated as rigid). ultimate_allowable -5: OK, rated. E=-1: ERR error.train_no_contact.
verdict.proposal_note: Put the check in gear-core (a `Material::refusal()` or a validation on the resolved material after overrides), not only in gear-io's from_toml. Overrides are applied in core (material.rs:353) and never pass through from_toml. Reuse one predicate for both the shipped-library test and the runtime check, so the bounds are written once. Use the physical bound -1<ν<0.5 at runtime; the test's 0.2 floor is a sanity band, not a physical limit.

title: A negative friction coefficient is accepted: mesh efficiency 1.004, path efficiency 0, and the case says the load is not reacted
claim: sliding_friction and static_friction have no bound anywhere: no Ranges entry, no core check, and the panel's numberField commits any finite value. A negative μ describes no contact. It produces an efficiency above one, and then a case refusal that blames the reaction.
evidence: Probe diff, Spur /shape/meshes/0/sliding_friction = -0.02: meshes/0/efficiency forward 0.98345 → 1.00414; paths/0/efficiency forward 0.98345 → 0.0; cases/0 and cases/1 gain train.load_not_reacted. Negative static friction (-1.16) is accepted with no change and no note.
proposal: Refuse μ < 0 in the shape's input gate (finding 1). Expose the bound to the panel as a MeshRanges{sliding_friction: Bound::between(Some(0.0), None)} next to member ranges, so the TS shows the core's bound rather than none.
validation: A law that every mesh efficiency lies in [0, 1] over the sweep of admissible friction, and that μ<0 is refused with its field named.

verdict.reason: Reproduced independently, and the effect is larger than reported. Nothing bounds either friction coefficient. The gate is missing in three places: the solve reads `meshes[k].sliding_friction` / `static_friction` directly (train/shape.rs:3190-3201), there is no friction entry in any Ranges, and TrainPanel.svelte:673-674 commits any finite value through `numberField` → `finite(set)` (line 1723). One correction to the evidence: a negative static friction is not 'accepted with no change'. It drives the path efficiency to 0 with no note. A negative μ describes no contact, so under rule 5 (refuse input that describes no shape) it should be refused.
verdict.evidence:
Own probe (probes/verify-lens-errors-policy-2, `fric` mode, Train::alone(Preset::X.build(),0.1,3000), JSON-pointer edit, solve_train diff):
- Spur sliding −0.02: meshes/0/efficiency 0.98345 → 1.00414; paths/0/efficiency 0.98345 → 0.0; cases/0 and cases/1 gain train.load_not_reacted.
- Spur sliding −0.2: mesh efficiency 1.0414.
- Spur static −1.16: paths/0/efficiency fwd/back 0.98345 → 0.0, and no note at all.
- Worm sliding −0.05: meshes/0/efficiency forward 0.618 → 1.630, path 0.0, cases gain train.load_shared.
`grep friction auto.rs params.rs` finds no bound.
verdict.proposal_note: Refusing at the train's input gate is right. The refusal should cross as a TrainError note like the other train refusals, so it shows up in the panel's failure slot; the Bound is then only a display hint. Put the law 'every mesh efficiency ∈ [0,1] for μ ≥ 0' over every preset, including the worm and crossed ones: the screw efficiency is the one that goes furthest above 1.

title: Clamps with no note: planet count 0, cutter teeth 0, tip below the base circle, negative root radius
claim: Each of these is a guard that changes the geometry or the load share with no Note, contrary to the Clamps doc ('a clamped result is never returned silently'). (a) `axes[a].count.max(1)` turns 0 planets into 1, which triples every planet-mesh load against the 3-planet preset, and the layout report vanishes. (b) `cutter.teeth.max(1)` turns a 0-tooth shaper into a 1-tooth one. (c) Tooth's `ra.max(rb*(1+TIP_ABOVE_BASE_FRACTION))` has no note, while Ring's equivalent pushes clamp.ring_tip_raised, and ring.rs:283 writes the same 1e-9 as a bare literal instead of guard::TIP_ABOVE_BASE_FRACTION. (d) `rho.max(MIN_FILLET_MODULES*m)` turns a negative root radius into a sharp corner silently. The panel reaches (a) and (b): its HTML `min="1"` does not stop a typed 0, and `finite()` commits it.
evidence: Probe diff, Planetary /shape/axes/1/count=0: axes/1/layout disappears; members/0/cases/0/torque 0.0333 → 0.1, bending 1.456 → 4.368 MPa, contact 122.1 → 211.5 MPa; no new note. Planetary ring/teeth (cutter) 0 → only clamp.cutter_no_tip_corner. Probe prof: ha=-3 and ha=-1.1 give ra = rb = 7.9874 with clamps=[]. rho=-1 → rho=0, clamps=[].
proposal: (a) and (b): refuse through the input gate (count ≥ 1 and cutter teeth ≥ 1 are 'no shape' bounds), and delete the `.max(1)` guards so an invariant break panics in tests instead of being absorbed. (c): push a `clamp.tip_raised_to_base` note (the mirror of ring_tip_raised) and use guard::TIP_ABOVE_BASE_FRACTION in ring.rs:283. (d): refuse a negative root radius (Ranges already says ≥ 0), and keep the 1e-9 floor as a silent degeneracy tolerance only for 0.
validation: Add a law: for every guard in params::guard and every `.max(1)` on a count, an input that makes it bind yields a clamp.* note or a refusal, never an unchanged note list. The degenerate sweep above makes a ready harness for it.

verdict.corrected_claim: Four guards alter the geometry without a note of their own, against params.rs:196-197 ('Every guard that fires appends a human-readable note'). (a) `axes[a].count.max(1)` (shape.rs:463) silently reads a planet count of 0 as 1. The result is bit-identical to typing 1: the tripled load and the missing layout are what one planet correctly gives, not an artefact of the guard. The defect is only that a typed 0 is shown as 0 while the solve uses 1, and TrainPanel.svelte:834's `min="1"` does not stop a typed 0. (b) `cutter.teeth.max(1)` (ring.rs:198) reads a 0-tooth cutter as a 1-tooth one. It is not silent: clamp.cutter_no_tip_corner fires, but that note says nothing about the tooth count. (c) Tooth's tip-above-base guard (tooth.rs:471) has no note, while Ring's mirror guard pushes clamp.ring_tip_raised, and ring.rs:283 repeats the 1e-9 as a bare literal instead of guard::TIP_ABOVE_BASE_FRACTION. (d) A negative root radius is floored to 1e-9·m with no note (tooth.rs:925); rho = 0 → 1e-9 is the intended removable-singularity floor.
verdict.reason: Every mechanism is real, but (a)'s headline evidence misreads it: the stress tripling is the correct answer for one planet, not damage done by the clamp. (b) does raise a note, just not a specific one. In the gear tab, (c) and (d) are outside admissible_ranges (the addendum lower bound includes above_base, auto.rs:671, and root_radius ≥ 0), so the panel already marks them invalid and does not commit them. The silent path is the library and a train member, whose panel commits any finite value.
verdict.evidence:
Probe `count`: Planetary axes/1/count = 0 and count = 1 give identical diffs against the 3-planet base (members/0/cases/0/torque 0.0333 → 0.1, bending 1.456 → 4.368, contact 122.09 → 211.47, layout absent, part.planets_share_load_equally gone). No note is added in either case.
Probe `cutter0`: members/2/ring/teeth = 0 → only clamps/0 = clamp.cutter_no_tip_corner ('no fillet: cutter has no usable tip corner').
Probe `tooth` (z = 17, m = 1, rb = 7.987): ha = −0.9, −1.1 and −3 all give ra = 7.987387 = rb with clamps = []; rho = −1 → rho = 0.000000, clamps = []. ring.rs:283 reads `let mut ra_min = rb * (1.0 + 1e-9);`.
verdict.proposal_note: (a) and (b): refuse them as TrainError / shape invariants (count ≥ 1, cutter teeth ≥ 1), which fits rule 5. Deleting the `.max(1)` only makes sense once the gate exists, or the train panel gains a panic path. (c): the new note needs a key and five strings. Also consider whether a tip below the base circle should be a refusal (it has no involute), rather than a clamp that yields a tooth with no flank.

title: The pressure-angle guard is applied to the tooth but not to thickness_shift(), so a clamped tooth is 7.4% too thin
claim: Tooth::build_with_z raises α_n to 0.5° with a note, but transverse_thickness takes `params.thickness_shift()`, which recomputes x_s = π(k−1)/(4 tan α_n) from the raw angle. The thickness is therefore evaluated with tan 0.5° against an x_s sized for tan 0.3°. At α=0, x_s = 0/0 = NaN when k=1, which is how Mesh::new comes to report outside_involute_domain for a pressure angle the tooth itself clamped.
evidence: Probe pa: α=0.3°, k=0.9 gives st=1.30899 (with clamp.pressure_angle_raised). Consistent at 0.5° it would be k·π/2 = 1.41372, the value α=0.5° itself gives. Spur train with pressure_angle 0 → error.mesh_outside_involute_domain.
proposal: Make the guard a single resolved value: `GearParams::normal_pressure_angle_rad()` returning the guarded angle, used by thickness_shift, transverse_thickness, tool_wanted_by, ranges_at_shift and Mesh. Alternatively, once finding 1's gate refuses α ≤ 0, keep the clamp and pass the clamped α_n into thickness_shift.
validation: A law that for every k and α in (0, 0.5°], st equals the value at α = 0.5° (the clamp's promise), and that thickness_shift at the clamp equals x_s(0.5°).

verdict.reason: Reproduced, and it is worse than 7.4 %. The error grows as α → 0: st ∝ tan(0.5°)/tan α. The clamp promises the 0.5° tooth, but `thickness_shift()` (params.rs:195-198) uses the raw α. It is also read raw by transverse_thickness (tooth.rs:833), by ranges_at_shift (auto.rs:678, which clamps `an` but calls thickness_shift raw), by Ring (ring.rs:244), by Mesh (mesh.rs:746) and by shape.rs:522/1175/1359. Only degenerate input reaches it, but Ranges admits pressure_angle ∈ (0,90) exclusive (auto.rs:697), so 0 < α < 0.5° is admissible input that gets a wrong tooth.
verdict.evidence:
Probe `pa` (Tooth::new, z = 17, m = 1):
- α = 0.3, k = 0.9: st = 1.308993 vs k·π/2 = 1.413717 (−7.4 %).
- α = 0.1, k = 0.9: st = 0.785379 (−44 %).
- α = 0.1, k = 1.1: st = 2.356 vs 1.728.
- α = 0, k = 1: st = NaN, with only clamp.pressure_angle_raised and clamp.fillet_capped.
- α = 0.5 and α = 0.51 both give exactly k·π/2.
A Spur train with pressure_angle manual 0 → Err InPart{part: 0, cause: Mesh(OutsideInvoluteDomain)}, although the tooth reports the angle raised.
verdict.proposal_note: Prefer the single resolved accessor (`GearParams::normal_pressure_angle_rad()` returning the guarded value), with thickness_shift computed from it. That removes the four repeated `.max(guard::MIN_PRESSURE_ANGLE_DEG.to_radians())` (tooth.rs:364, auto.rs:115/304/662) as well. Mesh::new should read the tooth's `alpha_n` (it already does, via g1.alpha_n), so only x_thick needs the guarded shift.

title: Gear::profile panics on a degenerate tooth, and Gear::new's 'never panics / guarded to one, as elsewhere' is false
claim: Gear::new guards z with teeth.max(1) for positions, but builds every tooth with Tooth::cut_by(params), which uses the raw z=0 (so r=0). The half-profile then comes back empty, and `&r[1..]` at gear.rs:564 panics. The same happens for module 0 and a NaN module. In wasm that is `RuntimeError: unreachable` (the wasm-boundary auditor's gear_profile teeth=0 and module=0 rows).
evidence: Probe prof: z0, m0 and nan all print 'built' and then panic at gear.rs:564:44 inside Gear::profile's closure. mneg, b90 and a90 return 426, 256 and 222 points of nonsense geometry. Tooth::new(z=0) gives r=0.0000 (probe main).
proposal: With the input gate in place, z=0, m≤0 and NaN never reach Gear. As defence in depth, make half_profile's contract non-empty (or return Option) and replace `&r[1..]` with `r.get(1..).unwrap_or_default()`. Remove the `.max(1)` in Gear::new so it matches Tooth, and correct the doc.
validation: A test calling Gear::new(p).profile(n) and outline() over the invariant bounds' edges and just outside them, under catch_unwind: none may panic. Also enable clippy::indexing_slicing on gear.rs and outline.rs only.

verdict.corrected_claim: Gear::new itself does not panic. Its '# Panics: Never' is literally true, but 'guarded to one, as elsewhere' is not: `new` guards z with `.max(1)` (gear.rs:132), while each tooth is cut by Tooth::cut_by with the raw z (tooth.rs:382), so r = 0. Gear::profile then panics at gear.rs:564 (`&r[1..]` on an empty half-profile) for z = 0, module = 0 and NaN module. Gear::outline does not panic but returns 65,538 vertices (z = 0) and 1,114,146 vertices (m = 0, NaN), an unbounded allocation. The gear panel does not reach this: it commits a field only when validate() passes (GearPanel.svelte:127-128) and draws the profile only when solve_gear returned ok. A train refuses z = 0 (Wiring MemberWithoutTeeth) and m = 0 (NoContact). The remaining path is the raw wasm gear_profile / export_dxf entry points and library callers.
verdict.reason: The panic is real and was reproduced. The claim that the Gear::new doc is false overstates it, because the panic is in profile(), not new(). Reachability from the application is lower than implied, since the panel gates its inputs.
verdict.evidence: Probe `prof`: z0, m0 and nan each give 'new ok; profile PANIC' with 'range start index 1 out of range for slice of length 0' at gear.rs:564:44. outline(0.01) is Ok(65538) for z0 and Ok(1114146) for m0 and nan. mneg gives profile 426 points. Probe `z0train`: Spur teeth 0 → ERR InPart{Wiring(MemberWithoutTeeth(0))}; module 0 → ERR NoContact. The profile call site is at GearPanel.svelte:252-253, gated by `"ok" in result`.
verdict.proposal_note: Fix the root rather than the slice: refuse z = 0, m ≤ 0 and non-finite values once, at a GearParams validation used by every wasm entry point (gear_profile_impl, export_dxf_impl and solve_gear_impl all take resolved_params unchecked). Also cap outline's vertex count, or refuse non-finite radii, so the 1.1 M-vertex outline cannot happen. The `r.get(1..)` fallback hides a broken invariant and is not needed if the gate exists.

title: English reaches the UI: gear-wasm's throw and adopt refusals, and the material/train import reasons
claim: Rule 2 keeps English out of gear-core, and the catalogues are complete (524 keys × 5, none missing). But the boundary crate composes English that a designer meets in normal use. The eccentric-throw messages ('a centre-distance throw of … mm is not reachable…') are shown in the gear tab's FieldNote in every language. MaterialError::Empty and DuplicateName, and the TOML parse reason, are shown in the Sidebar and inside ui.train_import_failed. The adopt refusals are English too.
evidence: GearPanel.svelte:452 renders `result.error` when sizing by throw. lib.rs:660-678 are format! strings. Sidebar.svelte:120 prints library.error, which is the MaterialError Display. Catalogue script: all [error], [clamp] and ui.train_edit_refused_* keys are present in de, pt, zh-Hans and zh-Hant; these messages have no key at all.
proposal: Return these as Notes. Throw refusals become error.throw_needs_mate and error.throw_unreachable {throw}. MaterialError implements Explain, giving error.material_empty, error.material_duplicate {name} and error.document_parse {line, column}, keeping the parser's text only as a {detail} value. Cross them in value outcomes (see the boundary-convention finding), not as thrown strings. The adopt refusals are defects, so they can stay thrown.
validation: check_strings.py plus a sweep of gear-wasm's non-test source for string literals in Err(...)/format! paths that reach a non-defect outcome. A wasm_probe step for each new key.

verdict.reason: This contradicts the project's own documents, not just a preference. reference.md says 'Every word the application shows lives in crates/gear-io/data/strings_<code>.toml'. rationale.md:2105-2110 says 'a refusal is data … only a boundary that actually broke is still thrown', and calls the old Display-at-the-boundary 'the one thing the application said in a language nobody chose'. Three kinds of message still break that. First, the eccentric-throw refusals (lib.rs:660-678, format! English) reach GearPanel.svelte:452's FieldNote in ordinary use. Second, MaterialError's Display (materials.rs:31-43) reaches Sidebar.svelte:120 via import_materials_impl's `e.to_string()` (lib.rs:961). Third, TrainError's Display ('geartrain file is not valid: …', train.rs:313-318) is substituted into ui.train_import_failed's {reason}. The catalogue has no key for any of them (grep of strings_en.toml for throw/duplicate/parse finds only the field label). The adopt refusals (lib.rs:1385, 1389) are defects by their own comment ('the panel lists what can be adopted'), so leaving them thrown is consistent, as the proposal says.
verdict.evidence:
lib.rs:660-663 'a centre-distance throw is commanded against a mate — set the mate's tooth count'; lib.rs:672-676 'a centre-distance throw of {:.4} mm is not reachable…'. GearPanel.svelte:452 `notes(null, byThrow && "error" in result ? result.error : null)`. core.ts:524 passes e.message through. Sidebar.svelte:120 `

{library.error}

`. TrainPanel.svelte:1987 `t("ui.train_import_failed", { reason: trains.importError })`. strings_en.toml has only `gear_axis_distance_throw = "Axis-distance offset"`.
verdict.proposal_note: The toml crate's parse message is itself English and cannot be localised. Keep it only as a {detail} value beside a translated sentence, and pass the line and column from toml::de::Error::span(). The throw refusals come from amplitude_for_throw's error type, so give that type a `note()` like TrainError, instead of composing the keys in gear-wasm.

title: Five different boundary conventions for a refusal
claim: The ways a refusal crosses are: (1) solve_train returns failure-as-value, TrainOutcome.failure {note, part}; (2) edit_train throws a JsError whose message is a catalogue key, and core.ts tells it from a defect with `message.startsWith("ui.")`; (3) adopt_member returns a failure Note in the value but throws English for other refusals; (4) solve_gear throws English for a user-reachable refusal (the throw); (5) relieve_case throws `format!("{e:?}")`, which TS swallows; and Maybe::Unavailable {note} is a sixth, per-field form. A designer's refusal and a broken boundary are told apart differently at every entry point.
evidence: Code read at the cited lines; core.ts:765-777 (the prefix sniff); core.ts:623-632 (relieve_case swallowed).
proposal: Make one rule: an entry point throws only for malformed JSON or a panic, and every refusal a design can reach comes back in the value as `refused: Option<Note>` (edit_train: {train, refused}; solve_gear/solve_ring: {ok, refused}; relieve_case: {case, refused}). Do the migration one entry point at a time with its wasm_probe step, then delete the startsWith sniff.
validation: check_wasm.sh --write records the outcome shape. Add a law in gear-wasm's tests that every EditRefused, every TrainError and every throw refusal arrives as `refused` and never as Err.

verdict.corrected_claim: Three conventions exist, not five or six. (1) Refusal as a value: solve_train's TrainOutcome.failure, and adopt_member's `failure` note. adopt_member's thrown English (lib.rs:1385/1389) is for requests its own comment calls defects, so it follows the rule rather than breaking it. (2) A thrown JsError whose message is a catalogue key: edit_train (lib.rs:1561, `e.key()`), which core.ts:823 tells apart by `message.startsWith("ui.")`. Any other thrown message, i.e. a real boundary defect, makes editTrain return null, the same value as a successful edit, so a broken boundary shows as an edit that silently did nothing. Separately, edit_train's own doc says a refused edit 'is returned unchanged' while its '# Errors' names only a malformed request. (3) Thrown text for user-reachable refusals: solve_gear's throw refusals and the import errors (finding 10), and relieve_case's `format!("{e:?}")` of a MotionError (lib.rs:1502), which relieveCase (core.ts:709-714) swallows entirely. Maybe::Unavailable is a per-field absence, not a refusal convention.
verdict.reason: The inconsistency is real, but (3) and the sixth form are miscounted. The cited core.ts lines are off: the prefix sniff is at core.ts:823 and relieveCase at 700-718. The most concrete harm is not listed in the finding: editTrain's defect path returns null, which the caller reads as 'no refusal'.
verdict.evidence: core.ts:817-829: `catch (e) { const message = …; return message.startsWith("ui.") ? message : null; }`. Offers.svelte:92 reads the return as `refusal`. core.ts:709-714: `try { … relieve_case(…) } catch { return; }`. lib.rs:1336-1340 is the adopt comment: 'A member the train does not have, or a worm, is a defect on the other side of the boundary … so each is a refusal rather than an outcome.' lib.rs:1532-1536 is edit_train's doc. The keys in edits.rs:155-168 all begin with 'ui.'.
verdict.proposal_note: The rule should be the one rationale.md:2105-2110 already states, applied to edit_train, solve_gear/solve_ring (throw), import_* and relieve_case. It should not be a second rule. Migrate edit_train first, to `{train, refused: Option<key>}`: that deletes the prefix sniff and closes the defect-as-success hole. The EditRefused keys live in the [ui] section although the core raises them; moving them to [error] would match the note convention, but that is optional.

title: Nine core error enums, plus Option returns and three note channels, where one Refusal-as-Note model would serve
claim: The core's error types are TrainError (13 variants), MotionError (5), kinematics::Refusal (3), flow::Refused (3), WiringError (4), EditRefused (10, whose keys live in [ui] although it is the core's word), MeshError (4), ScrewError (5) and MeasurementError (3). The core also has about 60 Option-returning public fns, of which ring::mesh_with duplicates Mesh::new(Internal)'s checks but drops the reason, plus clamp notes, case notes (flow refusals) and Maybe::Unavailable. Translations between them lose information. WiringError::MemberWithoutTeeth(i) collapses to an error.train_wiring with no values, so the member is not named. MotionError::Empty becomes 'no such body: body 0'. amplitude_for_throw reuses MeshError::OutsideInvoluteDomain for a negative target and for 'unreachable'.
evidence: refusals.txt (108 refusal-returning production fns); mod.rs:1636-1648 and 1680 (the lossy mappings); strings_en.toml:200 (train_wiring has no placeholder); gear.rs:1055-1060 and 1130.
proposal: Target shape: `pub struct Refusal { note: Note, at: Option<Piece> }` implementing Explain, with every enum keeping its variants only as the source of `note()`. Carry the payloads: train_wiring {member} for MemberWithoutTeeth, and a separate error.train_mesh_without_distance. Move EditRefused's keys to an [edit] section beside [error]. Make ring::mesh_with return Result<RingMesh, MeshError> by delegating the compatibility and domain checks to Mesh::new's code (one test of 'can these mesh'). Migration: implement Explain on every enum first (EditRefused, WiringError, Refusal, Refused, MaterialError), then flatten the From chains.
validation: The strings test (fire every note) extends to fire every variant of every error enum. Add a law that every refusal note names the index it is about whenever the variant carries one.

verdict.reason: The specific losses of information are real. The headline claim, that nine enums plus Options is itself a defect needing one Refusal struct, is a design preference. Each enum already implements Explain, and rationale.md:57-61 documents the single Note channel. Of the three lossy mappings, one is significant, one is marginal and one is documented.
verdict.corrected_claim: (1) TrainError::Wiring(_) renders as error.train_wiring with no values (mod.rs:1682; strings_en.toml:200 has no placeholder), while TrainError's English Display in the core (mod.rs:1752-1768) names the member or mesh. So the CLI tells a developer more than the translated note tells a user, and the same refusal is said twice, in two places, with different content. Every Wiring variant carries an index. (2) EditRefused::key returns raw 'ui.train_edit_refused_*' strings (edits.rs:155-168) instead of note::key constants with Explain, so a core refusal lives in the front end's [ui] section. (3) MotionError::Empty maps to NoSuchBody{at: GROUND}, which reads 'names a body the train does not have: body 0'. It is reachable only through solve_alone and Train::motion on a memberless shape, because solve_train handles an empty train at mod.rs:4192-4196.
