title: No fixture pins an uncapped helical fillet radius; ρ = root_radius·m_t is held only indirectly
claim: Both helical regression fixtures have a fillet that is either capped (z=13, ρ = 0.330 < 0.38·m_t) or zero (z=31), so neither reads root_radius·m_t. The choice of m_t over m_n for a helical tip round (which rationale does it cite?) is held only because a bound test and a screw test happen to fail.
evidence: Mutation M1 (`* mt` → `* m`) failed only extremes::the_geometric_bounds_are_exactly_where_the_generator_starts_clamping and screw::tests::the_crossed_interference_verdict_meets_the_parallel_one_at_the_limit, neither of which is about the fillet radius.
proposal: Add a helical fixture with an uncapped round (e.g. z=40, β=25, ρ=0.25) whose ρ, θ0 and r_j are checked against an independent derivation: the rack's normal-section round seen in the transverse section. Record the argument for m_t in docs/rationale.md if absent.
validation: M1 fails the new fixture.

verdict.reason: The test gap is real: the z=13 β=20 fixture is capped (ρ = 0.3302 < 0.38·m_t = 0.4044) and the z=31 one has ρ = 0 (1e-9), so no fixture reads root_radius·m_t uncapped. The M1 mutation (`* mt` -> `* m`) fails exactly the two tests named, and I reproduced that. But the 'held only because tests happen to fail' framing is too strong for the extremes test. It checks that admissible_ranges' root-radius bound is exactly where clamp.fillet_capped starts, and reference.md:163 states that bound as ρ ≤ 0.95·min(b_d, ρ_max)/m_t, so it is a direct consistency law on m_t. The rationale the finding asks about exists: docs/state.md:689-699 records 'The rack round is the coefficient times the transverse module' as a known approximation, with size (6 % at 20°), sign (conservative interference verdict) and the ellipse it stands in for. That part of the proposal is already handled.
verdict.evidence: regression.rs:124-150 (ρ 3.3015e-1, capped) and 151-177 (ρ 1e-9). tooth.rs:918 `let mut rho = params.root_radius * mt;`. Worktree M1: 604 run, 602 passed, 2 failed: extremes::the_geometric_bounds_are_exactly_where_the_generator_starts_clamping and screw::tests::the_crossed_interference_verdict_meets_the_parallel_one_at_the_limit. docs/state.md:689-699.
verdict.corrected_claim: No fixture pins an uncapped helical tip round. ρ = c·m_t is held by the admissible-range bound law and a screw limit test, not by a value check. The m_t choice is already documented in state.md as a stated-sign, stated-size approximation of the normal round's elliptical transverse section.
verdict.proposal_note: An 'independent derivation: the rack's normal-section round seen in the transverse section' does not give c·m_t. It gives an ellipse with semi-axes ρ_n and ρ_n/cos β, whose curvature radii run from ρ_n·cos β to ρ_n/cos² β, which is exactly the approximation state.md records. Such a fixture would therefore check the documented approximation, not an independent truth. Assert g.rho == c·m/cos β for an uncapped helical case (e.g. z=40, β=25, c=0.25) as a value pin, and leave the doc part alone. Regression fixtures are transcribed from handoff_inbound/gear.py, so a new one there needs a reference value from it or a note that it is not reference output.

title: Several threshold tests where an exact value is available
claim: contact_ratio_is_in_the_usual_range asserts 1 < ε < 2, which admits a base-pitch error of cos α (6 %). positive_shift_opens_the_centre_distance asserts 20.0 < a_w < 20.6 where a_w comes from an exact inv α_w relation. ring.rs:2222 asserts 1 < ε < 3. degenerate_input_is_clamped_and_reported asserts clamps.any() rather than the key it means.
evidence: M3 (normal instead of transverse base pitch) was caught, but by efficiency and screw tests, not by the contact-ratio test. Read the listed lines.
proposal: Assert ε = (approach + recess)/(π·m_t·cos α_t) with the base pitch written in the test; a_w = m(z₁ + z₂)cos α_t/(2cos α_w) with inv α_w = inv α_t + 2(x₁ + x₂)tan α_n/(z₁ + z₂), solved in the test by bisection; the specific clamp keys (CLAMP_PRESSURE_ANGLE_RAISED, CLAMP_DEDENDUM_CAPPED, CLAMP_FILLET_CAPPED).
validation: M3 fails the contact-ratio test.

verdict.reason: Each cited test is loose as described, but the finding overstates what that leaves unpinned, and its stated validation is impossible. (1) contact.rs:1659 checks spur pairs only, where m_t = m_n and α_t = α_n. M3 (normal instead of transverse base pitch) yields the same number there, so no spur test, exact or not, can catch it: 'M3 fails the contact-ratio test' is false unless the test gains a helical pair. The preceding test already asserts approach+recess against the textbook tangent-length sum to 1e-12, and the golden corpus prints contact ratios (strength_17_43, shifts_17_43, crossed, planetstage), so only the division by plane::base_pitch is loose. (2) mesh.rs:1343's 20.0 < a_w < 20.6 is loose, but backlash_is_zero_at_the_zero_backlash_centre_distance checks shifted pairs (13/41 x = 0.4/−0.2, 9/9 x = 0.5/0.5) through a thickness-based route, and the golden shifts outputs pin a_w. (3) ring.rs:2222's 1 < ε < 3 is a side sanity bound; the test's claim is internal > external. (4) degenerate_input_is_clamped_and_reported asserts clamps.any(). extremes.rs already checks clamp.dedendum_capped and clamp.fillet_capped by key at their bounds, but CLAMP_PRESSURE_ANGLE_RAISED is asserted by key in no test (grep finds it only in tooth.rs:404 and note.rs), so that key is the real gap.
verdict.evidence: contact.rs:1090-1101 pair() uses GearParams defaults (β=0); contact.rs:106 base_pitch = plane::base_pitch(g1.mt, g1.alpha_t); contact.rs:1640-1655 exact approach+recess check. mesh.rs:1352-1360 backlash-zero law over shifted pairs. extremes.rs:76-160 key checks for 'clamp.dedendum_capped' and 'clamp.fillet_capped'. grep -rn pressure_angle_raised crates --include=*.rs: tooth.rs:404, note.rs:60,271 only. grep -il 'contact ratio|ε_α' tools/golden: strength_17_43_2.0.txt, shifts_17_43.txt, crossed_*, planetstage_*.
verdict.corrected_claim: The contact-ratio, a_w and ring ε tests are range checks where exact values are available, but the quantities are pinned elsewhere (exact path length, backlash law, golden corpus). The contact-ratio test cannot see a transverse/normal base-pitch mix-up at all because it is spur-only. The pressure-angle clamp key is asserted by key nowhere.
verdict.proposal_note: To make the contact-ratio test catch M3, include a helical pair (e.g. β = 20°) and assert ε = (approach + recess)/(π·m_n·cos α_t/cos β) with the base pitch written out in the test. In the degenerate test, assert key::CLAMP_PRESSURE_ANGLE_RAISED specifically, since the other two keys are already covered by extremes.rs. For a_w, solving inv α_w in the test by bisection is fine, but the existing backlash law already gives most of the benefit, so this is optional.

title: A second wall-clock test outside train/
claim: solving_an_amplitude_is_quick_enough_to_type_over asserts under 20 ms per amplitude solve in the parallel suite. It is the same kind of threshold as the known train timing test and is exposed to the same instrumentation and load flake.
evidence: gear.rs:1338-1346; its comment calls the bound 'loose' and records a prior 102 ms.
proposal: Replace with a work count (the number of Tooth builds or root-solve evaluations per amplitude, asserted against the structural bound) or gate it behind cfg(not(coverage)), as proposed for the train test.
validation: The test is stable under llvm-cov.

verdict.reason: The test exists as described: gear.rs:1328-1347, 5 solves timed with Instant, asserting each < 20 ms, with a comment calling the bound loose and recording a prior 102 ms. It is a wall-clock threshold like the train test. The claim that it is 'exposed to the same instrumentation and load flake' does not hold as measured. Its margin is more than 10x, not the train test's roughly 1.9x shortfall. It passed under llvm-cov, and it passed through about 560 cargo-mutants runs of the debug build under parallel load. Every failure of it in the mutants logs panics at the .expect("reachable") on line 1341, which is a real mutation kill, not the timing assert at 1344. What remains is a matter of style: a wall-clock gate is a threshold where a work count would be a law. There is no demonstrated flake.
verdict.evidence: Ran the already-built debug test binary (target/debug/deps/gear_core-b0facde9ababd2f1) and the llvm-cov instrumented binary (cov-target/llvm-cov-target/debug/deps/gear_core-6a25aebcf4a838cc) three times each with --exact gear::tests::solving_an_amplitude_is_quick_enough_to_type_over. The whole process took 0.00-0.01 s wall, so all 5 solves took under 10 ms and each under 2 ms, against the 20 ms bound. In mutants.out/log, 4 logs have the test FAIL: gear.rs_line_919, auto.rs_line_623, gear.rs_line_1131 and gear.rs_line_986. All panic at gear.rs:1341:18, the expect, and no log contains 'solving an amplitude took'.
verdict.corrected_claim: gear.rs:1328 is a second wall-clock test. Its margin is more than 10x in both the debug and the coverage-instrumented builds (under 2 ms against 20 ms), and it has not failed on timing in coverage or in about 560 mutant runs. It is a threshold rather than a law and could become a structural count, but it is not a flake risk the way the train test is.
verdict.proposal_note: The work-count version is the better of the two options. The comment says the 102 ms regression was 'building gears whose teeth nothing read'. A count of Tooth/Gear constructions per amplitude solve, asserted against its structural bound, would catch exactly that regression on any machine. cfg(not(coverage)) is unnecessary because the test already passes under coverage. Low priority.

title: auto.rs carries ~524 lines of stage-era search machinery that production never reaches; Freedoms and Search::effort have no caller at all
claim: The shape's solve (train/shape.rs) searches through `Search::maximise` directly. auto::Freedoms<N> (new/count/boxes/place), Bounds, Pinned (freedoms/place/box_of), shifts_for_efficiency with its private helpers sides and member, the free fn auto::maximise, and Search::effort are unreachable from gear-io, gear-wasm and gear-cli. Freedoms, auto::maximise and Search::effort are called by nothing, not even a test. Their docs describe callers that are gone ('written out twice, identically, in two stage types'; 'a hula solves a crank and chooses the splits').
evidence: rustc dead_code with gear-core made private and seeded only by what io, wasm and cli name (dead_cli.txt): 'struct `Freedoms` is never constructed', 'associated items `new`, `count`, `boxes`, and `place` are never used', 'struct `Bounds`', 'struct `Pinned`', 'function `shifts_for_efficiency`', 'function `sides`', 'function `member`', 'function `maximise`', 'associated items `refined` and `effort` are never used'. `grep -rn 'Freedoms\b\|\.effort()'` finds only the definitions. feature_cost.py over those items: auto.rs 294 code + 230 comment lines. Search::refined is used only by train::tests::the_search_is_converged_not_budgeted, which is fine.
proposal: Delete Freedoms, Bounds, Pinned, shifts_for_efficiency, sides, member, the free fn maximise and Search::effort. Keep Search, Search::SHIPPED, Search::refined and Search::maximise. Then rewrite the Search and maximise docs to name their one caller (Shape's search in shape.rs, around line 1893).
validation: cargo clippy --all-targets -- --deny warnings and cargo nextest run stay green after the deletion, apart from the two tests in the next finding, which go with it. Re-run the seeded dead-code check: auto.rs should report nothing.

verdict.reason: The claim holds. `Freedoms` (auto.rs:936) has no caller anywhere. The free fn `auto::maximise` (auto.rs:1614) is called by nothing: the only `maximise(` calls are `search.maximise` at shape.rs:1893 and 1902, and inside the dead `shifts_for_efficiency` at auto.rs:1558. `Search::effort` (auto.rs:1750) has no caller, and its doc argues from 'a hula solves a crank and chooses the splits', a solver that is gone. `shifts_for_efficiency`, `Bounds`, `Pinned`, `sides` and `member` are reachable only from tests. The shape's search does the same work itself: its `place` closure and box (shape.rs:1819-1852) repeat the `(None,None,None)` cases of `Pinned::place` and `Pinned::box_of` line for line. It shares `MeshTrial`, `CrossedTrial`, `Cut` and `searchable_shift` with the dead function, so the dead function is not an independent oracle either. Nothing is lost by deleting it.
verdict.evidence: grep -rn 'Freedoms\b|shifts_for_efficiency|\bPinned\b|\bBounds\b|\.effort()|maximise(' crates/ gives only the definitions, auto.rs's own tests, train/mod.rs:5232-5290 (a test), and prose at gear-cli/src/main.rs:1542, contact.rs:495 and shape.rs:1790. No gear-io, gear-wasm or gear-cli code names any of these items (gear-cli's `shifts_report` goes through `solve` on `arr::pair` with `set_search`).
verdict.proposal_note: The validation is incomplete. Deleting `shifts_for_efficiency`, `Bounds` and `Pinned` also breaks a third test the finding does not name: train/mod.rs:5231 `the_search_beats_a_scan_of_the_same_interval`, which calls `crate::auto::shifts_for_efficiency` with `Bounds` and `Pinned`. Re-aim that test at the shape's search (see missed). Three pieces of prose that cite the dead items must change in the same commit: gear-cli/src/main.rs:1541-1543 ('the only command that drives `auto::shifts_for_efficiency`', which is false today), contact.rs:495 ('`auto::shifts_for_efficiency` searches the division') and shape.rs:1790 ('`auto::Pinned::place`'). The `Search` doc (auto.rs:1622, 'How hard [`maximise`] looks') links the free fn and needs its link retargeted.

title: Two auto.rs tests (148 lines) exercise only shifts_for_efficiency, which no shipped path calls, so they cannot catch a search fault
claim: the_shifts_it_chooses_are_the_ones_that_lose_least and a_pinned_shift_is_the_shift_it_was_given call shifts_for_efficiency, Pinned and Bounds. Production chooses shifts in Shape's own search (shape.rs, sum-and-division coordinates over MeshTrial/CrossedTrial), so both tests can pass while the shipped search is wrong.
evidence: feature_cost.py: those two fns are the only tests that name shifts_for_efficiency, Pinned or Bounds (82 and 66 lines). The rustc seeded analysis shows shifts_for_efficiency is unreachable from every non-test crate.
proposal: Re-aim both laws at the shipped search: build arr::pair(teeth) with set_search(true). (a) The chosen shifts beat every neighbour on a small grid, measured by solve_preset efficiency. (b) A member with Auto::fixed shift comes back at exactly that shift. Then delete the old tests with the dead code.
validation: Mutation check: perturb Coordinate::Division's place() mapping in shape.rs (for example swap the sign) and confirm the new law fails while the old tests stay green.

verdict.reason: The two auto.rs tests do exercise only the dead `shifts_for_efficiency`, so they can pass while the shipped search is wrong. 'The only tests that name shifts_for_efficiency, Pinned or Bounds' is false: train::tests::the_search_beats_a_scan_of_the_same_interval (mod.rs:5231) also drives the dead function, which leaves three tests aimed at dead code, not two. The shipped search is not untested: the_search_is_converged_not_budgeted (self-consistency at 14x effort), a_given_shift_survives_the_search (shape.rs:5455), a_fully_specified_pair_is_left_alone, a_given_distance_gets_the_gears_the_free_search_would_choose and the golden `shifts` cases all run it. None of them, however, compares the shipped pair search against an independent grid. I ran the finding's own proposed mutation: in a worktree I swapped the Sum/Division mapping in shape.rs's `place` (out[pa]=(s-d)/2, out[pb]=(s+d)/(2 sign)). All 604 gear-core tests passed, including all three dead-function tests. The golden corpus did move: `shifts 9 37` 'least loss' went from x=0.6746/0.7332 to 0.6677/0.7640, and `shifts 17 43` moved in the fourth decimal. Efficiency was unchanged to the printed 97.678 %, so the mutant is nearly equivalent.
verdict.evidence: Worktree mutation run: `cargo nextest run -p gear-core --no-fail-fast` gave 604 passed. The mutated gear-cli, diffed against target/release/gear-cli, showed changes on `shifts 9 37` and `shifts 17 43` and none on `shifts epicyclic` or `hula 18 0.5`.
verdict.corrected_claim: Three tests (auto.rs:2747, auto.rs:2833 and train/mod.rs:5231 the_search_beats_a_scan_of_the_same_interval) check only the dead `shifts_for_efficiency`. The shipped search in shape.rs has self-consistency, pinning and idempotence laws but no law against an independent scan. A mutation of its division mapping passes the whole nextest suite and is seen only by the golden corpus.
verdict.proposal_note: The cheapest fix is to re-aim `the_search_beats_a_scan_of_the_same_interval`: its `at` closure already solves fixed shifts through `solve_preset`. Replace `found` with the shipped search at a given distance (set the distance so the sum is pinned, `set_search(true)`, and read the chosen shifts back) and drop the `shifts_for_efficiency` admissibility pre-check. The proposed validation mutation (swap the division sign) is nearly equivalent, since the efficiency matches to 1e-5, so a neighbour-grid law with SLACK may still pass it. Validate instead with a mutation that visibly loses efficiency, for example halving the Division box width at shape.rs:1829-1832.

title: docs/reference.md and CLAUDE.md describe auto::Freedoms and auto::maximise as the shared search machinery, but Freedoms has no caller
claim: reference.md says '`auto::Freedoms` is the one mapping from what a search hands back onto the full set' and 'The searches share `auto::maximise`'. Freedoms is never constructed, and the free fn maximise is never called; the shape builds its own `place` closure (shape.rs:1834). maximise's doc still argues from 'a pair has its mesh, and an epicyclic has two meshes', the per-stage world.
evidence: grep finds no use of Freedoms outside auto.rs:936-1018. Shape's search calls `search.maximise` (shape.rs:1893, 1902) and maps back through its own `place` closure over Coordinate::{Own,Sum,Division}.
proposal: Rewrite the paragraph: the searches share auto::Search, the shape maps back through its Coordinate::Sum/Division/Own `place`, and name that function. Drop the Freedoms sentence when the type goes.
validation: tools/check_doc_links.py, plus a grep that every `auto::X` named in docs/ exists in the source.

verdict.reason: reference.md:781 says '`auto::Freedoms` is the one mapping from what a search hands back onto the full set', but Freedoms has no caller; the shape maps back through its own `place` closure (shape.rs:1837). reference.md:766 'The searches share `auto::maximise`' names a free fn nobody calls; the shared thing is `auto::Search::maximise`. rationale.md:478 ('`auto::maximise` is a search... Every shape that chooses profile shifts... calls') and CLAUDE.md:97 ('and `maximise`') are loose in the same way. auto.rs:1609-1612 still argues from 'a pair has its mesh, and an epicyclic has two meshes', the per-stage world.
verdict.evidence: sed -n 766,784p docs/reference.md; grep shows `Freedoms` only at auto.rs:936-1018; shape.rs:1893 and 1902 call `search.maximise`.
verdict.proposal_note: Update rationale.md:478 as well, to `auto::Search`. `tools/check_doc_links.py` does not check code identifiers named in docs, so the suggested grep for `auto::X` would be a new ad-hoc check, not an existing gate.

title: No gate runs rustdoc: 22 intra-doc links do not resolve, 9 of them to items that no longer exist
claim: Stale targets include Gear::span (now `extremes`), Tooth::profile and Tooth::outline (moved to Gear), Loading::for_cases, stated_helix, always_given, super::member_inputs, Port and Decided::Given, none of which exist. The rest are scope-only failures such as `kinematics::System::play` and `Freedom` written without a path. tools/check_doc_links.py checks pointers into docs/*.md and never intra-doc links.
evidence: `cargo doc --no-deps -p gear-core -p gear-io -p gear-wasm --document-private-items --message-format short` in a worktree gave 22 'unresolved link' warnings (list in rustdoc_unresolved.txt), plus 22 'links to private item' and 2 'redundant explicit link target' warnings. A grep for fn stated_helix, always_given, member_inputs, for_cases and enum/struct Port finds 0 definitions.
proposal: Fix the 22 links. Add `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links' cargo doc --no-deps --workspace` (with --document-private-items, since private items are linked widely) to flake checks and to CLAUDE.md's check table.
validation: The new check fails on HEAD and passes after the fixes. Reintroduce `[`Self::span`]` and confirm it goes red.

verdict.reason: Reproduced exactly. I ran `cargo doc --no-deps -p gear-core -p gear-io -p gear-wasm --document-private-items` in a worktree: it printed 22 'unresolved link' warnings plus private-item and redundant-link warnings (46 lines in all). The stale targets check out. Gear has no `span` (gear.rs:255; only `span_of` in tests). Tooth has no `profile` or `outline` (outline.rs:3, tooth.rs:324, dxf.rs:35). `stated_helix`, `always_given`, `member_inputs`, `Loading::for_cases` and `Port` have zero definitions. `Decided` has only Chosen and Absorbed (pair.rs:82-88). No CI gate runs rustdoc: flake checks are clippy, fmt and nextest, and ci.yml has no `cargo doc`.
verdict.evidence: notes/verify-ablate-features-1/rustdoc.txt lists 22 unresolved (auto.rs:1032, gear.rs:255, mesh.rs:765, metrology.rs:747, outline.rs:3, strength.rs:331, tooth.rs:324, conditions.rs:162, pair.rs:99, wiring.rs:87, wiring.rs:308, mod.rs:268, 740, 912, 1118, 1711, 2073, 2225, 2804, dxf.rs:35, gear-wasm lib.rs:1419, 1473).
verdict.proposal_note: Include gear-cli in the doc gate (`--workspace`). Rather than a separate nix check that builds docs, `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links -D rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links'` could be added as a craneLib.cargoDoc check. Decide whether private-item links are acceptable before denying `private_intra_doc_links`: with `--document-private-items` they resolve, and 22 of them exist.

title: English prose written into Value.note inside gear-core, and never read by anything
claim: Rule 2 says no English in gear-core. reversed_bending_allowable formats an English sentence ('… x the one-directional allowable of … MPa: a root loaded on both flanks endures less …'), yet its only caller (BendingReduction::bending_allowable) takes `.value` and drops the note. Material::overridden writes note: Some("supplied by the user"), which does cross the boundary inside GearResult.material, but web/src never reads Value.note.
evidence: grep 'reversed_bending_allowable' has one caller, train/mod.rs:2642 `...reversed_bending_allowable(m).value`. The wire analysis plus a manual check of TrainPanel.svelte:1029-1068 (the `property` snippet reads only `used.value` and `used.basis`) show no read of `.note` on a Value.
proposal: Make reversed_bending_allowable return f64, or a Value with note None and basis Derived, since the basis already says it is derived. In overridden() set note: None, since Basis::Overridden says it. If a note is wanted, use a Note key in strings_*.toml.
validation: A test that no Value produced by gear-core code (as opposed to parsed from a library file) carries Some(note). Run cargo nextest and tools/check_golden.sh; gear-cli output may move if the CLI prints the note.

verdict.reason: Two English sentences are authored in gear-core: material.rs:179 (a format! prose note) and material.rs:348 ('supplied by the user'). The first is discarded by its only caller (train/mod.rs:2642 takes `.value`). The second crosses the boundary but nothing reads it: no `.note` read on a Value in web/src, and gear-cli prints notes only of the library entries (main.rs:2429), never of overridden values. Rule 2 is breached, harmlessly for now, which makes this low severity.
verdict.evidence: grep -rn 'note: Some(' crates/gear-core/src gives material.rs:179 and 348 in production; the rest are tests. TrainPanel.svelte:1063-1066 renders only `used.basis`.
verdict.proposal_note: Setting `note: None` on an Overridden or Derived Value contradicts the documented invariant on `Value::note` (material.rs:200-201: 'Always present on anything that is not a plain datasheet reading'), which gear-io's library test enforces (materials.rs:222-229) and rationale.md#material-data-ships-estimates-deliberately restates. Better: make `reversed_bending_allowable` return `f64`, since its one caller wants only the number and `REVERSED_BENDING_FRACTION` documents it. For `overridden`, restate the invariant as scoped to library entries, where Basis::Overridden says it all. The 'no Some(note) from core' test would then be consistent.

title: The material basis badge shows the enum's English initial: datasheet and derived both show 'd', and TypeScript re-derives is_measured
claim: `{used.basis[0]}` prints the first letter of the serde name: overridden→o, datasheet→d, derived→d, chart→c, estimated→e. Datasheet and derived are indistinguishable, the letter is untranslated English in all five languages, and the weak/strong split restates Basis::is_measured, which only gear-cli calls.
evidence: Serde names from material.rs:64-85 (rename_all snake_case). Basis::is_measured is used only at gear-cli/src/main.rs:2260 and in tests.
proposal: Serve a per-basis `ui.basis_<name>` short label and title from the catalogues, and have Rust send `measured: bool` next to basis, or expose it on Value, so the panel does not restate the rule. Render the key, not `basis[0]`.
validation: tools/check_strings.py covers the new ui keys. A panel check that the five bases render five distinct labels.

verdict.reason: TrainPanel.svelte:1064-1065 renders `used.basis[0]`, so datasheet and derived both show 'd' (the shipped library has one derived value). The letters are untranslated and have no title or legend in the panel. gear-cli's `materials` legend uses 'D' for derived, so the two front ends disagree. `class:weak={estimated||chart}` is exactly `!Basis::is_measured()` (material.rs:89-91) restated in TypeScript. One detail of the claim overreaches: 'overridden→o' is never rendered, because an overridden property takes the `{#if gear.material_overrides[key] !== null}` branch and shows the clear button instead.
verdict.evidence: sed -n 1055,1068p web/src/TrainPanel.svelte; `grep basis = materials_default.toml` counts: 28 datasheet, 1 derived, 1 chart, 10 estimated; gear-cli/src/main.rs:2415 legend 'd datasheet   D derived ...'.
verdict.proposal_note: The validation should expect four distinct badge labels, not five, unless the badge is also shown beside an override. The gear-wasm doc (lib.rs:994-997) and rationale.md say the UI is expected to show which numbers are estimates and why. Serving the library's `note` as the badge's title would honour that at no extra cost.

title: Material provenance crosses the boundary but is never shown, and Family's doc claims a use that does not exist
claim: Material.class (Family), grade, condition, source and each Value.note cross in Material and GearResult.material, and no .svelte or .ts reads them. Family's doc says it is 'Carried because several conventions are per-family — the uniform fatigue fraction applied across the polyamides, and the reversed-bending penalty a planet gear takes'. In fact REVERSED_BENDING_FRACTION applies to any material (its own doc says so), and the only reader of `.class` is one gear-io test. CLAUDE.md says 'Two inputs the panel never reads'; the true count is at least six.
evidence: `grep -rn '\.class\b'` in crates/ finds only gear-io/src/materials.rs:247, inside a #[test]. Web greps for `.grade` or `.source` hit only ClassRef (JGMA) and nothing on Material. rustc's seeded analysis with serde off would flag these fields, but serde is on across the workspace.
proposal: Either show provenance in the material box (source, grade, condition, and the Value.note on hover), which is what the library's careful basis/note data exists for, or list these fields under CLAUDE.md's 'never reads'. Rewrite Family's doc to its real role: a library classification and the polyamide-estimate test's filter.
validation: wire_fields.py (in notes/) reports no unread Material field, or CLAUDE.md lists each one.

verdict.reason: Holds for the panel. `Material.class/grade/condition/source` and `Value.note` cross the boundary, and no .svelte or .ts file reads them. The panel reads only `name`, the five values and `basis` (TrainPanel.svelte:1064). Family's doc (material.rs:130-133) is half wrong. The polyamide 0.30 fraction really is a per-family convention, but it is a fact about the library data, checked only by the gear-io test at materials.rs:247. `REVERSED_BENDING_FRACTION` (material.rs:167) says itself that it 'applies to any material', and `reversed_bending_allowable` never reads `class`. So CLAUDE.md's 'Two inputs the panel never reads' undercounts. One nuance: gear-cli's materials command does print grade, condition, source and every `Value.note` (main.rs:2419-2429), so they are not dead. Only the panel ignores them.
verdict.evidence: grep '\.class\b' over crates/ finds only gear-io/src/materials.rs:247 (a #[test]). grep '\.(grade|condition|source)' over web/src finds only JGMA `tolerance.class.grade`. gear-cli/src/main.rs:2419-2429 prints m.grade, m.condition, m.source and v.note. material.rs:156-160: 'it applies to any material'.
verdict.proposal_note: If the choice is to list the fields in CLAUDE.md rather than show them, say they are read by the harness's `materials` command. Rewriting Family's doc as 'a library classification; the polyamide-estimate test filters on it' is right. The English-in-Value.note issue is already covered by ablate-features[4] and strength[15], so keep it out of this finding.

title: The uniform-tooth metrology API is test-only, duplicating the per-gear *_at/_around API the product uses
claim: gear-wasm uses only best_span_around, over_pins_at, pin_diameter_range_around, cutter_tip_width and between_pins. span_over_teeth, best_span, pin_geometry and over_pins (the Tooth-based twins) are reached only from tests/metrology.rs. best_span and best_span_around state the span-selection rule separately. best_span_around's doc says the k chosen is the one nearest the pitch circle 'averaged over the revolution', but the code minimises the worst offset (a max, not an average: `worst_offset < *w`).
evidence: rustc seeded analysis: 'function `span_over_teeth`/`best_span`/`pin_geometry`/`over_pins` is never used' even with gear-cli as a root. inventory.tsv: over_pins has 12 test uses and 0 production uses. pin_geometry is a one-line wrapper of pin_seat, which Space::seat already exposes.
proposal: Either move the four functions into tests/common as the uniform-gear oracle, stated as such, or keep them public with doc comments naming them as the Δx=0 oracle for the *_at functions. Also delete pin_geometry in favour of Space::of(g).seat(d). Fix best_span_around's doc to say 'the least worst-case offset from the pitch circle'.
validation: tests/metrology.rs still holds best_span_around(Gear::new(p)) equal to best_span(Tooth::new(p)) at angular_shift 0, bit for bit.

verdict.reason: `span_over_teeth`, `best_span`, `pin_geometry` and `over_pins` are reached only from tests: crates/gear-core/tests/metrology.rs, plus gear-io strings.rs:1298/1319, which sit inside `#[cfg(test)]` from line 293. The doc/code mismatch is real. `best_span_around` (metrology.rs:596) says 'averaged over the revolution', but the code keeps `worst_offset = worst_offset.max(...)` and picks the least of those maxima (`worst_offset < *w`). My probe found that on a uniform gear both rules choose the same k in all 12,214 cases I tried: z 4..200, x from -0.5 to 1.0, β 0 and 20°. That k agreement is not written down as a test anywhere.
verdict.evidence: Probe (probes/verify-ablate-features-2) comparing best_span(Tooth) with best_span_around(Gear) on uniform gears: n=12214, diffk=0, diffok=0, and diffbits=4847. The span values differ in the last ulp in 4847 cases, e.g. z=5 gives 4.374990725068645 against 4.374990725068644.
verdict.proposal_note: Two problems with the proposal. (1) Its validation step, 'bit for bit', fails: the uniform-tooth span and the per-gear span agree only to about 1 ulp in 40% of cases. The assertion should be same k plus the value to about 1e-15 relative. Alternatively, span_over_teeth_at's claim that it gives back span_over_teeth 'exactly' is itself only exact in the mathematics. (2) `pin_geometry` is not `Space::of(g).seat(d)`. `seat` adds the form, tip and root checks, and tests/metrology.rs:175/535/629/669 rely on the raw `pin_seat`, for instance expecting PinTooSmall only from the base-circle test. Replacing it changes what those tests assert. Moving the Tooth-based twins into tests/common as the Δx=0 oracle is the cleaner option.

title: teeth_clear and as_asked: their docs say several searches depend on them, but the only caller is one gear-cli line
claim: MeshReport::teeth_clear's doc says it exists because a filter 'quietly started accepting' fouling candidates. GearResult::as_asked's says 'a search choosing between designs wants exactly this question and there is more than one such search'. Neither has a caller in gear-core, gear-io or gear-wasm, and neither has a test; the production search asks interference inside shape.rs's trial objects. MeshReport::backlash_by_drive's 'the conversion, in one place' is likewise test-only: production PathReport builds its backlash with its own backlash_at (mod.rs:3517).
evidence: inventory.tsv: teeth_clear core 0, io 0, wasm 0, cli 1, tests 0; as_asked the same. backlash_by_drive: tests 18, production 0.
proposal: Move teeth_clear and as_asked into gear-cli next to their one filter, or trim their docs to 'the harness's filter'. Either make PathReport's backlash use backlash_by_drive, or delete it and let the tests read backlash[1]/[0] directly. Remove the history sentences ('within the hour', 'the day the two notes moved').
validation: The seeded rustc dead-code run with only io and wasm as roots reports nothing new in train/mod.rs. cargo nextest stays green.

verdict.reason: `teeth_clear` and `as_asked` have exactly one caller, gear-cli/src/main.rs:1156-1157, and no test. `as_asked`'s 'there is more than one such search' is false today. The history sentences ('within the hour', 'the day the two notes moved') are there as described. `backlash_by_drive` is test-only: its callers are crossed.rs from line 448, all after `#[cfg(test)]` at 139, and mod.rs:10416. Its doc's 'the conversion, in one place' plus the spur-stage history is stale. The claim goes wrong in implying that PathReport should use it. PathReport's `backlash_at` (mod.rs:3467-3482) computes a different quantity: the play along a whole path, summed over every mesh with `system.play` coefficients. `backlash_by_drive` only relabels one mesh's two per-member readings.
verdict.evidence: grep over crates: teeth_clear and as_asked appear only at gear-cli/src/main.rs:1156-1157 and in their definitions. backlash_by_drive appears only in crossed.rs test lines 448-1646 and mod.rs:10416-10418 (tests). mod.rs:3467 `backlash_at = |read, from| Backlash::banded(... coefficient(k, read, from) * play[band] ...)`.
verdict.corrected_claim: teeth_clear and as_asked are used only by the harness's filter, and backlash_by_drive only by tests. Their docs claim wider use and carry history. PathReport's path backlash is a different quantity (the whole-graph play), not a second copy of backlash_by_drive's per-mesh relabelling.
verdict.proposal_note: Do not route PathReport through backlash_by_drive, because that would replace path play with one mesh's play. Delete backlash_by_drive or move it into a test helper, and trim teeth_clear and as_asked to 'the harness's admissibility filter' (or move them into gear-cli). Related: missed_findings already notes that teeth_clear omits bottom clearance.

title: contact.rs keeps test-only closed-form split code, and sliding_at has a stale milestone note
claim: split_residual and efficient_split (the closed-form stationary condition docs/rationale.md says is deliberately not used) are reached only by contact.rs tests. sliding_at is reached only by tests, and Sliding with sliding_velocity only by gear-cli. sliding_at's doc still says 'The crossed-axis version of this arrives with the screw geometry it needs (milestone 7, step 5)'; the screw geometry has shipped.
evidence: dead_cli.txt: 'function `split_residual`', 'function `efficient_split`', 'function `sliding_at` is never used'. dead_prod.txt adds 'struct `Sliding`' and 'function `sliding_velocity`' (CLI-only).
proposal: Move split_residual and efficient_split under #[cfg(test)], or into tests/, as the record of why the closed form is not used. Delete sliding_at's milestone paragraph, and either route the CLI through sliding_at or delete it.
validation: The seeded rustc run shows nothing unreachable in contact.rs outside #[cfg(test)].

verdict.reason: `split_residual` and `efficient_split` are test-only. That is deliberate and stated in the code: contact.rs:490-497 has a '# Nothing in production calls this' heading, docs/corrections.md:564 records it, and auto.rs:1468 cites split_residual as the derived closed form the search does not use. The stale milestone paragraph in `sliding_at` (contact.rs:630-632) is confirmed. The finding misstates the sliding code: `Sliding` and `sliding_velocity` are not used by gear-cli. gear-cli:2159's `c.sliding_velocity` is a field of the train's case report (mod.rs:328), filled from shape.rs:2754. The function `sliding_velocity` is called only by `sliding_at` and by screw.rs tests (after `#[cfg(test)]` at 1494), and `sliding_at` by nothing outside tests. So the whole sliding chain is test-only in production. That point is already in missed_findings ('sliding_velocity / sliding_at / Sliding are public production API that only tests call').
verdict.evidence: grep 'sliding_velocity(' shows contact.rs:604 (the definition), contact.rs's use in sliding_at, and screw.rs:1797 inside the test module that starts at screw.rs:1494. gear-cli uses only the `sliding_velocity` field of the case report. contact.rs:630: 'The crossed-axis version of this arrives with the screw geometry it needs (milestone 7, step 5)'.
verdict.corrected_claim: The sliding_at doc paragraph about milestone 7 is stale. sliding_at, sliding_velocity and Sliding are production-dead: only contact.rs and screw.rs tests use them, not gear-cli. split_residual and efficient_split are test-only by a documented choice.
verdict.proposal_note: Moving split_residual under #[cfg(test)] breaks the intra-doc link in auto.rs:1468 (`[crate::contact::split_residual]`), which rustdoc resolves only in non-test builds, so that doc link must change too. The reasoning for keeping it public ('a derived and checked fact about the model') is weak but deliberate. Moving both into tests/ with the derivation is reasonable. For the sliding functions, the best fix is to have Contact::slip and sliding_velocity share one implementation, or delete the chain (see missed_findings).

title: gear-io/src/train.rs opens with ~200 lines of format change log for files the parser now refuses anyway
claim: The module doc's 'The shape can change' section lists every past migration: working_depth, thickness_mod, load_sharing, frictions, worm-as-pair, the load-case list, helix onto members, arrangement onto the train, stage kinds into one shape, thickness_mod as Auto, tip_clearance, and more. Nearly every one describes a format from_toml now refuses and `convert` does not read either, since Staged holds `Vec<Shape>`. It is history rather than a description of the current format, which the project's goals rule out for comments.
evidence: `awk 'NR<=200 && /^\/\/!/'` counts 200 module-doc lines. convert's StagedDocument (train.rs:395-411) deserialises only `stages: Vec<Shape>`, so none of the older layouts described can be converted either.
proposal: Replace the log with the current format and the one rule (an unknown or missing field is refused by name; `gear-cli convert` reads the last stage-list format). Move the migration list, if it is worth keeping, to docs/corrections.md or a CHANGELOG.
validation: tools/check_doc_links.py. A reader can find the document's current fields in one place.

verdict.reason: The module doc has 291 `//!` lines. The '# The shape can change' section runs from line 23 to about 257, roughly 235 lines of per-migration history, and nearly every entry describes a layout that from_toml refuses and that `convert` (StagedDocument, which holds `stages: Vec<Shape>`) cannot read either. The section contradicts itself: it opens with 'Two changes so far:' and then lists about 22 entries. A few entries do carry current facts: the defaults for an absent `tip_clearance`, `role`, `pressure_angle`, `overlap`, `min_contact_ratio` and `min_planet_clearance`. Those belong in a short description of the current format, not a log.
verdict.evidence: gear-io/src/train.rs:23-27 '...Two changes so far:' followed by bullets through line ~257. train.rs:392-411 `struct Staged { load_cases, reversed_bending, stages: Vec<Shape>, held }` with deny_unknown_fields, so only the last stage-list layout converts.
verdict.proposal_note: CLAUDE.md's 'A load-case input' row tells a developer to update 'gear-io/src/train.rs's change log'. Changing the log's form means changing that row as well. Keep 'No compatibility shim, deliberately', but see finding 11: two serde shims (`ground_if_null` and `coefficient`) already contradict it.

title: serde back-compat shims read shapes no current writer produces, and 'not carried' crosses the boundary as 0 in one type and null in another
claim: ground_if_null accepts `carried_by: null` 'as a stored train wrote it'. TOML cannot express null, and the web persists nothing but the language (core.ts:459-482), so no current input can reach that branch. coefficient() accepts the old `{auto, manual}` addendum shape. Separately, Axis.carried_by crosses as a Body where 0 means ground, while AxisGroup.carried_by crosses as Option<usize> where null means ground. The panel therefore tests `!== 0` in members.ts and `!== null` in TrainPanel.svelte for the same fact.
evidence: localStorage is read and written only for LANGUAGE_KEY. The wire types differ: core/Axis.ts has `carried_by: number` and core/AxisGroup.ts has `carried_by: number | null`. groupings.rs:123 converts GROUND to None.
proposal: Drop ground_if_null (keep `default`), and decide whether coefficient's legacy arm stays alongside the other refused formats. Make AxisGroup.carried_by a Body with 0 for ground like Axis, or drop it and have the panel read shape.axes[axis].carried_by.
validation: Round-trip every shipped TOML fixture and every preset through import_train/export_train. Check that the panel shows no carried chip for a ground axis in either view.

verdict.reason: The web's localStorage holds only the language code (core.ts:459-482). `git log -S localStorage`, `-S sessionStorage` and `-S indexedDB` show the only storage ever added was the language picker (a70ea4d). So the 'browser's stored train' that `ground_if_null` exists for (shape.rs:69-73, added in 6e24d50) was never persisted, and TOML cannot write null. The shim is exercised only by its own wasm test. The Axis and AxisGroup representations do differ: Axis.ts has `carried_by: number` with 0 as ground, and AxisGroup.ts has `carried_by: number | null` (groupings.rs:123). The panel tests the same fact as `?? 0) !== 0` (TrainPanel.svelte:241), `!== 0` (members.ts:34), `!== null` (TrainPanel.svelte:536/584) and `!= null` (:830). I also probed the `coefficient` legacy arm: it accepts unknown keys silently. That breaks the deny_unknown_fields promise which gear-io/src/train.rs states and enforces everywhere else (see missed).
verdict.evidence: Probe: MemberGear JSON with addendum={"manual":1.2,"junk":7,"whatever":"x"} gives Ok(1.2), while a top-level junk key gives Err('unknown field `junk`'). gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:1813 a_stored_train_with_a_null_carrier_still_loads is the only thing that reaches ground_if_null.
verdict.proposal_note: When dropping ground_if_null, delete the wasm test at lib.rs:1813 as well, and move the round-trip doc paragraph at lines 1800-1809 back onto its own test (see missed). Remove the `coefficient` legacy arm too, or give its struct variant deny_unknown_fields, and add a refused-format bullet to train.rs. Making AxisGroup.carried_by a Body with 0 as ground matches Axis and the rule that one fact should have one encoding.

title: The gear-wasm crate description still says 'three functions'; there are 23 entry points
claim: description = "The WebAssembly boundary. Thin by design: three functions, JSON in, JSON out.". tools/wasm_boundary.json lists 23, and lib.rs:984 still calls import_train 'The third of the three entry points docs/rationale.md#the-stack planned'.
evidence: tools/wasm_boundary.json 'entries' has 23 names, and every one is imported and called in web/src/core.ts:170-194.
proposal: Change the description to 'The WebAssembly boundary: pure JSON-in, JSON-out entry points (tools/wasm_boundary.json lists them)' and drop the 'third of three' sentence.
validation: Read it.

verdict.reason: Both stale sentences are there as quoted, and the boundary list has 23 entries.
verdict.evidence: crates/gear-wasm/Cargo.toml:3 reads `description = "The WebAssembly boundary. Thin by design: three functions, JSON in, JSON out."`. crates/gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:984, the doc comment on solve_train, says 'The third of the three entry points docs/rationale.md#the-stack planned.' `python3 -c ...len(json.load(open('tools/wasm_boundary.json'))['entries'])` prints 23. One small correction: the sentence is on solve_train (lib.rs:982-988), not on import_train as the claim says.

title: Other stale or aspirational docs on test-only items
claim: Gear::distinct_teeth says 'Reported because it is the cost of the feature'; nothing reports it (tests only). Gear::distinct says the over-teeth and over-pins measurements 'are the obvious next customers'; they shipped as *_around and don't use it. Ratio::cmp_checked is 'for a caller that wants to sort readable output'; there is none. Shaft::index_pub has tests as its only caller. Search::effort describes a hula solver that no longer exists.
evidence: inventory.tsv TEST-ONLY rows: distinct_teeth (2 test uses), cmp_checked (4), index_pub (9). effort has 0 uses.
proposal: Make each #[cfg(test)] or delete it (effort), and trim the docs to what is true now.
validation: The seeded rustc run and clippy both stay clean.

verdict.reason: All five hold. index_pub, cmp_checked and distinct_teeth are only reached from #[cfg(test)] code, effort() has no callers, and each doc names a customer that does not exist or no longer exists.
verdict.evidence: grep over crates/: distinct_teeth is used only at gear.rs:2629/2639 (tests start at gear.rs:1146). cmp_checked is used only at ratio.rs:323-330 (tests start at ratio.rs:216). index_pub is used at kinematics.rs:1049 (tests start at 730), train/mod.rs:6562/6578 (tests start at 1806), and planetary.rs:153-154, inside a #[cfg(test)] fn at 150, and 508/563/598 (tests start at 330). `.effort()` has 0 hits, and its doc (auto.rs:1745) describes 'a hula solves a crank and chooses the splits', a solver that is now only an arrangement list. Gear::distinct itself is used in production (gear-wasm lib.rs:404-405), so only its doc sentence is stale. metrology's span_over_teeth_at/over_pins_at/best_span_around take the Gear and an index, and none of them calls distinct().
