A 10 % change of the count moves `graph`, `trainfile` and `convert` in the corpus: efficiency 59.824913 -> 59.824912 %, output torque -841.196877739 -> -841.196877623 (1.4e-10 relative). The corpus therefore records quadrature error as signal. Any refinement of the integrator churns three outputs.
evidence: diff notes/ablate-rate/out_base/{graph,trainfile}.txt against out/path_samples/: 5 lines in graph, 1 each in trainfile and convert, all at the 8th to 10th significant digit.
proposal: Integrate the smooth periodic integrand with Gauss–Legendre or adaptive Simpson to a stated relative tolerance near 1e-13, so the printed digits are converged. Or have the harness print the path efficiency and torque to the precision the quadrature guarantees (6 significant digits).
validation: Doubling or halving the sample or tolerance setting leaves every corpus output byte-identical.

verdict.reason: Reproduced from the auditor's saved outputs: a 10 % change of PATH_SAMPLES moves graph (4 lines), trainfile and convert (1 line each) at the 8th to 10th significant digit. This directly contradicts the convergence test's own doc (screw.rs:2656-2658): 'a few hundred samples put it far below any digit this crate reports'. The corpus prints output torque to 12 significant digits (-841.196877739), and the test only asserts error(2048) < 1e-9. The implied O(h²) residual at 2048 is about 1.4e-10/(1-(2048/2253)²) ≈ 8e-10 relative, which matches the doc's 'below 1e-9' and is above the printed resolution.
verdict.evidence: diff notes/ablate-rate/out_base/graph.txt vs out/path_samples/graph.txt: 'efficiency 59.824913' -> '59.824912' (lines 1173, 1175, 2500, 2502); trainfile/convert: 'output torque Nm -841.196877739' -> '-841.196877623'. screw.rs:1176-1197: trapezium over zone [s0, s1]; screw.rs:2660-2710: the test asserts the error ratio is in (3, 5), i.e. second order.
verdict.proposal_note: The integrand is NOT periodic. It runs over the contact zone [zone0, zone1], which is why the trapezium rule is second order here (the test asserts exactly that), so 'smooth periodic' is wrong. Gauss–Legendre is still the right fix: the integrand is smooth on a finite interval, so about 16-32 nodes should reach 1e-15, and it cuts cost about 60×. That matters because locking_friction runs Brent over this efficiency, about 2049 contact evaluations per iterate. The cheapest alternative is Simpson weights on the same grid (O(h⁴), about 1e-15 at 2048). Either way the_path_average_has_converged must be rewritten for the new rule's order, and its 'far below any digit reported' sentence corrected.

title: shaper.rs module doc contradicts its own code on where σ appears, and names a module that does not exist
claim: The module doc says σ 'appears in exactly three places: the centre distance a = r + σ r_c, the side of the cutter its tip points from, and the sense the workpiece turns'. The code at shaper.rs:251-256 says '**No `σ` here** ... The two reversals cancel, and the workpiece turns `(s − phase)/r` either way'. docs/reference.md:1560-1562 says 'σ = ±1 appears in exactly **two** places ... Deliberately not in the rolling'. So the module doc is wrong on the one point the code comment calls a result rather than an oversight. The same doc twice names `profile::Tooth::trochoid_at` (lines 14 and 33), but gear-core has no `profile` module; the function is `crate::tooth::Tooth::trochoid_at` (tooth.rs:539). Line 6 justifies the module by 'the one genuinely new curve milestone 8 needs'. That is project-plan history with no referent in docs/.
evidence: shaper.rs:39-41 quoted above. In production, σ appears only in the centre distance (the `a_ref` line in `new`, and `reference_centre_distance` at line 218) and in the corner centre `a − σ r_c cos φ` and its derivatives (lines 232, 297-298 and 347-349). The rotation `(s − self.phase) / r` at lines 257 and 314 carries no σ. `grep -n 'pub mod' crates/gear-core/src/lib.rs` lists no `profile` module. `grep -rn 'profile::' crates/gear-core/src` finds only shaper.rs:14 and 33.
proposal: Rewrite shaper.rs:39-43 to say σ appears in two places, the centre distance and the side the tip points from, and not in the rolling, where two reversals cancel. Point to line 251 or to reference.md#the-shaper-trochoid instead of restating it. Replace `profile::Tooth::trochoid_at` with [`crate::tooth::Tooth::trochoid_at`] at lines 14 and 33. Delete 'milestone 8 needs' from line 6. Do this in the same edit as the External-row relabel from finding 12.
validation: Read the module doc against lines 251-257. check_doc_links.py does not cover this, so a reviewer checks it. After making line 33 an intra-doc link, run `cargo doc -p gear-core` and confirm no new warning.

verdict.reason: Holds as stated. The module doc says sigma appears in three places, one of them 'the sense the workpiece turns'. The code at shaper.rs:251-257 says there is no sigma in the rotation, and reference.md#the-shaper-trochoid says exactly two places. `profile::Tooth::trochoid_at` names a module that does not exist, and 'milestone 8' is plan history.
verdict.evidence: shaper.rs:39-41: 'appears in exactly three places: the centre distance a = r + σ r_c, the side of the cutter its tip points from, and the sense the workpiece turns.' shaper.rs:251-257: '**No `σ` here** ... The two reversals cancel ... let rotation = (s - self.phase) / r;'. reference.md:1560-1562: 'σ = ±1 appears in exactly **two** places ... Deliberately not in the rolling'. lib.rs lists no `pub mod profile`. `grep -rn 'profile::' crates/gear-core/src` hits only shaper.rs:14 and :33. The function lives at tooth.rs:539 `pub fn trochoid_at`. shaper.rs:6 reads 'curve milestone 8 needs.'
verdict.proposal_note: The fix is right. The same class of stale plan history is in contact.rs:634, '(milestone 7, step 5)', which promises that a crossed-axis version of `sliding_at` will arrive. See the missed finding on sliding_at: it has no production caller. Fix both in the same pass.

title: 14 broken rustdoc intra-doc links in gear-core, and no check builds the docs
claim: `cargo doc -p gear-core --no-deps` at HEAD emits 34 warnings. 14 are unresolved intra-doc links, most of them names that refactors removed: `crate::Ring` (not re-exported), `Self::span` on Gear (no such item), `Tooth::profile` twice (it is `Gear::profile` now, gear.rs:544), `Wiring::mounts`, `kinematics::System::play`, `stated_helix`, `Port`, `GROUND`, `minimum_profile_shift`, `rolling_curvature_radius`, and `MeshError::note`, `MeasurementError::note` and `TrainError::note`. 18 more are public docs linking to private items, and 2 are redundant link targets. Neither CI nor `nix flake check` runs rustdoc. check_doc_links.py checks pointers into docs/*.md, not Rust intra-doc links. So a pointer from one code comment to another code item can go stale silently. That is the class of drift the project gates elsewhere.
evidence: Output of `cargo doc --offline -p gear-core --no-deps` at the untouched tree, saved at /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-ring/doc_base.txt. It ends 'warning: `gear-core` (lib doc) generated 34 warnings'. Grouped: 14 'unresolved link to', 18 'links to private item', 2 'redundant explicit link target'. The run steps in .github/workflows/ci.yml are flake check, web build, check_doc_links, check_strings, check_bindings, npm check, golden, check_units, check_wasm and dxf; there is no `cargo doc`. The flake's `checks` hold clippy and fmt, and I found no cargoDoc.
proposal: Fix the 14 unresolved links: point each at its current item or drop the brackets. Then either fix the 18 private-item links or set `#![allow(rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links)]` in lib.rs, and add a gate: `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`, as a crane `cargoDoc` check in flake.nix or as a CI step, and add a row for it in CLAUDE.md's check table.
validation: `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` exits 0. Renaming any linked item then fails the gate.

verdict.reason: Reproduced in my own target dir: 34 rustdoc warnings, of which 14 are unresolved links and 18 are private-item links. CI and the flake run no rustdoc, and check_doc_links.py covers only pointers into docs/*.md.
verdict.evidence: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=.../wt-target/verify-added-1 gc /home/user/gearcalc cargo doc --offline -p gear-core --no-deps` printed "warning: `gear-core` (lib doc) generated 34 warnings". `grep -c 'unresolved link'` = 14 and `grep -c 'private item'` = 18. Spot checks: gear.rs:255 links `Self::span`, but Gear has no `fn span` (grep finds only a test helper `span_of` at 1603). mesh.rs:765 links `MeshError::note`, which is a method of the trait `crate::note::Explain` (impl at mesh.rs:749), not an inherent method. lib.rs does not re-export `Ring`. ci.yml has no `cargo doc` step.
verdict.proposal_note: Three of the links (`MeshError::note`, `MeasurementError::note`, `TrainError::note`) should point at `crate::note::Explain::note`, not be dropped. For the 18 private-item links: this crate's docs are read in the source, not published, so gating with `cargo doc --document-private-items` (RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings') is better than a crate-wide allow. It keeps the private links checked instead of silencing them. Whatever gate is added needs a row in CLAUDE.md's check table and in ci.yml, per the project's 'run everything the table marks yes' rule.

title: mesh.contact_ratio_below_one tells a helical pair with full overlap that it 'loses contact between teeth'
claim: The line-contact note fires on ε_α < 1 and says 'contact ratio {ratio}: below 1, the pair loses contact between teeth'. For a helical pair, contact continuity is governed by ε_γ = ε_α + ε_β. With ε_β >= 1, contact never lapses, even with ε_α < 1. The note therefore states a false physical fact, and it labels as 'contact ratio' a transverse figure while MeshReport.contact_ratio, the headline number, holds ε_γ. Flagging ε_α < 1 itself is defensible: ISO 6336's formulae are not applicable below a transverse contact ratio of 1.0. The wording is what is wrong.
evidence: Probe (verify-primitives): arrangements::pair([17,43]), helix +30/-30, addendum 0.55, face width 60, solved with solve_alone. Result: MeshReport.contact_ratio 10.310, (ε_α, ε_β, ε_γ) = (0.760, 9.549, 10.310), notes [("mesh.contact_ratio_below_one", {"ratio": "0.760"})]. With addendum 0.45: ε_γ 10.178, same note with 0.628. Only at face width 5 (ε_β 0.80) does overlap_below_one join it. The panel shows ε_α 0.7604 in warn colour beside ε_γ 10.3097 (TrainPanel.svelte:1119-1125), and the note says the pair loses contact.
proposal: Split the finding by what it means. (a) Raise 'loses contact between teeth' when the ratio that governs continuity is below 1: ε_γ on a line contact, the zone's ratio on a point contact. (b) On a line contact with ε_α < 1 <= ε_γ, raise a separate note, e.g. mesh.transverse_contact_ratio_below_one, 'transverse contact ratio {ratio}: below 1, outside the range ISO 6336 rates', since the rating's load-point clamp (strength.rs:1543) then sits at the tip. Raise both from the one helper that finding 15 proposes. Add the new key to note.rs and to all 5 catalogues.
validation: A test in train/mod.rs: a 30° helical 17/43 pair with addendum 0.55 and width 60 carries the ISO-scope note and not the loses-contact note. At width 5 with addendum 0.45 (ε_γ 1.42) it still does not say 'loses contact'. A spur pair with ε_α < 1 says 'loses contact'. gear_io::strings note-firing check.

verdict.reason: The note fires on the transverse ratio alone (train/mod.rs:471-473) and says 'the pair loses contact between teeth'. On a helical line contact with ε_β ≥ 1, total contact never lapses, so the sentence is physically false there. The headline `contact_ratio` field holds ε_γ (mod.rs:481), so the note and the figure beside it disagree. Warning about ε_α < 1 is legitimate: the rating's load-point clamp (strength.rs:1540-1545) depends on it. The wording is the defect.
verdict.evidence: mod.rs:471: `if r.transverse < 1.0 { notes.push(Note::new(key::MESH_CONTACT_RATIO_BELOW_ONE).number("ratio", r.transverse, 3)); }`. strings_en.toml:136: 'contact ratio {ratio}: below 1, the pair loses contact between teeth'. My independent computation for 17/43, m_n=1, α_n=20°, β=30°, h_a=0.55, b=60 gives ε_α=0.776 (bare tip circles; the solver's 0.760 differs by tip treatment) and ε_β = b sinβ/(π m_n) = 9.549, matching the probe's ε_β.
verdict.proposal_note: (a) and (b) are sound. A smaller alternative with the same effect: keep one key but branch its words on whether ε_γ ≥ 1. That is still a branch, though, so the two-key split is cleaner. The new key needs all 5 catalogues, and gear_io::strings' firing test needs a case that reaches it.

title: ALPHA_MAX's doc misstates the tool's pressure-angle limit and inv(60°)
claim: involute.rs:28-29 says 'a 60° pressure angle, the most this tool allows, gives inv α ≈ 0.51'. Both halves are wrong. The admissible pressure angle is Bound::strictly(0.0, 90.0) (auto.rs:696), and there is no 60° cap anywhere in params.rs or tooth.rs. inv(60°) is 0.685; 0.51 is inv(≈56°). The test comment at line 83 repeats 'The tool allows pressure angles to 60°'.
evidence: Probe: inv(60°) = 0.6848532563722791 and inv(56.5°) = 0.5247. auto.rs:696: `pressure_angle: Bound::strictly(0.0, 90.0)`. grep finds no MAX_PRESSURE guard: params.rs guard has only MIN_PRESSURE_ANGLE_DEG = 0.5.
proposal: Rewrite the ALPHA_MAX paragraph: 'At this value inv α ≈ 1e12; a pressure angle is admissible to just under 90°, so the bound only keeps tan off its pole. It is not a physical limit, and v beyond inv(ALPHA_MAX) is refused as unbracketed.' Fix the test comment at line 83 to match, and extend the round-trip test past 85° if the admissible range really runs to 90°.
validation: Read-only doc change; check_doc_links and check_figures stay green.

verdict.reason: There is no 60° cap. The admissible pressure angle is Bound::strictly(0.0, 90.0), and inv(60°) is 0.685, not 0.51 (0.51 is inv(56.1°)). The test comment repeats the false cap.
verdict.evidence: involute.rs:28-29: 'a 60° pressure angle, the most this tool allows, gives `inv α ≈ 0.51`'. involute.rs:83: '// The tool allows pressure angles to 60°'. auto.rs:696: `pressure_angle: Bound::strictly(0.0, 90.0)`. params.rs has only MIN_PRESSURE_ANGLE_DEG = 0.5. Python: tan(60°)−60° = 0.68485, and inv α = 0.51 at α = 56.13°. corrections.md:423 says the bare Newton 'Diverges above ~60°, inside the allowed pressure-angle range', which is consistent with there being no 60° cap.
verdict.proposal_note: Before writing that v beyond inv(ALPHA_MAX) 'is refused as unbracketed', check what `newton_bracketed` returns when there is no sign change. Say what it does, or omit the clause. Extending the round-trip loop from 85° to 89° is cheap and matches the admissible range.

title: The ring tab's 'smallest tooth count' ignores the ring's profile shift, and is computed in the wasm crate
claim: RingSummary.smallest_tooth_count is documented as 'the fewest teeth this design could have had and still cleared its own base circle'. It is computed as ceil(2 h_a cos β/(1 − cos α_t)) with no profile shift. The ring's tip is r − m(h_a − x) (ring.rs:278), so the true bound is z > 2(h_a − x) cos β/(1 − cos α_t), and every shifted ring shows a wrong figure. The formula is also the only engineering calculation in gear-wasm, against CLAUDE.md's 'gear-core: all the mathematics'. It open-codes plane::transverse_pressure_angle on the unguarded pressure angle. Its only other copy is inside a ring.rs test, which checks the test's copy, not the shipped one. ceil() also gives N, not N+1, when the threshold is exactly an integer, while the condition is strict.
evidence: Probe probes/verify-primitives-b finds the first z with no clamp.ring_tip_raised from Ring::cut_by (default cutter, h_a = 1, 20°). At x=0: 34, and the wasm formula says 34. At x=0.5: 17, but the wasm formula says 34 (the formula with −x says 17). At x=−0.3: 44, but the wasm formula says 34 (with −x: 44). A 40-tooth ring at x=−0.3 is shown 'smallest 34' and still gets its tip raised.
proposal: Move the figure into gear-core as a function of the ring's inputs, e.g. ring::smallest_teeth(params) = floor(2 (h_a − x) cos β / (1 − cos α_t)) + 1, using plane::transverse_pressure_angle on the guarded pressure angle. Have gear-wasm read it. Point the ring.rs test at that function and sweep x ∈ {−0.3, 0, 0.5} in addition to (h_a, α, β), keeping its existing check against the clamp boundary. Add −x to reference.md:1592's formula.
validation: New test: for each (h_a, α, β, x) case, a ring at smallest_teeth − 1 raises CLAMP_RING_TIP_RAISED and one at smallest_teeth does not. tools/check_wasm.sh --write: review the recorded ring summary's diff.

verdict.reason: The ring's tip is r − m(h_a − x) (ring.rs:278), so the base-circle condition is z > 2(h_a − x)cosβ/(1 − cos α_t). gear-wasm's smallest_tooth_count drops x, so the figure is wrong for every shifted ring. It is also an engineering calculation in the boundary crate, which breaks the project's own map ('gear-core: all the mathematics'). Its only test checks a private copy of the formula inside ring.rs, not the shipped function.
verdict.evidence: gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:548-555: `let threshold = 2.0 * params.addendum * beta.cos() / (1.0 - alpha_t.cos()); ... threshold.ceil()`, with no profile_shift. ring.rs:278: `let mut ra = r - m * (params.addendum - x);` and :282 `ra_min = rb * (1.0 + 1e-9)`. Hand check at h_a=1, 20°: x=−0.3 gives 2·1.3/(1−cos20°) = 43.08, so 44 (the probe measured 44, wasm shows 34); x=0.5 gives 16.6, so 17 (the probe measured 17). ring.rs:1238-1242: the test computes its own threshold. reference.md:1592's formula also omits x. The ceil-versus-strict point holds: at an integer threshold, z = T gives ra = rb, which the 1e-9 margin raises.
verdict.proposal_note: floor(T)+1 is right for the strict condition. Make the gear-core function read the same guarded params and the same `plane::transverse_pressure_angle` that `Ring::cut_by` uses. Better still, derive it from the ring's own quantities (r, rb, m, x), so the figure and the clamp cannot disagree. Keep the test's existing table as the x=0 rows.

title: Tooth width is not monotone above the base circle: reference.md and auto.rs say it is, and addendum_for_tip_width wrongly refuses some asks
claim: reference.md says s(r′) = 2r′(ψ_b − inv α) 'is monotone decreasing' and gives ds/dr′ = 2(ψ_b − inv α − tan α). That derivative equals 2ψ_b > 0 at r_b. The width actually rises to a maximum where 2u − atan u = ψ_b (u = tan α ≈ ψ_b) and only then falls to zero at the pointed radius. auto.rs's 'The tooth is at its widest where the involute starts' repeats the error, and its early return `width(0.0) < min_tip_width → None` refuses any ask between width(0) and that maximum, even though an addendum meeting it exists. The same paragraph of reference.md also calls this solve 'a bracketed Newton'; it is Brent.
evidence: notes/verify-primitives/width.py (m = 1, 20°) gives the peak width relative to width(0) and the radius it sits at: z=60 +0.03% at 1.0008 r_b; z=17 +0.19% at 1.0057 r_b; z=6, x=0.5 +1.8% at 1.052 r_b; z=4, x=0.8 +4.5% at 1.124 r_b. Probe: addendum_for_tip_width(&Tooth::new(z=6, x=0.5), 1.001·width(0)) = None, and likewise for z=4, x=0.8 and z=12, x=0; at 0.99·width(0) it returns Some. Derivative: d/du[√(1+u²)(ψ − u + atan u)] = u(ψ − 2u + atan u)/√(1+u²). In practice the effect is nil, since a minimum tip width is about 0.2–0.4 m against a base thickness of 1.6–2.3 m.
proposal: Correct reference.md:249-251 to: 's rises from r_b to a maximum where 2 tan α − α = ψ_b and then falls to zero at the pointed radius. The solve is a Brent on the falling branch.' Correct auto.rs:738. In code, either gate on the maximum width (u_max solves 2u − atan u = ψ_b, bracketed on [0, ψ_b] because 2u − atan u ≥ u), or keep the early return and state that asks above the base-circle thickness are refused by choice.
validation: Unit test: for z=6, x=0.5, an ask of 1.01·width(0) either returns the falling-branch addendum, with width(u) = ask to 1e-12, or is documented as refused. check_golden unchanged.

verdict.reason: ds/dr′ = 2(ψ_b − inv α − tan α), which is +2ψ_b at the base circle. The width therefore rises to a maximum where 2u − atan u = ψ_b before it falls. reference.md's 'monotone decreasing' is false, and so is auto.rs's 'widest where the involute starts'. The early return refuses asks in (width(0), max] for which an addendum on the falling branch exists. The Brent bracket [0, u_point] has exactly one sign change for any ask below width(0), so existing answers are right. The doc also says 'bracketed Newton', but the code is `brent`.
verdict.evidence: auto.rs:741-744: `// The tooth is at its widest where the involute starts. if width(0.0) < min_tip_width { return None; }` and :756 `brent(|u| width(u) - min_tip_width, 0.0, u_point, ...)`. reference.md:249-251. My own sweep (m=1, 20°, same width expression) gives the peak above width(0): z=17 +0.191% at r/rb 1.0057; z=6, x=0.5 +1.79% at 1.052; z=4, x=0.8 +4.47% at 1.124; z=60 +0.028% at 1.0008. These match the auditor's figures.
verdict.proposal_note: Simplest correct code: replace the early-return test with the peak width, found as u_max = the root of 2u − atan u − ψ_b on [0, ψ_b], a bracketed solve. Then bracket the Brent on [u_max, u_point]. The '# Returns None when ... even at the base circle' doc sentence (auto.rs:721-723) is wrong in the same way and should be fixed with it. Practical impact is nil (asks of 0.2–0.4 m against base thickness of 1.6–2.3 m), so the doc fix alone is acceptable if the refusal is stated as deliberate.

title: A rack whose flanks cross before its tip generates a self-intersecting outline, silently and inside every admitted range
claim: When w_tip,n = πm − s_n − 2m(h_f − x)·tan α_n < 0, the basic rack's two flanks cross above its tip. For k = 1 that is h_f > π/(4 tan α_n), independent of z and x: 1.360 at 30°, 1.684 at 25°, and every α > 32.1° at the standard 1.25. Rack::wanted_by responds only by setting rho_fit = 0. It keeps the full depth b_d, so the fillets of neighbouring teeth cross in the root and the outline self-intersects. With root_radius = 0 no note fires at all. Every input is still inside admissible_ranges: root_radius max = 0.95·min(b_d, 0) = 0 is inclusive, and the dedendum max is x + 0.9r/m. So the UI shows all fields valid, a DXF bound for CAD self-intersects, and train members (which skip validation) are rated on the crossed tooth. This is the external-gear twin of corrections.md:506 ('a ring's flank ran to the root circle whether or not the space had already closed'), which was fixed for rings only. tests/extremes.rs asserts pa 70° and 85° 'constructible' with a check (finite, closed, ra > rf) that cannot see a self-intersection, and rationale.md's 'Measured ... correctly ordered cross-sections' rests on it.
evidence: Probe probes/verify-primitives-a, modes selfx, ranges40 and pointed, an O(n²) segment-crossing count over Gear::new(p).profile(120). Default 17-tooth, h_f 1.25: pa 30: 0 crossings (w_tip/m_t 0.127); pa 32.1: 0 (0.003); pa 32.2: 2 (-0.004); pa 40: 17; pa 70: 52; pa 85: 432. The onset tracks the formula exactly: 'pa 30 hf 1.35: crossings 0 ... limit 1.3603', 'pa 30 hf 1.37: crossings 3; clamps []', 'pa 30 hf 1.4 z 40 x 0.5: crossings 2; clamps []', 'pa 25 hf 1.68: 0', 'pa 25 hf 1.70: 2; clamps []', 'pa 40 hf 0.93: 0 / hf 0.94: 4'. Ranges at 'pa 40 hf 1.25 rr 0': root_radius {max 0.0, min 0.0}, dedendum max 7.65, shift [-0.92, 0.84], yet crossings 17. 'pa 20 hf 2.2 rr 0': crossings 2, all fields in range. PRESSURE_ANGLES in tests/common/mod.rs:170 is [14.5, 20, 25], so the rack simulation never visits the region.
proposal: Treat the dedendum as the clearance it is (rationale's clamp rule). In Rack::wanted_by, after the depth clamps, cap the cutter depth at the rack's pointed depth, b_d ≤ (π m_t − s_t)/(2 tan α_t), i.e. w_tip ≥ 0, with a new note (for example clamp.cutter_pointed, carrying the depth reached). Write it as min(asked, limit) so the clamp stays continuous. Add the same half-line to the dedendum range in auto::ranges_at_shift, h_f ≤ x + (π − s_n/m)/(2 tan α_n), so the UI shows the true bound instead of pushing the root radius to max 0. Strengthen is_constructible in tests/extremes.rs with a no-self-crossing check (the O(n²) segment test is enough at 120 points per tooth) and let the pa 70/85 cases assert the new clamp. Add α = 30°, 35° and 40° to the rack-simulation grid.
validation: A law over α ∈ [14.5°, 85°] × h_f ∈ [0.8, 2.5] × x × k: the outline has no self-crossing, and clamp.cutter_pointed fires exactly when the asked w_tip < 0. The rack-simulation test at 30–40° agrees with the clamped depth. check_golden: no moves on the corpus, whose gears are all at 20–25° with h_f 1.25.

verdict.reason: Reproduced independently with my own probe (O(n^2) proper-crossing count over Gear::new(p).profile(120)). The onset follows w_tip,n = pi*m/2 - 2*m*h_f*tan(alpha_n) < 0, which does not depend on x, exactly as claimed. Tooth.rs:914-919 sets rho_fit = 0 and keeps bd. With root_radius 0, no clamp note fires. admissible_ranges then reports root_radius max = 0 (inclusive) and leaves the dedendum max untouched (7.65 at z 17), so every field shows as valid. The rationale's clamp rule (rationale.md:120: 'a cutter whose corner rounds overlap is not a tool ... refused') is applied to the shaper but not to the rack. A rack whose flanks cross is the same non-tool.
verdict.evidence:
probes/verify-added-2 output (pa, hf, rr, z, x -> crossings, clamps):
- 30, 1.35, 0, 17, 0 -> 0, [] (limit 1.3603)
- 30, 1.37, 0, 17, 0 -> 3, []
- 30, 1.4, 0, 40, 0.5 -> 2, []
- 25, 1.68 -> 0 and 25, 1.70 -> 17, [] (limit 1.6843)
- 32.0, 1.25 -> 0 and 32.3, 1.25 -> 2, [], rr_range max 0.0
- 40, 1.25 -> 17 crossings, only clamp.tip_capped_pointed
- 20, 2.2, z 17 -> 2; z 60 -> 16, both with no clamps and dedendum max 7.65 / 27.0
- 70, 1.25 -> 52
tests/extremes.rs:7-13 is_constructible checks only finiteness, ra > rf, rf > 0 and closure, so it cannot see a crossing. tests/common/mod.rs:170 PRESSURE_ANGLES = [14.5, 20, 25].
verdict.proposal_note: Sound, with one refinement. guard::MIN_FILLET_MODULES is 1e-9, so capping the depth at w_tip >= 0 is enough in practice. To be exact, cap it where the smallest admitted round still fits: w_tip >= 2*rho_min*(1 - sin a)/cos a. Write the dedendum range bound from the same expression (one helper shared by wanted_by and ranges_at_shift, as rho_fit already is in both), so the two cannot drift. Also add the case to the rationale's 'refused/clamped non-tool' sentence.

title: Ratio::cmp_checked has no production caller
claim: cmp_checked is documented as being 'for a caller that wants to sort readable output', but nothing in crates/, web/src or tools/ calls it apart from its own test. It also carries the same non-gcd cross-multiplication that finding 3 describes.
evidence: grep -rn cmp_checked crates/ web/src tools/: only ratio.rs:195 (definition) and ratio.rs:323-330 (its test).
proposal: Delete cmp_checked and comparison_is_exact_or_absent, following the project's rule that what nothing reads goes. If it is kept, compare num1·(d2/g) with num2·(d1/g), g = gcd(d1, d2).
validation: cargo nextest and clippy stay green.

verdict.reason: The only references are the definition (ratio.rs:195) and its own test (ratio.rs:323-330). No crate, web or tools caller exists. The doc's 'for a caller that wants to sort readable output' names a caller that does not exist.
verdict.evidence: grep -rn cmp_checked crates web/src tools -> ratio.rs:195, 323, 324, 325, 330 only.
verdict.proposal_note: Deleting it, with its test, is the right call under the project's 'what nothing reads goes' rule. The gcd refinement only matters if the function is kept.

title: A ring whose shift is given is still judged as a search candidate, so any ring clamp that does not depend on the candidate turns the whole search off
claim: trial_efficiency maps every BuiltMember::Ring to Cut::ByShaper, which `is_as_asked` judges by `clamps.is_empty()`, before it looks at plan.role. A rack member with Role::Given becomes Cut::Pinned and is not judged. Cut::Pinned's own doc gives the reason: 'a clamp the tool raised on this member is a fact about the design, not about the candidate ... a search that asked the pinned worm to be as asked refused every wheel'. In every planetary set the ring is Role::Given. So a capped cutter round, a reduced cutter tooth count, or an ungenerated flank at the given shift refuses every candidate, and the sun and planet shifts silently fall back to the closure. The ring_is_cut_as_asked doc argues 'a set whose tool cannot cut it has nothing to optimise', but that contradicts the Pinned rationale: the sun and planet optimisation is just as meaningful against the reported, clamped ring.
evidence:
Worktree experiment (notes/verify-ring-b/experiment.diff): Shape::chosen_at with set_search(true). Roles are [Free, Absorbs(0), Given] in every case.

planetary 20/20/60, ring ha 0.8, default cutter: Chose, shifts +0.0188/-0.0295, no clamps.

Same set with cutter tip_round 0.6 (clamp.fillet_capped):
- at HEAD: FoundNothing;
- with ring_is_cut_as_asked forced true: Chose +0.0188/-0.0295 again.

Same set with cutter 80 teeth (clamp.cutter_teeth_reduced): FoundNothing at HEAD, Chose +0.0188/-0.0295 with the veto off.

planetary 12/30/72, ring ha 0.8, cutter 80 teeth: FoundNothing at HEAD, Chose +0.2981/-0.1701 with the veto off.
proposal: In shape.rs's trial_efficiency `cut` closure, test `plan.role[i] == Role::Given` before matching the member kind. Give Cut a pinned form that either tool can take, e.g. `Cut::Pinned { ends: FlankEnds, tip: f64, root: f64 }`, which is everything Cut's accessors read. Alternatively add a `judged: bool` to ByShaper. Then rewrite ring_is_cut_as_asked's 'nothing to optimise' paragraph to match the Pinned rationale.
validation: Law: for every preset and arrangement whose ring is Role::Given, adding a candidate-independent ring clamp (cutter tip_round too large, or cutter teeth >= ring teeth) leaves the chosen shifts unchanged. The 20/20/60 ha-0.8 case must choose +0.0188/-0.0295 under both clamps. Run cargo nextest and diff the golden corpus.

verdict.corrected_claim: trial_efficiency (shape.rs:2217) maps every ring to Cut::ByShaper, which is judged by ring.clamps.is_empty() whatever the ring's role. In every planetary set the ring is Role::Given, so the clamp does not depend on the candidate. Any ring clamp therefore vetoes every candidate, and the sun and planet search falls back. The fallback is not silent, though. It raises part.optimiser_found_nothing ('no solution within the admissible range; shifts remain unaltered'), and that message is false: a solution exists and is found once the veto is lifted. In some sets (12/30/72) the fallback shifts happen to equal the optimum, and only the misleading note differs.
verdict.reason: Reproduced in my own worktree test, using an env toggle on ring_is_cut_as_asked. The inconsistency with Cut::Pinned's documented rationale is real. That rationale (a given member's clamp is a fact about the design, not the candidate) applies to a given ring exactly as it does to a pinned worm. The ring_is_cut_as_asked argument ('nothing to optimise') does not hold: the ring that is rated is the clamped one, and the sun and planet shifts can still be chosen against it.
verdict.evidence:
Roles [Free, Absorbs(0), Given] in all cases.

HEAD:
- 20/20/60 ring ha 0.8 -> Chose +0.0188/-0.0295
- same + cutter tip_round 0.6 -> FoundNothing +0.0000/-0.0200 [clamp.fillet_capped]
- same + cutter 80 teeth -> FoundNothing +0.0000/-0.0200 [clamp.cutter_teeth_reduced]
- 12/30/72 + cutter 80 -> FoundNothing +0.2981/-0.1701

Veto off: all four -> Chose, with 20/20/60 at +0.0188/-0.0295.

The note comes from train/mod.rs:1890 (Searched::FoundNothing -> PART_OPTIMISER_FOUND_NOTHING); its wording is strings_en.toml:105.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposal is sound: test plan.role == Given before the member kind, and let a given ring be carried unjudged. The smallest change is a `judged: bool` on ByShaper, or a Pinned variant that holds either tool behind flank_ends and tip/root. tips_are_clear matches on ByShaper by pattern, so it must keep recognising a given ring as a ring. Otherwise a pinned ring would silently skip the tip-interference check, which stays a mesh question and must remain judged.

title: MeshTrial::tips_are_clear's doc says the tips are asked at the zero-backlash distance, 'the tighter one'; the code asks at the running distance, which is the tighter one
claim: The doc section '# It is asked at the zero-backlash distance, which is the tighter one' says that opening the distance 'can only move the tips apart', and it points to a bias 'stated in docs/state.md'. The code calls TipRoom::at(ring, tooth, self.mesh.a_w), where self.mesh is 'the mesh as it runs', with the comment 'Where the mesh runs'. TipRoom::at's own doc says the reverse: 'Read at the latter [zero-backlash] the margin is looser than the teeth have'. An internal mesh runs a clearance inside its zero-backlash distance, which shrinks the far-side gap. docs/state.md states no such bias.
evidence: auto.rs:1316-1322 (quoted) against auto.rs:1331-1332 and train/mod.rs:572-575. `grep -n 'tighter\|zero-backlash' docs/state.md` finds only line 407, which concerns the planetary clearance.
proposal: Rewrite the section as: 'Asked where the mesh runs (self.mesh.a_w): for an internal pair a clearance inside its zero-backlash distance, and the tighter of the two, see TipRoom::at.' Drop the state.md pointer, or add the statement to state.md.
validation: tools/check_doc_links.py, and a reread.

verdict.reason: The code asks TipRoom::at(ring, tooth, self.mesh.a_w). MeshTrial.mesh is documented as 'the mesh as it runs, opened by whatever clearance' (auto.rs:1150). TipRoom::at's doc (train/mod.rs:572-575) says the running distance is tighter and that reading at zero backlash is looser. far_gap = ring.ra - pinion.ra + running shrinks as the running distance moves inside zero backlash. So the section heading and its 'opening it can only move the tips apart' argument are both backwards. docs/state.md contains no such bias statement: its only zero-backlash mentions, lines 376 and 407, concern other things.
verdict.evidence: auto.rs:1316-1322 heading vs auto.rs:1331-1332 code and comment ('Where the mesh runs'). train/mod.rs:572-586. grep 'tighter|zero-backlash' docs/state.md -> lines 376 and 407, neither about tip room.
verdict.proposal_note: Proposed rewrite is right; drop the state.md pointer rather than adding a bias that does not exist (the code reads at the tighter distance, so there is no bias to state).

title: the_general_contact_reading_reproduces_the_internal_one compares conjugate_radius with itself; the '[verified ...]' note in mesh.rs relies on it
claim: The test's doc says mesh_with 'computes where a tip touches from the internal relation written out here'. Since described_at was rewritten, both sides call crate::mesh::conjugate_radius with base radii and an alpha_w that agree to a few ulps, and the test asserts agreement to 1e-9. It cannot fail unless conjugate_radius is discontinuous at those inputs. mesh.rs:568's '[verified: it reproduces ring::mesh_with's two readings to the bit ...]' is therefore circular.
evidence: ring.rs:1058-1062: described_at computes both readings via conjugate_radius(rb=[pinion.rb, -ring.rb], alpha_w, ...). mesh.rs:576-579: Mesh::contact_radius_at is conjugate_radius(base_radii(), self.alpha_w, ...). Both alpha_w values come from the same operating_geometry (ring.rs:1033 and mesh.rs:272).
proposal: Replace the test with one that writes the internal relation out itself: sqrt(r_ring^2 - rb2^2) = a_w sin(a_w) + sqrt(r_p^2 - rb1^2), solved for each tip, checked against Mesh::contact_radius_at. Or delete it with RingMesh (finding 7). Reword mesh.rs:568 to cite the new test.
validation: In a worktree, flip the internal sign inside conjugate_radius. The rewritten test must fail; the current one, whose two sides share the mutation, cannot.

verdict.corrected_claim: The test's value comparisons are circular. Both sides call mesh::conjugate_radius with the same base radii and an alpha_w from the same operating_geometry, so no wrong value that both share can fail them. The test can still fail through its `checked >= 30` coverage guard when a mutation changes where conjugate_radius returns None. mesh.rs:568's '[verified: reproduces ring::mesh_with to the bit]' is a self-comparison. The internal relation itself is well guarded elsewhere, by about 30 independent tests.
verdict.reason: In a worktree I made conjugate_radius treat every mesh as external (s = 1). The test did fail, but at ring.rs:1188 (`checked >= 30`), because mesh_with began returning None. None of its value assertions fired. The same mutation failed 33 tests in all, including ring::tests::the_conjugate_relation_holds_at_the_pitch_point, the_general_contact_path_agrees_with_the_rings_own and the hula documented tables. So the stated validation ('the current one cannot fail') is wrong for that mutation. The substance holds: the test adds nothing beyond plumbing, and the [verified] tag is circular.
verdict.evidence: Worktree run of cargo nextest run -p gear-core with the mutation: 605 run, 572 passed, 33 failed. The failure in this test was a panic at ring.rs:1188:9 (`checked >= 30`). ring.rs:1058-1062 and mesh.rs:576-579 both call conjugate_radius.
verdict.proposal_note: Cheaper than rewriting: delete the test (it predates described_at routing through conjugate_radius) and re-point mesh.rs:568's [verified] tag at the_conjugate_relation_holds_at_the_pitch_point, which already checks the relation independently. Only if RingMesh survives is an explicit-internal-relation test worth writing.

title: Two inversions of the involute for one mirrored guard: Tooth's pointed-tip clamp runs its own Newton in roll while the ring's uses inv_inverse, and the ring comment calls it 'closed form'
claim:
ring.rs:289-291 says the tip guard is 'Closed form through the same inv-inverse everything else uses, and it mirrors Tooth's pointed-tooth clamp'. Neither half holds:
- inv_inverse is a bracketed Newton, not a closed form.
- Tooth's pointed-tooth clamp does not use it. It solves psi_b = inv_from_roll(u) with its own newton_bracketed, bounded by POINTED_TOOTH_MAX_ROLL.
The two routes give the same radius.
evidence: Probe over 175 rack-cut teeth carrying clamp.tip_capped_pointed (z 6-25, x 0-1.2, ha 0.8-1.6): rb/cos(inv_inverse(psi_b)) equals Tooth.ra to a worst 3.6e-15 mm.
proposal: In Tooth::new, compute ra_point = rb / cos(inv_inverse(psi_b)?), the ring's expression with the opposite sign of psi_b, and delete the local Newton and POINTED_TOOTH_MAX_ROLL if nothing else uses it. Reword ring.rs:289-291 to 'through the one inv-inverse, as Tooth's pointed-tip clamp'.
validation: cargo nextest (the pointed-tip tests); golden corpus unchanged at printed precision.

verdict.reason: ring.rs:289-291 calls its guard 'Closed form through the same inv-inverse everything else uses' and says it 'mirrors Tooth's pointed-tooth clamp'. inv_inverse (involute.rs:51-75) is a bracketed Newton, not a closed form. Tooth::new (tooth.rs:455-462) runs its own newton_bracketed in roll u over [0, POINTED_TOOTH_MAX_ROLL]. The two are the same equation, since u = tan a and rb*hypot(1, u) = rb/cos a. There is also a third solve of the same pointed radius that the finding does not name: auto::addendum_for_tip_width (auto.rs:745-750) brackets it with brent over the same POINTED_TOOTH_MAX_ROLL.
verdict.evidence: tooth.rs:455-469, ring.rs:289-300, involute.rs:51-75, auto.rs:745-750 (brent on psi_b - inv_from_roll(u) over [0, POINTED_TOOTH_MAX_ROLL]). grep POINTED_TOOTH_MAX_ROLL -> tooth.rs:460, tooth.rs:944, auto.rs:14, auto.rs:747.
verdict.proposal_note: POINTED_TOOTH_MAX_ROLL cannot be deleted while auto.rs:747 uses it. Better: give Tooth one pointed-roll accessor, u_point = tan(inv_inverse(psi_b)), and have Tooth::new, addendum_for_tip_width (its bracket end) and the ring (with -psi_b) all read it. That removes both local solves and the constant together. The two routes differ only for psi_b > inv(atan 50), about 48 rad, which no tooth reaches.

title: phase_resolution_has_converged never varies the phase step; MAX_ROTATION_STEP's stated justification is false and sharp-corner deviation is linear in the step
claim: MAX_ROTATION_STEP's doc says it was 'Chosen by the convergence study in phase_resolution_has_converged, which shows the reported deviation stable... at this step and no better at half of it'. That test's doc says 'halving the step must not materially change it'. But the test only varies profile_points (100 against 300); the step is a private const that check_cut cannot be given. On the test's own first case (z=31, x=−0.5, 14.5°, ρ=0) the deviation halves every time the step halves, so the sampling has not converged. This residual, 6.15e-4 mm, is the worst on the 1080-case grid and sits 1.6× under DEVIATION_LIMIT = 1e-3, which leaves the gate unable to resolve a 1 µm depth fault. MAX_PHASES = 4000 also silently widens the step on small gears (z=3 x=0.5 needs 5063 phases).
evidence:
Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-tooth-form, mode f1conv: a replica of check_cut, identical to verify::check_cut at step 1e-3, with the step as a parameter.
- z=31 x=−0.5 α=14.5 ρ=0, step 1e-3 → 5e-4 → 2.5e-4 → 1.25e-4: dev 6.151e-4 → 3.020e-4 → 1.541e-4 → 5.913e-5, always inside the fillet (r ≈ 13.96–14.23, r_f = 13.75).
- z=17 x=0.2 ρ=0: 2.575e-4 → 1.505e-4 → 7.50e-5 → 3.47e-5.
- The same z=31 tooth with ρ=0.25: 4.97e-7 → 7.5e-9.
Mode f1grid: worst over the rack_simulation grid is 6.151e-4 at z=31 x=−0.5 a=14.5 b=0 rr=0.
proposal:
1. Make the step a parameter of check_cut; keep the constant as the default.
2. Replace the parabolic refinement with a bracketed 1-D minimisation of the SDF over [k−1, k+1] phase steps around each point's sampled minimum. The parabola is exact only for smooth contact; a sharp corner's distance is V-shaped in phase.
3. Make phase_resolution_has_converged actually halve the step and assert the deviation changes by less than a fixed fraction.
4. Then lower DEVIATION_LIMIT to ~1e-6. That also gives finding 1's independent tool the resolution to catch micron-level depth faults.
5. Drop MAX_PHASES or make it a function of the step, so small gears are not sampled more coarsely than stated.
validation: The new test must fail on HEAD: the z=31 ρ=0 case changes 2× per halving. After the change, the deviation must be step-independent to within 10 % and below 1e-6 on all 1080 grid cases. A bd+1e-3 perturbation must then trip deviation by ≥ 100×.

verdict.reason: phase_resolution_has_converged only varies profile_points (100 vs 300). MAX_ROTATION_STEP is a private const, and its doc says the test shows the deviation 'no better at half of it'. That is false. With a sharp rack corner (rho=0) the reported deviation halves every time the step halves, so it is linear in the step and has not converged. That fits a V-shaped distance to a corner, which the parabolic refinement cannot fit. The smooth-round cases are 1e-7 to 1e-9, so DEVIATION_LIMIT = 1e-3 is sized by the rho=0 artefact alone. MAX_PHASES = 4000 does cap z=3 x=0.5, which needs 5062 phases, but that did not hurt the answer there.
verdict.evidence: Worktree verify-added-3: MAX_ROTATION_STEP and MAX_PHASES made env-configurable, check_cut at 200 points. z=31 x=-0.5 a=14.5 rho=0: dev 6.177e-4 / 2.982e-4 / 1.537e-4 / 7.69e-5 at step 1e-3 / 5e-4 / 2.5e-4 / 1.25e-4. z=17 x=0.2 rho=0: 2.865e-4 / 1.514e-4 / 7.28e-5 / 3.43e-5. The same z=31 tooth at rho=0.25: 3.2e-6 then 8e-9 to 4e-9 (converged). z=3 x=0.5 needs 5062 phases: capped at 4000 its dev is 1.26e-9, uncapped 4.28e-8, both noise. verify.rs:100-107: 'no better at half of it'. rack_simulation.rs:136-165: only check_cut(&g,100) vs check_cut(&g,300).
verdict.proposal_note: The proposal is sound. A cheaper route than a full bracketed minimisation: the minimum distance to a sharp corner is exactly the distance from the corner's own trochoid to the point, which verify.rs already builds. Alternatively, refine with a V-fit, |a(k-k0)|+c through the three samples, when rho=0. Either way the limit can then drop by about 1000x on every case. Do not choose 1e-6 as another number read off where the sweep stopped: tie it to the refinement's stated error. Make MAX_PHASES a function of the step, or state it as a runaway guard that the grid's z=3 case does hit.

title: metrology::cutter_tip_width reads the raw dedendum, not the settled tool, and is a third copy of w_tip
claim: cutter_tip_width computes π m − s_t cos β − 2m(h_f − x) tan α_n from params.dedendum. Whenever the tool's depth was clamped (clamp.dedendum_raised or dedendum_capped, or an eccentric gear's shared depth), the figure the panel shows describes a tool the gear was not cut by. gear-wasm's summarise() says cutter_tip_width describes 'a tooth the gear actually has'. The same quantity is w_tip_t·cos β, already computed from the settled b_d in Rack::wanted_by and again in auto::ranges_at_shift, so it is written three times. In finding 0's pointed case it is the only visible sign of trouble: it goes negative, with no note.
evidence: Probe mode tipw, default gear. At x=1.3 the settled bd is 0.05 (clamp.dedendum_raised): cutter_tip_width = 0.6609 against 0.5881 from the settled tool. At x=1.5: 0.6609 against 0.4425. At x=0 and at angular_shift 0.6 the two agree (0.6609).
proposal: Compute it from the tooth's settled depth: (π m_t − s_t)·cos β − 2·g.bd·tan α_n, i.e. w_tip in the normal plane. Better, expose one pub(crate) fn tip_width(st, bd, mt, alpha_t) that Rack::wanted_by, ranges_at_shift and metrology all call, so the fit cap and the reported figure cannot disagree.
validation: A law that cutter_tip_width(g)/cos β equals (π m_t − s_t) − 2 b_d tan α_t for every tooth, including clamped-depth ones (x = 1.3, 1.5). cutter_tip_width_is_independent_of_helix_angle must still pass, and check_golden records any moved output.

verdict.reason: metrology::cutter_tip_width uses p.dedendum - p.profile_shift, the raw depth. A Tooth whose depth was clamped (dedendum_raised or dedendum_capped) or given a shared eccentric tool (Gear::new: the mean is Tooth::cut_by(params, tool) with params.dedendum left raw and g.bd set to the shared depth) is cut by a different tool than the one reported. That contradicts the gear-wasm summarise() comment at lib.rs:310-316. The normal-plane tip width is exactly w_tip_t·cos β, where w_tip_t = (π m_t − s_t) − 2 b_d tan α_t is already computed at tooth.rs:912, because tan α_t cos β = tan α_n. So the formula exists twice with different depths, and a third time in auto.rs:678.
verdict.evidence: metrology.rs:727-732 uses p.dedendum. tooth.rs:902-912 clamps bd, then computes w_tip from the clamped bd. gear.rs:176-208: the shared tool depth goes to Tooth::cut_by and params.dedendum is unchanged. Algebra: at x=1.3, h_f=1.25 the raw bd is -0.05m and the settled bd is +0.05m (MIN_CUTTER_DEPTH). The difference is 2·0.1·tan20° = 0.0728, so 0.6609 against 0.5881, which reproduces the auditor's figures.
verdict.proposal_note: Returning g.w_tip-equivalent × cos β from the settled g.bd is the minimal fix. auto.rs:678 deliberately evaluates at raw inputs for a range, so it should share the helper function but not the settled depth.

title: ring.rs says an external gear 'has never been able to' close its space; reference.md's thickness bound claims to exclude racks with no tooth width
claim: ring.rs's CLAMP_RING_SPACE_CLOSED comment and test doc both say 'An external gear has never been able to do this, because its pointed-tooth cap is unconditional'. That cap is on the gear's tooth tip. The external counterpart of a ring's space closing is the rack's tooth coming to a point above the commanded depth, which finding 0 shows happens silently, with a self-crossing outline. reference.md's input table justifies 0 < k < 2 as 'a rack whose tooth or space has no width is not a rack', but the rack's tooth reaches zero width at its tip line at much smaller k: k > 1 + (π/4 − h_f tan α_n)·4 tan α_n/π, which is k > 1.42 at 20° with h_f = 1.25.
evidence: Probe mode f0cases: z=17 α=20 k=1.5 gives w_tip = −0.1245 mm, 17 profile crossings and no dedendum note. The mode f0sweep closed-form check (h_f + x_s > π/(4 tan α_n)) has 0 mismatches over 55,562 teeth.
proposal: Fix finding 0 with a 'space closed' clamp shared by the ring and the external gear, one key for one fact. Then the ring.rs sentences can say the two are one rule. Add the dedendum/thickness bound h_f + x_s ≤ π/(4 tan α_n) (minus the round term) to reference.md's table, with 'the rack's tooth must not come to a point above its tip line' as its reason.
validation: check_doc_links.py. The extremes.rs law covers the new bound, and the ring and external clamps fire on mirrored inputs.

verdict.reason: Reproduced on an external gear. With k=1.5 (inside the admitted 0<k<2, and s_t = 0.75 pitch passes the 0.95 thickness bound) the rack's tooth is pointed above its tip line (w_tip < 0). The half profile runs past the space centreline, and no note fires beyond clamp.fillet_capped, which also fires at harmless k=1.3. So 'an external gear has never been able to do this' is false. The pointed-tip cap it cites is on the gear's tip, not the tool's. The threshold h_f + x_s > π/(4 tan α_n) is correct: x cancels because the rack tip sits h_f below the rack's own reference line, which gives k > 1.42 at 20° with h_f=1.25. reference.md's reason for 0<k<2 is true only at the pitch line.
verdict.evidence: Worktree probe, z=17 default, half_profile(400): k=1.42 gives w_tip=+0.0011 and 0 points past π/z. k=1.45 gives w_tip=-0.046, 6 points past π/z. k=1.5 gives -0.1245 and 15. k=1.7 gives -0.4387 and 57. The notes are only ['clamp.fillet_capped'] in every case, and undercut=true, severed=false. ring.rs:394-398 and 1605-1608 carry the sentence.
verdict.proposal_note: A shared 'tool tooth closed' clamp is right: a ring's space closing is the same fact, the tool's tooth coming to a point before the commanded depth. Under rule 5 it should clamp the depth to the point and say so, not refuse. The bound for the reference.md table then follows from that clamp. It is not a new refusal.

title: A tip below the form (junction) radius on a tooth that is not undercut is admitted by the published addendum range: the drawn and DXF outline reach r_j above the reported tip, silently
claim:
The addendum bound only asks the tip to clear the base circle: h_a > max(−h_f, (r_b − r)/m − x). The involute actually begins at the junction r_j = r_b·√(1+(l/r_b)²), which sits above r_b on every tooth that is not undercut.

For h_a between that bound and (r_j − r)/m − x, the construction does the following:
- solve_junction returns u_j = l/r_b > u_tip.
- sample_section(Involute) lerps from u_tip up to u_j, so the half profile climbs from the tip circle out to r_j before the trochoid comes back down.
- The drawn profile, Gear::outline and the DXF all carry a sliver of material above r_a. Radius stops being monotone, although monotone radius is the profile's stated invariant.
- No note fires, and check_cut cannot see it: the sliver is generated geometry, so penetration is 0.

This is the non-undercut, addendum-axis twin of lens-numerical-robustness #3 (the undercut, shift-axis branch). Tooth-form #6 covers the part below the base circle.
evidence:
Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-tooth-form-b.

Mode f6, z=40, x=0, default rack (published h_a minimum −1.206):
- h_a=−1.0: r_a=19.000, r_j=19.1976, u_tip=0.1485 < u_j=0.2084, not undercut, notes=[]. The half-profile radius rises at 39 steps.
- h_a=−0.9: the same pattern, r_j − r_a = 0.098 mm.
- z=60 h_a=−1.1: r_j − r_a = 0.230 mm.

Mode f6band, z 8–200, x −1..1, h_a −1.5..0.5, β 0/20: 2,073 of the 12,807 admissible, non-undercut, unsevered teeth have r_a < r_j. The worst is z=60, x=−0.9, h_a=−1.25, β=20: r_a=29.775, but Gear::profile and Gear::outline both reach r=30.428 (+0.653 mm), with notes=[] and check_cut penetration 0.
proposal:
Fix it in the construction, one rule for all three branches (this, lens-numerical-robustness #3 and tooth-form #6).
1. In build_with_z, after solve_junction: if !severed && r_a < r_j, solve trochoid_at(s).0 = r_a on [s_j, 0] with brent. It is bracketed, because the trochoid falls from r_j to r_f.
2. Set s_j to that root, u_j = u_tip (the involute section is then empty; sections() may drop it when u_j ≥ u_tip), and θ_a = the trochoid's θ there.
3. Push one note, clamp.tip_below_form, with the radius and 5 catalogue strings.
4. Delete the base-circle floor at tooth.rs:471, or keep only an above-root floor. A tooth with fillet flanks only can still be cut (rule 5).
5. Reword reference.md:161's 'From' column. If an input bound is preferred instead, the closed form is h_a > (r_j − r)/m − x, with r_j = r_b√(1+(l/r_b)²) and l = m(x − x_min)/sin α_t.
validation:
- A law over the geometry_laws grid, including negative addenda: max over Gear::profile and Gear::outline of |p| ≤ r_a + 1e-9, and half-profile radius monotone.
- The z=40 x=0 h_a=−1.0 case fires the new note.
- gear_io::strings fires every note.
- check_golden records any moved output.

verdict.reason: Reproduced exactly. auto.rs's addendum bound only asks the tip to clear the base circle. On a tooth that is not undercut, solve_junction returns u_j = l/r_b, and r_j can exceed r_a. The half-profile, Gear::profile and Gear::outline then reach r_j above the reported tip. No note fires, and check_cut sees nothing. It needs an addendum below about -0.9 m, so it is rare, but it is admitted by the published range and goes silently into the DXF.
verdict.evidence: Worktree probe. z=40 x=0 h_a=-1.0: ra=19.0000, rj=19.1976, u_tip=0.1485 < u_j=0.2084, undercut=false. Half profile, profile and outline max are all 19.1976, notes=[], pen=0. h_a=-0.9: max 19.1976 against ra 19.1. z=60 h_a=-1.1: 29.1299 against 28.9. z=60 x=-0.9 h_a=-1.25 β=20: 30.4282 against ra 29.7753 (+0.653 mm), notes=[]. Control h_a=-0.5: max = ra = 19.5.
verdict.proposal_note: Clamping the fillet at r_a (brent on trochoid_at(s).0 = r_a, bracketed on [s_j,0]) with a note follows rule 5. The alternative, raising the addendum floor to r_j (closed form given), is simpler, but it refuses a cuttable tooth. Prefer the clamp, and keep a law that max |p| over outline ≤ r_a.

title: The documentation says the flank continues below the base circle; by construction the junction is always above it
claim:
Four places describe the undercut-junction fix as 'the flank continues below the base circle to its true intersection with the trochoid'. flank_ends adds that the junction 'sits below the base circle on an undercut tooth'. Both are inverted.

The code sets r_j = r_b·hypot(1, u_j) (tooth.rs:521), so r_j ≥ r_b always. The fixed profile's involute stops above the base circle, at its crossing with the trochoid. It is the fillet that is carried past the rack's tangent parameter to that crossing.

The legacy fixture (with_flank_clamped_at_base) is the one that ran the involute down to the base circle (u_j = max(l,0)/r_b = 0), then started the trochoid at s_tan, 0.31 mm higher. That 0.31 mm is the 'step'.

This is one of CLAUDE.md's 'things that look wrong and are not', so a reader is told the opposite of what the code does.
evidence:
- tooth.rs:521: `g.r_j = rb * f64::hypot(1.0, g.u_j);`
- Re-ran the tooth-form auditor's probe_tooth_form junction mode: 1,975 undercut, unsevered teeth give r_j − r_b in [5.9e-8, 0.337] mm, always positive.
- z=8, x=0: r_b=3.758770, r_j=3.806777, u_j=0.160. The legacy fixture has u_j=0 (involute to the base circle) and its trochoid starts at r=4.067965; the 0.309 mm gap is the documented 0.3 mm step.
proposal: Reword all four places to state what the code does. For example: 'On an undercut tooth the fillet is carried past the rack's tangent point to its true crossing with the involute, which lies above the base circle, and the flank ends there. Stopping the flank at the base circle and starting the fillet at the tangent point leaves a 0.3 mm step (Tooth::with_flank_clamped_at_base).' Drop 'sits below the base circle' from flank_ends.
validation: tools/check_doc_links.py stays green. The existing negative fixture test (with_flank_clamped_at_base) still fails the legacy, as it does now; there is no code change.

verdict.reason: By construction r_j = r_b·hypot(1,u_j) ≥ r_b (tooth.rs:521), and solve_junction's undercut branch returns u_j ≥ 0. The involute therefore ends above the base circle. What the fix carries past the rack's tangent point is the trochoid, up to its crossing with the involute. The legacy fixture is the one whose involute runs down to the base circle (u_j=0). The prose calls this 'the flank continues below the base circle', and flank_ends says the junction 'sits below the base circle'. Both are inverted. The claim is more widespread than the four locations cited: gear.rs:407 repeats it, and reference.md:1697 and corrections.md:384 say 'the flank is re-entrant below the base circle', when the re-entrant part is the fillet.
verdict.evidence: Worktree probe over z 4-29, x -1.0..0.5 at default rack, 258 undercut, unsevered teeth: r_j - r_b in [1.1e-6, 0.227] mm, always positive. z=8 x=0: rb=3.758770, rj=3.806777, u_j=0.1603. The legacy fixture has u_j=0 and its trochoid starts at r=4.067965, which is the 0.3 mm step. grep: tooth.rs:28, tooth.rs:281-284, CLAUDE.md:223, reference.md:121, gear.rs:407, reference.md:1697, corrections.md:384.
verdict.corrected_claim: The inverted description appears in at least seven places, not four: tooth.rs:28, tooth.rs:281-284 (flank_ends), CLAUDE.md:223, reference.md:121, gear.rs:406-408, reference.md:1697 and corrections.md:384 (the last two attribute the re-entrance to the flank, when it is the fillet's).
verdict.proposal_note: Reword all seven. In gear.rs:407 and reference.md:1697 the reason should become 'the fillet is re-entrant (θ not monotone) below the junction', which is still the correct argument for parametrising on radius.

title: state.md's transverse-round residual calls its sign conservative, but the undercut shift it moves is under-read, and no output size is given
claim:
The entry says the 1/cos β circle moves the junction radius upward and so makes the interference verdict conservative, and it ends with 'sign stated, size stated'. The only sizes it gives are the round's own (6% at 20°, seven modules at 82°).

The same circle also moves Rack::undercut_shift, and so Tooth::undercut and auto::minimum_profile_shift. It moves them the non-conservative way: the circle's flank runs out higher, at ρ_t(1−sin α_t) against the true ρ_n(1−sin α_n), so the automatic undercut shift is too small. The size is negligible, but rule 6 asks for size and sign of every known bias in the outputs.
evidence:
Script /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-tooth-form-b/undercut_ellipse.py uses an independent normal-plane rack mapped by x_n = x_t cos β.

| β | x_min under-read | True-hob penetration at the circle's x_min | Junction radius overstated (µm per mm of module) | Fillet shape difference (µm per mm of module) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20° | 0.0083 m | — | 2.5 | 5.4 |
| 30° | 0.019 m | 1.4e-7 mm (z=20); 4.0e-7 mm (z=12) | 8.6 | 14 |
| 45° | 0.041 m | 5.7e-7 mm (z=20) | 29.5 | 44 |

The junction and fillet columns come from ellipse.py.
proposal: Extend the entry with the output sizes: junction radius +2.5/+8.6/+30 µm per mm of module and fillet shape ≤5/14/44 µm per mm of module at β = 20/30/45°. Add that the undercut shift is under-read by 0.008/0.019/0.041 modules, the non-conservative side, but the undercut this leaves at the automatic shift is below 1e-6 mm. Tag the figures for check_figures.py. Tooth-form #10 retires all of this.
validation: tools/check_figures.py, with the numbers regenerated by the two scripts or by a gear-cli command added for the purpose.

verdict.reason: Rack::undercut_shift is x_min = (depth − ρ(1−sin α_t) − r sin²α_t)/m, with ρ = root_radius·m_t, the transverse circle. The true hob's flank runs out at height ρ_n(1−sin α_n), and heights are preserved in the oblique section. So Δx_min = [ρ_n(1−sin α_t)/cos β − ρ_n(1−sin α_n)]/m < 0 correction: the circle's run-out is higher, x_min is read too small, and the automatic shift is on the non-conservative side. state.md:689-698 gives only the round's size and claims the verdict it moves is conservative.
verdict.evidence: Independent hand computation with ρ_n = 0.38 m, α_n = 20°. β=20°: α_t=21.17°, 0.639/0.9397 = 0.680 against 0.658, Δ = 0.022·0.38 = 0.0083 m. β=30°: 0.7072 against 0.658, Δ = 0.0187 m. β=45°: 0.767 against 0.658, Δ = 0.0414 m. All match the auditor's table. tooth.rs:870-873 is the formula, tooth.rs:919 is rho = root_radius·mt. I did not re-run the penetration column (1e-7 mm). It is plausible because undercut depth is second-order near the limit.
verdict.proposal_note: Adding the sizes is right. Better still, make the round's run-out height use ρ_n(1−sin α_n) inside undercut_shift. That is a one-line closed-form fix that removes this sign problem without waiting for the ellipse work.

title: The 'buildable' profile-shift range runs deep into severed teeth and publishes no severing threshold
claim: ShiftRange advertises three advisory thresholds inside its bound (undercut, pointed, shallow_cut), and the panel prints the bound as 'buildable {min} to {max}'. The lower end is set only by the thickness and root-off-axis guards. For every small pinion the severing threshold lies well inside it, so the panel calls shifts 'buildable' where the tooth has been cut through below the base circle, and gives no advance mark where that begins. The same crate says the opposite elsewhere: member_is_buildable's doc (auto.rs:1014-1017) and reference.md:810-812 call a severed tooth 'a shape no cutter leaves'. admissible_ranges' dedendum, root_radius and thickness bounds also admit severing values, with no threshold either.
evidence: Probe verify-tooth-form-f12 `range` compares admissible_ranges(p, h_f).profile_shift with a bisected severing threshold. z=8, alpha=20, rho=0.38: buildable [-2.1304, 1.9421], undercut below 0.5321, pointed above 0.5662, severed below -0.9551. At the range's own minimum the tooth is severed, with r_a=0.687 against r_b=3.759 and note clamp.tooth_severed. z=5: buildable from -1.0, severed below -0.5396. z=12, alpha=14.5: buildable from -2.998, severed below -1.2147. At alpha=20, severing lies inside the range for every z from 4 to 12. Along other inputs: z=8 severs at h_f=2.4836, while the dedendum bound runs to r_f>0. z=5 at x=-0.5 severs for rho<0.2313, while the root_radius bound starts at 0. The test the_admissible_range_is_exactly_where_the_generator_starts_clamping (auto.rs:2318) deliberately counts thickness clamps only, so it does not see this.
proposal: Add `severed: Option<f64>` to ShiftRange: the shift below which the tooth is severed. Keep it a threshold like `pointed`, not a bound; per rule 5 the stub is cut and reported. To compute it once, factor check_severed's minimum (Brent on trochoid_theta_slope over [s_j, 0], with its end-point fallback) into `pub(crate) fn least_fillet_angle(&self) -> f64` on Tooth. check_severed then reads `< 0` from it. In admissible_profile_shift, bracket `|x| Tooth::new(GearParams{profile_shift: x + off_lo, ..*p}).least_fillet_angle()` on [min, undercut threshold] with the existing brent, returning None when the tooth at `min` is not severed. The low tooth of an eccentric gear severs first, as it undercuts first. Add a clause 'severed below {severed}' in GearPanel.svelte's shiftNote (a new ui string in all five catalogues), and regenerate the bindings. Reword auto.rs:1014-1017 so it no longer says a cutter cannot leave a severed tooth: it leaves a stub that cannot be used, which is why a search refuses it. Optionally give the dedendum and root_radius ranges the same threshold through the same function.
validation: Add a unit law in auto.rs over z 3-14, alpha 14.5/20/25, rho 0/0.38 and beta 0/30: the tooth at severed+1e-6 is not severed, the tooth at severed-1e-6 is, and severed is None exactly when the tooth at bound.min is not severed. Run cargo nextest run, tools/check_bindings.sh, tools/check_strings.py, tools/check_wasm.sh and cd web && npm run check.

verdict.reason: Reproduced independently. For every small pinion the lower end of ShiftRange.bound is deep inside the severed region, yet the panel labels the whole interval 'buildable', gives no severing threshold, and the crate's own prose calls a severed tooth 'a shape no cutter leaves'. check_severed does clamp the tooth and raise clamp.tooth_severed, so rule 5 ('clamp and say so') is met after the fact. What is missing is the advance mark and honest wording. The admissible_profile_shift doc says the ends give 'a legal but absurd tooth', but it does not say that a fifth of the range at z=17, and nearly half at z=5, is cut through.
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-added-4 (mode sev) called admissible_ranges(p, 1.25).profile_shift and bisected Tooth::new(..).severed. Results: z=8, α=20, ρ=0.38 gives bound [-2.1304, 1.9421], undercut 0.5321, severed below -0.9551, and at bound.min r_a=0.687 against r_b=3.759. This matches the auditor exactly. z=5: bound from -1.0, severed below -0.5396. z=12, α=14.5: bound from -2.9982, severed below -1.2147. The effect is wider than claimed. At the DEFAULT z=17, α=20 the tooth at bound.min is severed too (severed below -1.7035 against a bound of -2.1304). At α=14.5 and at ρ=0 the tooth at bound.min is severed for every z from 4 to 17. The only unsevered case in the grid was α=25, z=17. Panel string strings_en.toml:219 reads 'buildable {min} to {max} · undercut below …'. auto.rs:1014-1017 and reference.md:810-812 say 'a severed tooth and a root round that will not fit are shapes no cutter leaves'.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposal is sound. Factoring check_severed's minimum-θ search into one function and bracketing it over [bound.min, undercut] is well founded, because severing implies undercut, so the tooth at the undercut threshold is never severed and the bracket always holds. This costs about 50 extra tooth builds per admissible_ranges call. That is acceptable for the panel, but amplitude_for_throw also calls admissible_ranges (gear.rs:1102) and does not need the new field. Compute it lazily, or only in ranges_at_shift's panel path, so the throw search does not pay for it. Also reword ShiftRange.bound's own doc ('What can be built'), not only member_is_buildable's.

title: The export still hangs on large gears: the floor does not bound the work, and below ~2e-9·m the tolerance is silently missed
claim: The floor was added so an unreachable tolerance could not hang the UI (commit d62bc31). It does not bound anything: the depth cap alone does, at 65,536 spans per tooth. On a large gear that is enormous. Once the cap binds, the outline also misses the tolerance it was asked for, with no signal: the result claims a tolerance it does not meet. The only test of the pathological case uses the default z17 gear.
evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-gear-outline-c, mode dxf: gear_io::gear_to_dxf for z200 m1 at chord tolerance 1e-10 gives a 510 MB DXF in 13.3 s (native release), 13,107,600 vertices. z17 at 1e-9 gives 38.3 MB in 1.0 s. z200 at 1e-6 gives 9.3 MB in 250 ms. Mode tol: once the cap binds, the midpoint sagitta of depth-terminated spans reaches 1.97e-9 mm (z17 m1) and 9.84e-9 mm (z17 m5), which is 19.7x and 98x a requested 1e-10. At z200, 1e-9 the count is 6,281,460, not a whole number of teeth (per-tooth sagitta decisions flip with the tooth's rotation near the threshold). `an_unreachable_tolerance_stays_bounded` checks only GearParams::default() (0.6 s, under its 2 s budget). The panel field has min=0 and no lower bound, and export runs on the button (GearPanel.svelte:565).
proposal: This is the fix proposed under finding 12: a floor tied to the tooth (an absolute 1e-6 mm, or a multiple of the module), clamped in one place, reported when it clamps, and sent to the panel as a bound from Rust. Extend `an_unreachable_tolerance_stays_bounded` to the largest tooth count and module in `tests/common`'s grid. At the floor, assert that no span ends on depth, and assert a vertex budget.
validation: At the floor, count the spans that end on depth (a replica or an instrumented `subdivide` in a test). Expect 0 for z up to 200 and m up to 10. Time and size gear_to_dxf at the floor for z200.

verdict.reason: The depth cap, not the floor, is what bounds the work. For any tolerance below roughly 1e-10·m, every span runs to depth 14, so the floor at 1e-12·r_a never engages usefully. A large gear then produces tens of millions of vertices. Below the cap's reachable sagitta (about 2e-9 mm at m=1, about 1e-8 at m=5), the tolerance asked for is silently not met. This is export-only (export_dxf_impl and export_ring_dxf_impl), so it does not hang live solving. But the panel field has min=0, and a 500 MB DXF string in wasm is likely to fail the browser tab.
verdict.evidence: Probe verify-added-4, mode outline, native release, vertex counts: z17 m1 gives 1,034,518 at 1e-9, 1,106,904 at 1e-10 and 1,113,908 at 1e-18 (floored), so the cap binds at about 65.5k per tooth. z17 m5 gives 1,098,880 at 1e-9, already almost capped, which confirms the cap's sagitta scales with the module. z200 m1 gives 6,281,460 at 1e-9 (1.47 s) and 13,107,600 at both 1e-10 and 1e-18 (2.65 s for the outline alone; the auditor's 13.3 s and 510 MB include writing the DXF). outline.rs:88 is `if sagitta <= tolerance || depth >= MAX_SUBDIVISION_DEPTH`, with no signal when the second arm fires. The only test, an_unreachable_tolerance_stays_bounded (outline.rs:716), uses GearParams::default().
verdict.proposal_note: A floor 'tied to the tooth' has to scale at least with the module, because the cap's reachable sagitta is about L²/(8R) ∝ m. A module multiple of about 2e-8·m keeps the cap out of reach, but z200 still gives about 2.5M vertices there. The simpler and more robust fix is an absolute floor well above that, such as 1e-6 mm (238k vertices at z200), or a total vertex budget. Per rule 1 the panel's lower bound should come from Rust, and per rule 5 the result should carry a note when the floor clamps. If the depth cap stays as a pure safety stop, add a debug assertion or a test that no span ends on depth at the floor, as the validation proposes.

title: Comments credit the chord-tolerance floor with a bound that the depth cap actually provides
claim: Four statements are false today. gear.rs:599-602 says the floor sits at "what double precision can actually resolve" and that 1e-18 mm "otherwise costs a millionfold more vertices". outline.rs:43-48 calls the depth cap "a safety stop, not an expected limit ... far beyond what any sane tolerance needs", but a typed 1e-9 mm reaches it. outline.rs:59-62 says "below roughly this, double precision cannot resolve". The test doc at outline.rs:699-700 says "Before the floor was added this case took 45 seconds". reference.md#sampling promises "a segment is split until its measured sagitta is inside tolerance", which fails once the cap binds.
evidence: Mode nofloor: running the identical subdivision at raw 1e-18 with no floor gives 1,114,146 vertices on z17, against 1,113,908 with the floor (+0.02%, not a millionfold), and identical counts on z9, z43 and z200 m1. Double-precision coordinate resolution at ra = 9.5 mm is about 2e-15 mm, about 3.7 decades below the 9.5e-12 mm floor. The cap binds at 1e-9 mm on all five gears tested. Commit d62bc31's message says the 45 s case was the old "finest possible" fallback for a nonsense value, replaced by the default fallback in the same commit. The floor's own contribution cannot be separated from that and is nil today.
proposal: After finding 12's fix, rewrite these comments to say what bounds what. The floor sets the finest tolerance the export honours, and why that value. The depth cap is a safety stop that the floor keeps out of reach. Add to reference.md#sampling the finest tolerance honoured, and what happens to a finer request.
validation: The rewritten comments name no figure that the probe's nofloor/tol modes contradict. check_doc_links and check_figures stay green.

verdict.reason: The prose credits the floor with work the depth cap does. The test's own second paragraph admits this ('Every span drives to the stop here, so the count is spans × 2^depth'), which contradicts its first sentence and gear.rs:599-602. The 1e-18 request is floored to about 9.5e-12 mm, and both land on the cap, so 'a millionfold more vertices' is false. Commit d62bc31 says the 45 s case 'bottomed out at max depth everywhere', which is exactly what the floored case does today in 0.23 s. The 45 s therefore cannot have been what the floor removed (most likely a debug build or the old code path), and the test doc's attribution is wrong. reference.md:138-139 ('split until its measured sagitta is inside tolerance') does not hold once the cap binds.
verdict.evidence: Probe verify-added-4, mode outline: z17 m1 gives 1,106,904 vertices at 1e-10 against 1,113,908 at the floor (+0.6%). z200 gives the same 13,107,600 at 1e-10 and at 1e-18. So the floor changes the count by essentially nothing, not a millionfold. The d62bc31 message reads 'the fallback for a nonsense value was "finest possible", which subdivision cannot reach, so it bottomed out at max depth everywhere … It takes 0.23 s.' outline.rs:43-48 calls depth 14 'far beyond what any sane tolerance needs', yet 1e-9 mm reaches it at z17 m5 (64,640 of 65,536 per tooth).
verdict.proposal_note: Do this together with finding 19's fix, so the comments describe the new floor rather than being corrected twice. Remove the historical '45 seconds' sentence altogether: it is history, not a property of the code.
