title: Against ISO 6336 with all K factors at 1, the default fatigue bending rating of the shipped hardened steel reads up to about 1.6× (20°) and 2× (25°) less utilised than ISO. Recorded nowhere.
claim:
The overall direction of the bending rating against the standard is unconservative for 4340H, and no document says so.
- The production stress factor at HPSTC is 0.615–1.011× ISO's Y_F·Y_S at 20°, and 0.477–0.957× at 25°.
- The 750 MPa it is judged against sits inside ISO 6336-5's σ_FE band for through-hardened alloy steel.
- So the tool's utilisation σ/σ_allow is 0.63–1.03× ISO's at MQ quality (20°), and down to about 0.49× at 25°.
- Against AGMA 2001, whose stress definition is the tool's own (Savage J = 1/((Y_F − axial)·K_f)), 750 MPa is 1.9–2.5× the grade 1–2 s_at for through-hardened steel at the 400 HB chart cap.
- Finding 2 records the spur-base ratio; nothing records what it amounts to once the allowable is included.
evidence:
- Spur base: notes/verify-strength/cmp.py over the re-run grid (804 designs, Method B matching the tool's ISO set to 7.3e-10) gives 20°: min 0.615, max 1.011, mean 0.787; 25°: min 0.477, max 0.957, mean 0.675.
- ISO 6336-5:2016 Table 1 rows 30–32 (notes/verify-strength/iso5.txt:591-592): σ_Flim = 0.423HV+104 / 0.425HV+187 / 0.358HV+231. σ_FE = 2σ_Flim is 513–741 at the 360/390 HV cap and 596–790 extrapolated to 458 HV (46 HRC).
- Utilisation ratio = (σ_tool/σ_ISO)·(σ_FE/750); MQ at 458 HV gives 763/750 = 1.02.
- AGMA 2001 through-hardened s_at = 0.533HB+88.3 (grade 1) and 0.703HB+113 (grade 2): 301–394 MPa at 400 HB.
- Medium confidence: ISO's σ_FE is extrapolated past its hardness cap, and the quality grade is a choice.
proposal: Add one Known-approximate entry for the whole bending rating against ISO 6336 (K factors at 1, Method B, σ_FE from Table 1 at a stated quality grade), per shipped steel and per offered pressure angle, with size and sign. Generate it from a script that shares no code with the crate (extend iso_6336_3_stack.py as finding 2 proposes), and tag it for check_figures. State next to it that AGMA's allowable for the same stress definition is about half.
validation: The script reproduces the tool's ISO set to 1e-8 before it reports any ratio. check_figures then gates the published band.

verdict.reason: The numbers reproduce, but the claim 'Recorded nowhere' overstates it. The stress-side ratio against ISO's coherent set is already published and gated: state.md, 'One bending model', reads 'The external population reads 0.510 – 1.128, mean 0.827' under <!-- figures: gear-cli matrix -->. That is the parabola+K_f set over the tangent+Y_S set, with the same sign as the auditor's 0.615–1.011. It sits in a narrative section, though, not in 'Known-approximate' with a stated sign. What is truly unrecorded is the combined effect, once the allowable is included, against a standard's allowable for the same stress definition. That is sizable: 4340H's 750 MPa is about 1.9–2.5× AGMA 2001's through-hardened s_at at 400 HB. The material note does call 750 'optimistic', but sizes the optimism at only about 7% ('plausibly nearer 700'). Part of the gap is a separate, already-reported fault: 750 is an R=−1 smooth-specimen endurance estimate used as a one-directional allowable. It is not a notched, surface-finished, 99%-reliability allowable like s_at or σ_FE.
verdict.evidence: I re-ran the auditor's cmp.py against grid_rerun.txt (copy in notes/verify-added-4/cmp_rerun.py). The ISO set matches Method B to 7.3e-10. Ratios: 20° min 0.615, max 1.011, mean 0.787; 25° min 0.477, max 0.957, mean 0.675; 14.5° 0.757–1.039. The extremes are z=200, x=0.6, ρ=0.2 (low) and small z, x=-0.3 (high). AGMA check: 0.533·400+88.3 = 301.5 MPa and 0.703·400+113 = 394.2 MPa, and 750/394 = 1.90, 750/301 = 2.49. ISO 6336-5 through-hardened alloy steel at 458 HV, extrapolated past the table's HV cap: ML 2·(0.423·458+104) = 595, MQ 763, ME 790. Also checked: materials_default.toml:64 (the 750 note), state.md:617 and 1036-1050 (σ_Flim declined for lack of data), rationale.md:1502 ('an allowable measured under fully reversed loading … the library has no such column').
verdict.corrected_claim: The ratio of the tool's bending stress factor to ISO's Y_F·Y_S is already in state.md (external 0.510–1.128, mean 0.827, gated by gear-cli matrix). Two things are not recorded as a Known-approximate entry with size and sign: that ratio, and what it amounts to against a standard's allowable. For the shipped 4340H, the 750 MPa fatigue allowable (an R=−1 smooth-specimen estimate) is about 1.9–2.5× AGMA 2001's through-hardened s_at at the 400 HB cap, and roughly equal to ISO 6336-5's MQ σ_FE extrapolated past its hardness range. So against AGMA the default rating is unconservative by about 2×, and the material note sizes its own optimism at only about 7%.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposed per-steel, per-angle ISO utilisation table rests on σ_Flim extrapolated past ISO 6336-5's hardness cap and on a chosen quality grade. It would publish figures built on the very data rationale.md says this project does not have. A better fix has two parts. First, move the existing matrix ratio into 'Known-approximate' with its sign (the rating reads below ISO's Y_F·Y_S by up to about 2× on large, positively shifted gears). Second, correct the 4340H note to state what 750 is (an R=−1 polished-specimen endurance estimate, with no surface, size or reliability reduction) and its size against AGMA 2001 s_at (about 2× at grade 1–2), rather than 'plausibly nearer 700'. Do this together with the already-reported R=−1-versus-one-directional fault, because fixing that changes which allowable the comparison is against.

title: rustdoc never runs in CI; 15 unresolved intra-doc links, four of them in the outline/gear scope
claim: Nothing in CI, flake checks or tools/ runs rustdoc, so links to renamed or removed items survive silently. That is how outline.rs's 'Tooth::profile' and dxf.rs's 'gear_core::Tooth::outline' outlived their targets.
evidence:
grep finds no `cargo doc`, RUSTDOCFLAGS or broken_intra_doc_links anywhere in .github/workflows, flake.nix, tools/*.sh or the Cargo manifests. `cargo doc --no-deps -p gear-core -p gear-io`, run in a worktree, prints 37 warnings, 15 of them unresolved links:
- Tooth::profile ×2 (outline.rs:3, tooth.rs:324)
- gear_core::Tooth::outline (dxf.rs:35)
- Self::span (gear.rs:255)
- crate::Ring (auto.rs:1032)
- rolling_curvature_radius (strength.rs:331)
- Wiring::mounts (train/conditions.rs:162)
- GROUND (train/wiring.rs:87)
- kinematics::System::play (train/mod.rs:268)
- minimum_profile_shift, stated_helix, Port, TrainError::note (train/mod.rs:1118, 2073, 2804, 1711)
- MeshError::note (mesh.rs:765)
- MeasurementError::note (metrology.rs:747)
The remaining warnings are public docs linking to private items and two redundant link targets. Output is in notes/verify-gear-outline-b/cargo_doc.txt.
proposal: Add `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links" cargo doc --no-deps --workspace` to the flake checks and CI, fix the 15 links, and list the check in CLAUDE.md's 'Which check catches what' table. Decide separately whether private_intra_doc_links should be allowed crate-wide, since the crate deliberately documents private items.
validation: The command exits 0 on the fixed tree and fails when a link to a removed item is reintroduced.

verdict.reason: Nothing runs rustdoc anywhere: grep for `cargo doc`, RUSTDOCFLAGS, rustdoc and intra_doc over .github, flake.nix, tools, the Cargo manifests and lib.rs finds nothing. I checked the cited links against the code. outline.rs:3 and tooth.rs:324 link `Tooth::profile`, but no such method exists; `profile` is Gear's (gear.rs:544). gear.rs:255 links `Self::span`, and there is no `span` fn in gear.rs. dxf.rs:35 links `gear_core::Tooth::outline`, but `outline` is Gear's (gear.rs:611). The saved cargo_doc.txt has 15 'unresolved link' lines, which matches the claim.
verdict.evidence: `grep -rn "cargo doc\|RUSTDOCFLAGS\|intra_doc\|rustdoc" .github flake.nix tools Cargo.toml crates/*/Cargo.toml` returns nothing. `grep -n "pub fn profile\|pub fn outline\|fn span" tooth.rs gear.rs` finds only gear.rs:544 (profile) and gear.rs:611 (outline). `grep -c 'unresolved link' notes/verify-gear-outline-b/cargo_doc.txt` = 15.
verdict.proposal_note: tooth.rs:324 is stale in meaning, not only as a link. It says what 'is not meaningful on the result is Tooth::profile, which replicates a whole number of teeth', but that method now lives on Gear, so the sentence needs rewording, not just a retarget. Since the crate deliberately documents private items, run with `-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links -A rustdoc::private_intra_doc_links` (or `--document-private-items`) so the new gate fails only on broken links. Add it as a flake check so that 'nix flake check' covers it, and add a row to CLAUDE.md's check table.

title: No law looks at a drawn eccentric outline at λ≠0, so both a self-crossing export and a disabled root stretch pass unobserved
claim:
The only λ≠0 checks on drawn geometry cannot see either of the two λ-specific defects:
- the_root_runs_continuously_round_an_eccentric_gear skips the export at λ≠0, and on the profile it measures only radial jumps between consecutive points, which a retrace or a crossing along the root envelope does not produce.
- the_root_of_one_tooth_meets_the_next checks root_reach arithmetic, never the vertices the outline actually emits.
evidence:
- Finding 6's crossings (e.g. z9 Δx0.75 λ±1: 2 proper crossings in Gear::outline and Gear::profile, 0 at λ=0) pass the whole suite.
- The one-ulp mutation of the export root radius (outline.rs:147) opens 22 of 23 seams on z23 Δx1 λ1, and gear-core, gear-io and gear-wasm stay green (674/675, only the known timing test failing).
- gear.rs:2382-2385 is the `continue` that skips the export when λ ≠ 0.
proposal:
Add a law over z ∈ {9, 12, 17, 23}, Δx up to admissible_angular_shift (x̄ inside its window), λ ∈ {±0.5, ±1}, checking both Gear::outline (bulges flattened) and Gear::profile:
(i) seams coincide: each tooth's last root vertex equals the next tooth's first within 1e-12·ra, cyclically.
(ii) no proper self-crossing, using a grid-bucketed segment-intersection test.
Keep it beside the_root_of_one_tooth_meets_the_next.
validation: Against current code it fails on z9 Δx0.75 λ1 (finding 6) and under the one-ulp export mutation (finding 10); after those fixes it passes.

verdict.reason: Reproduced independently. At λ≠0, the_root_runs_continuously_round_an_eccentric_gear only checks the profile's largest radial jump between consecutive points, and skips the export (`if lambda != 0.0 { continue; }`, gear.rs:2382-2385). the_root_of_one_tooth_meets_the_next checks `seat + root_reach` arithmetic, never the emitted vertices. No test in tests/ turns index_offset: every regression.rs case has 0.0, and the common grid's axis is never widened. My own segment-intersection probe finds proper self-crossings where λ≠0 and none at λ=0, on a Δx well inside admissible_angular_shift (±2.06). The baseline suite is green on that geometry.
verdict.evidence: Probe probes/verify-added-5/src/bin/cross.rs does an O(n²) proper-crossing test on Gear::profile(150) and Gear::outline(1e-3) (bulges as chords). For z=9, Δx=0.75: λ=0 gives 0/0 crossings, λ=+1 gives 2/2, λ=−1 gives 2/2, λ=0.5 gives 0/0. z=12 Δx=0.5 and z=23 Δx=1 give 0 at every λ tried. So the λ grid must reach ±1 and small z, or the law misses the case.
verdict.proposal_note: Include z=9 and λ=±1 explicitly; λ=0.5 and z≥12 did not show the crossing. Checking the seam on emitted vertices with a relative tolerance is sound. For the crossing test, flatten bulges to a few chords rather than one, so that an arc near a seam is not misread as a crossing.

title: gear-cli `sweep` turns angular_shift and index_offset on Tooth::new, which reads neither: its eccentric axes are dead
claim: The harness sweep's comment says the eccentric feature is no longer outside the change detector. But it builds `Tooth::new(GearParams { angular_shift: dx, index_offset: offset, .. })`, and Tooth never reads either field; only Gear does. The dx ∈ {0, 0.15} and offset ∈ {0, 0.25} axes just build the same tooth four times, so the eccentric feature is still outside this change detector.
evidence:
- grep for angular_shift or index_offset in crates/gear-core/src/tooth.rs finds nothing.
- main.rs:2481-2489 is the comment claiming coverage; main.rs:2491-2505 is the loop building Tooth::new.
- Golden output: '94656 cases: 23792 undercut, 1008 severed, 18572 clamped'. All three counts are divisible by 4 (5948, 252, 4643), as they must be if the 2×2 eccentric axes change nothing.
proposal: Either build `Gear::new(p)` and count per-tooth outcomes (per_tooth_clamps().teeth, distinct().filter(|t| t.undercut / t.severed)), so Δx and λ reach the counts, or drop the two axes and the comment's claim. Regenerate the golden file with check_golden.sh --write.
validation: After the change, the counts are no longer all multiples of 4, and perturbing the eccentric construction (e.g. the shared-tool depth rule in Gear::new) moves the sweep's golden output.

verdict.reason: Tooth::build never reads angular_shift or index_offset. They appear nowhere in tooth.rs; only gear.rs, auto.rs and metrology.rs read them. The sweep builds `Tooth::new(GearParams{angular_shift: dx, index_offset: offset, ..})` (main.rs:2491-2505) beneath a comment claiming the eccentric feature is now inside the change detector. The golden counts are all divisible by 4, as a 2×2 dead axis requires. The alternative the proposal uses exists: Gear::distinct (gear.rs:260) and Gear::per_tooth_clamps (gear.rs:514). The sweep takes 0.06 s now, so building Gear::new, whose eccentric cases build up to z teeth, is affordable.
verdict.evidence: `grep -n 'angular_shift\|index_offset' crates/gear-core/src/tooth.rs` returns nothing. tools/golden/sweep.txt reads '94656 cases: 23792 undercut, 1008 severed, 18572 clamped', and 23792/4 = 5948, 1008/4 = 252, 18572/4 = 4643. `time gear-cli sweep` takes 0.063 s.
verdict.proposal_note: Prefer building Gear::new and counting per distinct tooth; dropping the axes would put the eccentric feature back outside the change detector. The case count should then count teeth (or gears with any undercut tooth), and the output line should say which, so the golden diff can be read.

title: Under the production Dolan–Broghamer model the unshared load point (HPSTC) is not the worst single-pair point for undercut pinions; sharing ON raises the rating below the band, contrary to rationale.md and state.md
claim:
The rated bending factor (Y_F − axial)·K_f is non-monotone along the single-pair zone for small, undercut teeth. It falls from the HPSTC and then rises toward the LPSTC.

Two things cause this. The axial relief sin α_Fen/((s_Fn/m)cos α_n) goes to 0 as the load point nears the base circle. K_f rises as h_Fe falls: (s/h)^M with M ≈ 0.45 at 20°. Together they outrun Y_F's fall; Y_F alone and the ISO product stay monotone.

So the unshared rating (full load at the HPSTC) under-reports the worst full-load point. With LoadSharing::LinearRamp on, the sweep moves to a point near the LPSTC at share 1.000, and the rating rises.

Three texts claim the opposite:
- rationale.md:765-771: 'the governing point becomes the highest point of single-pair contact ... the unshared one to the bit';
- state.md:735: 'Below the band it changes nothing';
- the bending_section_shared doc: 'Measured at 0.0–0.2 %'.

The test that should catch this, sharing_is_off_by_default_and_can_only_ever_relieve_the_tooth, asserts the ISO product at the DB-chosen point, so it cannot.
evidence:
Probe probes/verify-strength/src/bin/realmesh.rs uses real standard meshes (bending_section_shared, None against LinearRamp, both rated by DB). Sharing on raises the pinion:
- z=9 against 80: +0.803 %;
- z=9 against 150: +1.284 %;
- z=10 against 150: +0.370 %.
All at share 1.000; none for x1 = +0.2.

plateau2.rs grid (z 7–40, x −0.4 to 0.6, ρ 0.2/0.38, α 14.5/20/25, ε 1.1–1.9): the plateau maximum exceeds the HPSTC in 381 of 2520 cases, by more than 1 % in 205 and more than 3 % in 60. At α=20° the worst is +1.425 % (z=10 x=0 ρ=0.38 ε=1.7, maximum at d=0.991); overall the worst is +10.45 % (z=7 x=+0.6 α=25° ε=1.7).

plateau3.rs decomposition for z=10 x=0 ε=1.7, d from 0.70 to 1.00: Y_F 2.298 → 2.131 (falls), axial 0.124 → 0.004, K_f 1.707 → 1.767, DB 3.711 → 3.692 (minimum) → 3.757. Over the same range the tangent-section ISO product falls monotonically, 3.626 → 3.446.

Worktree: switching strength.rs:2010 to DolanBroghamer fails with 'z=12 β=0 ε=1.9: sharing raised the rating from 3.17387 to 3.17928'.
proposal:
Rate the unshared case at the maximum of the rated factor over the whole single-pair zone d ∈ [ε_n − 1, 1] at full load. That is a 1-D bracketed maximisation through solve.rs, with both ends as candidates since the maximum can be interior: d = 0.901 and 0.967 in the grid. Sharing off and sharing on then agree exactly below ε_n = 2, which is what the documents already claim, and the unshared convention becomes 'the worst point one pair carries alone', continuous with the contact rating's both-boundaries rule.

Alternatively keep the HPSTC convention and add a Known-approximate entry: 'up to +1.3 % on standard undercut pinions (z ≤ 10), up to +10 % on extreme small-tooth grids, unconservative'.

Either way, rewrite rationale.md:765-771, state.md:735 and the bending_section_shared doc. Change the test to assert on DolanBroghamer, and assert sharing-on == sharing-off to the bit below ε_n = 2 over tests/common's grid.
validation: Re-run probes/verify-strength/src/bin/plateau2.rs and realmesh.rs after the change: the plateau maximum should equal the rated value, and sharing on/off should be bit-identical below the band. Check the golden corpus: only undercut small pinions should move.

verdict.reason: Reproduced with public API only. With a spur tooth, rating it with LoadSharing::None at ε' = 1 + d places the full load at d, so sweeping ε' traces the Dolan–Broghamer factor over the single-pair zone. For z=10 x=0 ε=1.7 (undercut), the DB factor falls from the HPSTC and then rises past it: 3.71066 at d=0.70, 3.69151 at d=0.80, 3.75696 at d=1.00, zone maximum 3.76384 at d=0.99, +1.43%. bending_section_shared with LinearRamp returns 3.76094 at share 1, +1.36% over None. z=12 ε=1.9 goes from 3.17387 to 3.17928, the same figures as the auditor's worktree failure. Non-undercut or shifted teeth (z=17, 25; z=10 x=0.2) stay at the HPSTC maximum. So rationale.md:765-771 ('the unshared one to the bit'), state.md:735 ('Below the band it changes nothing'), and the SHARING_SAMPLES doc ('the unshared answer is reproduced exactly below ε_n 2') are false for small undercut pinions. The test at strength.rs:2008 rates the chosen sections with Iso6336, while worst_over_cycle picks them by DolanBroghamer, so it cannot see this. The existing state.md entry on sharing 'not always conservative' (the ring, +2.4%) is a different mechanism: toward the tip at partial share. One sub-claim is slightly overstated: 'the ISO product stays monotone' fails for z=9 x=0 ε=1.5, where the ISO product falls to 3.70037 at d=0.917 and rises to 3.71487 at d=1.0. There the load point nears the base circle and the axial term turns back up (0.0016 to 0.0399).
verdict.evidence: Probe probes/verify-added-5/src/main.rs, DB factor along d via bending_section_shared(&g, 1+d, None). z=10 x=0 ε=1.7: HPSTC 3.71066, zone max 3.76384 at d=0.990 (+1.433%), Ramp 3.76094 share=1 (+1.355%). z=12 x=0 ε=1.9: 3.17387 to 3.17928 (+0.170%). z=9 x=0 ε=1.5: the maximum stays at the HPSTC (4.17191), but DB has an interior minimum at d≈0.75 and a local peak 4.13602 at d=0.917. z=17, z=25 and z=10 x=0.2 are monotone falling, +0.000%.
verdict.proposal_note: Be careful with the first option. The production set (Lewis parabola + Dolan–Broghamer) is the AGMA 908 construction, and AGMA's J factor is defined at the HPSTC. Moving the unshared rating to the maximum over the zone would break comparability with published J tables and with `gear-cli matrix`. It would also lean on Dolan–Broghamer's photoelastic fit near the base circle, where the load angle → 0 and outside where the fit was calibrated. The alternative is the better default. Keep the HPSTC convention and write the bias into state.md with its size and sign (rule 6): up to about +1.4% at α=20° on z≤12 undercut pinions, larger on extreme grids, unconservative. Correct rationale.md:765-771, state.md:735 and both SHARING_SAMPLES/bending_section_shared docs. Change the strength.rs:2008 test to rate with the same model worst_over_cycle selects by, asserting only that the shared figure lands where the zone maximum is. Optionally, expose 'rate at the worst single-pair point' as a user-visible option rather than changing the default.

title: A line contact reports patch_length = face width while its pressure is computed over b/cos β_b; the point contact reports b/cos β_b — a 5.6 % seam at β = 20° absent from the limit table
claim:
contact_stress spreads the load over line_length = b/cos β_b (strength.rs:1836). ContactPatch::line reports patch_length = face_width (the mesh width). The point-contact rater reports min(2a, b/cos β_b), and when the line governs that is b/cos β_b.

So on a helical pair the line report's length is not the length its own pressure used, and the two contacts disagree by 1/cos β_b at the Σ → 0 limit. reference.md's 'where the two contacts meet — measured' table and the_two_contacts_report_one_patch_at_the_limit hold every other field to a size, but not the patch length.
proposal:
Pass the contact line length (face/cos β_b), the one the pressure used, into ContactPatch::line. The two then meet at the limit, and the report states the length its pressure is taken over.

Add patch length to the_two_contacts_report_one_patch_at_the_limit and to the reference.md table. Fix the ContactPatch doc ('On a line contact the length is the face the mesh is rated on') accordingly.
validation: the_two_contacts_report_one_patch_at_the_limit with a close('patch length', …, 1e-3) assertion; the golden corpus moves only helical patch lengths.

verdict.reason: contact_stress spreads F_bn over line_length = load.face_width / cos β_b (strength.rs:1848). ContactPatch::line sets patch_length: face_width (train/mod.rs:430), and shape.rs:3832 passes it mesh_widths[k]. The point contact's patch_at uses line_length = min over members of face / cos β_b (shape.rs:2564-2567) and reports it whenever the line governs. So the two reports differ by 1/cos β_b at the Σ→0 limit. I recomputed the probe figure: β=20°, α_n=20° gives α_t=21.17° and β_b=18.747°, and 30/cos β_b = 31.680. That matches the auditor's 31.6799. the_two_contacts_report_one_patch_at_the_limit (mod.rs:6106) compares at_pitch_point, max_pressure, curvature_across and patch_width but not patch_length. The reference.md table (line ~1159) has no patch-length row. The ContactPatch doc ('the length is the face the mesh is rated on') describes the current, inconsistent behaviour.
verdict.evidence: train/mod.rs:430 `patch_length: face_width,`; strength.rs:1848 `let line_length = load.face_width / cos_bb;`; shape.rs:2564-2567 `face[i] / s.member_base(i).1.cos()` folded with min; the test's close() calls cover four fields and omit patch_length.
verdict.proposal_note: Pass b/cos β_b into ContactPatch::line, or compute it from the stress record (store line_length on ContactStress), so the length is not re-derived in a third place. A pair's mesh width and the min-of-members the point contact uses should be the same number. Check that mesh_widths[k] equals the point contact's min(face[i]) before asserting a 1e-3 match.

title: strength.rs `finish` carries a dead `vertex` parameter discarded with `let _ = vertex;`
claim: `finish(g, method, param, on_flank, load_point, load_dir, crossing, vertex)` never reads `vertex`: line 790 is `let _ = vertex;`. The value is `crossing[1]`, which the function already receives. It is one argument too many, and the reason finish needs #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)].
evidence: `awk 'NR>=760 && NR<=840' strength.rs | grep -n vertex` gives only the signature and `let _ = vertex;`.
proposal: Drop the parameter and its three call-site arguments; if the argument count then fits, remove the clippy allow.
validation: cargo clippy --all-targets -- --deny warnings; golden corpus unchanged.

verdict.reason: finish never reads `vertex` beyond `let _ = vertex;` (strength.rs:790), and at the caller vertex = crossing[1] (root_section_with: `let vertex = crossing[1];`). crossing is already passed. The three call sites (lines 734, 744, 756) pass it. Dropping it leaves 7 parameters, which is within clippy's too_many_arguments default threshold (warns above 7), so the #[allow] can go too.
verdict.evidence: strength.rs:767 `vertex: f64,`, strength.rs:790 `let _ = vertex;`, root_section_with `let vertex = crossing[1];`, calls at 734/744/756 `finish(g, method, s, false, load_point, dir, crossing, vertex)`.
verdict.proposal_note: Also check whether load_point is still needed in finish; it is only stored into the result, so it may be fine. The `vertex` binding in root_section_with is still used by the Lewis condition closure, so keep it there.

title: Ring fillet is built on the wrong side and branch whenever the cutter's corner lies inside its operating pitch circle: no fillet, or a fillet that misses the flank by up to 0.22 mm
claim: ShaperCut::trochoid_at (and trochoid_point_and_tangent / the curvature form) places the fillet point at the pitch point + (1 + ρ/d)(corner − pitch point): always the far side of the round from the instantaneous centre. solve_junction also always looks for s_j on s < 0 (a bracket from −m_t outward). Both assume a prolate path, with the corner centre beyond the cutter's operating pitch circle. When corner_radius < cutter_operating_radius (= r_c·a_cut/a_ref), the path is curtate. The cutting edge is then the round's near side, and this flank's fillet lies on s > 0. This happens with positively shifted rings, cutters close in size to the ring, and short cutter addenda: exactly the hula and planocentric regime. Two outcomes follow. Most often solve_junction fails and the ring gets clamp.ring_flank_fillet_gap, whose message ('cutter does not reach this ring's flank') is false here. Otherwise it returns the mirror branch, whose start misses the involute's end.
evidence:
Auditor's grid, 28,800 rings (mode `gapcount`): 4,182 have the corner inside the operating pitch circle. Of those, 3,336 get ring_flank_fillet_gap, and only 5 get a fillet that meets the flank. Among the other ~24,600 rings, 333 get fillet_gap.
Of 15,610 non-fallback fillets, 841 have trochoid(s_j) ≠ involute(u_j) by more than 0.1 µm, and every one is curtate. 194 of them carry no clamp; the worst is 0.218 mm (z90 zc80 ρ0 ha0 0.8 k0.8 x1).
Hula ring, `gear-cli hula 18 0.5` (z19, x 0.607, ha 0.7, ha0 1.0, cutter clamped to 18; corner 9.80 against r'_c 14.63):
- The harness prints '! z19: flank and fillet do not meet: cutter does not reach this ring's flank' for both rings.
- trochoid_at(0) = 10.4127 while rf = 10.8127: offset to the wrong side by 2ρ.
- A fillet taken on the s > 0 branch with the near-side offset meets the flank within 1.4e-7 mm.
- check_ring_cut: 0.121 mm for the code's profile, 0.036 mm for the corrected one.
25/20 k0.6 x1 case: the corrected fillet matches the simulated cut to 0.0027 mm, against 0.0325 mm.
The automatic planocentric 29/30 ring (x 0.783, 20-tooth cutter; corner 11.05 against r'_c ≈ 11.18) also gets ring_flank_fillet_gap.
proposal: Carry one sign, κ = sign(corner_radius − cutter_operating_radius). Use k = 1 + κρ/d in the three trochoid forms in shaper.rs, and search or solve s_j on the branch sign(s_j) = −κ. Better, solve s_j in closed form from the line of action, which picks the branch by itself. Guard the degenerate κ = 0 case (the corner passes through the pitch point, d → 0 at s = 0; today that is a division by zero). Reword ring_flank_fillet_gap, or retire it if it then never fires. Check whether Tooth's rack trochoid (tooth.rs:539, k = 1 + ρ/d with b_c) makes the same assumption when b_c < 0.
validation: Law: for every ring with a fillet, trochoid(s_j) = involute(u_j) to 1e-9 mm. Gate: check_ring_cut < 5 µm over a grid that includes x from 0.5 to 1.5, ha0 0.8-1.25, and z − z_c from 1 to 10. Run both against HEAD first: the 25/20 case and the hula 18 rings must fail. Expect the golden hula outputs to lose the fillet-gap notes.

verdict.reason: Holds as stated. My own probe (probes/verify-added-6) builds each ring with Ring::cut_by and checks it against verify::ring_cut_envelope, which simulates the cut. When the corner centre lies inside the cutter's operating pitch circle, the code's trochoid is on the wrong branch. The far-side offset k = 1 + ρ/d puts trochoid_at(0) at rf − 2ρ. The same geometry with k = 1 − ρ/d, taken on s > 0, meets the involute end and matches the simulated cut. The rack side does not share the fault in practice: Rack::wanted_by caps ρ ≤ 0.95·b_d (tooth.rs:920), so b_c ≥ 0.05·b_d > 0. The shaper has no equivalent cap, so nothing keeps it prolate. The existing gate cannot see the fault: a_shifted_ring_is_the_shape_its_cutter_leaves (ring.rs:1576) stops at x = 0.5 with the default z20 cutter, which is just short of the curtate regime (43/20 x0.5 gives r'_c ≈ 10.4 < corner 11.05). No document mentions the fillet_gap clamp or this regime.
verdict.evidence:
Probe output (default cutter z20, ha0 1.25, ρ 0.2 unless noted):
- 30/20 x0.8: corner 11.0500, r'_c 11.1992 (curtate). rf 16.8496, but trochoid_at(0) = 16.4496, exactly rf − 2ρ. The ring clamps clamp.ring_flank_fillet_gap. The far branch's closest approach to the involute end is 0.149 mm; the near branch meets it to 6.4e-7 mm at s = +0.237. check_ring_cut gives 0.0589 mm for the code's profile and 0.0032 mm for the corrected one.
- Hula-like ring 19/14, x0.607, ha 0.7, ha0 1.0: corner 7.80, r'_c 8.187. trochoid_at(0) = 10.5239 against rf 10.9239. Clamps fillet_gap. The near branch meets the involute end to 4.1e-7. Cut check 0.065 mm for the code, 0.0024 mm corrected.
- 90/80, ρ = 0, ha0 0.8, k 0.8, x1: no clamp, but the code's junction gap is 0.2183 mm with s_j = −9.5227. The correct s_j is +9.5227 (gap 7e-8). The auditor's 0.218 mm is reproduced.
- Control 43/20 x0 (prolate): junction gap 1.6e-15.
- A 1,050-ring grid (z 20–90, z − z_c 1–20, x 0–1.5, ha0 0.8–1.25, k 0.8–1): 715 curtate, 675 of them with fillet_gap. No prolate ring got fillet_gap.
- `gear-cli hula 18 0.5` prints the false 'cutter does not reach this ring's flank' for both rings and shows sigma_F as '—'. The shipped golden file tools/golden/hula_18_0.2.txt carries the same notes twice.
- Algebra at s = 0: dy = r_g − r'_c < 0, so the code puts the point at a + r_g − ρ instead of a + r_g + ρ.
verdict.proposal_note: The sign fix (k = 1 + κρ/d with κ = sign(r_g − r'_c), and s_j on the side −κ) is the right fix; do not add a cap on the round. Unlike the rack's ρ ≤ 0.95·b_d, a curtate shaper path is a real tool at a real setting. It is cleaner to carry κ once on ShaperCut, as a stored sign next to corner_radius, so the three trochoid forms and solve_junction read the same value. The s_j bracket should start at κ-signed −m_t and run toward 0. tooth.rs:539 needs no change today, because Rack::wanted_by guarantees b_c > 0. The one exception is Gear::new's depth min at gear.rs:191, which the comment says binds only where no gear exists. Extend a_shifted_ring_is_the_shape_its_cutter_leaves to x up to 1.5 and to cutters within a few teeth of the ring, so the gate covers the curtate case. After the fix, check whether CLAMP_RING_FLANK_FILLET_GAP can still fire (UNFIRED list).

repro.reproduction:
1) Harness: `/home/user/gearcalc/target/release/gear-cli hula 18 0.5` prints "! z19: flank and fillet do not meet: cutter does not reach this ring's flank; profile not generated" (and the same for z18), with sigma_F "—" for both rings. The shipped golden file tools/golden/hula_18_0.2.txt carries this note twice.
2) Probe crate /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/repro-added-30 (src/main.rs), run through the public API with `cargo run --release` (arg `edge` for the threshold runs). The reference shares no code with the ring's fillet construction. I wrote my own cut kinematics: cutter axis at distance a from the ring axis, both turning the same way at equal pitch speed, and the tip round's disk swept in the ring frame. From the code it takes only the fixed parameters a, R_corner, rho, r'_c, r'_g and the phase. For each ray from the ring axis it finds the farthest radius the swept disks reach. The true flank end comes from the line-of-action closed form, sqrt(r_j^2 - r_b^2) = a sin(alpha_w) + r_bc (t_g + rho/r_bc).
Smallest case: ring z30, x 0.8, default cutter (z20, ha0 1.25, rho 0.2 m), m 1.
repro.observed:
30/20 x0.8 (corner 11.0500 < r'_c 11.1992, so the path is curtate):
- rf is 16.8496 in the code, and a+R_c+rho gives the same 16.8496 independently.
- trochoid_at(0) = 16.4496 = rf - 2rho: the offset is on the far side.
- The code gives fillet None and clamp.ring_flank_fillet_gap, and runs the flank on to rf (u_j 0.65496).
- In the independent sweep, the tip round reaches the true flank end exactly: r_j 16.7561, u_j 0.64277, diff 1.4e-13 mm. So the cutter does reach the flank and does cut a fillet, and the note's wording is false.

Hula ring 19, x0.6073, ha 0.7, cutter z14 ha0 1.0 (corner 7.80 < r'_c 8.187):

title: tip_clearance returns clear for any pointed tip (half-width ≤ 0), and Tooth caps pointed tips at exactly zero width, so rounding decides whether the check runs
claim: `if half_p <= 0.0 || half_r <= 0.0 { return f64::INFINITY; }` treats 'a tooth with no thickness at its tip cannot foul'. That is false: the other member's window has width, and the pointed tooth is thick just below its tip. Tooth caps a pointed pinion's ra exactly where the thickness is zero (CLAMP_TIP_CAPPED_POINTED), and the ring's psi_b < 0 tip-raise does the same for a ring. half_p is then ±1 ulp, and the tip verdict flips on rounding.
evidence:
24/19, xr 1.1, xp 1.2, zc 12, at a0 = 2.3613 (probe mode `pair`):
- half_p = -1.11e-16, so the margin is +inf.
- troch/invol/tip all false; ring clamps []; pinion clamps [tip_capped_pointed, fillet_capped].
- Unfolded signed margin -0.0251 rad; KHK -0.0199.
- My roll: -0.163 mm at 70.5 deg, near the tip crossing at about 74 deg.
In the train, the same counts got an automatic addendum of 0.93 and tip_interference true, so the train's default path avoided it.
proposal: Delete the early return and clamp each half-width to ≥ 0 before forming H. The window test with a zero-width window is the correct test for a point.
validation: The 24/19 case above must report tip interference. A law: the tip verdict is continuous in xp across the pointed-cap threshold.

verdict.reason: Reproduced exactly. When Tooth caps a pinion at its pointed tip, half_p comes out at −1.1e-16. The early return then reports the tips as clear (margin +∞). The same pinion with its tip radius lowered by 1e-15 relative reports interference at −0.025 rad. The verdict flips on the last bit of a float. The premise of the early return is also wrong. A zero-width tip is still a point, and that point is inside the ring tooth's window, which is material. Clamping each half-width to ≥ 0 gives the continuous limit, separation − half_r·z_r/z_p. This is on a production path: TipRoom feeds the train's engagement rule (train/mod.rs:622, tips_clear).
verdict.evidence:
Probe, `tip` mode:
- Ring z24 x1.1, cutter z12. Pinion Tooth::new z19 x1.2: ra 11.689300, half_p −1.110e-16, clamps [fillet_capped, tip_capped_pointed].
- mesh_at at a = 2.3613 gives (inf, false) as built; with ra × (1 − 1e-15) it gives (−0.025115, true).
- a = 2.40: (inf, false) against (−0.022111, true). a = 2.45: (inf, false) against (−0.018197, true).
- The nudged margin barely moves between 1e-15 and 1e-6, so the true answer is interference and the +∞ comes only from the rounding.
- Code at ring.rs:955-959: `if half_p <= 0.0 || half_r <= 0.0 { return f64::INFINITY; }`.
verdict.proposal_note: Clamp both half-widths with .max(0.0) and delete the early return, as proposed. Add a law: tip_margin is continuous across CLAMP_TIP_CAPPED_POINTED. Sweep xp through the threshold and assert that no step in margin exceeds a small multiple of the xp step. A ring whose tip is raised to its pointed limit (psi_b < 0) should get the same sweep.

title: The default bending model's axial term drops its sign: a tensile along-tooth load is subtracted as compression relief
claim: finish() computes `load_angle = load_dir[0].abs().clamp(-1.0, 1.0).acos()`, which confines alpha_Fen to [0, pi/2], and then `axial_compression = load_angle.sin()/(...)`, which is therefore always >= 0. Low on a small tooth, the load line passes through perpendicular to the tooth centreline, and its along-tooth component changes sign from compressive to tensile (alpha_Fen < 0). The DolanBroghamer factor `(Y_F − axial)·K_f` keeps subtracting it. Savage/AGMA carry the sign: a tipward radial component adds tension at the tensile fillet. The error is unconservative, and it puts a spurious V-kink maximum into the sharing sweep.
evidence: Probe probes/verify-strength-c, output in notes/verify-strength/v12-17/probe_final.txt. For a z=9, x=0 virtual spur tooth, load_at(roll) gives dir = (+0.99997, +0.00766) at d=0.909 base pitches from the tip, (+1.00000, −0.00002) at 0.920 and (+0.99811, −0.06142) at 1.008. axial_compression goes 0.00547 → 0.00001 → 0.04393, a V in |dir[1]|, when it should pass linearly through zero. The flip lies inside the single-pair zone (d <= 1) for z=7-10 at x=0 and z=7-8 at x=0.3 (flip d = 0.774, 0.848, 0.920 and 0.991 for z=7-10 at x=0). Effect with sharing on, 40-tooth mate at its real eps: the governing factor rises by +1.17% (z=7), +2.91% (z=7, x=0.3), +1.56% (z=8) and +1.75% (z=9) once the sign is carried. Signed, the worst full-load point for these pinions becomes the lowest point of single-pair contact, above the HPSTC figure the default reports. In a worktree, replacing the line with the signed angle leaves all 679 workspace tests passing and the golden corpus unchanged (fast run plus matrix; diff in notes/verify-strength/v12-17/signed_axial.diff), so nothing gates this region.
proposal: In finish(), replace the load-angle line with `let load_angle = (load_dir[1] * load_dir[0].signum()).atan2(load_dir[0].abs());`. That is alpha_Fen, signed and positive where the along-tooth component compresses. cos is even, so form_factor is unchanged; axial_compression becomes negative (tension) past the flip. Document RootSection::load_angle and axial_compression as signed. Add a test that fails today: on a z=9, x=0 tooth, sweep the roll across the flip and assert that axial_compression changes sign where load_dir[1] does, and that bending_factor(DolanBroghamer) has no local maximum at that point. Record the size and sign in docs/state.md. Consider whether the unshared convention (HPSTC) should take the worst point of the full-load zone [eps−1, 1] under this model.
validation: The new test fails on HEAD and passes with the fix. With the fix, the sharing probe shows no interior plateau maximum at the flip, and 200 against 800 samples converges below 1e-4 on z=9 and z=10. cargo nextest run and check_golden are unchanged, as already measured.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on the code and on my own sweep. `load_dir[0].abs().clamp(-1,1).acos()` confines the load angle to [0, π/2], so sin ≥ 0 and axial_compression is never negative. The applied force on the tooth is −dir, where dir = P − T. dir[1] > 0 therefore means the along-tooth component compresses (toward the root). dir[1] passes through zero at roll = ψ_b, where the base tangent point sits on the tooth centreline, and below that point the component is tensile. The code turns that into a V-shaped compression and a Λ-shaped peak in the Dolan–Broghamer factor. The proposed atan2 keeps the existing sign for the ordinary case (dir[0] > 0, dir[1] > 0 → positive) and carries it through the flip. The effect only reaches a rating with sharing on, on teeth of about z ≤ 10. The HPSTC used unshared normally lies above the flip. That makes it low severity, but it is unconservative where it bites.
verdict.evidence: Probe `share` mode, z9 x0 root_section over d = 0.60 … 1.20 base pitches from the tip. The independently computed direction goes (+0.99990, +0.01394) at d 0.90 → (+1.00000, −0.00002) at 0.92 → (+0.99990, −0.01398) at 0.94. Over the same points axial_compression goes 0.00996 → 0.00001 → 0.00999, a V where a linear pass through zero is expected. The DB factor peaks at 4.13876 at d 0.92 and falls symmetrically on both sides. The shared sweep's answer at eps 1.7 (4.13713) is that kink, where the unshared answer is 4.05916. The flip is at roll ≈ ψ_b = 0.1894 (π/18 + inv 20°), which confirms the geometric reading. strength.rs:794 and :815 are as quoted.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposed line is correct. Also update the RootSection docs for load_angle and axial_compression as signed. Once signed, the unshared HPSTC convention can sit below the worst point of the single-pair zone on small teeth. That belongs in docs/state.md with its size and sign, and it interacts with finding 33, so land the two together.

title: Load sharing below eps_n=2 can only raise the figure; docs say it changes nothing or relieves, and the sweep is neither exact nor converged on small teeth
claim:
worst_over_cycle seeds the HPSTC at a share of exactly 1, so below eps_n=2 the shared maximum is >= the unshared figure by construction, and equal only when the HPSTC governs. Several places say otherwise:
- The SHARING_SAMPLES doc says the unshared answer is 'reproduced exactly below a virtual contact ratio of 2' and that the HPSTC is 'where it provably is'.
- The convergence test's doc says it asserts exact equality, but it asserts only < 1e-4.
- state.md:735 says 'Below the band it changes nothing'.
- rationale.md:766-772 says 'Measured: 0.0–0.2 %' and 'an exact one'.
- sharing_is_off_by_default_and_can_only_ever_relieve_the_tooth says sharing only relieves.
All are false on undercut pinions. LoadSharing::None's doc ('this tooth carries the whole load wherever it is in mesh') describes tip loading, but under None the rating is taken at the HPSTC, which already assumes sharing outside the single-pair zone. That mismatch is why switching the ramp on can only add. The SHARING_SAMPLES doc is also two doc comments concatenated (1547-1556 and 1557-1570), each with its own summary line.
evidence: Probe over 582 cases (366 below the band): shared > unshared in 13 cases, shared < unshared in none. Rises (DB model): z=9 h_a=1 eps 1.7: +1.92%; z=9 beta=15 eps 1.7: +1.87%; z=10 eps 1.7: +1.36%; z=12 eps 1.95: +0.21%. A 20000-sample scan beats the seeded-only answer by up to 1.31% (z=9, eps 1.7): the maximum is inside the plateau at d≈0.92, the |axial| kink, and is not seeded. The convergence test's own measure fails on z=9/10 at h_a=1.0: 3.7e-4 to 8.2e-4 against its 1e-4 bound. Its grid (z 12-97, h_a 1.35) avoids this. The relief test measures bending_factor(Iso6336)·share at the DB-chosen section, which falls (0.921 at z=9, eps 1.55) while the DB figure the rating reports rises (1.0023).
proposal:
- Rewrite the claims as the one-sided law: below eps_n = 2, sharing leaves the figure unchanged where the HPSTC governs and otherwise raises it, never lowers it; give the measured size (up to +1.9% today, larger once the axial sign is fixed) in state.md.
- Assert that law exactly, in the DolanBroghamer measure, over a grid that includes z=9 and z=10 at h_a=1.0.
- Replace the relief test's Iso6336 product with the DB one.
- Extend the convergence test's grid to z=9 and z=10 (it fails today), or retire the scan as finding 12 proposes.
- Merge the duplicated SHARING_SAMPLES doc into one.
- Redocument LoadSharing::None as the HPSTC convention (whole load where one pair carries it), not 'whole load wherever it is in mesh'.
validation: The extended convergence test fails on HEAD. The one-sided law holds on the 582-case probe grid. check_doc_links and check_figures pass after the prose edits.

verdict.reason: Confirmed. worst_over_cycle seeds the HPSTC at share 1, so below eps_n = 2 the shared figure is ≥ the unshared one by construction. My probe shows it strictly greater on small teeth. Several prose claims say 'exactly' or 'relieve', and they are false there. The convergence test's doc promises exact equality but asserts < 1e-4, and its grid (z ≥ 12, h_a 1.35) avoids the teeth where the 1e-4 bound fails. The relief test measures Iso6336·share while the sweep maximises the DB product. docs/state.md contradicts itself: line 735 says 'Below the band it changes nothing', and lines 739-744 report a planetary ring '2.4 % higher with sharing on than off' and say the sweep 'asserts reach rather than relief'. That second statement also contradicts the test name ..._can_only_ever_relieve_the_tooth. The SHARING_SAMPLES doc is two doc comments run together (strength.rs:1547-1556 and 1557-1570).
verdict.evidence:
Probe `share` mode, DB factor × share (unshared → shared at 200 samples; relative change from 200 to 800 samples):

| Case | Unshared → shared | 200 → 800 |
|---|---|---|
| z9 eps 1.7 | 4.05916 → 4.13713 (+1.921%) | 3.7e-4 |
| z9 β15 eps 1.7 | +1.872% | 8.6e-4 |
| z10 eps 1.7 | +1.355% | 8.2e-4 |
| z10 eps 1.95 | +0.643% | 7.0e-4 |
| z8 eps 1.7 | +1.897% | 4.2e-4 |
| z7 x0.3 eps 1.7 | +3.820% | 1.5e-5 (4e-4 at 20k) |
| z12 eps 1.95 | +0.213% | — |

No case below the band came out lower. z17 is identical throughout. The cited text is at strength.rs:1557-1571 ('reproduced *exactly*'), :1928-1933 ('asserted here as an exact equality' beside `< 1e-4` at :1956), :2009-2016 (Iso6336 measure), docs/state.md:735-738 against :739-744, and docs/rationale.md:766-773.
verdict.proposal_note: Adopt the one-sided law: the shared figure is ≥ the unshared one below the band, with equality where the HPSTC governs. Assert it exactly (shared ≥ unshared in the DB measure), and add z = 7-10 at h_a 1.0 to both tests. Resolve state.md's self-contradiction in one bullet rather than two. Re-measure the size after finding 32's sign fix, because the signed axial term moves the maximum toward the LPSTC. Keep LoadSharing::None's doc accurate: it rates the whole load at the HPSTC, not wherever the tooth is in mesh.

title: ToothOutline::flank_curvature has no production caller
claim: The trait method flank_curvature (r_b·u) is implemented for Tooth and Ring, but only one test calls it (the_notch_radius_is_always_the_fillets, on a Tooth). finish() deliberately reads the fillet's curvature instead. Ring's implementation is never executed, and the cargo-mutants sample has a missed mutant there.
evidence:
- `grep -rn flank_curvature crates` finds the trait declaration, the two impls, the test at 2561, and an unrelated screw.rs free function.
- uncovered_lines.txt lists strength.rs 617-619.
- mutants_merged.json: strength.rs:618 '+' is MissedMutant.
proposal: Remove the trait method and both impls. In the test, compute the involute's radius as `v.rb * sec.s` directly.
validation: cargo build and cargo nextest run pass.

verdict.reason: grep over crates, web and tools finds flank_curvature only at the trait declaration (strength.rs:472), the two identical impls `self.rb * u` (:546, :617), and one test use (:2561). The screw.rs function of the same name is unrelated. finish() reads fillet_curvature by design (strength.rs:797-806). Removing the method and writing v.rb * sec.s in the test is safe.
verdict.evidence: `grep -rn flank_curvature crates web/src tools` gives strength.rs:472, 546, 617 and 2561, plus tools/worm_flank_curvature.py, which is unrelated. The two impls are byte-identical.

title: LoadPoint's struct doc says only a ring has a flank limit; the code and its own comment say both do
claim: The struct doc (1434-1436) reads 'A ring also has a limit an external tooth does not ... An external tooth's own limits are root_section's'. LoadPoint::at's comment (1456-1462) says 'Both stop; they stop at the two ends of the same bracket', and the code applies flank_bracket to both members. root_section itself applies no flank limit: it extrapolates past the bracket. bending.rs:983 repeats the inverted claim ('a roll off either end of the flank has no section') about root_section.
evidence: Code as cited. The worktree mutation that removed the bracket check changed no test (see verdict 13), which confirms that root_section has no limit of its own.
proposal: Rewrite the struct doc as one bracket for both members, with only the direction of travel differing. Reword the bending.rs comment to be about bending_section, and give it a real assertion: bending_section returns None when eps pushes the HPSTC past the fillet junction.
validation: The new assertion fails when the bracket check is removed in a worktree.

verdict.reason: The struct doc at strength.rs:1434-1436 says only a ring has a flank limit and that 'an external tooth's own limits are root_section's'. LoadPoint::at (1456-1466) applies flank_bracket to both members, and root_section (653-678) has no bracket check at all, only is_usable and finiteness. tests/bending.rs:957-958 says 'a roll off either end of the flank has no section', but its assertion (line 965) checks that the rolls at the bracket ends DO have sections, and root_section would extrapolate past them anyway. The comment describes a property that the test does not check and that root_section does not have.
verdict.evidence: strength.rs:1434-1436 against 1456-1466. strength.rs:670-678 has no bracket test. tests/bending.rs:957-965: `assert!(root_section(&v, hi).is_some() && root_section(&v, lo).is_some());` sits under the comment claiming None off either end.
verdict.proposal_note: Pin the new assertion on bending_section, or on a roll just past the bracket through the public sweep, not on root_section. Picking an eps that puts the HPSTC below u_j gives a clean None. The mutation that deletes the bracket check in LoadPoint::at must make it fail.

title: Material library header says fatigue allowables are published for 'the steels'; hardened 4340's is an estimate
claim: The header's 'WHAT IS WEAK HERE' paragraph says 'Fatigue allowables are published only for the steels'. Only annealed 4340's is published. 4340 Hardened Steel's is basis = "estimated" (0.5 × UTS, line 64), and it is the steel the canary and the presets use.

proposal: Change the sentence to 'published only for annealed 4340; hardened 4340's is a 0.5 × UTS estimate'.

title: The CI's independent DXF check cannot see a wrongly bulged arc, although its own comment says it is the part that would
claim: validate_dxf.py counts 3 bulges per tooth, expands the arcs, and checks that min and max radius hit the root and tip circles. Its comment says 'This is the part that would catch a wrong bulge: a bad arc leaves the tip or root circle.' A bulge applied to the wrong chord bows outward from rf, so it stays inside [root, tip]. Every check passes on the DXF CI generates, even though a third of its arcs are not concentric with the gear.
evidence: `gear-cli dxf 17 0.2 0.001 > gear17.dxf` (the CI command). Reading it back with ezdxf and computing each bulged span's centre from its chord and bulge (notes/verify-gear-outline/arccheck.py): '51 bulged spans, 17 with a centre off the axis by >1e-6 mm, worst 5.236 mm'. `tools/validate_dxf.py gear17.dxf --root 7.45 --tip 9.7 --base 7.987387276680222 --pitch 8.5 --teeth 17` prints 'all checks passed', including '51 arc segments' and 'root arc reaches the root circle exactly'.
proposal: For every bulged span, compute the centre from the chord and bulge (θ = 4·atan(b), R = c/(2 sin(θ/2)), centre on the chord's perpendicular bisector at R cos(θ/2)). Assert that the centre lies on the axis (|centre| < 1e-6 mm), that both endpoints share one radius, and that the radius is the root or tip radius passed on the command line. These three lines turn the independent parser into an actual check of arc exactness.
validation: On today's CI DXF the new assertion fails on 17 spans. With finding 0's vertex fix applied it passes. Rule 5 in CLAUDE.md's testing section is met by construction.

verdict.reason: I reproduced this independently. validate_dxf.py only checks the radii of the flattened path, its bulge count, its area and its periodicity. A bulge on the wrong span bows between root and tip, so every check passes, even though its comment claims this is the check that catches a wrong bulge. The CI DXF really has 17 non-concentric bulged spans: at the tooth-space centre the root arc's far vertex is missing, and the root half-arc bulge sits on the span from the root to the first fillet point. In this case the geometric error is about 1.08 um against a 1 um chord tolerance, so the defect is small. But the one independent check cannot see it, and the in-crate gates share the blind spot: only_the_tip_and_root_arcs_carry_a_bulge tests only the start vertex's radius, and the tolerance test in outline.rs:514-521 assumes every bulged span is concentric.
verdict.evidence: `gear-cli dxf 17 0.2 0.001` read back with my own script (notes/verify-added-7/arc.py) gives '51 bulged, 17 off-axis worst 5.236063830622456'. Vertex 0 is at r=7.450000, vertex 1 at r=7.451937, b=0.00189284 and R=12.683. The missing root-arc end at 7.45 mm and -10.154 deg lies 1.076e-3 mm off the bulged arc. The same file run through tools/validate_dxf.py prints 'all checks passed'. Comment at tools/validate_dxf.py:137-139.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposal is sound. Also add an angle check: the included angles of the root and tip arcs should add up per tooth to the analytic root and tip arc angles, because a dropped vertex can otherwise leave every remaining arc concentric while the total arc is short. The in-crate test only_the_tip_and_root_arcs_carry_a_bulge (outline.rs:659) needs the matching end-vertex check, which is already reported separately in all_audits.json. Both checks will stay red until the outline vertex bug is fixed, so land them together with that fix.

title: 'E2' is an undefined label in a public boundary type's doc and in rationale.md

E2 (and E3) are defined only in docs/history/design-record.md, the superseded record CLAUDE.md says nothing points at. A reader of the live docs or the boundary type cannot tell what E2 is.

proposal: Write 'the λ = 0 gear's' (and 'λ = 1' for E3) in gear.rs:675, gear.rs:1492 and rationale.md:1108. Regenerate the bindings with tools/check_bindings.sh --write.

title: At zero friction the shift search is degenerate: every candidate scores 1.0 and the answer is a tie-break, reported as 'Chose'
claim: With search on and sliding_friction = 0 on a component's meshes, the objective ∏η_k is identically 1 on the whole admissible set. Search::maximise then keeps the first start after its coordinate sort (sort_by is stable and `value > here` never holds), so the chosen shifts come from grid order, not from any criterion. The result is reported as Searched::Chose with no note, and it jumps discontinuously from the μ→0⁺ answer. μ = 0 is a legitimate input: tests use it for lossless trains (train/mod.rs:9106), and the panel field accepts it.
evidence: Worktree test probe_counts_and_mu_zero (notes/verify-auto-search-c/worktree.diff) with pair 9/37 and search on printed: 'mu=0: x=[0.5085, 0.0673] how=Chose eta(x)=Some(1.0)' and 'mu=0.000000001: x=[0.6746, 0.7332] how=Chose'. For 17/43 it printed 'mu=0: x=[0.0748, 0.0720]' against [0.4946, 0.7620]. Over the presets (probe_mu_independence), the μ=0 answer differs from μ=0.08 by 0.69 module on Spur, 0.81 on Idler, 1.36 on Compound and 3.06 on MeshedPlanets. No document describes the search at μ = 0 (grep of docs/ and auto.rs/shape.rs).
proposal: Search at the μ→0⁺ limit rather than at the literal value. For line contacts, contact::efficiency is affine in μ, so the limit is argmin Σ_k w_k·L_k with L_k = 1 − efficiency(path, mesh, tooth, 1.0, Forward). The weights w_k are μ_k/Σμ where some μ_k > 0 and equal where all are 0. For point contacts, use the slope at μ → 0. The simplest version: in trial_efficiency, when every mesh the component scores has sliding_friction == 0, score −Σ L_k (1 − η at unit friction) instead of ∏η. Alternatively, if no searched mesh has friction, fall back to Searched::NotAsked (the undercut floor) and raise a note saying there is no loss to choose shifts for.
validation: A law: for pairs and presets with search on, shifts_at at μ = 0 equals shifts_at at μ = 1e-6, within Search::resolution. cargo nextest run; check_golden unchanged, since no corpus case runs at μ = 0 with search on.

verdict.reason: Reproduced in my own worktree test. With every mesh at mu=0, contact::efficiency returns exactly 1 (1 - friction*..., contact.rs:436), so the product objective is flat. maximise then keeps whichever start its sort and strict `>` leave first, and reports Searched::Chose. For line contacts the efficiency is affine in mu, so a single-mesh component's argmax does not depend on mu for any mu>0. That makes the jump at mu=0 a pure artifact.
verdict.evidence: Worktree test (removed afterwards), pair with search on, Search::SHIPPED. 9/37: mu=0 gives x=[0.5085,0.0673] eta=1.0 how=Chose; mu=1e-9, 1e-3, 0.08 and 0.3 all give x=[0.6746,0.7332]. 17/43: mu=0 gives [0.0748,0.0720]; mu=1e-3, 0.08 and 0.3 give [0.4946,0.7620]. Relevant code: shape.rs:2240-2270 (the product), auto.rs:1826 (stable sort), auto.rs:1904 (strict `value > here`).
verdict.proposal_note: Prefer the loss-per-unit-friction score: for each scored mesh use L_k = 1 - efficiency at friction 1, and minimise sum w_k L_k whenever the component's meshes all have mu=0. Because line-contact efficiency is affine in mu, this reproduces the mu->0+ answer exactly. Falling back to NotAsked would instead report a different design from mu->0+, which is itself a discontinuity. At mu=1e-9 on 17/43 the answer already drifts by 5.5e-4 module against mu=1e-3, because the objective's differences sit near the rounding limit of 1.0. Scoring the loss instead of the product also removes that.

title: maximise's doc describes coordinate descent over a span, and Search's doc counts six constants; the code is a full-grid sweep plus an all-directions pattern walk over five fields
claim: The only doc the production search carries is Search::maximise's 'As [`maximise`], at this effort.' (auto.rs:1754). It points at the free fn's doc (auto.rs:1599-1612): '**Coordinate descent over a few free numbers** ... a bounded sweep on each axis in turn converges in a handful of passes'. The body does the opposite: a (scan+1)^dof grid over the caller's box, then a compass walk over all 3^dof−1 directions. Its own comment (auto.rs:1770-1774) says one-axis-at-a-time 'would stop short and report the point it stopped at'. The Search doc (auto.rs:1621) says 'as a value rather than as six constants', and rationale.md:483 lists 'a search span, a scan step, a stopping resolution, a work budget, a start count and a first step size'. Search has five fields; the span was removed when the sweep moved to the caller's box, as the scan field's doc at auto.rs:1661-1666 records.
evidence: I read auto.rs:1599-1618, 1621-1722 and 1757-1929, and docs/rationale.md:476-486. `grep -n 'search span\|six constants'` finds only auto.rs:1621 and rationale.md:483. Not reported by the auto-search auditor (its finding 9 covers the convergence figures only) or by any other scope in all_audits.json.
proposal: Rewrite the free fn's doc (or move it onto Search::maximise, since the free fn has no caller; see auto-search #7) to describe what runs. It sweeps the caller's box at scan+1 points per axis, walks from the best `starts` points and the sweep's extreme point on each axis, tries every direction in {−1,0,1}^dof at each step, and halves the step down to `resolution`. In auto.rs:1621 and rationale.md:483, replace 'six constants' and the list with the five fields actually in Search.
validation: tools/check_doc_links.py; read-through.

verdict.reason: The free fn's doc says 'Coordinate descent ... a bounded sweep on each axis in turn converges in a handful of passes'. The body instead sweeps the full (scan+1)^dof grid, then walks from multiple starts over all 3^dof-1 directions, and its own comment says one axis at a time 'would stop short'. The Search doc says 'six constants', but the struct has five fields (scan, resolution, budget, starts, first_step). rationale.md:483 lists a 'search span' that no longer exists: the scan doc says the fixed ±3-module span was replaced by the caller's box. The free fn auto::maximise also has no caller, only a comment mention at train/mod.rs:5487, so rationale's 'every shape ... calls' refers to Search::maximise.
verdict.evidence: auto.rs:1599-1603, :1621, :1661-1668, :1757-1774, :1780-1812 (full grid sweep), :1893-1900 (all directions). docs/rationale.md:482-483 'a search span, a scan step, a stopping resolution, a work budget, a start count and a first step size'.
verdict.proposal_note: Move the doc onto Search::maximise and delete the uncalled free fn. In rationale.md, keep 'bounded box sweep followed by a multi-start pattern walk', which is accurate, and drop only 'a search span'.

title: The JGMA transcription names its quantities in Traditional Chinese, not the standard's Japanese, and does not name its actual source
claim: The CSV header says the table was 'transcribed from the standard and verified against its rendered pages'. The native terms it quotes, 一齒嚙合誤差 and 全齒嚙合誤差, use Traditional Chinese characters (齒, 嚙合). JGMA 116-02 is Japanese: it reads 両歯面1ピッチかみあい誤差 and 両歯面全かみあい誤差 (1ﾋﾟｯﾁかみあい誤差 / 全かみあい誤差 in the a-mec reproduction). The source was therefore most likely a Chinese-language reproduction. That also explains why its diameter bands are printed '6.01~12.00' (a 0.01-step convention the Japanese table does not use: it prints 'をこえ … 以下') and why its first band starts at 1.51 where the Japanese reproduction prints '1.5以上'. Its module bands were probably ambiguous too, which is the root of finding 0.
evidence: jgma_116_02.csv:19-20 and jgma.rs:90-92 quote 一齒嚙合誤差 / 全齒嚙合誤差. The CSV comment says 'The fine table prints inclusive diameter bands stepping by 0.01 (6.01~12.00, then 12.01~25.00)'. notes/metrology/amec.html (the Ohtsuki Seiko reproduction of the same table) prints '1.5以上3以下', '3をこえ6以下', 'm0.6をこえ1以下' and the terms '1ﾋﾟｯﾁかみあい誤差' and '全かみあい誤差'. The previous auditor reports all 294 fine cell values equal between the two, so only the band labels and terms differ.
proposal: Name the source actually transcribed in the CSV header (edition and language). Quote the Japanese terms of JGMA 116-02 (両歯面1ピッチかみあい誤差, 両歯面全かみあい誤差) in the CSV and in jgma.rs. Record the band convention as the Japanese table prints it (以上/をこえ/以下), and cite the second reproduction the cells were checked against.
validation: Reading. After the finding-0 fix, the stored edges and inclusivity must match the Japanese labels, checked by a table-driven boundary test.

verdict.corrected_claim: The CSV and jgma.rs quote the composite-error terms in Chinese (一齒嚙合誤差 / 全齒嚙合誤差), not in the standard's Japanese (両歯面1ピッチかみあい誤差 / 両歯面全かみあい誤差). The header describes the source only as 'the standard ... its rendered pages'. The Japanese reproduction prints its bands as 以上/をこえ/以下 (m0.2以上0.6以下, m0.6をこえ1以下; 1.5以上3以下, 3をこえ6以下), not the 0.01-step inclusive bands the CSV describes. That is confirmed. The claim that the transcription was taken from a Chinese-language reproduction is a plausible inference, but it cannot be verified from the repository.
verdict.reason: The terms and band-label conventions check out against the Ohtsuki Seiko reproduction. The provenance is inferred, not shown. The concrete harm, band edges that disagree with the Japanese (m=1.0 falls in the 1-1.6 row in the CSV but in the 0.6-1 band in the Japanese table), belongs to the separate band-edge finding and is not this one.
verdict.evidence: jgma_116_02.csv:1-2, :16-20; jgma.rs:90-92. notes/metrology/amec.html prints 'JGMA-116-02', 'm0.2以上0.6以下', 'm0.6をこえ1以下', 'm1をこえ1.6以下', '1.5以上 3以下 3をこえ 6以下', '1ﾋﾟｯﾁかみあい誤差'. amec_03.html prints '両歯面全かみあい誤差と両歯面１ピッチかみあい誤差'. The CSV also points to 'see DESIGN.md 4.6.1' (line 10), and no such file exists (already reported elsewhere as 10d).
verdict.proposal_note: Fix this together with the band-edge correction. Record the band rule as the Japanese table prints it (lower edge exclusive, upper edge inclusive, the first band inclusive at 1.5 / m0.2), store the edges as printed rather than as '+0.01' approximations, and remove the dangling DESIGN.md reference in the same edit.

title: Search::budget is documented as 'a ceiling nothing reaches', but at 3 or more search coordinates most walks exhaust it unconverged
claim: Each walk step evaluates all 3^dof-1 directions. At dof>=3 a walk therefore reaches budget=2000 after a handful of moves and stops with its step at 8.85e-3, about 9 times `resolution`. The doc's claim that every start runs to convergence and the budget is 'a ceiling nothing reaches' holds only for dof<=2. The convergence gate, which quadruples the budget and demands the same answers, covers only pairs and sets (dof<=2), so nothing checks the shipped Idler, Layshaft, Compound or MeshedPlanets presets. The answers are still close, because some walk usually does converge.
evidence: A worktree instrumentation of maximise, logging each walk's evaluations, whether it hit the budget, and its final step. Line [17,29,43] (the idler's shape, dof 3): 3 of 7 shipped walks hit the budget with step 8.85e-3. Preset::Layshaft (dof 4): 7 of 10 walks hit it. Line [17,23,29,43]: 5 of 8. Line [17,23,29,31,43] (dof 5): all 12 shipped walks hit it with final step 8.85e-3 or 4.43e-3, and budget x100 raises η from 0.9455677769 to 0.9455678003 (+2.3e-8). For comparison, the converged walks at dof 5 spent 3,630-37,510 evaluations.
proposal: Either reduce the walk's stencil so the budget means the same at every dof (2*dof axis directions plus the Sum/Division diagonals), or scale the budget with the stencil (budget per step times the step count). Then extend the_search_is_converged_not_budgeted to the Idler and Layshaft presets with search on. Rewrite the doc at auto.rs:1687 to state the measured behaviour.
validation: With the change, instrument as above: no shipped-preset walk ends with budget_hit=true, and refined(3) moves η on Idler and Layshaft by less than 1e-6.

verdict.reason: I reproduced this independently with a worktree that logs every walk in Search::maximise (spent, whether it hit the budget, final step). At dof 2 no walk hits the budget. At dof 3 or more most walks stop on the budget, not on resolution. The effect on the answer is small but not zero, and one shipped preset exceeds the auditor's own 1e-6 validation line. The docs repeat the stale 'a ceiling nothing reaches' in two places.
verdict.evidence:
Directions are 3^dof-1 (auto.rs:1776-1789): 26 at dof 3, 80 at dof 4, 242 at dof 5, all tried every step against budget 2000 (auto.rs:1899). Walks that hit the budget, SHIPPED search, release build:
- line[17,29,43]: 3 of 7, final step 8.854e-3
- Preset::Idler: 4 of 7
- Preset::Layshaft: 7 of 10
- line[17,23,29,43]: 7 of 10
- line5 [17,23,29,31,43]: 12 of 12
- Preset::Compound: 3 of 5
- Preset::MeshedPlanets: 8 of 9
- pair 9/37: 0 of 5 (max 456 evaluations)
At budget x100 no walk hits it (converged walks spent up to 37,510 at dof 5). Product-of-mesh η, shipped vs budget x100: line5 0.9455677769 vs 0.9455678003 (+2.34e-8, matches the auditor exactly); MeshedPlanets 0.9565416627 vs 0.9565431861 (+1.52e-6); Idler, Layshaft, line4 and Compound within 1.4e-10. Even Search::refined(3) still hits its budget at dof 4 (Layshaft 3 of 14, line4 1 of 14). Stale text: auto.rs:1687 'a ceiling nothing reaches', repeated in docs/corrections.md:561. Logs: /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-added-8/budgets1.log and budgets2.log.
verdict.proposal_note: Do not extend the_search_is_converged_not_budgeted with Search::refined(3) at dof 4 or more. Its sweep is (12*3+1)^dof grid solves: at dof 5 that is 69 M, and my run of it had to be killed after ten minutes. refined(3) also still hits its own budget at dof 4, so it is not a converged reference. Escalate the budget alone, as the set half of that test already does, e.g. Search{budget: 100*SHIPPED.budget, ..SHIPPED}. Assert on Idler, Layshaft and MeshedPlanets with search on. MeshedPlanets is the one that currently moves (1.5e-6). Scaling the budget with directions.len() (for example budget = 80*directions.len()) is the simplest repair. Also fix docs/corrections.md:561, not only the doc comment at auto.rs:1687.

title: The SLACK comment describes a tolerance 100x smaller than the constant it documents
claim: The comment calls the tolerance 'a tenth of a thousandth of a point of efficiency' (1e-6 as a fraction, reading 'point' as a percentage point). It says this is 'some four orders below what knowing the friction coefficient to ±10% is worth' and 'two orders below the smallest gap this chooser exists to close'. SLACK is 1e-4. Every magnitude in the prose fits 1e-6 and none fits 1e-4. At 1e-4 the test the_shifts_it_chooses_are_the_ones_that_lose_least cannot see a lower-ridge answer of the 1e-5 to 4e-5 size found under finding 4.
evidence: ±10% on µ=0.08 for 9/37: η is 0.98258 at µ=0.06 and 0.96517 at µ=0.12, so dη/dµ ≈ 0.29 and Δη ≈ 2.3e-3. That is 23 times SLACK (1.4 orders), not four orders. F53's gap was 1.2e-4 (docs/history/audit.md:1058-1063), which SLACK=1e-4 barely separates, where the prose claims two orders.
proposal: Decide which number is meant. If the test is to catch wrong-ridge answers, set SLACK to the resolution-limited wall error (about 1e-6) and keep the prose. Otherwise keep 1e-4 and rewrite the prose with the real ratios: about 1.4 orders below ±10% µ, and roughly equal to F53's gap.
validation: With SLACK=1e-6 the test should still pass on its three pairs (9/37, 17/43, 13/37), or show where the unshipped chooser is off-ridge. Run it both ways.

verdict.reason: The prose describes a tolerance of 1e-6. In this codebase a 'point' of efficiency is a percentage point: the harness prints '0.14 points' for 98.488-98.345 %. SLACK = 1e-4 is compared against η as a fraction, so the prose is 100x off, and so are both of its ratios. But the proposal's first option (SLACK = 1e-6, keep the prose) fails on HEAD. The cause is not an off-ridge chooser: the test's grid oracle admits points the chooser correctly refuses.
verdict.evidence: auto.rs:2733-2739 prose vs `const SLACK: f64 = 1e-4`; the comparison `eta <= here + SLACK` (auto.rs:2820) is on a fraction. Harness `shifts 9 37` at µ=0.06: loss 2.44 %, so at µ=0.08 ±10 % µ gives about ±3e-3 of η. That is 30x SLACK (about 1.5 orders), not four orders. F53's gap was 1.2e-4 (docs/history/audit.md:1060), about 1x SLACK, not two orders. Worktree run with SLACK overridden: 1e-4 passes; 1e-5 and 1e-6 fail with 'z9/z37: [0.75, 0.8] keeps 0.97624206, better than the chosen [0.47415, 0.64937] at 0.97622993 by 1.21e-5'. Calling shifts_for_efficiency with both shifts pinned at [0.75,0.8] returns None: MeshTrial refuses that point. Search::refined(3) returns [0.47361, 0.64937], the same ridge as SHIPPED. So the chooser is on the right ridge.
verdict.proposal_note: Keep SLACK = 1e-4 only if the prose is rewritten. The better fix is to make the oracle ask what the chooser asks, then tighten. eta_at checks only undercut, severed, root radius and contact ratio. It misses bottom clearance, tip fouling and flank interference, all of which MeshTrial::efficiency refuses (auto.rs:1237-1265). Until that is fixed, part of SLACK is absorbing a constraint mismatch (1.2e-5 on 9/37), not a boundary approach. See the missed finding.

title: On the shipped Planetary preset, turning the optimiser on always gives 'no solution', and the note does not say why
claim: Preset::Planetary (12/30/72) ships with the ring's shift given at 0 and a full-depth ring tooth. With the ring pinned, the planet must absorb a negative shift (-0.17 to -0.42 across the sun's interval), and the planet-ring mesh then has involute flank interference at every admissible sun shift. So the search is FoundNothing on every run of the headline epicyclic preset, and part.optimiser_found_nothing gives no hint that the ring's addendum or shift is the cause. The interference itself is documented and deliberate (a_shipped_sets_full_depth_ring_interferes_and_a_shorter_tooth_clears_it). The consequence for the optimiser switch is not. Every test that searches a set first frees the ring's shift (members[2] automatic), so the preset as shipped is never searched in the suite.
evidence: Probe v6/v7: Preset::Planetary with set_search(true) gives roles [Free, Absorbs(0), Given] and chosen_at.how = FoundNothing in 0.4 ms. A 1-D brute force over the sun's interval (0.2981,0.85), 4001 points: every point closes, 0 are admissible. At sun 0.3/0.4/0.5/0.6/0.8 the planet's shift is -0.171/-0.221/-0.272/-0.322/-0.423, bottom gap about 0.28 mm, tips clear, eps 1.97-1.99, flank_interference [true,false] throughout. The golden corpus records the same flag in the default state: tools/golden/planetstage_12_30_72_3.txt:6 'planet-ring flank interference member 1 true'.
proposal: Make FoundNothing carry the binding constraint and the mesh it binds on. This falls out of finding 0's violation residual. The note would then read, for example, 'planet-ring: the ring's tip reaches below the planet's usable flank; shorten the ring's tooth or free its shift'. Add the shipped Planetary preset, as shipped with search on, to the tests that assert Searched, so the behaviour is pinned rather than unseen.
validation: A test solves Preset::Planetary with search on and asserts that the FoundNothing note names mesh 1 and flank interference on member 0. With the ring's addendum at 0.75 the same test asserts Chose.

verdict.reason: Reproduced with a probe through the public API. The shipped Planetary preset with search on returns part.optimiser_found_nothing and the same shifts as with search off. The note's text says only 'no solution within the admissible range', with no hint of the cause. The known default-state flank interference is in the golden corpus. No test searches the preset as shipped.
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-added-8: Preset::Planetary with search=true gives x [0.2981, -0.1701, 0.0000] and notes ['part.optimiser_found_nothing {}', 'part.planets_share_load_equally …']. With search=false, x is identical and that note is absent. The wording is at strings_en.toml:105. tools/golden/planetstage_12_30_72_3.txt:5 reads 'planet-ring flank interference  member 1 true'. MeshTrial::efficiency refuses any flank interference (auto.rs:1255-1262), so every candidate with the ring pinned at shift 0 at full depth is refused.
verdict.proposal_note: There is a cheaper alternative to (or companion for) a richer note: ship the Planetary preset with the short ring addendum that a_shipped_sets_full_depth_ring_interferes_and_a_shorter_tooth_clears_it already shows clears it. Then the headline epicyclic preset is an interference-free design and its optimiser switch does something. As shipped, the preset's default state is itself flagged as interfering, which is an odd first impression.

title: A given-distance pair's answer depends on member order: the reaching member is floored at x_min, the free one at max(x_min,0)
claim: At a held distance plan_held makes one member of a both-free mesh Free and the other Reaches, by index. trial_efficiency then maps Reaches to Decided::Absorbed (floor x_min) and Free to Decided::Chosen (floor max(x_min,0)), and the Free member's box starts at its search_floor. Which member may go negative therefore depends on the order the members are listed in. The same pair at the same distance is reached in one order and refused in the other. This violates rule 4: two answers to one question.
evidence: Release harness `gear-cli shifts 17 43`, 'axis distance given' row 30.0200: x (0.1453, −0.1453), η 98.366 %, reached. `gear-cli shifts 43 17`, same row: x (0.0000, 0.0057), η 98.339 %, 'no admissible shifts reach 30.0000 mm: the pair is built at 30.0057 mm instead'.
proposal: Give every member a search moves, directly or through a sum, the same undercut bound. The bound is the one finding 8 settles on; x_min makes the 17/43 standard distance reachable in both orders. Add a law: for every pair and every given distance, solving with the members swapped gives the mirrored shifts and the same efficiency to resolution.
validation: New test: for teeth in {[17,43],[9,37],[23,61],[31,37]} and distances std−0.5 … std+1 module, search on and off, swapped order gives mirrored shifts within 2·resolution and identical PART_DISTANCE_NOT_REACHED presence. It fails on HEAD at 17/43, 30.02 mm.

verdict.reason: Reproduced with the release harness, and the mechanism is in the code as described. plan_held gives the 'alike' tie to member b as Reaches, leaving member a Free. trial_efficiency maps Reaches to Decided::Absorbed (floor x_min) and Free to Decided::Chosen (floor max(x_min,0)). A 43-tooth wheel may therefore go negative when listed second but not when listed first. No test states a member-order symmetry law.
verdict.evidence: `gear-cli shifts 17 43`, search on, given 30.0200: x (0.1453, -0.1453), η 98.366 %, reached. `gear-cli shifts 43 17`, same row: x (0.0000, 0.0057), η 98.339 %, 'no admissible shifts reach 30.0000 mm: the pair is built at 30.0057 mm instead'. Every other row mirrors to 1e-3. With the optimiser off, both orders are unreached at 30.02, so the off path is symmetric and only the searched path depends on order. Code: shape.rs:1282-1292 `(None, b)`; shape.rs:2226-2229 Reaches→Absorbed, else Chosen; pair.rs:115-118 floors. grep for mirror/swapped/member order in train/mod.rs, shape.rs and auto.rs finds no symmetry law.
verdict.proposal_note: The symmetry law is the essential part and should land whatever floor policy is chosen. Choosing max(x_min,0) for both would also restore symmetry, but would refuse 30.02 in both orders. Choosing x_min for both matches reference.md's 'no admissible pair of shifts', since the -0.1453 wheel is a legal, uncut-free gear. That is the policy question finding 46 depends on. Decide it once, in pair::undercut_bound, and let plan_held's tie-break stop mattering.

title: Two tests enshrine the search floor's refusals as geometry; one passes only because its own fixture's distance is not reached
claim: a_manual_centre_distance_ignores_the_clearance asserts that a hand-set distance ignores the clearance, so backlash is 0. Mode 3 (distance_notes doc) says a given distance and clearance decide the shifts. The test passes only because the max(x_min,0) floor makes the asked sum (≈ −0.49) unreachable, and PART_DISTANCE_NOT_REACHED fires inside the test's own fixture. a_distance_the_shifts_cannot_reach_is_said_out_loud calls 9/37 at 23.00 mm, its standard centre distance, 'well inside what the teeth allow' and 'should not be assemblable'. A legal pair with neither tooth undercut reaches it.
evidence: Worktree test vasb::f8b_cases. HEAD: the manual 17/43 fixture gives x (0.0057, 0.0000), nominal 30.0057, clearance 0.0000, notes ['part.distance_not_reached']. verdict.evidence:
Probe verify-added-8:
