title: The walk's step floor in Search::maximise is gated by nothing, including the test written for it
claim: `(spacing * first_step).max(resolution)` exists so that a narrow box still gets walked. The doc of the_search_beats_a_scan_of_the_same_interval names exactly this fault. Removing the .max leaves every test passing: the test's shift sums give boxes where the 13-point grid alone lands within its 1e-5 tolerance.
evidence: Worktree mutation, env-gated so the walk uses spacing*first_step alone. `cargo nextest run --release -p gear-core --no-fail-fast` gives 603 passed and 1 failed. The failure, every_search_is_quick_enough_to_type_over, was load-related: it passes rerun alone, and the_search_beats_a_scan_of_the_same_interval passes under the mutation.
proposal: Add a direct unit test of Search::SHIPPED.maximise on a 1-D box of width 0.02, with a smooth objective whose maximum lies between two grid points. Assert the answer is within resolution of the true maximum. It fails without .max(resolution). Retarget or delete the scan test as part of finding 7.
validation: The new test fails with `.max(resolution)` removed and passes on HEAD.

verdict.reason: Mutation reproduced: with the step floor removed (env-gated in a worktree), all 604 gear-core tests pass (debug), and the fast golden corpus (32 outputs) is unchanged. But the proposed replacement test would not catch the mutation. In a box 0.02 wide the grid spacing is 0.02/12 = 1.67e-3, so the nearest grid point is always within 8.3e-4 < resolution (1e-3) of the peak, and the assertion passes without any walk.
verdict.evidence: Worktree: `let mut step = if VA8_NOMAX {spacing*first_step} else {(spacing*first_step).max(resolution)}`. With VA8_NOMAX=1: `cargo nextest run -p gear-core -E 'not test(va8)'` gives 604 passed, 0 failed. `tools/check_golden.sh --fast` gives 32 unchanged. `gear-cli shifts 9 37` output is byte-identical with and without the mutation, so the case docs/corrections.md:563 records (9/37 at a shift sum of 0.56) no longer exercises it. Proposed test, box (0,0.02) with peak 0.0123: HEAD gives 0.012333 and the mutant 0.011667; both pass. Box (0,0.08) with peak 0.0233: HEAD gives 0.023000 (pass), the mutant 0.020000 (fail).
verdict.proposal_note: Size the box so that grid error exceeds resolution while the first step falls below it: spacing between 2*resolution and 8*resolution, i.e. a box width between 24 and 96 resolutions for scan 12 and first_step 1/8. For example, Search::SHIPPED.maximise(&[(0.0, 0.08)], &|x| Some(-(x[0]-0.0233).powi(2))) must land within resolution of 0.0233. Better still, derive the width from Search::SHIPPED's own fields so the test tracks them.

title: An unreachable given distance a module or more below standard ends in Err(NoRootSection) 'too undercut' on teeth that are not undercut
claim: When the sum a given distance asks for is unreachable, closed() returns None and chosen_at falls back to the settled shifts. The pair is then rated at the given running distance, with overlap past a mm, and bending finds no root section. The whole solve is refused with 'the tooth is too undercut to have a root section', though the teeth sit at (0,0) or (0.0057,0) and neither is undercut. distance_notes' doc promises 'Notes rather than refusals … the designer is owed the number'. These distances are also reachable with legal negative shifts (finding 8).
evidence: Worktree test vasb::f8_floor at HEAD. At a = std−1.5 module, search on and off, 17/43, 23/61, 31/37 and 41/43 give ERR NoRootSection; 17/43 also errors at std−1. At std−1, 23/61, 31/37 and 41/43 return x (0,0) with reached=false. With the chooser floored at x_min, all of them are reached and solve: for example 41/43 at std−1.5 gives (−0.6323, −0.6323), η 0.98536.
proposal: Once finding 8 is fixed, most of these vanish. Independently, a part carrying PART_CLEARANCE_NEGATIVE should not escalate to a refusal: skip the bending rating with a note, as a_ring_with_no_notch_costs_its_bending_rather_than_the_set does for a ring. Reword ERROR_TRAIN_NO_ROOT_SECTION so it does not blame undercut, since the load point can fall off the flank for other reasons.
validation: Law: every pair at every given distance down to the CentreDistanceTooSmall limit returns Ok, with distance_not_reached or clearance_negative notes where relevant, and never NoRootSection with both teeth un-undercut.

verdict.reason: I reproduced it through the public API without the prior worktree. At a given distance about 1 module or more below standard, the pair ends in Err(NoRootSection), 'the tooth is too undercut to have a root section', while its teeth sit at the settled shifts. Those shifts are at or above each member's undercut limit, so neither tooth is undercut. A slightly larger given distance (std-0.75) answers with distance_not_reached and clearance_negative notes, so the verdict flips from note to refusal as the distance moves continuously. That contradicts distance_notes' own doc, which promises notes rather than refusals. The code already records the same misleading message on the ring path (shape.rs:4634: 'the message blamed undercut, which nothing here is'), but the external-member refusal at shape.rs:3234-3237 still raises it.
verdict.evidence:
Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-added-9/src/bin/given.rs (solve_alone over Train::alone of arr::pair; distance = std + dm + manual clearance). Outputs:
- 17/43, search on and off: dm=-1.5, -1.25 and -1 give ERR NoRootSection. dm=-0.75 gives x 0.0057/0.0000 with notes [part.distance_not_reached, part.clearance_negative]; the undercut x_min is 0.006/-1.515.
- 23/61: dm=-2.5 to -1.25 ERR NoRootSection. dm=-1 x 0/0 not reached; x_min -0.345/-2.494.
- 31/37: dm=-2 to -1.25 ERR NoRootSection, and dm=-2.5 is CentreDistanceTooSmall.
- 41/43: dm=-2.5 to -1.25 ERR NoRootSection.
- 20/20: dm=-1 ERR NoRootSection, dm=-0.75 answers with notes.
Refusal site: shape.rs:3234-3237, `if m.ring.is_none() && cut.on_a_line(i) && b.iter().all(|(_, b)| b.is_none()) { return Err(TrainError::NoRootSection); }`. Message: strings_en.toml:202 and mod.rs:1770. The notes promise is at mod.rs:1920-1923.
verdict.proposal_note:
Treat the proposal's two parts separately.
1. Reword the error key so it does not blame undercut. This is right in any case: the load point can leave the flank for other reasons, such as an overlapping running distance or a thick ring.
2. Skipping bending with a note for a part that carries PART_CLEARANCE_NEGATIVE is defensible, but rating at all at an overlapping distance contradicts distance_notes' own statement that 'every figure computed at that distance describes nothing'. A more consistent option is to rate a clearance-negative part at its shifts' own zero-backlash distance, with the notes, or to report no ratings at all for it. The goal is that the refusal and the ratings do not depend on how far past overlap the given distance is.
Add the law the finding names. Sweep given distances from the CentreDistanceTooSmall limit up to standard, with search on and off, and assert Ok with notes. Include 20/20, which fails at std-1.

title: pin_diameter_range_around solves z identical spaces on an ordinary gear: 9 ms at z=300, 88 ms at z=3000, on every gear-panel input
claim: pin_diameter_range_around runs the ~130-seat bisection for every one of the z spaces. On a concentric gear every space is bit-identical (space_half_angle carries the same ψ for all k), and summarise calls it on every gear-panel request, so an ordinary gear pays z times the cost of one space for nothing.
evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-metrology/src/bin/timing.rs, native release, concentric default gear. around: z17 0.60 ms, z100 2.95 ms, z300 9.2 ms, z1000 29 ms, z3000 88 ms. pin_diameter_range(Space::of(mean)): 0.03 ms at every z, and the results are bit-identical. Eccentric: z300 amp0.3 9.9 ms, z1000 amp0.3 29.8 ms. Nothing bounds z (Ranges.teeth: z ≥ 1), and wasm runs slower than native.
proposal: Compute each distinct space once. A space depends only on the ordered pair of teeth (tooth(i).0, tooth(i+1).0) and λ, so memoise on that pair (std::ptr::eq on the two &Tooth, or expose Gear's `which` index as a `distinct_spaces()` iterator). A concentric gear then costs one space and an eccentric one at most z. Combined with finding 11's per-condition solves, each space also stops costing ~130 seat() calls.
validation: The existing law and the bit-identity test for evenly cut gears still pass. Add an assertion that pin_diameter_range_around(Gear::new(p)) equals pin_diameter_range(&Space::of(&Tooth::new(p))) bit for bit on concentric gears. Time z=3000 before and after.

verdict.reason: I re-measured on this machine. pin_diameter_range_around costs about z times one space. On a concentric gear its result is bit-identical to one space, and it dominates everything else summarise does per gear-panel request, by roughly 10x over the next O(z) loop (the over-pins sweep). The absolute cost stays modest at realistic z, a few ms native.

- z300: 4.85 / 0.016 / 0.04 / 0.23 / 0.55 ms.
- z1000: 17.5 / 0.018 / 0.13 / 0.77 / 1.76 ms.
- z300 at amplitude 0.3: 5.07 ms.
around == pin_diameter_range(Space::of(mean)) is true for every concentric case. Cost per space: two 64-step bisections plus the walk, metrology.rs:193-213. Called from gear-wasm lib.rs:419 in summarise. My times are about half the auditor's; the scaling is the same.

A simpler first step: when gear.distinct_teeth() == 1, return pin_diameter_range(&space_at(gear, 0)) directly. title: jgma.rs cites 'the specification's default of grade 3', a specification that is nowhere in the repository
claim: available_classes' doc and the test available_classes_track_the_module justify the design against 'the specification's default of grade 3' / 'the specification's fixed default of grade 3'. No live document states such a default, so a reader cannot tell which specification is meant or whether it still binds. Neither mentions a grade-3 default. The phrase appears only in jgma.rs.

For example: 'a fixed default grade would name a class with no data — grade 3 exists only on the fine scale, below module 1.6 — so the dropdown offers what the table covers.' Alternatively, cite the document that set grade 3, if one exists outside the repository.
validation: Reading; a grep for 'the specification' in crates/ returns no unexplained uses.

The factual half of the sentence is right: fine-scale grade 3 exists only up to module 1.6, and the standard scale starts at grade 4, per jgma.rs:14-18 and the test. The citation, however, points at a source a reader cannot find. The finding treats this as a one-off, but 'the specification' is a project-wide term for an external requirements document that appears in no file. It is cited about 30 times across crates (auto.rs:3, 255, 2504; tests/extremes.rs:1-51; strength.rs:1232; params.rs; material.rs; screw.rs; gear-wasm) and in docs/rationale.md (1070, 1654-1657, 2184-2187 'Additions to the specification's field list'), and never defined in a live document.
verdict.evidence: `grep -rn -i 'grade 3'` over md/rs/toml/svelte/ts finds only jgma.rs:22, 165, 310 and 368, rationale.md:1538 and design-record.md:1697. None of these other than jgma.rs:165/368 mentions a default; the rest are about the ladder drop. `grep -rn -i 'the specification' crates web/src tools | wc -l` gives 30. handoff_inbound/ has no grade default. The app's own default is fine grade 0 where both scales apply (gear-wasm lib.rs:2048-2050, via jgma::default_class).

Either define 'the specification' in one place, for example a sentence in docs/rationale.md: 'the original requirements document, not in this repository', with what it fixed. title: limited_by_face's doc comment still says faces are centred on the pitch plane, and that an offset face merely gives 'a smaller zone'
claim:
The doc comment on CrossedPath::limited_by_face contradicts the function body and misstates what None means.
- It says 'a face of width b centred on the pitch plane holds it only while |s| ≤ b/(2 sin β_b). Faces are taken as centred there ... an offset one is a smaller zone than this reports rather than a different construction.'
- The body centres each face on axial_centre (the member's own mid-plane), with a comment saying the opposite: 'The face is centred on its own gear, which is axial_centre and not the origin of this parameter'.
- The comment also says None means 'a face so narrow that the teeth never meet on it'. In fact None also arises for wide faces whose mid-plane has slid off the zone.
evidence:
screw.rs:913-917 is quoted above. screw.rs:934-938: `let centre = self.axial_centre(screw, i).unwrap_or(0.0);` under that comment.

Probe verify-crossed-worm f0, 17/23 at 20 deg with x1 = 1: an 8 mm face returns None while the zone is only 3.7 path units long. The cause is centres at ±28, not the face being narrow.
proposal:
Rewrite the comment to match the body:
- Each face is centred on its member's mid-plane (axial_centre), and the bound is the intersection of |z_i(s)| ≤ b_i/2 over both members.
- An empty intersection means the contact is off at least one face, whether that face is narrow or offset.

Fix this together with the empty-zone handling of finding 0.
validation: Review only. cargo doc builds and check_doc_links.py passes.

verdict.reason: The doc comment at screw.rs:913-920 says faces are 'taken as centred' on the pitch plane (the parameter's origin). It also says an offset face is merely 'a smaller zone than this reports'. The body at 930-938 centres each face on axial_centre, with a comment saying the opposite. The doc says None means 'a face so narrow that the teeth never meet on it', but None also arises for a wide face whose mid-plane has slid off the zone.
verdict.evidence: Ran the existing probe probes/verify-crossed-worm f0 at HEAD. For 17/23 at 20 deg with x1=1: zone [-0.535, 3.184], axial_centre Some(28.06) and Some(-27.85). limited_by_face returns Some(Tips) at 60 and 30 mm faces, and None at 8 and 4 mm. So an 8 mm face is refused although the whole zone is 3.7 units long: the cause is centres at ±28, not narrowness.
verdict.proposal_note: As proposed. Also note what the probe shows at the train level: the same shifted pair at faces 8, 4 and 2 still solves, reports limited_by Face and gives the full eps 1.2598. So whatever the train does with a None zone deserves the same scrutiny (finding 0). The comment rewrite should say what a caller receives in that case.

title: At small shaft angles a crossed pair's stress scales as 1/√b like a parallel pair's, yet the UI says an automatic crossed face 'has nothing to size it'
claim: The policy that an automatic face on a crossed pair 'stands as entered' rests on the premise that a point contact's pressure does not depend on the width. That premise holds only while the elliptical term governs. Below roughly 5-10 deg the line term max(ellipse, line) with L = b/cos β_b governs. There the peak pressure depends on the face exactly as a parallel mesh's does, so a strength-sized width exists and could be inverted just as the line-contact stage does. Meanwhile the message gear.face_width_as_entered tells the designer there is nothing to size it on.
evidence:
Probe verify-crossed-worm f4b, 17/43, +20 deg helix, 0.02 mm clearance, fixed faces:

| Σ | Face (mm) → pmax (MPa) |
|---|---|
| 2 deg | 5 → 852.5, 10 → 602.8, 20 → 531.5, 40 → 531.5 |
| 5 deg | 5 → 837.4, 10 → 729.7 |
| 0.5 deg | 30 → 351, 16 → 481, 12 → 530, 2 → 1360 |

The 5 → 10 mm ratio at 2 deg is 852.5/602.8 = 1.414 = √2, the 1/√b law. strings_en.toml:121 reads 'automatic face width has nothing to size it on crossed shafts: it stands as entered'.
proposal:
Pick one:
- Keep the policy, but correct the message and reference.md to say what is true: a crossed face is not sized automatically, and at small shaft angles its width does govern the contact stress.
- Or, where the line term governs at the rated contact, compute Widths::contact from σ_line ∝ 1/√L as the line-contact stage does, and report it. Where the ellipse governs, keep None.

Either way, correct the string in all five catalogues.
validation: Add a law over shaft angles 0.5-90 deg: where the line term governs, doubling both faces divides pmax by √2 to within 1e-9, and where the ellipse governs pmax is unchanged. Also assert that the message text no longer claims independence.

verdict.reason: The crate's own contact model contradicts the premise. shape.rs:2568-2571 rates a crossed mesh with hertz::peak_pressure, which is max(ellipse, line) with line_length = b/cos β_b. hertz.rs:219-256 says in so many words that as the shafts come parallel the line term governs, and that it depends on the width (618 vs 369 MPa at Σ=0.5° on a 10 mm face). Even so, shape.rs:3143-3149 ('its pressure does not depend on the width, so no rating can be inverted'), train/mod.rs:676-685 ('a point contact's peak pressure does not depend on it at all'), reference.md:1052-1066 ('A crossed pair has no stress that depends on its face width') and strings_en.toml:121 ('has nothing to size it') all assert the opposite. The auditor's 852.5/602.8 = 1.4142 = √2 for 5 mm to 10 mm at 2° is exactly the 1/√L law of hertz::line_pressure. At a worm's 90° the ellipse governs and the policy is right, so the error is in the stated reason, not the default behaviour.
verdict.evidence: hertz.rs:219 `σ_H = max( σ_elliptical , σ_line )  σ_line = √((P/L)(1/R_y)E*/π)`; shape.rs:2529-2533 'each member's flank runs along its own ruling for b / cos β_b, and the shorter bounds the patch'; shape.rs:3144-3145 'its pressure does not depend on the width'; train/mod.rs:680-681 'a point contact's peak pressure does not depend on it at all'; the ratio 852.5/602.8 = 1.41424.
verdict.proposal_note: Option 2 is continuous and has no new branch if it is written as an inversion of the max. Let σ_e be the width-independent ellipse term and σ_allow the allowable. When σ_e < σ_allow, b_contact = the width at which σ_line(b) = σ_allow (closed form: L = P E*/(π R_y σ_allow²), b = L cos β_b). Otherwise no width helps, so the result is None, with a note. At the least, fix the comments in shape.rs:3143, train/mod.rs:676 and reference.md:1052 together with the five strings.

title: A helical span's contact radius and validity use the transverse projection W/(2 cos beta_b); coaxial anvils touch at W cos beta_b / 2, so the tool picks the wrong k, can accept a span whose anvils rest below the form circle, and can refuse the ideal one
claim: A span micrometer's two anvils are parallel planes, each tangent to its flank along a generator of the involute helicoid. Both generators lie in one base-tangent plane, and their common normal n lies in that plane at beta_b to the transverse plane. Along any common normal (the line coaxial anvils' centres sit on), the two contact rolls sum to W cos beta_b. The code assumes they sum to the transverse chord W/cos beta_b: span_over_teeth uses half = W/(2 cos beta_b), and span_over_teeth_at uses total = sweep. On a helical gear the reported contact radius is therefore too high by up to several mm, and the validity verdict and the chosen k are both wrong. The module's own premise (metrology.rs:5-8) is that reporting a span that touches below the form circle is worse than reporting nothing, and that is exactly what happens. KHK's exact helical formula, zmth = z K(f, beta) + 0.5, reduces algebraically to contact at roll W cos beta_b / 2. The steps: (cos^2 beta + tan^2 alpha_n)(sec beta + 2f)^2 = (R/r_b)^2; 1 + sin^2 beta/(cos^2 beta + tan^2 alpha_n) = 1/cos^2 beta_b; r_b cos beta_b = m_n z cos alpha_n / 2. Together they give W = 2 r_b u_R / cos beta_b.
evidence: (1) Independent helicoid geometry (notes/verify-metrology-b/helical_span.py, numpy/fsolve on the two flank surfaces, no crate code), z60 beta35 m1 k8: on every common normal the rolls sum to 19.8940 = W cos beta_b, not Wt = 28.0396. The symmetric contact is at r = 34.9151. If one contact sits at the code's 36.2860, the other on the same normal is at 33.9798. (2) The tool picks k = 8 with reported contact 36.286, but the true symmetric contact 34.915 is below r_j = 35.716, so no coaxial placement puts both anvil centres on usable flank. KHK zmth = 11.960, so k = 12. For k = 12 the true contact is 36.643 (r = 36.623), but the code reports 39.527 > ra = 37.623 and would refuse it. (3) Probe over 720 unsevered helical gears (z 8-120, x -0.3 to 0.6, alpha 14.5/20/25, beta 10-40): the tool's k differs from the same nearest-r rule applied at the true contact in 446 gears. In 214, the tool's chosen span has its true contact off the usable flank, worst by 5.871 mm. (4) In a worktree, replacing both lines (half = W cos beta_b / 2; total = sweep cos^2 beta_b) leaves all 679 tests passing, except the known timing test, which passes alone. Nothing checks a helical span's contact, and the wasm record's gear is spur.
proposal: In span_over_teeth set `half = nominal * bb.cos() / 2.0`. In span_over_teeth_at set `total = sweep * bb.cos().powi(2)`, the sum of the two contact rolls along a common normal. Better, derive both from one helper, since the two copies (finding 12) must not diverge on this. Fix the comment at :257-259 to say that the configuration is symmetric in the base-tangent plane and that each anvil touches W cos beta_b / 2 from the tangent line. Write the contact formula into reference.md#span-over-teeth, d_M = sqrt(d_b^2 + (W cos beta_b)^2), with its derivation. Add a law to tests/metrology.rs: over the shared grid with beta != 0, the span contact equals the common-normal contact computed from sampled helicoid geometry (as in helical_span.py), and on an evenly cut gear the chosen k matches KHK's zmth wherever the nearest-r rule governs.
validation: The new law fails on the current code (z60 beta35: 36.286 vs 34.915) and passes after the two-line change. KHK's zmth for z60 beta35 alpha20 x0 gives 11.96, and a span with k = 12 must then report contact about 36.64 and be admissible. Spur results are unchanged bit for bit (cos beta_b = 1), so check_golden and check_wasm do not move. Add a helical gear to the proposed metrology golden row so the change is recorded.

verdict.reason: I derived the geometry independently. The involute helicoid is the tangent developable of the base helix. Its normals lie in a base-tangent plane perpendicular to the generators, which are inclined at β_b to the axis. In that plane, a point at transverse coordinate t sits at radius sqrt(r_b² + t²). A common normal of length W (direction at β_b to the transverse direction) changes t by W cos β_b, so the symmetric contacts sit at roll W cos β_b / 2, and d_M = sqrt(d_b² + (W cos β_b)²). The code uses W/(2 cos β_b) at metrology.rs:260 and total = sweep (the transverse chord over r_b) at :364. Both overstate the roll by 1/cos² β_b. This reaches the UI through gear-wasm lib.rs:411 best_span_around → span_over_teeth_at. KHK's helical span-count formula agrees with the auditor only with its (1 + sin²β/(cos²β + tan²α_n)) = 1/cos²β_b factor. Without that factor it reproduces the code's value (8.4856 for z60 β35), which suggests whoever wrote the code used the transverse chord. The spur case (cos β_b = 1) is unaffected.
verdict.evidence: notes/verify-added-10/khk.py: for z60 β35 α20 x0, k at contact = pitch radius is 11.9602 with the helicoid rule vs 8.4856 with the code's rule, a factor 1/cos²β_b in roll. For z60 β35 m1: k=8 gives W=23.618, code contact 36.286, true 34.915 (< r_j 35.716 per the auditor); k=12 gives W=35.427, code contact 39.527 > ra 37.623 (refused), true 36.643. These match the auditor's numbers exactly.
verdict.proposal_note: The two-line fix is right. Derive half = nominal·cos β_b/2 and total = sweep·cos²β_b from one helper, so the two copies cannot diverge again. Add a helical row to the golden corpus. Separately, a helical span also needs enough face width for the anvils (see missed).

title: A crossed mesh whose first member has a negative helix is silently modelled as |β1|: the screw and the members built disagree
claim:
The cause is in Shape::screw_of, which hands Screw::new the diameter worm_pitch_diameter = z·m / cos(helix[m.a]). Cosine is even, so Screw::new recovers sin γ1 = cos|β1| and models the pair as β1 = |β1|, β2 = Σ − |β1|. Meanwhile, helix propagation (shape.rs:884-896, β_b = Σ − β_a) cuts the second member at Σ − β1. The consequences:
- Any opposite-hand crossed pair (β1 < 0, legitimate whenever β2 > Σ) is solved as a different pair. The reported gears do not fit the running distance, and efficiency, contact ratio and stress belong to a hybrid.
- The only guard, |helix[m.a]| ≥ 90, never checks the second member, so it can come out at 110° with a negative pitch diameter.
Nothing refuses and no note fires. The inputs are reachable: a member helix is admitted over (−90, 90) (auto.rs:698 Bound::strictly), and stating the second member's helix above Σ derives a negative first.
evidence:
Probe probes/verify-crossed-worm-b.
- Mode sign: crossed 17/23 at Σ 30° with member 2's helix stated 40° (member 1 automatic). Screw β1 10.0000, β2 20.0000, reference distance 20.8692. Members reported at helix −10 / 40, pitch diameters 17.2623 / 30.0244, tip radii 9.6311 / 16.0122. Members' pitch radii sum 23.6433, but the mesh runs at 20.8892: the cylinders overlap by 2.75 mm. Still reported: eps 1.791, eta 0.94798/0.94898, pmax 1750.65 MPa, interf [true, true], notes [].
- Control, with_first_helix(+10): radii sum 20.8692, running 20.8892 (= +0.02 clearance), consistent.
- Mode f10: with_first_helix(−20) at Σ 90° reports member helix −20 / 110, pitch diameter 18.0910 / −67.2475, eps 0, eta 0.743/0.785, pmax 1507.5 MPa, with no refusal.
- No test covers a negative first helix on crossed axes. crossed.rs:1115 sweeps β1 ∈ {15, 30, 45}; crossed.rs:1209 checks only ±90 and above.
proposal:
Best: the helix parametrisation of crossed-worm finding 10. Screw takes the signed β1 (β2 = Σ − β1), with d_i = z_i m_n / cos β_i, signed β_b,i in contact_normal (n_z = sin β_b1 keeps its sign) and in axial_rate, and lead as None at β = 0.
Interim (S effort), in screw_of:
- refuse helix[m.a] ≤ 0 with a named ScrewError, since the diameter parametrisation cannot represent it (and say so in the catalogue ×5);
- refuse |Σ − helix[m.a]| ≥ 90 for the second member alongside FirstMemberIsADisc.
validation: Law over every crossed mesh, sweeping Σ ∈ {30, 60, 90, 120} and β1 ∈ (−90, 90) \ {0}. Either the solve refuses, or all of the following hold to 1e-12: screw.worm_helix_angle_rad.to_degrees() == helix[m.a], screw.wheel_helix_angle_rad.to_degrees() == helix[m.b], and (d_a + d_b)/2 of the reported members == screw.reference_distance. It fails today at β1 = −10°, Σ = 30°.

verdict.reason: I reproduced it with a copy of the auditor's probe (probes/verify-added-10, modes f10 and sign). screw_of passes worm_pitch_diameter = z·m/cos(helix[m.a]) (shape.rs:529-530). Cosine is even, so Screw::new rebuilds β1 = |β1| and β2 = Σ − |β1|. Helix propagation (shape.rs:889-891) cuts member b at Σ − β1. With β1 = −10°, Σ = 30°, the screw is 10/20 but the members are cut −10/40. Their pitch radii sum to 23.6433 against a running distance of 20.8892, yet the pair is still rated and no note fires. With β1 = −20°, Σ = 90°, member 2 is cut at helix 110° with pitch diameter −67.2475 and still returns efficiency and pmax. The only guard, |helix[m.a]| ≥ 90 at shape.rs:505, never looks at member b. The helix bound (−90, 90) at auto.rs:698 admits negative helices, and opposite-hand crossed pairs are legitimate.
verdict.evidence: Probe output: 'S 30 b1 -10: screw beta1 10.0000 beta2 20.0000 ... helix -10.0000/40.0000 d 17.2623/30.0244 interf [true, true] notes []'; 'members' pitch radii sum 23.6433 vs running 20.8892'; 'S 90 b1 -20: ... helix -20.0000/110.0000 d 18.0910/-67.2475 eta 0.743071/0.785323 pmax 1507.50'. Control +10: radii sum 20.8692 vs running 20.8892.
verdict.proposal_note: The signed-β parametrisation is the right fix. The interim refusal of helix[m.a] ≤ 0 would also refuse the legitimate β1 = 0 case, which already fails today as the misleading WormTooThin (probe: 'S 30 b1 0: ERR Screw(WormTooThin)'). So the interim refusal should be only for β1 < 0, with β1 = 0 handled by the finding-10 fix.

**Σ60, β1 = −30:** member 2 is cut at exactly 90° with d2 = 3.756e17 mm. It is still rated (eps 2.27, eta 0.90, pmax 1946.9) and nothing fires.

**Σ60, β1 = −60:** members −60/120, d2 = −46, (d1+d2)/2 = −6.0 against running 28.52. Rated, with no notes.

**Why:**
- Screw::new receives only worm_pitch_diameter = z·m/cos(β1), so it rebuilds β1 = |β1| and β2 = Σ − |β1|.
- Helix propagation (shape.rs:889-891, β_b = Σ − β_a) cuts member b at Σ − β1.
- The only guard (shape.rs:505, |helix[m.a]| ≥ 90) never looks at member b.

The claim holds in every detail.
repro.note:
I keep the severity at high:
- The fault is silent: no note, no refusal.
- The input is reachable through the admitted helix range and through stating the second member.
- It changes geometry, contact ratio and efficiency for a legitimate class of design. Opposite-hand crossed pairs with β2 > Σ are standard.
- In the degenerate cases it yields a negative or 1e17 mm pitch diameter that still gets a stress and an efficiency.

Mixed-model evidence: pmax is bit-identical between β1 = ±10 while eps differs. So the stress comes from the screw (|β1|) and the contact ratio from the cut members (signed β1): one mesh is reported from two different pairs.

Validation law for the suite: over Σ ∈ {30, 60, 90, 120} and β1 ∈ (−90, 90)\{0}, either the solve refuses, or all of these hold to 1e-12:
- screw β1 == helix[a]
- screw β2 == helix[b]
- (d_a + d_b)/2 == reference_distance

title: contact::sliding_velocity and sliding_at are a second, production-dead implementation of the slip that Contact::slip computes
claim: sliding_velocity's doc calls it 'the friction side of the unification ... one expression covering parallel and crossed axes, with the shaft angle carried in axis_2'. No production code calls it or sliding_at. The crossed efficiency, force and rating all slip through Contact::slip, which evaluates the same v1 - v2 = w1 a1 x p - w2 a2 x (p - c) a second time with the speed ratio derived. The parallel efficiency is a closed form, and the pitch-point sliding is Screw::sliding_ratio. The comment at contact.rs:633-635 promised the crossed version would reuse this function with a different axis_2, and that did not happen. So the crate has two slip implementations, and the one documented as the unification is used only by tests.
evidence: `grep -rn 'sliding_at\b|sliding_velocity(' crates --include=*.rs` finds calls only inside contact.rs's #[cfg(test)] module (from line 950: lines 1409, 1436, 1490, 1520, 1552, 1572, 1624) and in screw.rs tests (line 1498 `use crate::contact::sliding_velocity`, called at 1797). The other hits are the unrelated MeshCase field sliding_velocity. Contact::slip is at contact.rs:731-736 and is used by moment_per_force, which drives Contact::efficiency and normal_force in production.
proposal: Pick one of two. (a) Make Contact::slip the only slip. sliding_at then builds a Contact from the parallel path and splits the slip along the contact line, and sliding_velocity goes. (b) Keep sliding_velocity as the deliberate independent instrument the tests check Screw::sliding_ratio and the parallel identity against. Then move it and sliding_at to testing.rs, which CLAUDE.md lists as 'numerical helpers the tests check closed forms against', and change its doc to say so. Either way, delete the stale 'milestone 7, step 5' paragraph.
validation: cargo nextest run is unchanged. With (b), grep shows no production reference to sliding_velocity and the tests still pass through testing.rs.

verdict.reason: grep finds sliding_velocity and sliding_at called only from sliding_at itself (contact.rs:657), from contact.rs's #[cfg(test)] module (starting at :950; calls at 1409, 1436, 1490, 1520, 1552, 1572, 1624) and from screw.rs's test module (:1494, used at :1797). Contact::slip (contact.rs:731-736) evaluates the same ω1 a1×p − ω2 a2×(p−c) in production. The doc comment at :633-635 about 'milestone 7, step 5' promised reuse that never came, and it is stale. The only document mention (corrections.md:438) is historical.
verdict.evidence: `grep -rnE 'sliding_at\b|sliding_velocity\(' crates --include=*.rs` returns only the lines listed above; contact.rs:633-635 'The crossed-axis version of this arrives with the screw geometry it needs (milestone 7, step 5)'.
verdict.proposal_note: Option (b), moving both to testing.rs as the independent instrument, keeps the value of an independent slip check. That is preferable to (a), which would make the tests check Contact::slip against itself.

title: The parallel-axes refusal and the low-efficiency note still speak of 'stages', and the English refusal has drifted from its four translations

The English reads 'a worm stage needs non-parallel shafts'. de, pt, zh-Hans and zh-Hant say more: 'parallel axes: a worm stage needs crossed shafts, and a parallel pair is a spur stage'. title: The tight end of a backlash band reports play where the teeth jam: point contacts clamp the separation at zero, and both models add axial float to a jam
claim: PointContact::angular_play computes `separation = 2.0 * (a - s.centre_distance).max(0.0) * n[0].abs()`, so a crossed or worm pair asked inside its zero-backlash distance reports zero play, or its axial-float term alone. A line contact at the same end reports negative backlash, which the crate calls interference. So the reading jumps as the shaft angle leaves zero, and a worm or crossed pair never shows a jam. Separately, both play_of (line) and angular_play (point) add the axial-float term to a separation gap that may already be negative. The code's own premise (shape.rs:2636-2637: a slide 'opens one [flank] exactly as far as it closes the other') means no axial position clears a negative total gap, so the float cannot turn a jam into play. The crossed.rs test's rationale, 'closing it below nominal cannot make the backlash negative, because the flanks would simply touch', is wrong: at the zero-backlash distance both flanks already touch, and closer means overlap.
evidence: Probe probes/verify-mesh-contact-bands, mode `angle`: crossed([17,43], Σ) at ±0.1 mm tolerance with 0.02 mm clearance gives a mesh minimum of −0.38912° at Σ = 0 (line contact) and 0.00000° at Σ = 0.01°, 0.1°, 1°, 10° and 90°. Mode `float`: helical 17/43 at β 20° and ±0.1 mm reads min −0.389° with no float but +0.0718° with 0.2 mm axial float (the same jammed tight end); the worm preset at ±0.1 reads min 0.0 with no float and 22.68° with 0.2 mm, where the tight end is 0.08 mm inside zero backlash. Mode `tolsweep`: the Worm preset's minimum stays at 4.5366° (its float term) for every tolerance from 0.02 to 5 mm. crossed.rs:476-503 asserts minimum == 0.0 'tighter than nominal is contact'. corrections.md:369 (4.4) fixed a different step at the same boundary, so this is not a closed finding.
proposal: In angular_play drop `.max(0.0)` so the separation is signed, as 2Δa sin α_n already is. In both angular_play and play_of, add the axial-float term only when the separation (or involute) gap is ≥ 0: `if gap < 0.0 { gap } else { gap + slide }`, then convert to an angle as now. The step at gap = 0 is physical (free float travel against a jam) and should be said so in the comment. Rewrite the crossed.rs test to assert a negative minimum when tolerance_minus > clearance, and that the minimum matches the parallel counterpart to first order as Σ → 0. state.md item 2 (the canary minimum 0.11342° at clearance − tol₋ = 0) stays correct, because there the gap is exactly 0.
validation: Law: for every preset and shaft angle, the band minimum is negative whenever tolerance_minus exceeds the clearance. Law: at Σ = 0.01° the minimum is within first-order agreement of the Σ = 0 line-contact value (−0.389° vs −0.389° for 17/43 at ±0.1). The golden corpus should not move at default tolerances, where clearance = tol₋ = 0.02 puts the tight end exactly at zero gap; confirm that with check_golden.

verdict.reason: At shape.rs:2638 the point contact clamps with `2.0 * (a - s.centre_distance).max(0.0) * n[0].abs()`. The line contact's l.design.backlash(a) is signed, and mesh.rs:341 documents that 'negative means the teeth interfere'. So the band minimum at the tight end jumps from negative (Σ = 0) to 0 (any Σ ≠ 0), and a crossed or worm pair can never show a jam. Both play_of's line arm (shape.rs:3524-3526) and angular_play add the axial-float term unconditionally. The code's own premise at shape.rs:2636-2637 (a slide 'opens one exactly as far as it closes the other') means float cannot turn a negative total gap into play. The rationale of the test at crossed.rs:476-478 ('the flanks would simply touch') is wrong: that test sets clearance 0, so the flanks already touch at nominal and any closer means overlap. state.md's canary (clearance − tol₋ = 0) is unaffected.
verdict.evidence: shape.rs:2638 `let separation = 2.0 * (a - s.centre_distance).max(0.0) * n[0].abs();`; shape.rs:3524-3525 `l.design.backlash(a).unwrap_or(0.0) * ... / a + 2.0*PI*slide/p_bn`; mesh.rs:341 'Positive is play; negative means the teeth interfere'; crossed.rs:497-501 asserts minimum == 0.0 with clearance 0 and tol₋ 0.05.
verdict.proposal_note: Removing .max(0.0) is the right fix. The proposed `if gap < 0 { gap } else { gap + slide }` puts a jump of the float's size into a reported number at gap = 0, and the owner's goals discourage jumps. A cleaner alternative keeps the play continuous (gap + slide, signed) and reports the jam as its own flag or note wherever the separation (or involute gap) is negative, since a negative gap means the mesh cannot be assembled, whatever the float. If the gated form is kept, state it as a deliberate step with its physical reason.

title: The train never reports bottom clearance on a mesh with given shifts, and teeth_clear, documented as 'the whole question', omits it
claim: Mesh::bottom_clearance is consulted only by auto::MeshTrial (the search) and by tests. MeshReport carries flank_interference and, for rings, TipRoom, but no bottom clearance and no note. MeshReport::teeth_clear (mod.rs:621-623) is documented as the whole question yet checks only flank_interference and the ring's tips. So a pair whose shifts the user gave, with tips running into the mate's roots, is reported with its teeth clear. TipRoom's own doc (mod.rs:510-516) says an external pair's one remaining question is bottoming, 'a radial comparison every mesh already makes'; the report never makes it.
evidence: Probe mode `bottom`, pair([20,20]) with profile_shift fixed 1.0/1.0: running 21.6286 mm, r_a 12.0000, r_f 9.7500, so bottom clearance 21.6286 − 12 − 9.75 = −0.1214 mm on both members. Mesh::bottom_clearance at the running distance agrees: [−0.12142, −0.12142]. flank_interference is [false, false], teeth_clear() is true, and there are no train or member notes. Also 30/40 at x 1/1 gives −0.0066 mm with teeth_clear true, and 40/20 at x 1.5/1.5 gives −0.0171 mm on member 0 with teeth_clear true. No note key for bottoming exists in note.rs or strings_en.toml. corrections.md:560 records bottoming as a search bound only.
proposal: Add `bottom_clearance: [f64; 2]` to MeshReport. For a line contact compute it at the running distance with l.operating.bottom_clearance([r_a1, r_a2], [r_f1, r_f2]), taking a ring's own radii; for a point contact use the radial comparison auto.rs:1194 describes. Include `bottom_clearance >= 0` in teeth_clear. Raise a note (e.g. `mesh.tips_bottom_out`, with the member and the depth) and add it to the 5 string catalogues; run check_bindings --write for the new field.
validation: Fixture: 20/20 at x 1/1 must report −0.1214 mm, teeth_clear false and the note. Law: every preset reports a non-negative gap and is unchanged (corrections.md:560 measured sets at 0.03–0.11 mm). The gear_io::strings test fires the new note. The golden diff should show only the new field, where printed.

verdict.reason: Reproduced independently. A pair with shifts the user gives is never checked for bottoming. Mesh::bottom_clearance is read only by auto::MeshTrial / CrossedTrial (the search) and by tests. MeshReport has no bottom-clearance field and emits no note for it, and teeth_clear (train/mod.rs:621-623), whose doc calls it 'the whole question', checks only flank_interference and the ring's tips. The TipRoom doc (mod.rs:510-516) says bottoming is 'a radial comparison every mesh already makes'. That is true of the search and false of the report. rationale.md#a-constraint-belongs-to-the-mesh says the question is 'asked once' and every arrangement gets it, but it is asked only of candidates a search chooses, never of a given design. This violates standing rule 5 (clamp or refuse, and say so): the tool says nothing.
verdict.evidence:
Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-added-11 (bottom.rs.txt): arr::pair with Auto::fixed shifts, solved by solve_alone(Train::alone(..)).
- [20,20] x 1/1, m 1: a 21.6286, ra 12/12, rf 9.75/9.75. gap [-0.1214, -0.1214]. fi [false,false], teeth_clear true, no train, member or mesh notes.
- [30,40] x 1/1: gap -0.0066 on both, clear true, no notes.
- [40,20] x 1.5/1.5: gap [-0.0171, +0.172], clear true. The only note is gear.addendum_held_to_tip_width.
An independent Python calculation from the standard formulas (inv αw, ra = z/2+1+x, rf = z/2-1.25+x, no tip shortening) gives -0.141 / -0.027 / -0.337 at zero backlash. The solver's running distance is opened about 0.02 mm for backlash, which accounts for the difference. Neither note.rs nor strings_en.toml has a bottoming key.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposal is sound. The field should cover both contact kinds: a line contact via operating.bottom_clearance, and a point contact via the centre − r_a − r_f comparison already written in CrossedTrial::efficiency (auto.rs:1194-1199), so there is one expression for each kind. Standing rule 5 also admits the textbook alternative: tip shortening (k·m addendum reduction, ISO 21771) applied as a recorded clamp with its own note, the way gear.addendum_held_to_tip_width already clamps. The owner should choose between reporting and clamping. Adding the field alone, without changing teeth_clear, would repeat the TipRoom::clear mistake that teeth_clear's own doc describes.

title: Two comments say the 17/23 crossed pair at 9°/81° cannot be driven forward at µ = 0.06; it drives at 59 % there
claim: `Directional::locked`'s doc says `gear-cli crossed 17 23 90` at 9°/81° 'cannot be driven **forward** at µ = 0.06'. The test doc for `a_pair_that_transmits_nothing_still_has_its_flanks_pressed` says it 'cannot drive forward at µ = 0.06'. Today the forward locking threshold is 0.1486. The pair reports locked only because the shipped static coefficient is 0.16; at 0.06 it drives forward at 59 %.
evidence:
Probe mode `mu` on arr::worm(17,23).with_first_helix(9.0), the train test's shape.
- sliding 0.06 / static 0.06: η forward 0.5899, backward 0.7048.
- locking_friction forward 0.14856.
- default 0.08 / 0.16: forward 0.0.
- sliding 0.14: forward 0.056; sliding 0.15: forward 0.
- The golden crossed_17_23_90.txt reads 'static μ 0.160 against a threshold of 0.1486'.
- train/mod.rs:11131 already says it correctly: 'at the shipped static friction'.
- corrections.md:580 and audit.md:1885 record the older state as history.
proposal: In both comments, replace 'at µ = 0.06' with 'at the shipped static friction (0.16, against a threshold of 0.149)'. Better still, say 'at a static coefficient above its locking friction', so the sentence does not date.
validation: Re-read the comments against tools/golden/crossed_17_23_90.txt. No code changes.

verdict.reason: The comments are imprecise rather than false. In `gear-cli crossed 17 23 90`, 'mu 0.06' is the sliding coefficient in the header. At sliding 0.06 with the shipped static 0.16 the pair really is locked forward, so 'cannot be driven forward at µ = 0.06' is literally true as the CLI prints it. What misleads is that the sentence credits µ = 0.06 with the locking: the cause is the static coefficient (0.16) exceeding the forward threshold (0.1486). With static friction also at 0.06 the pair drives at 59 %.
verdict.evidence:
Probe verify-added-11 on arr::worm(17,23).with_first_helix(9.0) (shipped sliding 0.08, static 0.16):
- sl 0.08 / st 0.16: η fwd 0.0, locking fwd 0.14856.
- sl 0.06 / st 0.16: η fwd 0.0.
- sl 0.06 / st 0.06: η fwd 0.5899, bwd 0.7048.
- sl 0.14 / st 0.14: η fwd 0.056.
- sl 0.15 / st 0.15: η fwd 0.
tools/golden/crossed_17_23_90.txt line 1 prints 'mu 0.06' and line 6 'static μ 0.160 against a threshold of 0.1486'. The two comments are at contact.rs:259-260 and train/mod.rs:5979-5981.
verdict.corrected_claim: contact.rs:259 and train/mod.rs:5981 credit the locking to 'µ = 0.06', which is the CLI's sliding coefficient. The locking comes from the shipped static coefficient 0.16 against a forward threshold of 0.1486. The sentences should name the static coefficient and the threshold, or say 'at a static coefficient above its locking friction'.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposal's second form ('at a static coefficient above its locking friction') is better because it does not date. The CLI header 'mu 0.06' could also say 'sliding' so the golden output is not ambiguous.

title: The production search's sweep test admits interfering and bottoming grid points, and one already uses 74 % of the slack
claim: `the_shifts_it_chooses_are_the_ones_that_lose_least` checks the chooser against a grid filtered only for undercut, severing, root round and ε ≥ 1.2. The chooser (MeshTrial::efficiency) additionally refuses flank interference and negative bottom clearance. So the gate compares a constrained optimum with a less constrained set. On 9/37 an unbuildable grid point beats the chooser, and the test passes only because SLACK = 1e-4 absorbs the gap. This is the same gap as finding 6, in the gate that matters more.
evidence:
Probe modes `autogrid` and `chosen`, using the test's grid, bounds, µ 0.08 and clearance 0.
- 9/37 chooser: [0.4741, 0.6494], η 0.9762299, clean.
- The grid's best: (0.80, 0.80), η 0.976304, flank_interference [true,false], bottom_clearance [0.086, −0.002].
- It exceeds the chooser by 7.4e-5, against SLACK 1e-4.
- The grid's best buildable point is (0.50, 0.70), η 0.976216.
- On 17/43 and 13/37 the grid's best is clean.
proposal: Give `eta_at` the same refusals as MeshTrial::efficiency: `mesh.flank_interference([a.flank_ends(), b.flank_ends()])` all false and `mesh.bottom_clearance([a.ra,b.ra],[a.rf,b.rf])` all ≥ 0. Better, build the grid point through MeshTrial itself, so the grid and the chooser cannot disagree about admissibility. Then re-derive SLACK from the remaining boundary-approach gap.
validation: After the change the 9/37 grid maximum is 0.976216 ≤ the chosen 0.9762299, and the test passes with far more headroom. Check that SLACK could then be tightened.

verdict.reason: Reproduced exactly. eta_at in the_shifts_it_chooses_are_the_ones_that_lose_least filters for undercut, severing, root-radius fit and ε ≥ 1.2, but not for flank interference or negative bottom clearance, both of which MeshTrial::efficiency refuses. On 9/37 the grid's best point is one the chooser may not choose, and it beats the chooser by 7.45e-5 against SLACK 1e-4: 74 % of the allowance goes to a mismatch in admissibility, not to the boundary-approach effect SLACK's doc justifies. The best buildable grid point sits below the chooser by 1.4e-5. On 17/43 and 13/37 the grid's best is clean and below the chooser.
verdict.evidence:
Probe verify-added-11 (the test's grid, bounds, µ 0.08, clearance 0):
- 9/37 chosen [0.4741, 0.6494]: η 0.9762299, clean.
- 9/37 grid best (0.80, 0.80): η 0.9763044, fi [true,false], gap [0.086, -0.0017]; excess 7.45e-5.
- 9/37 best clean (0.50, 0.70): η 0.9762157; excess -1.43e-5.
- 17/43: chosen 0.9847227, grid best clean 0.9847224.
- 13/37: chosen 0.9813734, grid 0.9813715.
auto.rs:2778-2800 shows eta_at without either refusal.
verdict.proposal_note: Better to build each grid point through MeshTrial (or through the same Cut/is_as_asked path) so the two cannot drift apart. The worst remaining excess is then about -2.8e-7 (17/43), so SLACK could fall to about 1e-5 or below. Re-measure it rather than pick a new figure, and state in SLACK's doc what sweep set it.

title: contact.rs's optimum-shift test claims an interior optimum; on 9/37 its 'best' is at the grid edge and is itself unbuildable
claim: The doc of `an_external_pair_loses_least_well_above_its_undercut_floor` says 'The optimum is interior: stepping either shift further makes it worse'. That holds for 17/43 only. On 9/37 the test's best is (1.45, 2.00), at the grid's upper x2 bound, and it both interferes and bottoms. A wider grid moves it to the ε ≥ 1 bound. reference.md (efficiency section) itself says the 9/37 optimum 'is against a constraint', so the test doc contradicts the reference.
evidence:
Probe mode `edge`, 9/37, the test's filters.
- x2 ≤ 2.0: best (1.45, 2.00), η 0.977166, fi [true,false], wheel bottom clearance −0.247.
- x2 ≤ 3.0: best (0.55, 3.00), η 0.982446, ε 1.0030, clean.
- With interference and bottoming filters, x2 ≤ 2.0: (2.30, 2.00) when x1 ranges to 3.0, and (1.85, 2.00) on the original x1 range. Each lands on a grid edge.
proposal: Delete the 'interior' sentence. If an interior-optimum law is wanted, assert it only for 17/43, by stepping ±0.05 in each shift around the best and requiring every buildable neighbour to be worse. For 9/37 either assert the binding constraint by name or drop it, since the production search's gate covers that pair.
validation: The test doc then agrees with reference.md. Any new 17/43 neighbour assertion passes on the current code.

verdict.reason: Reproduced, and the problem is wider than reported. The doc of an_external_pair_loses_least_well_above_its_undercut_floor says 'The optimum is interior'. On 9/37 the test's own best is (1.45, 2.00), on the grid's x2 edge, with a tooth that interferes and bottoms: 3 of its 8 neighbours are better. Widening the grid moves it to (0.55, 3.00) at ε 1.003. Even 17/43's (0.50, 0.75) is only a local maximum: all 8 neighbours are worse, but on a grid to x2 = 4.0 the test's filter finds (0.80, 3.25), η 0.98962, at ε 1.001. The same doc says 'at 9 teeth the floor pins x₁ at +0.50 and the optimum puts the rest on its wheel'. That describes the production chooser ([0.474, 0.649]), not this test's best (x1 = 1.45). reference.md:643-648 says 9/37 sits 'against a constraint', which contradicts the test doc.
verdict.evidence:
Probe verify-added-11, the test's filters (undercut, severed, ε ≥ 1.0):
- 9/37 on the test grid: best (1.45, 2.0), η 0.9771658, fi [true,false], gap [0.653, -0.247]; neighbours 5 worse, 3 better.
- 9/37 with i up to 60: (0.55, 3.0), η 0.9824459, ε 1.0030.
- 17/43 on the test grid: (0.5, 0.75), η 0.9847224; 8 of 8 neighbours worse.
- 17/43 with i, j up to 80, same filter: (0.8, 3.25), η 0.9896236, ε 1.0014. With root_radius_fits added: (0.5, 0.75) again. The wheel's root does not fit at (0.65, 3.0).
verdict.corrected_claim: The test doc's 'interior' sentence is wrong for 9/37, whose test-grid best sits on the x2 = 2.0 edge and is unbuildable. It holds only locally for 17/43: the test omits root_radius_fits, so its 17/43 answer is where it is because the grid stops at x2 = 2.0. Only the root-radius fit (which the production chooser applies) excludes the region past it. The '+0.50 on the pinion, the rest on the wheel' sentence describes the chooser, not this test.
verdict.proposal_note: Delete the 'interior' sentence and the x1 = +0.50 sentence, or re-attribute the latter to the chooser. If a 17/43 neighbour law is added, it must also apply root_radius_fits, or its premise depends on the grid bound. title: cargo doc warns 34 times on gear-core, 14 of them unresolved intra-doc links, and no check runs rustdoc
claim: The crate relies heavily on intra-doc links. `cargo doc -p gear-core --no-deps` reports 34 warnings: 14 unresolved links, e.g. `MeshError::note` at mesh.rs:765, `TrainError::note`, `Tooth::profile`, `crate::Ring`, `Port`, `GROUND`; 18 public docs linking private items, e.g. contact.rs:750 → `Self::moment_per_force`; and 2 redundant targets. Neither ci.yml, flake.nix nor tools/ runs rustdoc, and check_doc_links.py checks only `docs/*.md#anchor` pointers. The Contact doc mis-attachment (finding 11e) is the kind of fault only rendered docs show.
evidence: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=…/probe-target gc probes/verify-mesh-contact-b6 cargo doc --offline -p gear-core --no-deps` prints: "warning: `gear-core` (lib doc) generated 34 warnings" plus the per-site list. A grep of flake.nix, tools/*.sh and .github/workflows for 'cargo doc', 'RUSTDOCFLAGS' or 'rustdoc' finds nothing.
proposal: Fix the 14 unresolved links. Add `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D warnings' cargo doc --no-deps --workspace` to the flake checks or CI, with `--document-private-items` if links to private items are meant.
validation: The command exits 0 and CI runs it. Reintroducing a broken `[`X`]` link fails the build.

verdict.reason: Reproduced: cargo doc -p gear-core --no-deps reports 34 warnings. 14 are unresolved links (13 distinct targets; Tooth::profile appears twice), 18 are public docs linking private items and 2 are redundant targets. Some unresolved links point at names that no longer exist: tooth.rs has no fn profile, yet tooth.rs:324 and outline.rs:3 link [`Tooth::profile`]. Others point at private trait impls (MeshError::note at mesh.rs:753 is a non-pub fn in an impl). No check in flake.nix, tools/ or .github runs rustdoc.
verdict.evidence: Output of `cargo doc --offline -p gear-core --no-deps` saved in /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-added-11/doc.txt: "warning: `gear-core` (lib doc) generated 34 warnings", with the per-target list. `grep -rn 'cargo doc|RUSTDOCFLAGS|rustdoc' flake.nix tools .github Cargo.toml` finds nothing. `grep 'fn profile' tooth.rs` finds nothing.
verdict.proposal_note: The 18 private-item links are intentional in a crate whose private docs carry the reasoning. The gate is therefore `RUSTDOCFLAGS='-D rustdoc::broken_intra_doc_links' cargo doc --no-deps --document-private-items --workspace` rather than `-D warnings` on public docs, which would push authors to delete useful links. Per CLAUDE.md's table, add it to the flake checks so `nix flake check` covers it, and list it in the 'Which check catches what' table.

title: sliding_velocity / sliding_at / Sliding are public production API that only tests call
claim: The parallel-axis efficiency is the closed form, and the crossed mesh's slip is `Contact::slip`. The vector sliding functions are called only from contact.rs's tests and one screw.rs test. They serve as an instrument, like verify.rs, which CLAUDE.md lists as deliberately kept; these are not listed. `Contact::slip` computes the same `v₁ − k v₂` with the speed ratio derived.
evidence: grep 'sliding_at(|sliding_velocity(' over crates/: every caller is in contact.rs (cfg(test) from line 950) or screw.rs:1797 (cfg(test) from line 1494). The only non-test call is sliding_at's own call of sliding_velocity at contact.rs:657.
proposal: Either record them in CLAUDE.md's 'look wrong and are not' list as the instrument that checks the closed form's no-lengthwise-sliding claim, or move them to testing.rs. Any unification with Contact::slip should wait until something in production needs a sliding vector.
validation: cargo nextest run, with the tests importing them from their new home.

verdict.reason: Confirmed, and the prose around these functions is stale in a way that matters more than the dead code. Only tests call sliding_velocity and sliding_at: contact.rs 1409/1436/1490 (cfg(test) from line 950) and screw.rs:1797 (cfg(test) from 1494). The only production reference is sliding_at's own call. Two doc claims are now false. First, sliding_at (contact.rs:632-635) says the crossed-axis version 'will build a different axis_2 for the same function, not call a different one'. Production crossed sliding is Contact::slip (contact.rs:733-738), which re-derives v1 − k·v2 by its own cross products. Second, sliding_velocity (contact.rs:600-603) says the worm's pitch-point sliding 'arrives here as a value of this function rather than as a separate screw-gear formula'. screw.rs:246-249 computes it by a separate closed form, sqrt(1 − 2k cos Σ + k²). So one phenomenon has three expressions.
verdict.evidence: grep over crates/ and tools/ for sliding_at( and sliding_velocity( finds only test callers (gear-cli and gear-wasm 'sliding_velocity' are an unrelated CaseReport field at train/mod.rs:328). contact.rs:632-635 carries the 'milestone 7, step 5' promise. screw.rs:246-249 has its own formula. contact.rs:733-738 is Contact::slip.
verdict.proposal_note: Rather than only recording them or moving them, make one expression of slip: have Contact::slip (or a shared free function taking axes, centre, point and speed ratio) be the production form, and write sliding_velocity as its test-side wrapper, or delete sliding_velocity and point the helical no-lengthwise-sliding law at Contact::slip. Either way, fix the two stale doc sentences, and keep screw.rs's closed form only as an independent check.

title: A tip-sized internal distance leaves the tips at exactly zero room at running, so the shipped Planocentric preset's tips foul inside its own default tolerance band
claim: An automatic distance on an internal mesh opens out until the tips' room is zero, and the room is measured only at the running distance. `tip_room` (shape.rs:1515-1560) calls `TipRoom::at(&ring, &pinion, running)` and holds `min(far_gap − tip_clearance, tip_margin)` to nought. `sized` (shape.rs:1680-1700) finds the Brent root and leans only 1e-9 to the clear side. The report reads `TipRoom` at `bm.running` too (shape.rs:3844). Both rooms rise with the distance. On an internal pair the tips' room is therefore tightest at running − tol₋, the opposite end from flank interference, and zero room at running means the tips foul anywhere below running. The shipped Planocentric preset is one of these distances, as is every tip-sized distance (the hula and every planocentric count tried). Its tips clear at running and collide 0.02 mm inside it, within the ±0.02 mm the preset itself declares. The backlash band says nothing: its least play there is positive (0.087°).
evidence:
Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-mesh-contact-f12, modes `sized` and `tips`, calling `ring::mesh_at` (the function `TipRoom::at` uses) at running − 0.02, running and running + 0.02.

Shipped `Preset::Planocentric.build()` (30/33, tolerance ±0.02, tip_clearance 0): `DistanceReport` running 1.734179, sized_by Some(0), ring x 0.363947 (also in tools/golden/graph.txt:352). The report's `tips` gives tip_interference false and tip_margin 1.8e-14°. At running − 0.02: tip_interference TRUE, margin −0.0811°. At running + 0.02: +0.0810°.

Other planocentric counts, margin at running − 0.02 with the reported margin 0 at running: 30/31 −0.2049°, 30/34 −0.0679°, 30/36 −0.0528°. On 30/32 the far gap goes 0.0151 → −0.0049 mm at the minus end.

The tests hold the zero margin as intended: arrangements.rs:1858-1863 asserts 'the tips are what held it, so they sit at their limit' (|tip_margin| < 1e-4).
proposal: Size to the tight end of the band. Both rooms rise with the distance, so evaluate the room in `tip_room` (shape.rs:1515-1560) at `running − tolerance_minus`. Equivalently, the held distance becomes the current root plus `tolerance_minus`: one argument changes and nothing new is solved. Report `TipRoom` at the same tight end, or at both band ends combined as in finding 12's note: 'clear across the band'. Use one helper for every admissibility verdict (flank interference, bottom clearance, tip room) that evaluates both `at_band` ends. That needs no per-check sign, because tip room tightens at the minus end and flank interference at the plus end on the same internal mesh. The two sizing tests (arrangements.rs:1191, 1823) then assert zero margin at running − tol₋ instead of at running.
validation: Shipped planocentric: `ring::mesh_at(ring, pinion, running − 0.02)` must give tip_interference false and tip_margin ≥ 0. The running distance moves out by 0.02 mm, and the ring shift moves with it; tools/golden/graph.txt and kinematics.txt change. A fixture with tolerance_minus = 0 must reproduce today's distances to the bit.

verdict.reason: Reproduced independently. The tip-room sizing (`tip_room`, shape.rs:1515-1550) and the report (`TipRoom::at(ring, a.as_gear(), bm.running)`, shape.rs:3844) read the room only at the running distance. The sizing holds that room at exactly zero. On an internal mesh both rooms rise with the distance, so for the whole lower half of the declared tolerance band the tips of the shipped Planocentric preset overlap. The backlash is banded over the same band (`Backlash::banded` with tolerance_minus/plus, shape.rs:3553-3570), so the code already treats the band as distances the pair can really run at. Checking tip admissibility only at the band's centre is therefore inconsistent with the code's own model. The project has already fixed a narrower case of the same fault: rationale.md:1181 and ring.rs `mesh_at`'s doc describe the hula crank that was 'held open until its tip margin was exactly nought and then run a clearance inside it'. That correction moved the check from zero backlash to running, but it did not carry through the tolerance band. No document records this as a known bias (state.md has nothing on tip room against tolerance). The test at arrangements.rs:1858-1864 asserts |tip_margin| < 1e-4 at running, which fixes today's behaviour in place.
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-added-12 solves `solve_alone(Train::alone(..., 2.0, 1000.0))` and then calls `ring::mesh_at` on the solved pinion and ring (`Ring::cut_by`). For Preset::Planocentric (30/33; tip_clearance 0; tol ±0.02; clearance 0.02): nominal 1.754179, running 1.734179, sized_by Some(0), ring x 0.363947. The report's tips are (false, 1.8e-14 deg, far 1.598). The margin at running−0.02 is −0.08114 deg with foul TRUE; at running−0.01 it is −0.04055 (foul); at running−0.001 it is −0.00405 (foul); at running it is 0; at running+0.02 it is +0.08101. The other counts give margins at running−0.02 of: 30/31 −0.20490, 30/34 −0.06793, 30/36 −0.05283 deg, all sized_by Some(0). 30/32 is not sized, but its far gap goes from +0.01508 at running to −0.00492 at running−0.02. That is the same fault in the far-gap half of the room: the pinion's far-side tip reaches past the ring's tip circle, and the report still says the tips clear. These values match the auditor's to the digit.
verdict.proposal_note: Evaluate the room at `running − tolerance_minus` inside `tip_room` and in the report, then let Brent solve with that. Do not add tolerance_minus to today's root afterwards. The 'equivalently, root + tolerance_minus' shortcut is not exact. The ring's tip radius depends on its shift (ring.rs:278, `ra = r − m(addendum − x)`), and the ring re-shifts to reach whatever distance is held. The room at (e − tol) with shifts that reach e is therefore not the room at e − tol with shifts that reach e − tol. The far-gap half of the room needs the same treatment, which also catches the unsized 30/32 case. The report should state the room at the tight end, or 'clear across the band', so the panel's verdict and the sizing agree. A tolerance_minus = 0 fixture reproducing today's figures to the bit is a good regression guard.

title: reference.md says 'a shipped preset is never sized, its tips clearing where the shifts leave them', but the shipped Planocentric is sized by its tips
claim: The paragraph on tip-sized distances ends: 'on the hula's own 19/18 the shape sizes to its crank offset within 2 × 10⁻⁵ mm, and a shipped preset is never sized, its tips clearing where the shifts leave them'. For example: 'and of the shipped presets the planocentric is sized: at 30/33 its tips would cross at the distance the shifts leave, and it opens to 1.734 mm with the ring shifted +0.364 to reach it'. Tag it for tools/check_figures.py so the figure is held to what `gear-cli graph` prints. If the missed tip-sizing fix lands, the figure becomes the tolerance-padded distance.

verdict.reason: reference.md:2398-2400 says 'a shipped preset is never sized, its tips clearing where the shifts leave them'. `Preset::Planocentric` (arrangements.rs:946, planocentric(30, 33)) is a shipped menu preset, and its distance is sized by its tips. verdict.evidence: The same probe gives Preset::Planocentric.build(): sized_by Some(0), running 1.734179 (the counts' reference offset is 1.5 mm, which the clearance would put at 1.48), and ring x 0.363947 reaching it. tools/golden/graph.txt records 'member 2 z 33 ... x 0.363947' and 'distance 1 running 1.734179'.

If finding 66's fix lands, both the figure and the sentence change (the distance opens by about tolerance_minus, re-solved and not simply added), so the two edits belong in one change.

title: PATH_SAMPLES and SEARCH_SAMPLES point readers to a convergence test in the wrong module
claim: Both constants say the trapezium residual 'is below 1e-9' and cite `train::crossed` as where this is shown. The test that shows it, the_path_average_has_converged, is in screw.rs's test module. train/crossed.rs has no convergence test for the quadrature; its only 'converged' claim (crossed.rs:1477) is about the optimiser.
evidence: grep 'PATH_SAMPLES\|2048' shows the assertion error(2048) < 1e-9 only at screw.rs:2714. grep 'converged' in train/crossed.rs finds only line 1477, which is about the search.
proposal: Point both comments at `screw::tests::the_path_average_has_converged`. Better still, adopt a Gauss rule (see finding 18) and state its tolerance once, in one place both constants share.
validation: tools/check_doc_links.py does not check intra-crate test pointers; confirm by grep.

verdict.reason: Both comments cite `train::crossed` for the 1e-9 residual. The test that asserts it is `screw::tests::the_path_average_has_converged`; train/crossed.rs has no quadrature convergence test.
verdict.evidence: shape.rs:2644-2645: "the trapezium rule's residual is below 1e-9 here (`train::crossed`)"; auto.rs:1591-1592 says the same. The only assertion is screw.rs:2714 `error(2048) < 1e-9` inside `path_average_converges_for`, called from `the_path_average_has_converged` (screw.rs:2660). The one 'converged' in train/crossed.rs (line 1477) is about the search. Also, the test writes the literal 2048 rather than using `PATH_SAMPLES`, so the constant and the test that justifies it can drift apart.
verdict.proposal_note: Repoint both comments to `screw::tests::the_path_average_has_converged`. Make the test use the shared constant rather than the literal 2048 (expose PATH_SAMPLES pub(crate) from screw.rs or pass it in), so a change to the count re-checks the claim.

title: A crossed pair's path of contact flickers on and off as the shaft angle falls from 1e-3 deg to 1e-4 deg
claim: This adds to finding 3 and finding 18. Its measured seam ('below about 5e-4 deg the path is None') is not a clean threshold. The path is refused at 5e-4°, returns at 3e-4°, and is refused again at 1e-4° and below. So a sweep of the shaft angle across this band switches the contact ratio, zone and path efficiency between the full answer and the pitch-point fallback more than once.
evidence: Probe verify-crossed-worm-1, 17/43 pair with β1 = Σ/2 + 20°, tips at r+m_n. Contact ratio 1.663732 at 1e-3° and 3e-4°; None at 5e-4°, 1e-4°, 1e-5° and 1e-6°.
proposal: Same fix as finding 3: build the line in closed form, anchored at the pitch point, with no branch search and no Cramer solve. A test should sweep Σ log-spaced from 1° down to where Screw::new refuses and assert the path stays Some and ε stays continuous.
validation: Sweep test as above; it fails on the current code at 5e-4° and 1e-4°.

verdict.reason: My own sweep reproduces the flicker, and it is worse than described: the path comes and goes several times across about 1e-3 to 1e-4 deg before it disappears. Reachable: the shape builds a point contact for any shaft angle other than exactly 0 (shape.rs:477/492).
verdict.evidence: Probe verify-last-1: 17/43, beta1 = Sigma/2 + beta_add, tips r+1, Sigma log-swept over 61 points from 1e-2 deg to 1e-7 deg. beta_add 20: eps 1.663732 down to 1.0e-3; None at 8.25e-4; back at 6.81e-4..4.64e-4; None from 3.83e-4 down. beta_add 10: None at 4.64e-4 and 3.83e-4, back at 3.16e-4 and 2.61e-4, None at 2.15e-4, back at 1.78e-4, None at 1.47e-4, back at 1.21e-4, None from 1.0e-4. beta_add 30: None at 5.62e-4, back at 4.64e-4, None below. Screw::new refuses (E) from about 5.6e-7 deg. The on/off pattern is set by the fixed absolute threshold in mesh_branch (`offset < 1e-6 * reference_distance`) and the `d.abs() < 1e-12` guard in solve3 against a conditioning that shrinks with Sigma.
verdict.proposal_note: The closed-form, pitch-anchored line proposed is the right fix. The sweep test should cover several beta splits, not one, because where the flicker falls depends on beta.

title: Shape::assembly returns None ('rule does not reach') for a replicated axis with a single mesh, where the answer is known
claim: `if pairs.len() < 2 { return None; }` reports 'no answer' for a planet axis with one mesh to a central member. With one mesh, psi is free, so equal spacing always holds, and simultaneous meshing is N | z_c, which the function computes anyway. None is documented as meaning 'the rule does not reach', but here the rule gives a definite answer.
evidence: shape.rs:694-696 returns None before `simultaneous` is computed, although that line (`pairs.iter().all(|&(c, _)| c % n == 0)`) works on a one-element list. The docstring says None applies only 'where the rule below does not reach: an axis with a mesh to another replicated axis'. A carried axis whose planets mesh only a sun or only a ring is contrary to that docstring. So is a carried axis with more than one body, each with one mesh, which the panel can add (AddGear on NewBody of a planet axis).
proposal: Return Some((true, pairs.iter().all(|&(c, _)| c % n == 0))) when pairs.len() == 1. Keep None only for pairs.is_empty(), or drop None entirely once the cluster congruence rule (finding shape-b #3) replaces this function.
validation: Add a unit test: a carried axis with one planet meshing only the sun (N = 3, z_s = 12 and 13) returns Some((true, true)) and Some((true, false)) respectively. Cross-check against assembles_by_search with a single pair.

verdict.corrected_claim: The None for one mesh is real: a sun-only planet at N=3 reports equal_spacing None where the answer is (true, N | z_s). A worse fault sits on the same line. `assembly` collects pairs per axis, not per planet body, so a carried axis with two bodies is judged as if they were one rigid stepped planet. That gives a false Some(false) and a false 'planets cannot be evenly spaced' note.
verdict.reason: The rule works on the rigid body the planet gears share (one psi per body), but the code gathers every mesh from every body on the axis. The panel can create such an axis with Move{to: None} or AddGear{on: NewBody}.
verdict.evidence: Probe verify-last-1: epicyclic(3, [[18]], [Sun 12, Carrier]).assembly(1) = None, and for Sun 13 also None; solve shows layouts (1,3,None). Compound preset, then Edit::Move{member:4, to:None}: bodies on axis 1 become 5 and 6. Setting the moved planet to 18 teeth gives assembly(1) = Some((false, false)). Correctly, body 5 (18 meshing sun 24 and ring 60: 3 | 84) is true, and body 6 (one mesh with ring 59) is free, so the answer should be true.
verdict.proposal_note: Group the pairs by planet body. Each body with two or more meshes contributes its pairwise gcd condition. A body with one mesh adds nothing to 'equal', and simultaneous is still N | z_c over every central member the axis meets. Return None only for a mesh to another carried axis. The 1-pair case then falls out with no special branch. Add a test for the two-body axis beside the sun-only one.

title: The shipped Wolfrom preset is one whose planets cannot be evenly spaced, so its default warns
claim: Preset::Wolfrom builds wolfrom(18, [60, 61], 3): one 18-tooth planet meshing rings of 60 and 61 teeth, 3 planets. The shape's own assembly rule says 3 identical planets cannot be assembled equally spaced at these counts, so the preset shows part.planets_not_evenly_spaced as soon as it is picked. A menu default should be a set that assembles. For a single-planet Wolfrom the rule reduces to N | z_r2 - z_r1, and 61 - 60 = 1.
evidence: Probe verify-shape-b-3: `Wolfrom axes [(1, 0), (3, 1)] layouts [(1, 3, Some(false))] notes ["part.planets_share_load_equally", "part.planets_not_evenly_spaced"]`. The rule at shape.rs:711 gives (-60*18 - (-61)*18) mod (3*18) = 18, which is not 0. Every other epicyclic preset with a verdict (Planetary, Compound) reports Some(true). docs/state.md:638 covers only stepped-planet timing, not this preset.
proposal: Choose ring counts whose difference is a multiple of N, e.g. wolfrom(18, [60, 63], 3), keeping it within the tip-clearance and shift closure the shape solves. If the 1-tooth difference is deliberate (a high-ratio demonstration), either say so in Preset::build's doc and in docs/state.md, or drop the count to 1. Then update the golden corpus.
validation: Re-run the probe: Wolfrom should report equal_spacing Some(true) and no planets_not_evenly_spaced note. Add a law that no Preset::ALL default raises planets_not_evenly_spaced. Run cargo nextest run (the arrangement ratio tests reference wolfrom(18,[60,61],3) directly at arrangements.rs:1134 and shape.rs:4375, 5832, so those may need their own counts) and tools/check_golden.sh.

verdict.reason: The shipped Wolfrom default warns, and by first principles it should: with a simple planet meshing two rings, the phase condition is N | (z_r2 - z_r1), and 61 - 60 = 1 is not a multiple of 3. The warning's wording is also wrong for this preset: it speaks of a sun, and a Wolfrom has none.
verdict.evidence: Probe verify-last-1: Wolfrom preset gives layouts [(1,3,Some(false),true)] and notes [planets_share_load_equally, planets_not_evenly_spaced]. strings_en.toml:109 says "sun and ring tooth counts do not sum to a multiple of planet count", but the Wolfrom has no sun. The proposed fix does not close: wolfrom(18,[60,63],3) gives ERR NoCommonDistance, and so does [57,60] at N=3. What does solve cleanly: wolfrom(18,[60,62],2) gives Some(true) with no warning, and wolfrom(18,[60,61],1) gives no layout.
verdict.proposal_note: Do not use [60,63]: it does not close (NoCommonDistance). Use a count that assembles and closes, such as wolfrom(18,[60,62],2), or keep 60/61 at N=1, or use a stepped planet (the hula family) for a 3-planet Wolfrom. Also reword the note generically, e.g. 'tooth counts do not satisfy the equal-spacing condition for {planets} planets', and add a law that no Preset::ALL default raises planets_not_evenly_spaced.

title: The still port's flow weight of ±1 is added in rpm beside real rpm, so a case's answer depends on the given speed's magnitude
claim: `unit[i] += weight * v` with weight = s for a moving load and ±1 for a load given at 0 rpm. The flow (flow::solve(shafts, &meshes, &unit, …)) then takes each mesh's direction from `unit`. The ±1 is meant as an infinitesimal impending motion but has the weight of 1 rpm. When the other given speeds are near or below 1 rpm, it outweighs them and changes which way power flows. The same case then gives different torques at different input speeds, which is a discontinuity in scale that ought to be absent.
evidence: Probe probe_verify_train_mod_b_1 `mixweight`: planetary 12/30/72 with the ring released; sun given 2 N·m at sun_rpm; ring given 0 rpm with torque derived (seed ±1); carrier derived. Seed -1: carrier torque -13.675453 at 3000, 1 and 0.1 rpm. Seed +1: -13.675453 at 3000 and 1 rpm but -14.333568 at 0.1 rpm, with ring torque 12.3336 against 11.6755. Only the speed's scale changed, and at 3000 rpm the two seeds agree, which is the scale-free answer.
proposal: Treat the still ports' impending motion as a lexicographic tie-breaker, not an additive term. Compute the given-speed motion `speeds` and the still-port motion `still` (the ±1 solutions, with each sign chosen as finding 0 proposes, from given torques only) separately. Give flow::solve, per mesh, the sign of the relative sliding velocity from `speeds`, falling back to `still` only where that velocity is exactly zero. Equivalently pass speeds + ε·still with ε→0, taking signs mesh by mesh. Do not use `unit` for the duty turns (finding 3).
validation: Law: for every preset and case, scaling every given speed by k in {1e-3, 1, 1e3} leaves every torque and efficiency unchanged; the torque figures are scale-invariant in speed. Run it over the `mixweight` fixture and the stall cases.

verdict.reason: The mechanism is as described. At mod.rs:4410-4418 a still load's weight is +/-1, and it is added to real rpm-weighted motion at 4437 (`unit[i] += weight * v`). flow::solve takes mesh directions from `unit` at 4485. So when the given speeds are about 1 rpm or less, the tie-breaker outweighs them. No law in the suite checks that torques are unchanged when every speed is scaled.
verdict.evidence: Re-ran probe verify-train-mod-b-1 mixweight. Seed +1: carrier T -13.675453 at 3000 and 1 rpm, but -14.333568 at 0.1 rpm, with ring T 12.333568 against 11.675453. Seed -1: -13.675453 at every speed. The weight's sign also comes from `l.torque.manual` even when the torque is automatic (a derived torque's stale seed). grep over train/mod.rs and flow.rs finds no speed-scale test.
verdict.proposal_note: The lexicographic tie-break is right. The simplest form is to normalise: pass unit = speeds/|speeds|_inf + eps*still with a tiny eps (or decide the sign per mesh from speeds and fall back to still only where the relative speed is exactly 0). Also take the still port's sign from a given torque only, never from an automatic torque's manual seed. Add the scale-invariance law over every preset's cases.

title: A differential given one speed per port reports 'motion undecided: 0 more speed(s) to give'
claim: When every open port of a two-degree-of-freedom set has a given speed, determined=false, because each driver with the others grounded is over-constrained. `short` is 0, because driving every port at one turn is a consistent rigid rotation. The case is refused with case_underdetermined { short: 0 }, a message that contradicts itself. The same happens on a pair whose two given speeds agree exactly with the ratio: a consistent over-specification is refused (as short 4294967295).
evidence: Probe verify-train-mod-b-2. Planetary(12,30,72,3), release(3), held [], case_mobility 2, speeds given at 1, 2 and 3 gives note {key: train.case_underdetermined, short: "0"}. Pair with speeds 4300 and -1700 (exact ratio) gives short 4294967295.
proposal: Decide over- and under-determination by count against case_mobility() before solving: given > m gives case_overdetermined { over }, and given < m gives case_underdetermined { short = m - given }. Optionally accept an over-given case whose speeds are consistent with the motion, by solving with every given port driven at its speed and checking the residual.
validation: Unit tests: a differential with three given speeds gives overdetermined { over: 1 }; a pair with exact-ratio speeds either solves or gives overdetermined; no note ever carries short 0 or u32::MAX.
