verdict.reason: Two faults cause it. `determined` is false because each over-constrained driver's solve is not unique. `short` is computed with every given port driven at one turn, not at its speed. So a differential gets a consistent rigid rotation (short 0), and a pair driven +1/+1 is inconsistent (usize::MAX becomes 4294967295). Neither note tells the designer anything true.
verdict.evidence: Re-ran probe verify-train-mod-b-2. overspeed-diff (planetary released, mobility 2, speeds 3000/100/50 on sun/carrier/ring): case_underdetermined short "0". overspeed-pair (-1000): short "4294967295". overspeed-pair-consistent (4300/-1700, exact ratio): short "4294967295". strings_en.toml:153 prints '{short} more speed(s) to give'. A key for this situation already exists: error.train_overdetermined (note.rs:241).
verdict.proposal_note: A pure count against case_mobility is not enough: two given speeds on kinematically dependent bodies (say two bodies of one rigid chain in a layshaft) meet the count but are rank-deficient. Decide by rank instead. Solve with every given port driven at its own speed (as a rational): inconsistent means over-given (a case_overdetermined note naming the port), a residual means short by residual.len(), and a consistent unique solution should be accepted and solved. Never emit short 0 or u32::MAX.

title: docs/reference.md contradicts itself on whether an unmentioned chain end is reacted
claim: The same paragraph says 'A port the case does not mention is free.' and then 'The two ends it does not load are **reacted** ... Every other open port the case does not load is **free**'. Only the first matches the code (mod.rs:4360-4364).
evidence: Lines read directly. Probe: a pair case with only a load at 1 reports body 2 as Free.
proposal: Delete the sentences at 2747-2753 about reacted ends. Keep the fresh-case sentence, which states that the reaction is written explicitly.
validation: check_doc_links and check_figures still pass.

verdict.reason: In one paragraph of docs/reference.md, an earlier sentence says 'A port the case does not mention is free.' A later one says 'The two ends it does not load are **reacted** ... Every other open port the case does not load is **free**'. The code agrees only with the first. mod.rs:4351-4375 derives `reacted` only from entries the case declares with LoadRole::Reacted. The role closure gives Load, then Reacted, then Fixed (ground), and otherwise Free, so an unmentioned chain end is Free. The fresh-case sentence stays true because a fresh case writes its reaction explicitly.
verdict.evidence: docs/reference.md:2737 and :2747-2753, read directly. mod.rs:4352-4359 has the comment 'A port is what the case declares it, and free where it says nothing', and :4360-4364 filters on `declared(s, LoadRole::Reacted)`.
verdict.proposal_note: Delete from 'The two ends it does not load are **reacted**' through 'says so by loading it.' Keep the last sentence ('What each body is in a case ... ground first'). The free/reacted definitions earlier in the paragraph already say the rest.

title: An automatic face width tends to zero with the load, with no floor and no note
claim: On straight teeth the only floor under a strength-sized automatic face width is the overlap floor, which is 0 there. The width therefore falls in proportion to the torque with no limit. Typing a small torque produces a gear a few microns, or fractions of a nanometre, wide, and no note is raised. docs/state.md:746 says a gear with no face is 'a degenerate input rather than a reachable state of the controls'. It is reachable from the automatic width: any small typed torque produces a near-zero face. Rule 5 asks for 'clamp rather than refuse, and say so', and the rating models' validity (b/m ranges) is left far behind without a word.
evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-train-mod-b-3/src/main.rs, run on pair([17,43]) with both members' face_width.auto = true. Widths: 0.895 mm at 2 N·m, 4.48e-4 mm at 1e-3 N·m, 4.48e-13 mm at 1e-12 N·m, and a.notes empty at every torque. shape.rs:3461-3473: `width_for(...).max(for_overlap(i))`, where for_overlap is 0 for a straight mesh (reference.md:472: 'Given as a floor on straight teeth it asks nothing').
proposal: Add a stated lower bound on an automatic face width: a proportion of the normal module, exposed as a member input with its default computed in Rust (rule 1), or the box value used as a floor. Apply it where the overlap floor is applied, with a note when it governs. The same floor removes finding 14's jump at zero torque. Then correct docs/state.md:746 to say a vanishing width is reachable and what bounds it.
validation: A law: for every preset with automatic widths, the member width is non-decreasing in torque and never below the floor, including at T=0, and a note fires when the floor governs. Before the fix, the probe above fails it.

verdict.reason: I re-ran it in my own probe, which also collects member notes and clamps as well as part notes. pair([17,43]) with both widths automatic gives 0.8953 mm at 2 N·m, 4.4765e-4 mm at 1e-3 N·m and 4.4765e-13 mm at 1e-12 N·m. No note or clamp fires on the part or on any member, and recommended_face_width is None. At T=0 the width jumps to the box value, 10 mm. That happens because width_for (mod.rs:2553) returns `given` when want == 0, which is the discontinuity in finding 14. The width is linear in torque: bending asks b ∝ F, and contact asks σ_H ∝ sqrt(F/b), which also gives b ∝ F. The only floor is width_for_overlap, and it is None on straight teeth (mod.rs:2117). So docs/state.md:746, which calls a faceless gear 'a degenerate input rather than a reachable state of the controls', is wrong: the automatic width reaches it continuously.
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-last-2/src/main.rs. Output: 'T=2e0: widths [0.8953.., 0.8953..] rec [None, None] keys []', 'T=1e-3: widths [0.000447..]', 'T=1e-12: widths [4.476e-13, ..] keys []', 'T=0e0: widths [10.0, 10.0]'. shape.rs:3461-3473 is width_for(...).max(for_overlap(i)).
verdict.proposal_note: Rule 6 and the owner's goals (a rule of thumb only as a visible option) mean the floor must be a stated input with its default computed in Rust, for example b/m_n ≥ φ_min. Do not hard-code a proportion. At minimum, raise a note when a strength-sized width falls below the validity range of the rating model (b/m). The same floor removes the jump to the box value at T=0, provided width_for then takes max(want, floor) instead of falling back to `given`.

title: train.load_shared's words blame a double hold for what is a redundant mesh loop
claim: flow::Refused::Undetermined is raised whenever the lossy flow's torque system is rank-deficient. That happens both for two held ends and for a statically indeterminate mesh loop (twin countershafts, a doubled mesh). The only message tells the designer to 'hold one end only', which is impossible advice for a twin-layshaft train that holds nothing twice.
evidence: Probe bin dual: the twin-layshaft train with default holds gives case notes [train.load_shared]. strings_en.toml:155 reads 'held at both ends: how the load divides is a matter of stiffness this model does not state — hold one end only, or let a self-locking mesh hold it'.
proposal: Tell the two apart before the flow. A structural redundancy shows up in the kinematic System as a redundant structural row (solve() already detects Insert::Redundant for structural rows and discards it silently, kinematics.rs:577-583). Surface that as a separate note, for example train.mesh_loop naming the meshes, and keep load_shared for doubly held ends.
validation: Twin-layshaft and doubled-mesh trains raise the new note, not load_shared. An existing load_shared test (a reaction on both ends) still raises load_shared.

verdict.reason: I reproduced it. The twin-layshaft train (two identical 43/19 layshafts between the input and output on the centre axis) holds nothing twice and loads only its chain ends, yet its case comes back unsolved with train.load_shared. Without the second layshaft it solves with efficiency 0.968. The torque split between the two layshafts is statically indeterminate, so flow::solve's least_squares_exact reports undetermined and returns Refused::Undetermined (flow.rs:274-279). mod.rs:4499-4502 maps every such case to TRAIN_LOAD_SHARED, and the English text ('held at both ends ... hold one end only') gives advice this train cannot follow. kinematics.rs:577-583 does absorb a redundant structural row silently, as the finding says.
verdict.evidence: Probe bin /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-last-2/src/bin/dual.rs. Output: 'dual false: path 1->2 ratio 5.458204 eff 0.968084 ... case solved true notes []' and 'dual true: ... eff 0.000000 ... case solved false notes ["train.load_shared"]'. strings_en.toml:155.
verdict.proposal_note: The flow itself tells the two causes apart more reliably than a redundant kinematic row does. A doubled coupling is also a redundant row and might not make the torque system singular. Find the null space of the torque system: if it moves only internal mesh torques and no port torque, the problem is a mesh loop; if it moves the torques of reacted or derived ports, it is a double hold. Carry that in Refused (for example Undetermined { ports: bool }). Consider also an explicit, user-visible equal-sharing assumption for identical parallel paths, the planet-replication idea, so that such a train can be rated rather than refused.

title: docs/reference.md says the train flow applies 'the output has to absorb' (T_out w_out <= 0); flow::solve does not test it
claim: reference.md says the mesh-by-mesh flow makes 'the same decision' as planetary::power, whose second condition is that the output absorbs power. The flow's only energy test is total loss >= 0. It admits a branch in which the output delivers power (Wolfrom: eff 0, ring2 +265.8 W), and it relies on max-efficiency selection to reject that branch. The document names a criterion the train solve does not use.
evidence: Probe verify-kinematics-flow-2: flow::solve restricted to assignment (B,F) on the Wolfrom 18/60/61 with the carrier driven returns Ok(eff 0.0) with ring2 power +265.84. That flow passed flow.rs:319-322. planetary::power would reject it by its T_out w_out <= 0 test.
proposal: Reword reference.md:1803-1806: the flow keeps, of the direction-consistent assignments that lose power, the one of greatest efficiency. For a set with one input and one output this coincides with the closed form's two conditions. The eff-0 branch, where a derived port delivers power, is what that rule excludes. Point to flow.rs for it.
validation: tools/check_doc_links.py; reread against flow.rs:342-348 after the finding-6 comment fix.

verdict.reason: I reproduced it. With flow::solve restricted to one assignment, (B,F) on the Wolfrom 18/60/61 with the carrier driven returns Ok with efficiency 0.0 and ring2 delivering +265.84 W. It passes the direction test and the loss ≥ 0 test (loss = 61 + 265.8 > 0). Only the max-efficiency choice at flow.rs:346 rejects it, against the (F,B) branch with 0.4536. So the flow does not apply condition 2 ('the output has to absorb'), and 'the same decision made mesh by mesh' overstates it. Two comments in flow.rs are wrong in the same way. At :307-309, 'One input and one output reads as "the output absorbs what the input delivers"' is false, since loss ≥ 0 also admits an output that delivers. At :341-345, 'the first consistent one is the answer, and a second genuinely different one would be a finding worth a test' is contradicted by this case, which has two consistent and genuinely different assignments.
verdict.evidence: Probe bin /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-last-2/src/bin/f6.rs. Output: 'F6 only (F,B): Ok((0.45356.., [0, 61, 0, -27.667, -0]))', 'F6 only (B,F): Ok((0.0, [0, 61.0000, -0, 265.844, -0]))', 'F6 real solve: Ok((0.45356.., [Forward, Backward], ...))'.
verdict.proposal_note: Rewording reference.md:1803-1806 is right, but it should go together with fixing the two flow.rs comments (:307-309 and :341-345). A cleaner code option is to test outright that no derived (unknown) port delivers power while a known port drives. That is condition 2 generalised, and it would stop the answer depending on max-efficiency selection. A law should then check that no two admissible assignments remain.

title: The relief-law test's comment calls a tip-sized internal distance's clearance a floor; it is a ceiling
claim: The comment justifying the tips_hold skip says 'the clearance is a floor the mesh clears'. On the internal mesh it describes (Planocentric), clearance = nominal − running, and the tips hold the distance open from below. Every clearance above the tip-limited value is replaced by it, so the clearance is capped from above.
evidence: Probe bin ten, Planocentric pinned: typed clearance 0.01 → 0.01 (sized_by None); typed 0.03, 0.05 or 0.1 → 0.02 (sized_by Some(0)), with running constant at 1.73418 and nominal at 1.75418.
proposal: Reword: 'the tips hold the distance open, so the clearance cannot exceed what they leave; a larger one is not a figure the solve can reach'. Better, once a note for the replaced clearance exists (finding 10), remove the skip.
validation: Read the comment against the probe's table.

verdict.reason: I re-ran the Planocentric table. With clearance typed at 0, 0.01 and 0.02, running is 1.75418, 1.74418 and 1.73418, and sized_by is None. With 0.025, 0.03, 0.05 or 0.1 typed, the clearance comes out at 0.02, running stays at 1.73418 and sized_by is Some(0), with no note. On this internal mesh the reported clearance is nominal − running (the DistanceReport doc says 'signed as the mesh reads it'). When the tips hold the running distance open, the clearance they allow is a ceiling: anything typed above it is cut to it. The comment at mod.rs:7985-7990 names this very Planocentric case and calls the clearance 'a floor the mesh clears'. That would hold for an external mesh, where a wider running distance means more clearance, but not for the case it describes. The 'runs wider than its clearance asks' part is correct.
verdict.evidence: Probe bin /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-last-2/src/bin/ten.rs. Output: 'clr typed 0.03: ... nominal [1.75418] running 1.73418 clearance 0.02000 sized_by Some(0) notes []'. My honour sweep also shows Clearance(0) on Planocentric as the only given input whose nudge does not reach the solve.
verdict.proposal_note: The wording should cover both signs. For example: 'the tips hold the running distance open, so a clearance that would close it further is not reached: on an internal mesh like this one the clearance cannot exceed what the tips leave'. The better fix still stands: once the replaced clearance raises a note (finding 10), assert the note instead of skipping.

title: Relief has more than one fixed point for the same input: which inputs stay given is decided by the order freedoms() lists the groups
claim: For the same pinned shape and the same `just`, relieving with the groups in reverse order gives a different set of given inputs in 173 of 322 cases over every preset. The reversed result is also accepted unchanged by the declared-order relief. So the per-group counts do not determine a unique answer, and the thickness-mod and distance groups' precedence is set implicitly by their position in the Vec. relief_is_idempotent_from_any_start cannot see this, because it only uses the declared order.
evidence: A worktree test (removed after the run) copied relieved() with gs.reverse(): 'TOTAL 322 DIFFS 173 NONCONV 0', every diff 'rev stable fwd? true'. Example on preset index 1: the reversed order leaves Member(0, ThicknessMod) given where the declared order relieves it. Output: /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-train-mod-a-2/group_order.txt.
proposal: Either state group order as part of the declared precedence (document it in freedoms() and add a law that pins it), or move to a global resolution (a matching over all relations, as finding 2 proposes) whose result is invariant under group permutation. Add that invariance as a law.
validation: A test that relieves with freedoms() in several permutations and asserts equal toggles. It fails at HEAD and passes after a global resolution.

verdict.reason: I reproduced the dependence on group order independently. Starting from every toggle pinned, over every_arrangement() and every `just`, reversing the group Vec changes the given set in 237 of 393 cases. Every reversed result is accepted unchanged by declared-order relief. Part of the framing needs correcting. Dependence on declared order is intended: settle's comment says 'the answer depends on the order the *shape* declares', so the precedence is declared, not accidental. What is left undocumented is the order between groups. The doc heading of relieved ('Settled, whatever order the groups come in') is only claimed and tested for settling, never for which answer is reached. Two facts go beyond the finding. (a) In 200 of the 237 differing cases the declared order keeps fewer given inputs than an alternative it accepts itself. On a solved-and-pinned start, Planetary keeps 10 given against 12 reversed, Compound 16 against 18, Idler 12 against 13 and Crossed 8 against 9, and nudging each extra input still moves the solve. So the greedy walk relieves inputs a designer gave that did not need relieving. (b) Not every reversed fixed point is legitimate. The ThicknessMod rows (the Idler's Member(0, ThicknessMod), MeshedPlanets) come from the thickness groups being declared per mesh while the relation runs along the whole mesh chain. A state that is actually over-determined passes every group's count. See the missed finding.
verdict.evidence: Worktree test zz_group_order_probe (removed): 'TOTAL 393 DIFFS 237 fwd-keeps-fewer 200 rev-keeps-fewer 3'; 'DIFF 1 Parallel None: fwd-only [] rev-only [Member(0, ThicknessMod)] rev-stable true'. Worktree test zz_rev_honoured_probe: 'P5 rev false: given 10 unhonoured []', 'P5 rev true: given 12 unhonoured []', 'P7 rev false: given 16', 'P7 rev true: given 18 unhonoured []'.
verdict.proposal_note: First fix the ThicknessMod declaration (one group per mesh group with given_at_most 1, as for the module; see the missed finding). This removes the illegitimate fixed points. Then pick one of two options: (1) declare inter-group precedence explicitly and pin it with a law; or (2) resolve globally, relieving a minimum set of inputs, ties broken by the declared least-precious order. That makes the result invariant under permutation of the groups and stops over-relief. A law for it: under every permutation of freedoms(), the same toggles, and no given input relieved whose restoration leaves every group within its limits.

title: backlash_at feeds three precomputed values through Backlash::banded by faking a distance band and decoding its sign
claim: The path backlash already has its three values (row_play at minus, running and plus). To reuse banded's min/max it calls `Backlash::banded(0.0, 1.0, 1.0, |t| ...)` and decodes `t < 0 → 0, t > 0 → 2, else 1` back into an array index. `at_band` in shape.rs does the same sign decode a second time. The nominal of 0 and the band of ±1 are not distances; they are an encoding of an index.
evidence: mod.rs:3468-3476: `Backlash::banded(0.0, 1.0, 1.0, |t| { let band = if t < 0.0 { 0 } else if t > 0.0 { 2 } else { 1 }; ...`. shape.rs:3549-3558: `at_band` maps the sign of t to -tolerance_minus, +tolerance_plus or 0. shape.rs:3811: `let row_play = [-1.0, 0.0, 1.0].map(|t| play_of(k, at_band(k, t)));`.
proposal: Add `Backlash::of_ends([lo, mid, hi]: [f64; 3]) -> Backlash` (nominal = mid, min and max over the three). `banded` becomes `Self::of_ends([angular(n - minus), angular(n), angular(n + plus)])`, and backlash_at becomes `Backlash::of_ends(std::array::from_fn(|band| row_play.iter().enumerate().map(|(k, p)| coefficient(k, read, from) * p[band]).sum::<f64>().to_degrees()))`. In shape.rs, write row_play as `[-tol_minus, 0, tol_plus].map(|dx| play_of(k, running + dx))` and remove `at_band`'s sign decode.
validation: cargo nextest run: backlash_at_the_two_ends_differs_by_exactly_the_total_ratio and the planetary backlash tests; check_golden unchanged.

verdict.reason: The code does what the finding says. backlash_at calls Backlash::banded(0.0, 1.0, 1.0, …) purely to get three evaluations at t = -1, 0, +1, then turns the sign of t back into an index 0/1/2. at_band in shape.rs turns the sign back into a tolerance a second time, and it is only ever called with the literals [-1.0, 0.0, 1.0]. The nominal 0 and the band of ±1 are not distances. Nothing else is behind the encoding: banded has only two callers (mod.rs:3468 and shape.rs:3567).
verdict.evidence: mod.rs:162-173 banded evaluates angular(nominal-minus), angular(nominal), angular(nominal+plus) and takes min/max over the three. mod.rs:3467-3483 is the fake band with `let band = if t < 0.0 {0} else if t > 0.0 {2} else {1}`. shape.rs:3549-3558 is at_band's sign decode. shape.rs:3811 is `[-1.0, 0.0, 1.0].map(|t| play_of(k, at_band(k, t)))`. grep for `banded(` finds exactly these two call sites.
verdict.proposal_note: Adopt of_ends as proposed. One addition: coefficient(k, read, from) runs a play solve on the whole system, and the current closure calls it inside each band, so it runs 3x per mesh. The proposed std::array::from_fn form keeps that triple cost. Compute the M coefficients once per (read, from) and dot them with each band column instead. In shape.rs, pass the tolerances straight in: `[-d.tolerance_minus, 0.0, d.tolerance_plus].map(|dx| play_of(k, running + dx))`.

title: docs/rationale.md says TrainError's Display is kept 'for Debug', but Debug is derived; std::error::Error is what needs Display
claim: The rationale gives the wrong reason for keeping English in gear-core. `Debug` is `#[derive(Debug)]` and never calls Display. What forces a Display impl is `impl std::error::Error for TrainError/MeshError/MeasurementError`. That changes the decision: Display is required but can be language-free (the note's key), so rule 2 needs no exception.
evidence: docs/rationale.md:59-61: 'Their `Display` impls remain, for the CLI and for `Debug`'. mod.rs:1790 `impl std::error::Error for TrainError {}`. The CLI already renders notes through gear_io::strings::Catalogue::english() (gear-cli main.rs:281).
proposal: Rewrite the sentence to say that Display exists because std::error::Error requires it and prints the note's key, and that the CLI renders errors through the English catalogue like any other note. Pair this with finding 14's change.
validation: check_doc_links; a reading pass.

verdict.corrected_claim: The claim that Display exists 'for Debug' is wrong: TrainError is #[derive(Clone, Debug, ...)] (mod.rs:1559), so Debug never calls Display, and the same doc comment appears on the Display impls at mod.rs:1709 and mesh.rs:764. The claim that Display exists 'for the CLI' is true and load-bearing, and there the finding is wrong. The CLI prints errors through `{e}` (Display) at about 20 sites, for example main.rs:1929 'train did not solve: {e}' and 3337 'why it stops: z_ring {ring}: {e}'. The golden corpus records that English: tools/golden/planetary_17_17_3.txt:14 and kinematics.txt:1466/1475 carry 'no profile shift brings the meshes to one axis distance; these tooth counts cannot be assembled'. The words() Catalogue::english helper at main.rs:282 exists, but errors do not go through it. So a key-only Display would change the CLI's output and the golden corpus, and the CLI's error sites would have to render e.note() through the catalogue first.
verdict.reason: Half of the stated reason is false (Debug) and half is true (CLI). The finding also misstates what the CLI does today.
verdict.evidence: mod.rs:1559 #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum TrainError. mod.rs:1709 '/// English, for the CLI and for `Debug`.' mesh.rs:764, the same. gear-cli main.rs:709, 1238, 1468, 1630, 1658, 1697, 1742, 1767, 1929, 3186, 3301, 3337, 3385, 3508 all format `{e}`. The three golden lines above are English error text.
verdict.proposal_note: Minimal fix: drop 'and for `Debug`' from rationale.md:60 and from the doc comments on the Display impls (mod.rs:1709, mesh.rs:764, and the matching metrology/edits ones), and say std::error::Error requires Display. To remove the rule-2 exception outright, first move every CLI `{e}` on an error to words().render(&e.note()) or the equivalent, then make Display print the key. check_golden should stay byte-identical if the catalogue's English matches today's Display text. Where it does not, that is a finding in its own right: two English texts for one error.

title: reference.md says a set's clearance is always given and pinned by relief; the code and the test say otherwise
claim: docs/reference.md:420-426 says a planetary set's clearance 'is always given ... So the set has modes 1 and 3 and not mode 2, and its clearance toggle, alone in its own freedom group with none allowed automatic, is pinned back by relief.' The test an_epicyclic_kinds_clearance_is_pinned_back_whatever_was_touched states the opposite for a set: 'the set has the pair's rule now: touching the clearance pins the distance'. Relief does leave a set's clearance automatic with the distance given. That is mode 2, the state behind finding shape-a[4].
evidence: mod.rs:8153-8160 doc comment ('A set used to pin its clearance whatever was touched ... the set has the pair's rule now') and its assertion 'the clearance just touched is spared'. Run in a worktree: planetary(12,30,72,3) with clearance {auto:true, manual:0.3}, relieved(Some(Freedom::Clearance(0))) gives distance {auto:false}, clearance {auto:true, manual:0.3}. The test's name also contradicts its body for the set: the clearance is not pinned 'whatever was touched'.
proposal: Rewrite reference.md:420-426 to describe the current rule: at most one of the distance and its clearance is automatic, the one just touched is spared, and a hula's clearance is pinned regardless. Once shape-a[4] is fixed, add what an automatic clearance on a multi-mesh distance means (one derived clearance shared by every mesh). Rename the test so its name matches its body, e.g. 'a_distance_and_its_clearance_are_never_both_automatic'.
validation: tools/check_doc_links.py still passes; re-read the paragraph against relieved() on planetary and hula shapes.

verdict.reason: reference.md:420-425 says a set's clearance 'is always given ... So the set has modes 1 and 3 and not mode 2 ... is pinned back by relief'. The shipped test says the opposite, and it passes on the baseline, which is 679/679 green. After relieved(Some(Freedom::Clearance(0))) on a planetary set it asserts `d.clearance.auto && !d.distance.auto`, 'the clearance just touched is spared'. That is mode 2. The test's own doc comment says 'A set used to pin its clearance whatever was touched ... the set has the pair's rule now'. The test's name ('..._is_pinned_back_whatever_was_touched') is true only of the hula half of its body.
verdict.evidence: docs/reference.md:420-425 (quoted above). crates/gear-core/src/train/mod.rs:8155-8164 is the doc comment. mod.rs:8184-8188 is `if just == Some(Freedom::Clearance(0)) { assert!(d.clearance.auto && !d.distance.auto, "the clearance just touched is spared") }`. The test is in the passing baseline suite.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposal is right. Also check whether the modes 1/2/3 enumeration earlier in that section still names mode 2 as unavailable to a set anywhere else. The replacement text should state what one automatic clearance means on a distance with two meshes (the sun–planet and planet–ring gaps).

title: A crossed pair whose contact has slid off the face reports the unbounded path: ε jumps from 0.18 to 1.64 as Σ falls through ~0.5°
claim: When the face-bounded zone closes entirely, CrossedPath::limited_by_face returns None. That happens because the contact has slid bodily along the shafts, roughly Δa/sin Σ, off a centred face. Both the report (`.unwrap_or((*path, ZoneLimit::Face))`) and PointBuilt::zone (`.map_or(*path, ...)`) then fall back to the unbounded tip-to-tip path. The pair reports its full contact ratio, efficiency and pressure exactly when the model says the teeth do not meet on the face. The comment just above says the opposite: 'No zone at all is a contact ratio of nought'. The result is a discontinuity and an optimistic wrong answer.
evidence: crossed([20,40],σ).with_first_helix(15), 10 mm faces, instrumented limited_by_face. At σ = 0.45° the zone is [-4.15, 0.69] with face centres 26.2/27.0 mm, so lo 5.86 > hi 0.69 and the zone is closed; the report still reads ε 1.63867, η 0.985108, p_max 1754.7. At σ = 0.5623°, lo 0.48 < hi 1.02, bounded: ε 0.18185, η 0.975675, p_max 1633.5. At σ = 0.6°: ε 0.67290. At σ ≥ 0.7°: 1.638 (not face-limited). It is the same with 17/43 (dip at 0.57-0.63°) and with 20/40 at β 30° (dip at 0.45-0.57°). Below the dip every σ down to 5.6e-4° reports ε 1.639 with the face-bounded zone closed (σ = 0.01°: centres 1176/1177 mm).
proposal: When limited_by_face returns None, report contact_ratio 0 with ZoneLimit::Face, as the comment intends, and raise MESH_CONTACT_RATIO_BELOW_ONE. Have PointBuilt::zone return None as well, so the efficiency and the rating do not integrate over a path that is not on the face; the rating needs a defined answer for no contact, which could be a refusal or a note. Separately, ask whether centring the face on the axial_centre at the reference distance is the right convention for a clearance-opened crossed pair near parallel.
validation: A sweep of σ over (0, 5]° asserting that the reported ε equals limited_by_face's length/p_bn, or 0 when it is None, and that ε never rises as σ decreases while ZoneLimit is Face.

verdict.reason: Reproduced independently in a worktree test: crossed([20,40],σ).with_first_helix(15) with 10 mm faces, solved through solve_alone. The reported contact ratio is the unbounded tip-to-tip value, marked limited_by Face, for every σ below about 0.56° down to 0.01°. It then drops to 0.18 at σ=0.5623°, rises through 0.67 (0.6°) and 1.22 (0.65°), and returns to 1.638 marked Tips at 0.7°. It is non-monotone and discontinuous, and the optimistic side is the one reached as σ→0. Code: mod.rs:2714-2719 falls back to `.unwrap_or((*path, ZoneLimit::Face))`, and PointBuilt::zone (shape.rs:2500-2504) falls back to `.map_or(*path, ...)`. So the efficiency and the rating also integrate over the full path. The comment at mod.rs:2711-2713 says 'No zone at all is a contact ratio of nought', which only the p.path == None branch honours. limited_by_face documents None as 'the teeth never meet on it' (screw.rs:920-921).
verdict.evidence: My run printed 'sigma 0.5: eps 1.63861 eta 0.985101 lim Some(Face) notes []', 'sigma 0.5623: eps 0.18185 eta 0.975675 lim Some(Face) notes [mesh.contact_ratio_below_one]', 'sigma 0.6: eps 0.67290', 'sigma 0.65: eps 1.22023', 'sigma 0.7: eps 1.63835 lim Some(Tips)', 'sigma 0.01: eps 1.63925 lim Some(Face) notes []'. My p_max values differ from the finding's (for example 554.9 vs 1754.7) because of a different load and library. The ε and η figures match the finding to 5 digits. The diff is at /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-last-3/worktree.diff.
verdict.proposal_note: Returning ε = 0 fixes the lie, but the answer stays discontinuous in the other direction: ε is 1.64 at 0.7° and 0 at 0.5° with the teeth never meeting. The deeper question is the one the proposal raises last: the zone slides about Δa/sin Σ along the shafts, and the faces are held centred at the reference-distance axial_centre. At σ→0 with a clearance-opened distance, that convention puts the contact metres off the face (the finding measured centres at 1176 mm at σ=0.01°), which is not physical for a pair a designer has aligned. Decide the face-centring convention first, for example centring the faces on the operating contact, which is where a real pair is assembled. Then no-contact becomes a genuine limit and not an artefact. For a real no-zone, prefer a refusal or a note over rating a path that does not exist.

title: A crossed pair with a spur first member is refused (WormTooThin) at exactly β₁ = 0 but solves at β₁ = 1e-6°
claim: Screw::new refuses when sin γ₁ = z·m/d ≥ 1. A spur first member has d = z·m exactly, so sin γ₁ = 1 and the pair is refused with WormTooThin. A spur gear crossed with a helical gear at Σ = β₂ is an ordinary crossed helical pair, and the model solves it smoothly at any β₁ > 0. The refusal is a point discontinuity at the most natural value a designer would type, and its key describes a worm.
evidence: Worktree run of crossed([17,43],20°).with_first_helix(b): b = 0 gives Err(Screw(WormTooThin)); b = 1e-6 gives ε 1.61635, η 0.964013, p_max 2886.7, a 31.405478; b = 1e-3 gives identical figures. With b = 0 every σ in (0, 60]° is refused (2000 of 2000 in the sweep).
proposal: Make the bound strict (sin γ₁ > 1 refused), or parametrise the first member by its helix rather than its lead so γ₁ = 90° is a regular value. Check what the downstream uses of lead_angle_rad do at 90° (axial_module = m/cos γ, which is effectively infinite for a spur 'worm'), and keep axial_module out of any figure reported for a non-worm crossed pair.
validation: A law: for every crossed arrangement, the figures at β₁ = 0 equal the limit β₁ → 0⁺ to 1e-9.

verdict.corrected_claim: The discontinuity is real, and it spans β₁ up to about 1e-8°, not only exactly 0. β₁ = 1e-9° is also refused, because cos β₁ rounds to 1.0 and sin γ₁ = 1. It is a deliberate and documented refusal: crossed.rs:1160-1165 argues 'a spur gear is not a screw, and it has no lead', and TrainError's Display for WormTooThin (mod.rs:1723-1730) tells the designer 'a zero helix makes it a spur gear ... put the helical member first and the spur one second'. So the claim that the key 'describes a worm' is overstated: the English message names this case and its workaround. The argument behind the decision still does not hold on the merits. The pair's physics has a smooth limit, and the limit is the swapped pair: [17,43] at β₁=1e-6° gives ε 1.61635, and [43,17] at β₁=20° gives the identical ε 1.61635. Only the first member's worm-only quantities, lead and axial_module, go infinite. The workaround also swaps which member is first, which changes the drive direction: η 0.964013 vs 0.964909.
verdict.reason: The measured discontinuity is confirmed, and the decision is documented. Its reasoning (no lead, so no model) confuses a reported worm quantity with the pair model: every figure the pair reports is continuous into β₁=0. Rule 5 says to refuse only input that describes no shape, and a spur gear crossed with a helical one is an ordinary cuttable shape.
verdict.evidence: My worktree run on crossed([17,43],20°) printed 'beta 0: err Screw(WormTooThin)', 'beta 1e-9: err Screw(WormTooThin)', 'beta 1e-6: eps 1.61635 eta 0.964013 lim Tips', 'beta 1e-3: eps 1.61635 eta 0.964013', and for crossed([43,17],20°).with_first_helix(20): 'eps 1.61635 eta 0.964909'. screw.rs:229-232 is `if sin_gamma_1 >= 1.0 { return Err(ScrewError::WormTooThin) }`. The test crossed.rs:1188-1195 asserts the refusal, so the proposal must replace that test.
verdict.proposal_note: Making the bound strict (> 1) would let lead and axial_module come out as inf. Serde would then emit null, or a NaN would appear downstream, and a_crossed_axis_spur_pair_puts_the_spur_member_second asserts both are finite. Better: carry the first member's helix and not the lead as the primitive (γ₁ = 90° − β₁ with cos γ₁ = sin β₁ exact), report lead and axial_module as Option (None for a non-worm member, where the fields mean nothing), and replace the refusal test with the limit law the finding proposes. It should hold that [z1,z2] at β₁=0 has the same ε and p_max as [z2,z1] at β₁=Σ.

title: An absorbed sun or ring shift is capped at the admissible range and refused with a false message, while a planet absorber or a reaching shift is not
claim: When the absorber is in only one of the two meshes, absorb's bracket has one infinite side. It then falls back to the member's admissible profile-shift range (or a hard-coded +/-5). A needed shift outside that range makes absorb return None, and the whole solve is refused with 'no profile shift brings the meshes to one axis distance; these tooth counts cannot be assembled', although a shift that closes the set exists and the tooth counts assemble. A planet absorber is bracketed only by the involute domain, and the reaches branch explicitly lets a shift past the cutter's reach through to be clamped and noted. The same physical question is therefore answered by refusal or by clamp depending on which member absorbs. That breaks rule 5 (clamp rather than refuse, and say so) and makes the solve jump from a result to an error as a given shift moves continuously.
evidence: Worktree test (diff at /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-shape-a-3/worktree.diff) on planetary(12,30,72,3), sun and planet given at settled+dx, ring automatic. At dx=0.6 the ring gets x=1.8111 and the train solves. At dx=0.7 the closed form gives a ring x of 2.1125, at which the planet-ring mesh runs at 22.300774, equal to the sun-planet distance. But the ring's admissible range is -2.130..1.942, so absorb returns None, and solve_alone errs 'no profile shift brings the meshes to one axis distance; these tooth counts cannot be assembled'. It is identical at dx 0.8 to 2.0.
proposal: Compute a one-mesh absorber's shift in closed form (target = running_of(other mesh), nominal via kind.nominal_of, sum via shift_sum_reaching, then x_i = x_i + (sum - shift_sum)/coefficient), with no admissible-range cap. Let the member builder clamp and note an out-of-range shift, as it does for reaching shifts. Keep the bracketed Newton for a member in both meshes, bracketed by the involute domain only, and delete the +/-5 fallback. If refusing past the admissible range is kept deliberately, it should instead apply to every absorber and reaching shift alike, with a refusal key that names the shift limit and not 'these tooth counts cannot be assembled'.
validation: A test sweeping the sun and planet given shifts upward on planetary(12,30,72,3) with the ring absorbing. The solve must succeed (with a clamp note once past the range), and the residual between the two meshes' running distances must stay < 1e-9 until the involute domain ends. check_golden must be unchanged on the presets, where the closed form agrees with the Newton to 5e-15.

verdict.corrected_claim: The finding is confirmed as stated, and the refusal starts earlier than it reported: at dx = 0.65 (the needed ring x is about 1.96, above the admissible max 1.942), not 0.7. The same ring shift, given and not absorbed, solves with clamp notes. With the sun at settled+0.7, ring x = 2.1 and the planet absorbing, the solve succeeds with clamp.ring_space_capped, and ring x = 2.5 adds ring_space_closed and cutter_no_tip_corner. So the clamp-and-note route the proposal relies on already exists downstream. The refusal message 'these tooth counts cannot be assembled' is false here, since the same tooth counts assemble at other shifts. The same text also closes the golden planetary sweep (planetary_17_17_3.txt:14). That case is a planet absorber with a finite involute bracket, so it is not this fault, but the wording overclaims there too: only the planet's shift was free.
verdict.reason: Reproduced in a worktree. With a one-mesh absorber, one side of the bracket is infinite, so absorb falls back to admissible_ranges (or the literal ±5) at shape.rs:1470-1477 and returns None past it. closed() then propagates None, and the error reads as non-assembly. A planet absorber (both meshes, finite involute bracket) and a sun absorber at the same dx solve. So does a given out-of-range ring shift, with clamps. The same physical question gets a refusal or a clamp depending on the role. This breaks rule 5 and makes the solve jump from a result to an error.
verdict.evidence: Output of planetary(12,30,72,3) with the sun and planet given at settled+dx and the ring automatic: 'dx 0.6: ok x [0.898, 0.430, 1.8111]', 'dx 0.65: err no profile shift brings the meshes to one axis distance; these tooth counts cannot be assembled', the same error at 0.7, 1 and 2. The ring's admissible range is -2.1304..1.9421. 'ring given 2.1, planet absorbs: ok ... ["clamp.ring_space_capped"]'. The diff is at /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-last-3/worktree.diff.
verdict.proposal_note: The closed form for a one-mesh absorber is right. It is the same sum-to-shift step the reaches branch already does (shape.rs:1351-1389), so share that code and do not write a third copy. Once both-mesh brackets come only from the involute domain, the ±5 literal has no reachable use: check that a member in both meshes always gets two finite bounds (external sum_z>0 gives lo, internal sum_z<0 gives hi) before deleting it. Separately, have the refusal key for absorb returning None name the member whose shift was sought, not 'these tooth counts'.

title: An automatic thickness coefficient between two given ones depends on the order of the mesh list
claim: thickness_mods propagates a given k mesh by mesh, and the first mesh in list order to reach an unset member decides it. Relief allows one given k per mesh, not per group, so a member between two given ones is legal after relief. Its k then depends on how the meshes happen to be ordered in the file or the edit history. The same graph builds different teeth.
evidence: Worktree test: line(&[20,30,25]) with k0=1.2 and k2=1.1 given, relieved(None), keeps both. thickness_mods() = [1.2, 0.8, 1.1]; with s.meshes.reverse() it is [1.2, 0.9, 1.1].
proposal: Make the thickness freedom one group per mesh group (given_at_most 1, as for module), so a given k fixes its whole connected run and propagation has a unique answer. Correct Member::thickness_mod's doc to match.
validation: A law over every preset and a line fixture: permuting the order of shape.meshes (with indices remapped) leaves thickness_mods and every built gear unchanged; relief never leaves two given k in one mesh group.

verdict.reason: Reproduced through the public API. Relief keeps both given k because each thickness FreedomGroup covers one mesh with given_at_most 1 (shape.rs:4088-4097), and thickness_mods (shape.rs:1047-1077) lets the first mesh in list order decide the middle member. The finding also understates the effect: in the forward order mesh 1-2 comes out as (0.8, 1.1), and those do not sum to 2. That breaks the invariant stated in Member::thickness_mod's doc (shape.rs:172-176) and in docs/state.md:764-770, which says a pair off the rule 'is not offered, and relief keeps the pair on the rule'. So the same graph builds different teeth depending on mesh order, and one mesh always breaks the rule the model depends on (corrections.md:378 relies on k1+k2=2 to argue that thinning adds no play). It is reachable from the panel: give k on both end gears of a three-gear line.
verdict.evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-last-4: line(&[20,30,25]) with k0=Auto::fixed(1.2) and k2=Auto::fixed(1.1), then relieved(None). Given flags after relief: [(false,1.2),(true,1.0),(false,1.1)], so both stay given. thickness_mods() gives [1.2, 0.8, 1.1]; with meshes.reverse() it gives [1.2, 0.9, 1.1]. The existing test one_thickness_modification_satisfies_both_invariants (shape.rs:5364) only ever sets one given k per set, so it cannot catch this.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposal is right: one thickness FreedomGroup per mesh group, given_at_most 1 and order = every member of the group, which mirrors the module group at shape.rs:4103ff. Then propagation from the single given k is unique on any tree, and on any cycle whose rule is consistent. Add a law that every mesh satisfies its rule after relief (k_a + k_b = 2 for external, k_a = k_b for internal), not only that permuting the meshes changes nothing. Permutation-invariance alone would pass a rule that is broken the same way in every order.

title: A ring whose tip radius lies beyond its root radius is solved, drawn and exported as DXF with no refusal
claim: Ring::cut_by_at_virtual_z clamps rf down to rf_max (the space closure) and ra up to ra_min, each on its own, but never checks that ra < rf. At a large positive shift the tip radius passes the clamped root radius. solve_ring then returns ok, ring_profile returns an outline whose radii run from rf up to ra (inverted), and export_ring_dxf writes it. Rule 5 says to refuse input that describes no shape at all. The only signal is the clamp list, which is also present on shifts that do build.
evidence: Node probe against web/src/wasm (default cutter 20/1.25/0.2, m 1, alpha 20). z=60, x=5: tip_radius 34.000, root_radius 33.150, ring_profile radii 33.150..34.000, export_ring_dxf 29755 bytes, no throw. z=30, x=4: tip 18.000, root 17.803, DXF 9627 bytes. At z=60, x=4 the tooth height is 0.15 mm (tip 33.0, root 33.15), so the tooth degenerates continuously into nothing. The ring tests at ring.rs:1410-1433 and :2341 assert radii between ra and rf, which cannot catch ra > rf because the check is written in terms of the same two radii.
proposal: After both clamps in Ring::cut_by_at_virtual_z, refuse the part (or report an explicit catalogued clamp.ring_no_tooth and hold ra at rf) when ra >= rf. Better, derive the shift at which ra meets rf_max in closed form and expose it as the ring's upper shift bound in the ring ranges proposed for the gear tab. Add a law: over a sweep of z and x, every ring solve_ring accepts has ra < rf.
validation: The probe script is at /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-web-1/r2.mjs. After the fix, z=60 x=5 and z=30 x=4 are refused or flagged, and a gear-core test sweeping x in [-3, 6] for z in {20, 30, 60, 100} asserts ra < rf for every Ring built without refusal.

verdict.reason: Re-ran r2.mjs against the built web/src/wasm. Ring::cut_by_at_virtual_z clamps ra up to ra_min (ring.rs:301-304) and rf down to rf_max (ring.rs:399-404) separately, and nothing compares the two. At a large positive shift the space is capped, so rf stays fixed at rf_max while ra = r - m(h_a - x) keeps growing past it. solve_ring accepts the result, ring_profile returns an inverted radius band and export_ring_dxf writes it. The tooth height shrinks continuously to zero at z=60, x≈4.15, and there is no refusal at that point, so rule 5 ('refuse input that describes no shape at all') is broken. The clamps reported (space_capped, space_closed, cutter_no_tip_corner) are exactly the ones already present at x=2.5, where the ring does build, so nothing in them marks the degenerate case.
verdict.evidence: node verify-web-1/r2.mjs: '60 5 ra 34.000 rf 33.150 profile r 33.150 34.000 ... dxf 29755' and '30 4 ra 18.000 rf 17.803 ... dxf 9627'. At '60 4' ra is 33.000 against rf 33.150 (0.15 mm of tooth). Reading ring.rs:278-404 shows no ra<rf comparison between line 278 and the ShaperCut::new call.
verdict.proposal_note: Refuse rather than clamp once ra >= rf: there is no tooth left to clamp to, so this is the 'no shape at all' case. The crossing shift has a closed form: ra = rf_max gives x = h_a - (r - rf_max)/m, where rf_max comes from inv⁻¹(π/z - ψ_b) at the capped space. It can be exposed as the ring's upper shift bound. A minimum tooth height (for example the tip-to-root clearance of the mate) is a separate, user-visible question and should not be folded into this refusal.

title: corrections.md and F54 claim admissible_profile_shift already bounds a ring; measurement and state.md say otherwise
claim: corrections.md:559, repeating F54, says a ring's space 'takes the identical expression', so `admissible_profile_shift` already bounded it and 'there was never a second range to write'. state.md:634 says the rack's buildable range 'is not a ring's'. Measured, the external bound is independent of z here ([-2.130, 1.942] at z = 30, 60 and 100), while the ring's clamp-free window depends strongly on z. That makes corrections.md wrong and state.md right, and the gear tab currently acts on the wrong statement.
evidence: Node probe (r3.mjs): the ring is clamp-free (excluding ring_flank_ungenerated) on [-0.80, 1.94] at z=60, [0.10, 0.68] at z=30 and [-1.63, 1.94] at z=100. The external bound is [-2.130, 1.942] in all three cases. At z=60, x=-1.5 raises clamp.ring_tip_raised inside the 'bound'.
proposal: Correct corrections.md:559 so it says the space cap coincides with the rack's upper bound only where the ring's space is the binding limit, and that the lower end (the tip raised to the base or pointed circle) and small-z closure are the ring's own. Point it at the ring ranges the gear-tab finding proposes.
validation: check_doc_links.py still passes. Re-run r3.mjs as the evidence behind the corrected sentence.

verdict.corrected_claim: The part of corrections.md:559 (and F54) that concerns the space holds exactly: the ring's space cap and space raise sit on admissible_profile_shift's thickness bound. The overreach is 'admissible_profile_shift already bounded it and there was never a second range to write'. The ring has its own limits well inside that bound: the tip raised to the base or pointed circle, the space closing at the root, and the cutter losing its tip corner. They depend on z, and the doc handles them only as a post-cut clamp check. state.md:634 ('a rack's buildable range, which is not a ring's') is the accurate statement. The gear tab's shift note still shows, for a ring, the external undercut and pointed figures, which mean nothing for a ring.
verdict.reason: Swept the ring's shift in steps of 0.02 at z=30, 60 and 100 with the default 20-tooth cutter. clamp.ring_space_raised drops out at x=-2.12 (bound min -2.130) and clamp.ring_space_capped appears at x=1.96 (bound max 1.942), at every z, so the 'identical expression' statement holds. But clamp.ring_tip_raised or ring_space_closed fire up to x=-0.80 (z=60), +0.10 (z=30) and -1.62 (z=100), all inside the 'bound'. The finding's point that the external bound is independent of z is expected, because it is the normal-thickness bound. That point is not evidence against the doc; the ring-specific inner limits are. The same corrections row names the post-cut clamp check as the ring's own question, so the doc is internally aware of those limits. Its 'never a second range to write' contradicts state.md:634 and the tab's behaviour.
verdict.evidence: /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-last-4/r3b.mjs. z=30: -2.12 -> tip_raised,space_closed,fillet_gap; -0.58 -> tip_raised; 0.10 -> none; 1.96 -> space_capped. z=60: -0.80 -> none; 1.96 -> space_capped. z=100: -1.62 -> none; 1.96 -> space_capped. solve_gear bound = [-2.1304, 1.9421] at all three. GearPanel.svelte:91-93 uses shiftNote(result.ok.ranges.profile_shift) for the ring too (internal) and prints undercut -0.755 and pointed 1.622 for a 30-tooth ring.
verdict.proposal_note: Reword corrections.md:559 and audit.md's F54 paragraph (history, left as record but annotated): the thickness bound carries over exactly, and the ring's other limits (tip at the base or pointed circle, space closure, cutter tip corner) are its own. Point at the ring shift range once it exists, or at the clamp check that stands in for it. Separately, the gear tab should not print the external undercut and pointed clauses for a ring.

title: The adopt list's fallback makes a worm adoptable and loses role names when the train fails at the boundary
claim: memberRefs's doc says the names arrive whether or not the train solved. That is true of the core, which computes them before solving, but not of the boundary. When solveTrain's call throws (a NaN or a fractional count in the train), the fallback returns `names: []`. Every gear is then labelled 'Gear N', and `adoptable: names[index]?.role !== "worm"` evaluates to true for a worm, so a worm is offered for adoption, which the list otherwise refuses.
evidence: members.ts:82 `const names = solveTrain(train).names;` and L86 `adoptable: names[index]?.role !== "worm"`. core.ts:772-791 catch returns `names: []`. gear-wasm lib.rs:839 computes names from the shape alone.
proposal: Read names from a shape-only entry point (member_names). Or have memberRefs treat an absent name as not adoptable (`names[index] !== undefined && names[index].role !== "worm"`).
validation: Stub solve_train to throw: a worm member is not adoptable and its label is unchanged.

verdict.reason: The code is as described. memberRefs reads solveTrain(train).names, and solveTrain's catch returns names: []. `names[index]?.role !== "worm"` is then true for every member, so a worm option becomes enabled, and gearLabel falls back to 'Gear N'. Reachability is narrow: the catch fires only when the boundary breaks, a wasm panic or bad JSON, which core.ts:766-767 describes as 'nothing a designer typed'. A saved or imported train has passed serde, so a NaN or fractional count in tab state is unlikely. Choosing the worm then goes to adopt_member, which returns an error that the panel shows (workspace.adoptError). The harm is a mislabelled list with one wrong affordance. There is also a cost the finding did not name: memberRefs runs a full train solve for every open train tab on every GearPanel render (it is called both in the #each and in onchange), only to read names that need no solve.
verdict.evidence: web/src/members.ts:81-88; web/src/core.ts:768-791 (names: [] in the catch); crates/gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:839 computes names from req.train.shape.member_names() before solving; GearPanel.svelte:300,308 calls memberRefs(source.train) per train per render. No shape-only entry point exists among the 23.
verdict.proposal_note: The cheapest correct fix is `adoptable: names[index] !== undefined && names[index].role !== "worm"`, and disabling the optgroup when names is empty. Better, and it also removes the per-render solves: read the names from the train tab's already-computed outcome, which TrainPanel holds, or pass them in, instead of solving again in GearPanel. Adding a 24th wasm entry point only for names is not needed if the cached outcome is reused.

title: Viewport pan jumps under two-finger touch: pointer handlers ignore pointerId
claim: onDown, onMove and onUp keep a single dragging/lastX/lastY and never look at pointerId. With touch-action:none, a second finger's pointerdown resets lastX and lastY to its own position. Moves from the two fingers then alternate, so each delta is the distance between the fingers and the view jumps back and forth. Lifting either finger sets dragging=false while the other is still down.
evidence: Viewport.svelte:79-94: `function onDown(e){ dragging = true; lastX = e.clientX; lastY = e.clientY; ...setPointerCapture(e.pointerId) }`, `function onMove(e){ if(!dragging) return; view.panX += e.clientX - lastX; ... }`, `function onUp(){ dragging = false }`. There is no per-pointer state anywhere in the file. Line 212 is `touch-action: none`, so the browser passes both fingers through as pointer events.
proposal: Keep a Map<pointerId, {x,y}>. With one pointer, pan as now. With two, pan by the midpoint's motion and zoom through zoomAbout(midpoint, newSpan/oldSpan). On pointerup or pointercancel, delete that id and set dragging only when the map is empty. This also gives finding 19 the pinch zoom it asks for.
validation: Test by hand on a touch device, or with synthetic PointerEvents for two pointerIds in a browser test: two fingers moving apart must zoom about their midpoint without the pan jumping, and lifting one must leave a one-finger pan working.

verdict.reason: Viewport.svelte keeps a single dragging/lastX/lastY and never looks at pointerId. With touch-action:none (line 212) a second finger's pointerdown resets lastX/lastY to that finger's position. The first finger's next move then jumps the pan by the distance between the fingers, and the moves keep alternating. onUp for either finger ends the drag for both. There is no pinch zoom either (only onWheel), so a touch user cannot zoom at all. It is a desktop-first tool, which is why the severity is low.
verdict.evidence: Viewport.svelte:79-94 (onDown sets lastX=e.clientX with no id check; onMove adds e.clientX-lastX; onUp sets dragging=false); lines 182-186 bind pointerdown/move/up/cancel to these; line 212 touch-action: none.
verdict.proposal_note: The pointerId map with midpoint pan and zoomAbout(midpoint, span ratio) is the right fix. Also delete the id on pointercancel and lostpointercapture, and re-seed the remaining pointer's last position when the count drops from two to one, so lifting a finger does not jump the view either.

title: A gear on a body the train does not list is refused with the wrong reason (overdetermined) rather than as an unknown body
claim: Setting shape.members[i].body to a body absent from shape.bodies does not panic, but solve_train comes back with failure error.train_overdetermined {body: 1}. That names a real body and a wrong cause. held=[99], by contrast, gives error.train_no_such_body {body: 99}. import_train accepts such a file without complaint.
evidence: notes/verify-wasm-boundary-1/t0.mjs: 'member body 99 solve_train ok {"result":null,"failure":{"note":{"key":"error.train_overdetermined","values":{"body":"1"}}...' and 'member body 99 import ok'. graph.rs:266 axis_of_body returns None for the unlisted body, so the member silently gets no axis.
proposal: Include member.body in the Shape::validate() that finding 0 proposes, refusing with error.train_no_such_body naming the member's body. Until then, make axis_of_body's None for a member an explicit refusal rather than a filter_map drop.
validation: Law: for every preset, set each member's body to max_body+1. Solve must fail with error.train_no_such_body carrying that number, and import_train must refuse.

verdict.reason: Re-ran t0.mjs: member body 99 gives error.train_overdetermined naming body 1, which is a real body and the wrong cause, while held=[99] gives error.train_no_such_body 99, and import_train accepts the file. In graph.rs:267-268 axis_of_body returns None for a body the shape does not list, so the member silently gets no axis in its part. The unknown-body check in conditions.rs covers only holds (and loads), not members. The refusal is misleading but it is still a refusal, so nothing wrong is built, which keeps the severity low.
verdict.evidence: node verify-wasm-boundary-1/t0.mjs: 'member body 99 solve_train ok {"result":null,"failure":{"note":{"key":"error.train_overdetermined","values":{"body":"1"}}' / 'member body 99 import ok' / 'held 99 ... error.train_no_such_body ... 99'. graph.rs:267-268 `self.bodies.iter().find(|b| b.body == body).map(|b| b.axis)`; conditions.rs:425-426 returns MotionError::NoSuchBody for holds only.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposal is fine. A single Shape::validate at deserialisation (import_train and the wasm request) and at the top of solve_train should check every index a shape carries: member.body in bodies, body.axis < axes.len(), mesh a/b < members.len(), distance axes. It should refuse with train_no_such_body or a sibling key, so a hand-edited file fails with the right reason.

title: A continuous duty's 1000 h seed is a bare literal with no constructor, while the intermittent duty has one
claim: Train::set_duty(case, false) switches a case to `Duty::Continuous { runtime_hours: 1000.0 }`, written inline in production code. The intermittent default has a named, documented constructor (`Duty::intermittent`: 1000 sweeps of 25°), but the continuous one has neither a name nor a reason. edit_train's doc says a duty is 'seeded as a fresh case's is', yet a fresh case is always intermittent, so this 1000 h has no counterpart. The same literal is repeated in gear-cli (kinematics.rs:58, graph.rs:58, main.rs:1331, 1894) and in gear-io's round-trip fixture.
evidence: sed -n 1148-1165 crates/gear-core/src/train/conditions.rs shows `super::Duty::Continuous { runtime_hours: 1000.0 }`. grep -rn 'runtime_hours: 1000.0' crates finds 6 sites, and no `fn continuous` exists on Duty.
proposal: Add `pub const fn continuous() -> Self` on Duty, or a `DEFAULT_RUNTIME_HOURS` const beside Duty::intermittent's figures, with a doc line saying what 1000 h is, and call it from set_duty and the CLI.
validation: grep finds no production `runtime_hours: 1000.0` outside the constructor. A test asserts that set_duty(i, false) yields Duty::continuous().

verdict.reason: set_duty writes Duty::Continuous { runtime_hours: 1000.0 } inline. Duty has a constructor for intermittent but none for continuous. Its doc says it is seeded 'from the same numbers a fresh case starts with', and gear-wasm's edit_train says 'as a fresh case's is', but a fresh case is always intermittent, so the 1000 h matches nothing. The literal is repeated at five more sites. The intermittent default has a name but no reason either ('a thousand sweeps of 25°'), so a single named, documented source is the real fix for both.
verdict.evidence: conditions.rs:1144-1165 (the doc ends '...or a thousand hours'; the code at 1161-1163 is `super::Duty::Continuous { runtime_hours: 1000.0 }`). mod.rs:2763-2774 has `pub const fn intermittent(at)` and no continuous counterpart. grep 'runtime_hours: 1000' gives conditions.rs:1162, gear-io/src/train.rs:496, gear-cli kinematics.rs:58, graph.rs:58, main.rs:1331 and 1894, plus the mod.rs:10582 test. gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:1527 says 'seeded as a fresh case's is'.
verdict.proposal_note: Add `Duty::continuous()` (or a `DEFAULT_RUNTIME_HOURS` const) beside `intermittent`, with one doc line saying the figure is a placeholder seed and not a design life. Rewrite set_duty's and edit_train's docs so they no longer claim a fresh case's numbers for the continuous branch.

title: Commanded-distance readout flags floating-point noise as interference
claim: At tiny eccentricities the sinusoid_backlash lower value is round-off, about -6e-15 mm. The panel marks any value below 0 with class:warn and the note 'negative is interference, not slack', so pure noise is shown as a warning.
evidence: notes/verify-wasm-boundary-3/c.mjs: angular_shift=1e-12 with a 43-tooth mate gives sinusoid_backlash[0] = -5.77e-15 mm and sinusoid_error 3.55e-15 mm. GearPanel.svelte: `<span class:warn={p.sinusoid_backlash[0] < 0}>`.
proposal: Have the core decide whether the crank's backlash is interference, using a tolerance tied to the precision the profile is computed at (e.g. a few ulps of the mean distance), and return it as a flag or a Note. TypeScript then compares nothing: rule 1 applies, since the < 0 test is an engineering decision made in the UI.
validation: At angular_shift 1e-12 no warning is shown. At 0.001 with a real negative backlash (e.g. -5.8e-8 mm, far above noise) the warning still shows.

verdict.reason: Reproduced exactly: at angular_shift 1e-12 the core returns sinusoid_backlash[0] = -5.77e-15 mm and the panel sets class:warn on `< 0`. But the sign itself is not noise. Any eccentric gear with a least-squares sinusoid fit has a residual of both signs, so the true minimum is negative, about amplitude² ≈ 1e-24 mm here. The test at gear.rs:2022 asserts lower < 0 < upper for exactly this reason. What is noise is the magnitude, about 1e10 times the true value, from cancellation in 2·fit·(inv α_actual − inv α_ideal). So the warning is formally right about the sign and wrong about how much there is. A 1e-12 angular shift is not a realistic input, and the displayed value rounds to 0 µm.
verdict.evidence: Re-ran notes/verify-wasm-boundary-3/c.mjs. a=1e-12 gives amplitude 1.0006e-12, sinusoid_error 3.55e-15, sinusoid_backlash[0] -5.77e-15. a=0.001 gives a real negative value. gear.rs:976-1002 is the play loop, and gear.rs:2022 asserts the two-sided sign. GearPanel.svelte:780: `<span class:warn={p.sinusoid_backlash[0] < 0}>`.
verdict.corrected_claim: At negligible eccentricity the reported crank backlash is round-off in magnitude, though its sign (negative) is mathematically correct. The panel's `< 0` warning therefore fires on a value that displays as zero.
verdict.proposal_note: Better: in the core, compute j from (ideal − fit) directly, e.g. a first-order form in the difference or a cancellation-free inv difference, so the magnitude is right. Then have the core flag interference only above a stated resolution, or simply let the UI warn on a displayed value that is nonzero. Rule 1 is only lightly engaged here, because `< 0` is a display decision on a core-computed sign.

title: The out-of-band sharing figure is stated in five more places than the catalogue, with three different numbers
claim: One measured effect is quoted as '24 % relief to 15 % increase' (Bending::note doc, state.md:730, five catalogues), as 'up to a quarter in either direction' (reference.md:2847) and as '12–24 %' (state.md:1019). A sweep gives 33 % relief and 74 % increase. Saying the same figure in several places is how it went stale. The notes.rs module doc also names the retired key stage.load_sharing_out_of_band.
evidence: grep of the docs and code as quoted. The sweep in probes/verify-gear-io-1 bin sharing: 'relief max +0.3332, increase max -0.7361'.
proposal: Say the effect once, in state.md's known-approximations entry, with the sweep that measured it (or, better, say only that it has no fixed direction or size). Everywhere else, point to that entry. If the note carries the per-mesh change (finding 0), drop the fixed figure from all five catalogues and from Bending::note's doc. Fix the key name in notes.rs.
validation: grep -rn '24 %\|24%\|a quarter' docs crates/gear-core/src crates/gear-io/data should return only the one state.md entry, or nothing.

verdict.reason: Re-ran the sweep. The quoted '24 % relief / 15 % increase' are simply the extremes of the four hand-picked designs in gear-io/tests/notes.rs (z=40 ha=1.35 gives +23.6 %; z=100 ha=1.4 gives −15.2 %). A plain grid over z 20..150 and ha 1.0..1.5 at x=0 gives up to +33.3 % relief and up to −73.6 % increase: a stress figure raised by three quarters, where the user-facing message in all five languages says 15 %. The figure also appears in three inconsistent forms: '24 %/15 %' (Bending doc at mod.rs:716-726, state.md:732, five catalogues), 'up to a quarter in either direction' (reference.md:2848) and '12–24 %' (state.md:1021). This is exactly the 'bound that records where the sweep stopped' that CLAUDE.md warns against. Severity is raised because the message a designer reads understates the effect by about five times. The notes.rs module doc's 'stage.load_sharing_out_of_band' is historical narrative (the key was named that then), but it should name the current key mesh.load_sharing_out_of_band.
verdict.evidence: probes/verify-gear-io-1 bin sharing, re-run: the four test cases give +0.1563, +0.1169, +0.2357, −0.1517; the wider sweep finds 403 changed cases, relief max +0.3332 (z=20 ha=1.375) and increase max −0.7361 (z=150 ha=1.5). notes.rs:64-70 asserts hi ∈ [0.15, 0.35) and lo ∈ [−0.30, −0.05) over only those four designs. strings_en.toml:137: 'can vary from -24% to +15%'.
verdict.proposal_note: Drop the fixed magnitudes from the catalogues and the Bending doc ('no fixed direction, and it can be large'), or better, have the note carry this mesh's own change as a value, since the solve can compute ramp-off against ramp-on. Say the measured range once, in state.md, with the sweep named. Replace notes.rs's magnitude band with the two sign assertions plus a sweep, so the test no longer pins numbers taken from four chosen designs.

title: zh-Hant catalogue carries mainland vocabulary although its header says Taiwan terminology
claim: The zh-Hant header says the terminology follows Taiwan usage (臺灣常用的齒輪術語). Several values, though, are mainland words converted character by character: 加載 (TW 載入) in app_core_failed and app_loading_core, 內核 (TW 核心) for the calculation core (3 uses, against 核心 once), and 端口 (TW 連接埠, and this catalogue's own 軸口 five times) in train_load_port. train_load_port also uses 地 for ground where the panel says 機架. These values are character conversions of the zh-Hans lines, not Taiwan-usage translations.
evidence: Counts in strings_zh-Hant.toml: 端口 1, 軸口 5, 加載 4, 載入 0, 內核 3, 核心 1. Line 111: '…不能施加載荷的體進入：地、被固定的體，或不是端口的體'. Line 118: '計算內核加載失敗'. Line 119: '正在加載計算內核…'.
proposal_note: Use 載入 and 核心, and 軸口 for port and 機架 for ground in train_load_port. Add 加載/內核/端口 to the zh-Hant forbidden-variant list proposed for findings 9 and 10.
proposal: Replace 加載→載入 (app_core_failed, app_loading_core), 內核→核心 (3 uses), 端口→軸口 and 地→機架 in train_load_port. Add these to the zh-Hant deny-list check.
validation: The deny-list check fails on the current file and passes after the edit, and grep shows one term per concept.

verdict.reason: Counts reproduced. 加載 in the software sense ('load the core') appears at lines 118 and 119. The other two of the four hits are 施加載荷 (line 111, where 加載 is only a substring) and 所加載的齒面 (line 53, the loaded flank), which are a different sense. 內核 appears three times (118, 119, 255), while the header comment uses 核心. 端口 appears once (line 111) against 軸口 five times (73-76). Line 111 uses 地 for ground where train_ground (line 338) is 機架. There is also an inconsistency the finding missed: 'load' is 負荷 at lines 43 and 73-76 but 載荷 at lines 53 and 111. Confidence stays medium: these are terminology judgements, but the within-file inconsistencies are objective.
verdict.evidence: grep -c counts in strings_zh-Hant.toml: 端口 1, 軸口 5, 內核 3, 核心 1 (header line 7), 機架 1 (line 338). Line 111: '...不能施加載荷的體進入：地、被固定的體，或不是端口的體'. Lines 118/119: '計算內核加載失敗', '正在加載計算內核…'. Lines 73-76 use 負荷, lines 53 and 111 use 載荷.
verdict.proposal_note: Beyond the listed replacements, pick one word for load (負荷 or 載荷) and use it throughout. A deny-list for vocabulary is weaker than a small per-concept glossary check (port→軸口, ground→機架, core→核心), because variants are open-ended.

title: The zh-Hant catalogue contains a Simplified character: 属 in error.screw_axes_are_parallel
claim: The Traditional Chinese message reads '平行的一對属於直齒級'. 属 is the Simplified form; Traditional is 屬, which the same file uses correctly once elsewhere. This line was apparently converted by hand from zh-Hans and missed one character.
evidence: grep -n '属' strings_zh-Hant.toml returns only line 105. grep -c '屬' returns 1. zh-Hans:105 has the same sentence with 属.
proposal: Fix it to 屬 when the message is rewritten for finding 16(d). As a guard, add a test or a check_strings.py step that runs zh-Hant values against a small list of Simplified-only characters common in this vocabulary (属, 齿, 轮, 轴, 级, 啮, 载, 应, 数 …) and fails on a hit.
validation: grep for the Simplified list over strings_zh-Hant.toml returns nothing.

verdict.reason: 属 at line 105 is Simplified and confirmed. But it is not the only one: a scan finds 际 (for 際) at lines 43 and 252, 点 (for 點) at line 186 and 机 (for 機) at line 253. So the claim that this one character is the file's only Simplified slip is wrong, and a hand-written deny-list of nine characters like the one proposed would have caught none of the other three.
verdict.evidence: grep -n '际\|点\|机\|属' strings_zh-Hant.toml → 43: '實际輪系', 105: '一對属於直齒級', 186: '齒面與齒根圓角的交点', 252: '輪齒實际達到的範圍', 253: '机構必須隨之跟隨'. zh-Hans:105 has the same sentence with 属.
verdict.corrected_claim: The zh-Hant catalogue contains at least four distinct Simplified characters at five sites: 属 (105), 际 (43, 252), 点 (186) and 机 (253).
verdict.proposal_note: Fix all five sites. Build the guard from a complete Simplified→Traditional table, such as Unihan's kTraditionalVariant or OpenCC's STCharacters, filtered to characters that are Simplified-only, rather than a hand list: a hand list is where the sweep stops.

title: The note placeholder check takes the union of values over all firings, so one site that omits a value is masked by another that supplies it
claim: observed_values merges every firing's value names into one Vec per key. every_placeholder_is_a_value_the_core_supplies then checks each placeholder against that union. A note raised at two sites passes even if one site forgets a value the message uses. Four keys have two sites today (MESH_CONTACT_RATIO_BELOW_ONE, CLAMP_TOOTH_UNDERCUT, CLAMP_TOOTH_SEVERED, CLAMP_FILLET_CAPPED). I checked, and their sites supply the same names, so this is latent, not live.
evidence: strings.rs:587-592: `seen.entry(n.key.clone()).or_default().extend(n.values.keys().cloned())`. grep of Note::new(key::…) in gear-core shows the four keys raised at two sites each. A rough grep found both sites of MESH_CONTACT_RATIO_BELOW_ONE supply 'ratio' and both sites of CLAMP_FILLET_CAPPED supply 'radius'.
proposal: Check each firing on its own: in `record`, check each note's value set against the message's placeholders there, or keep a BTreeSet of per-firing sets and require every set to cover the placeholders. This fits the BTreeSet change in finding 16.
validation: In a worktree, drop a value from one site of a two-site note; the per-firing check fails while the current test passes.

verdict.reason: observed_values unions each firing's value keys per note key (strings.rs:587-592), and every_placeholder_is_a_value_the_core_supplies checks placeholders against that union (512-530). A raise site, or a conditional branch within one site, that omits a value is masked if any other firing supplies it. The finding is right that this is latent. The exact count of multi-site keys is slightly off: a production-only scan finds CLAMP_TOOTH_SEVERED, CLAMP_TOOTH_UNDERCUT, CLAMP_FILLET_CAPPED, GEAR_SHIFT_RAISED_FOR_UNDERCUT and GEAR_ADDENDUM_HELD_TO_TIP_WIDTH at two sites each. That does not change the finding. Separately, a key that never fires in the sweep is skipped entirely (`continue`), and a per-firing check does not reach that case either.
verdict.evidence: strings.rs:587-592: `seen.entry(n.key.clone()).or_default().extend(n.values.keys().cloned())`. strings.rs:519-521 skips unfired keys. A Python scan of gear-core/src up to each file's #[cfg(test)] counts the multi-site keys listed above.
verdict.proposal_note: Keep a per-key set of per-firing value sets (BTreeSet<BTreeSet<String>>) and require each one to cover the message's placeholders. The strings test already fires every note, so no sweep change is needed.

title: `gear-cli worm` rates contact and prints wheel torque at a hard-coded mu 0.06 while the same worm through wormstage runs at 0.08
claim: worm_report fixes `let mu = 0.06;` and uses it for torque_out (the wheel torque) and for s.contact(...). The shipped mesh friction moved to 0.08 (state.md:237), so the two commands on the same 1/40/7 worm disagree: 'wheel torque 54.953 Nm at mu 0.06' versus the wormstage efficiency of 61.805 % at 0.08. It is the same stale default as finding 0, but used as a number, not only a label.
evidence: main.rs:3144 `let mu = 0.06;` and 3146 `let torque_out = torque_in * s.ratio * s.efficiency(mu, Drive::Forward);`. worm_1_40_7_90.txt:33 reads 'worm torque 2.000 Nm  ->  wheel torque 54.953 Nm at mu 0.06'. arrangements.rs:30 has FRICTION = (0.08, 0.16).
proposal: Take mu from arr::worm(starts, wheel_teeth).meshes[0].sliding_friction (or expose the arrangements' FRICTION as a pub const) instead of the literal, and --write the corpus.
validation: After the change, worm's wheel torque at 2 Nm equals 2 × 40 × 0.61805 = 49.44 Nm, consistent with wormstage.

verdict.reason: worm_report hard-codes mu 0.06 for the wheel torque and the contact call, while every arrangement mesh runs at FRICTION.0 = 0.08. The two commands disagree on the same 1/40/7 worm.
verdict.evidence: main.rs:3144 `let mu = 0.06;`, 3146 `torque_out = torque_in * s.ratio * s.efficiency(mu, Drive::Forward)`, and s.contact(torque_out, ..., mu, ...) further down. arrangements.rs:30 `const FRICTION: (f64, f64) = (0.08, 0.16);`. Golden worm_1_40_7_90.txt: 'wheel torque 54.953 Nm at mu 0.06', peak pressure 3487.4 MPa. wormstage_1_40_7_2.txt: efficiency 61.805 %, contact 3376.1 MPa. state.md:237 records the default moving from 0.06 to 0.08.
verdict.proposal_note: Read mu from the shape's mesh (sliding_friction) instead of a literal. After that, the worm command's wheel torque becomes 2x40x0.61805 = 49.44 Nm. That is still not wormstage's 80 N·m tooth torque (see index 3), so the label should say which torque it is, e.g. 'delivered'. Expect the contact figure to move too, and to be compared against wormstage's 3376.1.

title: hulasweep's gap argument has no effect, so reference.md's 'tips foul until the gap reaches a quarter module, verified by hulasweep' cannot be reproduced
claim: hula_sweep writes the requested gap into distances[0].tip_clearance, but the tip rule sizes the crank offset, so every requested gap below the tip-sized one rolls the identical pair (got 0.2779 mm). The harness can therefore never show the fouling that reference.md says it verified, and the default in the command summary (0.2) differs from the recorded case (0.25).
evidence: `gear-cli hulasweep 18 0`, `18 0.1` and `18 0.2` each print 'gap asked X got 0.2779 mm ... least clearance -0.00001 mm ... (touching, as a mesh does)'. reference.md:1647-1651: 'the tips foul at 134° ... until the far-side gap reaches about a quarter of a module ... verified by rolling the two outlines ... (`gear-cli hulasweep`...)'.
proposal: Let hulasweep roll at an explicit, fixed crank offset (bypassing the tip-sizing), and record one corpus case below the bound that reports fouling near 134 deg. Otherwise reword reference.md to say what the recorded case does show. Align the summary default with the recorded argument.
validation: A recorded hulasweep case with a negative least clearance at about 134 deg from the line of centres, and one at or above the bound reporting touching.

verdict.corrected_claim: The gap argument does work above the tip-sized bound: 0.3 gives 0.3000 mm and 0.5 gives 0.5000 mm, with a different pair each time. At or below the bound of about 0.2779 mm it has no effect: 0, 0.1, 0.2 and 0.25 all roll the identical pair, touching at 20.2 deg. So no hulasweep invocation can show the 134 deg tip fouling that reference.md:1647-1651 says hulasweep verified. The summary default (0.2) and the recorded case (0.25) also differ, though both fall under the same bound and print identical output.
verdict.reason: The title's 'has no effect' is too strong. The substance holds: the tip rule sizes the crank offset, and below that size the requested gap is overridden. The fouling claim therefore cannot be reproduced with the tool that is cited for it.
verdict.evidence: Ran target/release/gear-cli hulasweep 18 {0,0.1,0.2,0.25}: each printed 'gap asked X got 0.2779 mm ... ring x+0.4519 ... least clearance -0.00001 mm at 20.2 deg (touching)'. With 0.3: 'got 0.3000 mm, x+0.4672, tip margin +0.2363 deg'. With 0.5: 'got 0.5000, x+0.6073'. main.rs:602-607: summary '(18, 0.2)', record 'hulasweep 18 0.25'. The doc comment on hula_sweep ('Through the shape ... because the offset answers to the tips as well') admits that the tip bound is applied first.
verdict.proposal_note: The better fix is to let hulasweep take the crank offset (or the far gap) as a fixed input that bypasses the tip sizing, and to record one case below 0.2779 that reports negative clearance near 134 deg. The recorded 0.25 case then also stops being a duplicate of the bound. Also say in reference.md that the quarter module is the tip-sized 0.2779 mm the stage chooses.

title: state.md claims load-case changes 'moved neither canary' as a check, but the strength canary never passes through the train
claim: strength_report builds Tooth/Mesh/ContactPath and calls strength primitives directly.
