claim: The docstring says the path reports nought exactly, 'not a rounding's width above it, which is what it said before breaking away was asked of the whole flow'. That records a past state, not a property. It also suggests the test gates whole-flow breakaway, which it cannot (finding lens-tests-train #2).
evidence: With `.once_moving(&at_rest)` removed from paths_of, the test still passes (full-suite run under mutation E). The fixture's moving flow already reads exactly 0, so the historical contrast the docstring draws is not what the test exercises.
proposal: When the fixture is replaced with the Wolfrom pair (sliding 0.05; static 0.05 and 0.10), rewrite the docstring to state only the law: a path whose whole flow cannot break away delivers nought, though every one of its meshes breaks away alone. Drop the 'what it said before' clause.
validation: Under mutation E the rewritten test fails with 'left: 0.23598…, right: 0.0'.

verdict.reason: The docstring records a past state ('which is what it said before breaking away was asked of the whole flow'). The fixture does not exercise whole-flow breakaway: its backward flow is already 0 while moving, not only at rest.
verdict.evidence: Worktree: removed `.once_moving(&at_rest)` from paths_of (mod.rs:3516) and a_path_holds_at_rest_where_no_mesh_does still PASSes. The flow instrumentation shows that for the back-driven hula every consistent moving branch has efficiency 0 (the output does not absorb), so the moving figure is already nought and there is nothing for at_rest to change.
verdict.proposal_note: Beyond the wording: give the test a fixture that moves backwards but cannot start, so the law it names can fail. The Wolfrom pair suggested (sliding 0.05, static 0.05 and 0.10) is one; confirm first that it fails under the mutation above.

title: The suite's wall time is one serial 1,080-case test, rack_simulation::profile_is_bounded_from_both_sides_by_the_cutter (~30 s)
claim: The cutter-simulation gate runs check_cut(&g, 150) on 1,080 independent cases in one #[test] loop. It takes ~28-30 s single-threaded, which is essentially the whole nextest wall time (~27 s, quoted as '~26 s' in CLAUDE.md). The other 678 tests finish in parallel long before it does, so every developer run waits on this one serial loop.
evidence: Built test binary run alone: `rack_simulation-36ef3f3060381ba7 --exact profile_is_bounded_from_both_sides_by_the_cutter --test-threads 1` gives 30.27 s wall and 30.25 s user, so it uses one core. The lens-tests-train timings.txt shows 27.793 s for it at position 679/679, with the next slowest at 9.74 s. The grid at rack_simulation.rs:30-38 is 10 teeth x 6 shifts x PRESSURE_ANGLES x 2 helix angles x 3 root radii. The test's own doc comment says 'this is the expensive test in the suite'.
proposal: Split the loop into several #[test] functions over disjoint slices of the same grid, for example one per helix angle and root radius (6 tests), or one per tooth count, with a shared helper that checks each case's penetration and deviation against PENETRATION_LIMIT and DEVIATION_LIMIT. nextest then runs the slices in parallel. The worst-case println can stay per slice. Keep the `cases.len() >= 1000` assertion as a separate cheap test over grid().len(). No case and no tolerance changes.
validation: Afterwards the union of the slices equals grid(), which you can assert in the cheap test. Each slice's worst penetration and deviation stay under the same limits, and the combined worst matches the current printed values. Wall time of `cargo nextest run` should drop from ~27 s to roughly the next longest test (~10 s) plus overhead on a machine with 6 or more cores.

verdict.reason: The test is one serial loop over 1,080 independent cases and sets a floor on the suite's wall time. Splitting it changes no case and no tolerance.
verdict.evidence: On this machine (22 cores, load ~6.5), `target/debug/deps/rack_simulation-36ef3f3060381ba7 --exact profile_is_bounded_from_both_sides_by_the_cutter --test-threads 1` gives 34.89 s wall and 34.87 s user, i.e. one core. profile.test is opt-level 2, so it is already optimised. The grid at rack_simulation.rs:30-38 is 10 teeth × 6 shifts × PRESSURE_ANGLES × 2 helix angles × 3 root radii = 1,080 cases.
verdict.proposal_note: Six slices (helix × root radius, ~180 cases each) via a shared helper is fine. Keep the '>= 1000 cases' and 'union == grid()' assertions in one cheap test. CLAUDE.md's '~26 s' will then need re-measuring.

title: Ring 'smallest tooth count' is computed in gear-wasm, ignores profile shift, and the test checks its own copy of the formula
claim: RingSummary::smallest_tooth_count, documented as 'the fewest teeth this design could have had and still cleared its own base circle', is 2 h_a cos beta / (1 - cos alpha_t). That is correct only at x = 0: a ring's tip moves outward with shift, so a shifted ring clears its base circle with far fewer teeth. The UI shows the figure under 'Smallest tooth count' for any design. The formula is engineering mathematics living in the boundary crate, against the map's 'gear-core: all the mathematics'. It recomputes alpha_t by hand, duplicating plane::transverse_pressure_angle with no pressure-angle guard. The ring.rs test the_smallest_ring_follows_the_design_rather_than_a_rule_of_thumb retypes the formula instead of calling the shipped function, so a wrong edit to the shipped function would pass it.
evidence:
Probe ringmin (default cutter, m=1, 20 deg, h_a=1); the wasm function returns 34 for all of these:
- x=0: z=32 is ra=rb (clamp.ring_tip_raised), z=34 clears (+0.025).
- x=0.3: z=26 has ra - rb = +0.084 with no ring_tip_raised note.
- x=0.6: z=26 has +0.384.
lib.rs:556 computes `(params.pressure_angle.to_radians().tan() / beta.cos()).atan()`. At alpha=0, 1 - cos 0 = 0, so the threshold is inf and it saturates to u32::MAX.
proposal: Move the figure into gear-core as a Ring method using the shifted tip: r - (h_a - x) m >= r cos alpha_t gives z >= 2 (h_a - x) cos beta / (1 - cos alpha_t). Better still, read it off the same tip-radius expression Ring::cut_by uses, so the two cannot drift. Use the guarded pressure angle. Have gear-wasm call the method. Have the ring.rs test call it too and check it against Ring::cut_by at z and z-1 over shifts {-0.3, 0, 0.3, 0.6}. Update the docstring and reference.md:1592 to carry x.
validation: New law: for x in {-0.3, 0, 0.3, 0.6}, h_a in {0.6, 0.8, 1.0}, alpha in {14.5, 20, 25} and beta in {0, 30}, Ring::cut_by at n = smallest_tooth_count raises no ring_tip_raised note, and at n-1 it does. This fails on HEAD at x=0.3.

verdict.reason: Reproduced. The ring's own clamp shows that the smallest unclamped tooth count follows 2(h_a − x)cosβ/(1 − cos α_t), while the wasm figure ignores x. The figure is wrong in both directions: it is optimistic for a negative shift, so a design the panel calls large enough is clamped. It is engineering mathematics in gear-wasm, against the map. It recomputes α_t by hand with no pressure-angle guard. The ring.rs test retypes the formula; it does call Ring::cut_by, but only at x = 0.
verdict.evidence: Probe (default cutter, h_a 1, 20°, β 0), smallest z above the last clamp.ring_tip_raised against the wasm formula (34 everywhere): x=-0.3 → 44 (the shifted formula gives 44); x=0 → 34 (34); x=0.3 → 24 (24); x=0.6 → 14 (14). gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:554-560 uses `(params.pressure_angle.to_radians().tan() / beta.cos()).atan()`; the core has plane::transverse_pressure_angle. ring.rs:278 `let mut ra = r - m * (params.addendum - x);` confirms that the shift moves the tip outward.
verdict.proposal_note: Put Ring::smallest_tooth_count(params) in gear-core, using (h_a − x) and the guarded α_t, and have gear-wasm call it. Rewrite the ring.rs test to call that function and check cut_by at n and n−1 over shifts {-0.3, 0, 0.3, 0.6}. The probe shows this law holds exactly for the shifted formula. Update reference.md:1592 and the RingSummary doc to carry x.

title: reference.md says the tip-width addendum is a bracketed Newton; the code uses brent
claim: The document describes the altered-addendum solve as 'a bracketed Newton between r_b and the pointed-tooth radius', quoting ds/dr' as if it were used. addendum_for_tip_width actually calls brent on u with no derivative, and finds the pointed-tooth end by a second brent.
evidence: reference.md:249-251: 'ds/dr′ = 2(ψ_b − inv α_{r′} − tan α_{r′}), so it is a bracketed Newton between r_b and the pointed-tooth radius.' auto.rs:750 reads `brent(|u| width(u) - min_tip_width, 0.0, u_point, Tol::default())?`.
proposal: Either make the code a newton_bracketed with the stated derivative (dw/du is available in closed form), or change the sentence to 'a bracketed root (Brent) in the roll u between 0 and the pointed-tooth roll'. With finding 7 applied, the pointed-tooth roll is tan(inv_inverse(psi_b)).
validation: tools/check_doc_links.py and check_figures.py unaffected; a read of auto.rs against the sentence.

verdict.reason: The docs describe a Newton solve that does not exist. auto.rs:750 solves with brent(|u| width(u) - min_tip_width, 0.0, u_point, ...) and uses no derivative, and u_point comes from a second brent at auto.rs:739-744. The same misstatement is in a second document, docs/rationale.md:419, whose solve table says row 2 'Tip radius for a given tip width | Newton, analytic ds/dr'. So two documents are wrong, not one.
verdict.evidence: docs/reference.md:249-251 says 'so it is a bracketed Newton between r_b and the pointed-tooth radius'. docs/rationale.md:419 says '| 2 | Tip radius for a given tip width | Newton, analytic `ds/dr` |'. auto.rs:739 is `let u_point = brent(|u| g.psi_b - inv_from_roll(u), 0.0, POINTED_TOOTH_MAX_ROLL, ...)` and auto.rs:750 is `brent(|u| width(u) - min_tip_width, 0.0, u_point, Tol::default())?`. grep finds no 'newton' anywhere in auto.rs.
verdict.corrected_claim: reference.md:249-251 and rationale.md:419 both say the tip-width addendum is found by Newton with analytic ds/dr. The code runs two Brent solves in the roll u, neither using a derivative.
verdict.proposal_note: Fix both documents, or change the code to match them. The pointed-tooth roll is closed form given inv⁻¹: u_point = tan(inv⁻¹(ψ_b)), because inv(atan u) = u − atan u. That removes one of the ten 'impossible closed form' solves in the table, and the table's count and wording should change with it. While the table is open, check row 4 ('Planet shift ... Newton') against the code too.

title: An unreachable chord tolerance still yields tens of millions of DXF vertices on a large gear; the safety stop bounds work per span, not per outline
claim: The depth cap bounds each span at 2^14 segments, so the total grows with the tooth count, and the relative floor binds only at very large z. The panel's chord-tolerance field has min=0 and Rust sets no absolute lower bound, so a small typed value on a large gear makes a DXF export produce millions of vertices. The canary's promise that 'an unreachable tolerance must not explode the vertex count' is tested only at z=17.
evidence:
Own probe, Gear::outline(t).len():
- z200 m1: 13,107,600 vertices at t=1e-18, and 6,281,460 at t=1e-9 mm.
- z2000: 49,747,990 at 1e-9.
GearPanel.svelte:548 has `<input type="number" step="0.0005" min="0">`. The outline is built only for export (gear-wasm export_*_dxf), so the effect is a huge file or a stalled export, not a frozen solve.
proposal: Bound the total rather than the per-span depth, for example cap subdivisions per section so that vertices per tooth stay under a fixed budget. Alternatively, have Rust report a floored tolerance as a Note (for example 'chord tolerance raised to X') and floor the absolute tolerance at a value tied to double precision at ra, such as 1e-12*ra. Expose that floor through admissible ranges so the panel's min comes from Rust.
validation: A law over z in {17, 200, 2000}: outline(1e-18).len() / z is bounded by the same constant, and a Note is emitted when the tolerance is floored.

verdict.reason: I reproduced the counts with my own probe (probes/verify-last-18, Gear::outline(t).len() with GearParams::default() and teeth set). The per-span depth cap of 2^14 does make the total scale with z. The 1e-12·ra relative floor only binds below about 1e-10 mm on a 100 mm tip radius. The canary an_unreachable_tolerance_stays_bounded (outline.rs:715) tests z=17 only, and its accepted band (400k–1.2M vertices) already admits about 1.1 million vertices as 'bounded'. The effect is limited to DXF export and is reached only through a typed value (the panel has min=0). It does not affect the solve.
verdict.evidence: From the probe: z=17 gives 1,258 / 37,638 / 1,034,518 / 1,113,908 vertices at t = 1e-3 / 1e-6 / 1e-9 / 1e-18. z=200 gives 8,400 / 238,000 / 6,281,460 / 13,107,600 (65,538 per tooth at 1e-18). The finding's z=200 figures reproduce exactly. gear.rs:611-615 floors only at MIN_RELATIVE_TOLERANCE*self.mean.ra. GearPanel.svelte:548 is min="0".
verdict.proposal_note: One of the two alternatives is already in the code: an absolute floor of 1e-12*ra is MIN_RELATIVE_TOLERANCE, applied at gear.rs:613. That floor is too low to bound the output, because at 1e-9 mm on z=200 it does not bind and 6.3M vertices result. The fix is a floor with physical meaning, for example about 1e-9·ra or a fixed nanometre scale, well below any JGMA grade. Report it as a Note when it binds, and expose it through admissible ranges so the panel's min comes from Rust. Alternatively, cap the total per tooth. The canary should be widened to a z-sweep asserting vertices per tooth is bounded.

title: One diameter floor offset by two different epsilons within one function (1.000_001 and 1 + 1e-9), plus 1 + 1e-6 for the room floor
claim: In the crossed-mesh sizing, the same `floor = z1·m_n` (the diameter below which no pair exists) is stepped off with two unrelated relative epsilons. The designer's number is clamped to `floor * 1.000_001` (928), while the Brent bracket starts at `floor * (1.0 + 1e-9)` (955, 957). A few hundred lines later, the tip-room floor is stepped off by `(1.0 + 1e-6)` (1620). All three mean 'just inside a domain edge where a term is singular', and none says why its size was chosen.
evidence: shape.rs:928 `let from = a.pitch_diameter.manual.max(floor * 1.000_001);`; shape.rs:955 `Some(turning) if from <= turning => (floor * (1.0 + 1e-9), turning),`; shape.rs:957 `None => (floor * (1.0 + 1e-9), grown(...))`; shape.rs:1620 `* (1.0 + 1e-6);`.
proposal: Name one crate-level constant for 'one step inside a singular domain edge' (e.g. `solve::EDGE = 1e-9`, relative) and use it at all four sites. Better, where a bracketed solve starts at the edge, let the bracket start exactly at the edge and have the objective return a finite signed value there (as brent already requires finite ends). A designer's number below the floor should clamp to the same bracket end the solve uses, so the two cannot disagree.
validation: Mutating each literal separately should leave the suite and corpus unchanged, which shows none is load-bearing at its size. A law that sizing at a target just above the minimum distance converges for the floor-side branch holds at the unified value.

verdict.reason: All four literals are at the cited lines. At 928 the manual diameter is clamped to floor*1.000_001. At 955 and 957 the brent bracket starts at floor*(1+1e-9). Nothing explains the size of either, and they differ by 1000× for the same edge, which is helix = acos(floor/d1) → 0. Line 1620 guards a different edge: the base-circle-sum distance, where the operating angle goes to 0. It is the same kind of guard ('one step inside a singular domain edge') but not the same quantity. Consequence of the mismatch: a designer's diameter between floor*(1+1e-9) and floor*1.000_001 is moved up by the clamp, while the bracket begins lower. The branch test `from <= turning` is almost unaffected, so this is a tidiness finding and not a wrong answer. I did not mutate the literals.
verdict.evidence: shape.rs:928 `a.pitch_diameter.manual.max(floor * 1.000_001)`. shape.rs:955 and 957 `floor * (1.0 + 1e-9)`. shape.rs:1620 `.fold(0.0_f64, f64::max) * (1.0 + 1e-6);`, which is the rack floor mt·|Σz|/2·cos α_t.
verdict.corrected_claim: Two different epsilons (1e-6 and 1e-9) step off the same crossed-mesh diameter floor within size_reaching. A third (1e-6) steps off a different edge, the base-circle-sum distance in tip sizing. None of the three sizes is justified.
verdict.proposal_note: Using one named relative step at 928/955/957 is enough to make the clamp and the bracket agree. For 1620, check whether room_at is finite at the exact floor before removing its step. The operating angle is 0 there and inv is defined, so the step may be avoidable entirely.

title: CLAUDE.md's claim that K_f perturbations leave the whole suite silent is stale
claim: CLAUDE.md says that perturbing K_f's H and L, ISO's Y_S, the tangent angle and the reversed-bending fraction 'leaves the entire test suite silent, and the corpus catches every one'. That is no longer true for K_f. H (0.331→0.3315), L (0.324→0.325), M and the H slope each fail `train::shape::hula_recorded::the_harness_hula_is_what_the_corpus_recorded`. That test copies corpus figures into the suite. The paragraph's conclusion still holds in spirit: no law in the suite catches it, only a recorded copy. As written, though, the statement is false, and a reader who sees a nextest failure after touching K_f is told it cannot happen.
evidence: notes/ablate-rate/table.tsv rows kf_H, kf_L, kf_M, kf_Hslope, kf_M_small: suite_failed 1, the hula_recorded test. shape.rs:5590-5593 describes the module as holding 'what the corpus printed for gear-cli hula 18 0.2'.
proposal: Reword CLAUDE.md:186-190 along these lines: 'leaves every law in the suite silent — K_f is caught only by the hula test that copies the corpus's figures — and the corpus catches every one'. Or, once finding 4's published-digit test exists, say that test holds K_f's digits and the corpus its sub-digit drift.
validation: Re-apply the kf_H perturbation in a worktree and confirm the hula_recorded test fails and nothing else does. The reworded sentence then matches.

verdict.reason: I reproduced it independently in a worktree. With K_f H changed from 0.331 to 0.3315 (strength.rs:1053), the full workspace suite (679 tests) failed on exactly one test, train::shape::hula_recorded::the_harness_hula_is_what_the_corpus_recorded, at its 'z18 σ_F' check. No other test failed. So CLAUDE.md's 'leaves the entire test suite silent' is false for K_f. It still holds in spirit: the only catch is a copied corpus figure (tolerance 0.05 MPa on 6663.3/η₁), not a law. For the other three constants (Y_S, the tangent angle, the reversed-bending fraction), the ablation table records the suite as silent, so the sentence stays true for them.
verdict.evidence: Worktree run: 'z18 σ_F: recorded 6685.432604603918, shape 6687.409532934055', then 'Summary 679 tests run: 678 passed, 1 failed'. CLAUDE.md:186-190 says 'Perturbing five of the rating model's cited constants — K_f's H and L, ISO's Y_S, the tangent angle, the reversed-bending fraction — leaves the entire test suite silent'.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposed rewording is right. Keep it short, e.g. 'leaves every law in the suite silent — K_f trips only the hula test that copies two σ_F figures from the corpus — and the corpus catches every one.'

title: The tip-sizing lean of 1e-9 mm is described as 'the solver's own tolerance' but is a million times larger than it
claim: After brent finds the distance at which the tip room is zero, the code leans `hi.min(e + 1e-9)` 'by the solver's own tolerance'. Brent's tolerance here is Tol::default (x_tol = 1e-15, plus 2ε|b|), about 1e-15 mm at a 2 mm crank. The 1e-9 is an unrelated absolute millimetre literal: its unit is not tied to the module, and the comment misstates it.
evidence: solve.rs:38 `x_tol: 1e-15`; solve.rs brent `tol1 = 2.0 * f64::EPSILON * b.abs() + 0.5 * tol.x_tol`. The probe shows the lean in the result: at 19/18/17/18 with a 0.3 gap, the far-side gap as built is 0.30000000328, i.e. 3.3e-9 over what was asked.
proposal: Lean by the bracket the solver actually returns, `e + tol1` with tol1 from the same Tol, or a named relative step (e.g. 4·ε·max(|e|,1)), and correct the comment. Alternatively, make brent return the endpoint on the clear side of the sign change, which removes the lean altogether.
validation: The planocentric/hula law asserting the far-side gap equals the asked gap tightens from 1e-6 to about 1e-12 and still passes, with `tip_interference == false` at the returned distance.

verdict.reason: shape.rs:1693-1698 leans `hi.min(e + 1e-9)` with the comment 'by the solver's own tolerance'. The solver's tolerance is Tol::default(): x_tol = 1e-15, and brent's tol1 = 2ε|b| + 0.5·x_tol, which is about 1e-14 mm at distances of a few mm. The 1e-9 is an unrelated absolute millimetre literal, so the comment is wrong, and the literal does not scale with module. I did not re-run the 3.3e-9 far-gap probe, but it matches the magnitude of the lean. Note also that the lean is never re-checked: nothing asserts room_at(e+1e-9) >= 0.
verdict.evidence: solve.rs:38 `x_tol: 1e-15`. solve.rs:87 `let tol1 = 2.0 * f64::EPSILON * b.abs() + 0.5 * tol.x_tol;`. shape.rs:1693-1698: '// Lean to the clear side of the root by the solver's own tolerance ... hi.min(e + 1e-9)'.
verdict.proposal_note: Leaning by exactly tol1 risks landing on the negative side still, because room_at is itself computed by closure and involute inversions with rounding noise above 1e-14. The robust fix is to have the bracketed solve return its final bracket end on the chosen sign (a brent variant returning the clear-side end), which removes the literal. Failing that, lean by a named relative step and assert room_at >= 0 at the result.

title: crossed.rs self-locking test accepts either the locked or the near-locked note, so it cannot catch the two branches swapped
claim: `self_locking_is_said_out_loud` asserts `efficiency.locked().backward` and then accepts `MESH_SELF_LOCKING || MESH_NEAR_SELF_LOCKING`. A locked mesh that said only 'close to self-locking' would pass, and so would a regression that fires the near note instead of the locked one.
evidence: crossed.rs:1079 `.any(|n| n.is(key::MESH_SELF_LOCKING) || n.is(key::MESH_NEAR_SELF_LOCKING))`, right after `assert!(r.meshes[0].efficiency.locked().backward)`.
proposal: Assert MESH_SELF_LOCKING present and MESH_NEAR_SELF_LOCKING absent, since the test has already established that the mesh is locked.
validation: Swap the two keys at shape.rs:2690 in a worktree: the tightened test fails, and the current one passes.

verdict.reason: The test is as loose as claimed: it accepts either key right after asserting the mesh is locked. But the claimed consequence is refuted. I swapped the two keys at shape.rs:2690 in a worktree. self_locking_is_said_out_loud still passed, as predicted, but the suite did catch the swap: train::crossed::tests::a_drive_that_cannot_break_away_delivers_nothing (crossed.rs:1719-1723) requires MESH_SELF_LOCKING with .expect and failed. The regression the finding describes is therefore detected. Also, the code's if/else-if at shape.rs:2698-2706 makes it structurally impossible to emit both notes, so the proposed 'near absent' assertion guards nothing the structure does not already guarantee.
verdict.evidence: Worktree run with `Drive::Backward => (key::MESH_NEAR_SELF_LOCKING, key::MESH_SELF_LOCKING)`: 'FAIL gear-core train::crossed::tests::a_drive_that_cannot_break_away_delivers_nothing', 'PASS gear-core train::crossed::tests::self_locking_is_said_out_loud', 'Summary 604 tests run: 603 passed, 1 failed'. crossed.rs:1722 is `.find(|n| n.is(key::MESH_SELF_LOCKING)).expect("self-locking must be said out loud")`.
verdict.corrected_claim: self_locking_is_said_out_loud accepts either key, so on its own it cannot catch the branches being swapped. The swap is still caught by a_drive_that_cannot_break_away_delivers_nothing, which requires MESH_SELF_LOCKING on a locked mesh.
verdict.proposal_note: Tightening the assertion to MESH_SELF_LOCKING is still a free improvement, because it makes the test say what its name says. Treat it as a clarity fix, not a coverage gap.

title: The sharing-sweep test says it asserts exact equality below ε_n = 2, but it asserts only a 1e-4 tolerance
claim: The doc of `the_sharing_sweep_has_converged` says 'Below the band it cannot move at any resolution ... which is asserted here as an exact equality'. The body applies the same `(fine - coarse).abs() / coarse < 1e-4` check to every ε, 1.2 and 1.9 included. No equality is asserted, so a change that broke the seeding below the band (e.g. dropping `highest_single_pair` from the sample list) could shift the answer by up to 1e-4 relative without failing.
evidence: strength.rs:1936-1967: only `< 1e-4` and `fine >= coarse*(1-1e-12)` are asserted. A probe shows equality does hold today: for every ε_n < 2 case on the test's grid, 200, 800 and 12800 samples agree bit for bit, and LinearRamp/None = 1.000000000000.
proposal: Where eps/cos²β_b < 2, assert `fine == coarse` and that LinearRamp's factor·share equals LoadSharing::None's factor exactly. Keep the 1e-4 bound for the band only.
validation: Mutate worst_over_cycle to drop `highest_single_pair(eps_n)` from the seeds. The new equality assertion fails, while the current test can pass or fail by margin.

verdict.reason: The doc of the_sharing_sweep_has_converged (strength.rs:1928-1933) says the sub-band case 'is asserted here as an exact equality'. The body (1951-1966) applies only `(fine-coarse).abs()/coarse < 1e-4` and `fine >= coarse*(1-1e-12)` to every ε, 1.2 and 1.9 included. So the doc describes an assertion the test does not make. The proposed fix, though, would assert something that is not a law. Equality below ε_n = 2 holds on this test's grid only (z ≥ 12, addendum 1.35). It does not hold for small standard teeth, whose Dolan–Broghamer factor peaks inside the single-pair zone (finding 27).
verdict.evidence: Probe probes/verify-last-19 (public bending_section_shared_with, DB factor × share), run on the test's grid (z 12/17/43/97, β 0/20, ha 1.35, ε 1.2-1.9 with ε_n<2): LinearRamp/None = 1.000000000000, and 200/800/12800 samples agree bit for bit. Off the grid, at addendum 1.0: z10 ε1.7 gives ramp/none 1.01355, with 200→800 moving 8.2e-4 relative. z9 ε1.7 gives 1.01921 (3.7e-4), z9 ε1.9 1.00356, z12 ε1.9 1.00170. So below the band, standard teeth show neither the equality nor even the test's own 1e-4 convergence.
verdict.corrected_claim: The doc claims an exact-equality assertion that the body does not make. Equality below ε_n = 2 holds only on the test's hand-picked grid, not as a law. Its grid also leaves out z9/z10 standard-addendum teeth: there the sub-band answer is neither equal to the unshared one nor converged to 1e-4 at 200 samples.
verdict.proposal_note: Do not add an unconditional `fine == coarse` / ramp == None assertion below the band, because it encodes a claim finding 27 refutes. Instead: (1) fix the doc sentence; (2) add z9/z10 at addendum 1.0 to the grid, which currently fails the 1e-4 bound (8.2e-4) and so shows 200 samples are not converged where the peak is interior to the single-pair zone; (3) assert equality only where the unshared factor is maximal at the HPSTC, or seed the zone's interior maximum (e.g. a bracketed max via solve.rs over [ε_n−1, 1]) so that a sub-band answer is exact by construction.

title: The documented range of what load sharing does above ε_n = 2 (−24 % to +15 %) is exceeded on the test's own grid, up to +30 % spur and ×3 helical
claim: state.md says sharing above a virtual contact ratio of 2 was 'measured from a 24 % relief to a 15 % increase across high-contact-ratio spur designs'. On the grid `the_sharing_sweep_has_converged` already uses (addendum 1.35), LinearRamp's governing factor·share against the unshared factor reaches 1.30 for spur z=97 at ε_α = 2.6, and 1.65 (z43) and 3.00 (z97) at β = 20°. A bound recorded where a sweep stopped is standing in for a fact. Separately, strength.rs:1600 'Measured at 0.0–0.2 % on ordinary meshes' is stale: below the band the answer is now bit-identical (0 %), as state.md:524 says.
evidence: Probe (probes/verify-ablate-constants-rating) calling public bending_section_shared_with(Tooth{teeth, helix_angle, addendum 1.35}, eps, LinearRamp|None, 200) and bending_factor(DolanBroghamer)·share: z43 β0 ε2.6: 1.0313; z97 β0 ε2.6: 1.3025; z43 β20 ε2.6: 1.6523; z97 β20 ε2.6: 2.9980; all ε_n < 2 cases: 1.000000000000. Caveat: ε is supplied as in the test, not derived from a mate, so a ratio this high may not be buildable. A rough spur z=97 addendum 1.35 self-mesh gives ε_α ≈ 2.45, so the spur figure is near reachable.
proposal: Re-measure over buildable meshes (derive ε from an actual mate, sweep z, β and addendum) and state the range, or state that it is unbounded in direction and size. Update strength.rs:1600 to 'identical below ε_n = 2'. Since the unshared default loads the full force at d = ε_n − 1, which in the band can sit far down the flank, consider whether the per-mesh note should name the direction and size of this effect.
validation: A test sweeping buildable high-contact-ratio meshes that records min and max of shared/unshared, with state.md's figure tagged to it for tools/check_figures.py.

verdict.reason: The numbers reproduce exactly, and the documented −24 %/+15 % range is exceeded in both directions even on buildable meshes. But the headline '×3 helical' and '+65 %' come from ε = 2.6 at β = 20°, which no mate of an addendum-1.35 tooth reaches: the transverse ratio tops out near 2.3. The 24 %/15 % figure has no source or generating tag anywhere in docs/. The proposed replacement for strength.rs:1600, 'identical below ε_n = 2', is itself false for small teeth (+1.4 % to +1.9 % at z9/z10).
verdict.evidence: Probe probes/verify-last-19 reproduces z43 β0 ε2.6: 1.0313, z97 β0 ε2.6: 1.3025, z43 β20 ε2.6: 1.6523, z97 β20 ε2.6: 2.9980. Reachable ε from notes/verify-last-19/eps.py (standard 20°, both addenda 1.35): spur 97/1000 gives 2.546, 97/97 gives 2.445, 17/97 gives 2.19; at β20, 97/1000 gives 2.30 and 43/43 gives 2.07. At those buildable ε: z97 spur ε2.55 gives 1.2032 (+20 %), z97 β20 ε2.3 gives 1.2513 (+25 %), z17 spur ε2.19 gives 0.6577 (−34 %), z17 ε2.05 gives 0.665. `grep '24 %' docs/` finds only state.md:732, with no measurement behind it. Below the band: z10 ε1.7 ha1.0 gives 1.0136 and z9 ε1.7 gives 1.0192, so 'Measured at 0.0–0.2 %' (strength.rs:1600) is wrong, and so is 'identical'.
verdict.corrected_claim: state.md:732's range is exceeded at buildable meshes: at least −34 % (z17 spur, ε≈2.19) to +25 % (z97 β20°, ε≈2.3), and +20 % on spur (z97, ε≈2.55). The ×3 and +65 % helical figures lie outside any buildable ε. strength.rs:1600 '0.0–0.2 %' is wrong: the sub-band effect is 0 on ordinary teeth but up to about +2 % on z9/z10 (finding 27).
verdict.proposal_note: Re-measure with ε derived from actual mates (mesh + ContactPath), sweeping z, β, addendum and mate, and tag the figure for check_figures.py. Do not change strength.rs:1600 to 'identical below ε_n = 2'. State the sub-band effect as 'zero where the unshared factor peaks at the HPSTC, up to ~2 % on small undercut-range pinions', or remove the effect by fixing finding 27.

title: contact::sliding_velocity and sliding_at have no production caller; the crossed-axis promise in their docs is stale, and Contact::slip is the second, live model of the same quantity
claim: `pub fn sliding_velocity` and `pub fn sliding_at` are called only from each other and from contact.rs's test module. No crate (gear-core production, gear-io, gear-wasm, gear-cli) calls them. Their docs claim the worm's non-vanishing pitch-point sliding 'arrives here as a value of this function rather than as a separate screw-gear formula'. sliding_at's doc promises 'the crossed-axis version of this arrives with the screw geometry it needs (milestone 7, step 5)'. In fact crossed sliding is computed by `Contact::slip` (contact.rs:725-738), which is the same relative-velocity expression written a second time. Line contacts report `sliding_velocity: 0.0` as a constant (train/mod.rs:494) without calling either. So one phenomenon has two implementations, and the one the docs present as the unified model is dead in production.
evidence: `grep -rn 'sliding_velocity(\|sliding_at' crates --include=*.rs` finds definitions at contact.rs:604 and :637, one internal call at :657, and calls only at test lines 1409-1624 (`mod tests` starts at contact.rs:952). Contact::slip: `let v1 = cross(self.axis_1, self.point); let v2 = scale(cross(self.axis_2, sub(self.point, self.centre_2)), k); Some(sub(v1, v2))`. That is the same `ω₁ â₁ × p − ω₂ â₂ × (p − c)` that sliding_velocity documents at contact.rs:569-571. contact.rs:633-635: 'The crossed-axis version of this arrives with the screw geometry it needs (milestone 7, step 5)'.
proposal: Make one function the model. Either have Contact::slip call sliding_velocity (passing axis_2, the speed ratio and centre_2), or drop sliding_velocity and sliding_at and move their parallel-axis tests (pitch-point sliding is zero; sliding is perpendicular to the contact line at every helix) onto Contact::slip for a parallel-axis Contact. Delete the 'milestone 7, step 5' sentence and the 'arrives here as a value of this function' claim, or make them true.
validation: After the change, grep shows the kept function has a production caller. cargo nextest run -p gear-core contact passes, with the parallel-axis tests exercising the live path. check_golden is unchanged.

verdict.reason: sliding_velocity and sliding_at have no production caller: only contact.rs tests and one screw.rs test (screw.rs:1797, inside mod tests at :1496) call them. The 'milestone 7, step 5' promise is stale, and Contact::slip repeats sliding_velocity's expression. Two corrections. First, the crossed sliding a user sees (MeshCase::sliding_velocity) comes from screw's s.sliding_ratio (shape.rs:2754), not from Contact::slip. Slip is used only inside moment_per_force (contact.rs:774), so production carries two live models besides the dead one. Second, the line-contact constant 0.0 (train/mod.rs:494) is correct and documented: the field is pitch-point sliding, 'exactly zero on parallel shafts' (mod.rs:326-327). sliding_velocity also has a verification role: screw.rs's test checks the screw geometry's sliding_ratio against it as an independent kinematic derivation.
verdict.evidence: grep -rn 'sliding_velocity(|sliding_at' crates: definitions at contact.rs:604/637, internal call :657, tests from :1409 (mod tests at :952), screw.rs:1797 (test). shape.rs:2754: `sliding_velocity: s.sliding_ratio * (speed/60*TAU).abs() * m.first_reference_radius`. contact.rs:774 is `let slip = self.slip()?;`, the only caller of slip. train/mod.rs:326: 'Sliding speed at the pitch point ... exactly zero on parallel shafts'.
verdict.corrected_claim: sliding_velocity/sliding_at are production-dead, and serve only as a test-side kinematic reference, including the screw.rs cross-check. Contact::slip (force balance along the path) re-derives the same relative-velocity expression, and the reported crossed sliding speed is a third route, screw's pitch-point sliding_ratio. Their docs' claims that the worm's sliding 'arrives here as a value of this function' and that the crossed version is still to come are stale. The line-contact 0.0 is correct, not a defect.
verdict.proposal_note: Keep one primitive for the relative velocity, ω₁â₁×p − ω₂â₂×(p−c): have Contact::slip call it (or a shared helper), rather than deleting it. The screw.rs test then still compares screw geometry against kinematics and loses no independence. Fix the two stale doc sentences. Consider whether the reported crossed sliding speed should be Contact::slip at the pitch point, so there is one live route rather than two.

title: SHARING_SAMPLES carries two stacked doc comments that say the same thing, and one asserts a proof that does not hold
claim: The const SHARING_SAMPLES has two consecutive doc blocks that rustdoc concatenates. The first starts 'How finely the mesh cycle is sampled when load sharing is enabled', the second 'Points swept along the mesh cycle when load sharing is allowed to move the governing point'. Each explains the explicit candidate seeding and the interior maximum, so one thing is said twice. The first calls the single-pair boundary the place the peak 'provably is once sharing is allowed'. The second says the unshared answer is reproduced 'exactly' below ε_n=2. Both are false under the production Dolan–Broghamer factor, which can peak inside the zone or at its low end (see finding 27).
evidence: strength.rs, the lines above `const SHARING_SAMPLES: usize = 200;`: '/// How finely the mesh cycle is sampled ... the single-pair boundary, which is where it provably is once sharing is allowed' followed directly by '/// Points swept along the mesh cycle ... which is why the unshared answer is reproduced *exactly* below a virtual contact ratio of 2'. Probe probes/verify-added-5/src/main.rs: z=10 x=0 ε=1.7 has its maximum at d=0.99, not at the HPSTC d=0.7.
proposal: Merge the two into one doc comment. Keep the measured-convergence note (the_sharing_sweep_has_converged) and the list of seeded candidates. Drop 'provably' and 'exactly' in favour of what holds: the seeds make sure the zone ends and the tip are evaluated, and the count refines interior maxima.
validation: Reading the rendered doc for SHARING_SAMPLES shows one paragraph set. After finding 27's doc fix, no sentence claims exact agreement below ε_n = 2.

verdict.reason: Two consecutive doc blocks sit above SHARING_SAMPLES (strength.rs:1547-1571), and rustdoc concatenates them. The first names two seeded places (the single-pair boundary 'where it provably is' and the tip). The second names four candidates and says the unshared answer is reproduced 'exactly' below ε_n = 2. The sweep code (worst_over_cycle, strength.rs:1487) does seed the four: 0, ε_n, ε_n−1, min(ε_n,1). 'provably' and 'exactly' are false under the DB factor for small teeth.
verdict.evidence: Read strength.rs:1547-1571 directly. Probe probes/verify-last-19: z10 ha1.0 ε1.7 gives LinearRamp/None 1.01355, and the sweep moves 8.2e-4 between 200 and 800 samples. z9 ε1.7 gives 1.01921. So the maximum is not at the single-pair boundary, and the unshared answer is not reproduced exactly.
verdict.proposal_note: Merge into one block that lists the four seeded candidates as the code does. State that the count refines interior maxima both inside the band and inside the single-pair zone, where the DB factor can peak (finding 27). Give the measured convergence, including that it is only 1e-3-level at z9/z10 with 200 samples, unless the zone's interior maximum is solved rather than sampled.

title: The ring cut's own gate stops just short of the regime where its fillet is wrong
claim: a_shifted_ring_is_the_shape_its_cutter_leaves sweeps x only up to 0.5 with the default 20-tooth cutter on z = 43 and 60. the_generated_profile_is_the_shape_the_cutter_would_leave uses x = 0 and cutters at least 17 teeth smaller than the ring. Every ring in both grids is prolate (corner radius > cutter operating radius), so neither gate can fail on the wrong-branch fillet (finding 30). That fault puts 59-65 µm between the code's profile and the simulated cut, and 2-3 µm once corrected. This is the project's own 'a bound records where the sweep stopped' failure.
evidence:
Probe verify-added-6 (Ring::cut_by plus verify::ring_cut_envelope):
- 30/20 x0.8 (default cutter): check_ring_cut 0.0589 mm; curtate (corner 11.05 against r'_c 11.199).
- Hula-like 19/14: 0.0649 mm.
- 43/20 x0 control: 0.0036 mm.
The existing gate's own bound is 5e-3 mm (ring.rs:1592), which both curtate cases would fail. On a 1,050-ring grid, 715 rings are curtate and 675 of those get fillet_gap. None of them is in either test grid.
proposal: Extend a_shifted_ring_is_the_shape_its_cutter_leaves to x up to 1.5, and add cutters within 1-10 teeth of the ring (the hula and planocentric regime), with ha0 from 0.8 to 1.25. For a ring with no fillet, assert check_ring_cut < 5 µm and that the fillet exists (no CLAMP_RING_FLANK_FILLET_GAP). Run it against HEAD first and watch it fail, then land it with the fix for finding 30.
validation: On HEAD the extended test fails on 30/20 x0.8 at 0.059 mm. With the κ-signed trochoid it passes, at 0.0032 mm in the probe.

verdict.reason: Both ring-cut gates, and the wrong-centre-distance gate, use only prolate configurations. Their largest ring-minus-cutter tooth gap is 23 (43/20). The shift reaches 0.5 on z43/60 with the default 20-tooth cutter, and x = 0 with cutters of 20-30 teeth. In the curtate case the code's profile misses the simulated cut by an order of magnitude over the gate's own 5e-3 mm bound. The ring does emit clamp.ring_flank_fillet_gap there, so the user is told the fillet was not joined, but the profile shipped is still 65 µm off the cut.
verdict.evidence: Probe probes/verify-last-19 (Ring::cut_by + verify::check_ring_cut at 400/4000, as in a_shifted_ring_is_the_shape_its_cutter_leaves). 30/20 x0.8: corner 11.05 < r'_c 11.199, curtate, check 0.0653 mm, no fillet, clamps [ring_flank_fillet_gap]. Every configuration on the gates' grids is prolate, at 0.0025-0.0028 mm: 43/20 x0/x0.5/x-0.4, 60/20 x0.5, 60/30, 90/25. Even 43/20 x1.0 and 60/20 x1.0 are prolate (0.0025/0.0026). So the regime comes from a small ring-minus-cutter gap plus shift, not from shift alone.
verdict.proposal_note: Extending x to 1.5 on z43/60 with the default cutter will not reach the curtate regime (43/20 x1 is still prolate). The grid must pair a large shift with a small ring-minus-cutter tooth difference (e.g. 30/20 x≥0.8, 24-25/20, hula 19/14 x≈0.6 ha 0.7), with ha0 varied. Select the curtate cases by the condition corner_radius < cutter_operating_radius, and assert that at least one is present so the grid cannot silently drift back to prolate-only.

title: The chooser test's grid oracle admits shifts the chooser correctly refuses, so SLACK is partly absorbing a constraint mismatch
claim: the_shifts_it_chooses_are_the_ones_that_lose_least says 'nothing on that grid may beat what it returns', with eta_at using 'the same bound the chooser obeys'. eta_at refuses only undercut, severed, a root round that does not fit, and a contact ratio below 1.2. The chooser's MeshTrial::efficiency also refuses negative bottom clearance, tip fouling and flank interference. So the oracle scores inadmissible points that beat the chooser. On 9/37 one does so by 1.2e-5, and SLACK = 1e-4 silently covers it. That size is what the SLACK comment says it would catch as a wrong ridge, yet here no wrong ridge is involved.
evidence: Worktree test with SLACK overridden to 1e-5 fails: 'z9/z37: [0.75, 0.8] keeps 0.9762420596, better than the chosen [0.47415, 0.64937] at 0.9762299323 by 1.21e-5'. shifts_for_efficiency with Pinned{shift:[Some(0.75),Some(0.8)]} (freedoms 0, so it returns loss_at(x)) gives None: the chooser refuses the point. With the chosen point pinned it gives Some. Search::refined(3), unpinned, returns [0.47361, 0.64937], the same ridge. Diff: /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-added-8/auto.diff.
proposal: Give eta_at the chooser's remaining refusals: bottom clearance via Mesh::bottom_clearance, flank interference via Mesh::flank_interference, and tips clear. Build them from Tooth and Mesh directly, not through MeshTrial, so the oracle stays independent of the search's arithmetic. Then lower SLACK toward the resolution-limited wall error (measure it; about 1e-6 is expected) and rewrite the SLACK prose with the real ratios.
validation: After the change, [0.75,0.8] on 9/37 is None in eta_at. The test passes at the lowered SLACK. Removing any one of the added refusals from eta_at makes the test fail at that SLACK on 9/37, 17/43 or 13/37.

verdict.reason: eta_at in the_shifts_it_chooses_are_the_ones_that_lose_least refuses only undercut, severed, root-round and contact-ratio failures. MeshTrial::efficiency (auto.rs:1236-1265) also refuses negative bottom clearance, fouling tips and flank interference. On 9/37 the oracle scores three grid points that beat the chooser, and all three fail flank interference on the pinion; one also has negative clearance on the wheel. The excess reaches 7.45e-5, not just the 1.21e-5 cited, so 3/4 of SLACK is spent on a constraint mismatch. No grid point the chooser admits beats it on any of the three pairs, so after the fix SLACK can drop far lower.
verdict.evidence: Probe probes/verify-last-19, the test's grid and eta_at plus Mesh::bottom_clearance and Mesh::flank_interference on Tooth::flank_ends. z9/37: [0.75,0.8] beats by 1.21e-5, fi [true,false]. [0.8,0.75] beats by 2.81e-5, fi [true,false]. [0.8,0.8] beats by 7.45e-5, fi [true,false], gap[1] = −0.00166. shifts_for_efficiency with both shifts pinned returns None for all three. The maximum excess over the chooser among points the chooser admits is 0 on 9/37, 17/43 and 13/37.
verdict.corrected_claim: On 9/37 three inadmissible grid points beat the chooser, by up to 7.45e-5, which is 75 % of SLACK = 1e-4. All three fail flank interference, and [0.8,0.8] also has negative bottom clearance. On 17/43 and 13/37 nothing on the grid beats the chooser.
verdict.proposal_note: The proposal is sound: add bottom_clearance, tips-clear and flank_interference to eta_at, built from Tooth/Mesh directly. Since the excess among admissible grid points is exactly 0 at SHIPPED, SLACK can be set from the measured wall error once the refusals are added. Rewrite the SLACK prose, which currently credits the boundary approach for margin that the mismatch is using.

title: summarise's per-z metrology loops: the over-pins 'around' sweep runs two full over_pins_at per start on a concentric gear whose every start is identical
claim: The pins closure calls over_pins_at for every start in 0..z, for both two and three pins, to report an 'around' range. On a concentric gear all starts are identical, so the same redundancy finding 50 names for the pin-diameter range also exists here. It is about 20x cheaper per start, though, and not a practical problem.
evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-added-9/src/main.rs: pins(2+3, all starts) takes 0.23 ms at z300 and 0.77 ms at z1000, native, concentric.
proposal: When fixing finding 50, apply the same shortcut here: gear.distinct_teeth() == 1 means one start answers for all. Better, give Gear one helper, e.g. `starts()`, that yields one representative per distinct configuration, and use it in pin_diameter_range_around, best_span_around and this sweep, so the three stay consistent.
validation: The around ranges are bit-identical before and after on concentric and eccentric gears. Time at z1000.

verdict.reason: The pins closure (crates/gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:357-372) calls over_pins_at for every start in 0..z, once for two pins and once for three. It also computes start 0 twice, once for `nominal` and again in the loop. On a concentric gear every start gives the same bits, so one start would answer for all. The cost is real but trivial: under a millisecond at z1000.
verdict.evidence: My probe (probes/verify-last-20, release build) collected the to_bits() of every start's nominal. Concentric z17, z300 and z1000 give 1 distinct value out of z for both Two and Three. Eccentric z60 at amplitude 0.3 gives 24 and 60 distinct values, with distinct_teeth 31. Timings per call: pins(2+3) sweep 0.237 ms at z300 and 0.760 ms at z1000. pin_diameter_range_around takes 4.86 ms and 17.9 ms at the same sizes, so it is about 20-25x dearer. best_span_around takes 0.037 ms and 0.126 ms.
verdict.proposal_note: The concentric shortcut (distinct_teeth() == 1, so one start answers) is safe and keeps the bit-identity the comment at over_pins_at cares about. The more general `starts()` helper, one representative per distinct configuration, is not simple for an eccentric gear. A measurement over pins depends on two or three spaces half a turn apart, and the eccentric z60 case gives 24 and 60 distinct values, not distinct_teeth, so no simple class exists to key on. Limit the helper to the concentric case, or drop it. Worth doing only together with added#50.

title: Helical span over teeth never checks that the face is wide enough for the anvils to straddle W sin β_b
claim: On a helical gear, the two anvil contacts of a span measurement lie along the generators, displaced axially by W sin β_b. So a span is only takeable when b > W_k sin β_b, plus the anvil's own size (DIN 3960 / ISO 21771 state this condition). best_span and best_span_around choose k from radial validity alone. The metrology module's premise is that a plausible number for an untakeable measurement is worse than nothing, yet a helical gear on a narrow face gets a span that cannot be placed.
evidence: For z60 β35 m1 x0: k=8 gives W = 23.618, so the face must be ≥ 12.73 mm; k=12 (the right k once finding 55 is fixed) gives W = 35.427, so the face must be ≥ 19.09 mm. metrology.rs never reads a face width (grep 'face' finds only a comment at :258), and GearParams carries none, since face width is a train member's input. Computed with the closed form W = cos β_b r_b[2π(k−1)/z + s_t/r + 2 inv α_t].
proposal: Pass the face width into best_span / best_span_around as an optional argument (the train member has it; a lone gear can pass None). Treat k as admissible only if W_k·sin β_b ≤ b. When the face is what excludes every k, report it as a distinct MeasurementError (e.g. FaceTooNarrowForSpan) with its catalogue key ×5. Document the condition in reference.md#span-over-teeth.
validation: A law over the helical grid: every reported span satisfies W sin β_b ≤ b. For a gear with a face below W_min sin β_b, the span is refused with the new key. Spur results are unchanged, since sin β_b = 0.

verdict.reason: The geometry and the numbers hold. On a helical gear the two anvil contacts are displaced axially by W sin β_b, and metrology.rs never reads a face width. The claim that a span 'cannot be placed' on a narrow face overstates what the code does wrong. A span is only computed for the lone-gear panel: summarise in gear-wasm calls best_span_around. That request (GearRequest) and GearParams carry no face width, so the tool has no face to check against. No train member gets a span at all: grep finds best_span only in metrology.rs, its tests and summarise. So the proposal's premise that 'the train member has it' does not apply, since the train path never reports a span.
verdict.evidence: Probe: z60 β35 m1 x0 gives span_over_teeth k8 = 23.6182 and k12 = 35.4267, both equal to the closed form m cos α_n[(k−0.5)π + z inv α_t]. W sin β_b = 12.730 mm and 19.094 mm, and best_span picks k=8. GearParams fields (params.rs:20-71) have no face width. GearRequest (gear-wasm/src/lib.rs:32-80) has none either. reference.md#span-over-teeth (around line 1392) states the radial admissibility only.
verdict.corrected_claim: On a helical gear, a span over k teeth needs a face of at least W_k sin β_b plus the anvil allowance. The only place a span is reported is the lone-gear summary, which has no face width, and neither the output nor reference.md states this requirement. On z60 β35 m1 the chosen k=8 needs a face of 12.7 mm or more, and a gear with a narrower face can only be measured with a smaller k, over pins, or over balls. No train path reports a span, so no known face width is being ignored.
verdict.proposal_note: Report the requirement instead of adding an input. Output `min_face_for_span = W_k·sin β_b`, a closed form in the same units as the span, beside the span in SpanOut, and state the condition (plus an anvil allowance, per DIN 3960 / ISO 21771) in reference.md#span-over-teeth. It is 0 on a spur gear, so spur output is unchanged. Adding an optional face argument and a FaceTooNarrowForSpan refusal only makes sense if a face width is added to GearRequest, or if spans are later reported per train member.

title: contact.rs test doc attributes the chooser's 9/37 answer to the test, and its 17/43 result depends on the grid bound because root_radius_fits is omitted
claim: Two problems in an_external_pair_loses_least_well_above_its_undercut_floor. First, its doc says 'at 9 teeth the floor pins x1 at +0.50 and the optimum puts the rest on its wheel', but the test's own best on 9/37 is (1.45, 2.00): the sentence describes the production chooser. Second, the test does not apply root_radius_fits, which is the constraint that confines the 17/43 optimum. On a grid wider than x2 ≤ 2.0 the test's own filter picks a point at the ε ≈ 1 edge, (0.80, 3.25), not (0.50, 0.75).
evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-added-11, mode 63b. With the test's filter (undercut, severed, ε ≥ 1.0) on i, j ≤ 80: 17/43 best (0.8, 3.25), η 0.9896236, ε 1.0014, versus (0.5, 0.75), η 0.9847224, on the test's grid. Adding root_radius_fits restores (0.5, 0.75). 9/37 on the test grid: (1.45, 2.0).
proposal: Apply root_radius_fits (and the interference and bottoming refusals, or better, build points through auto::MeshTrial) in this test's filter, so its answer does not depend on where the grid ends. Rewrite the doc's 9-teeth sentence to describe what the test asserts.
validation: Re-run the test with x2 up to 4.0: the best must stay where it is on the shipped grid. The three existing assertions still pass.

verdict.reason: Both halves reproduce. On the test's own grid and filter the 9/37 best is (1.45, 2.00). The doc's 'floor pins x1 at +0.50 and the optimum puts the rest on its wheel' is the production chooser's answer, (0.474, 0.649). On 17/43, widening the grid to 4.0 without root_radius_fits moves the best to the ε ≈ 1 edge at (0.80, 3.25). With root_radius_fits it returns to (0.50, 0.75). That point is also the one the doc's 98.47% and 'the optimum is interior... nothing is holding it there but the loss itself' describe, so the doc's figures are grid-bound. The three assertions (best Σx > 1, η margin, ε smaller) pass on either grid, so the test does not fail. The defect is the doc text plus a test whose answer depends on where the grid ends.
verdict.evidence: Probe (probes/verify-last-20, grid step 0.05, ε ≥ 1). 9/37: grid to 40 without rootfit gives (1.45, 2.00), η 0.977166, ε 1.2540. Grid to 80 without rootfit gives (0.55, 3.00), η 0.982446, ε 1.0030. With rootfit, both grids give (0.80, 0.80), η 0.976304. The chooser (shifts_for_efficiency, Search::SHIPPED, ε ≥ 1.0 or 1.2) gives (0.4741, 0.6494). 17/43: grid to 40 gives (0.50, 0.75), η 0.984722, ε 1.4776. Grid to 80 without rootfit gives (0.80, 3.25), η 0.989624, ε 1.0014. With rootfit, both grids give (0.50, 0.75). The chooser gives (0.5067, 0.7664).
verdict.proposal_note: root_radius_fits alone does not make the 9-teeth sentence true. With it, the test's 9/37 best is (0.80, 0.80), not x1 at the floor. To reproduce the chooser's answer, build each point through auto::MeshTrial so the interference, bottom-clearance and ε ≥ 1.2 refusals apply. Otherwise rewrite the sentence to describe what the test finds. The validation line 'the best must stay where it is on the shipped grid' needs restating: with root_radius_fits the 9/37 best moves from (1.45, 2.00) to (0.80, 0.80), and then stays there as the grid widens.

title: An unsized internal distance is also only checked for far-side tip room at running: Planocentric 30/32 reports clear while its far-side gap goes negative inside its own tolerance band
claim: The report's TipRoom (tip_interference, far_gap) is read only at running. On an internal mesh the tips' far-side gap `r_a,ring − r_a,pinion + a` falls as the distance falls. An automatic distance that the tips did not need to size therefore gets no check at the tight end either. planocentric(30, 32) runs at 0.98 with far gap +0.0151 mm, which is not sized. At running − 0.02 (inside its ±0.02 band) the gap is −0.0049 mm: the pinion's far-side tip reaches past the ring's tip circle. tip_interference stays false because the circles no longer cross (margin +inf), and the gap is not in the verdict. This is the same missing band check as finding 66, but in the far-gap half and on a distance that was not sized, so a fix scoped only to the sizing (`sized`) would miss it.
evidence: Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-added-12, 30/32 (tip_clearance 0, tol ±0.02): running 0.980000, sized_by None. Report tips (false, 1.2655 deg, far 0.015082). ring::mesh_at at 0.96: foul false, margin +inf, far −0.00492. At 0.97: far +0.00508. At 0.98: far +0.01508.
proposal: Implement finding 66's fix as one admissibility read, the room at `running − tolerance_minus` for both the crossing margin and the far gap. Use it in the sizing (`tip_room`) and in the report. The sizing then opens every distance whose room at the tight end falls short, 30/32 included. The report's tip_interference then covers the far gap as well, so a negative gap at the tight end is reported as a foul.
validation: planocentric(30, 32) solved alone: ring::mesh_at at running − 0.02 gives far gap ≥ tip_clearance and tip_interference false. A shape with tolerance_minus = 0 reproduces today's figures.

verdict.reason: The numbers reproduce. planocentric(30,32) runs at 0.98 with sized_by None, and at 0.96 (running − tol₋) the far gap is −0.00492 with margin +inf and tip_interference false. But the defect is broader than the claim and differently placed. tip_interference never reads the far gap at all, not only at the tight end of the band. Once the far gap is negative, the ring's tip circle lies wholly inside the pinion's, the circles stop crossing, and margin = +inf reads as clear. With the distance stated at 0.96, the report at running says far_gap −0.0141, tip_interference false, and no note. On the other hand, 'reports clear' is overstated for every example found. In 30/32, at both the automatic and the stated distance, the same mesh reports flank_interference [true, false], so the mesh is already flagged, just not for its tips. A sweep of planocentric zp 12-80, Δz 1-8 (519 solved) found only two unsized distances, 20/28 and 30/32, with a tight-end tip problem, and both have flank_interference true. Finding 66's proposal already moves both the sizing and the report to the tight end. What this finding adds is that the far gap must enter the tip verdict.
verdict.evidence: Probe (probes/verify-last-20). Automatic 30/32: running 0.980000, sized_by None, report tips (false, 1.2655°, far +0.015082), flank [true, false]. ring::mesh_at gives, at 0.960: foul false, margin +inf, far −0.00492; at 0.965: margin +2.493°, far +0.00008. Stated distance: a = 0.96 gives tips (false, inf, −0.01410), flank [true, false], no notes; a = 0.94 gives (false, inf, −0.04132); a = 0.90 gives Err(CentreDistanceTooSmall). TipRoom::at (train/mod.rs:579-589) sets tip_interference = m.tip_interference only, while far_gap is informational: the panel shows it (TrainPanel.svelte:1185) and no verdict reads it. Of the 519 solved, all but two hits are sized_by Some, which is finding 66's case.
verdict.corrected_claim: TipRoom's verdict ignores the far-side gap. When r_a,ring − r_a,pinion + a < tip_clearance, the tip circles no longer cross, so tip_margin = +inf and tip_interference = false, and the tips are reported clear. This happens at running on a stated distance (30/32 at 0.96: far gap −0.014 mm) and at running − tol₋ on an unsized automatic one (30/32: −0.0049 mm). In every case found, the mesh's flank_interference already reports a foul, so no case was found where a mesh is reported clean overall.
verdict.proposal_note: Fold the far gap into the verdict: tip_interference = margin < 0 || far_gap < tip_clearance. Read it at running − tolerance_minus, where both rooms are smallest, as finding 66 proposes. Use one admissibility helper for the sizing (tip_room already takes min(far_gap − asked, crossing)) and for the report, so the two cannot disagree. Validation: a stated 30/32 at 0.96 must report tip_interference true, and a law over the presets and a planocentric sweep must hold far_gap ≥ tip_clearance whenever tip_interference is false.

title: Shape::assembly pools meshes from every body on a carried axis, judging independent planet bodies as one rigid stepped planet
claim: The phase rule assumes one psi per planet body, but the pairs are collected per axis. A carried axis with two bodies, which the panel creates via Move{to: None} or AddGear{on: NewBody}, is judged by the stepped-planet gcd rule across bodies that turn independently. The result is a false planets_not_evenly_spaced warning.
evidence: Probe verify-last-1: Compound preset, Edit::Move{member:4, to:None} puts the second planet gear on new body 6 of axis 1 (bodies 5 and 6). With that gear at 18 teeth, assembly(1) = Some((false,false)). The correct answer is equal = true: body 5 (18 on sun 24 and ring 60, 3 | 84) assembles, and body 6's single mesh leaves its psi free.
proposal: Collect pairs keyed by the planet member's body. Apply the pairwise condition only within a body, so a body with one mesh adds nothing. Compute simultaneous over all centrals the axis meets. This also removes the `pairs.len() < 2` None branch.
validation: Unit test: the Compound preset with the second planet moved to its own body and set to 18 teeth gives Some((true, false)). The existing the_rule_agrees_with_the_search test still passes.

title: planets_not_evenly_spaced message names a sun and a sum, which is wrong for Wolfrom and stepped sets
claim: The note says "sun and ring tooth counts do not sum to a multiple of planet count". The rule it reports is the general gcd rule. The shipped Wolfrom preset, which has no sun, fires it by default, so its explanation is false for that case.
evidence: Probe verify-last-1: Wolfrom preset notes include part.planets_not_evenly_spaced. The Wolfrom has no sun member, and its condition is N | z_r2 - z_r1.
proposal: Reword it in all five catalogues to state the general condition, e.g. '{planets} planets cannot be evenly spaced at these tooth counts'. Optionally carry the offending pair of members as values.
validation: tools/check_strings.py; the strings firing test.

title: Thickness-coefficient relief is declared per mesh, but the relation runs along the whole mesh chain: an idler train can keep two given k's that break the mesh rule, with no word
claim: freedoms() pushes one ThicknessMod group per mesh with given_at_most 1. The mesh rule (k_b = 2 − k_a external, k_b = k_a internal) propagates along chains, so a component of the mesh graph has one thickness number, not one per mesh. On the Idler (meshes (0,1) and (1,2)), a designer who has given k2 and then gives k0 keeps both: each mesh has one given and one automatic, so relief moves nothing. thickness_mods() then fills k1 from whichever mesh comes first in the loop (k1 = 2 − k0). Mesh (1,2) is left with k1 + k2 ≠ 2, against the documented rule, and no note fires. The result also depends on the order of the meshes: listed the other way round, k1 would be 2 − k2.
evidence: Probe bin /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-last-2/src/bin/idler.rs: Idler, k2 = 0.9 given and relieved with just = Member(2), then k0 = 1.1 given and relieved with just = Member(0). Output: 'meshes [(0, 1), (1, 2)]', 'given: [(true, 1.1), (false, 1.0), (true, 0.9)]', 'ks [1.1, 0.8999999999999999, 0.9]', so mesh (1,2) sums to 1.8. It is also the source of the ThicknessMod differences in the group-order sweep (added2#11).
proposal: Declare the thickness coefficient the way the module and pressure angle are declared: one FreedomGroup per mesh_groups() component, with given_at_most 1 and automatic_at_most len − 1 (or len, since all automatic means k = 1). Order the entries by member, with `just` spared. thickness_mods() then has one source per component, and its result no longer depends on mesh order. The alternative is to make each gear's k an independent input and drop the 'sum to 2' invariant from the docs.
validation: A law over every preset and arrangement: after relief, each mesh-graph component has at most one given ThicknessMod, and thickness_mods() satisfies every mesh's rule to 1e-12 for random given values. Before the fix the Idler probe above fails it.

title: A set with all three shifts given and its distance automatic is refused as 'these tooth counts cannot be assembled' when the shifts merely disagree
claim: When no member absorbs, closed() checks that the two meshes' running distances agree to 1e-9 relative and returns None if they do not. The caller reports the same NoAssembly-style text used for a genuine non-assembly. Three given shifts that miss by 1e-4 (for example a ring shift typed to four decimals) are over-determined input, not tooth counts that cannot assemble.
evidence: Worktree run on planetary(12,30,72,3) with the sun and planet at settled+0.7 and the ring given at 2.1125 (the closed form to 4 decimals), distance automatic: 'err no profile shift brings the meshes to one axis distance; these tooth counts cannot be assembled'. Relief in the panel normally prevents this state, but a file or the CLI can reach it.
proposal: Give the over-determined case its own refusal key naming the two meshes' distances and their difference, or let relief's rule apply inside the solve. Keep 'cannot be assembled' for when no shift of the free members closes the set.
validation: A test giving all three set shifts at a 1e-4 mismatch asserts the refusal's key is the new one; check_strings and the string tests pass.

title: GearPanel shows an external gear's undercut and pointed-tip figures as a ring's shift note
claim: When the tab's kind is a ring (internal), notesFor still builds the profile-shift note from solve_gear's external ranges: 'bound, undercut, sharp-rack undercut, pointed'. For a 30-tooth ring it prints undercut -0.755 and pointed 1.622, and neither describes anything about a ring. The ring's own clamps start well inside that range (tip raised up to x=+0.10 at z=30).
evidence: GearPanel.svelte:91-93 uses shiftNote(result.ok.ranges.profile_shift) whatever `internal` is; r3b.mjs shows solve_gear ranges at z=30 {undercut:-0.7547, pointed:1.6223}, while the ring is clamp-free only on [0.10, 0.68].
proposal: For an internal tab, show only the thickness bound, which does carry over, plus a ring-specific range once one exists (tip at base or pointed circle, space closure, ra<rf). Until then show a sentence saying the ring's limits are reported as clamps.
validation: Open a ring tab at z=30: the shift note contains no undercut or pointed figure.

title: The sharing-note test pins magnitudes taken from four hand-picked designs
claim: the_sharing_note_quotes_a_number_the_sweep_still_produces sweeps only four (z, ha) pairs and asserts relief ∈ [15, 35) % and increase ∈ [5, 30) %. It certifies the message's '24 %/15 %', while a plain grid shows increases up to 74 %. The test cannot notice that the message understates the effect, because the design sample is where the quoted numbers came from.
evidence: Re-ran probes/verify-gear-io-1 bin sharing. The four test designs give +15.6, +11.7, +23.6 and −15.2 %. A grid over z 20..150 step 5 and ha 1.0..1.5 step 0.025 gives +33.3 % and −73.6 %.
proposal: Keep the two sign assertions and the below-band identity. Replace the magnitude band with a grid sweep whose extremes are compared with whatever the message states, or remove numbers from the message and drop the band.
validation: With the grid, the current '15 %' message fails the check. After the message change the check passes.

title: zh-Hant uses two words for 'load' (負荷 and 載荷)
claim: The same concept, a load or load case, is rendered as 負荷 in some messages and 載荷 in others, and 負載 appears in load_sharing_out_of_band (line 65).
evidence: Line 43 '均分負荷', lines 73-76 '負荷', line 53 '載荷作用點', line 111 '載荷工況', line 65 '負載分配'.
proposal: Choose one term, per the CNS vocabulary the header cites, and apply it throughout. Add it to the per-concept glossary check.
validation: grep shows a single term for load across the zh-Hant catalogue.

title: worm() seeds its helix from a hard-coded 7 mm even when the caller then sets another worm diameter
claim: The automatic helix seed in worm() is acos(starts/7), where 7 is the preset's diameter written as a literal a second time (Auto::fixed(7.0) sits two lines below). gear-cli builds arr::worm(starts, z).with_first_diameter(d), so for d != 7 the seed held in the helix boxes, which relief falls back to, belongs to a different worm.
evidence: arrangements.rs:712 `let helix = (f64::from(starts) / 7.0).acos().to_degrees();` and 715 `pitch_diameter = Auto::fixed(7.0)`. main.rs:26 `arr::worm(starts, wheel_teeth).with_first_diameter(worm_diameter)`.
proposal: Bind one `let d1 = 7.0;` and use it for both. Have with_first_diameter reseed the automatic helix boxes from the stated diameter, or leave the seed for the solve to fill.
validation: arr::worm(1,40).with_first_diameter(10.0): the automatic helix manual values equal acos(1/10), not acos(1/7).

title: A mesh with pinion flank interference is refused as 'the teeth never contact'
claim: When the mate's tip passes the pinion's interference point (approach > r1·sin α_w), Mesh::relative_curvature returns None at the path's start. contact_stress then returns None and the whole train fails with TrainError::NoContact, whose message is 'the teeth never contact'. The teeth do contact; the mesh interferes. This is a refusal of a shape that exists (against rule 5), and its message misstates why.
evidence: Instrumented worktree (removed): every NoContact in a pair([z1,z2]) sweep for z1 = 2..4 came from shape.rs:3322, with approach > r1 sin α_w (for example 2/5: 0.9496 vs 0.8926). ContactPath::new succeeded in each case.
proposal: Split the error: keep NoContact for ContactPath::new == None, and give interference its own case. Better still, rate the contact over the part of the path outside the interference points and raise the mesh's interference note, rather than refusing the train.
validation: A test that pair([2,5]) either solves with an interference note or fails with an interference-specific error, and a law that NoContact appears only where ContactPath::new returns None.

title: check_golden.sh --fast passes vacuously when the harness lists no cases
claim: If `gear-cli --golden-cases` fails or prints nothing, --fast mode compares zero files, keeps status 0, and prints 'tools/golden: 32 recorded outputs, all unchanged'. That is a false green.
evidence: Process substitution hides the exit status from set -e. The demonstration `done < <(false)` leaves an empty array and the script continues. The --fast comparison iterates only over cases (line 138), and the success line counts the store rather than what was compared (line 162).
proposal: Capture the list into a variable, which set -e checks, and refuse an empty list. In --fast, also refuse when no case survives the filter, and print the number compared rather than the store's file count.
validation: With a stub gear-cli whose --golden-cases prints nothing, --fast, full and --write each exit non-zero and leave tools/golden unchanged.

title: .cargo/config.toml: jobs = -1 is documented as 'all available cores' but means all but one
claim: `jobs = -1` carries the comment 'Use all available cores for parallel compilation'. In Cargo, a negative value is added to the logical CPU count, so -1 uses all cores but one. `color = "auto"` restates the default.
evidence: Cargo reference for build.jobs: 'If negative, it sets the maximum number of parallel jobs to the number of logical CPUs plus the provided value.'
proposal: Correct the comment to 'all cores but one, leaving one for the desktop', or delete the key if all cores was meant. Delete `color = "auto"`.
validation: Reread the file; cargo builds unchanged.

title: contact::efficiency's 'forward and backward are equal, physically it should be' is true only at first order in μ
claim: The doc says forward and backward efficiency are equal and that 'physically it should be'. The exact pointwise force balance is not symmetric: on 17/43, the backward η (gear 2 driving) is lower than the forward by 2.0e-5 at μ=0.06 and 5.6e-4 at μ=0.3. The equality comes from the linearisation, not from the physics.
evidence: notes/verify-last-8/eff.py: forward η = (1+sμρ2/rb2)/(1+sμρ1/rb1), backward η = (1−sμρ1/rb1)/(1−sμρ2/rb2), s = sign(ξ). Uniform path means: 0.98751530 against 0.98749496 at μ=0.06.
proposal: Reword: 'equal at first order in μ; the exact balance separates them at O(μ²), by about 2e-5 at μ=0.06 on 17/43'. Or adopt the exact closed-form mean, which reports the two directions separately.
validation: A test asserts (η_f − η_b)/μ² tends to a nonzero constant as μ→0 under the exact form, or the doc sentence is reworded.

title: Every gear-wasm request caller in core.ts swallows boundary errors, so request-shape drift fails silently
claim: relieveTrain, relieveCase, editTrain, previewEdit and offersAt all catch every exception and return nothing, [] or null. A malformed request, such as a renamed field or a missing field that serde rejects, looks to the user like 'no offers' or 'nothing happened', with no log. This compounds added2#42: untyped requests break silently at run time, and the breakage is also invisible there.
evidence: core.ts:853-856 `try { return JSON.parse(wasm_offers(...)) } catch { return []; }`. core.ts:680-683 `catch { return; }`. editTrain returns null for any non-'ui.' message.
proposal: Log non-refusal boundary errors (console.error with the entry-point name) before returning the fallback, or rethrow them in development builds.
validation: Rename a request field in the Rust; the dev console shows the serde error when offersAt is called.

title: Error Display impls in gear-core hold a second, drifted copy of the English error text
claim: The CLI's English (Display) and the browser's English (catalogue) give different sentences for the same error. Rule 2 says gear-core holds no English, and these impls keep a second copy that already disagrees with the first.
evidence: MeshError::OutsideInvoluteDomain reads 'no such gear pair: the profile shifts require the base circles to overlap' (mesh.rs:771-772) but 'profile shifts leave no operating pressure angle' in the catalogue (strings_en.toml:190). ShaftAngleImpossible reads 'that shaft angle leaves the wheel with no lead angle' in the Display and 'the shaft angle leaves the second member with no lead angle' in the catalogue. NoContact reads 'the teeth never come into contact' and 'the teeth never contact'.
proposal: Make the CLI render errors through gear-io's English catalogue, which it can already load, from each error's Explain::note(). Then delete the English Display bodies, or reduce them to printing the key. The error types would then satisfy rule 2 literally.
validation: Run the golden corpus with tools/check_golden.sh; outputs that print errors will change to the catalogue wording, and that is the intended diff. Then check that grep for English sentences in gear-core Display impls finds none.

title: A mesh endpoint out of range in a train file panics rather than being refused
claim: A document with meshes[0].a = 99 panics with an index out of bounds inside from_toml, during relief, and again in solve_train. It is not returned as an error. This may duplicate the 'finding 1' that added2#49 refers to; I list it only in case that finding does not cover the panic in from_toml itself.
evidence: Probe verify-graph-ops-1 `doc mesh`: 'mesh: from_toml Err("index out of bounds: the len is 5 but the index is 99")' (caught by catch_unwind, so it is a panic).
proposal: Add one structural index validator, called from from_toml before relieved() and at the wasm boundary. Refuse any out-of-range member body, mesh endpoint, body axis, carried_by, coupling end, hold or load-case body with a catalogue key.
validation: A fuzz law: for every index field of a preset's document, setting it to len+1 returns a structural refusal from from_toml and never panics.

title: smallest_tooth_count is engineering math living in the wasm boundary crate
claim: The ring's smallest-tooth-count limit is computed in gear-wasm rather than gear-core. The CLI and any other caller cannot reach it, and it cannot be tested against Ring's own clamp at ring.rs:278-281.
evidence: lib.rs:554 `fn smallest_tooth_count(params: &GearParams) -> u32` recomputes α_t from degrees itself instead of reading Ring::alpha_t. CLAUDE.md's file map says gear-core holds 'all the mathematics'.
proposal: Move it to gear-core's ring.rs as a function of GearParams, including x (see the finding on its formula). Have wasm call it, and add a law against the tip clamp.
validation: A new gear-core test sweeps x, β and α and asserts that at z = smallest_tooth_count the unclamped tip is at or above the base circle and at z − 1 it is below.

title: TrainPanel comment says Rust 'has already chosen between the dry and conditioned states', a choice the core no longer makes
claim: The property snippet's comment describes an older model in which a material carried paired dry and conditioned numbers and Rust picked one. Today each library entry is one material in one state, named by its condition. Nothing chooses between states, and the dry figures survive only in notes.
evidence: TrainPanel.svelte:1032-1034: 'The number shown is Rust's — it has already chosen between the dry and conditioned states'. materials_default.toml:13: 'Each entry is one material in ONE state, named by its `condition`'. gear-io materials.rs:141 test: 'the old paired dry/conditioned numbers'.
proposal: Replace the sentence with: 'The number shown is Rust's: the library entry's, for the one state its condition names, or the override.'
validation: Read the comment against materials_default.toml:13-20; npm run check is unaffected.

title: addCaseOfKind selects the wrong case when editTrain fails silently
claim: If edit_train throws a non-'ui.' error, addCaseOfKind still sets tab.view.case to load_cases.length - 1 and selects it. That is the existing last case, not a new one, so the UI presents an old case as the one just added.
evidence: TrainPanel.svelte: `editTrain(tab.train, { add_case: kind.key }); tab.view.case = tab.train.load_cases.length - 1; select({ case: tab.view.case });`. The return value is ignored, and editTrain returns null on a defect.
proposal: Check editTrain's return, and skip the selection change and show the refusal or boundary-failure note when it is non-null (together with the added2#80 fix).
validation: A mocked edit_train that throws: the selected case index is unchanged and a note is shown.

title: auto.rs's own tests of shifts_for_efficiency test production-dead code
claim: shifts_for_efficiency and Pinned (with its place and freedoms) have no production caller. Three tests in auto.rs's test module still drive them, alongside the train test in added2#87, so they hold up a second, parallel coordinate mapping that the shape's search (shape.rs:1786-1856) re-implements.
evidence: grep -rn shifts_for_efficiency crates: definitions at auto.rs:1484; calls at auto.rs:2764/2850/2876 (inside #[cfg(test)] starting 1932) and train/mod.rs:5253/5279 (test). There is no call from gear-wasm or gear-cli.
proposal: Delete shifts_for_efficiency, Pinned and Bounds if they have no other users. Re-aim or drop the three auto.rs tests together with the train test in added2#87, so that one coordinate mapping (the shape's) exists and is tested.
validation: cargo nextest run passes after the deletion, and the re-aimed tests fail under the shape.rs division-swap mutation.
