title: chosen_at closes the searched shifts at a plan the search never evaluated
claim: In Shape::chosen_at's up-to-3-round loop, `found` is set before the plan is re-sized and replaced. The post-loop `self.closed(&plan, &place(&v), helix)` therefore closes the last-found point at a later plan, whenever a later round finds nothing or the rounds run out with the plan moved. No admissibility check is made at that pairing, and `unwrap_or_else(|| settled.clone())` hides a closure failure. This is the general mechanism behind added2#94, and any shape whose tip-sized distance is released by re-sizing can reach it.
evidence: Worktree trace (Planocentric, search on): round 1 plan held [Some(1.734)], v admissible (η 0.99812, shifts [0.5235, 0.8874]). Re-size gives held [None]. Round 2 search gives None. The final closure at held None gives [0.5235, 0.0], which is outside the involute domain.
proposal: Carry the closed shifts, held and bound_by of the round that produced `found`. After the loop, prefer the latest plan's closure only if trial_efficiency is Some there. Otherwise return the round's own. Replace the silent `unwrap_or_else(|| settled.clone())` with that fallback.
validation: The candidate diff /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/notes/verify-last-16-plano-fix.diff (minus its eprintln lines) turns Planocentric searched from Err to Ok, and all 605 gear-core tests pass. A new law, every Preset::ALL and every arrangement solving with set_search(true), fails today and passes after the fix.

title: chosen_at returns shifts scored under one plan paired with a later, unevaluated plan
claim: Each round of the search's resize loop may replace `plan` (and `bound_by`) after sizing again at the chosen shifts. If the next round's maximise finds nothing, or the loop runs out of its three rounds, `found` still holds the earlier round's point. The final Chosen then closes that point under the new plan, which no trial ever built. The result can be an unbuildable design that the solve then refuses (Planocentric with search on), or a design scored under different held distances than the ones it is returned with.
evidence: Instrumented worktree, Planocentric with set_search(true): round 1 chose [0.5235, 0] at held Some(1.734) with trial η 0.998. The resize gave held None, the loop ended with nothing found in round 2, and the final build under held None failed (build_ok=Some(false)), which is the OutsideInvoluteDomain refusal.
proposal: Track the best as a tuple (v, plan.held, bound_by). Replace the plan only once a round under it has found a point. Return the Chosen with the plan that point was scored in. Alternatively, check that the final shifts build and fall back to the last evaluated pair.
validation: New law over Preset::ALL × each mesh searched: search on solves wherever search off solves. It fails on Planocentric at HEAD.

title: flow.rs's energy condition is 'total loss ≥ 0', weaker than the documented 'output absorbs'; max-efficiency hides it
claim: The document's condition 2 requires the output to absorb. The code rejects only a branch whose total body power is negative. Branches where the output (or a derived load) delivers power and friction eats everything pass the check and come out as efficiency 0. They are discarded only because max-efficiency happens to prefer the other branch.
evidence: Instrumented branch powers: every 0-efficiency consistent branch in the hula fixtures has the output's power positive. Replacing the max with 'prefer a branch with an absorbing body, else the first' keeps all 604 gear-core tests green.
proposal: Implement the documented condition directly: require some body to absorb beyond the zero, with no such branch meaning the flow holds. Drop the max and fix the comment.
validation: Full suite green, plus a debug check that the surviving absorbing branches agree within tolerance.

title: rationale.md's solve table also says the tip-width solve is Newton with analytic ds/dr
claim: The table 'Where closed form is impossible' lists row 2, tip radius for a given tip width, as 'Newton, analytic ds/dr'. The code uses two Brent solves with no derivative, and the first of them (the pointed-tooth roll) has a closed form given inv⁻¹.
evidence: docs/rationale.md:419 reads '| 2 | Tip radius for a given tip width | Newton, analytic `ds/dr` |'. auto.rs:739 and 750 both call brent.
proposal: Correct row 2 to 'Brent in the roll u, bracketed by the pointed tooth'. Compute u_point = tan(inv_inverse(psi_b)) in closed form. Alternatively, implement newton_bracketed with dw/du, which is closed form, and keep the table as written.
validation: Read the table against auto.rs. If u_point becomes closed form, check that the existing addendum_for_tip_width tests still pass.

title: The sharing-sweep convergence test omits the small teeth where 200 samples are not converged below the band
claim: SHARING_SAMPLES is justified by the_sharing_sweep_has_converged (a part in 10^4 on quadrupling). That grid uses z ≥ 12 at addendum 1.35 only. On standard z9/z10 pinions below ε_n = 2, the DB factor peaks inside the single-pair zone, and 200 samples move 1.4e-4 to 8.2e-4 on quadrupling, so the stated convergence does not hold there.
evidence: Probe probes/verify-last-19: z10 ha1.0 ε1.7 rel(800−200) = 8.20e-4, z10 ε1.9 4.40e-4, z9 ε1.7 3.68e-4, z9 ε1.9 1.39e-4. All exceed the test's 1e-4 bound.
proposal: Add z9 and z10 at addendum 1.0 to the grid, and either raise the count or find the single-pair-zone maximum with a bracketed maximiser (solve.rs) seeded between ε_n−1 and min(ε_n,1), so that the sub-band answer is exact rather than sampled.
validation: The extended test fails at HEAD with rel ≈ 8e-4 on z10 ε1.7, and passes after the maximiser is added.

title: TipRoom reports tips clear on a stated internal distance whose far-side gap is negative at running
claim: tip_interference is ring::mesh_at's crossing test alone. When the far gap r_a,ring − r_a,pinion + a is negative, the ring's tip circle lies inside the pinion's, the circles do not cross, margin = +inf and the verdict reads clear. This does not depend on the tolerance band: a distance the designer states shows it at running.
evidence: planocentric(30,32) with distance.auto = false and manual 0.96: running 0.96, tips (tip_interference false, margin inf, far_gap −0.01410), no notes. At 0.94: far −0.04132, still false. The same mesh reports flank_interference [true, false], so no case was found where the whole mesh reads clean. Probe /home/user/.cache/gearcalc-audit/probes/verify-last-20.
proposal: Make TipRoom::at set tip_interference = m.tip_interference || far_gap < tip_clearance (pass the distance's tip_clearance, or use 0). Evaluate it at running − tolerance_minus, together with finding 66.
validation: Stated 30/32 at 0.96 reports tip_interference true. Law: tip_interference false implies far_gap ≥ tip_clearance, over every preset and a planocentric sweep.
